# Changelog

All notable public changes to trust-cg are recorded here. The project follows
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) for release identifiers, while the
0.x APIs and file formats remain unstable.

## [Unreleased]

- Add `trust-cg-eqsat`, an eager acyclic e-graph over trust-ir function
  bodies that records a derivation for every rewrite, and
  `trust-cg-eqsat-check`, an independent checker that replays derivations
  against a rule registry and refuses moved, removed or reordered effects
  (PKG-U1). Library only: compilation does not call either crate, and no rule
  carries a discharge record yet.

- Strengthen scalar-wrapper regressions with before/after reads across calls,
  runtime inputs, and valid bool/char cases while retaining the original
  inlined atomic fixtures that expose scalar-cell selection failures.

- Recognize exact single-scalar memory images when projecting into an existing
  scalar cell, including local atomic constructors with C-aligned wrappers.
  Function argument and return ABI checks retain their separate authority.

- Accept canonical nonvolatile atomic load/store generics after checking the
  compiler-declared ordering and boolean types. Volatile accesses, invalid
  element types and illegal orderings stay refused; SeqCst stores retain their
  exchange-and-discard barrier path.

- Recognize the current Trust `abort_immediate` intrinsic and update its legacy
  corpus callers. The intrinsic keeps the trap lowering; libc `abort` and the
  Rust panic authorities retain their separate behavior.

- Iterator tuple arguments preserve scalar component widths and floating-point
  bit patterns in their rustc-layout lanes. Native narrow integer, boolean and
  float items use typed extension or bitcast instead of a 64-bit integer copy;
  pointer components and wasm32 word narrowing retain their existing paths.

- Release runner contract tests pin all 25 source-bound object/JIT cases across
  five targets, including the framed identity and nonleaf controls, with exact
  per-target counts and source-function checks.

- TLS fixture consistency compares Linux's single crate with Darwin's descriptor
  and accessor body lines, with quoted literals pinned and the C driver
  byte-identical. Rust line continuations use the compiler's whitespace semantics;
  runtime guest bytes and proof modes are unchanged.

- Added (x86-64 Linux Rust compilation through the bridge): the rustc bridge
  admits `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` on its ELF CGU-private function route
  (`PrivateSymbolFormat::for_target`), and the adapter's
  `ObjectSymbolPolicy::X86_64_ELF_MODULE` moves to a new
  `FunctionSymbolFactPolicy::AdmitElfSymbolVisibility` admitting
  `Hidden`/`Protected` on a codegen DECLARATION as well as a definition. These
  are one change: measured, the route flip alone lifts nothing, because it
  relocates the refusal from the bridge to the adapter on the allocator shim's
  bodyless hidden `__rdl_*` callee, which every `std` binary links — a program
  whose source only loops and prints refuses on `___rdl_alloc` exactly like an
  allocating one. On the maintained benchmark corpus, which
  DR-X86-LINUX-MAP-20261027 recorded as 18 of 18 refused (12
  `[TCG-VISIBILITY]`, 6 `[TCG-LINKAGE]`), **17 of 18 now compile and exit-match
  the LLVM arm**; `h3_box_leak` still refuses on `[TCG-BOX-DEREF]`, a MIR
  lowering gap of a different class. The facet is deliberately not
  `AdmitElfSymbolFacts`, which would also admit a function SECTION this emitter
  does not spell, and `WeakUndefinedReferencePolicy::Refuse` is unchanged
  (ruling OD-X86-BRIDGE-ELF-PRIVATE-ROUTE-20261106). Bounded: every result is
  the DIAGNOSTIC lane, since the PROOF lane still refuses them all with
  `[TCG-EH-UNPROVED]` over `panic=unwind`'s walk-through exception tables
  (trusted base TB-12); the private copies are spelled
  `__trust_cg_private.{cgu}.{index}` as `GLOBAL`+`STV_HIDDEN` rather than
  `STB_LOCAL` under the rustc name as LLVM spells them, and equality with LLVM
  is not claimed; and LIMITATIONS' fourth condition still wants a COMMITTED
  x86-64 native control, which does not exist for Linux (both
  `multi_cgu_link_*` targets are macOS-gated), so that condition is named as
  unmet rather than claimed.

- Mach-O linkage diagnostics retain saved per-CGU objects for symbol-binding
  comparisons and separately execute the bridge's published object against the
  same LLVM oracle. The certificates-on refusal control now uses a valid
  `extern_weak` definition instead of `common`, which current Trust rejects
  before codegen; pure policy tests retain `Common` coverage. Original binding,
  object-count, coalescing, export and runtime assertions remain in force.

- Signature-family regression test: retire the stale x86-64 closure
  function-pointer refusal. `clo_fnptr` must compile and match LLVM in all four
  combinations of library and caller backends at O0-O3. The complete target passed
  on native AArch64 and Rosetta x86-64 in its existing `no-proof-certs` lane;
  this adds runtime coverage, not proof or native x86-64 hardware qualification.

- Lean scalar division model: fault on signed MIN / -1 overflow for both
  division and remainder, matching the currently pinned TrustIR interpreter.
  Kernel-checked 8/64-bit boundary, adjacent-defined and unsigned controls
  accompany the guard. OD-57's masked-shift refinement remains unchanged.

- Lean source semantics: fetch from one immutable program throughout source
  runs, certified runs and per-thread concurrent steps. Returns and local
  faults terminate; unfetched instructions cannot invent calls or traps.
  `ProgramWitness` now certifies every finite run of a resident source/x86
  self-loop and exhibits nonempty execution, so the capstone premise is no
  longer universally false. Concrete arithmetic, return, fault and wrong-code
  controls build. Full library build: 32 build jobs; axiom audit: 3,747 declarations,
  zero `sorryAx`, zero project axioms, unchanged 35 native `bv_decide` axioms.
  This repairs model-level vacuity, not the production compiler's proof or
  performance claims; observable machine semantics and source-model binding
  remain open.

- Changed (x86-64 body theorem, OD-235): OD-188's exact fold spells a division
  by a constant power of two as its shift or mask: `bvudiv x 2^k` is `bvlshr x
  k` (`x` for `k = 0`) and `bvurem x 2^k` is `bvand x (2^k - 1)` (`0` for `k =
  0`), exact for every `x`; any other divisor, zero included, is left as it
  is. OD-233's defined cut inputs, the claims and the folded spelling all take
  it. A substituted definition can make a divisor constant that its own block
  did not, and AY build 13556 bit-blasts the division as a division circuit:
  on OD-233's bridge, `<EscapeAscii as Display>::fmt`'s part 2 of 7 (`(bvudiv
  s41 (_ bv1 64))`) timed out in the `no-x86-licm` `core` census (50.1 s
  offline, 0.2 s spelled `s41`). On the combined lane's bridge it replays
  Valid, and that census has 129 failed roots against 177, none newly failing.
  Trusted in addition: the two identities (unit-swept at ten widths from 1 to
  128 against the exact SMT-LIB evaluator). Every golden re-renders unchanged.

- Added (x86-64 body theorem, slice 24c, OD-228): if-converted regions,
  stated over segments. A machine block that lowers a single-entry region of
  LIR blocks (a diamond or two-way switch `X86IfConvert` folds into its
  head's block, with any chain `X86BlockMerge` joined to it) is
  paired with every source path through the region: the head `h` and the
  members `S` it lowers, every member but `h` live, neither the entry nor a
  loop header, entered only from `S` and ending in `Jump`, `Brif` or
  `Switch`, every call, incoming access, rounding operation, stop and indexed
  access of `S` in one member every run passes. The stamps choose the
  segments and `segment::check` re-derives the rule in every build; the
  machine block's successors must be exactly the exit targets, it is walked
  once per exit target from `h`'s entry state, and members walk no rows and
  state no items (re-checked where the theorem consumes the walks, which
  re-derives the effect member and refuses a walk on any other). The parts
  route never cuts inside a segment, at a parameterized exit target, or where
  a value only non-head members define is live (each by its own text). A
  refusal over segments names them (`… (over segments: …)`), and the
  chooser's decline is appended as `; no segment: …`. Every earlier golden
  is unchanged. Slice 24a's `D5` and `D5 parts` fixtures are now stated
  over a chain segment, and its folded-branch fixture (a wrong lowering) is
  stated and refuted on samples instead of declined; their builder rules
  keep quotient-level controls. Trusted in addition: no assumption; the
  theorem generator's trusted code grows by the check, the segment branch of
  the block correspondence, the segment walk and its effects rule, the
  internal-join rule, the region walk's member arm, the per-path member
  skip, the member guard and the choice of the segments it guards, the DAG
  claim floor over segments, the parts bans and the pieces' segment-equality
  guard (OD-228, *Trusted in addition*). The routeless-edge claim for an
  exit the machine cannot take (M2) is ruled and specified, not built: such
  an exit is refused by name. The long diamond fixture, stated in one part
  over OD-226's quotient, and two composition subjects (slice 9's five
  diamonds and slice 16's 34 through the O2 pipeline, each one query) are
  recorded replayer gaps on AY 13556 (no answer within 30 s, nor offline
  within 300 s); their rows stay unverified. Slice 9's `SlotJoin` through
  the O2 pipeline certifies on some runs and not others (deadline-bound on
  the x86-64 Mac). The
  slice's own `core` census: O2 254 -> 215 failed roots (39 promoted, every
  one over segments, 0 newly failing, 0 named mismatches; the ceiling, the
  slice-25 bridge with if-conversion and the `cmov` swap off, is 41, and
  its other 2 have effects in two members, which the rule refuses), O0
  20 -> 20 with byte-identical records, and O3 267 -> 261 against slice
  25's O3 census. Two bodies are refuted in parts, the same with slice
  25's bridge and neither stated over segments, and neither gets credit:
  `core::wtf8::slice_error_fail` (O2 and O3), the cut-interface gap OD-233
  is for, and `core::str::pattern::StrSearcher::new` (O3), a further
  instance of that gap by the 2026-11-07 ruling's diagnosis; whether
  OD-233's rule closes `StrSearcher::new` at O3 is not measured (it will be
  measured on the combined S24c + OD-233 bridge).
- Changed (x86-64 body theorem in parts, OD-233): a cut input the source
  brings as one term over the run's fixed inputs on every edge into its cut
  (entry registers and incoming stack eightbytes, parameter bindings,
  symbol addresses, frame bytes' initial values, `bool` caller views; no
  slot address; at most 64 nodes, normalized by OD-182's bit identities and
  OD-188's exact fold) is DEFINED as that term in the cut's region instead
  of being a free input, and on every edge into the cut, in the edge's
  part, under its guard and where the source runs, the theorem claims the
  input's source term equal to the defined name. The choice
  (`split::cut_definitions`: seeded from the forward edges, shrunk over
  every edge until consistent) reads only the theorem's own source terms;
  `build_theorem` refuses a definition naming an input not fixed for the run
  (K1) or an edge that does not claim one (K2), the claims count as no
  observable, and a defined name is never free. A statement that defines
  nothing is byte-identical to before. On the lane's fixtures this removes
  the refutation of correct bodies whose cut input is a copy the machine
  forwarded (`x86_slot_forward`'s single-predecessor forwarding, the
  `core::wtf8::slice_error_fail` reduction) or an item of two constants
  (slice 25's three slot fixtures).
  `SourceBoundX86Body::defined_cut_inputs`
  counts them, and the verifier's trace prints `defined cut inputs
  bytes=… items=…`. `run_fixed_term` (renamed from `closed_machine_term`)
  now resolves names on an explicit stack. The Darwin x86-64 `core` proof
  census at O2 goes from 254 failed roots to 253
  (`core::wtf8::slice_error_fail`, refuted in one part before, now replays
  Valid; none newly failing, no named mismatch, no refuted body); at O0 the
  20 roots, their records and every emitted object are unchanged. Trusted
  in addition: OD-182's
  meta-argument with defined cut inputs, the run-fixed check and the
  per-edge claim check
  ([record](reports/perf/2026-11-05-darwin-x86-64-od233-defined-cut-inputs/README.md)).

- Fixed (rustc bridge, native targets): a call to a function rustc marks
  `#[inline(never)]` or `#[cold]` stays a call in a native object, as rustc's
  own backend keeps every `#[inline(never)]` call. The bridge recorded those
  functions for the wasm32 lane only, so a native module compile had an empty
  `CompilerConfig::never_inline` and the IR inliner (OPT-4) spliced them into
  their callers wherever it ran: at O1 and above in a compile that makes no
  proof claim (ruling OD-225). Measured on the x86-64 bridge of `b30110fcd` at
  `-Copt-level=2`: no call to either function was left in `main`. The set is
  now recorded for every target, under the name each codegen unit's module
  gives the function (on Mach-O and AArch64 ELF an `Internal` function's
  CGU-private name, which lowering applies before the module is compiled),
  and each native module is given the marked functions it holds a body of.
  A module without such a function keeps its default policy digest and object
  cache identity. A compile that makes a proof claim runs no inliner, so its
  code is unchanged. The `dump-trust-ir` sidecar records the set, and
  `compile_corpus`'s replay of a dump reads it. New test: the bridge's
  `never_inline_native`, compiled with rustc's MIR inliner off
  (`-Zinline-mir=no`) so that only the backend inliner can splice its
  unmarked control. It asserts on Mach-O, where a codegen-unit-private name
  keeps rustc's symbol, and skips elsewhere; it also skips where the build
  compiler lacks `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args`, as on the Darwin x86-64 host, where
  the same steps ran by hand with the t011 overlay's `trustc`
  (OD-NATIVE-NEVER-INLINE-20261107).

- Fixed (bridge diagnostics): the rustc bridge files the codegen crate's
  `CompileError::Aarch64FramePointersUnsupported` (an explicit AArch64
  frame-pointer policy on a route that cannot honor it, added by `ed1c150c7`)
  under the compile driver's code, as it files the AArch64 ISA-profile
  refusal. `classify_compile_error` has no default arm, so from `ed1c150c7` to
  `main`'s arm for the variant (`adaf378f8`) the bridge did not compile
  (E0004, measured building `5a49bb594` on x86-64 Darwin). A test builds the
  variant (one test; a second copy of the same assertion, `3aeee1078`, is
  removed), and a raise-site test drives the real refusal (an x86-64 compile
  with the policy set) through `Compiler::compile` and the classifier.

- Added (x86-64 ELF undefined function references): the x86-64 ELF module
  emitter spells an UNDEFINED function reference's weakness (`STB_WEAK`) and
  visibility (`STV_HIDDEN`/`STV_PROTECTED` in `st_other`), and writes the
  undefined symbol of a weak or visible declaration that nothing in the object
  references, as llc 22 does. On ELF an undefined symbol's visibility binds the
  definition another input supplies — the most constraining one wins — so a
  hidden reference keeps that definition out of the linked image's `.dynsym`;
  writing it default-visible, as this emitter did, silently widened it. All
  five sites that can create an undefined symbol (a data address slot, the EH
  personality, a `GlobalRef` to a data import, an `ExternRefGot` and a call
  fixup) now go through one funnel, so none can widen a reference; with no fact
  stated the funnel writes exactly what `ElfWriter::add_symbol` wrote, and the
  objects are byte-identical. A direct `R_X86_64_PLT32` call to a weak
  undefined callee is refused by name rather than encoded — the displacement is
  a link-time constant and cannot be null, and the adapter addresses every
  declaration through the GOT; the AArch64 emitter has the same backstop for
  its PC-relative forms and x86-64 had none
  (OD-X86-ELF-UNDEFINED-REFERENCE-20261106). The adapter went on to admit an
  undefined reference's VISIBILITY for this target (see the bridge route entry
  above, OD-X86-BRIDGE-ELF-PRIVATE-ROUTE-20261106), which is what the ELF
  route's hidden declarations need; a WEAK undefined reference is still refused
  on its own facet, so `weak_undefined` remains unreachable from an admitted
  module and the call loop's GOT backstop stays a fail-closed second barrier
  rather than the gate. Developed at `b4954b8e4`, the last
  commit the x86-64 Linux host could build before its Trust floor was
  cleared, then
  re-verified at `main` on `trustc 0.12.0+g29ebb403d`
  (OD-HOST-TRUST-0.12-ISOLATED-20261106): the merge of `origin/main` checks
  clean and `x86_64_elf_symbol_binding` (5 cases, both native legs executing
  on this host), `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` (49), `v41_abi_residue_objects`
  (18), `direct_call_binding` (7), `static_indirect_devirtualization` (4),
  `compiler_preflight` (2) and the two in-crate undefined-reference cases all
  pass.

- Fixed: the Rust compiler backend builds with the x86 Mach-O symbol-collision
  refusal and classifies it as an object-emission diagnostic.

- Fixed: attestation record admission rejects ambiguous JSON, malformed record
  shapes and excessive nesting before promotion. Benchmark comparisons retain
  failed and inconsistent runtime outcomes without granting performance credit.

- Fixed: runtime-call payload descriptors reject existing globals whose storage or
  byte-array type differs from the generated immutable descriptor. x86 stack-slot
  address analysis refuses overflowing displacement sums instead of panicking or
  wrapping them in optimized builds.


- Added (x86-64 body theorem, slice 25, OD-227): the scaled-index load
  and store rows and the memory-destination `add`/`xor` rows that
  `X86Peephole`'s address folds and read-modify-write fusion produce at O1
  and above. `MovRMSib`, `MovRM32Sib`, `MovRM8Sib`, `MovzxRM8Sib`,
  `MovsdRMSib`, `MovssRMSib`, `MovMRSib`, `MovMR32Sib` and `MovMR8Sib` over
  `[b + i*s + d]` (a virtual or stack-slot base, a virtual index) are stated
  as the address `LeaSib` computes, by `LeaSib`'s own code, followed by the
  base-only row's access through the unchanged code; `AddMR`/`XorMR` and
  `AddMRSib`/`XorMRSib` into incoming memory are the next two accesses of the
  world trace, an 8-byte load and an 8-byte store of `old + r` or `old ^ r`
  at one address (`add` defines `AddRR`'s flags; `xor`'s stay unmodelled). A
  `MovRMSib` not of that virtual form, or through a register holding a jump
  table's address, is slice 14's dispatch load, which the walk reads as a
  table entry at scale 8, displacement 0 and in the table's own dispatch
  block only (neither the row shape nor the dispatch idiom implies it any
  longer; a read of a table in another block is refused by name). The
  stack-slot scan exempts a slot that is a scaled-index access's base, and
  its refusal now reads `… outside a modelled `[slot + disp]` operand or
  scaled-index base: block B row r, …` (it names its first row since slice
  25.0). Every earlier golden is unchanged. The Darwin x86-64 `core` proof
  census at O2 goes from 378 failed roots to 254 (124 promoted, none newly
  failing, no named mismatch; one root that failed before is now stated in
  parts and refuted in one part by a cut-interface completeness gap, no
  credit); at O0 it is unchanged (20 roots). Trusted in addition: the SDM
  meaning of `ADD`/`XOR r/m64, r64`; the SIB effective address was already
  trusted for `LeaSib` and the dispatch load; and, with no per-compile
  check of its own, the post-theorem lowering of these rows (frame-index
  elimination of a slot base, slot prune and remap, register allocation's
  use-only classification, the presequencing replay): `decode_check`
  re-checks only the encoding of the integer SIB and read-modify-write
  rows, not `MovsdRMSib`/`MovssRMSib`, and the new `e2e_x86_64_sib_rmw`
  target executes eleven O2 fixtures against clang references (OD-227,
  *Trusted in addition*).

- Fixed (wrong code): on x86-64 ELF, Mach-O and COFF and on RISC-V,
  `Compiler::compile` wrote an `Internal`/`Private` function that nothing
  referenced, or that only a `SymbolAddr` named, as a global symbol, so
  another object's call or weak definition bound to the module-local body at
  link time (L02-P1 closure audit, 2026-10-24). Those definitions are now
  local symbols, read back after emission; on x86-64 Mach-O and COFF and on
  RISC-V a `SymbolAddr` naming one is refused by name, as other references
  already were, while x86-64 ELF admits every such reference and binds it to
  the local symbol (OD-X86-ELF-LOCAL-BINDING-20261027; the x86-64 emitters
  take the binding from one carrier since
  OD-X86-BINDING-ONE-CARRIER-20261105). RISC-V writes weak
  and link-once definitions weak and relocates its own calls to them; COFF,
  which cannot spell them, refuses them by name. The link driver now refuses,
  on every linker, a shared-object link whose objects address a
  default-visibility symbol directly (`[TCG-LINK-PREEMPTIBLE-DIRECT]`), which
  gold had linked with the symbol bound locally (L02-P2), and `--shared`
  without `--relocation-model` compiles AArch64 Linux modules `pic`. The
  x86-64 Mach-O emitter binds a reference spelled `_x` to `__x`; it had
  bound it to the module's definition of `x` (a call, an address, a data
  import, a runtime call, the EH personality). A Linux `--shared` link of
  `static` or `pie` objects that define a default-visibility symbol is now
  refused by name on every linker (`[TCG-LINK-PREEMPTIBLE-DEFINITION]`):
  their code had inlined such functions into in-library callers, which
  `LD_PRELOAD` interposition then silently missed. The direct-address
  refusal no longer exempts a linker-defined name (`__start_<sec>`,
  `__ehdr_start`) or a name another input hides when a `-Wl` option can
  define, re-bind or redirect it (`--wrap`, a `--defsym` of a linker-defined
  name, a linker script option), or
  when the linked image's dynamic symbol table exports it with default
  visibility: gold had installed such a library under `--defsym` or
  `--wrap`, and an interposing executable's definition was ignored. It also
  refuses a conditional branch (`CBZ`/`CBNZ`/`B.cond`, `TBZ`/`TBNZ`) to a
  default-visibility function and a local-dynamic TLS access of a
  default-visibility thread-local: GNU ld and gold bound both to the
  library's own definition, without the PLT or a dynamic relocation, and
  the driver had installed such libraries on every linker
  (OD-SHARED-PREEMPTIBLE-BRANCH-TLSLD-20261105). On x86-64 and RISC-V the
  `[TCG-LINK-PREEMPTIBLE-DEFINITION]` refusal no longer advises
  `--relocation-model pic`, which only AArch64 implements
  (OD-MODULE-LOCAL-BINDING-OFF-AARCH64-20261024,
  OD-SHARED-PREEMPTIBLE-DIRECT-20261024, OD-SHARED-PIC-DEFAULT-20261024,
  OD-MACHO-NLIST-KEYED-SYMBOLS-20261024,
  OD-SHARED-NON-PIC-DEFINITION-20261024,
  OD-SHARED-EXEMPT-NAME-REBINDING-20261024).

- Added (x86-64 O2, OD-232): the tracked diagnostic opt-outs
  `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=no-x86-licm` (all of x86 LICM, every tier) and
  `no-x86-loop-unroll` (the full unroller, whose env opt-out had been
  deleted). Both are off by default. The unroller's and const-guard
  elimination's comments no longer describe them as opt-in.
- Added (x86-64 LICM, OD-231): the tracked opt-out
  `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=no-x86-pure-call-hoist` keeps every call to a
  proven-pure function where the source puts it. The pure-call tier has no
  translation-validation net. Its differential corpus
  (`fuzz/repros/purecall/`) had been blocked since the tier's env kill switch
  was deleted, and it runs again on this knob. The runner now also checks
  determinism, requires must-not-hoist objects to be unchanged and requires a
  positive program to hoist. It gains `pc11`, a call in a conditional arm that
  no iteration takes.
- Fixed (x86-64 O2 loop passes, OD-230): two default-on machine passes could
  miscompile in a compile without proofs. A compile that claims proofs would
  refuse or refute either body.
  - `X86LoopRotate` copied a loop test that redefines a register (ISel's
    `Setcc d; Movzx d, d; Test d, d`) as a test of the `setcc` byte, whose
    upper bits are undefined. It also mis-copied tied `AndRI [d, imm]`
    reads, and it threaded headers that read a register they define later.
    The copy now reads, at every position, the value the header reads, and
    the pass refuses the two shapes it cannot copy exactly.
  - LICM's pure-call hoist took calls from any loop block. A "pure" callee
    may diverge or trap, so a call in a conditional arm could hang or trap a
    run that never reaches it. A call now moves into the preheader only from
    the loop's first-iteration path, with no instruction before it that could
    trap or be observed, and calls keep their execution order.
  - Regression tests run both passes on fixtures, including every rotation
    header of up to three instructions.
- Added (x86-64 body theorem, slice 24a, OD-226): a machine block that the
  x86-64 block merge made out of a chain of LIR blocks (each an
  argument-free `Jump` into a block no other edge enters) is stated as one
  block. The theorem is built over the exact contraction of the chain on the
  LIR, the machine's stamps renumbered into its coordinates, by the
  unchanged slices 1 to 23, and binds the original pair; the new
  `Quotient::check` re-derives the contraction from the original pair in
  every build and refuses (`Construction`, no claim) otherwise. Only pairs
  whose block correspondence fails and whose walk needs one are affected;
  every other theorem is byte for byte as before (every earlier golden is
  unchanged; the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census at O2 falls from 582
  to 378 failed roots, none newly failing, and O0 is unchanged). A merged block whose
  chain is not contracted keeps its refusal, which now says why (`; not
  contracted: …`); a refusal over the quotient names its chains, and the
  verifier's body trace prints `merged chains=K absorbed=N` before `stated
  in parts`. Trusted in addition: no assumption; the theorem generator's
  trusted code grows by `Quotient::check`.
- Added (x86-64 O2 attribution): tracked opt-outs for five default-on x86
  machine passes that only had a `TCG_*` environment switch, which `trustc`
  refuses: `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=no-x86-block-merge` (`X86BlockMerge`),
  `no-x86-loop-rotate` (`X86LoopRotate`), `no-x86-licm-loads` (the LICM load
  tier; LICM keeps its pure-only tier), `no-x86-rmw-fuse` (the
  memory-destination read-modify-write fusion) and `no-x86-sroa`. Each is
  absent by default and only disables its pass, so default output is
  unchanged. Through the bridge they are the only way to attribute the O2
  body-theorem refusals each pass causes.

- Changed (proof claims at O1 and above, OD-225): a compile that claims proofs
  (`emit_proofs`, the rustc bridge's default; a verifying JIT validation mode,
  `CachedVerified` (x86-64's JIT default) or `AlwaysVerify`; a raw lane's
  shared LIR step under `InlineOnlyAdmission::Withhold`) no longer runs the
  module inliner (`ir_inline`) or unsigned-range simplification
  (`lir_unsigned_range`), on any target. Neither pass is validated, and every
  per-function proof takes the LIR instruction selection receives as its
  source, so the source of a proof-claiming compile's proofs is now exactly
  the adapter's LIR, as at O0. Compiles that claim no proof are unchanged.
  Such a compile splices no inline-only body (each is listed in
  `inline_only_bodies.withheld`), and a traced one records
  `lir_passes_skipped`. A function whose `Assert` (from a trust-ir `Assume`)
  the range pass used to delete keeps it, and the x86-64 body theorem refuses
  it, as at O0. LIMITATIONS now also names the O1+ post-RA `MovRR` coalescer,
  which runs after the body theorem with no enforced check.
- Fixed (diagnostics): a portable DRAT checker that is missing or cannot be
  read at its build-embedded path is named in a pass-validator refusal
  ("checker not found at <path>") instead of surfacing as the live solver's
  timeout; the 2026-11-03 Darwin x86-64 O2 census filed 17 such roots as
  `[TCG-PASSVAL-067]` solver timeouts. The checker-drift warning names the
  certificate set it is about, so the bound-memory sets' drift no longer
  reads as the canary set being disabled.

- Changed (x86-64 128-bit checked multiply, OD-224): the adapter's flag of
  an `i128`/`u128` checked multiply on x86-64 is the division-free limb check
  (two 64-bit checked multiplies, a carry compare and a both-high-limbs test;
  for `i128` on the magnitudes plus a sign check; for a constant operand a
  compare with `floor((2^128 - 1) / C)`) instead of a division of the product
  by an operand, which called `__udivti3`/`__divti3`. The value is unchanged
  and AArch64 keeps the division form byte for byte. The 11 Darwin `core`
  roots that were this check no longer trust OD-202's routine contract and
  all still certify; the adapter step's evidence (L04-P10) stays statistical.
  The two spellings that depart from the design (the constant form, the
  signed mask arithmetic) have their 128-bit lemmas proved by z3 alone,
  composed by hand and not replayed by AY/Clean.
  The [report](reports/perf/2026-11-02-darwin-x86-64-i128-mulo-divfree/README.md).

- Changed (x86-64 instruction selection): a 128-bit `Ishl`/`Ushr`/`Sshr` by
  a constant amount trust-ir defines (below 128) is folded into immediate
  shifts of the 64-bit halves (`mov`, `mov imm`, `shl`/`shr`/`sar imm`,
  `or`; no count register, compare or `cmov`): `x >> 64` is two rows where
  the general path took 25. An undefined amount (128 or more) and a
  non-constant amount keep the general path byte for byte (OD-215). Every
  row is one the source-bound body theorem already admits; no new trust.
  The [report](reports/perf/2026-10-27-darwin-x86-64-i128-const-shift/README.md).

- Added (x86-64 source-bound body theorem, slice 23): arithmetic congruence
  pairing and the generalization over arithmetic leaves. A machine product,
  unsigned division or variable shift whose stamp names a source operation
  of the same operator key (operation, width, signedness) is spelled as the
  source's, its operands claimed equal (OD-205); the pairing admits nothing,
  is kept only where the spelling does not absorb it, and a paired
  theorem's refutation is decided by the theorem without it. An obligation
  whose exact replay has no verdict is replayed once with every arithmetic
  node a fresh input, and only a Valid replay credits (OD-206). Nothing is
  trusted in addition: a paired theorem carries its pairing record, from
  which the verifier (before any replay) and every export (before any
  publication) re-derive the pairing and the statement; a theorem whose
  record does not re-derive is never replayed or published. An 8- or 16-bit
  variable shift row is refused by name. The three AY-capacity roots of census-s22
  (`align_offset::<u8>`, `u64::overflowing_pow`, `wide_mul_u128::scalar_mul`)
  certify offline on AY 13556 with Clean 5f09e36c; the 15 census-certified
  functions whose theorems change all still certify. The
  [slice-23 report](reports/perf/2026-10-27-darwin-x86-64-slice23-arith-pairing/README.md).

- Fixed (x86-64 source-bound body replay, OD-223): the Clean check of an AY
  proof ran under the AY solve budget (30 s), and a check that ran out of
  it was reported, and remembered by the negative memo, as "AY TIMEOUT".
  `u64::leading_zeros` (census s23final) was lost this way: AY answers in
  7.6-8.0 s, while Clean needs 41-53 s of CPU time for the ~11 MB proof.
  Every Clean check of a proof now has its own deadline: 180 s, never less
  than the solve budget, never unbounded, `TCG_CLEAN_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`
  within (0, 1 h]. That covers the one-shot and resident routes, the part
  and claim replays, the certificate store's re-check, the mint and the
  export's re-check. A checker timeout or refusal is labelled as the
  checker's. The negative memo (schema v6; v5 is never read) records a
  `checker-timeout` apart from a solver `timeout`, keyed by the checker
  deadline. Credit is unchanged: Clean accepts the exact proof or nothing
  is credited.

- Fixed (x86-64 source-bound body theorem, OD-210 amended): the AOT
  certificate lane routed a function on `source_admits_x86_body_owner`, and
  sent every function it rejected down a request-free walk that named no
  module, so a body theorem trusting a runtime routine was refused there as
  `Unnamed` (OD-210, OD-216, OD-217). That predicate is no
  over-approximation of the owner for a function stated in parts: the
  split admits each region from its cut interface (several edges into a loop
  header meet there), which the whole-body admission refuses. On the Darwin
  `core` census (census-s23final) `core::fmt::num::exp_u128` (`__udivti3`)
  and `parse_decimal_seq` (`memmove`) lost their credit so; a lost credit,
  never a false one. Every public x86-64 verifier entry that takes an ABI now
  takes the module's definitions by reference (the forms that name none are
  test-only), both walks of the lane name them (the link unit's included),
  and the lane routes on `pair_admits_x86_body_owner`: exactly the source
  admission for a pair one query states, the split's own pre-plan checks for
  a pair stated in parts, so such a body also keeps its exported theorem.
  No theorem text changes.

- Fixed (tests, x86-64 execution targets): three `trust-cg-codegen` targets
  failed on `main` on x86-64, with and without the `TCG_*`, AY and Clean
  controls; none was a backend defect. `e2e_x86_64_mixed_width_shift` (all
  seven tests) built shifts whose amount kept its own width (`I64 shl I32`),
  which trust-ir's validator refuses (`BinOpTypeMismatch`,
  `OperandTypeMismatch`) and every ingestion entry has refused since WS7.3
  (`3c2356c70`): its fixtures now convert the amount to the value's type as
  the rustc bridge does (`ZExt` a narrower amount, `Trunc` a wider one), and
  two new tests, run on every host, pin that the converted fixtures are
  admitted and that the unconverted spelling is refused at ingestion by
  exactly those two named findings (trust-ir's must-refuse corpus has no such
  row). `e2e_x86_64_i128_stack_abi::sysv_stack_i128_crosses_c_abi_in_both_directions`
  compiled a module with bodyless external declarations and no target
  (`TargetInfoRequired`, also since `3c2356c70`): the sweep module now pins
  the triple it is compiled for, so the System V `i128` stack differential
  runs again (resolves the failure LD-100 records as pre-existing).
  `e2e_x86_64_internal_multi_result::jit_internal_linkage_multi_results_execute_exactly`
  asked the verifying x86-64 JIT to publish bodies whose rows have only
  sampled evidence; the proof gate refuses them, correctly, on every x86-64
  host. Its execution lane now states the dev-only `Unchecked` mode and
  checks that the image says so, and a new test holds the verifying default
  to publishing with every function verified or refusing at the proof gate
  (OD-219). No proof credit moves.

- Fixed (x86-64 source-bound body theorem, OD-210's residuals): a division
  by a `__udivti3` (or a copy by a `memcpy`) the crate defines in another
  codegen unit, or in another function the rustc bridge compiled as its own
  module, was credited Formal although the call binds to that unchecked
  definition. The bridge now names every trusted runtime routine any
  codegen unit of the crate defines (rustc's mono items) to every module it
  compiles (`CompilerConfig::link_unit_definitions`, bound into the cache
  identity and the compile policy), and the verifier refuses such a theorem
  by a typed reason (OD-216). Slice 13's `memcpy`, `memmove` and `memset`
  are guarded like the `I128` division routines (OD-217), and the x86-64
  vectorizer no longer routes a fill inside `memset` itself to `memset`
  (OD-218). [Report](reports/perf/2026-10-27-darwin-x86-64-od216-link-unit-routines/README.md).

- Fixed (fail-open admission): direct strict lowering now refuses a binding
  frame used after a predecessor closed it, using TrustIR's lifetime finding.
  No wrong machine code was demonstrated; a frame that stays live across the
  edge remains supported.

- Fixed (x86-64 source-bound body theorem, the hostile review of slice 22):
  a body whose `I128` division calls a runtime routine the module under
  proof defines (`#[unsafe(no_mangle)] extern "C" fn __udivti3(..) -> u128
  { 0 }` beside a `u128 /`) was credited Formal; so was a `__udivti3` that
  divides through itself. Such a theorem is now refused by a typed reason
  (OD-210): the AOT certificate lane and the JIT name the module's
  definitions to the verifier, which binds them into its input digests; a
  definition elsewhere in the link stays trusted. OD-211 states the routine
  contract's half the call model does not assume (it writes no memory the
  caller observes, has no effect on the world, returns). Controls for three
  checks whose mutants survived: `catnf`'s same-term merge and its zero
  extensions (sign-extension near misses), and the zero constant of the
  `I128` guard. [Slice-22 report §8](reports/perf/2026-10-27-darwin-x86-64-slice22-i128-division/README.md#8-the-hostile-review-od-210-od-211-and-three-controls).

- Added (x86-64 ELF function binding and definition visibility): the x86-64
  ELF module emitter binds a bodied `Internal`/`Private` function definition
  `STB_LOCAL` in the symbol table's local partition, so every
  `R_X86_64_PLT32` call and `R_X86_64_64` address slot in the object reaches
  that object's own body and the name never enters a linked image's export
  surface. `Compiler::compile` therefore stops refusing a module whose bodies
  call or take the address of their own module-local functions on that path
  (`aot_object_binds_module_local_functions`), and reads the emitted object
  back — fresh or cached — with the arch-neutral ELF reader the AArch64 path
  uses, plus the code-reference backstop parameterized by this target's
  branch relocation (OD-X86-ELF-LOCAL-BINDING-20261027). The same emitter now
  writes `STV_HIDDEN`/`STV_PROTECTED` on a function DEFINITION, admitted by a
  definitions-only adapter policy (OD-X86-ELF-DEFINITION-VISIBILITY-20261027).
  Still refused there: a visibility on a function DECLARATION, weak undefined
  references, data-import visibility and explicit function sections. The
  x86-64 Mach-O and COFF writers and RISC-V still bind a module-local
  definition global or private extern, byte-identically to before (no binding
  fact is stated for them), so no lane this host cannot measure changes. New row `x86_64_elf_symbol_binding` reads symbols and
  relocations back with an ELF64 parser written in the test and, on an x86-64
  Linux GNU host, links two objects whose Internal `helper`s share a name
  beside a C global `helper`: each reaches its own body at O0-O3, a gcc twin
  with `static` helpers prints the same, and in a `-shared` link neither
  local `helper` reaches `.dynsym` while an `External` near-twin's does.
  Execution evidence, no proof credit. The rustc bridge is untouched: the
  crates it refuses under OD-BRIDGE-UNSPELLED-BINDING-20261024 it still
  refuses, because that ruling also covers hidden DECLARATIONS.

- Added (x86-64 source-bound body theorem, slice 22): the `i128` division
  class. An `I128` division is the call of its runtime routine
  (`__udivti3`/`__divti3`/`__umodti3`/`__modti3`) under the call model,
  its argument and result placement and symbol checked, and the `I128`
  divide-by-zero guard is slice 14's at 128 bits (OD-202). Trusted, new:
  the linked routine computes trust-ir's division on its defined domain,
  tested by a native differential of `compiler_builtins`' and libSystem's
  copies against an independent bit-serial reference (15.6 M checks each,
  0 mismatches), never proved. A 128-bit product is spelled by its 64-bit
  limbs (OD-203) and bit moves have a normal form (OD-204), identities that
  add no trust. 13 of the 14 targeted Darwin `core` roots certify offline
  on AY 13556 with Clean 5f09e36c; the 142 census-certified functions whose
  theorems the spelling changes all still certify. The
  [slice-22 report](reports/perf/2026-10-27-darwin-x86-64-slice22-i128-division/README.md);
  an AY issue note on an `equiv_simplify` step Clean rejects:
  reports/2026-10-27-ay-equiv-simplify-negated-constant.

- Added (x86-64 source-bound body theorem, slice 21): floating-point
  operations as paired rounding events and the remaining atomics. LIR
  `Fadd`/`Fsub`/`Fmul`/`Fdiv` of `f32`/`f64`, the 64-bit integer conversions
  and `FcvtToInt` of an `f64` are events of the world trace, like calls: the
  SSE row of the same operator key pairs with each, the theorem observes its
  operands against the source's, and both read one result (OD-198, which
  supersedes OD-73 for these operations); `Fcmp` and `ucomisd`'s flags are
  exact over the bits. The claim is refinement: no NaN payload is claimed,
  and the Intel SDM transcription and the default MXCSR (`0x1F80`) are
  trusted. `FcvtToInt` means the saturating conversion (OD-199). A theorem
  with a rounding operation is an abstraction, so AY satisfying its negation
  leaves its rows uncredited, never failed (OD-200; the trace reads
  `Unknown (FP abstraction)`). An `I128` atomic load (the `cmpxchg16b`
  pseudo) and `AtomicRmw Xchg` (the CAS-loop pseudo) are admitted with the
  single-threaded meaning (OD-201), trusting the frame's RBX restore and the
  loaded bytes' writability. All 12 targeted Darwin `core` roots build a
  theorem that certifies offline on AY 13556 with Clean 5f09e36c. The
  [slice-21 report](reports/perf/2026-10-26-darwin-x86-64-slice21-fp-atomics/README.md).

- Fixed (refinement, rustc bridge): Rust's float -> integer `as` casts and
  `to_int_unchecked` lower to trust-ir's saturating `fptosi.sat`/`fptoui.sat`
  at every width (f32/f64 to i8..i128, isize, u8..u128, usize). The bridge
  emitted the raw `fptosi`/`fptoui`, which trust-ir leaves undefined for NaN and
  out-of-range values: trust-ir's reference interpreter refused 2,514 of 6,960
  `as` calls, and a `cc`-linked build returned i128::MAX for `f64::NAN as i128`
  and i128::MIN for `2^127 as i128` on x86-64 Darwin (the bare `__fixdfti` call
  reached the platform's compiler-rt). `to_int_unchecked` takes the saturating
  op too: trust-ir's raw op is undefined on values Rust defines (`-128.9f32` to
  `i8`). With certificates on, x86-64 now refuses the 128-bit conversions
  `[TCG-PROOF-465]` (their guards compare floats). The wasm32 mid-end copies
  the saturating ops as it copied the raw ones. Regression:
  `crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg/tests/float_to_int_saturating_differential.rs`
  (O0–O3: the dumped trust-ir, the reference interpreter and a native
  differential against LLVM over 580 inputs).
  OD-BRIDGE-SATURATING-FLOAT-CAST-20261026; the
  record.

- Fixed: benchmark scratch cleanup refuses the shared temporary root and a
  replaced directory. Removed test mocks that could trigger recursive shared
  scratch deletion. The incident record
  discloses the lost temporary evidence and recovery boundary.

- Fixed (AArch64 O2/O3) and tests (Linux bridge lane): a loop header that
  dispatches through a jump table keeps its bounds compare as an immediate in
  the dispatch block. `const-trip-guard-normalize` read the table's
  `CMP index, #(len - 1); B.HI default` as a constant loop-trip guard and
  hoisted the bound into the preheader, and the switch binder, which binds
  the bound only inside the dispatch block, failed the compile closed
  (`[TCG-A64-SWITCH-BIND] ... no producer in the block`): through the rustc
  bridge, coroutine resume loops of five or more states at O2/O3 (measured
  with five and six; regression: trust-cg-codegen
  `aarch64_jump_table_loop_header_bound`).
  `static_data_linux`, `drop_heap_linux` and `coroutine_generator_linux` are
  Linux AArch64 ELF twins of the Darwin static-data, drop/heap and coroutine
  bridge fixtures and required targets of
  `scripts/check_linux_aarch64_bridge.py` (now nine). They keep the Darwin
  crates and drivers byte-identical, add Linux crates (zero-initialized and
  relocated statics; logged `Box`/`Vec` allocation, reallocation, free and
  drop order; the `ResumedAfterReturn` edge; upvar, resume-argument and
  branchy coroutines) and controls (a store to a read-only static, a
  misaligned exclusive pair, an out-of-bounds index, named bridge refusals
  with LLVM twins), and require each executable at O0–O3 to print exactly the
  model and end as modelled, CG equal to LLVM wherever an LLVM twin exists
  (the bridge-only allocator-interception lanes have none, as on Darwin); a
  modelled abort must name the panic entry it aborted through. All three pass
  (OD-BRIDGE-LINUX-RUNTIME-TWINS-20261024 in the decision record). Every
  bridge compile passes `no-proof-certs`: native testing evidence without
  certificates.
- Fixed (fail-open, rustc bridge): the bridge no longer drops a requested
  function binding or visibility silently (L02-P1, L02-P4 closure audits at
  `4a0668957`). A foreign `#[thread_local]` static declared with
  `#[linkage]` (`extern_weak` or any other import linkage) compiled to a
  strong TLS undefined reference, where rustc's LLVM backend reads a cell
  holding the weak symbol's address (null when absent); it is now refused as
  `[TCG-EXTERN-STATIC-LINKAGE]`. The allocator shim and the C `main` ignored
  `-Zdefault-visibility` and declared the `__rdl_*` callees default-visible,
  so a C shared object over a bridge staticlib exported them and
  `LD_PRELOAD` replaced the allocator; they now take the visibility rustc's
  LLVM backend gives them on AArch64 Linux, Mach-O and wasm32. On
  `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (and COFF), whose objects spell no function
  visibility or module-local binding, every `Internal`, hidden or protected
  function is refused by name (`[TCG-LINKAGE]`, `[TCG-VISIBILITY]`), which
  refuses almost every ordinary crate there until the x86-64 ELF writer spells
  them (OD-BRIDGE-TLS-IMPORT-LINKAGE-20261024,
  OD-BRIDGE-SYNTHESIZED-VISIBILITY-20261024,
  OD-BRIDGE-UNSPELLED-BINDING-20261024). Three required bridge rows red since
  the 2026-10-23 `ld -r` object publication read the published object, which
  now holds several items, per item again: `function_linkage` skips the
  partial link's `STT_FILE` rows and still requires every private definition
  `FUNC GLOBAL HIDDEN`; the TLS row accepts an accessor in the object that
  defines `X` while still requiring one `.tdata` definition reached only
  through TLS relocations; the unwind row finds each function's own FDE and
  LSDA in the concatenated `.gcc_except_table` instead of parsing the whole
  table as one LSDA (OD-BRIDGE-PUBLISHED-OBJECT-ROWS-20261024).

- Fixed (fail-closed): an attested soundness run no longer starts anything in
  its caller's working directory, which the host trust boundary does not judge
  (OD-XHOST-GATE-CWD-20261025, X-HOST-P13's sixth closure audit). Started in a
  `0777` directory holding a `0666` `json.py`, a full `--attest` run had passed
  the boundary, imported that module through the gate's own `python3 -c` and
  `python3 -` (and `gate_env.sh`'s `python3 -`), and written its record; the
  identities step also ran `lake --version` there, so a `lean-toolchain` in
  that directory chose the record's `toolchains.lake`. The run now works in
  `/` until the boundary has passed and in the judged candidate checkout from
  then on, as the landing train starts it, and every python3 the gate scripts
  and their Python tools start, inline or a script, runs with `-I`, which a
  static test holds them to. The gate also finds its own directory with
  `CDPATH= cd` (started as `scripts/soundness_check.sh --attest` with an
  exported CDPATH naming another user's directory, it had run that
  directory's `soundness_attestation.py` before the boundary and attested),
  refuses a directory that does not hold the script bash runs, and refuses a
  relative or empty PATH entry before its first program. The boundary now
  judges each directory a `.pth` file in python3's user site-packages names
  and refuses the startup code (`.pth` `import` lines, `sitecustomize`,
  `usercustomize`) a python3 run without `-I` would execute from there. The
  boundary's PASS line, the docs and LD-73 now claim only what the check
  judges, and the programs an ssh configuration names are stated out of its
  scope. Repair round 3 closes two older fail-opens: the boundary's own
  python3 was found by name after `gate_env.sh`'s prelude had put
  `$HOME/.elan/bin` first on PATH, so a python3 there (in a directory not
  yet judged) ran it; the gate now pins one python3 by its canonical path
  before the prelude (`SOUNDNESS_PYTHON3`), starts every python3 by it (the
  scrub, the boundary, every tool, and the helpers it starts), and the
  boundary judges exactly that file and refuses it unless it is the
  interpreter running the check. And an `--attest` run whose script bash
  read from standard input (`bash -s`) or a `-c` string had no
  `BASH_SOURCE`, so a `soundness_attestation.py` in the caller's directory
  ran before the boundary and the run attested; such a run, a sourced one,
  and one whose file is not the candidate's `scripts/soundness_check.sh` now
  refuse before any program. The boundary also refuses a user-site `.pth`
  holding a character `str.splitlines` breaks a line at besides `\n` and
  `\r` (CPython 3.13 reads its lines that way, 3.12 does not). Repair round
  4: the legs start python3 by name on the prelude's PATH, so the boundary
  now refuses the run unless that python3 is the pinned file with the same
  `pyvenv.cfg` around its name (a wrapper in `$HOME/.elan/bin` or a virtual
  environment's `bin/python3` first on PATH had been the legs' unjudged
  interpreter, and the run attested), refuses a pin that is a `#!` script or,
  on Linux, not the file `/proc/self/exe` names, and the scripts the run
  starts before the boundary are named by the gate's own directory, never by
  a caller's `TRUST_CG_DIR`.

- Fixed (fail-closed): the attested run's host trust boundary closes
  X-HOST-P13's round-4 pre-existing fail-opens over the git configuration it
  reads (OD-XHOST-GIT-PROGRAM-KEYS-20261024). The set of git keys that name a
  program git, a git helper or an extension runs is open (R1:
  `remote.origin.uploadpack = git web--browse -b <tool>` reached
  `browser.<tool>.cmd`; `diff.external` and the `difftool`/`mergetool` `.cmd`
  keys are the same shape), so instead of listing them the run's git now reads
  only judged configuration: every git the gate starts runs with
  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and, as its global file, one the boundary writes
  holding only the credential helpers, identity and `core.excludesFile` it
  judged from the user's configuration (read back with git, removed when the
  run exits), and the local and worktree configuration of every repository
  the run uses git in is judged against an allowlist of keys that name no
  program — any other key refuses by name. Those repositories include every
  repository nested in the work tree of one the run uses git in, whatever its
  layout: the first repair judged only submodule git directories below
  `<git-dir>/modules`, so a populated submodule with an embedded `.git` (or a
  `gitdir:` file naming a directory elsewhere) passed, and the gate's
  `git status` ran its `core.fsmonitor` and attested; that is closed. So is
  the same repository reached first as a local remote: each kind of
  judgement is now made once per repository and none stands in for another,
  so a populated submodule a remote also names still has git's view of its
  work tree judged (a `core.worktree` naming a `0777` directory, from which
  `git status` ran a program, had passed). A
  configured `remote.*.uploadpack`/`receivepack` refuses outright (R2: git
  passes a local remote's path to it, so `uploadpack = sh` ran a script the
  remote's url named), a local-path or `file://` remote is judged as a
  repository, as is a branch remote naming no configured remote, a legacy
  `remotes/`/`branches/` file refuses, and the preflight refuses to fetch an
  `origin` the source does not define. R3:
  `scripts/soundness_attestation.py`'s `exec-scrubbed` re-exec no longer runs
  `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` before the boundary (it drops a fixed,
  test-checked superset of git's repository-local variables), so no program
  runs before PATH is judged; `EDITOR`/`PAGER` and the like are dropped from
  the legs' environment, while the `allowlist-v1` verdict rules every
  existing record is verified by stay as they were (every local record
  verifies as it does with main's verifier). The FAIL summary names the
  `chmod go-w` remedy only for refusals of a path another user can write. The
  user's system and global files are still judged by the command, transport
  and path rules (Cargo's libgit2 reads them itself, so its default files are
  judged even when the caller's `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` names another), so a global key those
  rules refuse still refuses the run, as before; a Mac host's ordinary
  configuration (`osxkeychain`, a plain editor or pager, plain aliases)
  passes them. This host's `!/usr/bin/gh auth git-credential` helpers are
  carried and keep authenticating the pinned origins. Against `4a0668957` the
  boundary only refuses more. No attestation claim changes.

- Fixed: Linux peak-RSS sampling uses a small native wrapper to lower the
  inherited Python memory floor. Failed samples remain unmeasured, and the
  ledger requires an explicit eligible lineage when the RSS method changes.
  RSS gate thresholds and platform acceptance requirements are unchanged.

- Audit: original Linux AArch64 repeated-cell NaN inputs expose missing typed
  float byte-image coverage in the pinned Lean model. The historical
  seventeen-vector diagnostic lost its temporary raw evidence in the disclosed
  scratch incident. Fresh component qualification is retained separately;
  dependency adoption remains pending. No input is excluded and no proof or

- Fixed: Rust CPU/spec target-feature declarations now use the measured compiler
  catalog, preserving global flag/ABI checks and modern Wasm configuration.
  Configuration data remains a trusted dependency; no proof or platform
  acceptance claim is added.

- Fixed (fail-closed): the attested run's host trust boundary
  (`scripts/host_boundary.py`) closes the X-HOST-P13 round-5 verifier's three
  fail-opens and three lows, and the shapes its repair's verifiers then ran
  to an attestation (OD-XHOST-TRANSPORT-WORDS-20261024). It refuses any
  judged path whose resolution enters `/proc` or `/dev/fd` (the checker's own
  filesystem view, not git's child's); accepts only the program of
  `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`/`core.sshCommand`, refusing any later word (options
  belong in `~/.ssh/config`, which it judges); judges each source work tree
  (Clean, AY, aterm) as a whole tree and refuses a candidate, source or Cargo
  git database that git does not use as given (a `core.worktree` elsewhere,
  a subdirectory of a repository, no `.git` of its own, `core.bare`,
  `GIT_DIR`), and the gate refuses a pinned checkout whose work tree git
  reports elsewhere; reads every other git command key, `alias.*` included
  (a judged command can run git with an alias: `uploadpack = git x`), by
  the text of its words, refusing shell syntax, a first word the shell reads
  as reserved or that begins with `!` (git strips one `!` from an alias or a
  credential helper, so `!! <program>` refuses), a first-word assignment, a
  word naming git followed by a git option (`git -C <dir>`), and any later
  word that sets the environment, holds `..`, or holds a `/` or `~` without
  being exactly an absolute or `~/` path (judged, a directory as a tree), so
  `LESS=FRX less`, a bare `sed s/a/b/` filter and an alias such as
  `!git -C <dir> status` are now refused too; reads an alias without `!` as
  git's own arguments, refusing a first word that is a git option (`-c`,
  `--exec-path`, ...) and judging every word (`fetch --upload-pack=<path>`);
  skips only blanks after a `!`, not U+00A0; and judges `$SHELL`, `/bin/sh`
  and the passwd home's `.ssh`. This host's
  `!/usr/bin/gh auth git-credential` helper keeps passing. What a judged
  program makes of a plain argument by its own rules stays unjudged. No
  attestation claim changes; against `4a0668957` the boundary only refuses
  more (a differential over 13,096 git command-key values finds none it now
  passes that `4a0668957` refused), except that a configured path is judged
  as git reads it rather than whitespace-stripped.

- Fixed: the AArch64 memory-leaf checker (`source_bound_memory_leaf`) reads
  the byte-stride address `ArrayGep { elem_ty: I8 }`, the adapter's spelling
  of `base + offset` since `b79533c9c`, as the 64-bit sum of its operands.
  It had refused the opcode, so a load or store through `p + k` (the
  `load64_offset` and `chase` leaves) was withheld from the source-bound
  memory route at every level: fail-closed, no row was credited wrongly.
  Other element types and narrower operands stay refused by name, and a
  bound row is still credited only with every part Clean-checked
  (LD-101 in the decision record).

- Fixed (wrong code): the TrustIR adapter lowered a direct call of
  `memcpy`, `memmove` or `memset` as the bulk-memory operation by the
  callee's name alone, whatever its declaration (L02-P15's LD-74 re-check at
  `ff895a9be`; LD-100 in the decision record, not yet
  verified). A module declaring `i64 @memcpy(i64, i64, i64)` crashed where
  llc's build calls the function, and a `memset` declared returning its
  count returned the destination. A call is now the C library routine only
  when its callee is declared with C's prototype and convention for these
  LP64 targets; any other declaration is an ordinary call of the symbol, as
  llc builds it (the re-check's three reproducers and 15 of a 16-module
  prototype family run equal to llc in 24 of 24 configurations each; the
  `fastcc` one is refused by name, below).
  An LLVM intrinsic name the adapter reads (`llvm.mem*`, `llvm.bitreverse.*`,
  `llvm.objectsize.*`, `llvm.fma.*`/`llvm.fmuladd.*`) declared at another
  type is refused by name (`[TCG-NAMED-CALL-PROTOTYPE]`), and the LLVM
  importer refuses a `fastcc` declaration of the three routines, which it
  would read as C. The fsym scan reads the same decision, and AArch64
  SROA's memcpy fill rewrites only the `bl memcpy` instruction selection
  makes for a bulk-memory operation (`InstFlags::LIBRARY_ROUTINE_CALL`).
  The LLVM importer no longer signs one of the three from a call (the
  re-check at `f95ca7609`: an unprototyped `declare ptr @memcpy(...)` called
  with C's types was expanded where llc calls it, 0 of 24 equal): an
  unprototyped `(...)` header of a name the backend lowers by name, an
  unmodeled or missing header of the three, and a Mach-O `\01_` label naming
  one are refused by name (rule 8 of the ruling). A direct call whose
  stated function type, result or parameters, is not its callee's signature
  is refused by name, whatever the callee (rule 9; the re-check at
  `f37c48df9`: `call i64 @memcpy(ptr, ptr, i64 8)` against C's header, a
  call through a cast, was expanded where llc calls the symbol, 0 of 24
  equal; `double g(void)` called as `i64 ()`, its result passed to
  `printf`, printed another value, 0 of 24). A call the LLVM importer writes
  in place of an intrinsic is typed by the intrinsic, not by the module's
  header of the symbol it calls (rule 10; rule 9's verifier: beside
  `declare i64 @sin(double)`, `@llvm.sin.f64`, called as `sin`, read its
  result from `x0` where llc reads `d0`, 0 of 24 equal): a libm intrinsic
  beside another signature of its symbol, a libm intrinsic call at another
  type than its own, and on Darwin a `memset_patternN` declared otherwise
  beside a pattern fill are refused by name. AArch64 instruction selection
  refuses by name a direct call of a function named like a routine the
  backend calls on its own (`memcpy`, `fmod`, `__divti3`, ...) and declared
  with a hidden return buffer (rule 11; the fifth re-check at `848a8638d`:
  the selector keyed that fact by the symbol's name, so with `declare void
  @memcpy(ptr sret(%S), ptr, i64)` called once, its own `memcpy` call for an
  `@llvm.memcpy` in the same function passed the destination in `x8` and the
  import crashed where llc's build copies, 0 of 24 equal); and the LLVM
  importer gives a call's result the fresh-allocation facts of `malloc`,
  `calloc`, `aligned_alloc` or `reallocarray` only at C's prototype. The
  LLVM importer refuses by name a direct call of an `extern_weak` function
  declared with a hidden return buffer, or named like an LLVM intrinsic
  (rule 12; rule 11's verifier and the sixth re-check at `f8e524bc9`: the
  call, respelled through the function's address as trust-ir requires for
  a weak declaration, passed the buffer in `x0` instead of `x8` and shifted
  every argument, 0 of 24 equal, and a weak `@llvm.memcpy` called an
  undefined symbol so named, found by the repair's sweep).
- Changed: rustc-private clause-query adapters retain explicit supertraits and
  full usage-site constraints, including generic parents, binders and source spans.
- Tests: preserve all 216 map-provenance cells and add sixteen exported-helper
  witnesses, detecting removal of the type-erasure guard even when Linux's
  reference-storage guard refuses the caller first.

- Changed: the rustc-private function-item adapter preserves the original
  generic-argument binder and refuses resolution with escaping bound variables
  using `[TCG-FN-ITEM-BOUND-ARGS]`.

- LLVM importer, L02-P15's third closure audit (audit at `9a237122b`;
  LD-97 and LD-98 in
  the decision record, *Repaired* 2026-10-23, not yet verified). The
  keyword attribute `nobuiltin` and the string attributes `"no-builtins"`
  and `"no-builtin-<name>"` are refused by name wherever a function
  attribute is read: llc keeps the calls they mark, while the backend
  expands a constant-size `memcpy` or `memset` by its name, so a
  freestanding module's own `memcpy` was not called (0 of 24
  configurations equal to llc). Modules built with `-ffreestanding`,
  `-fno-builtin` or `#![no_builtins]` are now refused. An instruction that
  follows a terminator without a label (an implicitly numbered block) is
  refused by name, where the IR validator refused the merged block before.
  LD-16's premise that the importer calls exactly the functions the module
  calls is corrected: a plain constant-count `memcpy` or `memset` call may
  be expanded where llc 22.1.2 keeps it, a difference LLVM's LangRef
  allows.

- LLVM importer, L02-P13 third closure-audit repair (audit at `e0474f6ce`;
  LD-85; testing evidence, AArch64 Linux, no product
  change). The Linux floor target `symbol_linkage_elf` now pins the linkage
  and visibility of every global initializer shape: a host-neutral row
  states ten shapes (integer, floating-point, struct and pointer arrays, a

  pointer, a scalar) under every admitted definition linkage and visibility,
  as `global` and `constant` (520 definitions), through `import_text` and in

  hidden, protected, weak and ODR data of eight shapes into a `pic` shared
  object through GNU ld, gold and LLD at O0-O3 and checks `.dynsym`,
  `dlsym` and an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer against stated values, a gcc twin
  and llc. Before, only scalar globals were stated, and the audit's mutant
  S13 (every image global written with default visibility) passed every
  importer floor target; it now fails both rows. The floor's named-refusal
  row also pins the refusal of a hidden, protected or `extern_weak`
  declaration whose signature the importer does not model and of a
  non-private `.L` name, which only lib unit tests pinned. The Linux floor
  pins `symbol_linkage_elf` at 31 (was 29), the Darwin floor at 18 (was 17).
- LLVM importer, L02-P15's first closure audit (rulings
  LD-86, LD-87 and
  LD-88, *Repaired* 2026-10-16, not yet
  verified). Each of these was admitted and ran otherwise than llc 22's build
  at O1-O3:

    against llc's `strcpy`, 97);
  - `ldexp` under SVE (42 against an SVE `fscale`'s 12);
  - `exp10` on Darwin (llc calls `__exp10`);
  - a compiler-runtime helper such as `__udivti3` (42 against 33, since llc
    divides an `i128` by a constant inline).

  A definition, whatever its linkage and on every target, is now refused
  by name under any of these names:
  - the 18 fortified functions of LLVM 22's `TargetLibraryInfo.td`;
  - `ldexp`, `exp10` and their `f` and `l` forms;
  - the 602 runtime library calls LLVM 22's `RuntimeLibcalls.td` lists for
    AArch64 (`malloc`, `fmod`, `floor` and `pow` among them: stated
    over-refusals where llc's call reaches the definition as the import's

  A vector-typed intrinsic declaration and a vector reduction call are
  read only under the name LLVM gives their types: a declaration
  contradicting its name had been admitted beside a call llc rejects.

  The refusal tables are now checked against a committed `llvm-tblgen`
  extract (`scripts/extract_llvm_library_names.py`), so every single-entry

- x86-64 source-bound body lane (host qualification; evidence strength:
  AY proofs that Clean 5f09e36c accepts, on the x86_64 Darwin qualification
  host only): the qualification AY moves from AY build 12713 (`b1b0b9de0`)
  to AY main build 13556 (`ebde49de3`, with AY's resident-route and
  circuit-lane fixes), run from local overlays as before (ruling OD-190;
  `reports/perf/2026-10-19-darwin-x86-64-ay13556-requalification/`).
  Re-run one test per process on byte-identical queries, `u128::wrapping_sub`
  (build 12713's regression) certifies again in 3.6 s and leaves its gap;
  nothing else changes outcome and no gap joins; every wrong lowering stays
  refuted, each counterexample confirmed by z3. In a compile, the 32-bit
