- Historical Lean link-step result (2026-10-15; source-program and residency
  conclusions superseded by the later repairs above; X-LEAN-P7, X-LEAN-P6; evidence strength: kernel-checked theorems
  about the Lean model, no claim about the compiler or hardware): the four
  explicit axioms and the four `sorry` sites are gone, and the x86-64 capstone
  is proved vacuous. `Trust/Model/Machine.lean`, a dead second machine model,
  is deleted with its axioms `decode_encode` and `step_emitted`.
  `Trust/Model.lean` is now a link step that defines `srcStep` as
  `Source.SrcStep` and `x86Step` as fetch/decode/`execInstr`, so
  `srcStep_spec` and `x86Step_decode` are theorems; that the two definitions
  are faithful to trust-ir and to x86-64 hardware stays a modelling
  assumption (the 67-row golden matrix binds `encode` only). The new
  `Trust/MetaTheorem/Vacuity.lean` proves that the model machine is silent,
  `LoweredStep` and `CalleeContract` are uninhabited, the source relation is
  not indexed by a program, `Certified_compile P` is false for every `P`
  (so `compile_refines` constrains nothing), and no deterministic machine
  forward-refines the source semantics; the former `sorry` statements
  `opKind_event_eq`, `CalleeContract_of_IH` and `atomic_forward_sim` are
  refuted and `refines_machine_subset_of_determinism` holds only vacuously.
  `formal/lean/SOUNDNESS.md` states the missing lemmas. The soundness gate
  pins 0 `sorry` lines and 0 axioms (its axiom grep now also counts indented
  or modified declarations) and adds an environment audit,
  `formal/lean/scripts/AxiomAudit.lean`: no declaration may depend on
  `sorryAx` or a project axiom, and `compile_refines` only on `propext`,
  `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` (ruling OD-LEAN-LINK-STEP-20261015).
- x86-64 instruction selection (miscompile fix): the sign extension of a
  `bool` (LIR `Sextend { from_ty: B1, .. }`, trust-ir `SExt` of a `Bool`,
  LLVM's `sext i1`) made `true` +1 instead of all ones: the selector emitted
  `movsx` of the bool's 0/1 byte, and for `i128` widened the low half the
  same way, `(1, 0)`, while trust-ir widens `as_signed()` of the 1-bit value
  (-1). Every non-proof x86-64 compile reaching the cast (AOT and JIT, O0
  to O3; clang emits it for `-(long long)(a < b)` and `p - (_Bool)c`) was
  silently wrong; no Rust cast spells it, and the body theorem kept it out
  of its domain, so no proof credit was wrong. It is now `-zext(b)` (`movzx`
  of the low byte, or a parameter's 32-bit copy, then `neg`; an `i128`'s
  high half the `sar 63` of the low half), and `Sextend B1 -> I8`, which was
  refused, takes the same rows. AArch64 already selected `SBFM #0, #0` for
  32- and 64-bit results but copied the 0/1 value into an `i128`'s low half;
  it now selects the 64-bit `SBFM` there. A signed order of two bools, which
  trust-ir also reads with `true` as -1 and the adapter never emits, is
  refused by the x86-64 selector instead of computed on the 0/1 carriers,
  and the codegen golden-truth interpreter now returns -1 for `sext(true)`.
  The source-bound body theorem admits the cast with its exact meaning
  (OD-BODY-SEXT-BOOL-20261016). Native test `e2e_x86_64_sext_bool`;
  report.
- x86-64 instruction selection: `bool as u8` (LIR `Uextend { from_ty: B1,
  to_ty: I8 }`) is lowered instead of refused (`unsupported opcode for x86-64
  ISel`), which had failed `core::num::<impl u8>::carrying_add` (`carry as
  u8`) on the Darwin x86-64 `core` census. It zero-extends the bool's low
  byte exactly as `B1 -> I16/I32/I64` do (`movzx r32, r8`, or the 32-bit
  copy of a parameter its entry `movzx` already cleared); the sign extension
  into `I8` stays refused. The source-bound body theorem needed no change:
  the cast was already in its source domain and both rows in its machine
  domain; its new control refutes `true` extended to all ones and an
  extension of the wrong bit. The native test `e2e_x86_64_bool_to_byte`
  runs the cast of a parameter, of a compare and in `carrying_add` at O0-O3
  with bits 8..63 of every narrow argument register dirty.
- x86-64 proof lane, slice 17 of the source-bound body theorem: a private
  stack access at a non-constant offset (`T[i]`, `&mut buf[i]` passed to a
  call) is admitted (ruling OD-183). A load reads a select over the
  candidate offsets of the access (in the slot, aligned to the index's
  constant stride; the design's low-bit select, a balanced `ite` tree on
  the offset's bits), a store updates each byte a candidate covers by an
  `ite` chain, and a call argument is observed as the slot's address plus
  the offset, on both sides. Each side CLAIMS its own offset is a
  candidate (in-bounds is proved by AY, never assumed: trust-ir resolves
  `IntToPtr` provenance by address, so a premise could waive a defined
  run); the machine's offset is whatever its rows compute, never matched
  by shape. An `ArrayGep` of a private slot at a variable `I64` index
  (OD-185) is the same indexed address with the element size as stride.
  With it (OD-184), a private byte dead at a loop header or slice-16 cut
  point (overwritten before any read on every path) is left out of the
  cut's relation on both sides and starts unreadable. A theorem
  with an in-bounds claim is value-numbered as one slice-16 part after its
  bit-moving definitions are substituted; the select and this spelling
  were chosen by host qualification. Each of 15 rule mutants fails a
  control. On AY build 12713 with Clean every fixture certifies and 17
  wrong lowerings are refuted with counterexamples. Of the 51 `core`
  functions of the class, 43 build a theorem and 39 certify offline within
  the 30 s budget (`reports/perf/2026-10-15-darwin-x86-64-slice17-indexed/`).
- Custody, the X-HOST-P13 fifth closure audit's two blocking findings
  (rulings OD-XHOST-FETCH-TRANSPORT-20261016 and OD-XHOST-STRENGTH-NOTE-20261016). The
  attested run's host trust boundary now judges, in every run and not only
  with an x86-64 executor, `~/.ssh`, `/etc/ssh` and the program each of
  `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_SSH`, `GIT_PROXY_COMMAND`, `core.sshCommand` and
  `core.gitProxy` names, as git runs it: a program in a world-writable
  directory, or one named by a relative path into the Clean source's work
  tree, had run during the preflight's `git fetch origin` and the run had
  attested. A value it cannot judge (shell syntax, a leading assignment,
  whitespace in a program git runs without a shell, a relative path with a
  slash) is refused by name, as is a git configuration or
  `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` that can enable the `ext::` transport. A compile
  request demanding Formal strength, refused with `proof_strength_unavailable`,
  and the no-solver disclosure of an evidence summary now carry the AY
  refusal (code, directory, mode, remedy) of the proof-route resolution that
  decided them; they had named no cause.
- Custody, the X-HOST-P13 round-4 verifier's two fail-opens (LD-75,
  *Repaired* 2026-10-16). An attested run now refuses at its host trust
  boundary a `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `RUSTUP_HOME`, `ELAN_HOME`,
  `SOUNDNESS_DEPS_DIR` or `ATPKG_BIN` that is set and not an absolute path,
  naming the variable: a relative `SOUNDNESS_DEPS_DIR` started from a sticky
  directory, or a relative `CARGO_HOME` naming a world-writable directory,
  had passed where the absolute form was refused. It also refuses an empty
  `TMPDIR` (Rust's `std::env::temp_dir()` returns the empty path) and a
  program a git configuration key names by a relative path with a slash
  (git runs it from its unjudged working directory). The pinned Clean and AY
  checkouts' tree check now also refuses a POSIX ACL or default ACL that lets
  anyone but the gate's user or root write, before anything is built in them; a
  default ACL on an existing checkout had opened what the build created
  there until the check after the build. An ancestor refused only for its
  default ACL is no longer reported as one where another user can create
  `.cargo`.
- Custody, X-HOST-P13's last repair round (ruling LD-75: a verifier's four
  findings against the sixth closure audit's repair). The attested run's
  host trust boundary now judges the alternate
  object stores a judged git repository borrows objects from (a source
  cloned with `--shared` from a mirror every user could write had passed,
  and a substituted object reached the pinned checkout), refuses a
  directory whose default ACL would open what is created in it, runs every
  leg after the check under umask 077 (the trust-cg Cargo legs had kept the
  caller's umask) and refuses a `core.sharedRepository` that would set
  modes past it, and refuses a checkout, dependency directory, cache or
  Cargo home below a directory in which another user can create the
  `.cargo` Cargo reads: an attested run's checkout, given as an absolute
  path, can no longer live below `/tmp`. Relative roots and a default ACL
  inside an existing pinned checkout were left unjudged by this round (the
  entry above repairs both). The extra account files the tests use can no longer make a group
  count as private. The script suites' fixtures move to a per-user
  directory (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` on Linux) when the system temporary
  directory is `/tmp`.
- Custody, the X-HOST-P13 sixth closure audit (ruling LD-73, corrections to
  LD-70 and LD-66). The user's toolchain installs, git and its configuration
  and the candidate checkout are the host's trust boundary; an attested
  soundness run now judges them before it starts any other program
  (`scripts/host_boundary.py`) and refuses, naming each path and the remedy,
  any tool it executes or configuration it reads that another user can
  write: world-writable, group-writable by a group with another member,
  owned by another account, or open through a POSIX ACL. A lake renamed into
  a group-writable `~/.elan/bin` had turned a failing Lean build into an
  attested pass, and a substituted rustup ran as the gate's user. The export
  of the attested commit's own proofs is now read from the object store by
  hash, not by `git archive`, whose application of the global git
  configuration's filters had credited a substitute proof. The verifying
  x86-64 JIT's two module-gate refusals that name no single row now take
  their AY note from the rows, and tests pin both.
- Custody, the X-HOST-P13 fifth closure audit (rulings LD-70 to LD-72). An
  attested soundness run checks trust-cg's own proofs (`proofs/*.lean` and
  `formal/lean`) only in a private export of the attested commit, never in
  the candidate checkout, which no rule judges: a co-group writer of that
  checkout turned a failing proof into 132 of 132 and an attestation. The
  rest of the candidate checkout is still read in place. A symlink in a
  judged tree passes only when every hop of its literal target stays in the
  tree. The JIT IR-text cache publishes its seal key only whole, so
  concurrent first openers share one key (its concurrent-writers test had
  failed about one run in ten). The certificate routes' refusals are now
  tested to name the AY refusal of their request (except two refusals of
  the verifying x86-64 JIT's module gate, which the sixth audit found
  untested), and the Core route's machine-certificate refusal carries it too.
- Cache custody, the X-HOST-P13 fourth closure audit (rulings LD-65 to
  LD-68). The attested soundness gate judges its pinned checkouts as whole
  trees (`private_cache.py require-private-tree`): every directory and file
  must be this user's and writable by nobody else, before the checkout is
  used and again after the Clean build. Judging the root alone let a
  co-group writer rewrite a pinned proof that Clean rejects while the run
  was in progress, and the run recorded 132 of 132 and an attestation. A
  loose checkout is refused with the remedy to remove it. A proof-promotion
  refusal now carries the `TCG-AY-IDENTITY-*` refusal of the
  function-verification request its evidence came from (resolved once when
  the request was captured). It no longer resolves AY again: with the
  cache's symlink re-pointed in between, that second resolution left 4 of 20
  audited compiles refused without a note and claimed "no AY is admitted"
  in 3 others where AY ran.
  The opt-in JIT IR-text disk cache is used only from an owner-private
  canonical directory, and its entries carry an HMAC under a private seal
  key instead of an unkeyed SHA-256, so a planted entry misses instead of
  being compiled. The solver-identity memo is read only from a private
  canonical location; a memo another user could write is ignored.
- x86-64 proof lane, slice 16 of the source-bound body theorem: a function
  past the single-query bounds (more than 128 LIR blocks, 1024 LIR
  instructions, 128 machine blocks or 512 machine rows) is cut at its
  entry, its loop headers and planned block starts and clean mid-block
  stamp boundaries, and its one theorem is replayed in parts, one AY query
  and Clean check per region (ruling OD-182). At each cut, values and
  bytes fixed for the run are carried exactly and checked equal on every
  edge; every other live value and written private byte is a free input
  both sides share, stated equal on every edge into the cut. Rows are
  credited only when every part replays Valid; the part inventory is
  re-derived from the statement before any replay and any export, and the
  proof emitter publishes the parts. Every function within the bounds
  keeps its theorem byte for byte. Each part's definitions are
  value-numbered, after three exact bit-vector identities, so the
  machine's and the source's spellings of one computation become one name
  (a region whose claims all become identities is no part). Each of 11
  rule mutants fails a control. On AY build 12713 with Clean every control
  part and four of the five size shapes certify (the fifth's parts are
  recorded timeouts) and ten of eleven wrong lowerings are refuted with a
  counterexample (the eleventh is never credited). Of the 121 size-refused
  functions of main's `core` census, 106 are stated in parts and 86 have

- Gate scripts: a cache path that is checked is then used only by the

  handed on AY and Clean, through the cache path as given. With
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` a symlink in a `0777` directory, another user who
  re-pointed it after the check made 13 of the 14 clean-check legs run
  their program, and the attested run was green (132 of 132, record
  written); the icmp gate ran a planted AY and Clean the same way.
  `private_cache.py require-private` now prints the canonical path (refusing
  one that holds a newline), and checks a file by its name in the canonical
  directory; the soundness gate adds its checkouts below, uses and records
  only canonical paths; the icmp gate names its lock, slot, build and binary

  the executor's clone by its physical path (`cd -P`). AY admission
  (`ay_private_copy`) judges `<cache>` and `trust-cg` before creating
  anything in them, so it no longer creates `ay-exec` inside a pre-existing
  open or symlinked `trust-cg` before refusing. Behaviour on an ordinary
  private cache is unchanged. Tests: `test_private_cache` (canonical
  printing, the soundness and icmp symlink reproducers, the alias-named slot),
  `test_aarch64_aot_arithmetic` (the re-pointed copy, a copy below a `0777`
  directory), `test_soundness_remote` (the physical clone path), and
  `ay_identity::tests::private_copy::the_root_is_named_from_the_resolved_base_and_nothing_is_created_before_a_refusal`.
  Each new script case fails at `baf1a4dee`; the Rust case pins the order
  whose absence the audit observed there (an `ay-exec` created inside an
  open and inside a symlinked `trust-cg`).
- Linux link driver: the fifteenth L02-P10 closure audit's findings
  (2026-10-15, `b3070867f`).
  - **Partitions.** LLD 22.1.6 writes one file per LTO task where
    `--lto-obj-path` says, and under `--lto-partitions=<N>` it writes `<N>`
    empty files when it compiles nothing. The fourteenth audit's repair
    read only an empty `lto.o` alone as "nothing compiled". It therefore
    refused correct LLD links that load a fat object without
    `--fat-lto-objects` and pass `--lto-partitions=2` or more:
    `[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]`, with a reason that blamed a ThinLTO
    cache. Shared objects, static programs, static PIEs and the GOT-base
    PIE were refused this way, though `8cc4ab677` installed each and each
    ran correctly.
  - **Ruling.** Only empty files, one per task with none left out, now read
    as "LLD compiled nothing". These stay refused: an empty file beside a
    non-empty one (now with an accurate reason), a counted bitcode input
    with only empty files, and a task's file left out (new). LLD 22.1.6 was
    measured on 240 no-bitcode links under 1 to 4 partitions in every
    spelling, and on 60 links that compiled bitcode, whose files were all
    non-empty.
  - **Source naming.** An object compiled while a counted bitcode input
    and an uncounted fat object were both loaded is named after both. It
    was named after the counted input alone, though LLD compiled it from
    the fat object.
  - **Documentation.** LIMITATIONS now states that a `-Wl` request for an
    executable stack is refused for every link.
  - New `link_options` row
    `linux_got_page::lld_links_that_compile_nothing_are_installed_under_lto_partitions`
    and unit row `compiled_nothing_is_only_empty_files_one_per_task`; the
    floor minimum is now 71. Decision LD-69 (correction).
- Linux link driver: the fourteenth L02-P10 closure audit's finding
  (2026-10-15, `8cc4ab677`). Whether the driver read the code LLD compiled
  from a fat LTO object depended on LLD's map naming a file the input trace
  does not name. LLD names the object it compiles from a ThinLTO fat object
  `<input directory>/<output>.lto.<stem>.o`, which a user can predict.
  Through a C driver that adds `--fat-lto-objects`, with an input of that
  name in the link, the driver installed images over code it never read:
  a PIE and a shared object whose GOT-base load read another slot, and a
  static program that hung.
  - A link that loads an object holding bitcode, judged by its bytes and
    never by its name, now always runs again to keep what LLD compiled.
  - What LLD wrote must then be read in full, whatever the map names, or
    every check that needs it refuses the image
    (`[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]`).
  - An empty `lto.o` alone reads as "LLD compiled nothing": LLD 22.1.6
    wrote exactly that for each measured link that compiled no bitcode.
  - The decoy links (PIE, shared object, static program, archive member)
    are refused with their controls' tags. Ordinary fat-object links with a
    decoy are installed and run, through LLD with and without the option,
    GNU ld and gold.
  - New conservative refusal: an unmeasured LLD that loads a fat object.
    Each LLD link that loads a fat object is now linked twice.
  - New `link_options` row
    `linux_got_page::compiled_code_lld_wrote_is_read_whatever_the_inputs_are_named`;
    the floor minimum is now 70. Decision LD-69, with corrections to LD-58,
    LD-59 and LD-64.
- Linux link driver: the thirteenth L02-P10 closure audit's findings
  (2026-10-15, `baf1a4dee`).
  - **Code LLD compiles from LLVM bitcode.** The GOT-addressing and
    local-exec checks read the objects LLD compiles from bitcode only when
    the driver could read them all, and otherwise skipped them silently.
    Two dynamic links were installed and read thousands of wrong GOT slots
    through truncated `R_AARCH64_LD64_GOTPAGE_LO15` loads: a ThinLTO link
    with `--thinlto-cache-dir`, and one that named its own
    `--lto-obj-path`. Fat LTO objects linked with `--fat-lto-objects` were
    the same class.
  - The link the driver checks now puts its own `--lto-obj-path` and an
    empty `--thinlto-cache-dir=` after the user's options. A fat object's
    `.llvm.lto` bitcode counts as a bitcode input under
    `--fat-lto-objects`. The cache and `obj-path` routes and an AArch64 fat
    object named in the `-Wl` groups are read, and the reproducers are
    refused for the use in the compiled object.
  - The third verification of the repair found two fat-LTO routes still
    installed with wrong slots: a fat container that is not AArch64 LP64
    (LLD reads `.llvm.lto` in any ELF relocatable object), and a C driver
    that adds `--fat-lto-objects` itself.
    - Such a container now counts as bitcode whatever the `-Wl` groups say.
    - LLD's link map decides the rest. A file it places that the trace does
      not name is taken as an object LLD compiled: the link runs again to
      read it, and the image is refused by name when the map shows more such
      files than objects read (LD-64).
    - Both routes are refused for the use in the compiled object.
  - Ordinary links over those routes are installed and run.
  - Compiled code the driver has not shown read refuses every check that
    needs it, by name (`[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]`), in every link mode.
    That covers a counted input's unread objects, more map-placed untraced
    files than objects read, and an unread map beside a loaded AArch64 fat
    object.
  - New `link_options` row
    `linux_got_page::got_base_code_lld_compiles_from_bitcode_is_read_on_every_lto_route`.
    Decisions LD-58, LD-60 and LD-64; LD-07 corrected.
  - The floor target `link_options` failed 24 of 68. Its Linux fixtures
    were refused by WS7.3's `TargetInfoRequired` admission before any link
    ran. A module that needs a target now gets the host's in `write_module`,
    and `LTO_IR` its `target` line. Every assertion is kept, and the floor
    minimum is now 69 (LD-59).

- x86-64 hardening: a jump table on a 32-bit (`u32`/`i32`) selector
  zero-extends the selector into its 64-bit index (`mov r32, r32`) in the
  instruction-selection stream. The selector copied the selector's `Gpr32`
  vreg with a 64-bit `mov`, whose bits above 31 that stream does not
  define, so slice 14 of the source-bound body theorem refutes it (ruling
  OD-181). No miscompile was observed: natively the former form returned
  the right values for a `u32` argument with its register's high half set
  and for `match x as u32` on a `u64` with high bits set. A narrower
  selector was already zero-extended and a 64-bit one is unchanged. Tests
  `test_emit_x86_jump_table_zero_extends_a_32_bit_selector` and
  `tests/e2e_x86_64_jump_table_selector_width.rs` (both forms run
  natively, the current one asserted).
- x86-64 proof lane, slice 14 of the source-bound body theorem: definedness
  and dispatch. Division and remainder (`Udiv`, `Urem`, `Sdiv`, `Srem` of
  an `I8`..`I64`) are trust-ir's, their undefined behaviour (a zero
  divisor; the minimum by -1) a per-path premise that waives only the
  claims after an executed undefined division, and the machine's
  `div`/`idiv` #DE refuted wherever the source is defined (ruling OD-178).
  The divide-by-zero guard is an observable trap: the machine must trap at
  its carrier exactly where the guard fires (ruling OD-179). A `Switch`
  whose cases share a target is one edge of a disjunctive test, its
  machine routes disjoined (ruling OD-180); the selector's jump-table
  dispatch is stated from the function's own table, and the machine-table
  refusal is split by cause (ruling OD-181). Three exact spellings keep
  the theorems within AY's reach (a signed division's unit-divisor cases,
  power-of-two divisions and multiplies as shifts, a canonical machine
  division restated as the source's where the operands are equal). 26 of
  28 fixtures certify on AY build 12713 (the two divisions by other
  constants, through the magic-number multiply, are recorded gaps), 24
  wrong lowerings are refuted, each of 22 rule mutants fails a control,
  and the end-to-end compile promotes slice 14's functions. Of the 71
  Darwin `core` functions first refused in these classes, 44 build a
  theorem and 35 certify offline
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-09-darwin-x86-64-census-slice14/`).
- Composed transition records on AArch64 (L09-P3): each function prepared on
  a proof-grade route records one chain of checked transitions, legalization
  (TrustIR to LIR) and selection (LIR to raw MachIR) from the affine check,
  one link per optimizer pass or scheduler run that changed the function's
  interface (validated for the record by its dedicated validator or the
  generic region check; a CEGIS or extended-loop-rotation run that changes it
  has no validator and is an uncovered link, which refuses), the
  post-allocation value-flow comparison and a proof-grade, relocation-free
  encoding, each naming its relation, check, model and the SHA-256
  interfaces at both ends (`trust_cg_verify::composed_transition`). The
  record composes only when every required link is present and established
  and adjacent links share one interface; an accepted composition carries
  its claim and every link's strength. The sealed Core, the verifying JIT and
  `--emit-proofs` objects refuse a function the affine legalization check
  covers unless its record composes (checked right after preparation, before
  certificates are generated or promoted) and the bytes they publish are its
  terminal (the JIT's installed range before its certificate gate; the
  object's whole symbol extent with no relocation inside)
  (`CompileError::ComposedTransitionRefused`,
  `CompilationMetrics::composed_publications`); outside that domain the
  record says why no chain exists. Evidence strength per link: exactly
  decided over its own model by trusted Rust; the composition is no proof.
  Measured on the compile corpus at `2a42547f4`: 3 of 5,449 functions in
  the domain (101 of 6,085 at `a1a807fd0`, before trust-ir validation merged
  from `origin/main` refused the 98 `rustc_allocator_shim` modules holding 98
  of them), all composing
  at O0-O3 under the requirement, none refused, and every record-policy
  object carrying exactly their composed bytes (a census of records, not of
  the routes' own checks); the proof-grade lane +0.17% instructions retired
  (+1.57% at `a1a807fd0`), Identity PASS on all 534 entry/lane pairs. On
  this host no in-domain function passes proof promotion, so the routes'
  byte bindings are exercised by unit tests that waive promotion
  (test-only). New floor target `e2e_aarch64_composed_transition`
  (9) with corruption controls (dropped links, swapped interfaces,
  unvalidated rewrites, flipped published bytes, real AOT instrumentation
  refused by composition on both proof-required routes); unit tests drive
  unvalidated optimizer runs through a real preparation and both routes to
  their byte bindings (test-only hooks and promotion waiver);
  `compile_corpus --lane composed-census`.
- WS7.2 (F-111, `crit.misw10`): proof output names the adapter blind spot,
