- Post-allocation value flow on AArch64 (L10-P1): the function entering
  register allocation is compared with the final resolved stream through
  every post-allocation stage (spills, coalescing, rematerialization, reload
  CSE, late post-index formation, copy and frame lowering, stack probes, the
  stack protector, the ELF TLSDESC expansion and lo12 fusion, branch
  relaxation and resolution) under AAPCS64/DarwinPCS call clobbers, landing
  pads, the Darwin X18 reservation and callee-saved exit obligations.
  Proof-grade and certified routes refuse an unvalidated stage as
  `PassValidationFailed` (`post-ra-value-flow`); the default tier records it
  as uncovered. Evidence: per-compile translation validation under its
  model plus a bounded native differential, not a proof. All 13,702 compile
  corpus function compiles validated (split and composed, Identity PASS
  against main `1359b3bca`). Running it over the whole Darwin floor under
  the dedicated scope found model gaps (lo12 fusion, TLSDESC, late
  post-index pointers, a resolved self-loop) that are now modeled, one of
  them a soundness gap (a `#:lo12:sym` offset read as `#0`), and named
  LL/SC and dynamic-allocation refusals; no miscompile was found. Review
  found four acceptances the comparison now refuses: SP moved between a
  call's stack-argument stores and the call, and a spill slot moved
  consistently onto a live program stack slot (both shown to miscompile
  natively), a compare of two clobbered caller-saved registers decided
  "equal", and a spill cell below SP surviving a call. SP is now an argument
  of every call, frame-storage accesses must stay below the CFA and off
  program slots (a stack probe excepted), each clobbered register is its own
  unknown, and a call drops the cells below its SP. With them the whole
  Darwin floor under the dedicated scope validated 203,106 of 210,589
  comparisons, the rest the same named refusals and corrupted functions as
  before, and the compile corpus all 13,702 compiles. A second review found
  that frame-storage privacy left out the outgoing stack-argument area: a
  spill or inserted store over a stack argument between a call's
  stack-argument stores and the call (one shaped like a stack probe
  included) validated and miscompiled natively. Storage on that area is now
  refused, and a stack probe (inline or a summarized probe loop) may touch a
  program slot or the outgoing area only where it writes below every byte
  an earlier write on any path may have touched; the compile corpus still
  validates all 13,702 compiles (split and composed) with Identity PASS
  against the previous head, and with main `906b8a20a` merged the Darwin
  floor under the dedicated scope validated 203,343 of 211,047 comparisons,
  none refused for the outgoing area or a probe. The floor target
  `e2e_aarch64_post_ra_value_flow` (22 tests) refuses sixteen planted
  corruption classes, six also in the composed comparison, shows the
  outgoing-area corruptions miscompiling natively, and pins the refusal by
  name of an unmodeled function and the default tier's uncovered record. Cost in instructions retired over the same dedicated scope without
  it: +5% to +6% (AOT), +8% to +9% (JIT), up to 1.34x on one entry; default
  tier within noise (+6% on the bridge's proof-grade lane, which runs it). With main `7c60cee46` merged the whole
  Darwin floor under the dedicated scope validated 203,072 of 210,553
  comparisons; the
  rest are named LL/SC and dynamic-allocation refusals and correct refusals
  of deliberately corrupted or unsupported functions.
- On AArch64 macOS, exception tables now carry obligations, decided over the
  emitted bytes (ledger L03-P14). Every Mach-O object the module and
  single-function emitters write with exception tables, and every unchecked
  JIT image that publishes them (before it is mapped; not yet run on a Linux
  host), is emitted only after
  `trust_cg_verify::eh_obligations` re-parses it with Mach-O, LSDA,
  `__eh_frame`/CFA-program and A64 decoders of its own and decides, against
  the machine function's EH metadata and the frame owner's layout:
  - every call that can unwind lies in exactly one call-site record, read as
    the personalities read the table;
  - that record's landing pad is the IR's landing block for the invoke, or
    none for any other call;
  - every landing pad's action chain is the IR's clause list under the
    selector contract, typed slots GOT-relocated to the IR's typeinfo;
  - the compact entry, or the FDE and its CIE, names the function's
    personality and LSDA;
  - the compact encoding or FDE rows are the frame owner's frame, and at
    every call they recover the frame a data-flow over the decoded words
    computes (CFA, FP/LR and callee-saved slots, unsaved callee-saved
    registers unchanged; every store form at a known CFA offset, release,
    exclusive, atomic and SIMD structure stores included, applied to the
    slots it covers).
  A CIE marking signal frames (`S`) and a CIE or FDE pointer whose
  `DW_EH_PE_indirect` bit disagrees with its GOT relocation are refused.
  A violation fails emission by name (`[TCG-EH-OBLIGATION]`; the bridge's
  `[TCG-EH-UNWIND]`). Evidence strength: exact decisions made in process,
  testing grade, not a certificate. Under the evidence policy (OD-139) they
  are not promotion evidence, so certified promotion keeps refusing these
  objects (`[TCG-EH-UNPROVED]`, TB-12); the decision is recorded as
  OD-EH-OBLIGATIONS-TESTING-GRADE-20261012. Pinned on the Darwin RAII
  campaign (`e2e_aarch64_eh_raii_darwin`, now 12 rows): every object at
  O0-O3 holds with its exact report asserted (C++ 36 functions, 32 with EH,
  212 unwind points, 209 covered, none unreached; Rust 14, 12, 75, 74; JIT
  images 28/24/150 and 14/12/75), its unwind points equal to the test's own
  count of the call words; 34 object or IR-side corruptions (17 kinds at O0
  and O2) and 12 JIT image corruptions are each refused by the obligation
  they break. Unit tests cover a landing pad reached only by unwinding, a
  FRAMELESS description at a call, an unsaved D8 clobbered before a call
  and the frame record overwritten by each store form. The bridge's
  `unwind_cleanup_aarch64` compiles require the gate's report
  (`-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=eh-obligation-trace`, no unreached call) for the
  `panic=unwind` object its `catch_unwind` driver then runs. No emitted
  byte changes. Cost (debug build, Apple M4 Max, `/usr/bin/time -l` over
  the campaign's two object-pin rows, eight compiles, eight interleaved
  runs each, load average 6): instructions retired 14.15-14.25 G on main
  (median 14.17 G), 14.66-14.79 G with the gate (median 14.67 G, +3.5%);
  maximum resident set size 46.2-46.7 MB on main, 47.4-47.7 MB with the
  gate (about +1.3 MB in every run); peak memory footprint 8.47-9.03 MB on
  main and 8.44-8.75 MB with the gate in that run, while an earlier review
  run measured medians of 8.33 MB and 8.80 MB, so the footprint may rise by
  up to about 0.5 MB. AArch64 ELF, x86-64 and objects without exception
  tables are not gated.

- X-OPCODES-P13: the per-instruction `covered_elsewhere` certificate of an
  x86-64 `MovRI` is now `verified: true` only when the compile's ENC-3 decode
  check ran in `enforce` mode, and that of an AArch64 `AlignNop` only when the
  encoding pipeline's ENC-5 is enforced (proof grade, or the compatibility
  policy's default). Under `TCG_DECODE_CHECK=warn|off`,
  `TCG_DECODE_CHECK_A64=warn|off` on a compatibility route, or
  `TCG_NO_DECODE_CHECK=1`, the row is a `verified: false`
  `covered_elsewhere_withheld` certificate that names the check and blocks
  promotion. Before, both were positive whether or not their check ran.
  - The x86-64 verifying JIT bypasses its outer certificate cache unless
    ENC-3 is enforced, so a cached certificate is never served for unchecked
    bytes and an unchecked compile never populates the cache.
  - Audit: these are the only two covered-elsewhere opcodes whose credit
    cites a check a mode can switch off; the CALL/JMP/RET targets, `BLR`,
    `BR`, `CBZ`/`CBNZ`/`TBZ`/`TBNZ` and AArch64 `RET` are unchanged
    (pinned over every x86-64 and AArch64 opcode). The opcode-inventory
    certificate forwards no positive covered-elsewhere verdict, and the
    low-level `JitCompiler`'s own AArch64 certificate exists only at proof
    grade, where ENC-5 is forced to enforce.
  - Certificate text: under the default `enforce` mode the x86-64 `MovRI`
    row's `strength` now names ENC-3 ("constant materialization — the
    emitted MOV r,imm bytes passed ENC-3 ...") instead of the generic
    indirect-branch text. `proof_bundle_sha256` hashes `strength`, so the
    proof-bundle digest and the covered-elsewhere `.cert` text of every
    x86-64 compile with a `MovRI` row change, and a compile-artifact cache
    entry for such a module misses once. Emitted code is unchanged.
  - Evidence: unit tests (test rung, not proof). Through the real x86-64
    encode funnel, a test-only seam that forces ENC-3 to refute the `MovRI`
    shows the compile refused under enforce before any certificate exists,
    and the row withheld under warn and off. Through each production
    certificate lane (x86-64 AOT; x86-64 JIT, cached and uncached; AArch64
    JIT, verifying and emitting proofs under the `Unchecked` override;
    AArch64 AOT), a probe compile records, through a test-only hook, the
    decode-check mode every encode of the function ran and the backing the
    lane handed the certificate builder. The tests require the two to agree
    under the default, warn, off and `TCG_NO_DECODE_CHECK=1` environments,
    and the cited row to follow. Passing a fixed `Enforced` at the x86-64
    AOT, x86-64 JIT or AArch64 JIT lane fails them. The AArch64 AOT lane
    builds certificates only at proof grade, where the encode is enforced,
    so a fixed value there is equal by construction. An AArch64 JIT compile
    that the promotion gate refuses never reaches its encode, so it is
    checked against the policy alone.

- L13-P14: built for any target other than x86-64, `x86_sse_lane_gate` now
  carries its two SDM-vs-silicon tests as named `#[ignore]` stubs. A direct or
  full-matrix run on an arm64 host lists them as
  `ignored, x86-64 silicon differential NOT RUN ...`, and they fail under
  `--include-ignored`; before, they were compiled out and the target reported
  green with nothing compared against a CPU. `full_test_matrix_hosts.py`
  records them in `IGNORED_TESTS`.
  - No silicon evidence is added, and nothing is credited under Rosetta 2.
    OD-34 refused Rosetta as the anchor because it is translation, not
    silicon. The soundness gate's attest, portable and landing runs are
    unchanged: the release verdict still needs a native x86-64 record, and a
    landing names the ten SSE credits `NOT ANCHORED`. Its diagnostic
    `--self-test-cargo-gates` mode runs every dispatch argv on any host, with
    `--include-ignored` for this target, so on a host that is not x86-64 it
    now reports `x86_sse_lane_gate` FAIL where it used to pass with nothing
    compared.
  - Measured on the arm64 Mac (Apple M4 Max, macOS 26.6.2): Rosetta 2 is not
    installed (`arch -x86_64 /usr/bin/true` reports `Bad CPU type in
    executable`), and the Trust sysroot has no `x86_64-apple-darwin` std
    (E0463). Installing Rosetta is an owner decision and was not done.

- Proof-required AArch64 JIT coverage and the installed-artifact boundary
  (ledger `L11-P11`, `L11-P2`; Darwin, this host).
  - Installed-artifact replay (`L11-P2`): a verifying publication
    (`AlwaysVerify`, `CachedVerified`) re-reads its sealed, cache-walked
    MAP_JIT mapping before any function pointer exists. Every installed word
    of a certified range must equal the word of the publisher's image buffer
    whose digest that function's certificate records (on the publisher's own
    path both hashes come from one buffer, so the digest check only ties the
    baseline to the certificate and cannot fail there); every `BRANCH26` site
    is decoded by the verifier's independent A64 field decoder and must reach
    the entry or veneer its relocation names at the mapped address; each
    reached veneer must decode as `LDR X16, <+8>; BR X16` with the resolved
    address in its literal; any other relocation in a certified range is
    refused. A disagreement is `JitError::InstalledArtifactReplayRejected`,
    and the proof-required compiler route refuses a buffer whose
    `ExecutableBuffer::installed_replay` record does not cover every
    function. Evidence strength: a byte- and relocation-level check, not a
    re-proof of the certificate. Crate unit tests tamper the sealed mapping
    after the walk (a flipped byte, a branch re-encoded to a valid wrong
    target, a moved veneer literal) and each is refused by name; a mutant
    replaying the heap copy instead of the mapping fails 3 of the 4 native
    rows. Native floor target `jit_installed_artifact_replay` (3), which
    checks faithful replays only: the refusal controls need the publisher's
    test-only tamper hook and run in the `trust-cg-codegen` library suite,
    which the Darwin floor does not run.
  - The frameless whole-body theorem (`L09-P6` owner) now credits the live
    register copies and wide-move constants of the returned value's slice
    under OD-35's route C; an identity or constant-only body, dead rows and
    dead O0 constants stay refused, and a tool-free unit control places dead
    `MOVZ`/`MOVK`, `MOV` and `MovR` rows beside a live copy and a live
    constant and requires only the live ones credited. Evidence strength:
    formal per row (AY proof of the whole-body theorem fully verified by
    Clean; the Rust translators stay trusted). With the overlay AY
    `2657db47c`/Clean `ed21fee39` pair the whole-body qualification publishes
    67 of 88 compiles on the JIT and AOT routes (55 before), 50 of 53
    theorems certified and 305 of 305 corruptions refuted.
  - Census (`L11-P11`, testing evidence): the opt-in
    `jit_proof_coverage_census` (`TCG_JIT_PROOF_CENSUS=1`) sends 398 compiles
    of the repository's JIT corpora through the proof-required route. With
    the overlay pair 260 published before and 273 after; with Trust package
    9192's tools 21 before and 21 after. Calling frames, division and
    remainder rows, memory-leaf return copies, dead O0 constants and void
    beat-llvm shims stay refused by name
    (record).

- Scalar FP conversions, rounding and arithmetic against an independent IEEE 754
  reference (L04-P3). `trust-cg-verify` gains `ieee754_reference`, an
  integer-only binary16/32/64 reference: exact values plus one rounding
  routine, with the Arm default-FPCR NaN, tininess and flag rules, sharing no
  code with `fp_bitmodel`, `aarch64_fcvt_half` or the SMT evaluator, and pinned
  by known-answer vectors. `tests/aarch64_fp_ieee_differential.rs` (Darwin and
  Linux floors, minimum 10) runs the 72 emitted scalar FP forms: FADD, FSUB,
  FMUL, FDIV, FMADD, FMINNM, FMAXNM, FNEG, FABS, FSQRT and FRINTM/P/Z/N at
  H/S/D; FCVTZS/FCVTZU and SCVTF/UCVTF at every H/S/D x W/X pairing; and the six
  FCVTs. Each encoder word is decoded by ENC-5 first, and 15 assembler-only forms
  run alongside. Every form runs on this CPU against the reference (value,
  untouched registers, zeroed upper bits, FPSR flags) and against the
  verifier's machine-side model. `trust-cg-codegen/tests/e2e_aarch64_fp_ieee_lowering.rs`
  (minimum 5) runs 121 TrustIR functions against the reference on the
  proof-grade AOT route at O0-O3 (every FP value word ENC-5-matched and found in
  the object, then `dlopen`) and the JIT at O1/O2. The functions cover
  saturating and raw float-to-int at 8/16/32/64 bits, int-to-float,
  FPExt/FPTrunc and their round trips, floor/ceil/trunc/frintn, FAdd-FMax,
  FNeg/FAbs/FSqrt and `llvm.fma`. The release run recorded under
  `crates/trust-cg-verify/tests/fixtures/fp_ieee_exhaustive/` (revision
  `82e983a09`, after merging `main` `1359b3bca`; one Apple M4 Max) found no
  disagreement and repeats the counts of the first run at `99b754813` exactly.
  It is exhaustive over every binary16 operand, every binary32 operand, every
  32-bit integer and every binary16 pair: 128,850,067,456 of its
  130,677,880,598 instruction comparisons, plus 330,388,523,524 lowering
  calls. The lowerings run those 2^32 sets in full on AOT O2 and JIT O1; the
  other four routes run the binary16 and 8/16-bit sets in full and the first
  50,000 values of each larger set. 1,888 s and 774 s wall on 10 threads at
  load average 14-69. Binary64 sources, 64-bit integers, wider pairs and FMADD
  triples are statistical. The coverage gate names this in the
  24 scalar FP rows' notes, as a pure note append that moves no row (180/302
  accepted when it landed), FRINTN RED, FDIV/FSQRT formal obligations
  refused. No mismatch was found in the lowering or the models. Two QF_FP single-NaN boundaries of the
  FMINNM/FMAXNM model (signaling operand, opposite zeros) are counted and
  pinned. Evidence strength: testing on one host, exhaustive where stated,
  statistical otherwise; no proof; the Linux arms have not run.
- AArch64 opcode rows (L04-P1, X-OPCODES-P1, X-OPCODES-P2): the opcode
  evidence inventory moves from 180/302 accepted (122 RED) to 267/302
  (35 RED).
  - Atomics (Formal for the form): the 46 single-instruction atomic opcodes
    (LDAR/STLR, CAS, SWP, LD<op> at every ordering) get 48 form theorems
    (`aarch64_atomic_forms`: returned old value and memory effect per
    operation and width) with a committed DRAT certificate each in a new set
    (`verdict_db/atomic_memory_certs/`, own manifest; Trust 9192 AY build
    9624) that the vendored `drat-trim` replays before credit, and a
    word-bound decomposition per instruction (`aarch64_atomic_effect`: fields
    incl. A/R ordering bits, returned value, memory window) decided exactly
    in process (testing grade) and bound to the emitted word by ENC-5.
  - Scalar memory: the word-bound memory-effect decomposition covers every
    scalar form (H/S/D/Q via a new verify-side scalar encoder, LDRSB/LDRSH,
    pre/post-index, register offset); for H/S/D/Q rows it is the Formal-only
    rule's clause-2 check, so the walk credits them by their certificates.
  - NEON LD1/ST1 post-index (Formal for the form): 14 form theorems
    (`aarch64_neon_structure_forms`, LD1/ST1 x seven arrangements: the
    element loop against the operands' LDR/STR Dt|Qt intent, every byte and
    the writeback) with certificates in a fourth set
    (`verdict_db/neon_memory_certs/`; AY build 9624, 14/14 in 34 s).
  - CRC32/CRC32C (testing grade): decoded-word obligations
    (`aarch64_crc32_proofs`: Arm `Poly32Mod2` pseudocode of the decoded word
    against the reflected shift register of the intrinsic) decided exactly
    for every register value by a new GF(2)-affine procedure
    (`gf2_affine_decide`); 368 controls refute. The decision showed
    CRC32W/CRC32CW are symmetric in their two registers.
  - SUBS #imm (testing grade): destination and N, Z, C, V of the decoded
    word (`aarch64_subs_imm_proofs`, Arm `AddWithCarry`) against the
    operands' comparison, each decided by the bit-serial automaton; 96
    controls refute.
  - The coverage gate credits a memory, atomic or NEON row only when every
    legal form carries a replayed certificate, representative instructions
    credited through clauses 2-4 and every machine defect refuted
    (`bound_memory_row_credit`); the CRC32 and SUBS rows only through their
    families' credit hooks, as regression evidence, NOT a formal proof (the
    walk reports those instructions unverified). ENC-5 binds every new
    family's emitted word to the verified word.
  - Five new Darwin floor targets compare the models with this Apple M4
    (also on the Linux floor, not yet run there):
    `aarch64_atomic_silicon_differential` (312 words, 124,800 executions),
    `aarch64_scalar_memory_silicon_differential` (364 words, 8,976),
    `aarch64_neon_structure_silicon_differential` (14 words, 896),
    `aarch64_crc32_silicon_differential` (56 words, 30,464) and
    `aarch64_subs_imm_silicon_differential` (50 words, 13,000, NZCV read with
    MRS); native testing on one host.
  - Still RED (35): the 29 LL/SC rows (no exclusive-monitor model), FRINTN,
    the two TLSLE TPREL adds and the three TLSDESC slots. The atomic and NEON
    sets authorize only this host's checker, so those rows are not credited
    on Linux yet; ordering stays the L03-P3 mapping table's (conformance, not
    a memory-model proof).

- On AArch64 macOS, the validity intrinsics `assert_zero_valid`,
  `assert_mem_uninitialized_valid` and `assert_inhabited` now lower as they
  do on AArch64 Linux. rustc emits them at O0 inside `mem::zeroed`,
  `MaybeUninit::assume_init` and `mem::uninitialized`. The bridge answers
  rustc's own `check_validity_requirement` query, including its strict-init
  policy. A valid instantiation continues. An invalid one calls rustc's
  `panic_nounwind` with rustc's message, so the panic hook runs and the
  process aborts without running cleanups.
  - Before, `assert_zero_valid` and `assert_mem_uninitialized_valid` were
    refused here as unsupported intrinsics.
  - Before, a fallback admitted `assert_inhabited` for an inhabited type and
    refused it at compile time over an uninhabited one. The uninhabited case
    now aborts at run time, as LLVM's binary does.
  - Nothing in the lane depends on the OS; it was qualified on Linux only.
  - New target `intrinsic_validity_aarch64`, required by the Darwin bridge
    runner, compares against LLVM at O0-O3, under both panic strategies and
    both strict-init policies: 64 executions.
    - The Linux fixture runs unchanged. rustc's InstSimplify folds its valid
      asserts on concrete types, so its valid branch reaches the bridge only
      through `core::mem::zeroed` at O0/O1.
    - A new `generic` fixture puts all three intrinsics behind
      `#[inline(never)]` generic wrappers, which nothing can fold. Valid and
      invalid instantiations therefore reach the bridge at every level. Its
      driver requires SIGABRT and rustc's exact message for each invalid case.
    - Main `9287332be` refuses both fixtures: 5 and 12 roots at O0.
  - Self-host census (package 9192, certificates off, O0, `panic=abort`):
    `library/std` goes from 125 failed roots to 114. The eleven removed are
    every `mem::zeroed::<T>` instance in `std` (`libc::stat`, `dirent`,
    `sockaddr_in`/`in6`/`un`, `addrinfo`, `sigaction`, `stack_t`,
    `attrlist`, `pollfd` arrays and `u32`). No root is new.

- On AArch64 macOS, dropping a `Box<[T]>` whose element needs drop
  (`Box<[String]>`, `Box<[Box<str>]>`, `Box<[Vec<T>]>`, a user `Drop` type) now
  compiles. Its drop glue reads the box's `{data, len}` and then runs
  `drop((*_6))` of the `[T]`. That terminator had no lane: the field arm
  refuses a fat pointee and the general arm takes only an unprojected local.
  - A new `[TCG-DROP-GLUE-SLICE]` arm hands the pair to rustc's own
    `drop_glue::<[T]>`, the symbol LLVM calls. It recovers the pair whole and
    refuses otherwise. It checks that the glue's FnAbi takes the pointer as one
    `Pair` argument, and refuses a self-recursive glue. Under
    `panic=unwind` it is an invoke to the glue's cleanup block, which still
    frees the box.
  - This is the first use of the lanes the deref-led `Box<DST>` transmute
    loads. `deref_field_wide_image_store_aarch64` now requires two more
    subjects to match LLVM at O0-O3 under its size-checking allocator. The
    `strings` subject records each element drop: 33 drops, payload sum 1617
    for 33 elements. The `bombs` subject is built with `panic=unwind`, and an
    element's `Drop` panics at each position in turn. The remaining elements
    still drop, the box is freed, and the panic is caught. Main `4b3105700`
    refuses both at the element drop.
  - Self-host census (package 9192, certificates off, O0, `panic=abort`):
    `library/std` goes from 131 failed roots to 125. The six removed are
    `drop_glue::<Box<[T]>>` for `String`, `Option<..>` and four addr2line
    element types. No root is new. `library/alloc` stays at 0 roots with no
    traced hidden failure at O0/O2 under both panic strategies, and
    `library/core` at 0 roots.

- On AArch64 macOS, a fat-pointer-leaf value (`Box<[u8]>`, `Box<str>`,
  `NonNull<[T]>`, `Rc<[T]>`, `Arc<str>`, `Box<dyn Fn>`, a struct or tuple
  holding one) stored whole through a field of a pointer (`t.inner = b` with
  `t: &mut W`) now compiles. So does the drop glue of a `Box<[T]>` /
  `Box<str>` whose element needs no drop. Both were refused before, so a
  program that dropped a `Box<[u8]>` through its glue was refused on this
  target.
  - The store, `((*p).f…: T) = v`, is the write twin of the existing deref
    read. It copies the source's whole rustc image lane by lane
    (`store_operand_into_memory_at`). A constant source takes the const-image
    store. A scalarized source, or a `repr(packed)` container, keeps its
    refusal.
  - The drop glue's first statement,
    `_6 = copy (((*_1).0: Unique<[T]>).0: NonNull<[T]>) as *const [T]
    (Transmute)`, is the `Box<DST>` deref idiom through a pointer to the box.
    It now loads both lanes through that pointer into a `{data, len}` slot, with
    the same identity checks as the existing arm for a box held in a local.
    Only that shim produces this shape. In every glue it admits today, `_6` is
    read only by `drop((*_6))`, a no-op for an element without drop glue, and
    the free re-reads the box. So the loaded lanes are not yet observed by any
    test.
  - Effect on the self-host census (package 9192, certificates off): with
    the unsized-parameter change below, `library/alloc` has 0 failed roots at
    O0 (915 objects) and O2 (363) under `panic=abort`, and at O0 (921) and O2
    (378) under `panic=unwind`. Statement tracing (`trace-ty`) reports no
    hidden failure in any of the four. `<CStr as ToOwned>::clone_into` and the
    `drop_glue::<Box<[u8]>>` it calls, which the census did not count, both
    lower. `library/core` stays at 0 roots at O0. Its 6 traced hidden failures,
    fn-pointer shims passing projected tuple fields, are unchanged from main.
  - New target `deref_field_wide_image_store_aarch64`, required by the Darwin
    bridge runner, compares against LLVM at O0-O3. Each driver that runs
    bridge code uses a size-checking allocator, which turns a field store
    that drops or corrupts a length lane into a wrong dealloc size and exit 3.
    - The root-2 store and drop shapes match at every level. Before, 7
      functions were refused at O0 and 9 at O2.
    - Seven other fat-leaf kinds stored through a field match at every level.
      Before, the stores of `NonNull<[u8]>`, `Rc<[u8]>`/`Arc<str>`,
      `Box<dyn Fn>`, `(Box<[u8]>, u32)` and a multi-field struct holding a
      box were refused. The `&[u16]` and `Option<Box<[u8]>>` stores already
      had lanes. The crate failed anyway, because `Option<Box<[u8]>>` and the
      tuple need the box's drop glue.
    - A packed container stays refused. The drop of a `Box<[String]>` stays
      refused at its element drop and nowhere else. That is the row where the
      transmute's lanes first become observable.
  - Dropping a `Box<[T]>` whose element needs drop was still open here; the
    entry above closes it.

- Unsized by-value slice and `str` parameters (`fn f(s: [T])`, enabled by
  `unsized_fn_params`) now compile on AArch64 macOS. Before, they compiled
  only on AArch64 Linux, and every Darwin function with such a parameter, or
  calling one, was refused with `Ty::[T]` / `Ty::str`. The parameter keeps
  rustc's Rust-ABI indirect pair (data pointer, length), and the body reads and
  writes the caller's storage through a `&mut [T]` view, as on Linux.
  - Other Apple OSes share the calling convention but have not been run, so
    they stay refused (`unsized_arguments::plan`). A payload with drop glue
    (`[String]`) is still refused, as everywhere.
  - Effect on the self-host censuses (package 9192, certificates off):
    `library/alloc` goes from 2 failed roots to 1 at O0 and O2.
    `<[&str] as SpecExtendStr>::spec_extend_into` now lowers; the remaining
    root is `<CStr as ToOwned>::clone_into`. `library/core` stays at 0 roots
    at O0 (3449 objects).
  - New target `unsized_arguments_aarch64`, required by the Darwin bridge
    runner, compares against LLVM at O0-O3:
    - the Linux corpus, unchanged: 8 executions, 912,384 checks;
    - `[&str]` rows under both panic strategies: 16 executions, 359,424
      checks. They cover a mirror of alloc's by-value `self`, the data/length
      pair split across x7 and the stack, and the pair behind narrow scalars
      that macOS packs on the stack where Linux gives each an eight-byte slot;
    - drop-glue refusal controls.
  - The bridge before this change (main `901ccc517`) refuses every function
    with an unsized parameter in the two fixtures: 12 roots (`strs.rs`) and
    25 (`corpus.rs`), at both O0 and O2.
  - Still open on this target: a runtime-index READ of a wide element through
    the view (`s[i]` with `s: [&str]`) is refused by the slice-element lane.
- trust-cg-opt: `vectorize` checks what each planned instruction reads
  before it publishes an in-place rewrite (`clause_gap`,
  `planned_input_gap`), closing the class of planned inputs that register
  work the plan leaves scalar changes; the 2026-10-11 checks below refused
  single shapes of it. On MachIR, interpreted, `27aeaa0df` published:
  `x48 = movz #0` between the `acc64` bridge's load and its reducer, kept
  once per vector iteration (`acc64` = 0x8800000000000000 where the scalar
  loop leaves 0x0400000000000000); a `movz` of the `rbit` result between it
  and its bridge, laid out ahead of the body (the bridge drained the `rbit`
  lanes where the scalar loop subtracts 0); a compare idiom of the
  induction ahead of its lanes; and lane reads of values the rewrite builds
  no lanes for (a header copy, a constant set in the loop, a loop
  invariant, the previous iteration's value), where the rewrite read a SIMD
  register nothing writes. A publication is now refused when an in-loop
  definition the plan does not make can reach a planned read
  (`UnplannedDefinition`), or when a read the rewrite gives lanes, other
  than of the induction, does not see on every path a value its iteration
  computes by a planned lane producer (`UncomputedLaneInput`); the lane
  check counts compare idioms among the induction's readers. A plain (no
  induction) plan builds no lanes to start from and is no longer published:
  the one test fixture that published one
  (`test_plain_plan_with_a_run_time_counter_start_declines`) read `x95`
  through lanes nothing builds. Four unit rows in `vectorize.rs`, each red
  at `27aeaa0df` and again with its check reverted. Every plan,
  `clause_gap` verdict, rewrite and publication logged across
  `trust-cg-opt --all-targets`, two `trust-cg-llvm-import` programs and 37
  `trust-cg-codegen` targets is the same before and after, but for that
  fixture's plain plan.
- trust-cg-opt: `vectorize` refuses in-place rewrites it published with a
  wrong value at `23ed4a3e0`, all on MachIR, interpreted (a unit row of each
  kind in `vectorize.rs`, red there). Register work the plan leaves scalar
  runs once per vector iteration, and the coverage clause decides the
  iteration count only. (1) A copy in the latch that moved an ordered-sub
  bridge's address to another slot: both lanes of an iteration accumulated
  into the slot the first lane saw, because the recognizer read only the
  address's last definition in layout. It now refuses an address with any
  definition in the loop. (2) A second definition of the induction's alias or
  sign extension, or of the copy the sign extension reads: the vectorized
  `rbit` read the lanes where the scalar loop read 5. The recognizer now
  refuses each. (3) Lanes built at the first reader the plan lists did not
  reach a reader in an earlier block or one ahead of the first direct reader
  of the induction (the first iteration read an undefined register), and lanes
  built after the latch's write-back held the induction advanced by `vf` where
  the scalar loop reads it advanced by one; the rewrite now declines unless
  every reader, and every copy the lanes stand for, is in the lanes' block, in
  order, before the step. Every plan, `clause_gap` verdict and publication
  logged across `trust-cg-opt --all-targets`, two `trust-cg-llvm-import`
  programs and 37 `trust-cg-codegen` targets is the same before and after.
- trust-cg-opt: the loop-state contract's iteration-coverage clause
  (`loop_contract/coverage.rs`) refuses three more kinds of wrong rewrite,
  each admitted at `4a03eab40` (a unit row of each in
  `loop_contract/coverage/tests.rs`, red there). (1) An exit or trap of the
  new code on a value the model does not compute was taken as not taken
  wherever the scalar loop had such an exit to the same block, or any such
  trap: a new `rbit(iv) != 0` exit to the block a loaded `break` leaves to
  ran 4 iterations for 64. It now stands only for the scalar loop's own
  instruction, one for one: the same instruction in the same loop block,
  or in a block the rewrite names as its copy (`Lanes::copies`, which
  `loop_unroll`'s bounded-early-exit tier fills with its clones), leaving
  to the same block, where that block has as many instructions of its text
  as the scalar block (until 2026-10-11 a new exit of the text of the
  scalar loop's own was still taken as it: that `rbit` exit in flag form,
  `cmp; b.ne early`, ran 4 iterations for 64); and a trap whose test the
  model does not compute is never taken as not taken in the rewritten code
  when the run knows every operand it names, which are in the trip slice
  (until 2026-10-11 they were not, so a carrier on a modeled copy of the
  induction was undecided data, and admitted). An input only such operands
  make does not count toward the inputs sampled pair by pair: the others
  take the combinations they take without it, each run with every
  combination of such inputs over six pivots, the combinations of all the
  inputs counted together run as well, and past 12,000 crossed
  combinations the clause refuses (when they were first sampled, on
  2026-10-11, such an input moved two others to the sparse selection and a
  bound one too large only at n = 3, m = 5 was admitted). The pass's
  premise is that
  a tied exit's undecided value is the scalar exit's, so that it fires in
  the iteration the scalar one would; the clause checks the tie, not that
  value. (2) A kept
  scalar loop was compared by its trip effects, so swapping a load for
  `rbit` or deleting a store passed as unchanged; it is now compared
  instruction for instruction. (3) An unmodeled preheader result was one
  sampled input for both functions even when the rewrite computed it
  another way (the bound loaded from another address: 6 iterations for 64);
  the rewritten run now takes it only when its preheader agrees with the
  scalar one up to that result, else as unknown. New rows also pin the
  overflow carriers' polarity and width, the preheader's undecided-exit
  refusal and a kept block's fall-through. MEASURED at `d1b67e206`
  (aarch64-apple-darwin, `targo --unverified`, no proof claim): no in-tree
  rewrite changed its verdict (791 coverage verdicts outside the clause's
  own rows over the suites LIMITATIONS.md names, identical to
  `4a03eab40`'s, reasons included); LIMITATIONS.md and
  OD-LOOP-COVERAGE-20261008 are corrected, including the stale "790
  verdicts ... 35 binaries". MEASURED again at `fbdb55042` against
  `23ed4a3e0` for the 2026-10-11 rules: 804 coverage verdicts outside the
  clause's own rows over the same suites, identical, reasons included.
  MEASURED again against `27aeaa0df` for the carrier-only inputs: 805
  verdicts, identical, reasons and input counts included.

- Fixed wrong values at -O2 and -O3 on AArch64 on the exception path: a
  landing pad read a register that its invoke block wrote only after the
  invoke's call. When an invoke's normal destination is a loop header, LICM
  hoisted loop-invariant code into the invoke block behind the call, and at
  -O3 CSE or GVN replaced the pad's own equal constant with it, because the
  invoke block dominates the pad. When the landing pad is itself a loop
  header (a catch-and-retry loop), the invoke block is that loop's
  preheader, and the loop read LICM's hoisted constant directly at -O2 and
  -O3. An exception leaves at the call, so the pad used what the register
  held when the callee threw (`out=7` instead of 40000), with no refusal.
  CSE and GVN now treat a call that an exception can leave through as a
  mid-block exit, as they treat a switch cascade's branches, and LICM does
  not hoist into an invoke block; that LICM refusal alone closes the
  catch-and-retry loop (OD-EH-PAD-VALUES-20261010).
  `tests/e2e_aarch64_eh_invoke_trust_ir.rs` runs nine reproducers at O0-O3
  against a source model: 36 cells match, where the base diverged in 9
  cells (5 at -O3, and the retry loop's 4 at -O2 and -O3) and refused 3
  ([TCG-A64-SPILL-SLOT]).

- By-address cloning (`byaddr`, OD-166) on wasm32: the pass and its
  checker admit an `insertfield` only into the callee's own slot or over an
  operand typed as an aggregate value they name (struct, tuple, array,
  record, enum). Until 2026-10-10 both admitted one over any type but a
  thin pointer, including the `i64`/`u64` the wasm32 lane writes the field
  through, so a callee that wrote the caller's bytes through such a carrier
  and then read its slot was cloned, and the clone read the new bytes (no
  bridge corpus here is known to emit such a carrier on wasm32). The pass
  also reads a callee by the checker's prologue and typing now, so it no
  longer proposes clones the checker rolls back: an array the plan does not
  promote read ahead of the promoted array's lane copies, an `insertfield`
  over a `select` or `undef` value, and a `select` of pointers passed as
  the argument. Nor does it propose, for the checker to roll back, a clone
  of a callee whose kept thin-pointer parameter is entered as another
  pointer type than declared (`ptr` and `*mut u8`).

- When a panic under `panic=unwind` reaches a Rust-defined `extern "C"` fn,
  the bridge's behaviour is now ruled and tested
  (OD-NOUNWIND-CALLEE-EDGE-20261011). It runs that fn's cleanups and then
  aborts with "panic in a function that cannot unwind", as MIR states.
  LLVM's binary does the same unless its search meets a gap first. The gap
  can be in the caller's call-site table, or in a frame above it when LLVM
  infers `nounwind` for the caller; there it aborts before any cleanup runs.
  - Keeping the bridge's full-coverage `panic=unwind` tables is deliberate. A
    table that reproduced LLVM's gaps would still diverge in both directions
    without LLVM's inlining, `nounwind` inference and range merging. One wrong
    `nounwind` entry would also turn a caught panic into an abort.
  - `terminate_panic_differential_aarch64` gains a third test,
    `extern_c_callee_panics_run_mir_cleanups_aarch64`: 38 rows over 25
    unwind-built caller frames at O0-O3. Among them, a `qsort` comparator
    with a live `Drop` unwinds through libc's frame, and four controls panic
    from a region with no landing pad and must be caught. The evidence is in
    `reports/2026-10-11-extern-c-callee-cleanups`.
  - The ruling corrects the open entry pushed in 242d67d7d, whose mechanism
    and witness were wrong.

  MEASURED 2026-10-11 on aarch64-apple-darwin (`targo --unverified`, package
  9192, certificates off): of 152 cells, 127 match LLVM exactly.
  - 63 reach the Abi termination, 51 of them after the callee's cleanups.
  - 56 catch the panic.
  - 8 return.

  In the other 25, LLVM's search fails, and the bridge prints LLVM's output,
  then exactly the callee's cleanup trace, then the Abi hook.

- Some panics the Rust bridge raises for calls it lowers itself now carry
  std's own payload and Location, and run the panic hook, as in LLVM's binary
  (OD-170). These are an intercepted std call's failure edge, a formatted
  panic in a compiled body, a diverging std `#[track_caller]` helper and the
  `-Cdebug-assertions` precondition checks.
  - Before, they raised a synthesized message at the intercepted call's
    Location. Under `panic=unwind`, a nounwind or terminate edge trapped
    without running the hook.
  - The bridge now calls the entry that std's optimized MIR reaches for the
    failure. A route it cannot derive is refused by name as
    `[TCG-STD-PANIC-ROUTE]`.
  - On a target without the Rust terminate filter (x86-64), a panic on a
    `Terminate` edge keeps the trap, so it no longer unwinds through a frame
    that must abort.
  - Two review rounds of the port found nine defects, and eight are fixed
    (OD-170). Among them were a refused `&v[..]` at O0/O1, x86-64
    terminate-edge unwinding, a refused wasm32 `position` and two stale pins.

  MEASURED 2026-10-11 on aarch64-apple-darwin (`targo --unverified`, package
  9192, certificates off):
  - `std_panic_payload_differential` matches LLVM on 1680 of 1680 rows (3
    fixtures, O0–O3 x abort/unwind, every hook).
  - The stride family's synthesized-message count drops from 4 to 0, and the
    feature suites' `panics_unwind` family from 16 panic-message cells to 0
    (60 of 60 runs match).
  - The full Darwin bridge gate fails only the 15 targets main fails on this
    host, with the same 65 failed tests: 8 whose x86-64 rows have no
    execution route (no Rosetta), and 7 certificates-on targets that ruling
    OD-02 keeps red at `[TCG-PROOF-465]` / `[TCG-EH-UNPROVED]`.

  Still open: x86-64 ordinary calls on a `Terminate` edge (LIMITATIONS). The
  x86-64 and wasm32 rules were not executed.

- Under `panic=abort`, a frame the Rust bridge compiles now aborts no later
  than LLVM's when an unwind reaches it (OD-58). Four changes do this:
  - The frame's exception table covers the libm and compiler-rt calls LLVM
    keeps as calls.
  - A `fn` pointer, vtable or `Box<dyn Fn>` call whose target the MIR states
    is lowered as the direct call LLVM makes.
  - The frame inherits the terminate pads of callees LLVM may inline into it.
  - Thread-local resolver calls are treated as `nounwind`.

  Two review rounds found eight defects in the lane commit, and all are fixed.
  Three would have called the wrong callee: an argument counted as defined
  once, `&raw const` hiding a write, and `Pin<&S>` taken for a pointer. Each
  fix is pinned by one of 12 new differential rows, and each row was run
  against the code before its fix and failed.

  Where trust-cg cannot see LLVM's folding (for example a runtime `sin` whose
  result is unused, or an `i128` division LLVM keeps as a call), it aborts
  earlier than LLVM. OD-58 accepts that.

  MEASURED 2026-10-10 on aarch64-apple-darwin (`targo --unverified`, package
  9192, certificates off): `terminate_panic_differential_aarch64` pins 68
  region rows (8 cells, 544 native runs) against LLVM at O0–O3. The full
  Darwin bridge gate fails only the 15 targets main fails on this host.

- The family matrix (`tests/signature_placement_families_xback.rs`) now
  tests the forms `main` measured wrong for two of its three
  known-open-wrong-code rows. `tait_field` ran at O2 and O3 only, where each
  crate compiled its own copy of the closure body, and passed against
  `main`'s pre-merge bridge `65e816a73`, which has the wrong code. It is now
  an `#[inline(never)]` `FnOnce` closure with a `Pair` environment in a field
  typed by the `type_alias_impl_trait` alias, whose body the caller links at
  O0-O3; the row checks that import itself (`crosses`: `nm -u` of the
  LLVM-compiled caller object must list `callee::mkw::{closure#0}`), and its
  `min_level` knob is gone. `inline_never_parent`, wrong on `main` only with
  the library and the binary at different levels, also runs every pair of two
  different levels on AArch64 (`mixed_levels`, 12 pairs). MEASURED 2026-10-10
  on aarch64-apple-darwin (`targo --unverified`, no proof claim):
  `signature_placement_families_agree_aarch64` passes, 62 rows, 241
  one-level row-levels and 12 mixed pairs, 1012 cells, every one agreeing
  with LLVM. Against `65e816a73` (`SIGFAM_DYLIB`) the two rows report 42
  failures, among them `tait_field`'s bridge-library x LLVM-binary cell
  (SIGSEGV) at O0-O3 and `inline_never_parent`'s at library O0 with binary O2
  and O3 (exit 121 and 157, LLVM 85). Without `#[inline(never)]` the
  `crosses` check fails `tait_field` at O1-O3. The x86-64 lane was not run;
  it runs no mixed-level cell.

- An AArch64 leaf whose unread parameter has another width than its body,
  such as the SAT BCP status probe `fn(*mut Ctx) -> i32 { 0 }`, is now judged
  by the source-bound frame owner, so OD-35's MOVZ constant credit reaches it.
  Before, the owner's source domain refused every such signature as a
  "mixed-width function", silently, and the probe's `movz w0, #0` had no credit
  route: `ay_sat_bcp_install_gate` had been red since E0.2. A parameter no
  instruction reads keeps its own register width, so it can never reach the
  result; reading the other-width parameter stays outside the domain
  (OD-A64-UNREAD-PARAMETER-WIDTH-20261010). Such leaves now keep the FP/LR
  envelope on ELF and in proof-grade Darwin compiles, like every leaf the
  owner admits. The gate's calibration compile now carries the manifest's
  proof policy, so it binds the proof-grade bytes.

- The source-bound negative memo's "another AY" control passes on macOS. Its
  second fixture's private copy was a new executable whose first start the host
  assesses (0.1-0.2 s of wall clock with next to no CPU time), so the first
  replay looked starved and was correctly not recorded. Fixture AYs, which
  production never starts on its own, now have their copy started once when
  made. The memo's rules are unchanged.

- `raw_captured_saved_pair_query_changes_only_its_logic_header` follows
  OD-134's canonical-conjunction migration, which re-pinned every other exact
  query: the legacy right-spine reconstruction still reproduces both retained
  digests, and the canonical query is pinned separately, with the same
  prelude, `and` count and leaf order.

- `u64::reverse_bits`, and a `SetDiscriminant` of a niche-encoded enum at
  -O1..-O3, compile again. trust-ir's typed admission takes a signed integer
  constant only in its own range, and bridge producers wrote some patterns as
  their unsigned value (the `0xAAAA_..` masks of `reverse_bits`, a 32-bit
  niche), so the whole module was refused ("const type mismatch: expected
  i32, got int"). `typed_integer_constant` (and so `emit_i64_const` and
  `emit_typed_const`) and a final pass over every module
  (`canonicalize_signed_constant_spellings`, for the raw `Constant::Int`
  sites) spell an `I8`..`I64` pattern held as its unsigned value as the type's
  signed value with the same bits. A value outside both ranges is still
  refused. The feature-suite census and pins
  are re-measured: 22 cells now refuse first with [TCG-RET-ABI] (the call
  preflight), `m103_nested_collect_x86`'s `t0_vec_tuple` builds and matches,
  and `rb_u64` matches again.

- `Vec::resize_with`, `retain`, `retain_mut` and `dedup_by` keep the
  bridge's models for a closure that calls a captured closure returning a
  pair or a two-field struct. Such a closure had been sent to std's own body
  since the closure Pair ABI change, and std's `resize_with` reaches
  `extend_trusted`, which the bridge refuses by name: with
  `mk = |x| (x, x * 9)`, `t.resize_with(5, || { k += 1; let (a, b) = mk(k);
  a + b })` was refused at -O0..-O3. The models now decide by the closure's
  own output (and std's own adapter closures), since they call the closure's
  body, which calls `mk` itself. The iterator drives, and the other std
  calls on a `Vec` that no model runs the closure of (`pop_if`, `extract_if`,
  `Option`/`Result::map_or[_else]` producing a `Vec`), keep std's bodies for
  such closures, as do model calls whose arm would refuse the closure
  (passed as `&mut f` or `&f`) or the element (`u128`, `Option<u64>`).
  `tests/bridge_regressions_aarch64.rs`
  (`captured_pair_closures_keep_the_vec_models_matching_llvm`): 232 cells,
  224 match LLVM and the 8 cells of a closure whose own output is the pair
  are refused by name.
- A provenance-free raw-pointer constant (`NonNull::dangling()`, the
  `vec::IntoIter` end pointer, `usize::MAX as *const u8`, a newtype over
  one) is spelled as TrustIR's `IntToPtr` of its address instead of an
  integer constant the source floor refuses, so an empty `Vec` iterated by
  value builds again at -O2/-O3. A pointer with provenance keeps its
  relocation; `[TCG-NULL-RAW-CONST]` is now `[TCG-RAW-ADDR-CONST]`.
- Fixed a wrong value at -O2/-O3 on AArch64: a switch case constant read
  where it was never written. The switch cascade (and a binary-search
  switch's leaves) compares case by case in one block, materializing a case
  value that `CMP`'s 12-bit immediate cannot hold just before its own
  compare, after the earlier `B.EQ` exits. GVN and CSE treat a value defined
  in a block as available in every block it dominates, so each merged that
  constant into an equal one in the switch's join block. On the paths that
  left early, the join read a register that was never written: after a
  `match` on a `#[repr(u16)]` enum, a later `as u16` of its `65535` variant
  read 7 at -O2. Case registers are now materialized before the first exit,
  and GVN and CSE keep a value defined after a mid-block conditional exit to
  the rest of its own block. `tests/switch_join_constant_aarch64.rs` (a
  required Darwin bridge target): 40 cells match LLVM.
- `Vec::extend` from an iterator chain leaves std's capacity. The bridge
  pushed each element, so the Vec grew 4, 8, 16, ...; std's `SpecExtend`
  reserves a `TrustedLen` chain's exact count before pulling anything
  (`extend_trusted`), and any other exact chain's final length when an
  element meets a full Vec (`extend_desugared`). Thirteen elements from
  `a.iter().copied()` into `Vec::new()` now leave capacity 13, not 16.
  Chains whose lower bound is zero (`filter`, `take_while`) still grow a
  push at a time, as std's do. `collect` and `extend` share the `TrustedLen`
  classification (`chain_is_trusted_len`). `tests/vec_extend_capacity_aarch64.rs`
  (a required Darwin bridge target): -O0/-O1 match LLVM in every cell.
- `Vec::extend` over an exact chain whose final length passes `usize::MAX`
  raises std's capacity overflow. The reservation above added `len + n`
  with a wrapping add, so such a sum asked for a length the Vec already
  held and the drive pushed on (50 elements, capacity 64, until the test's
  payload panicked), where std's `reserve` raises before pulling anything
  (`extend_trusted`) or at the first full Vec (`extend_desugared`), with the
  destination untouched. The sum now saturates.
  `tests/vec_compact_user_trait_differential_aarch64.rs` pins both routes
  (4 -O0/-O1 cells that diverged, now matching LLVM).
- `Vec::extend` from a bare integer `Range` whose length std's `reserve`
  cannot hold raises capacity overflow. The bridge extends such a source with
  a count-up fill, not the chain drive above, and took its count as a signed
  `end - start` clamped at zero, so a span of `2^63` or more read as empty:
  `w.extend(i64::MIN..i64::MAX)` appended nothing and returned, where std
  panics (`alloc/src/raw_vec/mod.rs:28:5`, an abort under `panic=abort`).
  The count is now the span in the range's own type (`emit_range_span`) and
  the final length saturates. A `Range<i128>` / `Range<u128>` source now
  refuses in lowering (it reached object emission with an invalid `I128` to
  `I64` cast). `tests/vec_compact_user_trait_differential_aarch64.rs` pins
  two rows under both strategies (8 -O0/-O1 cells that diverged, now
  matching LLVM).
- `Vec::extend` from a bare `Range<u64>` or `Range<usize>` compiles, and so
  does a bare `Range` with constant endpoints at -O1. The fill moved each
  `I64` value to the element type with a `Trunc`, which object emission
  refuses for an element of the same width (`[TCG-IR-LOWER]`,
  `CastOp::Trunc ... src_ty=I64 dst_ty=U64`); a 64-bit element now takes a
  `Bitcast`. mir-opt at -O1 folds `v.extend(3..8)` into one `const Range`
  operand, which lowering refused for every integer type (`Vec::extend range
  source is not a place operand`); its endpoints are now read from the
  constant. `tests/vec_extend_capacity_aarch64.rs` (`range_widths`,
  `const_ranges`: the ten integer types, empty, inverted, at the type's
  bounds and across its middle) and two `u64` / `usize` capacity-overflow
  rows of `tests/vec_compact_user_trait_differential_aarch64.rs` pin it: 16
  -O0/-O1 cells that were refused now match LLVM.
- A bridge drive over `a.chain(b)` drives only a half whose `Option` is
  `Some`. core's `Chain` bodies set a half they exhaust to `None` (`next`
  clears `a`, `next_back` clears `b`, `nth` an `a` it runs past), and the
  drive, and the reservation of an `extend` or `collect`, read that half's
  payload as a cursor anyway: for `slice::Iter` the null `ptr` niche (SIGSEGV
  in `sum`, `fold`, `for_each`, `collect` and `extend` after such a call), for
  a `Range` whatever bytes the `None` write left (an `extend` pushed 209
  garbage elements where LLVM's pushed one; a `sum` returned
  50728486112550923 for 11 at -O1). `tests/bridge_regressions_aarch64.rs`
  (`chain_with_a_cleared_half_matches_llvm`: 7 of its 16 cells diverged) and
  `tests/vec_extend_capacity_aarch64.rs` (`cleared_halves`: its 4 -O0/-O1
  cells were killed) pin it.
- A String built by `format!`, `write!` or an integer's `to_string()` has
  std's capacity. The bridge sized each one to a static worst case up front,
  so `format!("{}", 5)` had capacity 12, not 8, and `format!("")` allocated a
  byte. `format!` now starts at `Arguments::estimated_capacity()` (a literal's
  length for a template with no placeholder), and every write reserves exactly
  its own bytes by the amortized rule, a negative integer's `'-'` separately,
  so the allocator also sees std's calls. Integer `to_string()` follows std's
  `SpecToString` (`with_capacity` of the type's widest value for a signed
  type, the exact digits for an unsigned one). The `bool` and `char` writers,
  which relied on the worst-case slack, now store only the bytes they
  reserve. `tests/format_capacity_aarch64.rs`
  (a required Darwin bridge target): 40 cells, including std's exact
  allocator call sequence and exact-fit Strings under a canary allocator, all
  match LLVM.
- The Rust bridge's in-place `Vec::retain`/`retain_mut`, `dedup_by` and
  `resize_with` models admit a consumed closure by the same check as every
  other intercepted std call: a closure whose skipped drop glue only frees
  `Global`-allocator memory, with no `#[global_allocator]` linked, builds and
  matches LLVM; every other closure with drop glue refuses as
  `[TCG-CLOSURE-DROP]`. The models' separate `[TCG-VEC-CLOSURE-DROP]`, which
  refused every closure with drop glue, is removed.
- The Rust bridge plans the complete closure/Fn-trait argument transport before
  emitting loads or copies, using the same original FnAbi ordinals and carrier
  plans as the declaration. Original MIR `Unreachable` edges use shared trap
  lowering instead of fabricating return values. Provenance-free thin raw-pointer
  constants require their actual Rust type and compiler-owned target layout.
- The Darwin bridge gate refuses all ambient `SIGFAM_*` matrix/backend overrides;
  signature-family fixtures refuse zero selected work before claiming evidence.
- The shared source floor consumes canonical constant-type and Rust reference
  producer findings from the existing validation report. Malformed nested and
  global constants refuse before carrier lowering on native and WASM paths.
  The Rust bridge now spells its entry function as the exact registered
  function item and sign-extends fixed-I8 image/sigpipe bytes without changing
  their bits, layout or ABI.
- The x86-64 vector-compare certificate gate reads trust-ir's rule as code
  and re-runs it with both tools built by revision (round 9b step G). The
  query dump (`examples/x86_icmp_certificate_queries.rs`, schema v2) writes
  `trust_ir::CHC_X86_ICMP_CERTIFICATE_RULE` and each cell's ground
  (`chc_x86_vector_icmp_cell_ground`) from the compiled trust-ir;
  `scripts/check_x86_icmp_certificates.py` parses no prose, re-derives no
  ground, builds the rule's AY and the rule's Clean by revision under the
  rule's Clean's `heavy_gate.sh run 12`, takes Clean's exit status as the
  verdict, refuses an unchecked `hole`/`lia_generic` step, and reports whether
  each binary is one of the rule's certifying builds. A dump supplied with
  `--queries` is re-run but never passes (exit 4, `SUPPLIED-DUMP`): its rule
  and grounds are not the compiled trust-ir's. A cold build past its bound,
  or one the gate is interrupted during, is stopped with its whole process
  tree, so none builds on outside the admission. The installed Clean
  0.9.0 package is no longer consulted: trust-ir measured it false-accepting
  31 of Clean's own 46 refutations of satisfiable problems and a truncated
  `pbblast` sum in a real `v16_i8` certificate. The unsigned compares' sign-bit
  bias is spelled per lane again (AY fixed the node cap the two-halves
  respelling worked around), and the 16 unsigned pins return to the per-lane
  bytes. Measured: PASS, 32 certificate cells (each `unsat`,
  `unproved_steps=0`, Clean exit 0 and fully verified), 8 instruction-model
  cells degenerate, 0 fail-closed, both binaries certifying builds; the three
  certificate mutants N1-N3 refused
  (`reports/2026-10-09-x86-icmp-certificate-rule-as-code.md`).
- The x86-64 vector-compare cells' spec side is trust-ir's bit-vector
  statement of `ICmp` (`trust_ir::chc_x86_vector_icmp_spec`), printed node for
  node by the new `trust_cg_verify::trust_ir_bv::SmtAlgebra`; this backend's
  copy is deleted, and the packed compare-mask reconstruction's source side
  uses the same statement. `trust_cg_lower::instructions::intcc_of_icmp` is
  the one `ICmpOp -> IntCC` map (the adapter and two verifiers call it). New
  tests hold every cell's spec to trust-ir's statement, every cell's machine
  side to the instruction models trust-ir publishes for it, and the x86
  instruction models independent of the statement; each is red on its
  measured mutant. The sixteen `ne`/`slt`/`sle`/`sge` digests did not move.
- trust-ir pin moved to `5c4f9e1d` (Clean `1ad47bdd`, AY `630842a8`
  unchanged) with `bump_trust_ir_pin.py`, carrying what the consolidated
  trust-ir landing demands of a consumer: the fsym UB map gains the two
  Lean-provenance sites (an ARC operand off its cell's object base, in
  `is_unique` and `arc_allocation_mut`); the AArch64 affine evaluator
  range-checks a constant at the module's pointer width
  (`Constant::value_matches_ty(ty, pointer_bits)`); and the shared admission
  refuses the corpus rows `rust_reference_as_permission_borrow` (a
  `Producer::TRust` function driving the borrow-permission machine) and
  `const_usize_beyond_target_width` (an `isize`/`usize` constant outside a
  narrower target's pointer width, which a 32-bit lowering would wrap) with
  trust-ir's own errors. The four pin guards and both must-refuse corpus
  targets are green.
- trust-cg-opt: the loop-state contract's ITERATION-COVERAGE clause. A rewrite
  that runs new code instead of scalar loop iterations is a refinement only if
  the new code and the scalar remainder together run exactly the iterations
  the scalar loop runs. WHY: the control and register clauses read the loop
  before the rewrite and cannot see what the new code computes. `vectorize`
  passed both and still divided its own induction's trip bound (16 of 64
  lanes, fixed privately in `4b1fb93c7`), left remainder lanes in blocks
  nothing branched to, and ran an undivided bound past an odd trip count, a
  nonzero start, an inclusive test and a run-time bound (`a0603f3bc`), each
  closed by a check of its own. `loop_contract/coverage.rs` states the rule
  once over both machine IRs: it runs the TRIP SLICE (every register a branch
  or trap condition depends on; memory is unknown) of the scalar and the
  rewritten function from the loop's preheader over sampled inputs, counts
  each entry into a block the rewrite names as the iterations it claims, and
  requires the counts, the exit and the reproduced registers to agree before
  the rewrite is published (`publish_covered`, `candidate::commit_covered`).
  `vectorize`'s in-place rewrite, `neon_fill` and `loop_unroll`'s
  bounded-early-exit tier publish through it; `vectorize`'s private coverage
  checks and its unreachable scalar epilogue are deleted. Every rewrite that
  still admits through the first two clauses only is listed in
  `loop_contract/coverage_routes.txt`, which a unit test recounts. A deletion
  rule (`DeadWork::check`: nothing kept reads what a deleted instruction
  wrote, flags included, on any path) replaces `loop_unroll`'s private
  dead-trip-test scans in its copy-counted, bounded-early-exit and diamond
  tiers and its address fold; the diamond tier's scan missed an exit that
  read the dropped compare's flags (a unit fixture of each diamond variant,
  red before the rule). Review before landing added a cycle rule: the
  clause merges runs that reach a block in the same state, so a rewrite that
  could cycle without passing a counted block left no run to compare and was
  admitted (a unit row, red before: the clause returned `Ok` for a rewrite
  whose only run spins); such a region is now refused undecided. MEASURED,
  `targo --unverified` (no proof claim): `trust-cg-opt --lib` 4458 passed,
  0 failed. With the clause's verdict ignored (a mutant), 34 unit tests fail,
  among them the row in which the clause alone refuses each measured
  `vectorize` miscover: with the private checks deleted the rewrite still
  builds those loops wrong (32 of 64 iterations when it also divides the
  bound), and the clause reports the counts. Whole programs
  (`opt_loop_state_run`'s two new rows,
  `tests/support/loop_coverage_program.rs`): 19 kernels in 9 loop forms
  (`<`, `<=`, `!=`, stride 2, counting down, bottom-tested, `for` over a
  range, `i32` and `u32` inductions) over 4 run-time starts and 36 run-time
  bounds, plus 10 kernels with a const-generic start and bound, 24859 rows;
  on aarch64 natively and on x86-64 under Rosetta, at O2 and O3, every row
  equals LLVM's both on `main` (`b4da4cb65`) and with this change, and every
  one of the 181 kernel functions keeps the vector-instruction count it has
  on `main`. `main` already printed every row right, so the whole-program
  rows show that the routed passes stay right and keep their vector code;
  that the clause is what refuses the miscover class is unit-rung evidence.
  The program hides its arrays from the optimizer behind
  their pointers: passing a `[T; 1040]` through `black_box` by value, as the
  first version did, made one kernel a 42418-instruction function (the bridge
  copies a by-value array one element at a time) and the program an 8 GB
  aarch64 bridge compile still unfinished after 34 minutes on a loaded host;
  through pointers it compiles in under a minute there. *Correction
  (2026-10-10):* not every private check could go, and the clause alone does
  not refuse every `vectorize` miscover. Beside it, `vectorize` refuses
  (`clause_gap`) a header that runs work besides its exit test, an instruction
  of the loop its plan does not account for that does more than compute
  registers (a memory access, call, trap or conditional branch other than the
  header's exit test), and a plan, induction or plain, whose trip is not fixed
  at compile time, which now includes a trip counter defined in the loop
  anywhere but by its step in the latch or a copy of the step's result after
  it; the address fold again requires every operand naming the address to be a
  load or store it re-points in that iteration, and a base the unrolled loop
  does not define. Each was wrong without its check: work on the exiting
  header entry, an `argc`-keyed trip and a store of the induction in the loop
  natively at O2 (the store printed `last=16777214` for 16777215); a start
  entering through a header copy of the step's result, a plain plan's run-time
  start (its profitability forced), a load ahead of the `Madd` of a carried
  address and a base bumped
  between the `Madd` and its load on MachIR. A row of each is in
  `vectorize.rs`, `loop_unroll.rs` and `trust-cg-llvm-import`'s
  `bitreverse_intrinsics.rs` (see OD-LOOP-COVERAGE-20261008's corrections).
- trust-cg-opt: `x86_dce`'s per-def local tier decides every candidate in
  one indexed sweep instead of scanning forward from each (quadratic in a
  long straight-line block). Measured when it was written (bridge, x86-64
  O2 under Rosetta): ten kernels of the first coverage program 143 s -> 9 s,
  both binaries byte-identical to the old build's; a generated-block test
  checks the sweep against the old scan.

- `CodegenLicensePolicy` gains `refuse_unbacked_claims_on_checks` (a public
  field, so a struct literal of the policy must now name it) and the builder
  `with_refuse_unbacked_claims_on_checks`: trust-ir's WS1.8 rule (f), a
  safety claim on an `Assert`/`CondBr` with no `ProofRef` binding it to a
  kind-matched obligation sited on that node, refused in `enforce_module`
  (every entry) through trust-ir's own `unbacked_claim_on_check_errors` and
  reported as `TrustIrAdmissionRefused` in trust-ir's words. Default off, as in
  trust-ir's `CodegenAdmission`, pending the producer fix (WS5); the canonical
  identity of every policy without it is unchanged. The JIT's refusal of an
  explicit `Global.section` is now the public function
  `refuse_jit_object_sections`, which `compile_module_to_jit*` calls and a
  consumer's own JIT lane can call (same error and text). The must-refuse
  corpus test gains a `host-jit` lane (`compile_module_to_jit`, AArch64 macOS):
  every row, the same accepted set as the AOT and service lanes. Record:
  `reports/2026-10-01-refusals-ty-inherits/README.md`.
- x86-64 register allocation (miscompile fix): the replay of the allocator's
  stream mutations dropped a split copy whose child only an original ISel copy
  read, so the emitted reader read a register nothing wrote. At `-Copt-level=3`
  with frame-slot forwarding (default on) a call-free kernel returned a wrong
  value under `no-proof-certs` and library callers, and `pop64_carried` was
  refused (`call-severed-vreg-read`, `[TCG-POST-RA-SPILL-INIT]`). The replay
  now states its omission rule once and checks the emitted stream against it
  (a read of an omitted copy's destination is a `RegAlloc` error). Pinned by
  unit tests in `x86_64/pipeline.rs` and `tests/e2e_x86_64_split_copy_replay.rs`
  (two unedited bridge dumps, link-and-run against a host oracle), a required
  Linux x86-64 floor row, and by the bridge's
  `tests/x86_split_copy_replay_run.rs` (20 whole x86-64 programs, O2 and O3,
  against LLVM), a required Darwin bridge target. Execution evidence on this
  change is Rosetta 2 only.
- A by-value iterator terminal over an owning `vec::IntoIter`
  (`v.into_iter()` then `for_each`, `fold`, `sum`, `count`, `max`, `last`,
  `collect` or `extend`) frees the iterator's buffer when its closure, or
  `Sum`'s checked add, unwinds. The bridge drives these terminals itself and
  released the buffer only on the drive's normal exit, so every such unwind
  leaked it (a `collect` into a fresh buffer leaked both), and in a frame that
  cannot unwind the abort came without the free. The terminal now owns a
  landing pad that frees the iterator, then a collect's partly built `Vec`,
  and continues the unwind.
- A `sum()` / `product()` that overflows under `-Coverflow-checks=on` reports
  the location of core's own check (its `|a, b| a + b` closure), as LLVM's
  build does. The bridge's own reduction step reported the reduction's call
  site, and inside a `#[track_caller]` function that function's caller; a
  panic hook reads that location. `tests/vec_compact_user_trait_differential_aarch64.rs`
  (a required Darwin bridge target) covers the two changes above, and
  `Vec::extend`'s `SpecExtend` reservation over owning, range and slice
  sources, also while an unwind out of the extend is in progress: 188 cells,
  120 match LLVM and 68 are refused at -O2/-O3, each pinned by its code and
  reasons, all raised before the bridge lowers the terminal.
- A bridge iterator drive over a `Range` or slice source drops the item a
  by-reference payload (`find`, `filter`, `take_while`, `skip_while`,
  `inspect`) holds when that payload unwinds, as std's frame does; it leaked it
  before. An interior-mutable item (`Cell`) a payload writes through its `&`
  is now the item the drive keeps, returns or drops; the drive used the image
  it stored before the call (`log: 1 2 3` where LLVM printed `11 12 13`). A
  terminal that carries a value needing drop across adapter closures (a `fold`
  / `reduce` accumulator, the result `last` keeps) refuses under
  `panic=unwind` (`[TCG-ITER-UNWIND-CARRY]`) instead of skipping its
  destructor, and a `!Freeze` tuple item refuses
  (`[TCG-ITER-INTERIOR-MUT-ITEM]`). `tests/iter_chain_unwind_item_differential_aarch64.rs`
  (a required Darwin bridge target): 416 cells against LLVM plus a per-site
  check of the no-EH refusal.
- A bridge `collect` into a `Vec` over a source that owns nothing (a range, a
  slice) frees the `Vec` it was building when a payload unwinds, as std's
  `from_iter` does; it left the buffer allocated (`live=7` against LLVM's
  `live=6` under a counting allocator, O0..O3). A held item's pad drops the
  item first and then frees the `Vec`. Without EH lowering such a collect
  refuses (`[TCG-COLLECT-UNWIND-RELEASE]`). The same test file gains 72
  collect cells, all matching LLVM, and pins each of its
  `[TCG-MIR-UNSUPPORTED]` cells by the reason the bridge gives, so a refusal
  for any other reason fails it.
- The bridge spells a `match` case in its selector's range again. trust-ir
  `8dfdd235` checks a switch case against its selector type, and the bridge
  passed MIR's raw bit pattern (`255` for an `i8` selector's `-1`), so any
  bridge-compiled program with such a switch (core's `unchecked_neg`
  precondition check, an `Option<Ordering>` byte) was refused whole. A signed
  selector's case is now its signed value.
- A constant of a single-scalar type over a `bool` (`Cell<bool>`, a
  `struct Flag(bool)`) compiles. It arrived as its scalar's bits, an integer
  constant at trust-ir `bool`, which admits only a boolean constant, so
  trust-ir refused the whole module (`const type mismatch: expected bool, got
  int`) wherever rustc folds such values into constants: an array of
  `Cell<bool>` constants at -O2/-O3, of `Flag` constants at -O1..-O3. It is
  now the `bool` with the same bits; another image is still refused. A signed
  single-scalar constant (`Cell::new(-3i64)`) is respelled by
  `canonicalize_signed_constant_spellings` (the `u64::reverse_bits` entry).
- A printed `.len()` compiles: the `[TCG-FMT-LEN]` refusal of every integer
  `format!` placeholder derived from a length is removed. The `str::len`
  miscompile it was added for had been fixed at its cause, and the
  `ChunksExact`/`RChunksExact` layout miscompile that removing it exposed is
  fixed too. `core::hint::black_box` of a `Vec` (by value, `&` or `&mut`) is no
  longer claimed by the Vec interceptor at -O0/-O1. `tests/format_length_black_box_aarch64.rs`
  (a required Darwin bridge target): 72 length cells and 32 black_box cells
  match LLVM.
- Fixed a compile that never finished: a loop reborrowing a slice by a
  sub-slice of itself (`while let [first, rest @ ..] = p { p = rest }` over a
  local array) made the address-identity fixpoint grow a place path once per
  pass. Derived paths are capped (`MAX_BORROWED_PLACE_PATH`), and a base whose
  path saturates is kept in real storage. `tests/subslice_loop_compile_bound_aarch64.rs`
  (a required Darwin bridge target): 16 cells, all compile in bounded time and
  match LLVM.
- Fixed two wrong orders in the bridge's slice-sort interception. A plain
  `sort`/`sort_unstable` of `u64` or `usize` compared zero-extended elements
  as signed, so values at or above 2^63 sorted first; it now compares with the
  element's signedness. `sort_unstable_by_key` is no longer replaced by the
  stable insertion sort (std's unstable sort may order equal keys
  differently); it takes the ordinary call path into std's own body.
  `tests/slice_sort_order_aarch64.rs` (a required Darwin bridge target): 16
  cells against LLVM, 10 agree, 6 refused by name.
- Cached key sorts route to std's actual body through the general closure
  argument-ABI and aggregate iterator lowering. The merged quadratic cached
  insertion-sort replacement is removed; stable `sort_by_key` retains its
  existing bounded purity/address/panic guards. This is an architectural
  routing change, not a measured speed or memory claim.
- rustc bridge: ONE rule for `extern "rust-call"` and closure-body crossings,
  reconciling round 10 (per-signature argument placement, F2's untupled
  `rust-call` declarations) with `main`'s 2026-10-02 refusals of the tupled
  form (`54cbe9426`, `53cab2796`, `948ab666f`). Every callable is declared as
  rustc's `FnAbi` lists it (a `rust-call` tuple's elements, a closure body's
  `Pair` arguments and by-value environment by rustc's own modes) and judged
  per signature (`check_signature_placement`); the refusals of the tupled
  declaration (`[TCG-RUST-CALL-ABI]`, `refuse_tupled_rust_call_escape`,
  `refuse_closure_pair_escape`, `refuse_by_value_closure_env_*`,
  `closure_defining_copy_reaches_body`, `fn_ptr_shim_dyn_entry`'s
  `[TCG-FN-DYN-ENTRY]`) are not kept, and every program they pinned is now a
  row that must compile and match LLVM: `main`'s `rust_call_pointer_calls`
  and `inlined_closure_bodies` modules (hosted on Darwin AArch64 as the new
  required target `rust_call_boundary_aarch64`, and still on Linux AArch64),
  and the family matrix's `bool_pair_body` / `inline_never_parent` /
  `tait_field` rows for the three shapes `main` listed as known open wrong
  code. *Correction (2026-10-10):* as merged, `tait_field` linked no closure
  body across the boundary, so it did not test its shape, and
  `inline_never_parent` built both crates at one level, not the mixed-level
  form `main` measured wrong; see the family-matrix entry above.
  Review fixes: F1, a closure whose environment is one `f32` / `f64`
  crosses in a floating-point register (`closure_slot_ty`), with `env_f*` /
  `fn_env_f*` / `dyn_env_f*` / `fnmut_env_f64` rows; F2, LIMITATIONS no longer
  claims a pointer-declared environment; F3, `rc_fnptr_rev` / `rc_fnptr_fwd`
  / `rc_trait_dyn` rows pin the `rust-call` fn-pointer fix (silently wrong
  in 16 of 24 cells per direction before F2); F4, one native narrow-cast rule
  (`narrow_cast_param_plan` over `integer_cast_args::plan`, which refuses
  `inreg` and any extension), scoped to AArch64 and x86-64 beside wasm32's
  `small_cast_param_plan`. `main`'s System V `bool` formal zero extension is
  carried into the lane's `x86_sysv_param_locations` formal arm. Fixed a
  wrong result the first O0-O3 run of the matrix found: a bridge-built
  x86-64 binary copied a returned one-float closure environment into its
  slot with an `i64` store of the `f64` value, which the x86-64 selector
  encoded as a store of an unrelated general register (`env_f64` /
  `env_f32`: exit 0 against LLVM's 7 at every level); the copy now stores a
  float lane at its own type (`slot_lane_value_ty`), and the x86-64 selector
  refuses a store whose value lives in the other register file instead of
  encoding it. The family matrix runs O0-O3 by default; `clo_fnptr` pins the
  x86-64 object path's function-identity refusal
  (`AotStaticFunctionIdentityBindingUnsupported`) instead of failing. On
  wasm32 the new corpus crate `r10-bridge-rust-call.rs` replaces `main`'s
  refusal paragraph. MEASURED 2026-10-08 (`targo --unverified`, no proof
  claim; aarch64-apple-darwin natively, x86_64-apple-darwin under Rosetta):
  the family matrix's 62 rows at O0-O3, 239 row-levels per target, agree
  with LLVM in every executed cell (956 on AArch64, 944 on x86-64, where the
  12 others are `clo_fnptr`'s pinned refusal); `rust_call_boundary_aarch64`
  296 native runs at O0-O3, none refused; `m140`, `m141`, `m144`, `m145`
  (both lanes, including the `w2_*` rust-call controls) and `m146` pass;
  `rust_call_shims_linux`'s fixtures re-run on Darwin (the Linux host was not

- Constant-index slice and array places lower on every target. A raw
  borrow `&raw (*s)[k of n]` / `&raw (*s)[-k of n]` (GVN's fold of a known
  index in core's `heapsort` and `find_existing_run`, or a slice-pattern
