- Soundness attestation: a LANDING verdict beside the release one
  (`soundness_attestation.py verify --landing`, SOUNDNESS_CHECK.md "Landing
  and the release boundary"). `soundness_check.sh --attest --scope portable`
  records every per-run and host-independent leg and no x86-64-native class;
  the landing verdict accepts it while the judging verifier's
  `DEFERRED_LANDING_CLASSES` defers that class (today `x86_64-native`, ruling
  OD-LANDING-X86-DEFERRAL-20261008: no native x86-64 executor exists), prints
  the class and its dispatch rows as NOT ATTESTED and the ten SSE lane-routing
  credits as NOT ANCHORED. Run anchored the deferral is the anchor's and only
  shrinks. The release verdict never reads it, never accepts a portable
  record and refuses a record made on a derived overlay toolchain (records now
  state `toolchains.trust.overlay`). The hook, the train and
  `landing_checks.sh` step 4 give the landing verdict; the owner's 2026-09-27
  `--no-verify` exception is replaced by one that ends by itself at the first
  commit attested for landing (`landing-exception`). The release boundary is
  enforced by `publish/pre-promote` (OD-RELEASE-BOUNDARY-20261008). Tested by
  fixture runs of the production gate and verifier, the real hook and train,
  and a pre-promote fixture; no commit is attested yet.

- Bridge: the 2026-10 differential-hunt fixes (ruling OD-173), each pinned
  by a differential test against LLVM on AArch64 Darwin with proof
  certificates off: `vec::Drain` in std's own layout and semantics
  (`vec_drain_std_layout_differential`); wide pointers keep both lanes in
  array `map` and in comparisons (`wide_pointer_lane_differential`); a
  `Vec` or map method is admitted by callee identity, not by name
  (`vec_callee_identity_differential`, `[TCG-MAP-CALLEE]`); `TakeWhile`,
  `FlatMap` and `StepBy` in std's own layout and state, with
  translation-validation lane 12c for the countdown `StepBy::next`
  (`iterator_adapter_state_differential`); `Range` counts in their own
  signedness and core's O(1) `Range` forms
  (`range_closed_forms_differential`); decoded `print!`/`eprint!` through
  std's own `_print`/`_eprint` (C7, `print_order_differential`); the
  128-bit division-by-zero guard tests the whole divisor (C8,
  `i128_const_divisor_guard_differential`); `zip`/`chain` store a slice or
  array argument as `slice::Iter` state (K3,
  `into_iter_adapter_argument_differential`); no dead-body trap stub is
  reachable through a static or shared generics (U1, U2,
  `dead_body_trap_stub_differential`); and `Vec<float>::partial_cmp` takes
  its `None` byte from `layout_of` (W2a, which main also fixed;
  `vec_partial_cmp_option_ordering_differential`). Where main had fixed a
  cluster itself (the panic edges and U3, the in-place `Vec` models' unwind
  state and element semantics, `Chain`'s `Option` halves, the chunk/window
  iterators), main's implementation is kept and the landing's tests run
  against it.
- Bridge: `for_each` and the `fold` consumer, which run rustc's drop glue for
  the closure they take by value (`owned_closure_drop_plan`,
  `[TCG-INTERCEPT-OWNED-DROP]` when they cannot), resolve that closure's body
  without the `[TCG-CLOSURE-DROP]` check, whose premise is a loop that skips
  the glue. A `for_each(move ..)` or `fold(.., move ..)` closure owning a user
  `Drop` or an `Rc` now builds and matches LLVM where it was refused
  (`bridge_regressions_aarch64` rows `for_each`, `fold`, `rc_fold_strong_count`,
  `rc_for_each_strong_count`; `vec_of_refs_collect` matches too). Every other
  synthesized loop keeps its refusals.
- Bridge: the by-value drop accounting (`unaccounted_owned_drop`) and the
  `for_each`/`fold` closure drop plan admit a value whose drop glue only frees
  `Global`-allocator memory, with no `#[global_allocator]` linked, as the
  leak `[TCG-CLOSURE-DROP]` admits (`L06-P3`, ruling OD-171), through one
  shared predicate (`skipped_drop_glue_only_leaks`). They refused it before,
  as `[TCG-INTERCEPT-OWNED-DROP]` or, where the drive ran the glue, at the
  glue's projected `Box` drop (`[TCG-MIR-UNSUPPORTED]`), so the
  `bridge_regressions_aarch64` controls `map_sum_owning_box`,
  `map_sum_owning_box_pair` and `fold_owning_option_box` were refused at -O0
  and -O3 where main builds them; they match LLVM again. Each consumed-closure
  row there now pins its destructor-counting LLVM exit and must match it or
  refuse by name: on AArch64 Darwin 18 of 40 cells match, 8 refuse as
  `[TCG-CLOSURE-DROP]` and 14 as `[TCG-INTERCEPT-OWNED-DROP]` (main refuses
  all 40). Two of the matching cells
  (-O3, a `Box` in the closure's glue) refused at that `Box` drop before
  main's `L06-P8` box glue was merged; other targets may still refuse there.
- Bridge: the `#[global_allocator]` condition of that leak admission
  (`global_allocator_linked`) also sees an allocator defined in the crate
  being compiled or in one of its dependencies (`has_global_allocator`).
  rustc's `allocator_kind` is `None` for an rlib, so an rlib defining a
  counting allocator admitted `Box`-owning `fold`, `for_each` and `retain`
  closures and skipped frees its allocator counts (a wrong free count at -O0
  and -O3, on main too); they are now refused. An allocator defined only
  downstream of the rlib is still not seen (LIMITATIONS, ruling OD-171).
- Bridge: strict `p3c-refine` refuses a queued translation-validation job its
  lane cannot state (a fold miss, an out-of-shape store set, an encoder or
  verifier miss, or a session outside the 64-bit word model) as
  `[TCG-REFINE-SHAPE]`, which replaces `[TCG-SLICE-HEADER-REFINEMENT]`; it
  skipped such a job before. The default lanes still skip it and credit
  nothing (ruling OD-172).
- Bridge: a one-lane local that a loop changes only through a mutable borrow
  of it is threaded across the loop. A `&mut x` call argument of a
  scalarized local is written back by reloading `x` after the call, and a
  store through a `&mut x` taken before the loop rebinds `x`; neither is an
  assignment, so a pointer whose only pre-loop definition was a call result
  (`let mut p = f(); for .. { g(&mut p) }`) got no loop-header phi and the
  loop exit read the pre-loop value. `*const`/`&`/`&mut`/`fn`/`NonNull`/`Rc`/
  newtype pointers came out wrong (also for a borrowed newtype field,
  `&mut w.0`, and for two `&mut` arguments of one call) and a `Box` was used
  after free and freed twice, at -O0 through -O3. `compute_loop_header_params`
  and `loop_carried_completeness_error` now read one `MutableBorrowReach`: the
  `&mut`/`&raw` borrows of a local's own storage a loop takes, and the
  references derived from them (carriers) that it uses. Such a local gets a
  header phi, also when it is read only through a carrier, and one the phi
  cannot carry is refused as `[TCG-LOOP-MUT-BORROW]`. Pinned by
  `tests/loop_mut_borrow_writeback_differential.rs` (O0-O3).
- Darwin arm64 per-program runtime against LLVM `-O3` (L14-P8, L14-P10;
  `reports/perf/2026-10-01-darwin-runtime-per-program/`). Measured on 2026-10-07
  against `main` `f0350c84e` (21 interleaved rounds, load 5-7), the corpus goes from
  1.021x to 0.916x LLVM `-O3` cycles (minimum; median 1.025x -> 0.923x). Over two
  runs and the ±0.5% noise band, 11 programs are faster than LLVM `-O3` (7 on
  `main`; `h1_vec_push_sum` reads parity under heavy load), 6 are at parity
  (`h3_box_leak`, whose time is 63% the system allocator, `p2`, `p3`, `p4`, `p8`,
  and the load-sensitive `v2_memfill`) and `p6_branch_match` is slower (1.012x:
  mispredicted dispatch; a compare tree measured 1.022x and was not kept). LICM
  and SROA follow a field address formed with a constant register
  (`AddRR slot, k`), so `Vec` loops hoist their pointer and keep `cap`/`ptr`/`len`
  in registers (`h1_vec_push_sum` 2.90x -> 0.99x, `h2_vec_grow` 1.23x -> 0.89x);
  the new `xorshift-pair-fusion` pass computes a loop-carried
  `t = x ^ (x << a); t ^ (t >> b)` pair through `UBFM` (3 cycles of recurrence
  instead of 4 on the M4, whose shifted ALU operand is read 2 cycles late);
  `scalar-unroll` admits the bridge's unsigned, copied top-tested header for
  gather reductions and reads lane loads from one pointer (`ldp`);
  `mul-shift-reduce` adds a late `Madd` addend last for `2^k - 1` constants
  (`p5_struct_acc` 1.00x -> 0.89x). The fusion pass follows OD-109 (numeric-ID
  clobber barriers, ordinary metadata, unique block ownership, refusal before
  allocation). Review round 2 (re-measured against `main` `a7ce025ee`, two
  21-round runs: 1.022x -> 0.918x cycles, 12 programs faster, 5 at parity, `p6`
  1.015x) adds three size offsets, all clang's shapes: `trust-cg-lower` divides by
  an even constant whose magic needs the add-back form as `(x >> z) / k`
  (`lsr; umulh; lsr`, the reduced-range band check being the same cited
  Granlund-Montgomery lemma for an N-bit dividend), writes a 64-bit remainder whose
  only use is an `i32` truncation in the W form, and the new `const-chain-dedup`
  pass (O2/O3; `TRUST_CG_DISABLE_PASSES=constdedup`) materializes a repeated
  `movz`+`movk` constant once per block (`p3_gcd`, `p4_matmul`). Emitted-code size
  1.0233x (`main`) -> 1.0315x (round 1) -> 1.0201x LLVM `-O3`: the branch now emits
  56 bytes fewer than `main`; the task's 1.0x bound is still not met and landing
  above it needs the owner's acceptance. In `done` the W-form tail saves nothing
  (the call's argument copy remains: the allocator gives no definition the register
  of an operand dying at the same instruction). No program is slower than on `main`
  beyond the ±0.5% band; `p4_matmul` reads +0.4-0.5% at its edge, not attributed
  (its hot loops are byte-identical, also at identical addresses). The record traces
  `main`'s move from the 2026-09-30 record's 0.951x to the Rust failure-path calls
  six programs' `main` now makes. Compiler instructions retired 0.9999x of
  `main`. Evidence strength: measurements in the diagnostic `no-proof-certs` lane
  on one host (cycles and instructions retired, not wall time); unit tests with
  negative controls and mutants, some against independent opcode evaluators (the
  fusion for every shift pair, the late addend for every subtracting multiplier at
  64 and 32 bits, the lane-offset loads on an order-sensitive SERIAL chain and on
  loop-defined bases, where a lane permutation and a disabled invariance guard had
  passed the whole earlier unit suite); for the size offsets, the reduced-range
  band equal to brute force at w = 8 and the pre-shift exact for every dividend of
  every even divisor at w = 4-12, isel shape tests with negative controls, and
  `const-chain-dedup` tests with a straight-line evaluator and a control per
  condition; a new native differential, `runtime_parity_rewrites_aarch64` (333 rows
  at `-O2` and `-O3` against LLVM, with read-back witnesses that the rewrites ran,
  absent on `main`'s and round 1's backends), registered in the Darwin bridge gate;
  `diff_int_divrem` comparing every JIT configuration with host arithmetic for even
  divisors and truncated remainders (mutants of the pre-shift and the k >= 32
  exclusion fail it); exit codes of all 18 programs equal to LLVM's. No proof
  claim, and the production lane still compiles none of the corpus
  (`[TCG-PROOF-465]`).
- L10-P5 (machine-IR identity admission): `MachFunction::admit_id_counters`
  re-derives every register, instruction, block, stack-slot and jump-table
  identity a function references and refuses, by name, a live ID at or above
  the counter that issues its domain's next ID (`[TCG-MIR-STALE-ID-COUNTER]`)
  or an exhausted domain (`[TCG-MIR-ID-EXHAUSTED]`). It runs at the
  instruction-selection exit (`ISelFunction::try_to_ir_func`), the optimizer
  pass manager's entry and exit, each pass's first allocation (every pass
  entry marks the function; legacy and checked allocators re-derive before
  issuing an ID), the AArch64 codegen phase boundaries and the AOT profile
  instrumentation entry; the verdict is `PassStats::id_admission` and
  `PipelineError::MachIdAdmission` (filed as `TCG-REGALLOC` by the rustc
  bridge). The legacy allocators (MachIR and the selector's) saturate at the
  `u32::MAX` sentinel instead of wrapping or narrowing; the machine inliner
  admits its splice and declines otherwise; the constant-address unroll clone
  allocates through the counter; SROA allocates its planned shadow registers
  through the new `MachFunction::try_alloc_vreg_range` before writing any
  (it used to number them by hand and raise the counter itself, which hid a
  counter left stale before it and, through the pass manager, refused a
  well-formed memcpy fill); and the NEON candidate rewrites admit the function
  (new `MachFunction::admit_ids_before_allocation`) before their private copy
  synchronizes its counter, so a stale counter is refused, not repaired
  (`xorshift-pair-fusion`, which landed beside this change and synchronizes
  the function's own counter before allocating, admits it first the same
  way); frame insertion, which numbers its prologue/epilogue in a staged plan,
  admits the function before planning.
  Breaking API changes: `PassManager::run_once` and `run_once_with_provenance`
  return `Result<bool, MachIdRefusal>` (was `bool`); `MachFunction` gained a
  private field, so it can no longer be built by a struct literal outside
  trust-cg-ir; `PassStats` gained the public `id_admission` field and
  `PipelineError` the `MachIdAdmission` variant, which exhaustive matches
  must handle. Emitted bytes are unchanged: the compile corpus reports
  Identity: PASS on all 534 (entry, lane) pairs against origin/main
  `a7ce025ee` (two alternating three-repetition runs per side, load average
  10-16). Instructions retired: +0.27% to +0.34% on the JIT lanes in every
  pairing (same-binary repeats differ by at most 0.05%); the AOT lanes pool
  at +0.04% (aot-object) and +0.09% (aot-proofs), inside the 0.25% by which
  same-binary repeats of those lanes differed (pairings -0.15% to +0.26%).
  Scanning after every pass instead cost 2.0-3.0%. Evidence strength:
  testing and named refusal controls, not proof.
  Every pass of the O1/O2/O3 ladders sits behind the pass-manager entry
  admission, which refuses six injected corruptions with the function
  untouched (the same scan for every pass); an allocating pass is refused at
  its first allocation when the pass before it left the register counter far
  below or a near miss below a live register, on hand-built fixtures and on
  194 committed-corpus functions at O2 (SROA, the NEON candidate passes,
  mem-pair formation, mul-shift reduction, loop-latch layout, scalar unroll,
  if-conversion); a boundary observer over 48 generated kernels and the corpus
  functions finds every boundary admitted and every new register inside the
  range the counter advanced over during its pass. Within one pass, a
  hand-written ID issued again after the pass's first allocation is not
  detected, nor a pass that raises the counter past its own hand numbering;
  the x86-64 path (`X86ISelFunction`) is not admitted. New floor targets
  (Darwin and Linux, minimum 6 and 5; Linux not yet run on a Linux host):
  `trust-cg-opt/mach_id_admission`,
  `trust-cg-codegen/mach_id_admission_property`.
- AArch64 NEON (ledger L04-P6). A live silicon differential
  (`trust-cg-verify` `aarch64_neon_silicon_differential`, Darwin floor 11)
  runs every modeled encoder form of the 60 audited NEON value opcodes
  (1,294 forms) on the host CPU against the `neon_semantics` model the
  obligations use. Inputs are exhaustive for byte lanes, plus edge triples
  and random vectors elsewhere: 3,250,138 vectors in all. Integer lanes and
  non-NaN FP lanes agree bit for bit. 5,936 FP lanes where both sides are a
  NaN are compared by class, because the model returns the default NaN. No
  model disagreed. Before this, UDOT, UADDLP/SADDLP/UADALP, SMLAL/UMLAL(2),
  UADDW/SADDW(2), EXT, REV64/REV32, RBIT, CNT, ABS, BIT, FMLA/FMLS/FMLA-lane,
  UCVTF/SCVTF, FCVTL(2), UMOV, INS, DUP, MOVI and the immediate shifts had no
  hardware differential. The 29 encoder-only forms (DUP element into `D`,
  REV64 `.8B`) have no value model; their lane-effect decompositions now run
  on the CPU as well. ADDP (scalar, `.2D`) gets a model, a faithful
  cross-lane obligation with five refuting controls, and gate credit. It
  leaves the fail-closed allowlist: AArch64 goes from 179/301 to 180/302 on
  top of L04-P12's trap carriers, still 122 RED. No lowering selects ADDP
  yet, so it is the one emittable-class row with no emitter. The horizontal
  reductions and permutes get a word-bound lane-effect decomposition
  (`aarch64_neon_lane_effect`), and LD1/ST1 post-index joins the
  memory-effect decomposition. ENC-5 binds both to the word, and a codegen
  unit test pins that binding against every single-bit corruption. Both are
  decided exactly in process. They refute or annotate rows and never credit:
  the lane effects have no live replay lane, and the four post-index rows
  stay RED. Unsigned-lane vector arithmetic, compares and selects,
  `<4 x u32>` uniform shifts, `<8 x u8>` bitwise ops and compares, V64
  integer constants and vector OR-NOT now lower. Packed `<4 x u32>` and
  `<2 x u64>` constant lanes are range-checked against their unsigned lane
  type, so a negative unsigned lane is refused as before.
  `e2e_aarch64_neon_admission` (Darwin floor 3) runs 93 functions at O0-O3
  against clang -O3 NEON intrinsics with no mismatch. The `<8 x u8>` compare
  is covered only by adapter tests: nothing in TrustIR consumes its V64 mask
  in a way a native test can observe. Strength: testing evidence on one
  macOS arm64 host, plus in-process exact decisions. There is no proof
  credit beyond the ADDP row's accepted-obligation inventory entry. The
  Linux floor registers both targets; they have not yet run there.
- Bind AArch64 memory rows to their source (ledger `L07-P2`,
  `X-OPCODES-P1`). The save and restore pairs of a source-bound leaf frame are
  bound to the frame theorem's record and now need the replayed theorem AND a
  Clean-checked certificate of every part of their word. A frameless
  straight-line leaf's scalar loads and stores are bound, access by access, to
  their LIR `Load`/`Store` by a lock-step trace checker
  (`source_bound_memory_leaf`); such an access is credited `Formal` only when
  every memory-effect part has an AY proof the accepted Clean checker fully

  receipts, wrong slots, operands, widths and directions are refused).
  Admitting Clean-checked parts on this source-bound route only is ruling
  OD-139; OD-39 still refuses them for an unbound row.
  Evidence strength: formal per row (an in-process exact binding plus
  independently checked proofs), measured with an overlay of AY `2657db47c`
  and Clean `ed21fee39`, under which (with the form certificates disabled)
  the verifying JIT publishes and runs 8 copy-free load/store leaves; with
  Trust package 9192 every bound row stays refused by name, and the native
  target pins both outcomes by tool digest. On the census corpus no row moves
  (`main` `b422f87fd` against the branch before its first merge with
  `origin/main`, with either tool set: 1,324 of 1,345 functions refused, 45,775
  blocking rows): its 820 memory rows, which the Formal-only rule credits
  since this host's `drat-trim` was authorized, sit in 276 functions outside
  the leaf domain (153 multi-block, 84 with a call, 21 with an address
  reference, 18 with a division guard). A formal `--emit-proofs` sidecar that
  carries the frame theorem now also carries the twelve frame-record parts;

  `aarch64_memory_source_binding` (4).

- Run the rustc bridge's differential corpus and x86 feature suites natively on

- AArch64 memory ordering (L03-P3): a `Release` fence selects `DMB ISH`
  (it was `DMB ISHST`, which orders only stores, so a load before the fence
  could be satisfied after a store that follows it); LLVM's choice. A
  FEAT_LSE2 SeqCst 128-bit atomic load is `DMB ISH; LDP; DMB ISH` (it was
  `LDP; DMB ISH`, not ordered after this backend's SeqCst store-releases; an
  inline-assembly replica of the old pair showed the SeqCst-forbidden
  store-buffering outcome on an M4 in three of four runs, up to 8,512 of
  2^20 rounds). ISel refuses
  Release/AcqRel loads and Acquire/AcqRel stores by name.
  `trust_cg_verify::aarch64_memory_order` checks every selected atomic form
  against the C11/Rust -> AArch64 mapping on its decoded words (acquire,
  release, SeqCst entry/exit, fence access pairs, width, single-copy
  atomicity) with named refusals, and the cmpxchg failure-ordering lift over
  all 25 pairs; `aarch64_memory_order_obligations` drives it over every
  admitted request on the Darwin AOT, LSE and baseline profiles at O0-O3
  (4,800 rows) with word-mutation controls and an Apple clang barrier
  differential. Evidence strength: mapping conformance (exhaustive over the
  selector's request space) plus testing; the instructions' ordering
  semantics and the mapping's whole-program soundness are delegated, and no
  Clean certificate exists. `e2e_aarch64_memory_order_litmus` runs native
  MP/SB/LB/IRIW/2+2W litmus tests over trust-cg-compiled thread bodies:
  no forbidden outcome, with plain MP and SB controls that show theirs.
- rustc bridge, ledger L06-P8 (Darwin AArch64; native execution and

  loop) get frame homes, and a landing pad threads only the scalars it reads
  (both shapes used to be refused, `[TCG-EH-CLEANUP-LOOP]` and an SSA "passes
  0 arg(s)" error); a pad that needs no SSA input gets no homes, so a body
  that compiled before keeps its code (measured on a generic pad probe, not
  proved for every body). An indirect call with a live cleanup or terminate
  edge (a `thread_local!` access, a `dyn` method or `Box<dyn Fn>` call, a
  `Box<dyn Trait>` drop) goes through the typed forwarding thunk Linux AArch64
  already uses (refused by name on Darwin before). The bounded scalar FP
  `asm!` grammar (`fmadd`, `fsqrt`, `frintn`) is admitted on Darwin, through
  the backend's encoder and ENC-5 decode check.
  `#[link_section]` statics are placed in their Mach-O (and AArch64 ELF)
  sections, a `__DATA,__mod_init_func` constructor included; a function's
  `#[link_section]`, which was dropped silently, is refused as
  `[TCG-SECTION-TARGET]`. The families that stay unmodeled are refused with
  named codes: `[TCG-TAIL-CALL]` (`become`), `[TCG-INLINE-ASM]` (every `asm!`
  outside the bounded FP grammar), `[TCG-MIR-NOT-RUNTIME]` (`Yield`,
  `CoroutineDrop`, the false edges, `CopyForDeref`: removed before runtime MIR
  on the pinned compiler), `[TCG-UNSAFE-BINDER]`, and `[TCG-GLOBAL-ASM]` as
  before. New required Darwin bridge target `mir_families_aarch64` (6 tests:
  `SetDiscriminant` over 18 slots and 19 writes and `Rvalue::Discriminant`
  over 43 reads at -O0..-O3, user `Drop` glue and indirect calls with real
  panics caught in an LLVM harness that counts every allocation over 16
  scenarios at -O0..-O3, `#[link_section]` placement against LLVM's `nm -m`,
  the FP `asm!` corpus against its hardware-checked C driver, seven named
  refusals with certificates on); `dyn_heap_glue_differential_aarch64` now
  links its six-box `Box<dyn>` chain (7 of 7 freed) and
  `real_program_runtime_aarch64`'s three unwinding `array::IntoIter<D>` guests
  match LLVM on Darwin. Not done: a guaranteed tail call, general inline and
  global assembly, `Vec<Box<T>>` with a droppable `T`, these lanes on x86-64
  and AArch64 Linux, and assigning an enum call result into a field of a
  memory-backed aggregate.
- Imports (roadmap WS7.9): `trust-cg --link <dep>` (repeatable, native
  lanes) authenticates a module's cross-crate imports with trust-ir's
  `validate_linked_module` (every import row digest-checked, cited or not;
  every call to an imported declaration signature-checked; every dependency
  validated) and then admits exactly the `InheritedFromCallee { external }`
  certificates the walk authenticated; they stay data. Without `--link` the
  refusal (`ExternalEvidenceInheritance`) is unchanged. Library:
  `trust_cg_lower::authenticate_linked_imports`, `AuthenticatedImportSet`
  carried by `CodegenLicensePolicy::with_authenticated_imports` (bound to one
  root by stable digest, `AuthenticatedImportsBoundElsewhere`; disables
  compile-artifact reuse), and the floor variants `*_with_imports`.
  `--emit-proofs` writes `linked_dependencies.json` (the authenticated
  dependency modules, not object files). `--link` is refused on wasm32.
- `--link` (WS7.9 review): the floor admits an authenticated cross-crate
  inheritance only when the local obligation it discharges and its local
  callee's name are the ones the linked walk checked (a module that kept the
  certificate but rewrote the claim was admitted by a set made for another
  module), and the authentication moves onto the backend's dialect-legalized
  module through `CodegenLicensePolicy::for_backend_rewrite` when that keeps
  the name, import table and proof tables (a linked module with a legalized
  dialect op was refused with `AuthenticatedImportsBoundElsewhere`).
- `merge_modules` re-interns import rows by content and remaps
  `FunctionSummary::backed_by` instead of refusing every module with
  imports; a row naming a merge peer's digest is refused as
  `ImportSatisfiedByMergePeer` (until trust-ir's library merge, WS4.11), and an
  input's own duplicate row as `ImportTableNotInterned`.

- x86-64: a System V `bool` register parameter is `movzx r32, r/m8` of its
  argument register's low byte at entry (it was a 32-bit copy). The psABI
  defines only bits 0..7 of a `bool` argument register (bit 0 the value,
  bits 1..7 zero), while the backend passes a `bool` argument as a clean
  32-bit bool, which an LLVM callee relies on (`b as u32` is `movl %edi,
  %eax`); so a function that forwarded its `bool` parameter passed a psABI
  caller's bits 8..31 on unchanged. Callers that extend the bool to 32 bits
  (LLVM, clang, this backend) see no change. Found by slice 15 of the
  source-bound body theorem, whose psABI caller view refutes the copy
  (ruling OD-113). Regression test
  `test_lower_formal_arguments_sysv_bool_register_is_movzx_of_the_low_byte`,
  failing before the change (`MovRR32` for `Movzx`).
- x86-64 proof lane, slice 15 of the source-bound body theorem: the value,
  call and observable residue. LIR `Fconst` is trust-ir's
  `float_bits_from_f64` (an `F32` NaN constant stays outside) and
  `Fneg`/`Fabs` are the IEEE sign-bit operations, exact in `QF_BV`
  (ruling OD-112), with the selector's constant-pool `movss`/`movsd` and
  three-operand `pxor`/`andps`/`andpd` modelled. A `mov` or ALU row of
  mixed 32- and 64-bit registers defines the low 32 bits of its operation.
  A `bool` parameter may be forwarded as a `bool` argument, observed as the
  clean 32-bit bool under every caller view (ruling OD-113). A load or store
  through an address that may derive from an escaped slot observes the
  escaped slots' bytes, and a store redefines them, as a call does (ruling
  OD-114; slice 7 refused such an access). An `I128` parameter or argument
  past the integer registers takes two 16-byte-aligned eightbytes of the
  stack areas. A body with no observable stays refused (ruling OD-115).
  22 fixtures certify on AY build 12713, 14 wrong lowerings are refuted,
  each of 14 rules disabled alone fails a control, and a mutation probe of
  1341 streams credits no wrong one. On the Darwin `core` O0 census on AY
  build 12713, failed roots go from 499 (`main` `cf982f936`) to 466: 29
  promote in the slice-15 classes and 4 are the baseline run's replay
  noise; none newly fails, no mismatch is named and no body is refuted
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-06-darwin-x86-64-census-slice15/`).

- x86-64: a `SeqCst` `AtomicStore` is `mov; mfence`. The selector ignored
  the store's ordering and emitted a plain `mov`, which x86-TSO may reorder
  with a later load, so a sequentially consistent store was not; the
  `mfence` is the row a `SeqCst` fence already emits (its `FenceSeqCst`
  proof origin). Relaxed and Release stores stay a plain `mov`. The rustc
  bridge never emitted the opcode (it lowers such a store to an exchange);
  a direct trust-ir producer could. Found by slice 13's review; regression
  test `test_select_atomic_store_seqcst_is_followed_by_mfence`, failing
  before the fix (`[MovMR]` for `[MovMR, Mfence]`).
- x86-64 proof lane, slice 13 of the source-bound body theorem: memory and
  values. A private stack address may be stored as data (one free input per
  slot, `slot{x}`, plus the offset); its slot escapes where the memory it
  went to is shared (to incoming memory or an escaped slot at once, into a
  private slot when that slot escapes, transitively), and a DAG join takes
  the union of its edges' escaped slots. Integer parameters past the six
  argument registers are read from `[rbp + 16 + 8k]` and integer or
  private-address arguments past them from the outgoing `[rsp + 8k]` area
  (a return with the area open is RSP not restored). `Memcpy`, `Memmove`
  and `Memset` are calls to the C routines by symbol. Scalar atomic loads
  and `Relaxed`/`Release` stores are their single-threaded plain
  counterparts (ruling OD-83); a sequentially consistent `AtomicStore` is
  refused by name, because the x86 selector lowers it to a plain `mov`.
  20 fixtures certify on AY builds 10530 and 12713, 15 wrong lowerings are
  refuted, each of 19 rules disabled alone fails a control, and a mutation
  probe of 1111 streams credits no wrong one. On the Darwin `core` O0
  census on AY build 12713, failed roots go from 573 to 493: 80 promote,
  none newly fails, no mismatch is named and no body is refuted
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-05-darwin-x86-64-census-slice13/`). A latent
  index fault of the walk's affine form past the eighth parameter is fixed.

- x86-64 proof lane: the x86_64 Darwin qualification host's replayer moves
  from the stage-1 toolchain's AY 0.27.0 build 10530 to AY build 12713
  (`b1b0b9de0`, word-level certification), run from a local overlay
  toolchain because no published x86_64 Darwin pack carries it (ruling OD-85;
  Clean 5f09e36c unchanged). Every pinned outcome was reviewed one by one:
  five fixtures now certify (`MulU32`, `AddShl2/LeaSib`, `SlotJoin`,
  `BoolDag`, `MulI64`); `u128::wrapping_sub` (`SubU128`) no longer does, an
  AY regression reported to AY (the same search, but a proof 4.4 times
  larger, past the 30 s deadline); the other gaps now mostly time out; every
  wrong lowering is still refuted, each counterexample confirmed by z3.
  On the Darwin `core` census the same tree's bridge fails 573 roots against
  1095: 525 are promoted, and 3 newly fail on AY regressions
  (`u64`/`usize::wrapping_mul` on AY's resident route, which does not take
  the word-level path, and `str::traits::check_range`, whose certification
  slowed from 29.5 s to 49 s). No mismatch is named and no body is refuted.
  `scripts/assemble_trust_overlay.py --pack-kind wrapper-sysroot` assembles
  the bridge's overlay from a sysroot whose `trustc` is a shell wrapper with
  a hard-coded `--sysroot`, and the x86 body query export covers slice 9's
  snapshot family (main's own capture was refused at its first slice-9
  record).

- x86-64 proof lane, slice 9 of the source-bound body theorem: acyclic
  control flow past the slice-6 bounds. A several-path source with more
  than sixteen blocks, more than sixteen entry-to-end paths or a path of
  more than 256 instructions is stated over its DAG, in size linear in its
  blocks:
  - The theorem uses 1-bit block and edge guards. The entry's is 1. A
    join's is the `bvor` of its incoming edges'. A conditional edge's is its
    block's guard `bvand` its slice-6 test.
  - Values, machine registers and private bytes are joined by the SOURCE
    edges' guards.
  - Each block's observed items are stated under its guard, and each
    conditional edge's machine `jcc` literals under the edge's guard.

  The theorem is EQUIVALENT to the slice-6 per-path conjunction input by
  input (the edge tests partition the runs). A sampled equivalence test
  checks it on every slice-6 fixture, refutation and variant and on every
  slice-9 fixture.

  Admission and the machine walk run block by block over a state merged at
  joins (`AdmitState`, `MachineState`). These are named refusals: a join of
  different escapes, a `Switch` with two cases of one value, a redefinition
  after a join, a register holding different kinds of value at a join, and
  loops. Flags never cross a block boundary, including flags a slice-10 ALU
  row wrote. One-path chains may run past 256 instructions. New bounds: 128
  LIR blocks, 1024 LIR instructions, 128 machine blocks and 512 machine
  rows (no theorem of more rows certified offline).

  A DAG's theorem and a long chain's are trimmed (no copy names; only the
  definitions the claims reach), every single-use definition is
  inlined, and each claim equation the substitution makes an identity is
  dropped. Host qualification chose this spelling: offline, AY 0.27.0
  certifies 22 of the 52 newly bound `core` bodies this way against 1
  untrimmed (decisions OD-71, OD-72). Several-path sources within the
  slice-6 bounds keep their theorems byte for byte.

  Tests:
  - A new soundness library gate, `x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice9::`
    (20 solver-free tests, digest-pinned `slice9_snapshots.smt2`). Each of
    21 rules disabled alone fails a control.
  - The replay in `slice9_qualification`: 4 of 15 fixtures certify,
    11 are recorded gaps, and 14 wrong lowerings are refuted.
  - Three slice-9 functions in the end-to-end proof-required compile.
  - A mutation probe against an independent interpreter: 2299 mutants,
    and no wrong stream holds.

  The probe found the gate's sampler stepping the third argument register
  through a theorem's constants at a fixed stride of five, which missed a
  third switch's wrong case. Every input now takes every constant and
  neighbour, at a stride coprime with their count.
  The Darwin `core` O0 census: 1166 failed roots against main
  `cffb7e876`'s 1198. 32 roots promote, 28 of them slice 9's (4 others
  certify only at a lower host load, with unchanged theorems). None newly
  fails and no mismatch is named. The 76 newly bound bodies certify at 37%.
  Report: `reports/perf/2026-10-02-darwin-x86-64-census-slice9/`.

- A sealed-Core address-free compile now lowers frames as the proof-grade
  publication it is, on both AArch64 Core triples. Its pipeline builder never
  selected the proof-grade policy; sealed-Core preparation now takes this
  frame policy from its admission, as its raw dataflow check, final-stream
  recheck and encoder already did. No proof authority is added.
  - On `aarch64-apple-darwin` there is no red zone, and the zero-storage leaf
    policy keeps its FP/LR envelope. Darwin used to keep the red zone here, so
    the source-bound frame owner, and with it the ALU and OD-35 A2 constant
    owners, could not bind a Darwin Core leaf. On a host whose proof tools do
    not replay the frame theorem, such leaves are now refused on the
    unreplayed envelope rather than on a frameless MOVN or a certificate with
    no verified row; the affected tests branch on
    `host_replays_source_bound_frame`.
  - On `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, a U10
    stack-limit request is refused at frame lowering with the typed
    `StackLimitNotProofQualified`, as the U10 design states for Core
    proof-grade. It was refused before, but only later and incidentally: on
    Darwin by a machine certificate with no verified row, on ELF by the
    affine-bytes check ("final instruction must be RET X30").

- AArch64 ELF and the LLVM importer, L02-P13 second closure-audit repair

  it (`.data.<symbol>`, `.bss.<symbol>`, `.rodata.<symbol>`,
  `.data.rel.ro.<symbol>`, or a second section of its explicit name), where

  failed links llc's object passed, and LLD's `__start_`/`__stop_` walk saw
  three members where llc's saw one); the x86-64 ELF emitter places a
  retained global alone too. A hidden, protected or `extern_weak`
  declaration nothing references is now an undefined symbol with that fact,
  as llc writes it: an unreferenced hidden declaration again hides the C
  definition a `pic` library links (an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer had rebound

  differential over 15 retention and declaration modules (O0-O3; static,
  PIE and shared, `LD_PRELOAD` where it applies; 420 runs) in which every
  run equals llc's, where the base differed in 208; the 24 of 180 objects

  private or `unnamed_addr` global's own section name, a `static`-model

  and 2,304 function modules, four configurations each) unchanged but for
  the 96 configurations of unreferenced declarations, now equal to llc's; a
  sweep of every section name LLVM 22
  classifies by name, in which only the four coverage names differed (now
  refused); a recount of 3,675 texts (the in-tree `.ll` files, the earlier
  rounds' corpus, `opt` prints, rustc modules and this suite's new texts) in
  which the only changes are the two texts with a used global or an
  unreferenced hidden declaration and this suite's new rows; and mutation:

- AArch64 and x86-64 ELF, Mach-O and the LLVM importer, L02-P13 second
  closure-audit repair, verifier round 1 (LD-20 corrected, LD-21 extended,

- LLVM importer and x86-64 COFF, L02-P13 second closure-audit repair,

  `available_externally` global with hidden or protected visibility is refused by name, listed in

  `available_externally` forms (a default global, listed and not, and
  hidden and protected functions) equal llc's objects (12 of 12, undefined

- Live AArch64 register copies can earn source-bound credit through a raw
  source/result theorem replayed by AY and independent Clean (OD-35 C).
  The query threads the actual allocated W/X registers from ABI inputs;
  only copies in the return's backward slice receive credit. Unused scalar
  register-formal copies are removed before allocation, preserving ABI
  liveness metadata. With constant credit, the unchanged Linux arithmetic
  matrix publishes all 160 cases and executes 23,040 calls. Controls reject
  78 live-copy byte mutations and 124 constant byte mutations. Exact
  `A64Body` payloads survive object export and sidecar deduplication. Rust
  source/frame binding and term construction remain trusted; identity bodies,
  multiword MOVK sequences and unsupported body shapes receive no new credit.

- AArch64 single MOVZ/MOVN materializations can earn source-bound credit
  inside a replayed Formal frame (OD-35 A2). The owner binds the actual LIR
  Iconst's coordinates, digest, value and width; AY and independent Clean
  replay its ground theorem, including dead constants. Exact queries survive
  object export as `A64Constant` payloads. Multiword MOVK expansions remain
  uncredited. ALU labels now distinguish Rust body binding
  from replayed local arithmetic (OD-36), and both arms compute degeneracy
  from the obligation (OD-37).

- Both native certificate adapters reject every structurally degenerate proof,
  including names in the genuine-identity classification table (OD-38). That
  table grants no publication authority. The regression exercises both targets
  at Exhaustive, Statistical and Formal strengths and checks the final object
  publication gate. Current registry identity candidates already remain
  uncredited; this removes the latent exception for a future report producer.

- A trust-ir level-S template (amendment S, wire v57) handed to a module
  reader is refused by name (`pipeline::TEMPLATE_IS_NOT_A_MODULE`) on every
  reader entry: the `TRUST_IS` blob through `load_module_from_bytes`, `Auto`
  sniffing and the text parser (it previously fell through to the JSON
  fallback there), and template text. Level R gains no construct (the `Ext`
  arms are uninhabited), so nothing new reaches a lane or the wasm32 mid-end;
  `wasm_v57_templates` pins that, and drives host-instantiated template bodies
  through `trust-cg-irmid` at O2 and both wasm32 lanes at O0 and O2 against
  the reference interpreter. A gated instance body is left alone by the
  mid-end (`body_gate`).

- The native adapter's refinement representation boundary (refined narrow
  argument and return extension, the refined volatile `i128` refusal) and
  the shared admission's refusal of a refined `gep` index are pinned on
  wasm32 by `wasm_refine_representation`. Both wasm32 lanes refuse a refined
  parameter, result, call argument or volatile access by naming its `Refine`
  type at O0-O3 while the unrefined module compiles. `trust-cg-irmid` at O2
  keeps every volatile access and every load that crosses a refinement from
  its slot's store, and its store-forwarding, copy-propagation and
  scalar-replacement checkers refuse a witness that changes a type there. No
  wasm32 lowering of a refined value is claimed.

- On wasm32 the bridge's `[TCG-RUST-CALL-ABI]` refusal of `rust-call` calls
  of a callee it did not declare admits only a tuple that passes nothing (no
  wasm32 tuple placement is stated). A call through an `extern "rust-call"
  fn(..)` pointer, a dynamic call of a non-`Fn*` trait's `extern "rust-call"`
  method and a call of a foreign `extern "rust-call"` item are refused by name
  there. This removes a measured wrong result (a pointer to a reified
  `<C as Fn<..>>::call` trapped with `function signature mismatch` where
  rustc+LLVM returns a value) and also refuses a `(u32, u64)` fn-pointer call
  and a non-`Fn*` `dyn` method call that compiled correctly before. `Fn*`
  dispatch, generic `F: Fn*`, direct calls of a non-foreign item and
  `call`/`call_mut`/`call_once` on a closure are unaffected.
- AArch64 ELF, L02-P6 sixth closure-audit coverage (audit at `23ee1104a`;
  tests, floor configuration and one refusal message, no emitted byte
  changes). One of the audit's two coverage skeptics kept the row partial:
  mutant K19, which drops visibility from `compatible_external_declarations`
  (the function catalog's check of two declarations of one symbol in one
  module), passed the seven floor targets the audit ran for the row. Under
  it, two declarations of one symbol that differ in visibility compiled, and
  the object spelled the one the symbol table met last: hidden then
  protected gave `GLOBAL PROTECTED UND`, which a linked shared library
  exported. K20, which admits `external_weak` beside `external` at the same
  site, also passed: the pair compiled to a `WEAK` undefined reference, so a
  library linked under `-z defs` without the definition, and its call died
  with SIGSEGV.
  trust-ir's validator reports `DuplicateFunctionSymbol` for any repeated
  name, but the adapter does not enforce that finding, so the catalog is the
  only guard.
  - **Repeated declarations, every entry.**
    `repeated_declarations_that_disagree_about_visibility_or_linkage_are_refused_on_every_entry`
    declares `rd_ext` twice for every ordered pair of (`external` or
    `external_weak`, default/hidden/protected): 30 pairs that differ, three
    identical `external_weak` pairs (outside the rule, which admits only
    `external`) and three identical `external` pairs. Each module goes
    through the `.trust_ir` text parser, the bare `TRUST_IR` and `tMBC`
    binary containers (`decode_binary`) and JSON
    (`load_module_from_bytes`), keeping both declarations, into
    `Compiler::compile` under `static`, `pie` and `pic` at O0-O3. The 33
    refused pairs must fail as an ambiguous symbol whose two bodyless
    declarations disagree (1,584 compiles). The identical `external` pairs
    must compile to one undefined `STB_GLOBAL` `rd_ext` with the stated
    visibility, GOT-addressed and called directly (144 compiles).
    `merge_modules` does not reach the check: it folds one input's repeated
    `external` declarations into the most constraining visibility in either
    order, as it does across inputs, and refuses an input with an
    `external_weak` function by name. The row pins both (decision LD-06).
  - **Default `available_externally` under `pic`.** The audit's K6 (splicing
    a preemptible default `available_externally` body) failed one object row
    only. The native declaration-library row now also carries a default
    `available_externally` function: under GNU ld, gold and LLD at O0-O3 its
    call must go through the PLT, and an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer must take
    it.
  - **Unit test.** The catalog's mutation list now also varies `ExternalWeak`
    linkage (one and both), `body_gate`, `display_path`,
    `source_provenance`, section, visibility (hidden, protected, and both)
    and retention. A new control shows that agreeing hidden, protected,
    section and retention metadata still shares the symbol. The refusal
    detail for two bodyless declarations now names visibility, section and
    retention, and that both must be `external`.
  - **Mutants, replayed.** Each was applied alone to `d146b224f` and the
    target run with `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD=1 TCG_REQUIRE_GOLD=1` (debug build;
    unmutated 82/82 with no `SKIP` line, trust-cg-lower lib 1,992/1,992).
    K19 and K20 each fail the new row (the first pair, an `external` default
    declaration beside a hidden one or an `external_weak` one, compiled) and
    the catalog's unit test. K6 fails the object row and the native
    declaration-library row, the latter first at the compile result's splice
    disclosure; with that row's object and link checks turned into reports
    in a scratch build, its `LD_PRELOAD` run printed the template's 55 where
    the interposer's 555 belongs (O1, GNU ld). K5 passes this target and
    fails the floor target `e2e_aarch64_sequences` (13/14,
    `calls_to_replaceable_sequence_returning_bodies_are_refused_by_name`).
  - **Documentation.** `LIMITATIONS.md` said the fifth repair's four rows had
    run only in that repair's own runs; gate 40's `run-i57` ran them 81/81
    at `e3508e8d4`, as did this audit. It also said the visibility table's
    45 bodyless definition-linkage cases fail `Compiler::compile` with an
    unnamed error and that the table asserts only trust-ir's validator for
    them. Since `907e8f9d6` they are refused as `[TCG-DECLARATION-LINKAGE]`,
    and the table asserts that code under `static` and `pic`.
  - **Floor.** The Linux floor pins `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` at 82 (81);
    the target passed 82/82 with no `SKIP` line in the floor's `--release`
    build and in a debug build. The Darwin floor's host-neutral minimum is 49
    (48), with a table sum of 2,004 (2,003).
- Linux link driver: the twelfth L02-P10 closure audit's findings
  (2026-10-03, `23ee1104a`). Each reproducer is refused now with the
  output's bytes left as they were (`link_options`
  `linux_got_page::tls_templates_that_do_not_hold_trust_cgs_thread_locals_are_never_installed`,
  `segments_without_the_permissions_trust_cgs_sections_need_are_never_installed`,
  `llvm_bitcode_inputs_are_read_through_the_objects_lld_compiles`).
  - **Thread-local template** (`[TCG-LINK-TLS-TEMPLATE]`). GNU ld 2.42 given
    a `PHDRS` script whose `PT_TLS` held `.tbss` alone, LLD 22.1.6 given an
    `INSERT` script with `-z norelro` (a PIE and a shared object) and LLD
    given `-Wl,--section-start=.tbss=0x700000` installed images whose
    trust-cg thread-locals read wrong values without a crash. An image's
    `PT_TLS` must now hold its thread-local sections as linked (one with
    memory, starting at the first, `p_align` dividing `p_vaddr`, its file
    part in one `PT_LOAD`'s and holding `.tdata` and no other section, zero
    bytes under a `.tbss` there); trust-cg's own thread-local sections, as
    the map places them, must lie in it, its local-exec and relaxed
    `MOVZ`/`MOVK` accesses in an executable must hold `align_up(16, p_align)
    + (S + A - p_vaddr)`, and its global thread-locals' symbol values their
    offset from `p_vaddr`.
  - **Read and execute permission** (`[TCG-LINK-SEGMENT-PERMISSIONS]`).
    trust-cg's `.rodata` in a `PT_LOAD` without permissions and its `.text`
    in a read-only one were installed and died with SIGSEGV. An allocated
    section of trust-cg's needs `PF_R` and its code `PF_X` of the segment
    holding it, through the predicate the `PF_W` rule of
    `[TCG-LINK-WRITE-PROTECTED]` shares. gold's map prints trust-cg's
    `.text` (the last code input of its output section) at
    `0xffffffffffffffff`; it is placed by the symbols listed under it.
  - **LLVM bitcode**. A static LLD image whose bitcode archive member defined
    libgcc's outline-atomics helpers was installed and hung at start-up, and
    every static LLD link with a direct bitcode input was refused as if the
    bitcode were a linker script. Bitcode (raw and wrapped) is recognized in
    inputs and archive members and never read as a script; a link whose
    trace names bitcode runs again through LLD with `--lto-obj-path`, that
    link is checked and installed, and the objects LLD compiled are read as
    loaded inputs. The outline-atomics member is refused by name
    (`[TCG-LINK-IRELATIVE-UNAPPLIED]`), and static full, ThinLTO and archive
    bitcode links are installed and run. A static link whose compiled
    objects are not shown (a ThinLTO cache, its own `obj-path`, another
    linker) is refused by name. Decision LD-07.
  - LIMITATIONS no longer says the page-granular rule is not implemented.
  - The repair's first verifier found two holes, both closed now. First, a
    GNU ld `-z nosectionheader` image skipped the thread-local section rules.
    Its `.tbss`-first `PHDRS` layout let trust-cg's zero-fill thread-local
    read 42. An image without section headers that has a `PT_TLS` with
    memory is now refused. Second, trust-cg's `.eh_frame` in a segment
    without read permission was installed through LLD and gold, and those
    programs died with SIGSEGV at their first `backtrace`. The read rule now
    sees LLD's own `.eh_frame` pieces and gold's merged `** eh_frame` data.
    The reasons for two conservative thread-local refusals now say they are
    conservative: LLD and gold measure offsets from `p_vaddr`, and the
    check does not show that a template's file bytes are in memory past a
    `PT_LOAD`'s file part.
  - The repair found a third class. Through GNU ld and LLD, trust-cg's
    `.data` in no segment in an image without section headers, and its
    `.rodata` marked `(NOLOAD)`, were installed, and their programs read 0.
    trust-cg's own sections are now held to the loaded-bytes rules where
    the map places them (`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]`): in a `PT_LOAD`'s
    memory, in its file part when they have contents, and over zero bytes
    when they are zero fill.

- Calls through an unsigned variadic declaration are refused by name. The
  Trust producer publishes a C callee it cannot sign (the variadic `fcntl`,
  the non-variadic `posix_spawn_file_actions_*`) as `(...) -> (i32)`, which
  the adapter lowered as `CallVariadic { fixed_args: 0 }`; under DarwinPCS
  that passes every argument on the stack, and `fcntl(fd, F_SETFD,
  FD_CLOEXEC)` measured as a silent `F_DUPFD` (Trust run-make
  `trust-cg-f1-c-callee-abi`). `AdapterError::UnsignedVariadicCallee`
  (`[TCG-UNSIGNED-VARIADIC]`, shared predicate
  `trust_cg_lower::reject_unsigned_variadic_callee`) now refuses a direct call
  or invoke whose callee is variadic with `params: []`, or variadic under
  `CallingConv::Rust`, on every adapter entry and target, before intrinsic
  recognition and before any output gate; the wasm lane names it the same
  way. A variadic declaration that states its fixed prefix still lowers to
  `CallVariadic { fixed_args: params.len() }`. Decision OD-55.

- Call edges into a variadic callee that carry no fixed/anonymous split are
  refused by name (review of OD-55, decision OD-56). An invoke of a variadic
  callee is admitted only under base AAPCS64, named by both the TLS dialect
  and the module's declared triple: x86-64 shipped one without `AL` (a
  callee prologue that tests it skips saving the vector argument registers),
  and `TlsDialect::RejectThreadLocals` or an ELF dialect beside an Apple
  triple let a Darwin one through. A non-variadic `CallIndirect` whose pointer
  visibly names a variadic declaration (`SymbolAddr("fcntl")`, a reified
  `FnDef`) is refused: `[TCG-UNSIGNED-VARIADIC]` for an unsigned declaration,
  `[TCG-VARARG-ABI]` otherwise. The LLVM importer now carries each direct
  call's own function type: an unprototyped `declare R @f(...)` takes the
  type its calls state (clang's K&R calls, which were refused since OD-55 and
  lowered with zero fixed arguments on Darwin before it), and a call whose
  split differs from its callee's signature, such as
  `call i32 (i32, i32, ...) @f` against `declare i32 @f(i32, ...)`, is
  refused instead of lowered by the declaration's split.

- Decisions are taken, not deferred. `docs/decision-record.md` (formerly
  `docs/aarch64-owner-decisions.md`) records every open design choice as a
  dated ruling with its reasoning and remaining work; agents take the
  fail-closed, reversible option instead of waiting. Rulings applied with this
  change: the public-release gate runs `check_companion_coherence.py` on every
  AArch64 host, both native floors with `--require-offline-deps`, the Darwin
  bridge runner (`darwin-aarch64-bridge`) on Darwin, and on Linux AArch64 the
  48-case AOT arithmetic matrix against a CLI the lane builds from the tree
  (an exclusion without AY and Clean). `benchmarks/beat-llvm/contract/gates.json`
  version 4 nulls the program peak-RSS geomean, and a ledger row's per-program
  RSS ratio, when a comparison is floor-bound. The rustc MIR inventory parser
  refuses an unknown state word instead of dropping the row. The Linux x86-64
  floor requires `e2e_x86_64_swiftcc` again. The TY/TLC contract 0.1.0 is
  approved before any measurement and stays out of the public snapshot.
- Cache privacy under umask 0002, the rest of the writers (X-HOST-P13
  closure audit, 2026-10-03). The 2026-09-26 repair made every directory
  trust-cg itself creates under `<cache>/trust-cg` `0700`, but three gate
  scripts added afterwards still created theirs with the umask's mode: on a
  fresh cache under umask `0002` each made `<cache>/trust-cg` `0775`, and AY
  was then refused in every later process (`TCG-AY-IDENTITY-UNMATERIALIZED`).
  The first repair's verification found two more writers under those caches
  that kept the caller's umask (the soundness gate's Clean lane in its pinned
  checkout, and the x86-64 legs in the remote clone); both now write under
  umask 077 as well.
  - **One rule for scripts.** `scripts/private_cache.py` is the scripts' copy
    of `private_fs`: each directory it creates is exactly `0700` whatever the
    umask (made under umask 077; a set-group-ID bit a parent passes on is
    cleared through a descriptor opened without following a symlink; a new
    directory that cannot be made private is removed and the call fails),
    files are created exclusively `0600`, an existing directory is never
    changed, and its ownership and ancestor checks are `private_fs`'s. A
    default POSIX ACL overrides the umask for what is created in a directory
    that has one, so each directory the helper creates drops the default ACL
    it inherited (Linux; a directory that already has one keeps it, and no
    macOS ACL is removed). `soundness_check.sh` creates `SOUNDNESS_DEPS_DIR`
    through it, writes each pinned checkout under umask 077, and runs the
    Clean lane (its Cargo builds and tests, and `clean check`) under umask
    077 through one runner, `run_clean_bounded`, in whichever Clean checkout
    it uses. `check_x86_icmp_certificates.py`
    creates `ay-cli`, its slots and its lock files through it and builds AY
    under umask 077 (the export `tar.umask=0077`, the binary `0500`).
    `soundness_remote.sh` sends its source with the remote script, creates the
    executor's clone and `incoming` directories through it, initializes,
    fetches and checks out the clone, runs the x86-64 legs (their build tree,
    Python caches and record) and writes both bundles under umask 077, and
    `send_file` runs under umask 077.
  - **The icmp slot is checked, not trusted.** A slot's identity record sits
    beside the binary it names, so a warm slot is refused
    (`ay-cache-not-private`, with the remedy) when the cache directory has an
    ancestor another user may rename entries in, or the slot, binary or record
    is writable by another user (a group or other write bit), or the slot is
    a symlink; the slot is checked again after a cold build. Before, a binary
    planted with a matching record in a `0775` slot was returned as the
    pinned AY. Read and execute bits are allowed, so a slot the earlier
    script built under umask 0022 (`0755` slot, `0555` binary, `0644` record)
    is reused as it is; one it built under umask 0002 is group-writable and is
    refused with the remedy, deleting the slot (the next run rebuilds it in
    about ten minutes). The first version of this repair refused any group or
    other bit on the binary and record, which falsely refused the umask-0022
    slot with a message ("another user could replace its contents") that was
    wrong for it.
  - **The remote's arguments.** ssh joins its arguments into one command line,
    which dropped an empty `SOUNDNESS_X86_REMOTE_DIR` and shifted the rest:
    with it unset, the remote probe stopped on `$1: unbound variable` (or
    created `~/trust`) and `run` read the commit as the clone directory. The
    arguments are now quoted into that line, and the fixture's fake ssh joins
    them as OpenSSH does. The quoting also stopped the remote shell from
    expanding a `~` in `SOUNDNESS_X86_REMOTE_DIR` (`~/tcg-x86` would have
    become a directory named `~` in the remote HOME), so the remote script
    reads a leading `~/` as the remote HOME itself, as the unquoted argument
    was read before; a relative path is read below the remote HOME, and a path
    with spaces now arrives whole.
  - **Rust writers.** The solver-identity memo is written through
    `private_fs::create_private_file` (`0600`; `std::fs::write` made it
    `0664`), and a temporary at its name is removed first instead of written
    through. The JIT IR text cache (`trust-cg/jit`, with
    `TRUST_CG_JIT_DISK_CACHE`) and the test-only executable-buffer disk tier
    write their entries `0600` (`File::create` made them `0664`). Unit tests of
    `trust-cg-verify` write the memo only under an explicit
    `TCG_PROOF_CACHE_DIR`; a test run had left 8 fixture identities in
    `~/.cache/trust-cg/solver-identity-v1`.
  - **Diagnosable CEGIS.** `PipelineError::CegisIncomplete` carries
    `ay_refusal` (`ay_bridge::solver_refusal_note`), so a CEGIS-enabled
    compile that fails because AY cannot run names the AY refusal, its
    directory, mode and remedy. A build that records no AY carries none.
  - **Tests.** `scripts/tests/test_private_cache.py` pins the rule under six
    umasks, a set-group-ID parent, an inherited default ACL and an injected
    mode-fix failure, and runs under umask 0002 with a fresh cache:
    `soundness_check.sh --attest --preflight-only`; a whole attested run of
    the soundness fixture, after which no entry under `<cache>/trust-cg` (the
    Clean lane's `target/` included) or under the fixture remote's
    `~/.cache/trust-cg` (the clone with the legs' Python caches and record)
    has a group or other bit; the icmp cache warm, as the earlier script left
    it under umask 0022 and 0002, through a symlink, and cold (`build_ay`,
    with a fixture AY repository and a fixture targo that writes its target
    tree with the umask's modes, under a set-group-ID cache directory, and
    with an ancestor loosened during the build). `test_soundness_remote.py`
    holds the remote side, a `~/` remote directory with a space included. The
    `private_fs` fixture that failed under umask 0002
    (`canonical_private_directory_...`) makes its scratch directory `0700`,
    and the test's umask-0002 child now makes its own scratch directory, so
    the child's run is what checks that fixture.
  - **Measured** (this Linux AArch64 host, umask `0002`, a fresh `0700`
    `XDG_CACHE_HOME`; AY admission read with `trust-cg --print-ay-identity`,
    which runs no AY; 280ea37bf against this change).
    `soundness_check.sh --attest --preflight-only` (SOUNDNESS_DEPS_DIR at its
    default): `trust-cg`, `soundness-deps` and the pinned AY checkout were
    `0775`, all 15,289 non-symlink checkout entries had group or other bits,
    and AY was refused; now all three are `0700`, no entry has a group or
    other bit, and AY is admitted. `check_x86_icmp_certificates.py ay-path`
    with an absent AY source: `trust-cg` and `ay-cli` `0775` and a `0664`
    lock, AY refused; now `0700`, `0700`, `0600`, AY admitted. A planted
    `0775` slot (a shell script and a record naming its digest) was returned
    with exit 0; now `ay-cache-not-private`, exit 1. The remote side through
    an ssh stand-in that joins arguments as OpenSSH does, remote umask
    `0002`, fresh `0700` HOME: the probe stopped on the dropped argument and
    `send_file` left `.cache`, `trust-cg`, `soundness-remote` and `incoming`
    `0775` and the bundle `0664`, AY refused under that HOME; now the probe
    creates them (and the clone directory) `0700`, the bundle is `0600`, and
    AY is admitted. `e2e_cegis_superopt` under a `0775` `trust-cg`: 5 of 11
    fail, each naming `TCG-AY-IDENTITY-UNMATERIALIZED` (the audit counted 0
    mentions); with a private cache 11 of 11 pass. The `trust-cg-process-env`
    lib tests pass 49 of 49 under umask `0002` and `0022`, its 9 `private_fs`
    rows included (8 of 9 at 280ea37bf under `0002`); the JIT IR cache entry
    was `0664` at 280ea37bf (the new row fails there) and is `0600`.
  - **Measured after the verification** (same host and method; 4dcfb9787,
    the first version of this repair, against this change). The soundness
    gate's own `pin_dependency_checkout` and Clean lane, evaluated verbatim,
    pinning Clean `3c82461c` and running `cargo check --locked -p
    clean-kernel` in it: at 4dcfb9787 its `target/` held 1,130 group-writable
    entries (the verification's count); now none of the 36,472 non-symlink entries under
    `<cache>/trust-cg` has a group or other write bit, three (zstd-sys headers
    its build script copies with their source's `0644`) have read bits, and
    AY is admitted. A cache base with a default ACL (`u::rwx,g::rwx,o::rx`):
    all 35,337 entries of the pinned checkout were group-writable at
    4dcfb9787; now none is, and no directory the helper made keeps a default
    ACL (AY was admitted in both, since none of them is an ancestor of
    `ay-exec`). The icmp slot as the 280ea37bf script left it under umask
    0022: refused at 4dcfb9787, now warm (exit 0) under umask 0002, 0022 and
    0077 with nothing changed; left under umask 0002 it is refused and names
    `delete <slot> to rebuild`. A real cold AY build (`ay-path --ay-source
    ~/ay --keep-build`, umask 0002, a fresh cache whose `ay-cli` is
    set-group-ID) took 12 minutes and exited 0; none of its 17,670
    non-symlink entries has a group or other bit, the slot is exactly `0700`,
    the binary `0500`, record and lock `0600`; the warm re-run exits 0 and AY
    is admitted. Through the OpenSSH-like stand-in (dash login shell, remote
    umask 0002), `SOUNDNESS_X86_REMOTE_DIR='~/tcg-x86'`, which made
    `$HOME/~/tcg-x86` at 4dcfb9787 (the verification's probe), makes `$HOME/tcg-x86` (`0700`); a
    relative and an absolute path with spaces arrive whole. The x86-64 legs'
    writes are measured through the fixture only (no x86-64 host here): with
    the legs under the login umask, as at 4dcfb9787, the clone's Python caches
    and record objects carry group or other bits and the tests fail. Of 27
    single changes that remove or weaken a step of this rule in the scripts
    (the verification's 5 surviving mutations of the cold build, 10 for
    this round, 12 earlier ones), every one fails
    `test_private_cache`, `test_soundness_remote` or
    `test_check_x86_icmp_certificates` under umask 0002, and each of the four
    scripts as of 4dcfb9787 fails them too. Dropping `scratch()`'s `0700` now

    `test_private_cache`, `test_soundness_remote`,
    `test_check_x86_icmp_certificates`, `test_gate_env`,
    `test_soundness_leg_inventory`, `test_soundness_attestation`,
    `test_soundness_capture`) pass under umask 0002, 0022 and 0077, with one
