- One user-cache rule for every reader (X-HOST-P13 second closure audit,
  2026-10-03; ruling LD-18). Each function-verification
  request froze `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `HOME` anchored to its working
  directory, so with an empty or relative `XDG_CACHE_HOME` (or an empty
  `HOME`) AY's private copy was resolved below the working directory inside
  every request, while `trust-cg --print-ay-identity`, the Linux floor's
  `--require-proof-tools` preflight and the refusal note resolved
  `$HOME/.cache` and reported AY admitted.
  - **The rule.** `private_fs::user_cache_base` (and
    `scripts/private_cache.py` `user_cache_base`, same rows and refusal
    texts) resolves every trust-cg cache root: an absolute `XDG_CACHE_HOME`,
    else an absolute `HOME`'s `.cache`, else no cache; an empty or relative
    `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is ignored (a leading space makes a value relative; an
    absolute value is used exactly as given, a trailing space included).
    AY's private copy, the
    solver-identity memo, the default Alethe certificate store, the CEGIS
    cache, the JIT IR and buffer caches, the soundness gate's
    `soundness-deps` and the icmp gate's `ay-cli` all use it. A request
    freezes `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `HOME` as given; only the explicit
    `TCG_PROOF_CERT_STORE` and `TCG_PROOF_CACHE_DIR` keep their
    working-directory meaning. With a relative or empty `HOME` and no
    absolute `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, AY is refused alike by every reader
    (`TCG-AY-IDENTITY-UNMATERIALIZED`, `HOME= is not absolute`).
  - **Soundness gate.** `soundness_check.sh` refuses, never repairs, a
    `soundness-deps` directory before a checkout is written into it, a
    pinned checkout before it is used, and the built Clean binary and its
    directory before any Clean check runs, when another user could rename
    entries in them or write the binary (`private_cache.py
    require-private`, the rule the icmp gate holds `ay-cli` to). Before, a
    pre-existing `0777` `trust-cg` and `soundness-deps` gave a green attested
    run with Clean built and run below them.
  - **Remote directory names.** `soundness_remote.sh` refuses a
    `SOUNDNESS_X86_REMOTE_DIR`, and any remote argument, with a character
    outside `[A-Za-z0-9 ~/._+,:@=-]`: bash's `%q` writes such characters as
    `$'...'`, and a dash login shell ran the tail of a value holding a tab
    and a quote as commands.
  - **Test fixtures.** `proof_gate_strict`'s
    `a_real_proof_check_records_the_tools_that_ran` gives its child a `0700`
    `XDG_CACHE_HOME` (tempfile's `0775` under umask 0002 refused AY there and
    failed that attested-gate leg); the Darwin `fixed_cost_budget_aarch64`
    workdir is `0700` (not run here: macOS only). `test_private_cache` pins
    `create_private_file`'s `fchmod` under umasks 0277, 0377 and 0477. New
    floor row `trust-cg-verify/ay_cache_root_agreement` (Linux floor; also a
    Darwin floor row, not yet run on a Darwin host): under umask 0002,
    0022 and 0077, empty, relative, unset and absolute `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, a
    `0775` and a `0700` working directory, a relative and an empty `HOME` and
    an `XDG_CACHE_HOME` below a `0775` directory, process-level admission and
    a function-verification request admit the same single private copy or
    refuse alike, the note carries the refusal, and nothing is written in the
    working directory.
  - **Measured** (this Linux AArch64 host, 64932ffd7 against this change; a
    fresh private case directory, HOME and TMPDIR per case).
    `jit_cert_cache_identity_aarch64` under umask 0002 with a `0775`
    working directory: 0/9 at 64932ffd7 with `XDG_CACHE_HOME` empty or
    relative (no `TCG-AY-IDENTITY` mention; `ay-exec` created in the working
    directory) while `--print-ay-identity` admitted AY, now 9/9; with an
    empty `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and a `0700` (umask 0002) or `0755` (umask 0022)
    working directory it passed but wrote a second 655,359,032-byte AY copy
    there, now none. Now 9/9 under umask 0002, 0022 and 0077 for absolute,
    unset, empty and relative `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, one copy under the resolved
    cache, no cache entry with a group or other bit, nothing in the working
    directory; with an empty `HOME` both the CLI and the target refuse
    (0/9, each failure naming `TCG-AY-IDENTITY-UNMATERIALIZED`).
    `jit_fail_closed_proof_policy` (3/8 at 64932ffd7 with an empty or
    relative `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and a `0775` working directory) and
    `jit_source_bound_arithmetic` (0/4 there) now pass 8/8 and 4/4, and
    `e2e_cegis_superopt` 11/11, under umask 0002 (absolute, empty and
    relative `XDG_CACHE_HOME`), 0022 (absolute, empty) and 0077 (absolute,
    relative); at 64932ffd7 the CEGIS
    target with a relative `XDG_CACHE_HOME` also wrote its CEGIS cache and
    Alethe certificates below the working directory, now nothing. A
    proof-required `trust-cg -c --emit-proofs` with an empty `HOME`: at
    64932ffd7 its refusal said no AY was admitted while its requests wrote a
    655 MB AY copy to `<cwd>/.cache`; now the refusal is the same and nothing
    is written. The floor's own admission check (`ay_admission`, which
    `--require-proof-tools` runs) answers as before in each of these
    environments; the targets now agree with it.
    `proof_gate_strict --exact a_real_proof_check_records_the_tools_that_ran`
    (`TRUST_CG_RUN_FORMAL_PROOF_TESTS=1`): fails at 64932ffd7 under umask
    0002 (the child refuses AY beneath its `0775` tempdir), passes under
    0002, 0022 and 0077. `ay_cache_root_agreement` passes under 0002, 0022
    and 0077. Each of 8 Rust mutations (the request anchoring
    `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `HOME` again; `user_cache_base` accepting a relative
    value; the certificate store, CEGIS cache, solver-identity memo and both
    JIT caches reading a relative value; `proof_gate_strict`'s child cache
    back to tempfile's mode) is killed by its test under umask 0002. Each of
    10 script mutations (the `fchmod`, the three
    soundness-gate checks, the remote character check, the cache-base rule,
    the icmp default, two halves of `require_private`, the deps default) is
    killed by its test under umask 0002, and the nine touched script suites
    (336 tests, 2 skips) pass under umask 0002, 0022 and 0077.

- L02-P15 (LLVM importer reads names, strings, metadata and module flags as
  LLVM decodes them; testing evidence, AArch64 Linux): LLVM decodes the
  `\XX` and `\\` escapes of every quoted name, metadata name and string
  before it reads it, while the importer matched raw spellings, so
  LLVM-valid text was read differently. One decoder with LLVM's
  `UnEscapeLexed` rules now serves every reader. Before any reader runs,
  every quoted name and metadata name is rewritten to the spelling of its
  decoded name (`lexical::canonicalize`): `!\65xclude` is `!exclude` and is
  refused like it (llc's `SHF_EXCLUDE` section was linked from the imported
  object; `!\6Bcfi_type` lost its hash word), `@"foo"`, `@"\66oo"` and
  `@foo` are one symbol (the imported object used to define `"foo"`, quotes
  included), and `%"x"` and `%x` one value. A symbol name that is no plain
  LLVM name after decoding is carried only for an internal or private
  definition, a name decoding to NUL and an empty quoted name are refused,
  and a `\01` asm label is read only under an Apple `target triple` (on ELF
  llc writes `_foo` where the importer wrote `foo`). Attribute keys and
  values are decoded before they are checked:
  `"target-features"="+v8a\2C+call-saved-x9"` hid a refused mode feature,
  and the imported callee clobbered x9, which the llc-built caller relied on
  (wrong code, 24 of 24 configurations), and `-fp-armv8` behind the same
  escape was admitted. Named metadata and module flags llc acts on are read
  or refused by name (`crates/trust-cg-llvm-import/src/metadata.rs`, from a
  survey of LLVM 22's readers): `!llvm.dependent-libraries` (llc's
  `.deplibs` made LLD link libm; the imported object did not),
  `!llvm.linker.options` and the other names llc reads are refused,
  `!llvm.ident`, `!llvm.commandline` and `!llvm.dbg.cu` are read; the module
  flags clang writes that change nothing the importer builds are read, and
  every other flag is refused by name, the `stack-protector-guard` flags
  among them (llc read the canary from `sp_el0` and trapped where the
  imported build read `__stack_chk_guard`). `"branch-target-enforcement"` is
  refused in every form: llc 22 builds BTI landing pads whenever it is
  present, `"false"` included, unless the module states an ARM or AArch64
  triple. Module flags, metadata references, attribute values and literals
  LLVM's parser or verifier rejects are refused (a duplicated or malformed
  flag, an undefined `!N`, an empty or unsigned target feature, a
  `frame-pointer`, `denormal-fp-math`, `warn-stack-size` or
  `sign-return-address-key` value LLVM does not read, `probe-stack` other
  than `inline-asm` or Apple's `__chkstk_darwin`, a `stack-probe-size` that
  is no plain decimal, `ret double 2`, `float 0.1`, `float
  0x3FB999999999999A`, `i32 0x10`, `double inf`), as is a global defined in
  section `llvm.metadata`, which llc does not emit. Upstream llc 22 aborts
  on `__chkstk_darwin`, which the importer admits as Apple's LLVM reads it:
  the one spelling admitted where upstream llc refuses the module. Evidence:
  unit tests in `parser.rs` (56 of 57 mutants of this change's decisions
  killed; the survivor disabled a redundant branch, since removed); the
  verifier's reproducers all refused by name; the importer's suite (355
  tests, `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`GOLD`/`LLC`, no skip); a recount of the 1,177
  texts the base's and this change's tests import, with the 10 in-tree `.ll`
  files, in which no text both suites import and no in-tree file changes
  verdict and one shared text's module changes (`@"g"` is now `g`), and of
  2,039 `opt` prints and rustc modules, which change only with their
  originals; 50,000 token mutants without a panic; and an llc differential
  over 247 generated modules (llc 22.1.2, one C driver, GNU ld 2.42, gold
  1.16 and LLD 22.1.6, O0-O3, static and PIE, 2,496 compared
  configurations): 104 equal to llc, 142 refused by name, one
  (`__chkstk_darwin`) imported where upstream llc aborts, none different;
  the base differed on 29 and imported 37 llc rejects. Rerun, the verifier's
  and L02-P13's corpora (355 modules) differ only where they did before this
  row (a deep `tail call` recursion at O0/O1, three overflowing `ssp`
  frames).
  First verifier round, repaired: a `half` literal's `0xH` NaN was read as
  a positive quiet NaN, losing its sign, payload and signaling bit (old
  code, contradicting the claim above): `ret half 0xHFE00` returned
  `0x7e00` where llc's build returns `0xfe00`, on `aarch64-apple-darwin`
  and, through store, return, phi and `fadd`, on Linux with the FP16
  profile (the default Linux profile refuses every `half` constant at
  instruction selection, which hid it from the first differential). A
  `0xH` NaN now keeps its sign and payload, and a signaling one is refused
  as the double spelling's is. A module flag's integer is read as LLVM's
  `iN` constant (`i8 255` is -1, `i1 2` is 0) after the parser's behavior
  upgrades (`PIC Level` error/max to min, `PIE Level` error to max, branch
  protection error to min), so `!{i32 1, !"PIC Level", i32 -1}`, its
  behavior-7 twin and `!{i32 8, !"PIC Level", i8 255}`, which llc rejects,
  are refused. A `!DICompileUnit`, a `!DIAssignID` or a defining
  `!DISubprogram` without `distinct`, which LLVM's parser rejects, is
  refused (a non-distinct compile unit in `!llvm.dbg.cu` imported); the
  debug records are otherwise not validated. Read now: `ptrauth-elf-got`
  and `ptrauth-sign-personality` at 0 (llc acts on each only at 1; clang 22
  writes them only when on, and later clang's modules are refused, below),
  and an empty `!llvm.dependent-libraries` or
  `!llvm.linker.options`. Tests kill the
  verifier's surviving mutants (an escaped COMDAT name, a leading-digit
  metadata name, two `half` exactness checks, the second
  `true`/`false`/`null` float site, three named-metadata refusals).
  Evidence: unit tests (251; each new case also run through llc 22.1.2,
  which accepts or rejects it as the test states); 40 mutants of the
  repair's decisions and the verifier's survivors, all killed; the suite
  (358 tests, `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`GOLD`/`LLC`, no skip); an llc differential
  over 174 generated modules (`half` literals in nine shapes with the FP16
  profile and `+fullfp16`, module flags, `distinct` nodes, escaped names;
  O0-O3, GNU ld, gold and LLD, static and PIE; 2,496 compared
  configurations): 104 equal, 70 refused by name, none different, where the
  base differed on 36 and imported 21 llc rejects; on
  `aarch64-apple-darwin` (eight `ret half` literals, O0-O3), the base's
  constant differed from llc's in 24 of 32 objects, and now 24 are equal
  and the eight with a signaling literal are refused; the
  earlier corpora (651 modules) keep every verdict but the first round's
  three llc rejects, now refused; and a recount of 1,246 texts in which no
  in-tree file and no text both suites import changes verdict or module.
  Second verifier round, repaired: the first repair read a
  `stack-probe-size` module flag unsigned at its width, which admitted `i64
  -4096` and `i64 -1` (refused before as negative literals). LLVM 22 reads
  the interval, flag or attribute, as a `uint64_t` it asserts is positive as
  an `int64_t`; with `"probe-stack"="inline-asm"` and a 300000-byte frame,
  llc 22.1.2's build crashed (SIGSEGV) in all 24 configurations where the
  imported one printed `f=7`, as it did for the positive spellings at or
  above 2^63 and the attribute `"18446744073709547520"`, admitted since the
  row began. The flag and the attribute now share one predicate, 4096 to
  2^63 - 1, the flag read at its width (`i16 61440` is 61440). A
  `!DISubprogram`'s `spFlags` is read in every spelling LLVM's parser reads,
  `u0x` hexadecimal included (`spFlags: u0x8` without `distinct` imported
  where llc rejects it), and one it rejects is refused. The
  `!stack-protector` instruction attachment, which llc's stack protector
  reads (no canary for an alloca marked `!{i32 0}`), is refused by name
  instead of dropped. Refusal reasons now state what llc does: a
  non-`!DICompileUnit` `!llvm.dbg.cu` operand and any other `!llvm.dbg.`
  name are debug information llc drops with a warning, and a `u0x`/`s0x`
  module-flag integer is one LLVM reads and the importer does not.
  `PIC Level`, read as before, does change llc's AArch64 build of an `ssp`
  function: at 0, or without the flag, llc addresses `__stack_chk_guard`
  PC-relative, and its object did not link into a GNU ld PIE or a GNU ld or
  LLD shared object, where the imported one, which always uses the GOT,
  linked and ran; no run differed otherwise. Later clang (upstream clang at
  2f8eb5b4be, and at least since 2026-07-24, before that commit) writes the
  two pointer-authentication flags read at 0 together
  with `ptrauth-init-fini`, its address-discrimination twin and, on Linux,
  the `aarch64-elf-pauthabi-platform`/`-version` pair, which llc writes into
  a `.note.gnu.property` property even at version 0; such a module is
  refused. Tests kill the round's surviving mutants (`Code Model` `i1 true`
  and `stack-probe-size` `i16 61440` read unsigned, the definition bit among
  others, the `PIE Level`, `PIC Level` and branch-protection upgrades only
  from the behaviors LLVM upgrades). Evidence: unit tests (252; each new
  case also run through llc 22.1.2, 61 texts); 28 mutants of the repair's
  decisions and the verifier's survivors, all killed; the suite (359 tests,
  `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`GOLD`/`LLC`, no skip); an llc differential over 59
  generated modules (O0-O3, GNU ld, gold and LLD, static and PIE
  executables and shared objects; 552 compared configurations): 20 equal,
  34 refused by name, and 5 where only llc's object failed to link, where
  the first repair differed on 12 (six crashing stack-probe intervals, six
  llc link failures) and imported 7 llc rejects; the earlier
  corpora (1,422 modules), rerun with both importers, keep every verdict but
  twelve of the second round's, now refused (six crashing stack-probe
  intervals, two `spFlags` llc rejects, four that ran equal); and a recount
  of 1,301 texts in which no in-tree file and no text both suites import
  changes verdict or module.
  Third verifier round, repaired: on an Apple triple, a `\01` asm label
  whose name after `\01_` holds a byte outside `[-a-zA-Z$._0-9]` was
  written into the Mach-O symbol table with the canonical escapes
  (`_a\20b`, `_caf\C3\A9`) where llc writes the decoded bytes (`_a b`,
  `_café`), for a definition, a global and a called declaration (the second
  repair's canonical spelling; the base wrote `_g v` correctly). Such a
  label is now a quoted name under the documented rule: carried only for an
  internal or private definition, and one symbol with the plain `@"a b"`
  for the collision check (LD-03). `"target-cpu"` and `"tune-cpu"` of
  `thunderx3t110` are refused by name: LLVM 22's tuning for it implies
  `strict-align`, which `+strict-align` is refused for, and llc then loads
  an unaligned value byte by byte; an enumeration of LLVM 22.1.2's AArch64,
  x86 and RISC-V processor tables (with `llvm-tblgen`) and an llc sweep of
  every AArch64 name found no other processor implying a refused feature,
  and the claim that a processor's features only add instructions is
  corrected (LD-04, pre-existing from L02-P13). Text llc rejects in what the
  importer's readers decide is refused: a `"sign-return-address-key"`
  without `"sign-return-address"` among a function's or call's attributes,
  an `isDefinition` other than `true`/`false`, and a `distinct` inside
  another node (LD-05). Wording: `getZExtValue` asserts on a value needing
  more than 64 bits, not on the constant's type (`i128 8192` is read); the
  later-clang pointer-authentication flags predate 2f8eb5b4be. Evidence:
  unit tests (255; their 118 new texts and 82 probe texts also run through
  llc 22.1.2: no text llc rejects is imported, where the second repair
  imported 21 of the probe's); 28 mutants of
  the repair's decisions, all killed; the suite (362 tests,
  `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`GOLD`/`LLC`, no skip); identical non-local symbols to
  llc's for every admitted probe text on `arm64-apple-macosx14.0.0` and
  AArch64 Linux (68 object pairs); an llc differential over 58 generated
  modules (O0-O3, GNU ld, gold and LLD, static and PIE; 816 compared
  configurations): 34 equal, 24 refused by name, none different, where the
  second repair imported 13 llc rejects; the earlier corpora (1,540
  modules, the third verifier round's 59 among them), rerun with both
  importers, keep every verdict and refusal message; and a recount of 1,419
  texts in which no in-tree file and no text both suites import changes
  verdict, module or message.
  Fourth verifier round, repaired: `"target-features"="+thunderx3t110"`
  was read, though llc sets every feature a `+feature` implies and that
  tuning feature implies `strict-align` (llc loaded an unaligned `i64` byte
  by byte for it); every feature and processor whose `Implies` closure
  holds a refused feature is now refused, and both tables are derived by a
  unit test from a committed extract of LLVM 22.1.2's AArch64, RISC-V and
  x86 tables (`scripts/extract_llvm_subtarget_features.py`), in which only
  `thunderx3t110` qualifies (LD-04). On an Apple triple, the name after a
  `\01_` label was quoted only when it held an escape, so `@"\01_1x"` (`1x`)
  and the plain `@"1x"` (`"1x"`), one Mach-O symbol `_1x` to llc, escaped
  the collision check: llc bound a call of the label to an internal
  `@"1x"` where the importer left `_1x` undefined, and two definitions
  that llc rejects were imported. The name after `\01_` is now read as the
  plain `@"S"` is, so a label that starts with a digit or is empty is a
  quoted name too, carried only for an internal or private definition
  (LD-03; an external `@"\01_1x"`, written as llc writes it before, is now
  refused). A numbered symbol (`@0`), which the importer wrote as `0` where
  llc writes `__unnamed_N`, is carried only for an internal or private
  definition, and a module with one refuses a name holding `__unnamed_`
  (LD-08; pre-existing: mixed links with llc's objects failed). The
  signing checks reach the calls the importer drops (`llvm.assume`,
  `llvm.lifetime.*`), which it imported though llc rejects them, and no
  longer refuse an `llvm.*` declaration with the key alone, whose
  attributes LLVM's parser replaces (LD-05, whose "removes nothing llc
  accepts" is corrected); a `!DISubprogram` with `isDefinition` or
  `spFlags` written twice is refused. Two tests in `entry_block_any_label.rs`
  that wrote one temporary file now write their own. Evidence: unit tests
  (259; their 70 new texts also run through llc 22.1.2, which rejects 20,
  all refused); 33 mutants of the repair's decisions, 32 killed and one
  equivalent (a field's first or last occurrence, now that a field written
  twice is refused first); the suite (366 tests, `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`GOLD`/
  `LLC`, no skip); importer tippy clean; the extract reproduced from LLVM's
  sources (`--check`); the verifier's 52 reproducers and an 86-text probe
  through llc and both importers (llc rejects 20: 18 refused, and two
  `llvm.*` declarations that are no intrinsic to LLVM, `@llvm.foo` and
  `@llvm.assume(i64)`, import with the key alone, as stated in LD-05; of
  its 66 accepts, 33 import with the same non-local
  symbols as llc's, undefined ones included, on `arm64-apple-macosx14.0.0`
  and AArch64 Linux at O0 and O2, and 33 are refused by name, five of them
  over-refusals stated in LD-03); an llc differential over 37 generated
  modules (O0-O3, GNU ld, gold and LLD, static and PIE; 408 compared
  configurations): 17 equal, 20 refused by name, none different, where the
  third repair differed on 3 and imported 9 llc rejects; the earlier
  corpora (1,598 modules, 18,252 configurations), rerun with both
  importers, keep every verdict and refusal message; and a recount of
  1,489 texts in which no in-tree file changes, two shared texts (external
  `@"\01_1x"` and `@"\01_"`) are now refused, and two `opt -S` prints of
  `@0 = global i64 1` are refused; no rustc module changes.
  Fifth verifier round, repaired (each pre-existing, but the declaration
  exemption): outside an Apple triple llc names a private `@X` `.LX` and
  reads every `.L` name as an assembler temporary, so it bound a call or
  load of a declared `@.Lfoo` to a private `@foo` (14 and 22 where the
  importer's build printed 107 and 1011 against a peer, or did not link);
  every symbol that is not private is now refused under a `.L` name
  (ruling "A name starting with `.L` outside an Apple triple"). A Mach-O
  `\01_llvm.*` label, an ordinary function to LLVM, was read as the
  intrinsic (calls dropped, lowered inline or sent to libm's `_sin`, and the
  declaration exemption applied); such a label is refused, the exemption
  reads the IR name, and the calls the importer drops or lowers as
  `memcpy`/`memmove`/`memset` are matched as LLVM names intrinsics, so
  `@llvm.assumex`, `@llvm.sideeffect.x`, `@llvm.memcpyx` (ordinary calls
  to llc; 100, 1000 and a changed copy against a C peer where the importer
  printed 0, 0 and a plain copy) and `@llvm.memcpy.inline` (for 4096
  bytes no call in llc's object, `memcpy` in the importer's) are refused
  (ruling "A Mach-O
  `\01_` label spelling an `llvm.` name, and intrinsic names as LLVM
  matches them"). On a RISC-V triple `+e`, `+d` and `+f` select llc's
  calling convention (`RISCVABI::computeTargetABI`) while the backend
  builds `lp64d`: a definition is refused under `lp64e`, and under `lp64`
  or `lp64f` when its text or a named type names a floating-point or
  vector type, and every 32-bit RISC-V definition is refused, with the
  features and processors derived from the committed LLVM extract (ruling
  "The RISC-V calling convention llc selects from a function's features";
  LLVM 22 source and an LLVM 18.1.3 STOCK EXCEPTION run, no RISC-V llc 22
  here). Evidence: unit tests (264); 28 mutants of the repair's decisions,
  27 killed and one survivor (the exemption's IR name read without
  decoding), claimed equivalent and not: a quoted `llvm.` declaration whose
  signature the importer does not model is skipped before the quoted-name
  rule runs (sixth verifier round, below); the suite (371 tests, `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`GOLD`/
  `LLC`, no skip); importer tippy clean; the extract `--check` reproduced;
  an llc differential over 24 modules (O0-O3, GNU ld, gold and LLD, static
  and PIE; 144 compared configurations): 6 equal, 18 refused by name (4
  rejected by llc too), none different, where `4d2d43261` differed on 11
  and imported the 4 llc rejects; the earlier 1,635 modules keep every
  verdict and refusal message (one `ssp` run timed out under host load; its
  executable is byte for byte `4d2d43261`'s and aborted as llc's does in
  reruns); a probe of 166 texts through llc 22.1.2 and both importers (of
  118 llc accepts, 37 newly refused, 7 of them stated over-refusals; the 66
  texts both import give the same module; 42 object pairs of admitted texts
  with llc's non-local symbols, undefined ones included); and a recount of
  1,589 texts in which only 60 of the 100 texts this repair's tests add
  change (55 refused, 5 refused with a new message), and no in-tree file,
  shared text, `opt` print or rustc module changes.
  Sixth verifier round, repaired (each pre-existing): the `.L` and `\01`
  label rules read the triple's OS alone, while llc writes the object
  format LLVM's `Triple` derives (`arm64-apple-macosx14.0.0-elf` is ELF:
  14 and 107, 5 and 9 against peers), and every rule read the module's
  triple where the driver compiles for its `--target` (a triple-less `+e`
  module compiled for `riscv64` got `lp64d`'s registers for arguments 7
  and 8). The importer now takes the compile target
  (`import_text_for_target`, which the driver passes), which takes the
  place of the module's triple as llc's `-mtriple` does, and reads it by
  one function as LLVM 22.1.2's `Triple` does (`src/triple.rs`; compared
  with LLVM's own over 78,128 triples), failing closed with no target
  known (ruling "The compile target and its object format, read as llc
  reads them"). A private `@sin`, `@pow`, ... or `@memset_pattern16`
  captured the call the importer writes for `@llvm.sin.f64` and the
  others, where llc calls libm and names the private symbol `.Lsin`
  (0.479 and 42): such a private symbol is refused (ruling "A private
  symbol named as a call the importer writes in place of an intrinsic").
  `fastcc` is refused for RISC-V and with no target known, where
  `CC_RISCV_FastCC` is not C (ruling "`fastcc` on RISC-V"). The statement
  that llc 22 rejects `e` beside `i` is corrected (its `RISCVISAInfo`
  erases `i` and builds `lp64e`), and the fifth repair's equivalent
  mutant is not: the declaration exemption keeps reading the decoded name,
  as LLVM does (a quoted `@"llvm.fmuladd.a b"` is an intrinsic to it), and
  a test kills the mutant. Evidence: unit tests (268; driver 31); 36
  mutants, 35 killed and one equivalent on this host (the driver's spec
  triple unresolved); the suite (376 tests, `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`GOLD`/
  `LLC`, no skip); importer tippy clean; an llc differential over 24 new
  modules (O0-O3, GNU ld, gold and LLD, static and PIE; 192 compared
  configurations): 8 equal, 15 refused by name, one llc reject imported
  (stated), none different, where `53422d199` differed on 9; the earlier
  1,659 modules keep every verdict (17 refusals reworded); 12 module and
  target pairs at O0 and O2 (Mach-O and Linux), every admitted object (10)
  with llc's non-local symbols, where `53422d199` differed on 6; RISC-V
  objects against LLVM 18.1.3's llc (STOCK EXCEPTION, no program run); a
  probe of 222 texts (18 newly refused, none newly imported, the 81 both
  import unchanged); and a recount of 1,650 texts (one newly imported, a
  `-macho` triple llc writes as Mach-O; 28 newly refused, all but one
  among the added texts; 48 reworded) in which no rustc module changes and
  one triple-less `opt -S` print with `fastcc` is now refused.
  Seventh verifier round, repaired (each pre-existing): LLVM reads an
  overloaded intrinsic's types from its function type and renames it,
  while the importer read the libm function from the name's suffix
  (`@llvm.sin.f32` declared `double (double)`: 0.479426 under llc, 0.5;
  `@llvm.pow.f64` declared `float (float, float)`: 9 and 0); such a name is
  now refused at a declaration and a call, for every overloaded intrinsic
  the importer reads (ruling "An overloaded intrinsic named with type
  suffixes other than its type's"). llc 22's code generator calls library
  functions on its own (`sincos` for a `sin` and `cos` of one operand,
  which an internal `@sincos` received: 42 against 1.357; `cbrt`,
  `bzero`, `memset_pattern16`, the plain functions of fortified calls) and
  replaces calls of others (`sqrt`, `sin`/`cos`, `memcmp`, `mempcpy`): a
  module defining such a name, or a name the importer gives a rewritten
  intrinsic call, is refused whatever its linkage, which supersedes the
  sixth repair's private-only rule and corrects its reasons (ruling "A
  definition under a library name llc's code generator calls or
  replaces"); `@llvm.experimental.memset.pattern.*` is lowered only for
  macOS, iOS, tvOS and watchOS, where llc calls `memset_pattern16`, as llc
  expands a loop elsewhere (ruling "A pattern fill for a target where llc
  calls no `memset_pattern16`"). `import_text` passed over a last
  `target triple` that is not UTF-8 for an earlier one; the last is read
  whatever its bytes and refused by name when not UTF-8, and a test now
  kills the surviving mutant of the no-target RISC-V reading (ruling "The
  compile target and its object format, read as llc reads them"
  corrected). Evidence: unit tests (273; driver 31); 36 mutants of the
  repair's decisions, all killed, the verifier's survivor among them; the
  suite (381 tests, `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`GOLD`/`LLC`, no skip); importer
  tippy clean; llc 22.1.2 probes at O0 and O2 for Linux and Darwin
  triples; an llc differential over 23 new modules (O0-O3, GNU ld, gold
  and LLD, static and PIE; 168 compared configurations): 6 equal, 16
  refused by name and one different, a pre-existing `llvm.objectsize`
  answer LangRef allows (-1 where llc evaluates 16), where `dba826661`
  differed on 12 more; the earlier 1,683 modules keep every verdict but
  five llc builds alike, now refused by the library-name rule (round 6's
  internal and private `sin`/`sinf` controls, L02-P13's `nobuiltin`
  `memcpy` and `memset` loops), and one that hit the run time limit under
  load in the `dba826661` run (18,876 configurations); 6 Mach-O modules at object level (two
  `dba826661` admitted, a `memset_pattern4` and a `bzero` definition, now
  refused); and a recount of 2,052 texts (none newly imported or imported
  otherwise; 369 newly refused, 358 among the added texts; 23 reworded)
  in which no rustc module changes and the triple-less `opt -S` prints of
  an `i32` pattern fill are refused.
- L02-P13 (LLVM importer reads tokens as LLVM does; testing evidence,
  AArch64 Linux): the importer reads one line at a time and splits on
  whitespace, while LLVM's lexer is token-based, so LLVM-valid text could be
  read one way by llc and silently another way here. A second pre-parse pass
  (`crates/trust-cg-llvm-import/src/lexical.rs`) splits the whole module as
  `LLLexer.cpp` does and refuses by name: a NUL, or a carriage return that
  ends no line, outside strings and comments (whitespace to LLVM, part of a
  word here: `define hidden\0` and `internal\0` imported exported and
  interposable functions, `linkonce_odr\0` a strong one, `addrspace\0(1)`
  passed the address-space check), any other control or non-ASCII byte
  there; a keyword, number, name or string glued to the token after it
  (`section"x"` was dropped, `prologue[...]` admitted, `partition"p"`
  admitted); a second top-level entity on a line (`attributes #0 = { ... }
  declare hidden i64 @dh()` dropped the declaration) and an entity
  continued on a later line; a function header continued on a later line
  (`define` alone on its line, which the first version of this pass
  answered with a panic), a body starting on its header line and a closing
  `}` sharing its line; a second instruction on a line (two stores imported
  as one: 1 where llc returns 2), a label sharing its line and an
  instruction continued on a later line, except a `switch` case list; every
  calling convention but `ccc`/`fastcc` on a definition, declaration or
  call, `cc N` included (`preserve_nonecc`, `ghccc`, `cc 10` were lowered as
  C); a numbered ID or integer type spelled with a leading zero, which LLVM
  reads by value and the importer matched by spelling (a function marked
  `#00` lost the `sspstrong` of group `#0`, so its overflow ended in SIGBUS
  where llc's build aborts; `i064` returned nothing); and a metadata
  attachment whose kind llc's code generator or object writer reads
  (`!exclude`, `!associated`, `!section_prefix`, `!absolute_symbol`,
  `!func_sanitize`, `!kcfi_type`, `!pcsections`, `!implicit.ref`: an
  imported `!exclude` global linked where llc's object does not, and
  `!func_sanitize` lost its signature words). `fastcc` is read as C, which
  LLVM's lowering of it is without `-tailcallopt` (executed for AArch64 in
  the differential below; the x86-64 leg rests on LLVM's tables). A tab
  outside a string reads as a space (`, align\t32` was dropped). The readers
  after the pass read tokens as LLVM splits them and refuse unknown ones by
  name instead of skipping them: before a function's name (`inreg` returns
  refused), its return type where it stands (a type the importer does not
  read was skipped for an earlier token, so `{ i64, i64, i64 }`, `[9 x
  i64]` or `%S` returned `void`; a call that dropped such a result passed
  no result buffer and the program crashed where llc's ran); after the
  parameter list (`gc`, a function `align` above 4 and an SEH personality
  refused; `align` up to 4, metadata attachments and `personality ptr @f`
  read); a call's prefix (fast-math flags, return attributes, address
  space, the return type and an explicit function type; a call read `{ i64,
  i64, i64 }` as its last `i64`) and the text after its arguments; and a
  global's clauses after its initializer, metadata attachments among them
  (a global's line used to be cut at its first `, !`, so a `section`,
  `align` or `comdat` after an attachment, and LLVM's printed `, align 8,
  !dbg !0 #0` attribute group, were dropped; a `c"section "` initializer
  was read as a section and refused; a double-spaced `section` was
  dropped; `code_model` and the sanitizer clauses refused). Function
  attributes, inline or in a group a definition, declaration or call uses,
  are read only when they change nothing the importer builds
  (`crates/trust-cg-llvm-import/src/attributes.rs`: optimization facts and
  hints, sanitizer and profiling markers llc builds no code for, `ssp`,
  and an allowlist of string attributes, `"target-features"` checked
  feature by feature); every other one is refused by name, among them
  `naked`, `returns_twice`, `strictfp`, `shadowcallstack`, clang `-pg`'s
  `"instrument-function-entry-inlined"="mcount"` (llc called `mcount`; the
  import did not), `"patchable-function-entry"`, `+strict-align`,
  `-neon` and any string attribute the allowlist does not name. An operand
  bundle on a call is refused by name (`clang.arc.attachedcall` made llc
  call the retain function; the import retained nothing). A header is no
  longer cut at its last `{`, and an attribute string ends at the next quote
  as in LLVM (a backslash before it hid the rest of the group, `sspstrong`
  included). An ODR or link-once definition written without a `comdat`
  clause, which LLVM places in no group and llc emits as a plain weak
  symbol, is imported as the backend's ungrouped `LinkOnce`/`Weak` function
  or `Weak` global; before, it went into a self-named group, so an AArch64
  ELF object linked before an LLVM object whose same-named group has a
  second member lost that member at link time (SIGSEGV through GNU ld and
  LLD, gold refused the link). A function definition in `@llvm.used` is
  refused by name, its name matched as LLVM names symbols (`@"reg"` and
  `@reg` are one symbol; a quoted spelling escaped the refusal and LLD
  `--gc-sections` removed the hook); a global in it is retained under
  either spelling; an `@llvm.compiler.used` global is no longer marked
  retained, as llc retains nothing for it. Attributes on a global are
  refused by name, among them the `#pragma clang section` attributes,
  which were dropped. Evidence: unit tests in `parser.rs` (46 mutants of
  the repair's decisions and the 37 of the first version all killed); a
  recount of the 620 module texts the importer's test suite imports here
  (351 import and 269 are refused at the base, the first version and now;
  the 25 that the first version imports differently from the base differ
  only in a clause-less ODR or link-once definition's linkage, 33 symbols,
  or one compiler-used global's retention, and no imported module changed
  since), and of 1,086 more texts (`opt -S` and `opt -O2 -S` prints of
  that corpus and 58 rustc modules) with no verdict and no imported module
  changed; 66,880 structural and insertion mutants of those texts import
  or are refused without a panic (the first version panicked on 469); and
  an llc differential over 156 generated spellings (llc 22.1.2, one C
  driver, GNU ld 2.42, gold 1.16 and LLD 22.1.6, O0-O3, static and PIE
  executables and `pic` shared objects under `LD_PRELOAD`, 1332 compared
  configurations): every module is equal to llc (52) or refused by name
  (104); the first version differed on 21 of the 38 spellings added for
  this repair and panicked on one. `symbol_linkage_elf` passes 10/10 with
  `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`GOLD`/`LLC`. Not covered: the instruction readers
  still match operand text with spelled patterns, so punctuation spacing
  LLVM's printer does not produce is left to each reader; an instruction's
  metadata attachments are dropped unread (only the kinds llc's object
  writer reads are refused); and `"probe-stack"` is read on every target
  although only AArch64 frames are probed (x86-64 and RISC-V frames are
  not). `musttail call` is now refused by name (a recursion relying on the
  guaranteed tail call overflowed the stack at O0/O1 where llc's build
  completed); `tail` and `notail` stay hints. Known open after the second
  verifier round (pre-existing, wrong code or ignored semantics, not yet
  refused): `\XX` escapes are not decoded in metadata kind names
  (`!\65xclude` is `!exclude` to LLVM, admitted and dropped) or in
  attribute-group string values (`"+v8a\2C+call-saved-x9"` hides a refused
  target feature: the imported callee clobbered x9); module flags and named
  metadata llc acts on are ignored (the `stack-protector-guard` sysreg
  flags, `!llvm.dependent-libraries`); `"branch-target-enforcement"="false"`
  is read as off, where llc 22 enables BTI whenever the attribute is
  present; and some text LLVM rejects is admitted. Closed by L02-P15
  (above), save that the importer is not an LLVM validator.
- x86-64 zero-extending narrow loads. `mov r8/r16, m` (`MovRM8`/`MovRM16`)
  writes only the low byte or word and merges into the destination's old
  bits, a loop-carried false dependency on the register the previous
  iteration wrote; the bool loads of 2026-09-29 paid for it in tight loops
  (1.9-2.5x at O2). Five opcodes join the x86-64 IR, appended:
  `MovzxRM8`, `MovzxRM16` (`movzx r32, m8/m16` over `[base + disp]`),
  `MovzxRM8Sib` (`[base + index*scale + disp]`) and the volatile
  `VolatileMovzxRM8`/`VolatileMovzxRM16`, each with its encoder arm, ENC-3
  decode intent (the decoder now also compares the extension's source
  width), effects, register roles (destination a pure definition), and the
  load arms of copy propagation, LICM, bounds-check elimination, cmov swap,
  DCE, SIB and LEA folding and the byte vectorizer tiers. The selector emits
  them for every `I8`/`I16`/`B1` load: plain, volatile, atomic (same proof
  origin), formal stack parameters, aggregate lane assembly and memory-copy
  chunks; a `bool` load is `movzx z, m8; add 255; shr 8`. A consumer that
  would re-extend a zero-extended register (an unsigned extension, a
  condition, an i128 or shift operand, a float conversion) copies it with
  `MovRR32` instead, a fresh copy of it keeps the fact, and a signed
  consumer still sign-extends. Proof rows, with no exception: the x86-64
  coverage gate is 206/206 (the five are emittable, covered jointly by the
  byte-level address lane and the `MemLoad` value reconstruction; the two
  volatile ones also by the `VOL-x86` boundary trace); the address lane's
  SDM decoder reads `0F B6`/`0F B7` (and `0F BE`/`0F BF`, to refute a sign
  extension) and gains a destination-write facet: the decoded register write
  over dirty old registers and set top bits must equal the access value
  zero-extended to 64 bits, and a merging `mov`, a sign extension or the
  other width refutes inside the credit hook. `x86_addressing_gate`
  re-derives the 32 corpus encodings from the live encoder, sweeps every
  destination, base, index and scale (55,296 encodings) and checks the
  destination models against this CPU. The body theorem models
  `MovzxRM8`/`MovzxRM16` as the exact zero extension (no free input); the
  carrier-hygiene checker models them as `ZeroExt`, and the merging forms,
  which it had modelled as zero-extending, as unknown above the value. The
  slice-4/5 memory snapshots change for the nine byte and word load shapes,
  and the slice-7 snapshots for `SretNarrow` (its `bool` read back from an
  escaped `sret` buffer); both digests are re-pinned, every shape still
  certifies with AY 0.27.0 build 10530 and Clean 5f09e36c, and the merging
  load treated as zero-extending is a named refutation. Measured on this x86_64 Darwin host, paired and
  alternating against the bridge of the same base without the change: O2
  `count_true` 0.48x the time, `sum_as_u32` 0.45x, `and_pairs` 0.51x,
  `byte_histogram` 0.32x, `u8_max` 0.67x. The Darwin `core` census on the
  slice-7 base goes from 1626 to 1617 failed roots (ten bodies replay that
  did not, mostly the replayer's run-to-run variance); one root is new,
  `DebugMap::finish`, whose `MovRR32` re-extension of a zero-extended byte
  AY 0.27.0 b10530 does not certify within budget (an open solver gap,
  reproducer queries in `reports/2026-09-30-movzx-narrow-loads/`).
- AArch64 objects from `Compiler::compile` are read back for symbol
  discipline: one symbol per emitted function, at its start, with the binding
  its linkage and visibility dictate (hidden definitions re-read as `N_PEXT` /
  `STV_HIDDEN`), and no other symbol or unnamed bytes in the text
  (`AotObjectSymbolDisciplineViolated`). Add `Compiler::preflight`, a
  diagnostic per-function census of the license, binding and adapter
  refusals `compile` would stop at the first of, and
  `CompilerConfig::never_inline`, names OPT-4 never splices.
- Address-free sealed-Core compilation captures its verification request on
  the proof-verifier stack, as the x86-64 certificate lane does. Since
  `257feca72` it captured it on the compiling thread after acquiring that
  thread's environment permit; capturing applies the request's policy as
  thread-local overrides, so every compile that reached the final permit check
  failed `CompilationEnvironmentChanged`, as
  `address_free_core_binds_sparse_definition_after_external_declaration` did
  on the Linux AArch64 host with AY admitted; it now returns the artifact. A
  unit test pins that the capture leaves the permit valid and binds the reuse
  identity of a capture on the compiling thread.
- `e2e_aarch64_sequences` checks replaceable sequence callees for explicit
  Darwin and ELF targets instead of the host's. It expected `WeakOdr` and
  `LinkOnceOdr` callees refused everywhere, which holds only where dyld may
  coalesce them; in an ELF executable they keep their length, and on AArch64
  Linux GNU their callers now execute at O0-O3 with the object's own
  definition and with an equivalent strong C one the link keeps instead.
- `symbol_linkage_elf` pins an imported hidden `external` function on
  `aarch64-apple-darwin` as a private extern (`N_SECT | N_EXT | N_PEXT`, as
  llc writes it), which the Mach-O object path admits since `cee8dc937`, and
  keeps the named refusals of protected functions, hidden functions of other
  linkages, hidden declarations, function sections and `extern_weak`
  references.
- Pin closure float-pair returns across the rlib boundary in
  `rust_call_shims_linux`, on both closure-call return lanes. The L06-P16
  rust-call rewrite (`483974058`) refused closures returning `(f64, f64)`,
  `(f32, f32)` or a `#[repr(C)]` float pair with an internal `[TCG-IR-LOWER]`
  `ExtractField` type error, for by-reference and `move` closures alike. A
  backend built at `df26bde2b` (the rewrite plus one docs commit) refuses the
  test's pre-existing fixture at O0, O2 and O3. The rewrite is in main's
  history, but the `9e6ff1714` merge kept main's tree and archived the lane's
  diff as a patch, so its code never ran on main. At `13a7b0ad9` these
  closures print LLVM's bits. An env-gated trace of
  `finish_closure_call_aggregate_return` shows every one-argument closure call
  in the test taking the closure `PassMode::Pair` return (`67122610f`). The
  test's capturing zero-argument closures are the only calls that reach the
  float-carrier `hfa_return` return (`1048f47f3`), which the test did not
  cover before. The test now checks its four by-reference lanes and 24 more at
  O0, O2 and O3 in every bridge/LLVM pairing. Eleven of the new lanes are
  zero-argument closures. The others are `move`, float-environment, `FnMut` and
  `FnOnce` closures, generic and `&dyn Fn` calls in both directions, an
  `impl Fn` and a library `Box<dyn Fn>`. Three env-gated mutants each copy
  lane 0 over lane 1: one in the closure `Pair` return, one in `hfa_return`
  and one in the dynamic-call `Pair` store. The test fails under each of them;
  the test at `13a7b0ad9` fails only under the closure `Pair` mutant. New
  refusal controls pin `[TCG-CLOSURE-FNPTR]` for a closure coerced to a
  float-pair `fn` pointer and `[TCG-SRET-ABI]` for `[f64; 2]` through
  `&dyn Fn`, and a third, new on this branch, pins `[TCG-FN-DYN-ENTRY]` for a
  fn item returning a float pair behind `&dyn Fn`, at O0, O2 and O3.
- Keep x86 vector address provenance within full-width carriers and the current
  loop. Truncated or preheader-captured indexes retain scalar execution; genuine
  wide scaling and invariant bases remain admitted.
- Preserve genuine `Box<dyn Trait>` data/vtable lanes at branch joins and
  normalize collection allocator addresses before erased-pointer joins.
- Require path-local construction receipts for map-containing dyn drop images,
  including Linux pointer-wrapper conversions and fully known scalar joins;
  incoming Boxes, loads, unknown back edges and nonowning origins refuse. Add
  independent LLVM real-map ownership and borrowed-address controls.
- Keep x86 demanded-bit substitutions within matching register widths and
  canonical nonzero shift counts; masked counts 32/64/65 retain their original
  consumer, with boundary regressions and a valid 64-bit shift-by-32 control.
- Require, on Linux AArch64, that a bridge-built `std` binary links against a
  bridge-built library over the `Internal` copies rustc places in both crates
  under one crate-agnostic name (`<u64 as From<u16>>::from`,
  `<i128>::wrapping_mul`, and from O2 a cross-crate-inlinable trait method).
  The new `cross_crate_definitions` test in `aarch64_c_fnabi_aggregate_linux`
  runs all four LLVM/bridge pairings at O0–O3 against an independently
  computed result. It also compares each crate's defined ELF symbols with
  rustc's LLVM objects: no `Internal` copy may be defined non-locally, every
  other shared definition must have LLVM's binding and visibility, and the
  two crates may share no strong definition. The duplicate-definition link
  failures a 2026-09-27 verifier reported were measured with the bridge at
  `f0ccd49b0`. They do not reproduce at `13a7b0ad9`, where the ELF
  function-linkage layer of the 2026-09-28 repair and the crate-private
  native copies of the wasm32 merge are both in place. That layer gives each
  `Internal` function a CGU-private hidden name and re-binds every other
  function to rustc's linkage and visibility. Disabling both layers at
  `13a7b0ad9` brings back the `From<u16>` and trait-method duplicates (that
  build's binary emits no `wrapping_mul` copy). The test fails on that build
  and on the `f0ccd49b0` bridge. With only the function-linkage layer
  disabled (`PrivateSymbolFormat::for_target` returning `None` on AArch64
  Linux, which turns off the private names and the re-binding together),
  every pairing still links at O0–O3, but the symbol comparison fails.
- Refuse by name (`[TCG-RUST-CALL-ABI]`), at compile time, a bridge call
  that would pass an `extern "rust-call"` argument tuple as one by-value
  parameter to a callee the bridge did not declare. This covers a call
  through an `extern "rust-call" fn(..)` pointer, a dynamic call of a
  non-`Fn*` trait's `extern "rust-call"` method, and a call of a foreign
  `extern "rust-call"` item. Such a call stays admitted only when rustc's
  untupled `FnAbi` passes each element in one of the tuple's own register
  lanes (a lane may be wider than its element, as for the `u8` of `(u8,
  u64)`), extends no element, and no argument register class runs out first.
  A `bool` element is refused: rustc marks it `zeroext`, and LLVM's AArch64
  callee tests all 32 bits of a register in which the bridge's lane carries
  the tuple's padding. Where the bridge links another crate's `extern
  "rust-call"` item or trait method and calls it directly, the
  `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` declaration refusal now applies the same `bool` rule; an
  item the bridge defines and exports keeps a `bool` element. Before, on
  Linux AArch64 at `13a7b0ad9`, an LLVM-built library's `extern "rust-call"
  fn((u64, [f32; 4], u8)) -> u64` called through a pointer from a
  bridge-built binary returned a different wrong value on each run. At
  `5e0696862` a `(bool, u64)` whose padding was nonzero read `false` as
  `true` through a pointer, a method pointer, a non-`Fn*` `dyn` method, a
  foreign item, and a direct call of the upstream item or trait method (961
  against 41 at O2/O3); the pointer, item and trait-method calls were wrong
  at `13a7b0ad9` too. An ordinary `Vec<(bool, u64)>` loop through a pointer
  printed 32640 against 10965 at O2. The `rust_call_pointer_calls` test in
  `aarch64_c_fnabi_aggregate_linux` pins the refusals at O0–O3 and runs the
  admitted shapes in all four LLVM/bridge pairings, including a `(u8, u64)`
  with 0xAB padding. It also runs an LLVM binary against a bridge library's
  `(bool, u64)` item. It fails on the `13a7b0ad9` and `5e0696862` backends
  and with any one refusal disabled. A 2026-10-02 matrix of 345 two-crate
  programs (23 tuple kinds × 15 call routes, O0/O2/O3, three pairings with a
  bridge side) had 291 wrong or crashing cells before. After, 1371 cells
  match LLVM and 1734 are refused by name. A 44-program `bool` matrix
  (O0–O3) has no wrong cell, against 41 wrong cells at `5e0696862`
  (O0/O2/O3). The 189-program bridge corpus is unchanged.
- Refuse by name (`[TCG-ARG-ABI]`) a by-value `FnOnce` closure body whose
  environment of at most 16 bytes rustc passes in registers while the bridge
  declares a pointer, wherever code the other backend compiled reaches it.
  That covers three cases. The first is a body this crate links from another
  crate. The second is a body this crate exports when another crate compiles
  its own copy of the closure's cross-crate-inlinable defining function and
  that copy hands the closure to anything but a generic instance this crate
  exports. The third is the body's address: `<F as FnOnce<A>>::call_once`
  reified for a `FnOnce` closure, or the body in a vtable slot or a constant
  or static fn pointer. Before, on Linux AArch64 at `13a7b0ad9`, stable code
  crashed at O0 with a bridge-built library and printed pointer-like values

The following audit changes are in the development source, not a released
package. Validation and remaining failures are tracked by the current audit.

- WS7.3 (F-113): every ingestion entry refuses what trust-ir's validator
  refuses. `Compiler::compile` (the object/CLI path and the MIR lane through
  it), `compile_module_to_jit[_with_profile_hooks]` (the host JIT and the
  compile service) and the wasm lane now admit the module through
  `trust_cg_codegen::ingest::admit_module` / `trust_cg_lower::admit_module`:
  the codegen license first (its named diagnostics unchanged), then trust-ir's
  composed codegen admission (structural validator, license evidence,
  lowerability, `global_asm`) under the authority tier's import policy, so a
  proof-bearing import row is `UnauthenticatedImport`. Every finding refuses:
  the ones the adapter consumes by name keep their refusal, every other is the
  new `CompileError::InvalidTrustIr` / `AdapterError::InvalidTrustIrModule` /
  `WasmLowerError::InvalidTrustIr`, naming the module, the stage, the first
  three findings and the count. The one exemption is consumer-owned: a
  `DialectOp` namespace this backend's dialect registry lowers is not "no
  registered lowering" (matched on trust-ir's exact text). The module a
  dialect rewrite produces is re-admitted before it is lowered
  (`AdmissionStage::Rewritten`). The production adapter entries take an
  `AdmittedModule` typestate (`translate_admitted_module_for_arch_with_
  access_model_and_stats`, `translate_admitted_module_for_arch_with_tls_and_
  validation`); `translate_module_for_arch_with_access_model_and_stats_with_
  license` is now crate-private (tests only). The compile service's
  `first_verifier_rejection` maps every validator finding it used to drop to
  `trust_ir_invalid_module`. `--format=text` input is refused under
  `--refuse-unlicensed` / `--emit-proofs` and warned on the default path
  (`TEXT_INPUT_NOT_TOTAL`: the text codec cannot carry summaries, bindings,
  every layout fact or `global_asm` at this pin). The store-form InsertField
  is now refused at ingestion as `FieldAccessInvalid` (the adapter's
  `AggregateInsertNotValueForm` stays behind it on the raw entries). New gate
  targets `trust-cg-codegen --test ingest_admission` and `--test
  v41_abi_residue_objects` in `soundness_check.sh`; `ingest_admission` ports
  the proof program's GENERAL.consumer.accepts_head_invalid_modules row onto
  an injected `ConstTypeMismatch` module and holds every public
  `compile*`/`translate_*` entry to admission by source scan.
- WS7.3 census (what the admission found trust-cg's own producers emitting):
  the rustc bridge now stamps the session target on every module it compiles
  that names none (the `main` entry shim, the allocator shim and the
  `__trustcg_*` helpers carried FFI declarations without `target_info`,
  `TargetInfoRequired`), and spells `rust_main` as a value with
  `Constant::FnDef` at its own signature instead of a capture-free
  `Constant::Closure` typed `Ty::Func` (`ConstTypeMismatch`). `merge_modules`
  gives a declaration and the definition that upgrades it ONE signature id when
  the two are name-resolved equal (trust-ir compares `Ty::Func` nominally, so a
  caller's `FnDef` constant typed with its own copy was `ConstTypeMismatch` in
  every batch that took a sibling's address); the `func_types` table is not
  compacted. Test fixtures that trust-ir refuses were rewritten in its spelling
  (pinned targets, field-typed `ExtractField`, `PhantomData` for `()`, bool
  branch conditions, dead blocks behind a constant branch instead of
  unreachable ones) or now expect trust-ir's named finding where the refusal is
  the point (`tests/common/admission_expect.rs`). Frozen frontend-emitted
  fixtures are brought to a conforming producer's module before they compile
  (`tests/common/emitted_fixture.rs`: pinned target, duplicate declarations
  folded by the batching merge, a mixed-type shift amount converted), and
  aggregate-typed `ExtractField`s are rewritten to the field type
  (`tests/common/field_typed.rs`). Refused at ingestion now, by trust-ir's
  finding, where the backend used to compile: closure application
  (`UnlowerableForCodegen`, F-055, until trust-ir WS3.13), a refinement-typed
  `ExtractElement` index (`InvalidVectorElementOp`, so the WP-2
  lattice-guard differential is refused until trust-ir reads a refined
  integer as its base), a `FnDef` of or direct call to an `external_weak`
  declaration (spelled `SymbolAddr` + `CallIndirect` in the fixtures), a
  `Discharged` row without a replayed certificate and a node `ProofRef` that
  names none (the guard-probe fixtures), and a declared `()` return with a bare
  `ret`. The adapter's own definition-preserving transforms (Swift ABI
  scalarization, divisor annotation) stay held to the prerequisites walk; only a
  pre-adapter rewrite that produces new core IR (dialect lowering) is
  re-admitted. `merge_modules`' signature unification compares a declaration
  and its definition with the full type-comparison budget (it was given 0, so
  no signature with a parameter or return was ever unified and the merged
  compile of such a batch was refused, falling back to per-function objects).
- WS7.3-pre: the rustc bridge's MIR lane emits valid trust-ir for ordinary
  Rust, so WS7.3's admission does not refuse it. A slot field read is the
  field's byte address and a typed `Load` (never an `ExtractField` over the
  slot pointer, `FieldAccessInvalid`); a lane read of an aggregate value
  declares the lane type (`ExtractElement` for an array image); typed-pointer
  compares, same-width integer operands and constants are spelled at their
  declared types. `abi_edges` legalizes every module the compiler receives,
  after the per-codegen-unit merge: a slot address passed or returned where
  the declaration names a lane aggregate is `Load`ed as that aggregate, a thin
  address of another pointer type is `PtrToPtr`-ed, an entry parameter takes
  its declared reference type, a runtime code address is called through
  directly, unreachable `unreachable` stubs are dropped, and an indirect call
  through a function item names the item's own signature id where the two
  entries are equal (`CallEdgeSignatureMismatch` at `-Copt-level=2`).
  Measured (`targo --unverified`, no proof claim): `tests/mir_lane_valid_trust_ir.rs`
  validates every module the backend compiles for its probe at `-O0`/`-O2`
  and matches LLVM on the run twin; a 20-program bridge-corpus census has no
  invalid module at `-O0` or `-O2` with WS7.3 in place.
- WS7.7: v42 declared tuple layouts (`Module.tuple_layouts`) are consumed on
  the native byte path instead of refusing every module that carries one. A
  row is admitted only when it EQUALS the declaration-order layout the byte
  path emits for that tuple (every field offset, size and align), so the
  declared layout is honoured by construction; a row that differs is refused
  as `AdapterError::DeclaredTupleLayoutDisagrees`, naming the first component

- x86-64 proof lane, slice 7 of the source-bound body theorem: calls through
  memory. A direct call may receive a private stack slot's address as an
  ordinary 64-bit argument (a `&mut`/`&` out-parameter) or as argument 0 of
  a callee in `Function::sret_arg_callees` (its hidden return buffer, in
  RDI; the call has no result), so the frame condition "an sret-arg callee"
  no longer refuses (an indirect return-buffer callee still does). The slot
  escapes to that call and every later one on the path, and the
  Ackermann-reduced call model extends to it exactly: each call observes
  the escaped slots' contents at the call (8-byte chunks; chunks both sides
  spell alike are not stated) besides its scalar arguments, and after the
  call every byte of every escaped slot is one free input per call site and
  byte (`d{site}s{slot}o{offset}`) shared by the two sides, so no callee
  behaviour is assumed (an LLVM callee may write any byte of a buffer,
  padding included, or none). The walk checks that the machine passes
  exactly the paired slot and offset (`X86BodyMismatch::CallStackAddress`
  otherwise); an incoming access through an address that may derive from an
  escaped slot (a call result, an incoming load or a call-defined byte after
  the first escape, or anything computed from one) is outside the domain; a
  `bool` read of one call-defined byte is `byte != 0`. 15 fixture shapes
  certify on the qualification host and 6 wrong lowerings are refuted
  (`x86_source_bound_body_slice7_tests.rs`, digest-pinned
  `slice7_snapshots.smt2`; slices 1-6 snapshots unchanged); the solver-free
  tests run in a new soundness library gate
  (`x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice7::`), the replay in
  `slice7_qualification`; each of five walk rules disabled alone fails a
  control; the e2e proof-required AOT test promotes four slice-7 bodies on
  Darwin and Linux. The slice-3 domain test's "slot address passed to a
  callee" case now also returns the address (still outside); the passing
  form is admitted and tested in `slice7`. The bridge build fix `eaa5d9ca8`
  is cherry-picked (main did not build the bridge at this base). Darwin
  `core` census at O0 with proofs required: 1817 (the `main` 336a49f14
  bridge) -> 1634 failed roots (183 promote: 131 escape-into-call, 52
  sret-callee functions; none newly fails, no mismatch named); 151 newly
  bound bodies do not certify (AY rejects its own proof in strict
  certification, an incomplete certificate, or a few attempts at AY's
  budget; none refuted). A
  proof-required rlib of exactly the credited callers, with LLVM-compiled
  callees, matches the LLVM oracle in all four rlib x bin cells at O0-O3,
  `reports/perf/2026-10-01-darwin-x86-64-census-slice7/`.

- AArch64 source-bound Booleans, comparisons, branches, bitwise rows and

  add/sub/neg, `Band`/`Bor`/`Bxor`/`Bnot`/`BandNot`/`BorNot`,

  B.cond/CBZ/CBNZ/TBZ/TBNZ and the rest as emitted) with one theorem per
