- The wasm32 target is completed past the closed module. The lowering covers
  the trust-ir value domain (narrow and 128-bit integers, overflow, rotates,
  IEEE `min`/`max`, `FRem`, `select`, aggregates, tuples, enums,
  fat pointers, atomics, bulk memory) under the WebAssembly BasicCABI, with
  `sret` for multi-lane results. `wasm::compile_object` writes relocatable
  objects in the tool-conventions format, and every one passes the CFG
  structural checker first. The CLI writes them with `-c` and links several
  inputs with an external `wasm-ld` (`--wasm-ld`, `$WASM_LD`, `PATH`). The
  checker now types `memory.copy`/`memory.fill` and `select`. The lane refuses
  an operand used at another value-type width. It refuses a memory-carried
  value used as a scalar; that gate caught a by-value `ExtractField` that
  yielded the aggregate's address instead of its lane. It honors the `0xFADE`
  global-address stub. The ill-typed `abi_frame` fixture of the wasm ABI proof
  gate (an `i64.store` of an `i32`) is repaired. `wasm_value_domain_differential`
  runs 135,317 interpreter checks over 170 functions, as a closed module and
  as a linked object.
- The rustc bridge compiles `wasm32-unknown-unknown` sessions through that
  object lane (`panic=abort`, `no-proof-certs`); rustc links with `wasm-ld`.
  A word pass narrows the MIR lowering's native 64-bit address arithmetic to
  the 32-bit wasm word (`src/wasm32_words.rs`) and refuses mixed classes by
  name. Data images, vtables, virtual calls, pointer casts, fat-pointer
  lanes, the allocator shim and the slice-cursor models follow the session's
  pointer width. Models still written for 64-bit layouts are refused on
  wasm32. `tests/wasm32_differential.rs` runs a 36-export `no_std` corpus
  compiled by this lane and by LLVM in node (10,735 checks, no
  disagreements). `scripts/build_wasm32_sysroot.sh` builds the wasm32 `core`
  it needs from the compiler's own library sources.
- The coverage gate's wasm opcode inventory follows the new lowering. The 15
  opcodes it emits that `WasmOpcode` did not list (`clz`/`ctz`,
  `rotl`/`rotr`, `eqz`, `copysign`, `select`, `memory.copy`/`memory.fill`)
  entered it, and `f.min`/`f.max`, allowlisted out as never selected, are now
  emitted and entered the denominator: 19 new value-bearing rows.
- The wasm stack-operand reconstructor credits 11 of those 19 opcodes.
  `clz`/`ctz`, `rotl`/`rotr`, `eqz` and `select` decode their real bytes and
  rebuild the WebAssembly spec numerics. Each is compared with a trust-ir
  encoder that follows the reference interpreter: `RotL`/`RotR` reduce the
  amount modulo the width, `CtLz`/`CtTz` of zero is the width, and a `Bool`
  is carried as `i32` 0/1. The rotate and bit-count sides use different
  constructions (shifts against bit permutations, population counts against a
  bit-scan chain). `eqz` and `select` share their core predicate with the
  trust-ir side, so those obligations check the decoded byte and width, the
  0/1 carrier and the stack order, as the two-operand compares do; `eqz` is
  emitted only inside the overflow and wide-integer sequences and the
  dynamic `Alloca` count check, so its row credits the zero test's value
  semantics. Negative controls refute a rotl
  byte for an intended rotr and the reverse, a clz byte for an intended ctz,
  `eqz` as a nonzero test, and `select` with swapped values, an inverted
  condition, or a `c == 1` or low-bit test over a full 32-bit condition. An
  i64 byte at i32 width fails closed. A new test checks every decoded
  single-byte opcode against the constant the wasm encoder writes. The
  published wasm ratio moves from 111/113 to 122/132. The 10 RED rows are
  `f32.const`/`f64.const`, `copysign` (the direct `FCopySign` lowering, with
  no reconstruction arm), `min`/`max` (emitted only inside the FMin/FMax
  sequence) and `memory.copy`/`memory.fill`.
- An adversarial audit of the wasm32 target confirmed 105 wrong-result,
  crash and wrong-refusal bugs, each reproduced by an independent skeptic and
  root-caused, and reported 87 refusals as wasm32-only or wrong. Seven fix
  groups repaired them; each fix was adversarially reviewed and its repros
  rerun. Wasm lane:
  - Values. Signed `icmp` on `bool` reads `true` as -1. A call returning
    one memory-carried value beside `()` values binds its result. A
    zero-sized untagged enum's discriminant is read. 128-bit element, GEP
    and memset/memcopy operands are read as values, not as their operand's
    address. Float to 8/16-bit and float/128-bit casts, multi-value returns
    with `i128` or aggregates, niche discriminants above `i64::MAX` and
    `symaddr` constants in bodies are lowered. Undeclared tuples and structs
    use the interpreter's C layout everywhere. Invalid IR (bool-lane
    `bitcast`, float to `bool`) and arrays too large for wasm32 are refused
    by name, as is `symaddr<function + k>` with a non-zero addend.
  - Frames. A by-address aggregate entry parameter that the entry block
    rebinds, or whose address may escape, gets its own home instead of
    writing the caller's memory. An `Alloca` in a loop whose earlier pointer
    may still be observed is carved fresh on every execution, as the
    interpreter defines it. A closed module with static data checks every
    new stack pointer against that data and traps instead of overwriting
    it. Home slots share frame bytes by liveness (block parameters are
    defined per edge), and functions with 64 or more locals coalesce them:
    recursive `rec` frames drop from 38,400 to 1,536 bytes and a 1.6 KB
    array constructor from 51,198 locals to 6. A function still over an
    engine limit is refused with `WasmLowerError::ImplementationLimit`.
  - Objects. Function addresses in data, vtables and constants are
    undefined FUNCTION symbols with `R_WASM_TABLE_INDEX_I32` relocations,
    and any function address imports `__indirect_function_table` (`NO_STRIP`),
    which fixes a `wasm-ld` crash. Initializer-less weak or link-once globals
    are strong undefined references, not weak symbols bound to address 0.
    `frem` binds only the C library `fmod`/`fmodf`. Relocations are emitted
    in offset order. Hidden functions and `available_externally` globals are
    admitted under the object policy. In closed modules table slot 0 is the
    null function pointer, so function 0's address is never null; the ABI
    and encoding verifiers check that convention. `--wasm-ld` naming
    `rust-lld`/`lld` gets `-flavor wasm`, and CLI links use rustc's
    `-z stack-size=1048576 --stack-first` layout.
- The same audit's rustc-bridge fixes for wasm32 sessions keep native
  (64-bit) objects byte-identical unless they fix a native bug:
  - Pointer widths. Slice and `str` fat pointers loaded or stored through a
    thin reference, `split_first`/`split_last` tails, `Option<&[T]>`, arrays
    and slices of `&dyn Trait` (two-word elements), const `Range<usize>`
    bounds, the take/skip/enumerate/step-by counts and the `zip` cursor use
    the target's pointer width. `#[repr(packed)]` fields through a reference
    use rustc's offsets. Before, 8-byte accesses read or overwrote
    neighbouring fields.
  - Runtime calls. `memcpy`/`memmove`/`memset` are declared with their C
    prototype (`-> ptr`). Before, `wasm-ld` bound every call to a trapping
    signature-mismatch stub, so every `copy_from_slice`/`ptr::copy` trapped.
    A mis-typed bulk-memory declaration is refused as `[TCG-WASM32-LIBCALL]`.
  - ABI. Aggregates rustc passes or returns as one integer (`[u8; 4]`,
    3-byte structs, `RangeInclusive<u8>`, small enums) lower to one `i32`.
    Indirect calls returning through a caller buffer pass it as the leading
    argument. Closures take scalar-pair and small cast aggregates by value.
    Narrow shifts mask the amount to the value's width in release builds.
  - Newly accepted on wasm32: returning or storing `&dyn Trait`, upcasts to
    a non-first supertrait, `size_of_val`/`align_of_val` on `dyn`,
    `wrapping_offset`, `write_bytes`/`fill`, `bool as u8`, `ptr as u64`,
    statics holding function pointers, `&&T` loads, `iter().rev()`,
    `derive(PartialEq/Debug)`, `<[T]>::swap` at O2, `zip` over `Range<u32>`
    or `Range<usize>`, and a `zip` with a `Range<u64>`/`Range<i64>` side,
    which runs core's general `Zip` as 32-bit targets do.
  - All targets. Signed `offset_from` divides signed. Only mono-reachable
    blocks are lowered, so debug `pow` and `if T::CONST` dead arms no longer
    name uncollected instances. f32 signalling-NaN constants keep their
    bits. `Iterator::sum`/`product` honour `-C overflow-checks` and model
    `Saturating`/`Wrapping` accumulators. `[TCG-LINK-UNDEF]` also derives
    the crate tag from an instantiating-crate suffix. The SSA-071 anti-swap
    gate accepts an in-loop join only when every incoming edge value derives
    from the same slot, so optimized `pow` compiles and a cross-slot
    misroute through a join is still refused.
- A second wasm32 audit replayed the first audit's 2,288 programs at O0 to
  O3, `Os` and 16 codegen units, ran a random well-typed trust-ir
  differential (575,819 interpreter comparisons over closed, relinked,
  split-object and island lanes, with no miscompile of valid trust-ir), and
  added ten new finders. Its fixes:
  - Layout. A Rust aggregate in memory uses rustc's layout on every target:
    reordered structs, tuples and single-variant enums, `repr(packed)`,
    `repr(align(N))`, over-aligned newtypes and tagged single-variant enums
    passed by value. Before, the bridge read and wrote the declaration-order
    C-rule image. Address-taken locals of these types live in a slot of
    rustc's size and alignment, and any remaining tuple-image access is
    refused as `[TCG-TUPLE-IMAGE-LAYOUT]`. A native address-taken object
    aligned above 16 bytes is refused by name. Most of these were wrong
    natively too.
  - Frames and addresses. Per-use temporaries live in the entry block, so a
    loop no longer grows the frame each iteration (wasm32 loops past about
    65,536 iterations trapped). Borrows of a register-held local share one
    home, so `ptr::eq(&y, &y)` and address compares match rustc; shapes that
    cannot get a home are refused as `[TCG-ADDR-IDENTITY]`.
  - Widths. The pointer-word value refinements whose model uses 8-byte cells
    state no obligation in a 32-bit session. The `usize` fields of stride
    iterators, `Option<&[T]>` and the zip cursor use rustc's width.
    Closures returning an aggregate rustc casts to one `i32` compile, and
    ABI refusals name wasm32 values instead of native registers.
  - Closures as `fn` pointers. Statics, consts, locals and `dyn Fn` over
    non-capturing closures and fn pointers land on entries with the
    caller's signature, not the tupled `call_once` shim; this trapped on
    wasm32 and gave wrong values natively. A const `fn` pointer is the code
    address, not a data cell. `<[T]>::swap` over 16-byte elements and
    `Cell<[T]>` pointers are admitted.
  - Multiple codegen units. rustc's per-CGU linkage reaches every wasm32
    function definition: CGU-private copies become hidden `linkonce_odr`
    definitions under a crate-private name, so `wasm-ld` coalesces them
    within a crate but never with another crate's copy. Before, any wasm32
    crate built with more than one codegen unit could fail with
    `duplicate symbol`. Unsupported linkages are refused as
    `[TCG-WASM32-LINKAGE]`.
  - Lane frames. The lane reads the bridge's same-size reinterpreting
    `extractfield [i64 x N]` as one lane, not a 16-byte view; an indirect
    `repr(C) {f32, f64}` argument with an `sret` return had written 8 bytes
    past its frame. A new frame-bounds guard (`wasm/frame_bounds.rs`)
    refuses a lowered function with a constant-offset frame access outside
    its allocated frame.
  - Coverage. The wasm ratio moves from 122/132 to 130/132. `f32.const` and
    `f64.const` are credited by an independent decoder of the spec's float
    immediates, `copysign` by a reconstruction arm, and `min`/`max` by the
    captured FMin/FMax body run under the spec semantics, each with
    refuting controls. `memory.copy`/`memory.fill` stay RED: they trap on a
    zero-length out-of-bounds range that trust-ir defines as a no-op.
- A third and fourth wasm32 audit (a second random trust-ir differential over
  66,350 modules with no lane miscompile, ten more finders, and a replay of
  the 3,746 earlier audit programs) led to these fixes:
  - Stores and borrows (all targets). A whole-value store through `&mut` or
    `*mut` writes at rustc's field offsets, including lane-shell pointees
    (array or nested-struct fields, arrays of reordered tuples); `*d = *s`,
    `mem::replace`, `clone_from` and `FnMut` state updates had written wrong
    or out-of-object bytes. A borrow of a zero-sized element or field has
    rustc's address. Stores that cannot be placed exactly are refused as
    `[TCG-TUPLE-IMAGE-LAYOUT]` or `[TCG-ZST-LANE-INDEX]`.
  - Zero-sized fields before sized ones (all targets). Stores, literals and
    whole copies read each leaf of a scalarized aggregate under the key its
    construction gave it, so a source with a zero-sized field before a sized
    one (`RawVec`'s `Unique { pointer, _marker }` before `cap`, which
    `Vec::new` stores) compiles instead of being refused
    `[TCG-ZST-LANE-INDEX]`. A whole copy of such an aggregate out of memory or
    through a pointer had returned the next field for the first one at -O0.
    Field types declared through an associated-type projection
    (`o: <u8 as Tr>::O`, `T::O`) are normalized before the key scheme is
    chosen, as construction does; reading `s.a` of
    `S { z: (), a: u32, o: <u8 as Tr>::O }` had returned `o` at -O0.
  - Iterators and enums (all targets). `take(n)` tests its count before
    pulling, so closures below it no longer run once too many; a `Skip`
    under a `Take` over a random-access source evaluates nothing when
    nothing is taken. A fieldless enum reassigned in a loop is no longer
    matched against its pre-loop variant at O0. Calls to empty drop glue are
    elided, which admits `binary_search*` and `partition_point` on wasm32.
    Chains over `RangeFrom`, and over core's general `Zip` on wasm32, lower
    core's real `fold`/`try_fold`/`next` bodies; this also fixes a native
    O2/O3 `(lo..).take(n)...sum()` that reached a trapped stub.
  - Statics, consts and linkage. A const `fn` pointer is the code address
    and can be called directly. Statics and consts pointing into one
    allocation share one definition, so `ptr::eq`/`offset_from` agree with
    rustc. Reading an `extern`-block static no longer ICEs. Native crates
    with several codegen units define each CGU-private copy once (the
    x86-64 Mach-O/ELF writers now bind weak and link-once functions weak).
    `#[thread_local]` is a plain static on single-threaded wasm32.
  - wasm32 ABI. Aggregates aligned above 16 bytes get memory slots at
    rustc's alignment, and by-value ones follow rustc's `PassMode::Indirect`
    under the Rust and C ABIs. `extern "C"` functions pass `repr(C)` unions,
    padded and over-aligned aggregates and mixed float/int unions through
    memory with an `sret` return, as rustc's wasm32 C ABI does; a mixed
    LLVM/trust-cg link test checks both call directions. A Rust-ABI union
    reaching a `fn` pointer or another backend stays refused as
    `[TCG-WASM32-BYVAL-ABI]`. A new bridge pass (`wasm32_frames`) turns
    constant fills into `memset`, so arrays in disjoint scopes share frame
    bytes (two 600 KB scopes take 600,000 bytes, as LLVM, not 1,200,016).
  - Wasm lane. Output is byte-reproducible (frame homes were ordered by
    hash iteration). Structuring and `switch` lowering run on an explicit
    work stack, so 20k-block chains and 24k-case switches no longer overflow
    the compiler stack. Irreducible CFGs lower as a dispatch loop that
    passes the CFG structural checker, and an `Alloca` with a runtime count
    is carved from the shadow stack. 128-bit `atomicrmw`/`cmpxchg` are
    lowered. Weak and link-once definitions are treated as replaceable at
    link time, so their callers pass argument copies; a foreign strong
    definition had been able to corrupt the caller's value or a pooled
    constant. Frame-slot sharing follows an address through integers, so an
    address rebuilt from its bits keeps its allocation. Padded or
    over-aligned singleton aggregates pass by address, as clang does. New
    named refusals cover static data past the owned memory, Rust-convention
    aggregates at an object link boundary (`[TCG-WASM-RUST-ABI-LINK]`),
    duplicate or linker-owned symbols (`[TCG-WASM-SYMBOL]`), non-dominated
    uses and mistyped branch arguments (`IllFormedSsa`) and closure values
    (`[TCG-WASM-CLOSURE]`).
  - Verification evidence. `memory.copy`/`memory.fill` are guarded by
    `n != 0`, so a zero-byte copy through a pointer past memory is the no-op
    trust-ir defines, and their rows are credited against a relational
    contract with operand-provenance checks and truncated-count controls.
    The encoder cross-check compares every `0xfc` form's full sub-opcode;
    memarg offsets are modeled and bound to layout offsets; each constant
    `call_indirect` site is bound to its own element-segment entry through
    a definite-assignment analysis; and never-selected opcodes are excluded
    from the denominators and checked absent from live-compiled code. The
    WebAssembly ratio is 128/128, the value domain 16/20.
- A further round fixed rustc-bridge miscompiles shared by every target:
  - Retained addresses. When a callee could keep a local's address (an
    out-parameter, a static, a returned raw pointer or `NonNull`, an
    integer round trip, `AtomicPtr`, a trait object or closure), the local
    stayed in registers and a later write through the kept address was
    lost. A conservative escape analysis (`retained_address.rs`, with
    per-argument callee summaries) now gives every such local a memory
    home; a deref through a pointer local whose own address may be kept is
    refused as `[TCG-RETAINED-ADDR]`.
  - Call models. A model now replaces a call only when the callee is the
    std item it stands in for (by impl, diagnostic item or core path),
    never by name. User items named `funnel_shl`, `reverse`/`then`/`is_*`
    on `Ordering`, `chars`, `eq` on a `ControlFlow`, `new -> Box<T>` or
    `black_box` had been silently replaced. `Iterator::max`/`min` compare by
    the item's `Ord`, so `Reverse<T>` and user newtypes are ordered
    correctly.
  - `#[track_caller]` follows rustc's `FnAbi`: definitions, declarations,
    direct, virtual and `&dyn Fn` calls carry the hidden `&Location`, with
    the value rustc's shims pass; a `#[track_caller]` closure called from a
    hand-built closure lane is refused as `[TCG-TRACK-CALLER-ABI]`. A virtual
    call to a `#[track_caller]` trait method is measured against LLVM on
    AArch64 and wasm32; x86-64 keeps the `[TCG-ABI-TRACKCALLER-VIRTUAL]`
    refusal until that boundary is measured there.
  - Two frontend miscompiles around loops (a store through an argument
    reassigned before a parameterless loop header, and a write-only cursor
    reassigned inside a loop) are fixed; constant single-float wrappers are
    spelled as floats; long straight-line debug functions compile in near
    linear time (a 7,000-assert function from 652 s to 21 s).
  - Cross-crate and wasm32 ABI. Exported and address-taken functions
    follow rustc's ABI instead of a crate-internal one; a downstream crate
    references an upstream static instead of copying it; two bridge-built
    crates no longer define the same `#[inline]` core copy strongly; the
    `Iterator::position` model writes a 4-byte `Option<usize>` payload on
    wasm32; by-value `AtomicU64`, `rev().take(n).fold(..)` and
    `find`/`filter` over `u64` items compile on wasm32; LLVM intrinsic
    imports such as `memory_grow` are refused at compile time
    (`[TCG-WASM32-LLVM-INTRINSIC]`).
  - A CGU-private function placed in one codegen unit is a strong hidden
    definition, so the lane can analyse its capture facts and frame sharing
    still applies; the lane's capture rules count any operation that may
    trap depending on an address's bits (asserts, divisions, shifts, loads
    through bits-derived pointers) as a capture.
  - A relaxation of the SSA-071 loop gate that would have admitted rotation
    and swap loops was reviewed by three independent adversarial rounds,
    each of which found new unsound admissions; it was not merged, and those
    loops stay refused by name.
  - After merging upstream into the wasm32 work. The wasm lane copies a
    memory-carried lane (`i128`, an aggregate) that `ExtractField` reads
    through a pointer into a home of its own, as a `Load` does; it had
    aliased the pointee, so `let old = p.b; p.b = n; f(old)` over a `u128`
    field handed `f` the new value, and std's `RangeInclusive<u128>` reversed
    folds (`mem::replace(&mut self.end, ..)`) skipped `end`. On wasm32 at
    -O2/-O3, rustc inlines `RangeInclusive::rfold` into the caller, so a
    `spec_try_rfold` into a `NeverShortCircuit` of a primitive scalar is
    driven back to front by the bridge (it reached a trapped std body). A
    library crate's dead-iterator trap stub that the crate's own code reaches
    through emitted calls (a `&mut`/`by_ref()` or `char` reversed inclusive
    fold, a `bool`/`char`/newtype accumulator) is refused as
    `[TCG-ITER-STUB-REACHABLE]` instead of trapping at run time. The wasm32
    gate that compares a one-scalar aggregate parameter with rustc's `FnAbi`
    indexes rustc's arguments, so a capture-free closure taking a one-field
    struct or fieldless enum through `Option::map` compiles again.
  - After merging upstream's v52 panic cohort and memory/allocator ABI
    repairs. A canonical MIR bounds check whose failure would trap is
    refused natively as `[TCG-ASSERT-PANIC]`; a wasm32 `panic=abort` session
    instead calls core's genuine `panic_bounds_check(index, len)` with the
    caller location, so the `#[panic_handler]` observes the same location
    and formatted payload as LLVM's module (the pre-merge trap skipped it:
    `wasm32_bounds_check_panic_runs_the_handler_like_llvm`). The wasm lane
    refuses a v52 source `Assert` by its panic kind, at the shared floor and
    in its own backstop, never as a generic trap. Upstream's actual-`usize`
    allocator ABI, genuine `memcpy`/`memmove`/`memset` lang-item
    declarations and `Box<dyn>` join layout check follow the session's
    pointer width (`U32` size_t on wasm32) instead of requiring 64 bits.
    The lane's former `Assert`-to-trap lowering is removed. Native
    capability lost to the `[TCG-ASSERT-PANIC]` refusal: four bridge tests
    that passed before the merge failed on it,
    `zst_leaf_key_differential`, `call_identity_native`
    (`track_caller_abi`),
    `static_data_aarch64::statics_pointing_at_extern_statics_link_and_run_aarch64`
    and `unsupported_program::retained_pointer_locals_compile` (their
    programs were migrated in the next round and pass again). Natively the
    old route trapped where LLVM runs the panic hook before aborting.
- A seventh wasm32 round (correctness, then output quality):
  - wasm32 lane frames. A pointer rebuilt with `ptrtoint`/`add`/`inttoptr`
    keeps sharing frame bytes only while its displacement provably stays
    inside its allocation. The proof can come from constants, from a
    remainder or mask, or from a dominating unsigned bounds check against a
    constant or against a length parameter of a function whose entry block
    no branch re-enters. A displacement carried into a block parameter keeps
    its index only while the index cannot have been rebound, and callees
    record the displacements they need of their pointer arguments. Otherwise
    the allocation is pinned, or carved per loop execution, so a probe that
    the interpreter resolves into a neighbouring allocation can no longer
    make two live allocations share bytes. Zero-sized allocations take one
    byte, so every live allocation has a distinct address. A function whose
    only frame need was staging two by-address entry parameters compiles
    instead of failing with "no stack-pointer global". Declared C
    `memset`/`memcpy`/`memmove` with their exact C shapes no longer pin
    their pointer arguments, so `slice::fill` and `copy_from_slice` on large
    local arrays share frame bytes again. Slice iterators over large local
    arrays still pin them (a fail-closed shadow-stack trap at `-O2` where
    LLVM's module runs).
  - rustc bridge iterator models (wasm32 and native). `.cloned()` is modeled
    as a load only when the element's `clone` is a bitwise copy: the builtin
    derive's (checked with `is_builtin_derived`, not the ungated
    `#[automatically_derived]` attribute), a primitive's, or core's own for a
    `Copy` type. A hand-written `clone` now runs through core's real
    `Cloned::try_fold`; before, it was silently skipped, natively too.
    `Vec::dedup`'s leaf-equality model uses the same check. `find`/`nth`/
    `last` over a `bool` chain store `Option<bool>::None` through the `u8`
    niche tag (wasm32 returned `Some(false)`; native refused), and the wasm
    lane refuses an out-of-range `const bool`. Optimized
    `copy_try_fold`/`clone_try_fold`/`map_try_fold` glue over struct items,
    and any closure called with a `((), C)` argument tuple, now lower.
    `repeat`/`repeat_with`/`from_fn`/`successors` chains take core's real
    bodies instead of trap stubs or refusals. On wasm32, `count()`
    (including a `chain` of ranges or slices under inherited overflow
    checks) and debug `position()` past `u32::MAX` items panic as core does
    (a direct count over a range of at most 32-bit items, which cannot pass
    that limit, carries no per-item check);
    `.enumerate()` over `u8`/`u16`/`bool`/`f32` or `u64` items compiles;
    `<[T]>::swap` handles any element of up to 16 aligned lanes. wasm32
    `flat_map(..).count()` and a `chain` count whose half can itself
    overflow are refused by name (`[TCG-ITER-UNMODELED]`).
  - rustc bridge C ABI and compile resources. A C-ABI 8- or 16-bit integer
    held in a one-lane memory slot (`Option<NonZeroU8>`,
    `Option<NonZeroU16>`, `Option<#[repr(u8)] enum>`,
    `Result<(), NonZeroU8>`, a newtype around one, `(u8,)`, `(u16,)`,
    `Option<NonZeroI8>`) is passed and returned with rustc's `ArgExtension`
    on every target; before, wasm32 sign-extended unsigned values and Apple
    AArch64 zero-extended signed ones, so an LLVM-built crate, a C function
    or a host read wrong values. A declaration that cannot carry the
    extension is refused as `[TCG-ARG-ABI]`/`[TCG-RET-ABI]`. On wasm32 a
    `#[repr(C)]` struct around one `i128`/`u128` crosses `extern "C"` as
    rustc's cast (two `i64` halves; a return through the caller's buffer)
    instead of being refused. Two `extern` items sharing a `#[link_name]`
    whose signatures lower to different value shapes are refused
    (`[TCG-ARG-ABI]`) or kept out of the merged module. Exact
    retained-address callee summaries are solved once per crate, callees
    first, and the points-to state once per body: a 300-deep call chain
    passing a local's address compiles in 0.9 s instead of 21 s, with
    byte-identical objects (each body keeps its own reach cap). A momentary
    host-memory reading narrows the large-stack worker width but never
    refuses a compile, and when the fixed-module executor cannot spawn its
    workers it compiles inline. The four native tests that
    `[TCG-ASSERT-PANIC]` broke reach array elements through `get`,
    patterns or iterators and pass again.
  - Output quality: `benchmarks/wasm-vs-llvm/`, the wasm32 output-quality
    ratchet. It compiles 144 committed programs for wasm32 at
    `-C opt-level=2` with the bridge and with rustc+LLVM (B1; B1 plus
    `wasm-opt -O2` as B2 context) and checks every export on a
    deterministic grid. A disagreement, a signed-zero difference on an
    export the manifest does not list, or a trust-cg module that fails to
    compile, instantiate or return where LLVM's ran is a reject. It measures
    file and code bytes, static and instrumented dynamic counts, the
    shadow-stack high-water (stack-pointer writes and memory touched below
    the stack pointer) and node timing in default, TurboFan-only and
    Liftoff-only tiers. `scripts/check_perf_ratchet.py` routes its results
    to a new `wasm32` ledger row family (`scripts/wasm_perf_ratchet.py`):
    deterministic metrics are ratcheted with zero tolerance per toolchain
    and measuring-code digest, timing with a 10% floor per host and engine.
    The first row (at `3af946d8f`; not evidence: loaded host) reads 2.77x
    file bytes, 2.05x TurboFan time and 1.98x stack against B1. The plan is
    `docs/wasm32_perf_roadmap.md`.
  - Output quality, bridge (roadmap P1b/P1c). On wasm32 the bridge emits
    trust-ir's own `ctpop`/`ctlz`/`cttz`/`bswap`/`bitreverse`/`rotl`/`rotr`
    at the receiver's width for the integer bit methods, their intrinsics
    and self-funnel rotates, instead of a 64-bit or-smear and popcount; a
    width-sensitive bit op on a pointer-word class is refused
    (`[TCG-WASM32-WORD]`) rather than retyped. It reads a constant aggregate
    of two bytes or more from its read-only data global instead of
    rebuilding it byte by byte on every call: directly when the local is
    only read as scalars (core's `isqrt` tables, for example), otherwise
    with one `memcopy`. Native output is unchanged (objects byte-identical
    on 186 compiles). The lane's 128-bit `mul.overflow` (P1a, already
    upstream as `Inst::Overflow` for every target) gains edge-class
    differentials against the trust-ir interpreter and LLVM.
  - Output quality, lane (roadmap P2). 128-bit `udiv`/`urem`/`sdiv`/`srem`
    call one per-module trust-ir helper, compiled by the lane itself, instead
    of a 128-iteration restoring loop inlined at every site. The helper has
    fast paths for 64-bit operands, for a 64-bit divisor (two-step long
    division, Knuth D on 32-bit digits) and a short normalized shift-subtract
    for wider divisors. A closed module carries one copy; an object defines it
    as a weak hidden `__tcg_divmod128_<digest>` symbol, so several trust-cg
    objects link with one copy. Every object refuses a module that names any
    `__tcg_divmod128_` symbol, whether or not that module divides
    (`[TCG-WASM-SYMBOL]`). Checking only dividing modules let a crate link
    when the bridge's per-function fallback put a user definition of the name
    and the division into different objects, and that definition replaced the
    helper. An object trust-cg did not compile can still define the name.
    Results on a zero divisor and on `MIN / -1`, which trust-ir leaves
    undefined, are unchanged, and no trap is added. Evidence is execution
    only: an interpreter differential on edge classes and random operands
    (closed and linked), a link test with several trust-cg objects plus a
    clang object, and the bridge wasm32 differential.
  - Combined, on the committed harness at OPT=2 (not evidence: dirty tree and
    runaway processes on the host; one run of each bridge back to back),
    trust-cg / B1 moves from the `3af946d8f` bridge to the round-7 bridge:
    file bytes 2.77x -> 2.59x, dynamic instructions 7.88x -> 7.01x, stack
    high-water 1.98x -> 1.68x, time 2.20x -> 2.02x (default tiering) and 2.04x
    -> 1.86x (TurboFan only). 144/144 programs agree with LLVM; 57 get smaller
    and none larger, 54 execute fewer instructions and none more. Declared
    locals rise 4.6% (largest in the bit-op and constant-table programs, since
    the lane still declares one local per SSA value) and the division helper
    adds calls (+2.4%). Both are ratcheted with zero tolerance, so the trade
    is a reviewed entry in `ratchet/perf_baseline.json` and the first wasm32
    evidence row must be measured at or after this round. Details in section
    0.1 of `docs/wasm32_perf_roadmap.md`; run identities and hashes in
    `reports/perf/2026-10-01-r7-wasm32-merge/`.
  - Merged with main at trust-ir `8a0d54c0`. Both wasm lanes refuse the v53
    non-propagating call boundaries (`Inst::CallCannotUnwind`,
    `Inst::CallIndirectCannotUnwind`) by name through the shared floor, and
    `wasm::lower_function` refuses them in its own per-function scan too (a
    function its module does not hold never reaches the floor); an ordinary
    call in the same place compiles. The pin's new must-refuse row
    `unop_not_scalar_bool` (trust-ir WS2.21) was compiled by both wasm
    lanes into a `Bool` of -1/-2; every wasm entry now refuses `Neg`, `Not`
    and `CtPop` at a non-integer type by name, as the native adapter does,
    and `must_refuse_corpus` drives that row through both wasm lanes. The
    rustc bridge's
    `[TCG-POINTER-CARRIER-STORE]` guard, new on main, compares the pointee
    with the session's pointer width instead of 8 bytes: with the literal,
    every wasm32 `slice::Iter::next_back` (`.iter().rev()`) store of its
    4-byte `end` pointer was refused.
- An eighth wasm32 round (admission, the validated emission pass, bridge array
  iteration):
  - wasm32 admission. The closed-module, object and single-function entries
    now admit their input as the native entries do. Each runs trust-ir's
    codegen admission (`validate_codegen_prerequisites`, which no policy
    widens), then the caller's codegen-license policy. The new
    `compile_module_with_license`, `compile_module_with_policy_and_license`,
    `compile_module_with_evidence_policy_and_license`,
    `compile_object_with_license` and
    `compile_object_with_evidence_and_license` entries take that policy
    (`compile_object_with_license_optimized`,
    `compile_object_with_evidence_license_optimized` and
    `compile_module_with_evidence_policy_license_optimized` take it with an
    optimization level); the existing entries keep the default. The CLI's wasm
    path now honors `--recognize-authority` and `--refuse-unlicensed`, and the
    rustc bridge passes its session policy. The lane also refuses, with the
    native reasons: a `RegionHavocStore` marker, an annotated `Undef` and an
    `Undef` outside the native scalar carrier set; a non-array `ArraySplat`; a
    pointer op at a non-pointer type or with a result arity other than one; a
    `PtrMetadata` or `PtrFromParts` whose metadata type is not the pointer's
    metadata at 32-bit pointers; an `AlwaysMemory` module, and an
    `Unclassified` module passing an aggregate by value; and a C declaration
    whose narrow parameter has a recorded slot with no recorded extension.
    `wasm32_target_info` now stamps `NativeC`, and the bridge keeps its own
    `struct_passing` claim. Both wasm lanes are full lanes of both
    `must_refuse_corpus` targets, so
    `body_gate_kernel_tv_without_certificate`,
    `body_gate_refuted_by_failed_tv` and the rows the default license had
    masked are refused by name. Before the emission pass was merged, emitted
    bytes were unchanged for every admitted program measured (144 benchmark
    programs and 2,457 audit jobs); with it, the merged bridge's O0 output
    still equals the round-7 bridge's (39 of 39 sampled audit programs that
    compile at O0, compared on every non-custom section, and 40 of 40 at O2
    with `no-wasm-local-opt`).
  - wasm32 local emission pass (roadmap P3, stages A and B). At O1 and above,
    `wasm/opt.rs` and `wasm/opt/rewrite.rs` rewrite each function: single-use
    stackify with `local.tee`, dead-definition drop/vacuum, narrow-mask and
    sign-extension elimination, memarg offset folding where the address
    provably does not wrap (through the frame base only under a closed
    module's stack guard), loads and stores in place of a `memory.copy` of at
    most 32 constant bytes, copy-affinity colouring of locals, self-copy
    deletion, reordering by use count, and constant rematerialization
    including chains of copies. A rewritten function is emitted only when the
    new `trust_cg_verify::wasm_local_tv` accepts it against the lane's own
    body, per straight-line segment: identical control; equal ordered effect
    traces (addresses as base plus offset, folded only under a no-wrap bound
    it re-derives), end stacks and live-out locals over hash-consed terms; one
    term per evaluation of a float operation whose NaN result is
    nondeterministic; typed `global.get` results; its own stack heights
    re-checked against wasm typing; memory 0 only. A residual equality refuses
    the function, so no solver runs while compiling and the bytes do not
    depend on the host; any function the validator does not accept keeps its
    baseline body. At O0 (the bridge's debug default) and with the new bridge
    kill switch `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=no-wasm-local-opt`, every function keeps
    its pre-pass bytes. New entries `wasm::compile_object_optimized`,
    `compile_object_with_evidence_optimized` and
    `compile_module_with_evidence_and_policy_optimized` take the level; the
    entries without one compile at O2. The bridge follows `-C opt-level` or
    its `opt-level` knob; the CLI's wasm route always compiles at O2 and still
    refuses an explicit `-O`. `WasmCompileEvidence::local_emission` reports
    whether the pass ran, its counts and its fallback reasons; the verdict
    stays `MissingEvidence`. The bridge knob `trace-wasm-local-opt` prints the
    per-CGU summary. The wasm ABI evidence family checks the lane's O0 bytes,
    and a gate requires every optimized fixture function to be a validated
    rewrite of them; the P4 encoding tally is now 208 proven / 0 refuted / 110
    not-applicable. TV fallback rate: 0 of 1,746 functions on the harness
    corpus and 2 of 144,654 (0.0014%) on the 2,457-job audit replay with its
    O0 rows run at O2. Against rustc+LLVM -O2 on the committed harness (not
    evidence: loaded host and dirty tree, one run of each bridge back to back,
    the merged tree against `7bfbf6d39`): file bytes 2.60x -> 1.75x, code
    bytes 5.27x -> 2.73x, declared locals 5.90x -> 2.24x, dynamic instructions
    7.01x -> 3.10x, dynamic memory operations 3.46x -> 3.61x (the expanded
    small copies), time 2.01x -> 1.84x default tiering, 1.86x -> 1.79x
    TurboFan and 3.51x -> 1.83x Liftoff. All 144 programs agree with LLVM and
    every one is smaller. Against stage A alone, stackify slows
    `c28_iters__it_zip` (TurboFan) and `narrow_i8` (Liftoff) and
    dead-definition removal slows `s_cmp` (TurboFan). Sections 0.2-0.4 of
    `docs/wasm32_perf_roadmap.md` have the measurements.
  - wasm32 bridge array iteration. By-value array iteration no longer refuses
    its common shapes; they compile and match LLVM at -O0 through -O3: `for x
    in [a, b, c]`, `[..].into_iter()` chains
    (map/fold/sum/count/filter/any/all/find/skip/take/rev with non-capturing
    or by-reference closures), a partly consumed or returned
    `array::IntoIter`, and `next_back`/`nth`/`size_hint` on it. The
    `array::IntoIter` model reads its `alive` index width from rustc's layout
    at the session pointer width. In a wasm32 cdylib, its drop glue (a no-op
    for scalar elements) now lowers. On wasm32, `IndexRange::try_fold`, which
    the -O2 inliner exposes, is driven as a `Range<usize>` source, and core's
    own `size_hint`/`next_back`/`nth`/`advance_by`/`rfold` bodies run over
    that faithful state. Every other method that receives the iterator stays
    refused by `[TCG-OWNING-ITER-METHOD]`. Native code generation is
    unchanged. 18 programs were built as rlibs at O0 and O2 with the merged
    and the `7bfbf6d39` bridges. 13 give byte-identical crate objects (246 in
    all; 10 at both levels and 3 at O2 only, with identical refusals at O0),
    including the 121 objects at O0 and 79 at O2 of the bridge-width probe
    that exercises the width-keyed `array::IntoIter` paths. Both bridges
    refuse the other 5 identically at both levels. New corpus crate:
    `wasm32_differential/r8-bridge-width.rs` (39 exports, six configurations).

    - Interval-bounded unrolling (`bounded_unroll`, OD-159): a loop whose
      exit test the checker proves taken on visit `B <= 8` from intervals
      of values defined before the loop becomes `B` copies that keep their
      exit tests. `min_zip2` TurboFan 4.00x -> 1.76x B1.
    - The select-branch rules (`select_branch`, OD-160): a `switch` or
      `condbr` decided by a named `bool` branches on it, and a `select` on

      TurboFan 2.86x -> 1.81x B1, its file 1,024 bytes larger.

      has its type's whole range, an edge into the entry guards nothing,

      block. The rustc bridge always opens a function with a fresh entry
      block, so no Rust program reached either case.

  - wasm32 mid-end full unrolling, strength reduction and invariant code
    motion's tier (b) (round 14 stage A and its fixup, O1 to O3 only).
    Eight passes join the `Wasm32` profile (fifty passes in all):
    constant folding; algebraic simplification; full unrolling of
    constant-trip loops; address folding of the bridge's integer address
    chains into `gep`s; removal of dead block parameters; block merging;
    induction-variable strength reduction with pointer roots; and lowering
    of the bridge's `extractfield`/`insertfield` through a pointer to the
    load or store the lane emits (OD-121).
    - Full unrolling keeps side exits (OD-118). It unrolls at most 16
      trips (the checker accepts 32) and at most 1,024 copied
      instructions, of which an estimated 256 survive constant folding
      (OD-122). There is no cost model.
    - Invariant code motion now also hoists a load past non-volatile
      stores to provably other bytes of an `alloca` or global.
    - Dead-code elimination removes a dead `inttoptr` from an integer no
      wider than a wasm32 address, and dead shifts and divisions by a
      constant that cannot fault (OD-117).
    - A refused output first re-runs the mid-end once without the loop
      passes, block merging and field-access lowering, before the inliner
      is withdrawn (OD-119).
    - Each rewrite carries a witness that an independent
      `trust_ir_mid_tv` checker rebuilds, and the interpreter differential
      runs on it.
    - The fixup corrects tier (b)'s allocation identity (OD-123). Stage A
      treated two `global_addr` of one global as two allocations. A
      `#[thread_local]` probe then returned a wrong value at O1 to O3, and
      the new bridge differential crate `r14-bridge-loop-memory.rs` keeps
      it. Both the pass and the checker now identify an allocation by its
      `alloca` or its global's name.
    - The fixup also adds a simplification rule that rewrites a rotate
      whose every use masks only the bits it brings round into a right
      shift (OD-124). V8's Liftoff calls out of line for a rotate, and
      the unrolled `cmp_accum` had gone from 3.44x to 3.86x B1 under
      Liftoff. The fixup's run measured 1.38x.

      measurements.

  - wasm32 mid-end closed-form induction and loop-invariant code motion
    (round 13 stage A and its fixup). Two passes join the `Wasm32` profile
    at O1 and above after the range rules (twenty-six passes in all).
    Closed-form induction (`passes/loop_cf.rs`) replaces a counted loop
    that exits only from its header on `<u`, `<s` or `!=` of a `+ 1`
    induction variable against an invariant bound, has an acyclic body of
    removable instructions, and whose other header parameters are
    invariant or affine accumulators of the induction variable (directly,
    or its `zext` under `<u` / `sext` under `<s`), by its trip count and
    their final values computed in the preheader, modulo each
    accumulator's width, as LLVM does for `(0..n).sum()`; the trip count
    at a wider type and the induction sum are computed once per type and
    extension and shared. Loop-invariant code motion (`passes/licm.rs`)
    replaces unchanged header parameters by their preheader argument and
    moves invariant instructions that cost a wasm operation to the
    preheader under the native pass's tier (a), restated over trust-ir's
    poison semantics: speculatable forms on never-poison, well-typed
    operands, or instructions guaranteed to execute in the header, a load
    only out of a loop with no store, call, allocation or atomic. Each
    rewrite is kept only when its independent checker
    (`trust_ir_mid_tv_loop.rs`, its own loop, dominance, never-poison and
    typing analyses; OD-89, OD-90) and the interpreter differential accept
    it; the closed form's algebra is eight lemmas checked by tests, not a
    per-compile proof (OD-91). The fixup made the checker re-derive operand
    types for speculation after a review probe showed it accepting a
    hoisted ill-typed `add`. The round's final fixup makes the checker and
    the pass read a constant shift amount or divisor as the bits it holds
    at the operation's width (OD-97), after a review probe showed both
    accepting `sdiv u32 x, 4294967295` (a division by -1, which traps on
    `0x80000000`) as speculatable and the interpreter differential missing
    the overflowing dividend. The merge fixup makes the pass admit only the
    constants the checker types, and both admit the bridge's
    global-address stub of a module global at offset zero, so a loop
    indexing a static by an invariant index is no longer rolled back
    (OD-99); the differential's view gives a global the module only
    declares a 1 MiB zero-filled object, so a read past its placeholder
    type no longer reads another allocation (OD-100). Of the 144 harness
    programs only `sl_ptr` changes, at O2 (1,930 -> 1,848 file bytes: the
    scalar replacement in `e_from_raw_parts` is no longer rolled back); the
    round's measurements above predate the fixup. The CFG structural gate's two loop shapes now
    accumulate by `xor` so the optimizing lane keeps their loops (OD-92).
    Strength reduction, unswitching, LICM tier (b) and bottom-tested loops
    are not done. Sections 0.19 and 0.21 of `docs/wasm32_perf_roadmap.md`
    have the measurements.
  - wasm32 P7 trigger measured, and a validated control cleanup in the
    local emission pass (round 13 stage B and its fixup). With binaryen

    refuses a compile (OD-94); a panic handler's `loop {}` is the only

  - wasm32 mid-end argument promotion and constant 128-bit shifts (round 12
    stage A and its fixup). At O1 and above a frame slot whose address
    escapes only into plain calls of functions defined in the module, at
    parameters those callees use only as the address of plain loads and
    stores (and the bridge's field access through a pointer) at constant
    offsets, is passed to a clone of one such callee as the values of the
    scalar fields the callee reads; the clone returns the fields it writes
    after its own results, through the internal multi-value ABI, and the
    caller stores them back (`passes/argpromo.rs`, run callees first after
    the first scalar replacement and constant-table promotion, followed by
    the pointer-chain rewrite, copy propagation and dead-code elimination:
    twenty-four passes in all).
    A parameter of an aggregate type the bridge passes by address is
    promoted to the lanes the callee reads. Only a strong hidden callee
    under the bridge's crate-private name is cloned, as
    `<symbol>.tcg.ap<h>.tcg.crate.<tag>`; the original stays for every
    other caller. Every byte copied in at the call (an aggregate's lanes
    included) and every byte copied out at a `ret` must be last written on
    every path by a value that is never poison; the slot must be reached by
    no other argument of the call; a call carrying a proof annotation or
    proof context is left alone. The independent checker
    (`trust_ir_mid_tv_argpromo.rs`) shares only the clone-name function with
    the pass and re-derives every premise, the clone and the rewrite, with
    negative controls per premise. Because a clone copies its callee's
    validation findings, the lane re-runs the mid-end without the unclean
    clones' callees (`argpromo_callees`), then without the pass
    (`argpromo`). A pair-carried 128-bit value shifted or rotated by an
    integer constant now uses that amount's constant half shifts
    (`lower/wide.rs`). The fixup withdrew stage A's exemption of arrays
    passed by address from the slot and never-poison premises: the lane
    reads such an array's lanes lazily and the bridge lowers
    `[MaybeUninit<T>; N]` as `[T x N]`. Over the 144 harness programs at O2
    the bridge's trace counts `alloca`s 748 -> 710 (41 promoted calls in 35
    callers, 0 rollbacks, 0 fallbacks); section 0.16 of
    `docs/wasm32_perf_roadmap.md` has the measurements.
  - wasm32 argument promotion's re-run ladder and clone admission (round 12
    final fixup). A refused output no clone is blamed for now withdraws the
    inliner's unclean callees, then the inliner, before the whole of
    argument promotion, which goes only if an output with clones is still
    refused after them; a clone whose own body carries a module-level
    finding (validated with every other body removed) now blames its
    callee. A plan whose clone would keep a parameter whose entry type
    differs from its declared one (which copies the callee's

    ranges and `switch` folding (round 12 stage B and its fixup). In a block
    entered by a single `condbr` edge, and in every block that edge
    dominates, an `icmp`'s operands are narrowed to the hull of their values
    that satisfy it, and a later compare of the same two values the
    dominating one decides is folded (`icmp_implied`). A block parameter
    carries a claimed interval that the checker verifies on every incoming
    edge (entry and step), which folds counted-loop bounds and overflow
    checks. A `switch` drops the cases (and the default) its value's
    interval excludes and becomes a branch when one edge is left. The
    checker (`trust_ir_mid_tv_range.rs`) recomputes reverse postorder,
    dominance and each edge's condition itself; narrowing and implication
    agree with brute force at widths 1-4 in the pass and in the checker

    compile). The fixup indexes guard facts by dominator-tree preorder in
    both the pass and the checker, so deep guard chains compile in linear
    time (a program of 1,000 sequential early exits compiles at O2 in
    8.50-8.59 s with the unindexed stage B bridge and 1.56-1.57 s with the

  evidence): all 144 programs match LLVM; file bytes 1.649x -> 1.574x B1,

  dynamic memory operations 3.124x -> 2.540x, dynamic calls 1.543x ->
  1.322x, stack high-water 1.562x -> 1.485x, and TurboFan time 1.717x ->
  1.541x (framed functions 798 -> 723); no program executes more
  instructions, 2 have larger code (inlining). The differential compares
  77.8% of the merged pipeline's candidate rewrites on the harness corpus
  and 86.1% on the audit replay's O2 half, and the 2,457-job audit replay
  agrees with LLVM on every job (5,000,098 checks). The combined output
  equals stage B's alone except in `sl_ptr`, where the differential rolls
  back a promotion in a function reading a static its codegen unit only
  declares (the interpreter's object for it is smaller than the array).
  Section 0.12 of `docs/wasm32_perf_roadmap.md` has the measurements.
  - wasm32 mid-end, interpreter differential. The differential behind every
    irmid rewrite (`trust_cg_verify::trust_ir_mid_tv::Harness`, new
    `trust_ir_mid_tv_harness.rs`) now builds inputs for pointer, slice and
    by-value aggregate parameters, not only scalars. Memory is planned from
    the function's own accesses (four calls and three pointer slots deep)
    and the interpreter's layout and passed by a driver function; for a
    function with two or more pointer or slice parameters two more inputs
    bind them to one object (same base, and the second part-way into the
    first). Module callees run through the call; fuel is sized from the
    function and its loops (at most 262,144 steps, 65,536 when a loop
    allocates); globals the function and its callees name (up to 64 beyond
    its own) are allocated before the call, so a pointer to one keeps its
    identity. After the call the bytes of the input's memory the source left
    initialised are read back and compared; struct padding or poison narrows
    the read instead of dropping it. The runs interpret a typed view of the
    rustc bridge's lane idioms, with alignment 1 as wasm executes them. Each
    compared input names what it observed (memory, results or a panic); an
    input on which both sides return with nothing to compare is not counted,
    and every candidate not compared is counted under one reason, per pass,
    in `IrmidReport::tv` (additive fields, among them
    `samples_memory_narrowed`, `samples_aliased_compared` and
    `samples_nothing_observed`). Alone, it leaves the emitted code
    unchanged (byte-identical at O0-O3 on the 144-program harness corpus);
    measured on its own tree, candidates compared rose from 19.9% to
    80.2% on the harness corpus and from 19.8% to 87.6% on the audit replay's
    O2 half. New negative controls catch a wrong forwarding through a
    pointer parameter, a wrong DCE of a call-reachable store, a wrong
    forwarding between aliased parameters, a store dropped beside struct
    padding and a pointer to the wrong global, none of which the
    scalar-only differential could reach.
  - wasm32 mid-end, scalar replacement (P5 stage A, `passes/sroa.rs`). A
    count-free frame slot reached only by plain loads and stores through
    `gep`s by constants, `ptrtoptr`s to thin pointers and copies, whose
    accesses each cover one of its disjoint fields, becomes one SSA value per
    field, joined by new block parameters placed by a postorder liveness
    worklist. A same-width view of a field is a `bitcast`, or a
    `ptrtoint`/`inttoptr` through `ptr` for a pointer, and only of values
    that can never be the poison image of uninitialized bytes. Mixed widths,
    partial overlaps, volatile and atomic accesses, escaping or observed
    addresses, undefined reads, a stored `undef`, 128-bit fields, joins at
    the entry or behind an unwind edge, unreachable blocks and irreducible
    CFGs are left alone. The checker (`trust_ir_mid_tv_sroa.rs`,
    `PassWitness::Sroa`) re-derives the slot on the source and proves every
    claimed reaching definition and block-parameter argument by backward
    walks over all CFG paths; each rewritten access counts as a refinement.
    Dead-code elimination now also removes `gep`/`ptrtoptr`/copy chains
    rooted at a fresh allocation, so promoted slots leave the frame, and a
    function left without slots emits no prologue, epilogue,
    `__stack_pointer` update or stack guard (`tests/wasm_p5_sroa.rs` also
    pins the frame-bounds guard on a frame that remains).
  - wasm32 mid-end, call-site inlining (P5 stage B, `passes/inline.rs`): the
    OPT-4 inliner ported to `trust_ir::Function`, run callees-first after the
    scalar cleanup and before store forwarding and scalar replacement, so a
    small callee's out-pointer becomes the caller's promotable slot. Callees
    of at most 12 instructions with no `alloca` are inlined at every call;
    single-call-site callees that are not exported and never address-taken
    up to 400 instructions; loop-free callees up to 40 instructions within
    caller and module growth caps. Never spliced: a recursive callee, a
    link-replaceable one (weak, linkonce, the ODR forms, extern_weak,
    available_externally) or a proof-carrying one. A spliced slot is part of
    the caller's frame for its whole activation, so an allocating callee is
    never spliced into a loop, with a slot made in a loop of its own, or into
    a caller on a cycle of direct calls, and one caller takes at most 1,024
    bytes of spliced slots.
    `#[inline(never)]` and `#[cold]` are honoured through a bridge side table
    (`WasmInlineHints`, `MidConfig::never_inline`; no trust-ir change). Each
    splice is checked by `trust_ir_mid_tv_inline.rs`, which re-derives
    admission, the stack bound, the argument binding and freshness, rebuilds
    the caller and runs OPT-4's CFG, single-definition and
    opcode-conservation checks; each splice counts as a refinement. An output
    with a splice that the validator or the admission refuses (a splice
    copies its callee's findings) re-runs the mid-end without the spliced
    callees whose bodies carry a finding, then without the inliner; the final
    report names every withdrawal (`passes_withheld`: `inline_callees`,
    `inline`). New
    bridge corpus crate `wasm32_differential/r10-bridge-inline-stack.rs`
    pins the stack bound (an allocating callee spliced into a recursive
    caller overflowed the stack before it).
- A ninth wasm32 round (output quality: emission-pass tuning and the trust-ir
  mid-end):
  - wasm32 local emission tuning and CLI `-O`. Single-use stackify may no
    longer raise the number of same-type locals live at a local write above
    the input's peak for that type (`opt/rewrite.rs`, counted in
    `RewriteStats::pressure_kept`). Where that kept a definition in its
    local, the unlimited candidate is built too, and the pass emits the
    validated candidate with fewer code bytes (then fewer declared locals),
    or, at a cost of at most 4 bytes, the pressure-limited one when it
    declares at most 12 locals, all `i32`/`i64`, and the other declares more:
    V8 Liftoff caches only that many integer locals (measured on arm64 V8
    14.6; one `f32`/`f64` local disables the cache). The pass also removes
    dead `local.tee`/`local.set` writes before and after colouring; a
    candidate the translation validator refuses after that removal is rebuilt
    once without it, and the first refusal is counted by reason in
    `WasmLocalOptSummary::dead_write_retries` (and its JSON). Every candidate
    still goes through `wasm_local_tv`. `trust-cg --target wasm32` now
    accepts `-O0` to `-O3` and passes the level to both wasm routes: `-O0`
    emits each function's baseline body byte for byte and runs neither
    optimization, `-O1` to `-O3` run the mid-end and the local emission pass,
    and the default stays `-O2`. Measured alone against `3ac43e732` (loaded
    host, not evidence): no program larger or executing more instructions, 98
    smaller, declared locals 2.238x -> 2.211x B1, Liftoff time 0.983x, and
    `narrow_i8` under Liftoff 3.06x -> 1.80x B1; TV fallback stays at 2 of
    144,654 functions on the audit replay. The other reported slowdowns
    (`s_cmp`, `min_sf4`, `c19_smallagg__e_a1`, `c28_iters__it_zip`) were
    traced to V8 TurboFan's caller-relative inlining budget and stay open.
  - wasm32 trust-ir mid-end, P4 stage A. A new crate, `trust-cg-irmid`
    (profile `Wasm32`), rewrites the module before lowering at O1 and above
    (`wasm/mid.rs`): copy propagation; `inttoptr(ptrtoint(alloca) + k)` to a
    byte-offset `gep` for an in-bounds constant `k`; constant-branch folding
    with unreachable-block removal; and pure dead-code elimination that keeps
    every instruction whose definedness depends on its operands' values and
    the bridge's write-through `insertfield`. There is no constant CSE. Per
    pass and per function, a rewrite is kept only when the independent
    witness checker `trust_cg_verify::trust_ir_mid_tv` accepts it and the
    reference interpreter finds no disagreement on eight seeded inputs
    (scalar parameters only; inputs on which the source raises undefined
    behaviour excluded; coverage counted, never implied); otherwise that
    function is rolled back. Each pass's proof table goes through a validated
    `ProofTableTransformTransaction` (every obligation `Preserved`), and
    proof-carrying functions are skipped. The optimized module is emitted
    only when it passes the input's admission again, adds no trust-ir
    validator finding (module-wide by kind, and by full text in each changed
    function), the lane lowers it, and the CFG structural invariant is not
    refuted on its bytes; any failure falls back to the input. The input is
    lowered as well (its baseline bodies) and its admission or lowering
    refusal is the compile's; an entry that reports the CFG structural
    invariant (the evidence entries, every object) also checks it on that
    lowering of the input and fails the compile when it is refuted there. O0
    output is unchanged. The bridge knob `no-wasm-irmid` switches the
    mid-end off and `trace-wasm-irmid` prints its report;
    `WasmCompileEvidence` gains an additive `mid_end` (`"irmid"`) field
    (schema name unchanged, pending owner review). New entries
    `compile_object_with_license_options`,
    `compile_object_with_evidence_license_options` and
    `compile_module_with_evidence_policy_license_options` take
    `WasmOptOptions` (level, mid-end on or off). At O1 and above a one-byte
    GEP index is added unscaled.
  - wasm32 trust-ir mid-end, P4 stage B. After stage A's cleanup the
    `Wasm32` profile runs single-dominating-store forwarding (a load from a
    frame slot used only by plain loads and stores, directly or at a
    constant byte offset, becomes the stored value when one store is the
    last write of exactly those bytes on every path; integer, `bool`, `char`
    and float values of the load's own type only; pointers, partial
    overlaps, mixed widths, undefined reads and irreducible CFGs are left

    promotion (a local table written only with integer or `bool` constants,
    read within proven bounds, whose address is never observed or passed on,

    propagation and DCE again. Each has a witness checker in
    `trust_ir_mid_tv` that re-derives the slot or table on the source with

  - The promoted table's static data never shortens the stack the input had.
    The CLI's closed module goes through the new
    `compile_sized_closed_module_with_evidence_license_{optimized,options}`,

    run of a pass, and `refinements` as covering dead-slot store removal and

  - Combined, against `3ac43e732` on the committed wasm-vs-LLVM harness
    (one run of each bridge back to back, loaded host and dirty tree, not
    evidence): all 144 programs match LLVM; file bytes 1.748x -> 1.649x B1,
    code bytes 2.731x -> 2.518x, declared locals 2.238x -> 2.107x, static memory

    `local.set` reached a join, no longer touches memory, and the first-site

    have the measurements.
- L14-P5 / L14-P6 (warm compile time, `aarch64-apple-darwin`): a fresh
  profile of warm bridge compiles, and the largest costs it found removed
  without changing one emitted byte. Evidence strength: measurement on one
  shared M4 Max (Trust 9192, 1-minute load 9 to 32 during the runs, so wall
  time is reported only with its load and decisions use instructions
  retired and peak RSS from `/usr/bin/time -l`), plus unit differentials
  against the code each change replaced. No proof claim; the
  `no-proof-certs` lane is never ledger evidence. Reproducers:
  [`reports/perf/2026-10-01-darwin-warm-compile-l14p5p6/commands/`](reports/perf/2026-10-01-darwin-warm-compile-l14p5p6/commands/build.sh)

  - **Profile (base = `main` `aca923418`).** A warm `p3_gcd` compile's main
    thread spends 237 ms in the Trust front end's whole-crate verification
    (`CleanIslandSession::new`), which the LLVM lane runs too, then 94 ms in
    `codegen_crate`, 83 ms of it the MIR-to-trust-ir refinement lane: nine
    stored-certificate replays (a fresh Clean process each, 4 to 14 ms) and a
    resident AY start, one after another. The backend proper (ISel 0.1 ms,
    optimization 1.4 ms, register allocation 1.1 ms per CGU) is about 6 ms.

    about 117 ms of CPU) are custody checks and stay. On compile-scaling's
    120-loop function (CLI, `TRUST_CG_TIME_PASSES` and `xctrace`, 5.96 G

    re-analysis (81 ms), neon-fill's loop-state liveness walks (53 of its
    59 ms), the allocator (59 ms, 41 of them the allocation validator's
    value flow), the post-RA spill-slot frame net (49 ms), encoding (31 ms)

    functions, 74.7 G) the serial lowering thread spent 633 ms re-probing
    the solver for every function and 114 ms in the SSA loop-completeness
    check's dominance walks.
  - **Changes.** (1) Certificate replay prefetch
    (`trust_cg_verify::cert_replay_prefetch`): each compile records the
    certificates it consumed as a per-scope hint, and the next compile of
    the same scope replays them on the identity-warm thread while the front
    end runs. Each prefetch replay is the consume path's full check, and only
    a success enters the positive replay memo, under the key the consume path
    derives from the exact query, certificate bytes, solver identity and
    authority context; a hint is an untrusted scheduling input and a stale
    one costs background replays, never a verdict. Kill switch
    `no-replay-prefetch`. (2) The default refinement lane's solver probe runs
    once per crate (`CrateRefineMemo::default_lane_solver_available`); each
    query still admits and revalidates its AY. (3) O(1) dominance in
    `ssa_loop_complete`. (4) One `LoopStateIndex` per neon-fill recognition
    sweep: liveness from a whole-function index once the literal walks have
    cost as much, the same least fixpoint. (5) Dense `DomTree` tables. (6)
    Dense vreg-use and layout indexes in the loop-latch-layout driver.
