- trust-ir dialect constructs are legalized by a registry (`L05-P11`;
  `trust_cg_codegen::dialect_legalization`, wired into `Compiler::compile` and
  `compile_module_to_jit`). A registration declares a namespace, version,
  semantic owner, payload grammar, and one rule per op (kept for the adapter,
  rewritten through trust-ir's `lower_module`, a bound runtime call with a
  payload descriptor, or a stated refusal) and per nominal type (a core
  carrier, admitted only under trust-ir's nominal rule). Malformed
  registrations and unregistered dialects, ops and types are refused by exact
  name (`[TCG-DIALECT-*]`); the legalized module is re-validated and takes the
  core adapter and proof path; each applied rule leaves a replayable receipt on
  `CompilationResult`/`JitCompilationResult::dialect_legalization` and in the
  CLI metrics (the registry digest names rules but cannot see their code;
  the replay compares their effect). Proof-required compiles (`emit_proofs`,
  or a verifying JIT validation mode on its own) admit only adapter-kept ops
  and the checked carrier substitution; cited-theorem, tested-only and
  runtime-contract rules are refused by name. A runtime call passes a nominal
  operand as its carrier; a dialect op spelling or consuming another
  namespace's nominal type is refused. New capability, AArch64 only (other
  targets refuse by name): `vector.reduce`/`shuffle` (trust-ir's
  `VectorLoweringPass`) and `vector.fma` (one fused `fmadd` per lane).
  Behaviour change: the default registry no longer applies trust-ir's
  illustrative `verif` lowering (an erased `frontier_drain`, a `bfs_step` call
  to function id 0); `verif` ops are refused unless a runtime is bound.
  Modules whose dialect ops all stay with the adapter reach it unchanged.
  Evidence strength: native differential tests on this macOS AArch64 host
  only: the pinned corpus's four dialect rows plus a per-op sweep and a
  runtime call over a nominal type, AOT and JIT at O0-O3, against trust-ir's
  reference interpreter or a source-payload reading, with `ty_dialect_v39`'s
  object byte-identical to its core twin; the Linux arm has not run. `mask_to_bits` of a parameter mask and
  `reduce`/`shuffle` of `<8 x i8>` stay refused by name.
- Linux AArch64 Rust bridge: keep cleanup-live scalars in stable frame cells,
  load live reference/one-leaf temporary values from those cells, check thin
  pointer wrapper projections, and use the actual unsigned `usize` allocator
  ABI. Preserve structural loop headers with memory-only carried state and
  type projected scalar borrows at their producer. Retry genuine thin raw
  pointers through checked cells while rerunning all admission gates.
  Independent LLVM/CG native controls cover O0–O3, normal returns and caught
  panics. Complete sealed
  candidate 17 attempts retain 441 full-graph and 114 std-body refusals; whole
  CG std/sysroot and formal qualification remain open. The
  October 1 audit binds every result to its
  source and records the separate evidence lanes.
- x86-64 latch merging: reject a tail splice when its predecessor has an
  earlier terminator, even if deduplicated CFG successors show a single edge.
  This preserves valid same-target conditional/unconditional branch pairs.
  The multi-block fuzz driver's row counter now expects its six scalar and
  six control inputs per seed.

- Source-bound negative memo: a timeout is remembered only when the QUERY
  ran out of its budget, not the host. The replay's budgets are wall-clock
  deadlines; on a host at load 40-80 the solves of bodies that certify at
  rest timed out, every such `Timeout` was recorded, and later processes were
  answered `Timeout` without solving for the entry's retry budget, so
  proof-required builds and six codegen/cli proof-promotion tests failed on
  that busy host. The subprocess supervisor now measures, before it kills a
  child whose deadline expired, the CPU time its whole process group used
  under the deadline (`subprocess::DeadlineExpiry`; AY solves in a worker it
  forks into the group; macOS through `proc_listpgrppids`/`proc_pid_rusage`
  converted by the Mach timebase, Linux through `/proc/<pid>/stat`, `None`
  elsewhere); the resident route measures one query's exchange. A `Timeout`
  is recorded only when the replay saw a deadline expire and every expiry
  used at least 90 % of its budget in CPU time; a starved, unmeasured or
  unexplained timeout records nothing and leaves an existing entry as it is.
  Schema and namespace move to v3 (`source-bound-negative-v3/`, entries carry
  `cpu-ms`), so the v2 entries of earlier builds, whose timeouts may be
  starved ones, are never read.
- AArch64 Mach-O objects bind module-local functions. `Compiler::compile`
  admits direct calls to and every address form of an Internal/Private
  function for Apple AArch64 triples (it used to refuse them with
  `AotDirectModuleFunctionBindingUnsupported` /
  `AotStaticFunctionIdentityBindingUnsupported`, as x86-64 and RISC-V still
  do). The emitted object is read back by an independent Mach-O reader: every
  `_f` spelling must be the one non-external (`N_EXT`/`N_PEXT` clear) `N_SECT`
  definition in an instruction section, and no external symbol, relocation,
  data atom or backend-made text reference may reach it
  (`AotModuleLocalFunctionBindingViolated`); a Mach-O code-reference backstop
  refuses a `BRANCH26` or personality reference into data
  (`AotCodeReferenceReachesData`). The ELF-only object facts (weak undefined
  references, function visibility and sections) are now a separate
  predicate and stay refused on Mach-O. A referenced module-local `sin` or
  `cos` is refused on Apple AArch64 (`ModuleLocalFunctionShadowsRuntimeSymbol`):
  the Darwin `sincos-merge` pass reads those callee names and replaced the
  module's calls with `___sincos_stret` (measured wrong value at O2/O3 before
  the refusal). Native macOS AArch64 controls: ld64 executables and
  `run_link` at O0-O3, dyld interposition into `-interposable` dylibs, and the
  linked-image replay (which refuses an image with two same-named local
  helpers rather than guess their owners).
- AArch64 instruction-derived obligations (`L07-P2`) now cover 13 more scalar
  memory opcodes: LDRSB/LDRSH with an immediate offset, W/X LDR/STR with
  pre-index or post-index writeback, and LDR/STR/LDRB/LDRH/STRB/STRH/LDRSW with
  a register offset. ENC-5 now also requires each admitted emitted word of
  these opcodes to equal the verifier's re-derived word. The obligation is not
  credit itself. It is the in-process refutation check that the Formal-only
  bound-memory rule requires, so on a host whose checker the manifest
  qualifies, the 24 general-purpose scalar forms it now judges are credited
  again by their committed form certificates. FP scalar forms stay uncredited.
  A writeback whose base is its transfer register and a W index under a 64-bit
  extend stay unadmitted.
- AArch64 pair-memory obligations: the pair decoder accepted a word with bit
  25 set (a data-processing word, not a pair), and a word whose `V` bit named
  the other register file at the same element width (W/S, X/D) held. Both are
  now refused by the obligation itself. Not wrong code: the function verifier
  decodes the word it re-derives from the operands, and the Formal-only rule's
  binding check already refused both words before consulting a certificate. A
  wrong-theorem control over every admitted pair shape now runs at the
  compiler's sample budget.
- trust-cg-opt: one loop-state contract for every rewrite that runs new code
  instead of scalar loop iterations. WHY: `p09_sieve` exited 192 (LLVM 198)
  at O2/O3 because `neon_bytesum`'s count-if kernel vectorized `count += 1`
  and skipped the `sum += i` in the same arm; a bool-load change later hid
  the guest, not the defect. Each pass carried its own partial statement of
  "what else the loop leaves", most checked only the carried half or only
  the exit half, and `neon_array` checked neither. MEASURED at `47f63ec1d`
  and again at `c84d39e93`, whole `no_std` programs built by the bridge
  against LLVM (byte-sum, byte-count, popcount, fill, zero-fill, i32-sum and
  count-if kernels with a second carried register or a live-out-only `last =
  i`, N in {0, 1, 15, 16, 63, 64, 1000, 1024}): 21 of 144 rows wrong at each
  of O2 and O3 on aarch64 and 37 of 144 on x86-64 under Rosetta, the same
  rows at both commits. On this change every row agrees on both targets at
  both levels, including four bottom-tested `last = i` kernels added after
  that measurement (no pass vectorizes that shape yet, before or after, so
  they guard a future rewrite); the count / byte-sum / i32-sum (and aarch64
  fill) controls keep the same vector code; `p7_sieve` and `v3_popcount`
  keep 23 and 18 NEON ops in `main` (unchanged) and agree with LLVM; on
  x86-64 `p4_matmul` still takes the saxpy-Q row-register nest and
  `v2_memfill` the fill tier, both exiting as LLVM does
  (`crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg/tests/opt_loop_state_run.rs`, a required
  target of the Darwin bridge runner now, its x86-64 rows under Rosetta).
  The same file adds the RUN lane the shared real-program corpus lacked
  (`real_program_corpus_a64` compiles with proof certificates on, so every
  row is refused `[TCG-PROOF-465]` and none ever runs: that is why
  `p09_sieve` was invisible): all 13 guests at O0, O2 and O3, linked and run
  against LLVM, proofs off. 37 of 39 rows agree and `p13_sort_std` at O2/O3
  is refused by name (`[TCG-MIR-UNSUPPORTED]`, `core::slice::sort`), the
  same before and after this change, listed in a shrink-only table.
  `src/loop_contract.rs` states the rule once over both machine IRs
  (`LoopStateView` for `MachFunction` and `X86ISelFunction`): every register
  carried across the back edge or live at an exit must be one the new code
  reproduces; flags are a register; calls, phis, physical-register operands
  and implicit register effects refuse. 24 AArch64 pass modules and every
  `x86_vectorize` plan build their plans only through its sealed
  `LoopLocality` token, and the private liveness scans they carried were
  deleted. Latent defects the move closed, each with a failing-first unit
  row: `neon_array`'s forward-chain reduction (the shape the bridge emits
  for `for i in 0..N` over a fixed array) fired with a second carried
  register and with a live-out-only one; `neon_farray` / `neon_fpred`
  admitted the post-increment index as a live-out although the vector code
  never writes it; the closed-form reduction deleted a loop whose induction
  was read after it (left at its initial value); `dead_loop` missed a
  narrower-view (`w` of an `x`) live-out and a flags read at the exit. With
  the contract bypassed, 46 unit tests fail (5 of them the contract's own
  table), at least one per routed pass except the x86 CRC-table and
  window-scan recognizers, which have no fixture anywhere. With only the
  EXIT half removed, 15 unit tests fail (three of the contract's own and
  live-out rows of 10 passes), but every whole-program row still agrees: the
  header half alone catches each measured live-out row, so the exit half's
  evidence is the unit rung. Built and tested with `targo --unverified` (no
  proof claim); the evidence is tests, not proof.

- trust-cg-opt: the loop-state contract's CONTROL clause. A rewrite that runs
  new code instead of scalar iterations is a refinement only if every way the
  scalar loop can leave is one the new code reproduces or one the pass proves
  no replaced iteration takes. WHY: the register clause alone let `neon_fill`
  vectorize fills whose loop also leaves by a `break`, a `return` or a bounds
  check against a shorter slice, and evaluate those exits only in the scalar
  remainder; `strided_store_unroll` admitted any exit into a panicking block
  although its unrolled stores carry no bounds checks. That is silent wrong
  code and out-of-bounds writes from safe Rust at O2/O3 on aarch64. MEASURED
  (aarch64, O2 and O3, the same rows at `c84d39e93` and on the register
  clause alone; x86-64 right on all of them): `while i < cap { if i == stop
  { break } *p.add(i) = 7; i += 1 }` with cap 1000 and stop 64 over a 64-byte
  buffer returned 1000 and wrote over 900 bytes past it; safe `while i < n {
  a[i] = 7; i += 1 }` over a 64-byte slice with n = 1000 wrote 896 to 903
  bytes past the slice before its bounds-check panic; the stride-3 marking
  loop `while q < 1024 { a[q] = 1; q += p }` over a 64-byte slice died of
  SIGSEGV where LLVM panics; and 30 whole-program early-exit rows per level
  (u8 / u32 / u64 fills and zero-fills, constant and runtime values and
  stops, `break` and `return` at index 40 or 700, a safe slice) were wrong.
  With the clause every row agrees on both targets
  (`crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg/tests/opt_loop_state_run.rs`:
  `pre_loop_rewrites_never_run_past_an_exit` and the program's
  `EXIT_KERNELS`). The contract enumerates the loop's exits itself
  (`loop_exits`: edges and fall-throughs out of the loop, trap carriers,
  returns, indirect branches); a plan accounts for each as its loop test, an
  exit the new code reproduces (`neon_find`'s match), or an exit proved
  untaken. Proved untaken is either a pre-guard the pass checks before its new
  code (`swap_range_guard`, `mac_row_unroll`, `mac_reg_block`, the x86
  saxpy-Q runtime obligations, the window scan), taken on the pass's word, or
  an unsigned bounds check of the induction against a bound at least the loop
  test's, which the contract admits only under its own conditions
  (`ExitPlan::and_induction_guards`: the check runs only in iterations the
  test admitted and before the induction's advance), so `a[i]` over an array
  of the loop's length still vectorizes. The exit checks
  `strided_store_unroll`, `mac_row_unroll` and `dead_loop` carried privately
  were deleted. A unit row the clause closed: `x86_vectorize`'s byte-eq count
  tier admitted a bounds carrier placed after the induction's advance, which
  traps on the last iteration, and its positive-control test encoded that.
  Dropping the clause again fails 12 unit tests, brings the three canary
  programs' wrong exits back, and stops the aarch64 loop-state program
  compiling (`strided_store_unroll` unrolls `strided_brk` past its `break`
  and the AArch64 spill-slot check refuses the result). The 18 beat-llvm
  programs give the same exit codes and the same vector-instruction counts
  as before the clause at O2 and O3 (`p7_sieve`, `v1_saxpy`, `v2_memfill`,
  `v3_popcount` and `b1_mispredict` keep theirs; four heap programs stay
  refused `[TCG-SSA-071]`). The review's probe of
  131 kernels (each its own program, 16 trip counts, aarch64 and x86-64 at O2
  and O3, 522 judged cells, LLVM as the oracle) changes in exactly the 20
  cells that were wrong (84 rows, all `neon_fill` exits): they agree now and
  lose that vector loop. Every other cell keeps its result, its refusal (27
  refused before and after, fail-closed) and its vector-instruction count.
  Built and tested with `targo --unverified` (no proof claim); the evidence
  is tests, not proof.

- x86-64 proof lane, slice 6 of the source-bound body theorem: acyclic
  control flow. A LIR CFG that is a DAG of at most sixteen blocks (`Jump`,
  `Brif` on a scalar, `Switch` whose cases are the adapter's normalized
  constants and whose edges reach different blocks, `Return`, `Trap`) is
  admitted path by path: each entry-to-end path (at most sixteen) is a
  slice 1-5 chain, a join's block parameters are the values its
  predecessor's copies defined on that path, and a path may end in a bare
  trap or a call-then-trap (reaching the trap is its observable end). Each
  source path is paired with its machine path through a one-to-one
  correspondence of machine and LIR blocks found from the rows' TV-1
  provenance, never from block ids, which O1+ passes renumber (a `jcc` is
  taken exactly when its target lowers the source's next block; every step
  is a real machine transfer, so soundness never rests on the pairing); the
  theorem is one `(or (not C_P) (and M_P O_P))` claim per
  path: the source's branch literals, the machine's `jcc` conditions through
  the shared EFLAGS model (every condition code; from a `cmp` or the newly
  modelled `test` of the same block; flags never cross a block boundary and
  a call leaves them undefined), and the path's observed items. A machine
  CFG without the correspondence (a block merged, if-converted, split,
  added, deleted or retargeted, a switch search tree, a jump to a
  selector-only block) makes no claim, never a named mismatch; nor does a
  jump table. A one-path source with a `jcc`-free machine is the slice 1-5
  chain, whatever its blocks. The exact affine refusal (a named return,
  call-argument or memory mismatch) applies to one-path bodies only: on
  several paths a value is observed under the path condition, which the
  theorem states and the affine evaluation does not. `test r, imm32` is
  admitted on a 64-bit register only (the encoder emits REX.W); loops stay
  `SourceShape` (whose message now names which bound or shape: `a loop`,
  `N blocks`, `N entry-to-end paths`, ...). `jcc` rows are covered, and
  credited, by the theorem. Slice 6 also admits `Select { NotEqual }`
  against `cmovcc`/`cmovcc32` (a tied destination), and a path's read of a
  private byte no store on it wrote, as the slot's initial value `f_k`
  shared with the machine. Encoding, by host qualification (AY 0.27.0 build
  10530, Clean 5f09e36c): `or`/`not` claims (the `=>` spelling is holey),
  no name defined for a copy, and only the definitions the claims depend
  on; on the Darwin `core` census's 345 several-path theorems that
  certifies 281 (162 with copies defined), and the qualification test pins
  the outcomes of the rejected spellings. All 25 fixture shapes and 3
  alternative machine forms certify, and 20 wrong lowerings are refuted
  (`x86_source_bound_body_slice6_tests.rs`, digest-pinned
  `slice6_snapshots.smt2`; the slice 1-5 snapshots are unchanged); the
  solver-free slice-6 tests run in a new soundness library gate
  (`x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice6::`), the replay in
  `slice6_qualification`. The e2e proof-required AOT test promotes six
  slice-6 bodies on Darwin and Linux, and a library test judges the real
  x86 optimizer's O1-O3 output of every fixture (13 of 25 build a theorem
  that holds at each level, 12 make no claim, none is a mismatch). Recorded
  successors are compared with a block's transfers as a set: the
  branch-layout pass reorders the transfers, not the record, and the ordered
  comparison named correct O1/O2 bodies mismatches (found by the slice's
  cross-backend matrix before landing). Review fixes, each with a test that
  fails on the reviewed tree: block-id pairing named a correct O2 body a
  mismatch after `renumber_blocks_contiguous` (the review's
  `if i < n { if i < n { i } else { unreachable_unchecked() } } else { 0 }`
  repro, reproduced from the bridge's LIR); the affine refusal named a
  correct multi-path machine a mismatch; a 32-bit `TestRI` was modelled at
  32 bits; and the gate's ignored fixture printer failed the new library
  row (it now lives in `slice6_qualification`). On the census's O0 modules
  the provenance pairing binds exactly what the id pairing bound, with
  byte-identical theorems (1813 of 3445 functions). Darwin `core` census at
  O0 with proofs required: 2114 (the `main` 73e5a69f5 bridge) -> 1816
  failed roots (a slice-6 bridge on a base that also carries e6288b598; 298
  promote, none newly fails; control flow is no longer one refusal but 76
  functions over sixteen blocks, 64 loops and 33 long paths); a
  proof-required rlib of exactly the functions credited at each level
  matches the LLVM oracle natively in all four rlib x bin cells at O0-O3,
  `reports/perf/2026-09-30-darwin-x86-64-census-slice6/`.

- L01-P11 (LLVM importer `sret`; testing evidence, macOS AArch64 native,
  Linux legs not run): the importer carries `sret` on a `define`/`declare`
  parameter (or a declare-by-use call) onto trust-ir `ParamAttrs::sret`, which
  the backend lowers through X8; before, the hidden buffer went in X0 and a
  call returning a large struct crashed (reproduced: with the attribute
  dropped, the native row dies with SIGSEGV). Refused by name: a direct call
  whose `sret` disagrees with its callee's, a declaration/definition pair that
  disagree, an indirect `sret` call, two `sret` or a non-`ptr` one, and
  `byval`, `byref`, `inreg`, `inalloca`, `preallocated`, `nest`,
  `swiftself`, `swifterror`, `swiftasync` anywhere. New Darwin floor target
  `trust-cg-llvm-import/sret_abi_e2e` (minimum 4): clang's IR of C sret
  definitions and sret callers of C callees (24- and 32-byte aggregates) at
  -O0..-O3, compiled by trust-cg (O0 and O2 for -O0 IR, O2 otherwise), linked
  by ld64 with a clang-compiled driver, prints exactly the all-clang output
  (5 rows); clang's indirect sret call is refused at every level. The Linux
  floor lists its 2 host-neutral rows, not yet run on a Linux host; the GNU
  ld, gold and LLD legs the ledger row names are not written.
- L01-P11 (LLVM importer `zeroext`/`signext`; testing evidence, macOS AArch64
  native, Linux legs not run): the importer typed every LLVM `i8`/`i16` as
  trust-ir `I8`/`I16`, which the backend sign-extends at a call edge, so an
  imported caller passed `(unsigned char)255` to a clang callee as -1 and an
  imported `unsigned char` function returned 200 to a clang caller as -56. A
  `zeroext` `i8`/`i16` parameter, argument or return value now types its call
  edge as `U8`/`U16` (zero-extended by the backend), with a `Bitcast` to and
  from the body's signless type at the definition's entry, before `ret` and
  at each direct and indirect call; `signext` and unstated edges stay
  `I8`/`I16`, and `zeroext i1` stays `Bool`. Refused by name: `signext i1`,
  either attribute on a narrow variadic argument, and a call or header whose
  extension disagrees with its callee's edge type. New Darwin floor target
  `trust-cg-llvm-import/int_ext_abi_e2e` (minimum 4): clang's IR of a C
  callee unit and a C caller unit (narrow parameters, returns, a mixed
  signature, two calls through function pointers) at -O0..-O3, compiled by
  trust-cg (O0 and O2 for -O0 IR, O2 otherwise) and linked by ld64 with the
  other unit built by clang and by trust-cg, prints exactly the all-clang
  output (15 builds; `_Bool` units at -O1..-O3, 9 builds, since clang's -O0
  `_Bool` reload is a `trunc i8 to i1` the backend refuses). With the edge
  typing removed, the native row and both host-neutral rows fail. Linux
  floor: 2 host-neutral rows, not yet run on a Linux host.
- L02-P14 (LLVM importer string escapes; testing evidence): `c"..."`
  initializers and `section` names decode as LLVM's `UnEscapeLexed`
  (`\\` is one backslash, recognized before a hex escape; `\XX` one byte;
  any other backslash itself), so `c"a\\\00"` is three bytes, not four. A
  decoded length that differs from the declared `[N x i8]` is refused by name,
  as LLVM's parser refuses it, and a non-UTF-8 section name is refused. Three
  unit fixtures that declared a wrong length are corrected. New Darwin floor
  target `trust-cg-llvm-import/c_string_escapes_e2e` (minimum 4): an escape
  corpus of every rule and every byte value imports to the bytes LLVM decodes,
  trust-cg O0/O2 objects and clang reading the same `.ll` print identical
  bytes through ld64, and clang rejects every module the importer refuses.
  Linux floor: 2 host-neutral rows, not yet run on a Linux host. Not
  changed: a quoted symbol name (`@"..."`) other than a `\01` asm-label is
  still kept verbatim, quotes and escapes included, where LLVM decodes it.
- Reds on main after 5ff639bc2 (testing evidence; no product change, no
  refusal relaxed): 5ff639bc2 keeps the FP/LR envelope around proof-grade
  Darwin leaves, so their publication needs the source-bound frame theorem
  replayed; this host's toolchain AY answers that obligation
  `incomplete self-check-rejected`, and `AY_SOLVER_PATH` no longer admits
  the 2026-09-18 development AY (`[TCG-AY-IDENTITY-MISMATCH]`; the overlay
  toolchain of `scripts/assemble_trust_overlay.py` is the admission route,
  not built for this work). A test-only probe
  (`host_replays_source_bound_frame`, ELF identity leaf; any refusal other
  than the unreplayed frame fails the caller) selects the owner's assertions
  on a capable host and, elsewhere, the exact unreplayed-frame refusal:
  `compiler::tests::test_compile_module_to_jit_rejects_unproved_calling_frame`,
  `aarch64_instruction_word_binding` (4/4) and
  `test_aarch64_parallel_and_serial_multi_function_byte_identical` (serial and
  parallel refusals identical). `aarch64_instruction_word_binding` consults
  the same probe, so the host's capability decides which refusal it must see,
  and it also pins the envelope's `StpPreIndex`/`LdpPostIndex` rows in the
  proof-grade lowering whatever the host replays (reverting 5ff639bc2's
  Darwin red-zone exclusion now fails it). The capable branches are not
  exercised on this host.
- `intmm_o2_e2e` (testing evidence): Apple clang defaults to `-fcommon`, and
  the importer's `common` refusal (trust-ir has no tentative-definition
  linkage) is intended, so the test requires that named refusal for the
  default IR and imports the same programs built with `-fno-common` (2/2).
- `test_linux_aarch64_gate`: main's own fix of the llc preflight test (readelf
  and the platform stubbed) is kept; this branch adds
  `test_preflight_refuses_a_missing_host_tool_and_a_non_linux_host`, which pins
  that the preflight still refuses a missing cc, c++ or readelf and a

- Test temporary-directory hygiene (about 3,300 leaked entries, 20 GiB, were
  found in `$TMPDIR`): scratch directories in trust-cg-codegen, trust-cg-cli,
  trust-cg-llvm-import and trust-cg-verify tests are owned (RAII
  `ScratchDir`/`tempfile::TempDir`) and removed when the test ends, pass or
  fail; `TRUST_CG_KEEP_TEST_OBJECTS` keeps a failing test's directory, and
  the named retention variables keep working. Python gate tests, beat-llvm,
  the trust-cg-test ratchet tests and four fuzz scripts clean up the same
  way. The Darwin floor runs each target with its own `TMPDIR` and fails a
  target that leaves anything there (`temporary_leftovers` in report.json),
  and removes only its own per-target directories. Two tool caches are
  recorded, not failed, and only in the shape the tool leaves them: xcrun's
  `xcrun_db` as a regular file and lldb's `lldb` root as an empty directory;
  anything under `lldb` makes it a leak. Its first full run found two more
  leaks, now fixed (the fixed-name `trust_cg_aarch64_data_reloc` and
  `trust_cg_aarch64_read_global` directories), and lldb's root, now recorded
  as that cache; a static sweep found the same pattern in
  `e2e_x86_64_scale_emergent` and `e2e_x86_64_swiftcc`. The floor checks
  integration targets only; a `--lib` run is not checked. One library leak
  found by hand is fixed: every AY query (trust-cg-verify `ay_bridge`) is
  written in a private directory of its own, so the partial Alethe proof AY
  leaves when it ends before renaming it into place
  (`<query>.alethe.tmp-<pid>-<n>`; trust-cg-codegen `--lib` left one per run)
  goes with the query. Full Darwin floor at b35c59130 (this branch merged
  with main 9bd719584; `--jobs 3`, clean tree): 282 required targets, 277
  pass, none leaves anything in its TMPDIR; the 5 failures are main's known
  red targets (`e2e_aarch64_elf_relocation_model` LLD SKIP,
  `jit_fail_closed_proof_policy` 3/9, `jit_source_bound_arithmetic` 0/2,
  `e2e_cegis_superopt` 5/10, `local_function_address_jit` 2/3), the same
  tests as at ae8cb564f except `jit_source_bound_arithmetic`, which timed out
  there (1200 s, no per-test result) and here fails its 2 tests on the same
  cause as the other source-bound JIT reds (an unreplayed source-bound frame),
  with product code identical to main's. `aarch64_instruction_word_binding` and
  `intmm_o2_e2e` are no longer red (main fixed `jit_cert_cache_identity_aarch64`
  and `aarch64_raw_dataflow_boundary`).
  Not changed: benchmark harnesses that print and keep their artifact
  directory (abi-xback, bridge-fuzz, decline-shapes, sret-xback), and the
  bridge workspace's xback tests, which remove their directory on success but
  not on a panic.
- AArch64 optimizer audit: preserve flags read at a loop head across a
  backedge, retain loop-trip comparisons whose flags survive into an exit,
  and stop constant-trip analysis at intervening calls or opaque flag
  clobbers. Negative/positive regression pairs cover select fusion,
  compare/branch fusion and copy-counted full unrolling. Both new remote
  native flag/unroll regressions are required in the Linux and Darwin gates.
- AArch64 target features, `L03-P9` (Darwin, D03): per-function admission,
  a 23-feature vocabulary, baseline fallbacks and runtime dispatch. The closed
  `AArch64IsaFeature` domain grows from `lse`/`lse2`/`dotprod`/`fp16` to the
  23 rustc spellings Apple M-series CPUs implement (`aes`, `bf16`, `crc`,
  `dit`, `dotprod`, `dpb`, `dpb2`, `fcma`, `fhm`, `flagm`, `flagm2`, `fp16`,
  `frintts`, `i8mm`, `jsconv`, `lse`, `lse2`, `rcpc`, `rcpc2`, `rdm`, `sb`,
  `sha2`, `sha3`), each tied to its Darwin `hw.optional.arm.FEAT_*` keys; all
  read `1` on the qualifying M4 Max (recorded in
  `docs/darwin-aarch64-completion.md`). A function's trust-ir
  `target_features` now reach LIR and extend the profile for that function
  alone (`TargetMachine::for_function`): selection uses them for LSE, LSE2,
  FP16, the optimizer's DotProd shape and the new `llvm.aarch64.crc32*`
  intrinsics (eight `CRC32`/`CRC32C` opcodes with encoder, ENC-5 decode arm
  and census row, deferred RED rows in the coverage gate, 174/296); an
  attribute-free function keeps the baseline lowering (LL/SC loops; a
  bit-serial CRC expansion, 3 against 37-264 words at O2). An unmodeled name
  is refused by name (`UnknownTargetFeature`, `[TCG-TARGET-FEATURE]`,
  `[TCG-DISPATCH]`), a misdeclared CRC intrinsic by `[TCG-CRC32-INTRINSIC]`,
  and the raw JIT refuses a stated feature the CPU lacks. Inliners never
  splice a feature-stating callee; the stated list is bound into the LIR
  verifier identity (`stated_target_features_separate_verifier_identities`)
  and the retained identity (schema v8). The JIT evidence fold requires each
  function's admission to equal the profile plus its own stated set. A JIT
  buffer records the stated features: `serialized_target_contract` names
  them beside the host-JIT contract, `publish_serialized_buffer_for_target`
  replays an extra name only for a modeled feature this CPU implements
  (`SerializedBufferFeatureUnsupportedByHost`), and the jit-matrix TCJ1 cache
  and relocatable-image capture (`FunctionTargetFeatures`) refuse such a
  buffer.
  `trust_cg_codegen::aarch64_dispatch` resolves the host from the sysctls and
  chooses the first covered variant else the baseline. Evidence:
  `aarch64_function_target_features` (12, Darwin floor) runs linked LSE/FP16
  twins under the baseline profile, the CRC forms through the JIT at O0-O3
  against the LLVM-compiled `__crc32*` and a bit-serial reference over 550
  inputs each (the Apple AOT leg counts CRC32 words in O2 objects only), a
  serialized replay of a `crc` buffer, and a dispatch executing both chosen
  paths; ENC-5 decodes the CRC words against clang-assembled words. Strength:
  native differential testing on one host plus independent decoding; no value
  obligation, and the CRC rows stay RED coverage-gate rows (checked beside
  credited controls) that block proof promotion. Open: the bridge does not state `#[target_feature]`, the
  JIT refuses a module holding a variant the host cannot run, no AOT resolver
  is emitted, and the Linux profile controls have not run.
- AArch64 emitted-code size (L14-P10, gates S3/S4): 1.147x -> 0.951x LLVM
  `-O3` geomean over the 18-program beat-llvm corpus on Darwin arm64, worst
  program 2.000x (`b1_mispredict`) -> 1.602x (`p4_matmul`), 14,920 -> 12,484
  emitted bytes, with every exit code still equal to LLVM's. A per-function
  attribution against LLVM (linker map plus disassembly classes,
  `reports/perf/2026-09-30-darwin-emitted-size/`) found the excess in a fixed
  runtime-entry chain (164 bytes per program), loop-head alignment padding and
  the `__trustcg_array_fill_*` helper, not in the user functions. Seven
  changes: innermost-loop-head alignment is opt-in (bridge knob
  `a64-loop-head-align`, `TCG_LOOP_HEAD_ALIGN=1` outside the bridge, refused by
  proof-grade routes; 712 bytes); TCO of a call result narrowed into an `i32`
  (or f16/f32/f64) return whose RET reads only that view (`_main`); SROA
  promotion of register-passed aggregate argument slots and retirement of
  dead slots, with TCO ignoring a deleted slot root (neither admission nor
  retirement applies to a slot a debug variable names, which keeps the
  debugger tests' frame-slot locals); an indirect-call target
  that dies at its `BLR` may use a caller-saved register (both allocators and
  the translation validator); constant folding of SXT*/UXT* of a known
  constant; a bitwise-chain vector drain that skips a provably empty scalar
  tail (NZCV deadness via the fail-closed successor walk); and a W write
  defining its X register in the incoming-argument span scan. Runtime
  unchanged (median of 11, interleaved: 0.960x -> 0.958x LLVM `-O3`; program
  instructions retired after/before 0.99996), compile instructions retired
  -0.05%, compiler peak RSS unchanged. Evidence strength: measurements and
  unit tests with negative controls, not proof; every ratio is from the
  `no-proof-certs` diagnostic lane on a loaded shared host, which the ratchet
  refuses, so no ledger row was appended and S3/S4 stay unmet as evidence.
- AArch64 memory rows (`L07-P2`, `X-OPCODES-P1`, `L04-P7`): admitted scalar
  immediate LDR/STR and LDP/STP rows gain a word-bound memory-effect
  decomposition (`aarch64_memory_effect`). It is a set of small obligations
  over the word literal: fields, lane addresses, writeback, and per-lane
  little-endian bytes with zero or sign extension. Each is at most 2,148
  bytes, with no array, shift, multiplication or `zero_extend`; the
  one-formula pair obligation was up to 79,767 bytes. ENC-5 binds the emitted
  word to the literal.
  - Place in the walk: it runs after the row's own lane and `main`'s
    Formal-only bound-memory rule, which stays the only route to credit. A
    refuted part fails the row, credited or not. An uncredited row records the
    parts' status (`MEMORY_EFFECT_IS_NOT_CREDIT`).
  - Evidence strength: exact in-process decisions (testing grade). Under the
    diagnostic `memory-effect-replay` knob only, live AY/Clean replays, which
    are recorded and never credited.
  - On this host the development AY `2657db47c`, with Clean 8606 or
    `ed21fee39`, checks 488 of 488 corpus parts. The Trust package's AY 9192
    checks none.
  - Census at `main` `9bd719584`: unchanged, 1,324 of 1,345 functions
    refused. This host's `drat-trim` is not authorized by the bound-memory
    manifest, so its 912 memory rows are checker-identity misses.

    Proofs-off `__text` is byte-identical.
  - The record's payloads are kept out of tree, listed in its `PAYLOADS.md`
    (report).

- Source-bound proof lanes: a NEGATIVE memo, so a theorem AY does not certify
  is not solved again at every occurrence (owner decision). A live replay that
  ends in AY's strict self-check rejection, a disclosed incomplete
  certificate, the working checker's rejection of the exact proof, or
  `Timeout` is recorded under a key that binds the exact query bytes, AY's
  recorded identity and digest, the Clean digest and path, the sanitized
  verifier environment, the solve budget, the model option, the resident-route
  state, the replay protocol (rendered from the real command builders) and the
  verifier's source identity (`VERIFIER_SOURCE_SHA256`, recorded by
  `build.rs`); an identical later replay returns the same non-credit outcome
  without running AY. A hit is only ever `Unknown` or `Timeout` (the entry
  stores an outcome kind, never an `AYResult`), is never a reuse receipt, and
  is consulted after the in-process `Verified` memo and the per-box Alethe
  store, so positive credit is unchanged; a live `Verified` deletes the entry.
  Two tiers: in-process (the CT-BATCH per-function fallback's second replay
  and byte-identical bodies) and the per-box certificate store
  (`source-bound-negative-v2/`, written by rename under a namespace `flock`;
  non-regular, corrupt, truncated, foreign-schema, foreign-key and
  self-inconsistent files are misses; recordings prune expired entries). Retry
  policy: per box, a first failure is reused by 2 later processes, doubling
  per failed re-solve up to 32; in one process, 64 hits within 60 minutes;
  never after 24 hours. An outcome after a SAT verdict is never recorded and
  deletes the entry. It serves the x86-64 body and envelope and the AArch64
  frame and ALU replays (one shared replay path). Bypass:
  `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=source-bound-no-negative-memo`
  (`TCG_SOURCE_BOUND_NO_NEGATIVE_MEMO` outside the bridge). Two new soundness
  library gates (`source_bound_negative_memo::`,
  `x86_source_bound_body::tests::negative_memo::`). MEASURED through the rustc
  bridge on a shared host
  (`reports/perf/2026-09-30-darwin-x86-64-negative-memo/`): the slice-5 probe
  crate 146.5/148.0 s -> 45.0/44.7 s with an empty per-box namespace ->
  8.7/9.6 s warm (147.5 s with the bypass); the Darwin `core` census 3994 s ->
  2824 s cold -> 1031 s warm, 2114 failed roots and the same 165 uncertified
  and 1271 Valid bodies on every row, no root differing. The AY nondeterminism
  behind the retry policy is packaged for the AY owners in
  `reports/2026-09-30-ay-strict-selfcheck-nondeterminism/` (a query that
  certifies 18 of 20 times one at a time and 0 of 24 four at a time, always
  rejected at about 9.1 s). Review fixes (an adversarial review confirmed the
  memo never grants credit): the key gained the verifier's source identity and
  a protocol rendered from the commands (it carried only the crate version and
  a hand-written string); only the measured-stable classes are recorded (every
  `(:reason-unknown …)` was, including memout, resourceout, interrupted,
  internal_error and split limits); the in-process tier gained a hit and time
  budget (a long-lived process such as the JIT never retried); a model-query
  timeout after SAT is no longer recorded as `timeout`; a reuse write-back can
  no longer resurrect a concurrently deleted entry; a FIFO at an entry path no
  longer hangs the compile; a stored reason must classify as its label; and a
  fresh-process test pins the per-box proof ahead of the memo. Each has a test
  that fails on the old behaviour. After the fixes the probe crate compiles in
  145.0 s before, 43.8/43.0 s cold, 7.8/8.1 s warm and 145.0 s with the
  bypass.
- rustc bridge: constant function pointers use canonical code addresses and
  the indirect-call ABI. Nested raw field borrows keep their live scalar
  storage. The shared 13-program native corpus executes at O0–O3 on AArch64
  Linux; constant and loaded function pointers have separate native regressions.
- AArch64 Rust arguments: exact single-integer `PassMode::Cast` aggregates
  use scalar carriers, with checked packing and unpacking of their live
  bytes. This covers declarations, entries, direct calls, function pointers
  and dynamic methods. Linux mixed-backend tests cover 1–8 bytes and register
  exhaustion. Native Darwin validation remains open.
- rustc bridge: supported default-Global Vec/String values and their Box payloads use
  rustc's checked inline header. Collection references, indirect arguments,
  sret results and shared drop glue use that same image. Supported empty
  slice-header copies retain zero capacity; explicit constructor capacity and UTF-8 push widths remain
  observable. Constructor overflow and null-allocation checks are qualified
  separately from ordinary value tests. Strict slice-header refinement
  refuses the conditional allocation CFG until its proof model is implemented.
  The real std/sysroot audit retains the
  broader graph's complete refusal lists.
- rustc bridge: full-range byte wrappers use checked scalar storage for
  canonical Rust arguments and their field projections, including ExitCode.
  Supported scalar Vec/String constructors and reserve operations check byte bounds before

  Optimized unwind constructors preserve live RawVec fields through the checked
  standalone Vec image; nested owning aggregate images retain their gates.

- x86-64 proof lane, slice 5 of the source-bound body theorem: scalar pairs,
  symbol addresses and branch-free compares. Two results are the System V
  RAX:RDX return pair, observed lane by lane at each lane's return bits (a
  Rust `ScalarPair` return); a call may return such a pair (it defines RAX
  and RDX, its result registers must be declared in that order, and RDX
  after a one-result call is an undefined read); pair parameters are two
  LIR parameters numbered like any other. `GlobalRef`/`ExternRef` are one

  AArch64 `27fc93a0e`): rustc's `Indirect { on_stack: false }` argument is an

- A loaded `bool` is its byte read as `!= 0` on every backend. trust-ir's
  `Load Bool` reads one byte `m` and yields `m != 0` (the pinned reference
  interpreter's `decode_leaf`; `AtomicLoad` decodes the same way), trust-ir
  states no validity range for a load, and the adapter lowers it to LIR
  `Load B1` unchanged, so the backend computes exactly that (owner decision
  2026-09-29; `reports/2026-09-29-bool-load-semantics/`). x86-64: plain,
  volatile and atomic `B1` loads are `mov r8, m` (one access, opcode and
  proof origin unchanged) then `movzx; add 255; shr 8` into fresh 32-bit
  registers, the backend's clean bool; the x86-64 selector returned the byte
  itself (2 for a stored 2) since the zero extension. AArch64: LDRB, its
  volatile twin and LDARB are followed by `tst x, #0xff; cset b, ne`; they
  returned the raw byte. A stack-passed `bool` parameter is a value, not a
  load, and keeps its zero extension. The AArch64 i128 overflow idiom's
  deferred `B.VS` now requires nothing but its own skipped intermediates
  between the `ADDS` and the branch (a compare there, or a bool load's
  `TST`, would overwrite V; it falls back to `CSET VS` after the `ADDS`).
  The x86-64 body theorem admits a bool loaded from incoming memory with no
  validity premise: its paired input is the whole byte and the source value
  `l != 0`; four fixtures join the qualified memory shapes (31 -> 35; golden
  file: four theorems added, `LocalBool`'s machine side gains the `add`/`shr`
  rows; digest re-pinned), and the stage-1 host qualification (AY 0.27.0
  build 10530, Clean 5f09e36c) certifies all 35 and refutes the new controls
  (a bool returned or passed as its byte, read as bit 0, read as `>= 2`)
  with counterexamples. Fails before, passes after: selector unit tests
  (both backends; the selected rows run for all 256 bytes), the overflow
  idiom test, `bool_load_semantics` (bytes 0/1/2/0x80/0xFF against trust-ir's
  reference interpreter: native x86-64 JIT 280/520 wrong -> 0, AArch64 object
  interpreted on the host 248/520 -> 0), `x86_64_bool_load_abi` (C harness
  over the same bytes) and the new bridge matrix `m147_bool_byte_xback`
  (trust-cg rlib x LLVM/trust-cg bin, O0-O3: 53/56 cells wrong -> 0;
  `m145_xback.py` honours a file's `XBACK_CELLS`). Darwin `core` O0 census:
  2707 roots (`PanicInfo::can_unwind` now proves). Cost, measured (paired
  A/B): tight bool reductions 1.9-2.5x slower at O2, bool-field branches and
  selects 6-10%; the report explains why and how to recover it.

- x86-64: every `bool` the backend defines by a LOAD is a clean 32-bit bool.
  The selector lowered a `B1` load to `mov r8, m` alone; that writes only the
  low byte, and register allocation treats its destination as a pure
  definition, so bits 8..31 were whatever the register held, and the value
  was then returned with `mov eax, r32` or passed as a 32-bit call argument,
  which an LLVM callee of a `bool` relies on (`b as u32` is `movl %edi,
  %eax`). Plain, volatile and atomic `B1` loads and a `bool` parameter read
  from the stack are now followed by `movzx` into a fresh register, which is
  the value (the atomic load keeps its proof origin; the stack parameter's
  extension follows the whole formal group, so the prologue's parallel copy
  is unchanged). `I8`/`I16` loads keep the narrow-carrier contract. No x86
  pass removes a `movzx` on the belief that a byte load zero-extends
  (audited: peephole, CSE, DCE, copy propagation, LICM, SROA, constant
  folding, loop unrolling, the vectorizer and the pipeline). Fails before,
  passes after: selector unit tests; `x86_64_bool_load_abi` (the production
  x86 passes at O0 and O2 keep the extension before `RET` and `CALL`, and a
  native C harness that fills every register with `0xA5` bytes before the
  call read `0xa5a5a5xx` from all five functions before the fix); and the
  bridge's `m146_x86_bool_load_xback` matrix (driven by
  `tests/tools/m145_xback.py --test`, whose shape check is now exact for any
  matrix file): with the bridge from main db6c150ee 34 of 56 bridge-callee
  cells passed a dirty bool to the LLVM or bridge callee and every LLVM-rlib
  cell agreed; with this tree's bridge all 112 cells (O0-O3) agree. Slice-4
  consequences: the `LocalBool` fixture (a private slot's `bool`) proves and
  joins the qualified memory shapes (31; the golden gains its theorem,
  additions only; AY 0.27.0 build 10530 and Clean 5f09e36c certify it), and
  `a_slot_bool_returned_without_extension_is_refuted` now deletes the
  `movzx` from the real selection. A `bool` from incoming memory stays
  outside the domain (the trust-ir `byte != 0` FINDING in LIMITATIONS.md is
  unchanged). The return direction has no LLVM oracle: an LLVM O0 `-> bool
  { *p }` itself leaves EAX bits 8..31 set. The Darwin `core` O0 census
  (stage-1 trustc, proofs required) is unchanged against main db6c150ee:
  2708 failed roots, all `[TCG-PROOF-465]`, the same roots, and the same
  body-trace verdict for all 3446 traced functions (`PanicInfo::can_unwind`
  stays outside the domain: its `bool` comes from incoming memory).
- x86-64 and the adapter: the other two producers of a dirty `B1`. The
  selector lowered a LIR `Bnot` of a `B1` to a bare `not r32`, so `!true`
  returned EAX=0xFFFFFFFE, `!false` 0xFFFFFFFF, and `(!b) as u32` 254/255;
  the result is now masked to bit 0 (`not`, then `and` with 1, as a `B1`
  `BandNot`/`BorNot` already was). trust-ir `not bool`
  (`BinOpRequiresInteger`) and `bitcast u8 -> bool` (`CastLayoutUnsupported`)
  are invalid trust-ir, and the reference interpreter executes neither, but

  CLI's path, which runs no trust-ir validation) compiled them to that
  `Bnot` and to a plain register move into a `B1` from a byte load (bits
  8..31 dirty). The adapter now refuses scalar `not` on `bool` and a
  `Bitcast` into `bool` from anything but `bool` (`bool -> u8`, which the
  rustc bridge emits for `b as u8`, is unchanged), and the x86-64 selector

- Product fix (the verifier of the eleventh L02-P10 repair, at
  `61627b7a6`): the Linux link driver still installed images whose loaded
  memory was not what their sections hold, and one whose data a store
  could not write.
  - **Every page size.** The page model held at 64 KiB only, on the false
    claim that a layout that holds there holds at every smaller page. LLD
    22.1.6 wrote programs whose trust-cg `.data` page ended, at 4 KiB, with
    a segment without file bytes (a zero page: `tcg_val` read 0), and GNU
    ld 2.42 and LLD ones with a read-only segment there (SIGSEGV). The
    model now also runs at each smaller page an AArch64 kernel uses (16 and
    4 KiB).
  - **Sections outside every segment.** The claim that reading such a
    section faults was false: a `PHDRS` `:NONE` section in a mapped page
    read 0, or another section's bytes. Every allocated section must now lie
    in a segment's memory (`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]`).
  - **Zero fill reads zero.** A `.bss` in a segment's file part read the
    bytes LLD put there (42). A `NOBITS` section's file-part bytes must be
    zero.
  - **Write-protected data** (`[TCG-LINK-WRITE-PROTECTED]`). trust-cg's
    `.data` inside GNU ld's `PT_GNU_RELRO` (an `INSERT` script) or in a
    read-only `PHDRS` segment (LLD) died on the first store. The driver's
    map places each input section of the link's own objects. One that may
    hold mutable data is refused in a segment that is not writable, and in
    the pages of a `PT_GNU_RELRO` that `ld.so` or glibc's static start-up
    applies.
  - Of the host's 6,779 ELF images the rule still refuses only the 273
    debug-information files, and 1,026 ordinary links through three
    linkers get the same verdicts as before. `link_options` gains one
    native row (65 on Linux), and the codegen library two.

- Product fix (the eleventh L02-P10 closure audit, at `159f53415`): the
  Linux link driver installed images whose loaded pages held other bytes
  than the sections its checks read, and refused seven kinds of ordinary
  link.
  - **Loaded memory is modelled by page.** The tenth repair's byte-range
    rule missed that the kernel and glibc's `ld.so` map each `PT_LOAD` in
    whole pages, in program-header order. A linker script with `AT()` load
    addresses made GNU ld 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 map the page of trust-cg's
    `.data` and `.bss` from a file page of a C `.pad`. The driver installed
    no-PIE, PIE and static programs and a shared library whose trust-cg
    globals read 0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a. The rule now maps the segments in
    pages of the host's page or the largest `p_align`, at most 64 KiB on
    AArch64. It refuses (`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]`):
    - an `ET_DYN` image whose `PT_LOAD`s are out of order;
    - a `p_vaddr - p_offset` that is not a multiple of the page (`-z
      max-page-size=16`, SIGSEGV through all three linkers);
    - two segments that share a page with different file pages, or whose
      later mapping lacks the earlier one's permissions (LLD's `-n`,
      SIGSEGV at the entry);
    - a later mapping that does not read zero under an earlier zero fill;
    - a read-only zero fill the kernel leaves uncleared.

    The next-64 KiB-page twin of the audit's layout is installed and runs.
    Of the host's 6,779 ELF images, the rule refuses only the 273 separate
    debug-information files under `/usr/lib/debug`, which are never loaded.
    *Correction (2026-09-27):* the rule modelled only that one page and
    left sections outside every segment unread; see the entry above.
  - **Extended section numbering.** The independent ELF reader reads

    opened) and GNU ld's `--gc-sections` note on standard output (a static
    NSS program) no longer make the trace unreadable.

    gold's `-d -T`), the spelled-out one-dash `-hash-style=<v>` and, in a

  every constant or copy return frameless, so neither the frame nor the ALU
  theorem formed: the verifying host JIT refused these leaves on sampled or
  vacuous evidence, and Mach-O `--emit-proofs` refused them on sampled ADD/SUB
  evidence. Proof-grade publication now has no red zone and takes the ELF
  lane's zero-storage leaf policy, including its owner-applicability choice (a

  checker discovery, with the red-zone line reverted and the tests kept, four

  The macOS JIT control is now

- x86-64 coverage gate, the sixteen VOLATILE memory rows: they are now credited
  only by their JOINT obligation (ADDRESS + VALUE + BOUNDARY) and are RED when
  any leg fails. Since 88de9e199 the joint row's VALUE leg asked
  `opcode_to_proof_query`, which has no volatile arm, so the joint row returned
  nothing for all sixteen. Each row then fell through to the ADDRESS row and was
  credited by the address lane alone, with the VALUE and BOUNDARY
  (`x86_volatile_trace`) legs gating nothing. That is the byte-identical plain
  MOV proof the rows' deferral reason called insufficient. Measured on
  ea8492fd9: all sixteen rows carried the address row's note, and
  `x86_volatile_joint_audit_row` returned nothing for any of them. The VALUE
  leg is now the opcode's MemLoad/MemStore reconstruction discharging `Valid`.
  The gate returns the joint row for every volatile opcode, a failing leg is
  `ProofNotDischarged` naming it, and `x86_address_audit_row` refuses a volatile
  opcode. The comments that said "neither obligation alone credits these rows"
  and that a failing leg falls back to the deferral table were false and are
  corrected. The deferral table is consulted before the joint row. All sixteen
  reconstructions discharge, so none moved.
- x86-64 coverage gate, the 37 plain ADDRESS rows: the row now also requires
  the VALUE leg, the opcode's reconstruction discharging `Valid`. Before, the
  gate returned the address row before any reconstruction ran, so the value
  facet its note attributed to "the reconstruction" was checked by nothing, for
  memory-ALU forms such as `AddRM` and `XorMR` too. The compare-exchange joint
  rows already required their reconstruction; they now read it through the same
  VALUE hook, so one injected failure reaches all three row kinds. All 37 plain
  rows discharge, so none moved.

- Darwin runtime outlier `h1_vec_push_sum` (5.10x LLVM `-O3` in the
  2026-09-28 diagnostic lane): its sum loop `while k < v.len() { acc +=
  v[k] }` reloaded the `Vec`'s pointer and length from the header's stack
  slot every iteration and kept a second, taken `cmp; b.lo` bounds check
  (9 instructions and two taken branches executed per element; the loop's
  tenth, a `brk`, never runs), while LLVM runs an 8-lane `ldp q; add.2d`
  loop. The reloads sat behind the loop's exit test,
  so LICM refused them as not guaranteed to execute; the check compared
  against a reload, so nothing could see that the header had tested the
  same `k <u len`; and with both in the loop `neon-array` declined it.
  - **LICM** (`licm.rs`) now also hoists a loop-invariant plain load that is
    not guaranteed to execute when its address resolves, through copies,
    immediate offsets and constant-index GEPs, to bytes inside one
    fixed-size stack slot (the x86 invariant-load tier's argument: the frame
    is mapped for the whole activation). The value-stability tiers are
    unchanged. Disable-list key `licmframespec`.
  - **Miscompile fix in LICM's insertion point** (`preheader_insert_pos`).
    Hoisted code went before the preheader's first `is_branch()`
    instruction, which on AArch64 includes the mid-block guard carriers
    (`TrapBoundsCheckExact` and the other falls-through trap pseudos), and
    the point then stepped back over any non-value side effect, including a
    store ending the preheader. A hoisted load therefore read memory before
    preheader stores that the value-stability tiers never examine (they see
    in-loop writers only): `a[x & 3] = x + 4; for .. { acc += a[2] }`
    returned 0. The frame tier above made this reachable for loads behind
    the exit test; a load in the loop header was already miscompiled on
    main. Hoisted code now lands after every preheader store, call and
    falls-through trap guard, stepping back only over a flag-only compare.
    The bridge does not emit these preheaders: all 18 corpus programs'
    `__text` is byte-identical before and after this fix.
  - **aarch64-bounds-check-elim** gains a register-bound arm: an explicit
    `cmp idx, len ; b.hs trap` whose failing successor only executes `BRK`
    folds to `b cont` when a dominating strict unsigned guard tests the same
    index root against the same length root, or against an equal load of
    the same bytes in the same block with no write between. Non-strict and
    signed guards, proof-annotated checks and functions with a volatile
    access are declined. Disable-list key `bcetrapbranch`.
  - **Soundness fix in the existing carrier arm**: the guarded-region scan
    sliced the carrier's block at the carrier even when that block could run
    again without passing the guard (an inner loop inside the guarded
    region), so an index increment after the carrier was missed and a needed
    `TrapBoundsCheckExact` was deleted. The block is now scanned whole in
    that case (unit test `keep_carrier_whose_block_reenters_without_the_guard`
    deleted the carrier before the fix).
  - Both transforms and the placement fix run on every AArch64 O2/O3 route
    like the other structural passes; they move or remove instructions and
    add no opcode. `e2e_aarch64_vec_len_guard_differential` (Darwin and
    Linux floors) runs the Vec and boxed sum shapes and four negative
    controls at O2 and O3 with the transforms on and off against a C
    reference (540 kernel runs x 4 builds, trapping controls in forked
    children), and requires the fold and the neon-array rewrite exactly
    where expected. Its four preheader-writer rows (a store after a carrier,
    or ending the preheader, with the load behind the exit test or in the
    header) run 288 kernel runs x 4 builds: 320 of the 1152 build runs
    mismatched under the old insertion point, including both OFF builds of
    the header-load row, and none do now. Unit tests also pin the fold's
    `T`-dominates-`C` and copy-link-window conditions and the frame
    resolver's dominance condition (each survived its mutation before).
    Evidence is a bounded differential and unit tests, not a proof.
  - Measured (instructions retired, `/usr/bin/time -l`, min of 3, bridge
    with `no-proof-certs`, before -> after, LLVM `-O3` in brackets):
    `h1_vec_push_sum` 830.5M -> 121.7M (-85.3%) [110.8M];
    `h2_vec_grow` 155.5M -> 114.2M [137.4M]; `h3_box_leak` 580.3M -> 459.4M
    [403.9M]; `h4_vec_dropper` 334.1M -> 301.4M [329.2M]; a rerun after the
    placement fix reproduces them within 1%. The other 14 programs emit
    identical code. Interleaved wall min-of-21 at load 4.35: `h1` 28.1 ms
    -> 8.89 ms against LLVM's 8.83 ms. The diagnostic lane is 18 of 18
    MATCH (after the placement fix, load 14.8 -> 6.3, and again with the
    bridge rebuilt after merging main `59f72f9d4`, load 7.1 -> 14.4). Its
    runtime geomean is not evidence for this change: three runs read 1.067x to
    1.101x LLVM `-O3` while 14 programs' code was unchanged, and
    `v2_memfill` alone read 1.048x to 1.593x. Compiling a corpus program
    costs the same within the ~0.8% run-to-run spread (compiler
    instructions retired, min of 5, main -> this branch: `h1` +0.08%,
    `h3` -0.004%, `p4_matmul` -0.03%).
  - `v2_memfill` (1.36x) and `v3_popcount` (1.22x) in the campaign table
    were run-to-run noise on 6-10 ms programs (rel_spread 0.69 and 1.31):
    measured by cycles and interleaved wall, `v2` runs at LLVM's speed
    (8.16 vs 8.30 ms) and `v3` faster (4.21 vs 5.80 ms); their code is
    unchanged.
- L14-P6 (crate-size scaling on `aarch64-apple-darwin`): the superlinear
  compile growth `scale_gate.py` measured on 2026-09-28 (12.14x LLVM time and
  25.35x peak RSS, 9.45 GB, at 33,605 lines) is located and removed. Every
  emitted object is byte-identical: all 21 bridge objects and 7 linked
  binaries of a 25-to-2,400-function ladder, the backend-only objects of
  every generated trust-ir module measured, all 413 objects and binaries of
  the 102 Rust benchmark programs at `-O1` and at `-O3`, and all 844 CLI
  objects of 129 trust-ir modules (the 122 committed fixtures included) for
  `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
  and `x86_64-apple-darwin` at `-O1` and `-O3` (proofs off). Evidence strength: measurement on
  one host (Apple M4 Max) under concurrent load, plus unit differentials;
  `reports/perf/2026-09-28-darwin-scaling-l14p6/` has the numbers and
  commands.
  - **Cause.** `scale_gate`'s `main` is one basic block of 2,400 calls. The
    pre-RA scheduler gave every call an edge from every earlier and to every
    later instruction (`O(calls * instructions)` edges per block), and three
    register-allocation loops asked every live interval about every call site
    (`find_call_crossings_in`, `LinearScan` reservation checks, the
    validator's physical-register interference check).
  - **Fix.** The scheduler builds its DAG from barrier-free segments chained
    through the barriers (`build_scheduling_dag_for_insts`), which keeps the
    same partial order, priorities and start cycles; the register-allocation
    scans binary-search each live range into sorted positions
    (`LiveInterval::first_live_point`). The `LinearScan` reservation checks
    now use main's equivalent range-side search over a memoized union
    (`9f0e4a24b`, landed independently), and each segment's edges are
    collected by main's `DenseEdges` bit matrix (`f1ae76c31`); this entry's
    measurements predate that merge. The same investigation removed four
    quadratic loops of one long block of memory accesses: the scheduler's
    all-pairs memory-order edges (now the total-access chain), frame-index
    IP-scratch liveness (a per-block backward table), spill-slot first-fit
    coloring (per-color range unions) and post-RA redundant-reload elimination
    (def/use position indexes). Each has an old-versus-new differential.
  - **Measured effect** (bridge, `-O3`, proofs off, instructions retired and
    peak RSS from `/usr/bin/time -l`): the 2,400-function crate went from
    232.7G to 88.1G instructions and from 9,541 MiB to 547 MiB. From 800 to
    2,400 functions, instructions now grow 2.72x (was 5.03x) and RSS 1.81x (was
    9.17x). `scale_gate.py --rss` read xlarge at 1.50x LLVM time and 1.45x
    memory (was 12.77x and 25.22x in the same session), at a load of 8 to 12.
    Backend alone (CLI on generated trust-ir), 2,400 functions: 98.0G to 41.4G
    instructions and 6,372 MiB to 221 MiB. A 4,096-pair store/load block: 138.7G
    to 18.4G and 3,568 MiB to 147 MiB.
  - **Regression test.** `trust-cg-codegen/tests/aarch64_compile_scaling.rs`
    compiles generated modules at 1x, 4x and 16x size and fails when heap
    bytes, allocations, peak live heap or (on macOS) instructions retired grow
    more than 5x per 4x step. It fails on the old scheduler (13.4x allocated
    bytes) and on the old allocation scans (5.83x instructions). It also links
    the call-heavy module against a C reference. It is a Darwin floor target.
  - **Work-count bounds on every host.** Each replaced scan is also bounded
    in its own crate by a deterministic, test-only work counter
    (`trust-cg-regalloc` `scan_work`, frame.rs's scratch-scan counter), which
    the new code and the replaced scans' primitive probes (`is_live_at`,
    `overlaps`, the forward scans) both charge. Seven
    `*_cost_grows_linearly` unit tests allow at most 5x per 4x step. Forcing
    each fast path back to its old scan reads 14.97x to 16.09x and fails; with
    the fixes each step reads about 4x. These run on Linux too, where the
    instructions-retired probe does not.
  - **Debug builds stay linear too.** Main's `becb4b9df` re-derives the
    provenance reverse index after every mutation in debug builds, which made
    a debug compile quadratic in function size. `aarch64_compile_scaling`
    runs in the test profile and failed after the merge (external-call
    block: allocated bytes 14.5x then 15.6x, instructions 14.1x then 16.1x
    per 4x step). The
    re-derivation now runs on an amortized schedule: after every mutation
    while the map holds at most 32 instructions, then after every `size / 32`
    mutations, plus once unconditionally in `build_transitive`. Main's oracle
    test still checks after every operation. Release builds are unchanged,
    and the debug CLI on that block now reads 1.71G, 6.14G and 25.08G
    instructions at 128, 512 and 2,048 calls (was 6.00G and 81.1G at 128
    and 512).
  - **Merge with main at `59f72f9d4`.** The merged backend emits the same
    bytes as main's: `benchmarks/compile-corpus` Identity PASS on all 534
    (entry, lane) pairs (steady-state instructions: `aot-object` 0.943x,
    `jit-raw` 0.993x), and 844 of 844 CLI objects of 129 trust-ir modules on
    four targets at `-O1`/`-O3`. Against main's CLI, the 2,400-function
    scale_gate shape compiles in 30.47G instead of 88.55G instructions and
    225.5 MiB instead of 8,666.8 MiB peak RSS.
  - **Not done.** One long block of memory accesses still has a superlinear
    CPU term, `LinearScan::allocate`. After the merge with main, the pointer
    block grows 5.1x then 5.2x instructions per 4x step (256 to 4,096
    pairs), and the stack-tuple block 9.6x then 5.2x (500 to 8,000 pairs;
    `allocate-core` 3.8 ms, 124 ms, 662 ms). Main's `becb4b9df` removed the
    other term, `ProvenanceMap::record_merge`. There is still no proofs-on
    scaling measurement, since the production lane refuses the corpus
    (`L07-P2`).
- JIT-path LIR inlining with inline-only runtime bodies
  (`docs/jit-inline-only-bodies.md`). `prepare_jit_lir_module` is the shared
  pre-ISel LIR step for every JIT consumer; `Compiler::compile_module_to_jit`
  runs it (both targets) and raw lanes call it. OPT-4's inliner, AOT-only
  until now, also splices module definitions through the JIT's exact module
  edges, and splices trust-ir `AvailableExternally` bodies
  (`translate_inline_only_bodies`) into by-name calls: a runtime ships a
  helper's fast path once, beside its one out-of-line definition, and a call
  not inlined stays the external call. Every spliced body is a disclosed
  one-definition-rule premise (`JitCompilationResult.inline_only_bodies`); a
  compile that makes a proof claim (`emit_proofs`, or a verifying JIT
  validation mode) withholds them. The range pass runs over the functions
  inlining changed. Kill switch `TCG_NO_JIT_LIR_PREPARE`.
- Inline-only bodies at the AOT seam: `Compiler::compile` admits them through
  the same `admit_inline_only_bodies` (every AOT target), withholding a body
  that is preemptible under `pic` and every body under `emit_proofs`, and
  records what an object rests on in `CompilationResult::inline_only_bodies`.
  `TCG_NO_INLINE_ONLY_BODIES` withholds every inline-only body on both seams.
  Structural purity inference no longer reads a bodied `AvailableExternally`
  function (a codegen declaration whose calls reach another object's
  definition), which it had used without disclosing the premise. A ONE-block
  inline-only body with memory operations or external calls (a field read)
  is now a template through the CFG-splicing tier; module definitions keep
  the two-block floor there, so their inlining is unchanged. The
  CompileService's `ObjectArtifactPayload` and `ExecutableArtifactPayload`
  carry the same `inline_only_bodies` disclosure.
- Authenticated inline-only bodies: `Compiler::with_inline_only_dependencies`
  (and `InlineOnlyAuthority` for raw lanes) supplies dependency modules; a
  body is authenticated when an import row of the module that
  `Module::verify_import` accepts against one of them names a dependency
  defining the symbol with the same translated LIR
  (`Function::canonical_body_identity`, `translate_body_template`). Its
  premise is recorded as discharged (`InlineOnlyBodyEvidence::authenticated`)
  and it is the only kind a proof-claiming compile splices. Supplying
  dependencies disables compile-artifact reuse.
- The LLVM importer imports `define available_externally` as trust-ir
  `AvailableExternally` instead of an `External` definition: the object no
  longer carries a strong symbol LLVM would not emit, and the body is an
  inline-only template at O1+.
- L14-P5 (compile time, Darwin arm64): per-process fixed cost of a bridge
  compile, measured and cut. The evidence strength is measurement on one
  M4 Max (macOS 26.6.2, Trust 9192) on a shared host, medians of 5
  interleaved compiles, cold = a fresh private `XDG_CACHE_HOME` per compile as
  `run.py --cold` does; it is not a ledger row. The harness, its programs and
  every raw sample are retained in
  [`reports/perf/2026-09-28-darwin-fixed-cost/`](reports/perf/2026-09-28-darwin-fixed-cost/README.md).
  - **Where the fixed cost was.** A DYLD interposer and `/usr/bin/time -l`
    show that loading and initialising the 112 MB backend costs 19 M
    instructions (0.5% of an LLVM `--emit=metadata` compile of an empty
    crate). The rest was proof-tool custody work: four `clean` control-proof
    processes and SHA-256 digests of four 91-116 MB executables (about 700 M
    instructions) per compile. The authority capture re-ran the control proof
    on both default checkers that the scheduling hint had already probed at
    backend `init`, and it digested the Trust toolchain's `clean` (108 MB),
    which that probe had found unusable. About 60 ms of this was on the
    critical path of every compile. The cold lane also held the whole 91 MB AY
    in memory while writing its private copy. Its first start of the new copy
    waited for a macOS XProtect scan: 0.67-1.0 s against 8 ms later, and
    concurrent starts share one scan.
  - **Changes.** A process now runs the control proof once per checker file
    state and child environment. The two lanes share the verdict recorded for
    the identical state, so the authority capture can select on a verdict the
    scheduling hint reached. A candidate whose recorded verdict is a stable
    defect is not digested (in authority-first order it is digested before
    its probe). A capable answer still carries the digest of the selected
    checker's current bytes, a reused one only if the file state is unchanged
    after that digest, and `TCG_PARANOID_FILE_HASH` still re-probes.
    The private copy is streamed in 1 MiB chunks, digested as written, and
    published only with the admitted digest. It is still digested again
    before use. On macOS, a copy published by this process is started once
    (`--version`) on the identity-warm thread through the same revalidation
    as every start, so the scan overlaps the front end. One thread per
    process writes a given copy, and an AY digest is computed once per file
    state (a concurrent caller waits for it). The identity-warm thread and the
    first proof query used to race: cold compiles of the fixture's library,
    run six at a time, read one AY-sized file twice (6 digests, 481.9 MB) in
    12 of 48 runs; with only the digest made compute-once, 30 of 48 streamed
    two copies; with both changes, 48 of 48 read 5 (390.4 MB).
    `trust_cg_verify::process_cost` counts checker probes, executable digests
    and AY starts, and the bridge prints them under `time`. No identity,
    custody or fail-closed check was removed.
  - **Effect (instructions retired / wall / peak footprint).** From the
    retained run (base = main `e29e8006d`, 1-minute load 4.6 to 7.0 on 16
    CPUs). Every row compiled byte-identical objects before and after.
    `fn main(){}` (`no-proof-certs`): warm 4,819 M to 4,616 M instructions and
    0.36 s to 0.30 s (LLVM 3,944 M, 0.30 s). Cold went from 5,082 M to
    4,846 M, 1.05 s to 1.02 s, and 136.8 MB to 61.1 MB peak footprint (RSS
    187.6 to 150.0 MB). `p3_gcd` / `p1_xorshift` / `m1_call_chain`: warm
    -201/-201/-201 M instructions and 0.41/0.43/0.41 s to 0.37/0.35/0.38 s;
    cold -237/-234/-235 M and 1.26/1.25/1.29 s to 1.17/1.19/1.18 s, peak
    footprint 138.6 to 65.8 MB. A certificates-on one-function library: warm
    4,731 M to 4,527 M and 0.34 s to 0.28 s (LLVM 0.27 s); cold 4,986 M to
    4,750 M, 0.34 s to 0.28 s and 135.1 to 68.8 MB. For that library, checker
    probes per compile fell from 4 to 2, and executable digests from 5 to 4
    (warm) and from 6 to 5 (cold). A reviewer's independent run reproduced
    the instruction and footprint figures within 0.5%.
    **Cold wall time is not a decision metric.** Each cold compile's first AY
    start waits for an XProtect scan of its new private copy, and
    `syspolicyd` runs scans one at a time for every process on the host: in
    the retained run's 95 s window it completed 153 scans, 51 of them this
    run's AY copies. A reviewer's run at load 6.8 to 8.5, sharing that queue
    with other agents' test binaries, measured cold `fn main(){}` medians of
    1.25 s (base) and 1.31 s (head), both lanes bimodal. When the queue was
    idle, head's scan started 0.35-0.56 s into the compile against base's
    0.70-0.73 s. So the cold wall figures depend on other processes' exec
    activity, and a cold wall gain is not claimed.
  - **Evidence.** All 18 `beat-llvm` programs linked to byte-identical
    binaries before and after, cold and `no-proof-certs`, and every exit code
    matched LLVM's. Certificates-on compiles emitted identical objects, and
    `p3_gcd`, `m1_call_chain` and `h2_vec_grow` refused with the same codes.
    New tests bound the work: `trust-cg-verify`
    `a_compile_probes_each_checker_once_and_digests_only_the_selected_one` (a
    mutant without the reuse fails it with (2, 2) probes),
    `an_authority_probe_answers_the_later_availability_question`,
    `paranoid_file_hash_reprobes_on_the_authority_lane`,
    `a_checker_replaced_before_the_digest_is_probed_not_bound_to_the_old_verdict`,
    `a_capability_probe_whose_checker_state_moved_records_nothing`,
    `a_verdict_recorded_under_one_child_environment_is_not_reused_under_another`
    (each fails a mutant that drops the guard it names: the post-digest state
    recheck, the state-held condition on recording, the environment key),
    `only_a_copy_published_in_this_process_has_one_first_start_to_take` and
    `a_streamed_copy_is_published_only_with_the_admitted_digest`,
    `concurrent_resolutions_in_one_process_write_one_copy` (8 copies without
    the writer lock) and `concurrent_digests_of_one_file_state_read_it_once`
    (8 reads without the held slot). The bridge
    fixture `fixed_cost_budget_aarch64` bounds a real cold and warm compile at
    <= 2 probes, <= 5 / <= 4 digests and <= 1 / 0 AY starts. It is registered in
    `scripts/check_darwin_aarch64_bridge.py` as a new `fixed-cost-bound` kind,
    never counted as native execution.
  - **Still open.** Cold compiles of the four binaries remain about 3.4-4.0x
    LLVM's wall time in the retained run. The rest of the gap is the XProtect
    scan, which a small crate cannot hide, plus the live discharges an empty
    certificate store needs (`LIMITATIONS.md`). Warm,
    the three required digests (AY, its private copy, the selected checker:
    about 540 M instructions) stay off the critical path on a background
    thread. Each stored certificate is replayed in its own `clean` process
    (about 4.5 ms each, 8 for `p3_gcd`).

- AY first start off every solver deadline (TRUSTCG-13; one registry with
  the L14-P5 prime above). On macOS the first start of a new private AY copy
  waits for the host's assessment of the new file: 1.6-11.8 s for a fresh
  copy of the 158 MB toolchain AY (0.27.0 build 10934) at load 34-54, once
  32.2 s during a compile (2026-09-27), 2.4-6.1 s at load 50-59 on
  2026-09-28, and 0.01-0.06 s for every later start. The identity-warm
  prime took that start off a compile's critical path, but only in a compile,
  only for a copy the compile published, and a query that arrived while it
  ran paid the rest inside its own deadline. Every other process (this
  crate's tests, the CLI, a process that found a copy another process
  published and never started) paid it inside its first query's deadline:
  on `62d355f4c`, `cegis::tests` on a fresh copy spent 3.005 s in its first
  resident solve against 0.001-0.005 s for the rest, and on `7e85a7fa7` the
  first query of `cegis_layer_a`, `cegis_stats_trace` and `cegis_layer_b`
  timed out at 1.006-1.007 s against a 1 s budget. Now `ay_private_copy`
  holds one first-start state per copy. `PinnedAy::command` and the resident
  path (before admission) make a pending first start (`ay --version`, empty
  environment, stopped after 120 s) or wait for the thread already making
  it; the warm thread still makes it early for a copy its compile published.
  A completed first start is recorded beside the copy (`ay.first-start`,
  bound to the copy's device, inode, size and change time), so a later
  process starts nothing extra; a copy found without that record is started
  once before its first deadline. Other hosts make no first start on their
  own. Measured on this change (2026-09-28, load 40-82, a fresh cache per
  run): the same fresh-copy `cegis::tests` run makes the first start in
  2.422 s and answers its first resident solve 0.03 s later; the lib `cegis`
  filter passes 106 of 106; interleaved with the same integration tests built
  from main's code, `cegis_layer_a` passed 3 of 3 runs (main's code 0 of 3,
  each with a first-query `server_timeout` at 1.007 s), `cegis_layer_b` 3 of
  3 (0 of 3) and `cegis_stats_trace` 32 of 32 (1 of 6). In an earlier
  window at load 70-77, 9 of 15 fresh-cache `cegis_stats_trace` runs of this
  change failed `Layer A rewrite must commit` with no server timeout, solver
  error or Clean replay failure traced, which fits the proof-bearing
  re-solve overrunning its 1 s wall-clock budget (main's code measured those
  re-solves at 0.96-1.01 s); that cause was not measured directly. The
  bridge's `fixed_cost_budget_aarch64` held in 6 of 6 runs with cold (<= 2
  probes, 5 digests, 1 AY start) and warm (2, 4, 0) counts. The first-start
  allowance is a hang guard, not a solver budget, and no per-query budget is
  a deterministic fuel (`LIMITATIONS.md`).

- AArch64 Mach-O relocation inventory digest: `Compiler::compile` now parses
  the relocation records back out of every proofs-on AArch64 Mach-O object it
  returns (emitted or compile-artifact cache hit) with the independent
  `macho::reparse` reader and requires their kind multiset to equal the
  `object_relocation_inventory` rows, as the ELF digest already did. It also
  refuses a lane-covered record whose `r_pcrel`/`r_length` is not the shape
  its value-proof lane models, an `ARM64_RELOC_SUBTRACTOR` not immediately
  followed by its `ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED` minuend, and an `ARM64_RELOC_ADDEND`
  that is not a non-extern 4-byte prefix of a same-address
  BRANCH26/PAGE21/PAGEOFF12 record. The comparison is by kind: a record moved
  to another section or address, or retargeted, with its kind and shape kept
  is not detected. Mach-O EH modules remain refused by the inventory.
- x86-64 internal multi-result convention past RAX:RDX: a TrustIR function
  with more independent scalar results than System V's C return file holds now
  returns the rest in RCX,RSI,RDI,R8,R9 / XMM2-XMM7 (`X86_INTERNAL_RET_GPRS` /
  `X86_INTERNAL_RET_XMMS`, the C file their same-index prefix, so every
  previously placed return is placed identically) instead of being refused at
  the third result of a class — target parity with AArch64's X0-X7 / V0-V7 for
  every producer (TY's semantic lane was AArch64-only because of it). Admitted
  on `Fast`/`Cold` edges only; a `C`/`Rust` edge of that shape is refused by
  name (`[TCG-X86-MULTI-RESULT]`); Windows x64 is unchanged. Such a `ret`
  carries its internal result registers for post-RA liveness, its return moves
  reach the allocator as explicit producers with return sinks, and TV-5 admits
  the registers as System V call results. Also: TV-5 modeled a VOLATILE
  `movss`/`movsd` store as reading all 16 bytes of its source, failing closed
  on a correct f32 call result stored after a later call.
- trust-ir pin `c603897b` -> `bf7ee706` (Clean `352b9d73` -> `7330fa6c`):
  trust-ir now gives `Dealloc` of a reference-counted (`SwiftHeap` /
