  `CleanHeap`) cell one meaning, undefined behaviour, since such a cell is
  released by the `Release` that takes its count to zero. The bounded fsym
  scanner judged that free `Safe` (it tracked every `HeapAlloc` alike); it now
  records the cell's origin and reports the free as an invalid free, and
  `fsym_ub_map` carries the new interpreter UB site with an `InvalidFree`
  verdict owed at every `Dealloc`. Codegen is unaffected: every `Dealloc` is
  already refused there.
- JIT tier-up (`trust_cg_codegen::tier_up`, design and plan in
  `docs/jit-tier-up.md`): `TierUpSession` compiles tier 0 of a `TierPlan`
  (1-4 strictly increasing optimization levels) on the caller's thread and the
  higher tiers on one background worker, after tier 0, concurrently with it
  (`start_concurrent`) or when the consumer promotes a hot session
  (`start_on_demand` + `promote`), delivering them through `poll`/`wait` or to
  a background installer (`install_with`). Every tier is an ordinary
  compile-service request derived from the caller's (`tier_request`: same
  generation, fence, proof policy, provenance and manifest; higher tiers get
  the session's cancellation token and none of the caller's per-artifact
  proof/TV evidence), is delivered only while neither cancelled nor stale
  (checked before and after its compile and at delivery), must carry tier 0's
  source identity and exact callable surface, and is byte-identical to a plain
  compile of its request. A refused tier is a named code and never disturbs
  the installed one. `ServiceTierBackend` compiles a TrustIR module through
  `CompileService` (delivering exactly what a synchronous compile would
  install); `TierEntryTable` swaps entry addresses atomically and keeps every
  installed tier's code mapped (execution leases, or a caller's owner for its
  own JIT artifacts). Tooling: `compile_corpus run --opt-level`, `run.py
  tier-cost` / `profile --opt-level`, and `tier_up_bench` (the ay BCP kernel
  and the scripts/fuzz kernels through base/top/tier/tierc arms under one
  checksum). Evidence (`reports/perf/2026-09-28-jit-tier-up`): one checksum
  in every arm of 22 cells; at O0 the corpus's JIT lane costs 0.966 of the
  production compile on TY semantic images, 0.902 on the ay kernels and 0.608
  on the fixtures, and up to 1.50x O1 on large TY batches, because allocation
  and the frame-net verifier grow on unoptimized code by almost what the
  optimizer saves — the next lever for a cheap first tier.
- Compile time, byte for byte: `benchmarks/compile-corpus` is a committed
  regression corpus of 247 TrustIR modules from four frontends (TY semantic
  images and production modules, rustc-bridge programs, the ay jit-matrix
  kernels, this repository's fixtures) compiled through the raw JIT and AOT
  lanes, recording per module the verdict, the emitted-code digests and the
  frame-net verifier's counters beside per-phase instructions and cycles
  (`compile_corpus`, `run.py measure/compare/profile`). A change is admitted
  only with Identity PASS on the whole corpus. Against origin/main fa7d0ce12
  (same harness, same host, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1, steady state of 3 reps):
  Identity PASS on all 534 (entry, lane) pairs; instructions retired x0.325
  on rustc-bridge aot-object (per-program median x0.747; the matmul shape
  programs x0.164), x0.762 on TY semantic images through the raw JIT
  (x0.715 with the sealed-function link), x0.753 / x0.632 on the ay kernels
  (raw JIT / AOT), x0.772 on the fixtures (AOT). Of that, the frame-net
  commits of lane/cc-compile-debit (cherry-picked here) account for x0.989
  on the bridge and x0.969 on TY. The changes, each checked with a verbatim
  or randomized oracle of what it replaced: provenance merges rewrite only the
  lists they change (was quadratic per merge); SROA computes dominators,
  positions and a vreg-users index once per run instead of per slot and per
  traced alias; the frame net keeps cells in a sorted vector and joins only the
  differing middles; ENC-5 decides bit routings on borrowed names; the linear
  scan allocator searches reserved positions from the range side over a
  memoized union; the scheduler's DAG deduplicates edges in a bit matrix; the
  operand-role table is memoized per opcode behind a per-count truncation
  check; every AArch64/shared pass, the adapter and the hot codegen maps hash
  with the shared deterministic `trust_cg_ir::fast_hash` instead of SipHash;
  the raw dataflow pairing digest hashes a compact LIR rendering with the same
  separation as the canonical one; the register-allocation validator's
  return-sink bindings run their fixpoint on per-block summaries.
  Evidence: `reports/perf/2026-09-28-compile-speed` (also TY's native
  preparation on its 40 semantic-exact rows: whole-process instructions
  x0.789 with identical results, `[patch]` builds of TY's pin). New API: `Pipeline::prepare_function_checked`
  and `JitCompiler::compile_raw_checked(_relocatable)` carry the final-stream
  check a preparation passed, so the raw JIT link skips re-running an identical
  check (and re-runs it when the diagnostic mode changed since preparation).
  No verification pass is removed or weakened.
- AArch64 bridge: the indirect argument lane (rustc's Rust-ABI
  `PassMode::Indirect { on_stack: false }` — one pointer to a caller-made
  copy) and every refusal that comes with it (padded scalar returns and
  arguments, `rust-call` escapes and shared symbols, by-value closure
  environments shared by symbol, rustc-aligned homes for padded scalars) now
  apply on AArch64 as on x86-64, scoped by ONE predicate
  (`rust_abi_indirect_lane_target`). Before, a 9-16-byte `Memory` argument
  travelled in two X registers where rustc passes a pointer: measured on an
  AArch64 Darwin host with the `m145` cross-backend matrix (now run natively
  for the host's architecture), 213 of 460 rlib x bin cells disagreed with
  LLVM x LLVM (SIGSEGV / SIGBUS or wrong values); now every cell agrees or is
  refused by name. Two layout images the bridge derived from declared fields
  instead of rustc's layout are fixed on every target: a single-variant enum
  whose `#[repr(C)]` / `#[repr(uN)]` keeps a TAG was typed as its payload
  scalar (`&TagC::V(-51)` read by LLVM answered 0) and is now a Direct-tagged
  memory enum; a write to the sized field of `struct ZstLead((), u64)` was
  lost (8738 against 4242) and now updates the local. Through a REFERENCE, a
  tagged single-variant enum and a single-variant enum whose fields rustc
  REORDERED (`enum Reord { V(u8, i64) }`) were typed as declaration-order
  lanes: a bridge-built `fn(v: &TagC)` read the tag as the payload (0 against
  40), and `fn(v: &Reord)` read garbage even with both sides bridge-built; both
  now take the memory-enum pointee lane, which addresses every field at rustc's
  offset. The Trust run-make `trust-ir-cg-layout-abi-authority` exercised all
  of these; the `m145` matrix pins them (`tag_c_*`, `tag_u8`, `zst_lead_write`,
  `reorder_ref`) in all four rlib x bin cells.
- Bridge: two `alloc` shapes every `vec![..]` / `Rc<[T]>` program reaches.
  (1) At `-O2`/`-O3` the current std's MIR fuses the `Box.0.0` Field(0)
  descent into the transmute reading the box's fat pointer, which the box ->
  Vec chain recognizer accepted only as two statements, so the chain abandoned
  and the `Box<[T; N]> -> Box<[T]>` Unsize refused; the fused statement is now
  admitted under both statements' conditions. (2) The tag-only-enum field
  discriminant arm read `discriminant((align.0: AlignmentEnum))` of a
  single-scalar `Alignment` newtype through a hand-built `Projection` key the
  local never has, so every inlined `Layout == Layout` — `Rc::<[u8]>::from`,
  `Arc::<[u8]>::from` at every level — refused; it now reads through the place
  kernel. `std_alloc_shape_differential` runs both against LLVM at O0/O2/O3.
- AArch64 Darwin shrink-wrapping: a frame path that reached a leaf-shared
  bare `ret` through a JOIN block the save block does not dominate returned
  with the callee-saved registers, the frame pointer and the link register
  still the frame's. The planner classified returns by dominance at their
  IMMEDIATE predecessors, so a join of the leaf path and a frame path counted
  as a leaf predecessor and got no restore
  (`core::char::methods::encode_utf8_raw_unchecked` at `-O0`, reached by
  `str::starts_with(char)`; the final-stream spill-slot net refused it as
  `[TCG-A64-SPILL-SLOT]` `callee-saved-not-restored`, so nothing wrong was
  emitted, but every program reaching it failed to compile). The planner now
  separates the frame region from the leaf region by reachability and places
  the restore on the last frame-only block before any block a leaf path also
  reaches (or declines, keeping the whole-function prologue), and the plan
  verifier is an independent forward frame-state dataflow over every path
  instead of the dominance proxy.
- Frame dataflow net (`post_ra_spill_slots`, TV-6) compile cost, measured on
  TY: bcbe2ce1c's V8-V15 upper-half rule derived operand roles for every
  instruction on every fixpoint visit; they are now derived only when a V8-V15
  operand is present. The checking pass no longer formats a location string
  for every instruction (only for a recorded report), and the join of two cell
  maps is one ordered sweep instead of a sort plus a range search per interval.
  Verdicts, declines, statistics and rendered diagnostics are unchanged; the
  previous derivation and join are kept in the unit tests as references.
- x86-64 bridge: rustc's `PassMode::Indirect { on_stack: false }` argument —
  a pointer to a caller-made copy, the Rust ABI's choice for every sized
  `Memory` value larger than a pointer — is now lowered as rustc does
  (the indirect argument lane, trust-ir §17's pre-lowered crossing): the
  callee declares one `Ptr` and copies the pointee into its slot, every call
  site passes the address of a fresh copy in rustc's layout, the argument gate
  compares the pointer against rustc's placement, and every `Call` to such a
  callee is checked to carry a fresh copy. Before, the bridge passed the bytes
  (System V lanes or a `byval` copy): measured across a real boundary, an LLVM
  caller of a bridge callee SIGSEGV'd and the other direction read wrong
  values, while every all-bridge program agreed. The lane has a SCALAR
  sub-lane for an over-aligned single-scalar newtype (`#[repr(C, align(16))]
  struct A16 { a: u64 }`, the `#[repr(align(128))]` `CachePadded` shape),
  which the bridge types as one scalar but rustc passes by pointer: the
  caller stores the scalar at offset 0 of a padded copy (rounded up past the
  16-byte stack alignment when needed) and the callee loads it back. Refused by
  name instead of lowered: such a newtype RETURNED by value (rustc returns it
  through the hidden buffer; `[TCG-RET-ABI]`), a padded `f32` rustc casts to an
  integer register (`[TCG-ARG-ABI]`), and the address of a `rust-call` shim the
  bridge declares with its argument tuple as one parameter escaping into a
  vtable, a reified fn pointer or a constant when that tuple places differently
  from rustc's untupled arguments (`[TCG-ARG-ABI]`; `&dyn Fn(T12)` and
  `&dyn Fn(u64, u64, u64)` measured 176 / 218 against 151 / 195 before, and the
  latter was wrong even with both sides bridge-built — 45 / 128 at O0 / O2).
  Every `dyn Fn*` vtable carries `FnOnce::call_once` as such a shim, so a
  closure trait object whose arguments do not place as their tuple
  (`dyn Fn(T12)`, `dyn Fn(u64, u64, u64)`, `dyn Fn(u8, u8)`) is refused too.
  The scalar arms compare a POINTER carrier too: a padded pointer newtype
  returned by value (`-> #[repr(C, align(16))] struct AP { p: *const u64 }`,
  measured a bus error / 0 against 30), a pointer-carrier union by value
  (`union UP { p: *const u64 }`, SIGSEGV / 112 and a bus error / 3 against
  40 / 33) and such an element in a `dyn Fn*` spread (SIGSEGV against 41) are
  refused by name; only the intercepted collections keep their own-slot
  pointer, recognised by identity. Two more routes by which the other backend
  reaches a tupled `rust-call` declaration are refused by name when the tuple
  places differently: a `rust-call` fn ITEM shared BY SYMBOL (a generic this
  crate exports or links under `-Zshare-generics`, the O0 default — `<&F as
  Fn<(u64, u64, u64)>>::call` measured 220 / 190 against 231 — or a non-generic
  exported `extern "rust-call"` fn, SIGSEGV / 0 against 117), and a `FnOnce`
  closure body shared by symbol, whose type escapes its defining function
  (`-> impl FnOnce`), when rustc passes its small by-value environment in
  registers while the bridge passes a pointer (209 / SIGSEGV against 57); the
  `core` census is unchanged (2 roots at O0).
  Every stack HOME of such a padded newtype — the temporary behind a `&a`
  call argument, a scalar cell, a `&dyn` data pointer — now has rustc's size
  and alignment with the scalar at offset 0; before it was an `Alloca` of the
  scalar, so `&a` was 8 mod 16 (wrong even with both sides bridge-built) and
  an LLVM `-O2` callee whose `movaps` loads the promised 16 bytes SIGSEGV'd.
  Evidence: `m145_x86_indirect_arg_xback` (cross-backend matrix and
  refused-by-name controls, driven by `tests/tools/m145_xback.py`) and the
  `indirect_arg_lanes` / `indirect_scalar_newtype_lanes` /
  `padded_scalar_home_alignment` corpus fixtures.
  AArch64 is not on the lane (the 9-16-byte case stays open there) and the
  intercepted collections (`Vec` / `String` / the maps) are still not in
  rustc's layout across a boundary; both are recorded in `LIMITATIONS.md`.
  Lowering evidence only (`no-proof-certs`); no proof claim.
- `p4_matmul` (Darwin campaign runtime outlier, L14-P8 diagnostic lane): the
  rustc bridge's matmul nest now reaches `mac-reg-block`'s register-blocked
  fast path. The campaign's 8.87x was not a vectorization gap. LLVM `-O3`
  does not vectorize this i64 kernel (AArch64 NEON has no 64-bit integer
  multiply): it unrolls the 24-wide j-loop, keeps the `c` row in 24 registers
  across the k-loop and elides every bounds check, 41 instructions per 24
  multiply-adds. The bridge ran 17 instructions per multiply-add with three
  bounds checks because both matmul passes refused its nest. It emits
  constant-length slice checks as trapping `TrapBoundsCheckExact` carriers
  (canonical `icmp ult` + `assert`), not the `cmp; b.lo` diamond the
  recognizers modeled, and it threads the outer loop's counter, bound and
  accumulator through the nest as block parameters, which the
  bypassed-live-out rule refused.
  - **Recognition.** The review bar classifies every carrier in the nest: a
    constant length of at least `N*N` on a recognized index of the current
    iteration. A register length, a non-index value or a stale index is
    refused by name (`UnprovenBoundsCarrier`), a carrier in a header as
    `HeaderWork`, and a carrier between a check's compare and branch as an
    unproven branch. A live-out is admitted only when every write of it in
    the nest copies back a dominating single-definition copy of itself. The
    fast path is unchanged except that it takes a 12-accumulator tile when 12
    divides `N` (else 8), which also admits `N` = 12, 36, 60, ...
  - **Evidence.** 11 new unit tests on hand-built machine IR (53 in the
    module) cover both admitted forms and each new refusal. `e2e_aarch64_mac_reg_block_differential`
    grows from 5 to 11 tests: every kernel list again in the bridge's check
    form with a trapping C reference, each build run in a forked child so a
    trap is an outcome every build must reproduce (12 runs trap), the tile
    width checked in each rewritten object, and the bridge's own `p4_matmul`
    trust-ir rewritten once at O2 and O3 and equal to a C transcription over
    nine repetition counts. A mutation that dropped the carrier length check
    was caught by both the rewrite counts and the native driver. The Darwin
    floor minimum is 11. This is a bounded native differential, not a proof;
    the pass keeps its existing schedule (default on at O2 and O3 in the
    shared AArch64 optimization pipeline, with no certificate of its own).
  - **Measured** on the Apple M4 Max, proofs-off bridge, min of 7 runs of
    `/usr/bin/time -l` at 1-minute load 8.7: `p4_matmul` 4.590G -> 0.566G
    instructions retired and 912M -> 117.3M cycles, against LLVM `-O3` at
    0.525G and 117.3M (0.999x in cycles, 1.079x in instructions). The 8-lane
    tile alone reached 0.610G and 120.8M. The other 17 corpus programs
    compile to byte-identical `__text` with the same exit codes, so their
    runtimes are unchanged. The `run.py` diagnostic lane (certificates off,
    warm, LOADED at 1-minute load 10.5 before and 7.8 after, so not
    evidence): 18 of 18 MATCH, `p4_matmul` 0.997x LLVM `-O3` (campaign
    8.868x), vectorizable geomean 0.841x (1.553x), all programs 1.075x
    (1.267x).

- L14-P8 and X-DARWIN-P8 (Darwin arm64 performance): the first
  `aarch64-apple-darwin` ledger row, and a finding that the certificates-on
  bridge compiles none of the benchmark corpus on this host. The evidence
  strength is measurement: one quiet, clean, same-session campaign on an Apple
  M4 Max under macOS 26.6.2 at `01fc13b13`, retained in
  `reports/perf/2026-09-28-darwin-aarch64-campaign/`. It is not proof, and it is
  not a claim about any other revision.
  - **Host target everywhere.** `run.py`, `compile_time_canary.sh` and
    `compile_determinism_sentinel.sh` already took the Trust compiler's host
    triple (`d98110a32`). The two scaling gates did not:
    `benchmarks/beat-llvm/scale_gate.py` fixed `x86_64-apple-darwin` for both
    lanes, which fails with E0463 here because the Trust package ships only the
    `aarch64-apple-darwin` standard library. `benchmarks/compile-scaling/run.py`
    defaulted to a Linux `.so` backend path. Both now take the driver's host. `scale_gate.py` has
    `--target`, and `compile-scaling` loads the host-suffixed backend (or
    `--dylib`) and refuses a stale one. `scripts/tests/test_perf_host_target.py`
    lints every performance entry point for a fixed default triple or backend
    suffix; it matches all four retired spellings.
  - **The row.** `run.py --cold`, the full corpus at the contract N in the
    production configuration, was eligible evidence (quiet: load 1.29 before,
    1.66 after, threshold 8.0; clean tree; Clean 0.9.0 ran). The ratchet appended
    it as this host/target's first baseline. It records **0 of 18 MATCH**
    (coverage 0.0%): every program fails closed with `[TCG-PROOF-465]`, because
    proof promotion rejects emitted opcodes whose only evidence is statistical
    sampling (`StpPreIndex`, …) or a registry name lookup (`Movz`, `TailCall`).
    That is ledger `L07-P2`, the class the Linux canary reached at `159f53415`.
    `G5` fails at 0.0%, and the other ten gates are unmeasured. The canary is
    GATE RED and the sentinel DETERMINISTIC-FAILCLOSED (5 of 5 cold attempts),
    for the same reason.
  - **Diagnostic lane (never evidence, not in the ledger).** With
    `--bridge-cg-arg no-proof-certs`, 18 of 18 MATCH. Runtime geomean is 1.267x
    LLVM `-O3` (scalar 1.010x, worst 8.87x `p4_matmul`). Warm compile is 1.367x
    `-O2` and cold 4.263x. Linked size is 1.0006x and compiler peak RSS 1.188x.
    Read as gates, only G1a (scalar <= 1.30x), G5 and S1 (size <= 1.10x) would
    pass; the lane is never evidence.
  - **Scaling (proofs off).** `scale_gate.py --rss` measured compile time of
    1.38x, 1.57x, 3.25x and **12.14x** LLVM and peak RSS of 1.23x, 1.65x, 4.57x
    and **25.35x** (9.45 GB at 33,605 lines). A repeat gave 12.22x and 25.12x. The
    growth is roughly quadratic from 11k to 34k lines and is not yet located.
    `compile-scaling`'s four shapes, which stop at 400 functions, stay within
    its 0.6 exponent-excess limit (excess +0.02, +0.28, +0.14, +0.00).
  - Host conditions recorded with the run:
    - the Trust package's own Clean lacks `carcara-verify`, so the backend used
      managed Clean 8606 (`X-HOST-P8`);
    - the vendored `drat-trim` built by Apple clang 21 / SDK 27.0 does not match
      `canary_certs/manifest.v1`, so the portable certificate set is disabled;
    - macOS cannot pin the 12P+4E cores.
  - `check_perf_ratchet.py`'s ledger badge printed a null compile geomean as
    "Nonex". It now prints "not measured" and names the row's target. The
    committed `LEDGER.md` also picks up the RSS columns the renderer gained in
    `d98110a32`.
  - L14-P8 now has a Darwin row, but that row measures only the refusal. No
    runtime, compile, size, RSS or proofs-on scaling value exists for the
    production lane on this host, and no TY workload was timed (`L14-P4`,
    `L14-P6`, `L14-P7`).

- L10-P6 (emission-time independent decode, Darwin lane): ENC-5 now has an arm
  for every word-encodable emitted AArch64 form. Two new slices read each word
  by its Arm ARM encoding class, require every non-field bit to hold the
  class's fixed value and compare every field with the machine-IR intent:
  `aarch64::decode_check_fp_simd` (every scalar FP form in the H/S/D banks:
  data processing with one, two and three sources, FCVT, the half-precision
  FCMP an F16 `fcmp` lowers to (S/D FCMP keeps its flag-consumer decoder), FP
  immediate, FP/integer conversion, FMOV; every Advanced SIMD form the machine
  IR names: three same, three different, two-register miscellaneous, across
  lanes, scalar pairwise, by element, copies, modified immediate, shifts, EXT,
  UDOT, LD1/ST1 post-index) and `aarch64::decode_check_int` (shifted and carry
  add/sub, NEG, ADDS/SUBS immediate, BIC, logical immediates, TST, ROR,
  SMULH/UMULH/ UMULL, ADRP/ADR/ADD lo12, GOT/TLV/GOTTPREL loads and ELF TPREL
  adds with their holes, LDRSW, TBZ/TBNZ, LSE atomics and CAS, LDAR/STLR,
  barriers, BRK, NOP, unconditional trap pseudos), plus the typed MOVZ, STR,
  BL, BLR and Bcc aliases and LDR (literal): 302 of the 325 opcodes have an
  arm (127 before); no emission site produces a word for the 23 without one
  (the encoder refuses 18 of them; it would spell `Phi`, `StackAlloc`, `Copy`,
  `Retain` and `Release` as NOP, which ENC-5 counts or, on a proof-grade
  route, refuses). The integer slice follows the machine IR's width
  convention: the width-selecting operand (the destination, Rt of an LSE
  atomic, Rs of CAS) or the opcode fixes a word's width and other data
  registers are compared by number in either W/X view, as register allocation
  spells them (`AND Xd, Wn, #1` for Trunc of I32/I16/U32/U16 to `Bool`, UMULL
  with 64-bit sources from the masked-UMULL fusion); scalar FP operands must
  share one width, so the 198 mixed H/S/D shapes the encoder accepts are
  mismatches. Proof-grade AArch64 routes (proof-required and verifying
  compiles and JITs, the Core compiler) now refuse a word ENC-5 did not
  decode, tagged `[TCG-DECODE-CHECK-UNDECODED]`; compatibility routes still
  count it. The need was measured, not assumed: `TCG_DECODE_CHECK_CENSUS_DIR`
  makes every encode append its per-opcode ENC-5 outcomes and real samples,
  and `scripts/enc5_floor_census.py` reduces a Darwin floor run into the
  committed `tests/aarch64_enc5_floor_census/darwin_floor.tsv`. Measured on
  this host: before, the Darwin floor emitted 227 opcodes, 114 of them (53 of
  the 67 scalar FP/Advanced SIMD opcodes) with undecoded words, 435,921 of
  5,012,423 checked words and 19 of the 297 proof-grade ones; after, the same
  227 opcodes emit 5,012,456 words and none is undecoded (both censuses are
  committed; the earlier one's 473 undecoded real samples all decode now). The
  new `aarch64_enc5_floor_census` target pins the emitted and still-undecoded
  lists, replays every committed sample, requires every single-bit corruption
  of each FP/SIMD and integer-slice sample and of 218 clang-assembled words to
  mismatch, runs the live encoder over the shapes it enumerates (1,771
  same-view shapes, 1,581 encoded, and all 772 W/X view assignments of the
  integer-slice forms it lists, 764 encoded and 411 of them mixed, each with
  every-bit corruption), compiles Trunc to `Bool` from I32/I16/U32/U16, the
  masked-UMULL product and the 12 F16 `fcmp` predicates from TrustIR on both
  routes, and checks the proof-grade refusal. The census covers the floor
  corpus only, which reaches none of those last lowerings. The new decoder
  found an encoder disagreement: a NEON bitwise op read any nonzero trailing
  selector as 16B, so the 64-bit 4H/2S arrangements wrote the upper half of
  the register; the encoder now takes the width from the arrangement and
  refuses a selector outside 0..=6 (no floor corpus emits those selectors).
  `coverage_gate_tests` now pins 0 credited rows without an ENC-5 arm (104
  before), the 12 emitted rows without one (the opaque LL/SC carriers, 167
  rows before) and 28 named arm exits (29). All of this is testing evidence:
  agreement between the encoder and an independently written decoder is
  redundancy, the census covers the Darwin floor corpus on this host only
  (Core admission refuses the census variable, so Core routes are covered by
  the refusal, not the census), and nothing is bound to a formal ISA model.
  The Linux floor registration is not yet run on a Linux host.

- Three false refusals and one nondeterministic refusal the Trust
  superproject's trust-cg pin move surfaced (2026-09-28; all fail closed,
  none miscompiled):
  - `[TCG-A64-SWITCH-BIND]` refused every AArch64 compare whose constant
    operand the O1+ constant folder had materialized as `MovI`: "compare
    constant decodes as `Movz x0, #23, lsl #0` but the intent is `MovI
    [..]`". The encoder spells `MOVZ Rd, #imm16, LSL #0` from four intents
    (`Movz`, and the shift-free two-operand `MovI`, `MOVZWi`, `MOVZXi`), the
    same class the decode check and the constant-materialization proofs use;
    the binding's move-wide chain now accepts exactly that class (register,
    width, `imm16`, opc and halfword are still bound per word, and a shifted
    or three-operand alias is refused). Unit tests pin every MOVZ intent and
    nine corruptions; `const_folded_movi_compare_constant_binds` drives the
    real pipeline at O0-O3 and fails without the fix.
  - The rustc bridge's fat -> thin pointer cast seams
    (`lower_wide_to_thin_ptr_cast`, `lower_dyn_fat_to_thin_ptr_cast`) bound
    the destination to the fat pointer's plain `Ptr` data lane, while a later
    reborrow `&*p` retypes through a `PtrToPtr` that declares the destination
    LOCAL's own type as its source, so the adapter refused it ("CastOp::PtrToPtr
    source type mismatch: declared src_ty=PtrConst(..), operand .. has type
    Ptr"): `<[T]>::as_array`, and so every `<[T] as PartialEq<[T; N]>>::eq`.
    The seams now bind the lane at the destination's own type
    (`retype_plain_address_to_local`, the retype whole-local slot addresses
    already used); `fat_thin_reborrow_differential` compares four such shapes
    with LLVM at O0 and O2.
  - Since thin pointers became loop-header phis (275e8973a), the bridge's
    back-edge faithfulness check counted a store THROUGH a carried pointer
    (`(*r) = ..`) as a mutation OF the pointer and refused the pointer's
    identity phi as a dropped update ("loop-carried local _2 is mutated
    inside the loop but its back-edge value is the unchanged loop-header phi
    parameter"): any loop writing through a `&mut` live across it, e.g.
    `let r = &mut v; while .. { *r = .. }` at O0 or an inlined closure
    capturing `&mut` at O2/O3. The completeness gate beside it already
    skipped `Deref`-led stores; both gates now read one def-site map
    (`own_storage_assign_blocks`), so whole and field stores still count.
    `loop_store_through_pointer_differential` compares three such loops with
    LLVM at O0, O2 and O3.
  - The bridge's memory-backed analysis walked two `HashMap`s in hash order
    while asking a layout query that can refuse, so a function with two
    refusable referents (an escaping `&Nat` owning a `Vec<u64>` and an
    escaping `&Name` owning a `String`) named either one depending on the
    run; Trust's `trust-ir-cg-collection-owner-image`, which asserts the
    `Vec<u64` text, failed at random. Both walks now go in local order;
    `refusal_order_determinism` compiles such a function eight times and
    requires one text.

  Evidence for all four: tests on this host in the unverified `targo` lane
  and an out-of-tree replay of the 24 Trust `trust-ir-cg` run-make recipes
  against the rebuilt bridge with the installed Trust toolchain, not proof.

- Linux x86-64 round 5: the greedy allocator's split cascade is BOUNDED
  (`trust-cg-regalloc`'s `split_depth_cap`, LLVM's RS_Split2 rule, default
  generation 1). `GreedyAllocator::apply_split` had re-enqueued both halves at
  `Stage::New`, so a split product was itself splittable without bound: one
  function performed 159 813 splits, spilled 157 852 of the pieces and cost 331s
  of a 343s compile. Seven Clean-kernel fixtures are 125x-1117x faster with
  machine code 9.2x-11.1x SMALLER, and `clean_fixture_host_lowering` goes from
  1844s with seven fixtures undecided to ~54s with **all 38 lowering at O0 and O1
  and an empty refusal class map**. That target is now a ratcheted Linux x86-64
  floor row (68 -> 69 targets, minimum 5 so its three structural guards cannot
  satisfy it alone), because the wall-clock nondeterminism that kept it out had
  exactly this one cause: it now measures 54.28s / 54.47s / 54.28s over three
  consecutive runs. An earlier claim that the bound was a measured no-op outside
  that corpus was FALSE and is retracted in the commit that made it; the corrected
  A/B over all 34 `e2e_x86_64_*` suites finds eight functions in three suites that
  differ, every one with fewer instructions, spills and splits. Execution speed of
  the changed bodies is unmeasured. Recorded in
  `reports/perf/2026-09-28-linux-x86-64-round-5/`, which also states, with the
  reproducer, why `benchmarks/beat-llvm` cannot yet produce an x86-64 Linux ledger
  row: since the 2026-09-17 credit withdrawal the x86 lowering has no operand-exact
  evidence for `MovRR`/`Lea`/`MovRM`/`MovMR`/`LeaRip`, so a bridge compile of a
  trivial program fails closed on `std::rt::lang_start`.

- x86-64 128-bit atomic LOAD (`AtomicU128`/`AtomicI128::load`, core's
  `atomic_load::<u128/i128>`): a new pseudo-instruction, `AtomicLoadCmpxchg16b`,
  that the encoder expands to `XOR EAX,EAX; XOR EDX,EDX; XOR EBX,EBX;
  XOR ECX,ECX; LOCK CMPXCHG16B m128` (LLVM's lowering on a CX16 target). The
  zeroing that makes the compare-exchange a load lives inside the pseudo, not
  in separate `MOV` copies a later pass could drop: its reconstruction models
  the whole expansion over arbitrary incoming RAX/RDX/RBX/RCX (a model missing
  any one XOR, or clearing only the low 32, 16 or 8 bits of one, refutes),
  ENC-3 decodes all five instructions (a dropped, retargeted or narrowed XOR
  fails the compile; the soundness manifest's `CAS-x86-128` family runs that
  check in the pre-push gate), and ENC-2 checks the five objdump rows. RAX/RDX/RBX/RCX are implicit clobbers; the frame now
  saves every callee-saved register a fixed (explicit or implicit) def writes,
  which is RBX here and nothing new elsewhere. Admission is per function: the
  adapter refuses (`[TCG-ATOMIC128-CX16]`) any x86-64 128-bit atomic in a
  function without the `cmpxchg16b` target-feature claim, and the rustc bridge
  makes the claim only on a target-spec CX16 baseline with no `-C target-cpu`
  override and no feature entry, in the spec or in `-C target-feature`, that
  disables CX16 in LLVM: `-cmpxchg16b`, the LLVM names `-cx16` and `-cx8`
  (LLVM's `cx16` implies `cx8`), and any negative entry rustc does not
  recognize, which reaches LLVM verbatim; the bridge's
  `cfg(target_feature = "cmpxchg16b")` now follows LLVM's answer (a measured
  CPU table, `native` from the host, the spec's features with LLVM's names and
  implications, then `-C target-feature` by rustc's own untrimmed rules)
  instead of claiming CX16 on every x86-64 target. 128-bit store, swap, RMW and
  compare-exchange stay refused by name. x86-64 opcode inventory 200/200 ->
  201/201 (0 RED); under E0.2 the new row's sampled evidence earns no
  per-compile credit, so proof-required compiles of functions containing it are
  still refused (`[TCG-PROOF-465]`).
- x86-64 reconstruction ADDRESS-teeth audit made SEMANTIC: a perturbed-address
  obligation now counts as address evidence only if it evaluates `Invalid`.
  None does, and the narrow `Cmpxchg8`/`Cmpxchg16` rows, which the structural
  version had credited with address teeth (their two sides differ as trees at
  every operand), are now carried by the byte-level address lane together with
  `AtomicLoadCmpxchg16b`: the lane's SDM decoder learned `F0 0F B0 /r`,
  `F0 66 0F B1 /r` and `F0 REX.W 0F C7 /1` (LOCK required; a dropped LOCK, a
  dropped REX.W or `/6` refutes), 18 captured encodings re-derived from the live
  encoder, and the gate credits the three rows only when BOTH the address lane
  and their value reconstruction discharge (53 -> 56 address-lane rows).
- CMPXCHG frame-window preconditions: "the probe byte lies outside the modeled
  window" is now bounded by the window's INCLUSIVE last byte. At the largest
  start the no-wrap precondition admits, the exclusive end wrapped to 0, the
  test was false for every probe, and a probe seeded over a neighbour was
  admitted — the sampler found it for the CMPXCHG16B row (zero base,
  displacement -24) as a refutation of the correct model; the narrow
  `Cmpxchg8`/`Cmpxchg16` rows carried the same bound, latent at their
  representatives. Both are pinned by tests that evaluate the boundary point.

- X-DARWIN-P4 (D01, with `L01-P2`, `L01-P3`): the strengthened Linux L01
  C-boundary oracles now execute on `aarch64-apple-darwin` against Apple clang
  at O0-O3. Three macOS-native twins join the Darwin floor with exact
  minimums: `e2e_aarch64_aggregate_stack_darwin` (186 signatures, 494
  checks per level: the Linux Wide/Large corpus, packed narrow named stack
  arguments ahead of every composite class, odd-register `__int128` and
  16-aligned composites with the X7 shadow, HFA packing, the all-or-nothing
  FPR rule and the HFA membership limits, and anonymous aggregates read by
  `va_arg`), `e2e_aarch64_variadic_darwin` (40 signatures, 80 checks per
  level; TrustCG caller only, since variadic definitions stay refused with
  `[TCG-VARIADIC-DEFINITION]` and anonymous by-reference aggregates with
  `[TCG-VARARG-ABI]`) and `e2e_aarch64_bool_abi_darwin` (4,072 checks per
  level: Bool arguments with DarwinPCS-legal dirt at every register and stack
  position, packed narrow stack words, callee extension of Bool/narrow results
  and caller extension of TrustCG arguments, through hand-written Apple
  assembly callers and probes; since `Trunc` already zero-extends, only the
  caller's sign extension of negative `i8`/`i16` arguments is observable, not
  its zero extension of `bool`/`u8`/`u16`). They share `tests/common/darwin_c_boundary.rs`,
  whose expected digests are computed in Rust, so the clang-to-clang call is
  checked too. The HVA/V64/V128, vector-type, global-layout and nested-bytes
  oracles already executed here since 2026-09-18. The twins found two defects,
  both fixed: AArch64 `Trunc` to `Bool` was a register move, so `trunc(2)` was a
  true Bool holding 2 (ELF and Mach-O; now `AND #1`), and a DarwinPCS by-value
  composite on the stack took its natural alignment and a size rounded to 8,
  where clang coerces a non-homogeneous composite of at most 16 bytes to
  8-aligned words and packs an HFA's members (53 of the 494 aggregate checks
  failed at O0 before the fixes; unit tests pin both). `benchmarks/abi-xback`
  derives its `gcc-ld` shim from the resolved compiler's host triple and its
  backend suffix from the host; its first Darwin run
  (`reports/perf/2026-09-27-darwin-abi-xback`) matches 320/320 for seeds 1-40
  at O0-O3 in both directions, and an AAPCS64-forced negative control fails 62
  of 80 halves at O2. Still without a Darwin execution twin: the
  by-reference-copy, zero-sized-member HFA and `f16` corpora and the bridge's C
  `FnAbi` aggregate regression. Evidence strength: native execution testing on
  one host with the stock 1.97.1 lane (abi-xback halves in the explicit
  unverified Trust lane with proof certificates off), not proof; no ledger row
  closes here.

- X-DARWIN-P7 (Darwin unwind/EH, rows D03/D11): new Darwin floor target
  `e2e_aarch64_eh_raii_darwin` (9 tests, minimum 9), a mixed-codegen
  exception/RAII/destructor-count campaign. Two trust-ir modules build
  functions from `Invoke`/`LandingPad`/`Resume`, each as a compact-unwind
  twin and a runtime-sized twin. trust-cg's conservative compact-unwind policy
  sends the runtime-sized twin to the DWARF fallback; Apple clang would give
  such a frame a FRAME-mode encoding.
  - The C++-personality module has 15 chains. They cover cleanup pads running
    the C++ destructor of a guard in the CG frame's own slot, catch-all and
    typed pads over a `[CaseError, int]` table (a derived class included), a
    guard destroyed before a typed handler, two invokes in one frame, CG to CG
    to CG nesting, a plain frame, a CG `__cxa_rethrow`, a C++ frame that
    catches and rethrows between CG frames, a cleanup with no destructor that
    throws and catches a second exception, and an empty cleanup.
  - The same module has a three-function touch family: the Linux 768-case
    campaign's frame, which stores to a GOT-imported memory word and calls a
    throwing C++ provider directly and through a relocated function-pointer
    slot. One variant adds a CG cleanup pad and one is a CG catch-all over it.
    They run the Linux campaign's 64 inputs (64-bit edges included) and three
    throw stages, with all three memory words checked.
  - The Rust-personality module has 7 chains, whose cleanup pads run Rust
    drop glue, including a Rust frame that `catch_unwind`s and resumes
    between CG frames.

  Every case must equal a C++-only (632 chain and 1,152 touch cases) or
  Rust-only (184 cases) reference build of the same matrix and the test's
  models. The chain model covers catch site and guard destructor order; the
  touch model covers the whole line. AOT at O0-O3 ran 14,272 C++ cases, with
  the object linked into executables and into a CG dylib that imports its
  helpers and typeinfo from a separate C++ dylib, and 736 Rust cases. Apple
  `objdump`/`otool`/`nm` read the linked `__unwind_info` and the dylib
  boundary back. The unchecked JIT at O0-O3 ran 6,496 C++ cases (the untyped
  chains and the touch family) and 736 Rust cases, with each FDE read back
  through the process unwinder. In all, 22,240 trust-cg cases ran, and CG
  pads ran 6,784 guard destructors with an exception in flight. The object
  rows walk `__eh_frame`: one `zPLR` CIE and one FDE per runtime-sized twin.
  Negative controls: a cleanup pad that skips its destructor, two invokes
  bound to each other's pad, a typed pad bound to `int`, the touch family's
  pad without its destructor and a lost memory store each change exactly the
  cases they reach (24 AOT and 4 JIT mutant runs). The JIT refuses each typed
  chain by name (`JitUnwindTypedCatchUnsupported`) and a proof-grade request
  by name (`JitUnwindProofEvidenceUnavailable`). trust-ir has no indirect
  invoke, so no CG pad covers an indirect call site. The drivers flush each
  trace line as its case finishes, so a crashing case is named by the last
  line before it. No compiler change was needed.

  Evidence strength: native execution against reference builds, models and
  object/image decoding on the Apple M4 Max host in the stock lane. It is not
  a proof of the LSDA, the CFI, the personality routines or the unwinder, and
  the proof-grade JIT still refuses EH. The file also compiles for Linux
  (three host-neutral rows) but is not a Linux floor target: the native test
  host matrix admits only files that execute natively on Linux there, so it
  lists this one as macOS-only with its reason.
- L10-P4 (`mac-reg-block` release gate, Darwin lane): the default-on O2/O3
  matmul register-blocking recognizer now refuses each publication review item
  by name (`NestReject`, `crates/trust-cg-opt/src/mac_reg_block/review_bar.rs`).
  It checks 64-bit data values as well as the 8-byte stride, and requires
  every bounds check in the nest (including the k-loop's `a[i*N+k]` check,
  which was never inspected) to compare against at least `N*N`, with backing
  stack slots of at least `N*N` elements. The index a check compares must be
  defined in a non-header block of its own loop, before the check and in the
  same loop, so it is the current iteration's `x*N + y` with both counters
  below `N`. The only conditional branches allowed are the counted-loop header
  tests, each exiting to its parent loop, and those passing checks. A loop
  header may hold only copies, the counter compare and its branches, because
  it runs once more than the body. Every recognized index, address, load,
  multiply-add and the store must sit in a non-header block of its own loop.
  Every single-definition value the nest reads must be defined on every path
  before the read. A loop counter may be read only inside its own loop and
  not after its latch step, and must be reset once per parent iteration (its
  init in the parent loop, dominating the header). No value the nest writes
  may be live into its exit. Array bases must be single-definition, exact
  `AddPCRel [dst, sp, StackSlot]` slot starts, and the nest may not touch
  physical or frame operands. A bounds length or loop bound held in a
  register, and the element-scale register, must be one `Movz`(+`Movk`)
  materialization outside the nest: the last-wins definition map could
  otherwise read a later redefinition instead of the value reaching the nest.
  Measured on `318f896ed` with the pass on at O2 and O3, four nests the old
  recognizer admitted miscompiled natively: an early exit in the j-loop was
  skipped, a loop live-out returned after the nest came back as 0, i32 values
  in 8-byte cells had the upper half of every `c` cell rewritten, and a short
  `a` check's trap was elided. Review of the first version of this change
  (`eb812128c`) found two more admitted trust-ir shapes that miscompiled the
  same way: an index computed in a loop header before its test and checked
  again after the loop exits (`i*N+N` there, so the check fails for
  `i = N-1`; the fast path returned 0 where the scalar nest returned -1), and
  the whole j body in the j-header (run `N+1` times, so the fast path dropped
  a store to `c[i*N+N]`). The pass-off builds matched the C reference in every
  case. Each named refusal has a unit test on hand-built machine IR; removing
  any one of the header, placement, dominance, counter-read or counter-reset
  guards fails its test. The new target
  `trust-cg-codegen/tests/e2e_aarch64_mac_reg_block_differential.rs` is
  required on the Darwin floor and listed on the Linux floor, not yet run on
  a Linux host. It compiles trust-ir kernels at O2 and O3 with the pass on and
  off through the pipeline's in-process disable list. It runs them natively
  against a C reference, comparing return values, every buffer byte and
  canaries. It covers 14 square i64 kernels in the modeled `i, k, j` shape (N
  in {1, 7, 8, 9, 16, 24, 32, 56, 63, 64, 65, 72, 128} and an outer repeat
  loop). The 9 with N a multiple of 8, including the repeat nest, must be
  rewritten exactly once, and the 5 others must not be. Another 17 kernels
  must be left unrewritten: the `ijk` order, a rectangular nest, f64, i32, and
  13 negative controls, including the two review shapes and `j` or `k` carried
  across parent iterations. A 28-kernel fixed-seed sweep ports
  `scripts/fuzz/matmulfuzz.py`'s generator; that script tests `neon_map`, not
  this pass, and stays unwired. Rewrites are counted through the new per-pass
  change counts `PassStats::changed_runs` and
  `PreparationMetrics::optimization_pass_changes`. Every unrewritten kernel
  must also compile to identical code on and off. Evidence strength: a bounded
  native differential on this host plus recognizer unit tests. It is not a
  proof, and the pass stays scheduled by default. `publish/DECISIONS.md` no
  longer says the bar is not re-checked.
- x86-64 unsigned vector compares: the sign-bit bias in every unsigned
  compare obligation is now spelled as two 64-bit constant halves, not one
  `concat` per lane. The value is unchanged, so the lowering model is
  unchanged (unit-tested per arrangement). AY `f28345ff`'s proof-producing
  checker counts a term as a tree with no sharing and declines one over 4096
  nodes. The per-lane chain, repeated in each `bvxor`, made the four
  unsigned `<16 x i8>` proofs holey. On the new query bytes all 16 unsigned
  cells certify hole-free (AY `unsat` under `--strict-proofs`, Clean 0.9.0
  fully verified, measured twice, byte-identical). The 12 available cells'
  pins in `x86_icmp_manifest_cells.rs` moved to the new digests. The four
  `<16 x i8>` digests are recorded as measured-not-admitted, and those cells
  stay refused until the pinned trust-ir manifest makes them available
  (`reports/2026-09-27-x86-vector-icmp-cells.md`). This works around an AY
  limitation; it does not fix it.
- trust-ir v50 splat follow-ups (memory proportional to the program, not to
  a splat's length):
  * **EH type table.** The reserved `__trust_cg_eh_type_table` spelled
    `splat[ @typeinfo; n ]` was expanded into `n` owned strings per function
    that caught a typed exception. The table is now `EhTypeTable`
    (`trust-cg-ir`): a list shared behind an `Arc`, or a splat kept as one
    symbol and a length, canonical like trust-ir's spelling, with O(1)
    length, lookup and clone. The adapter reads it once per module
    translation and shares it with every function; ISel and the pipeline
    forward it by clone; retained identity (payload v6) encodes the tagged
    spelling in constant size. The LSDA type table (`LsdaTypeTable`) stores
    only the slots the pads bind: the NULL slots below a catch-all are one
    zero run in the image, the table length matters only to a catch-all
    (whose slot `n + 1` must be an `i32` filter, refused by name otherwise),
    and a typed catch against a 2- or a 2^40-entry splat compiles to the
    same object.
  * **Uniform-array floor.** The §3.1 spelling walk descends into sequence,
    set and vector elements as trust-ir's validator does
    (`ChildTypes::Repeated`), so a uniform list nested in a collection is
    refused, and every `Constant` variant has its own arm.
  * **Core admission.** `Inst::ArraySplat` has an explicit census arm (pure
    value construction, no memory effect) instead of the wildcard.
  * **wasm data image.** A non-zero `Splat` global reserves its image
    fallibly (`try_reserve_exact`, refused by name when the host cannot hold
    it) and writes it by one doubling copy; a global whose extent runs past
    the wasm32 address space is refused from its layout before any image is
    built, a BSS one included.
  * **fsym layout.** `FsymLayout::written_mask` / `read_mask` (one `bool` per
    byte, a loop over every array element) are replaced by
    `written_coverage` / `read_coverage`, a `ByteCoverage` structure over the
    type in which an array is one periodic run of its element; the
    interpreter-probe tests compare it byte for byte as before.
- `L05-P9`: borrows, binding frames and `Undef` now lower through one named
  legalization stage, `borrow-frame-undef-legalization`
  (`trust_cg_lower::borrow_frame_undef`). The adapter runs it per function on
  every entry, the strict one included. It records a receipt
  (`ProofContext::borrow_frame_undef`), which the retained strict-LIR
  identity hashes (payload schema v7, golden re-minted). `Borrow`/`BorrowMut`
  lower to a copy of the operand pointer, recording the root and kind.
  `EndBorrow` emits nothing. Each frame is one zero-filled stack slot:
  `BindSlot` stores in place, but only where a static SSA liveness check
  (within blocks and across block edges) finds no superseded handle live
  after the rebind. A scalar `Undef` whose poison is only transported
  becomes the zero of its carrier (the NoUndef model).
  Named `[TCG-BFU]` refusals cover a shared-to-unique reborrow, a borrow of a
  non-pointer or of null, an `EndBorrow` of a non-borrow, an escaping or
  merged frame handle, a handle reaching an entry-block parameter, a
  non-scalar slot, an unclosed frame and a live superseded handle (in the
  same or a later block). They also cover poison that reaches any inspecting
  use, including arithmetic and a volatile store, which trust-ir makes
  undefined behaviour, a slot bound on only some paths and then inspected,
  and an aggregate or annotated `Undef`. The must-refuse row `undef_fresh_havoc_feeds_assume`
  stays refused, now by this stage's reason on all three compiler lanes,
  pinned in `must_refuse_corpus`. Evidence is test-strength and Darwin-only:
  `e2e_aarch64_borrows_frames` (five tests, a new Darwin floor target) runs
  100 (function, input) pairs natively at each of O0-O3, thin and fat-slice
  borrows included, equal to the trust-ir reference interpreter, and checks
  18 refusals by name at O0 and O3, including the interpreter's own
  undefined-behaviour verdict for each poison fixture. No admitted program
  observes the NoUndef zero natively; the conformance manifest pins the zero
  constant of all 16 scalar carriers at LIR level. x86-64 (ELF, Mach-O) and
  aarch64 Linux ELF compile the same target-independent lowering with no
  execution evidence. No ELF twin exists and no proof is claimed. The
  construct-inventory, conformance-manifest and gate pins moved with the
  rows.
- L04-P11 (switch and call forms, Darwin lane): every AArch64 encode now
  binds its switch dispatch to the final bytes independently of the encoder
  (`trust_cg_verify::aarch64_switch_binding`, `[TCG-A64-SWITCH-BIND]`, fail
  closed): each jump-table entry lands on its recorded successor, the `BR`
  register is the `ADD` of this dispatch's `ADR` base and
  `LDRSW [Xbase, Xindex, LSL #2]` entry, the `CMP/B.HI` bounds check covers
  exactly the table with no intervening NZCV writer and lands on the successor
  outside the table, the compared and loaded index values have one origin, a
  non-zero `min_val` is subtracted by the index producer (immediate or
  MOVZ/MOVK chain), every `CMP` whose flags reach a `B.cond` in its block
  binds register, width, constant chain, condition and displacement, and
  every fused `CBZ/CBNZ/TBZ/TBNZ` binds its register, bit and displacement; a
  `BR` that ends no bound jump-table dispatch is refused. Index origins follow
  64-bit `MovR`/`MOVXrr` copies and `SPILL_SLOT_ACCESS`-flagged reloads of a
  frame-pointer-based slot: a reload is the register a 64-bit store to that
  slot earlier in the block wrote, or an opaque value two reloads share only
  when no word between them can write the slot (calls, pairs, atomics,
  writeback and register-offset words, stores through another base or to
  overlapping bytes can); `SP`-based or unflagged reloads are refused, not
  modeled. Move-wide chains are evaluated forwards with each word's width.
  It runs after the layout cross-check on every pipeline encode route
  (`PipelineError::Aarch64SwitchBinding`) and on both `lower` routes
  (`LowerError::SwitchBinding`: the relaxing route after its relaxed layout
  cross-check, and `lower::encode_function`, which has none and until now
  emitted a jump-table `ADR` placeholder with no table; neither route appends
  tables, so a jump-table dispatch is refused there). The rustc bridge
  classifies both new variants as `Regalloc` layer refusals; its 181
  `compile_error_diag` tests, `pipeline_machine_code_validators_are_regalloc`
  among them, pass on this host in the unverified `targo` lane (targo
  1.99.0-dev 321aaeda7, compiled without Trust verification, so no
  verification claim). Evidence, all tests on this host, none a proof:
  `tests/aarch64_switch_binding.rs` (7 tests, Darwin floor target) binds
  dense, holed, negative, wide-minimum and table-sized jump tables and
  binary-search and linear compare trees at O0-O3, refutes a word battery
  (entry off by one, swapped entries, bounds off by one, wrong condition or
  target, BR register swapped, LDRSW operands or scale changed, ADR
  displaced, normalization or case constant changed, branch inverted,
  materialization chunk changed; 496 table and 376 tree cases at O0-O3) and
  an intent-consistent battery that passes the word-versus-intent comparison
  and reaches each semantic check (bound off by one or on another register,
  table target off the recorded CFG, `min_val` or normalization changed,
  default edge moved onto a table arm), and binds a selector spilled under
  register pressure and reloaded for the bounds compare and the table load,
  refusing it when the second reload reads another slot; 13 module unit
  tests cover hand-encoded dispatches, copies through both intents, reload
  pairs across every class of intervening writer, a spilled normalized index
  and a W-form base under an X-form `MOVK`. A mutation run that removes each
  semantic check, the copy and reload following, or the memory-writer
  classification fails at least one of these tests.
  `pipeline_switch_binding_tests` drives every pipeline encode entry point
  (compatibility and proof-grade) with a bound one past its table and
  expects `PipelineError::Aarch64SwitchBinding`, and two `lower` unit tests
  cover a relaxed `TBNZ`-over-`B` binding, a refused compare constant and a
  refused unappended table. The binding trusts the recorded CFG on every
  route: the hand-built `max` fixture of `e2e_run`, whose `B.GT` jumped to an
  unrecorded successor, records its edges, and the runtime-allocation block
  split (`frame::FrameInsertionPlan::split_block_tail`) now keeps the edges
  of branches that stay in the head, and keeps a head-named jump table's
  entries on both halves (L05-P8's run-time length witness
  branches to its trap block mid-block, before a runtime stack allocation;
  its edge moved to the tail, so the binding refused `inc`, `add_k_i8` and
  `chain` of `e2e_aarch64_sequences` at O0/O1 and the proof-grade layout
  cross-check would have refused the same edge). The function verifier's
  covered-elsewhere exemptions are reconciled with the coverage gate by a
  test (`Br` names the per-compile binding, `Ret` is a named deferral in both
  places, `COVERED_ELSEWHERE_NAMED_DEFERRALS`; register copies are no longer
  exempted, since main binds them per instruction). Darwin floor target
  `e2e_aarch64_switch_forms` (3 tests) executes dense, holed, negative,
  wide-minimum, jump-table-sized, binary-search-sized and linear-scan
  switches over i64/i32 selectors, a spilled selector, and indirect calls
  through function-pointer tables at O0-O3 against clang; both new targets
  are registered on the Linux floor but have not run there. This is a
  per-compile consistency check of final bytes against the final machine-IR
  intent and recorded CFG, backed by tests, not a proof: tree membership and
  the source case-to-block map stay bound at ISel by the normalization gate
  and the modelled BST proof, the compare-tree binding is group by group,
  two exchanged recorded successors (and, in a table with holes, a default
  edge moved onto another table arm) are not told apart, and a bounds branch
  relaxed over a `B` is refused.
- rustc bridge: a synthesized panic now reports the location rustc reports.
  Every raise (the unwinding panic block, the `Assert` failure edge, the 18
  intercepted bounds-check raises, the direct-call interceptions of diverging std
  `#[track_caller]` helpers) passed a raw span to `core::panicking::panic` — the
  FUNCTION's start for an `Assert`, the callee's body inside a `#[track_caller]`
  frame. They now ask `caller_location_value_for(site)`, rustc's
  `Body::caller_location_span` walk: a `#[track_caller]` body forwards its incoming
  location, an inlined frame reports its call site. Measured with the
  track_caller acceptance suite (std binaries, unwinding): all ten panic-location
  rows (index, unwrap, plain index, literal, overflow; O0 and O2) now equal LLVM
  (e.g. `pl_index.rs:10:13`, was `7:1`); lowering census unchanged (2 roots).
  LIMITATIONS.md now also records that a failing bounds check under
  `panic=abort` traps (SIGILL/SIGTRAP, no message, no hook) where LLVM aborts.

- trust-ir pin `066e1765` -> `7b0947ee` (no wire change; Clean `414913cc`
  and AY `f28345ff` unchanged), moved by `scripts/bump_trust_ir_pin.py`,
  carrying trust-cg's half of three owner decisions taken on the owner's
  behalf. The two format/backend disagreements the KIND 4 must-refuse corpus
  had recorded (`dealloc_instruction`, `vector_unsigned_cmp_wide_lanes_x86`)
  are each settled by ONE rule, stated in trust-ir and enforced here; neither
  row is in any known-accepted table any more (report:
  `reports/2026-09-27-owner-decisions-trust-cg-half.md`).
  * **Deallocation (G18-1, re-decided).** Every `Inst::Dealloc` is refused, in
    every body (licensed, claim-less or `Ungated`), with `[TCG-DEALLOC]` citing
    trust-ir's `UnlowerableForCodegen`, by trust-ir's own verdict on every
    public entry: `validate_codegen_prerequisites` consumes it where that layer
    runs, and the validated strict entry (which reuses a complete
    `validate_module` report) reads it from trust-ir's lowerability layer
    (`codegen_lowerability_errors`) over every body, including one this backend
    skips rather than lowers (an `AvailableExternally` definition, which the
    strict entry admitted until a review probe caught it). The instruction arm
    stays as a backstop no public entry reaches. The provenance lowering
    (`translate_dealloc`, 2887cbf01) and all of its machinery are deleted;
    this backend no longer recovers an allocator origin or a layout from
    dataflow. The allocator-balance controls now release through calls
    (`__rust_dealloc` / `free`). `refuse/dealloc_instruction` is refused on
    every lane and by the binary, with its reason pinned.
  * **x86-64 vector compares.** Every x86-64 module entry asks trust-ir's one
    reader (`chc_x86_vector_icmp_cell_status`) and refuses a fail-closed cell
    (`[TCG-X86-VECTOR-ICMP]`, `VectorCompareCellFailClosed`) — today the four
    unsigned `<16 x i8>` compares. The unsigned `v4_i32` / `v2_i64` / `v8_i16`
    lowerings are manifest-available on a certificate MEASURED outside this
    repository (AY `f28345ff` + Clean 0.9.0), which this build does not re-run;
    `trust-cg-verify/tests/x86_icmp_manifest_cells.rs` pins the obligation
    ground of every available cell (degenerate for `eq`/`sgt`, otherwise
    non-degenerate with its certified query digest), and
    `trust-cg-codegen/tests/x86_vector_icmp_feature_guard.rs` that each cell
    compiles exactly from its feature guard up. `refuse/vector_unsigned_cmp_wide_lanes_x86`
    is retired upstream; `refuse/vector_unsigned_cmp_bytes_x86` is refused by
    name. `<8 x i8>` eq/ne on x86-64 stays an ungoverned gap, pinned.
  * **Aggregate passing (SPEC §17).** The `Unclassified` gate reads trust-ir's
    one by-value-aggregate-slot predicate (`Module::is_by_value_aggregate_slot`),
    so a refined aggregate, a vector and a closure passed by value are refused
    (each measured ADMITTED before on the AArch64 and X86_64 entries). The
    rustc bridge's half of §17 (refuse or pre-lower a memory-placed argument
    whose `NativeC` placement differs from rustc's) is NOT landed: a refusal
    of every such argument was measured to refuse all-bridge edges that agree
    (215 x86-64 `core` roots; `m142_deref_store_leaf_offsets_match_llvm` on
    AArch64), so the bridge keeps declining that placement and the
    cross-backend miscompile stays open and documented in `LIMITATIONS.md`
    until the pre-lowered crossing lands. The bridge's `STRUCT_PASSING` doc
    now says so.
  Tests: `targo --unverified` (no proof claim). Each new test carries a
  recorded mutation control (the report lists them).

- rustc bridge, a SILENT MISCOMPILE fixed: a scalar field read through a
  reference to a struct whose earlier field is a `repr(transparent)` newtype over
  a `str` / slice pointer (`NonNull<str>` — `core::panic::Location::filename`)
