  `&str` field already takes, typed from rustc's layout. Found by the adversarial
  review of the `#[track_caller]` design; census unchanged (3 lowering roots).
  The same review measured a larger, still-open cross-backend hole: a by-value
  `Memory` aggregate over 8 bytes (`struct { u32, u32, u32 }`) is a POINTER to a
  copy under rustc's Rust ABI, which the bridge passes by value — see
  LIMITATIONS.md; its fix (an indirect-argument lane) is in design.

- trust-ir pin `524d8ded` -> `066e1765` (wire v50): `Inst::ArraySplat` and
  `Constant::Splat`, the constant-size uniform array `[v; n]`, lower in
  constant size in `n`. A byte-uniform element (zero, `-1`, any `u8`, `bool`,
  `+0.0`, or an aggregate/nested splat of one repeated byte) is ONE `Memset`
  of `n * stride` bytes; any other element is written once into lane 0 and
  copied by doubling (`ceil(log2 n)` non-overlapping `Memcpy`s, at most 64 for
  any u64 `n`). Offsets and counts are u64 products of the authoritative
  element stride; an extent past what the u32 LIR carrier or one stack slot
  can describe is refused by name, never truncated. A `Splat` global
  initializer renders its element once (zero elements stay a zero run) and
  relocates each lane of an element that carries a relocation. Consumers
  decide both constructs explicitly: module merge, core admission, the
  golden interpreter, retained identity (Constant tag 16), SSA value uses,
  definite-init, fsym (admitted as pure value construction; the element
  escapes), the wasm data image, the niche codec and the bridge's symbol
  walk. The rustc bridge now spells a uniform byte run of a global image as
  `splat[ b; n ]` (trust-ir's validated one-spelling rule refuses the raw
  `Bytes` list) and its typed-reference repair emits canonical arrays. The
  reference interpreter lost its memory budget (address-space exhaustion is
  `OutOfMemory`, not UB): fsym's run model is now fuel plus clean entry
  arguments, and the UB map and layout port were re-derived against the new
  interpreter. Evidence: `tests/array_splat_lowering.rs` (small versus huge
  lane counts by LIR census, no execution), the construct inventory
  (ArraySplat and Splat executed by the insts sweep at O0-O3 against the
  interpreter and C), and the conformance manifest rows.
- x86-64 proof lane, slice 1: a SOURCE-BOUND WHOLE-BODY THEOREM
  (`trust_cg_verify::x86_source_bound_body`), the x86 analog of the AArch64
  source-bound frame that upstream identified as missing (the XD-01 operand
  binding refutes, but nothing on x86 could EARN `Formal` after E0.2). For a
  System V function whose LIR is an I64 chain of copies / constants / add / sub
  ending in a return, the verifier builds one definitional SMT query over the
  pre-RA machine stream and the LIR source (observable: RAX, with the
  callee-saved registers and RSP in the one canonical encoding — their
  preservation is judged by the trusted walk, not the solver), replays it through
  the identity-admitted AY with Clean/Carcara checking, and credits the covered
  rows `Formal` ONLY on a checked UNSAT; `sat` fails the rows, anything
  inconclusive leaves them unverified. TV-2 and carrier hygiene still run after
  the credit. On this host (AY 0.27.0 build 10530, Clean 1.2.0) add, sub,
  identity, constant returns and copy chains promote at O0-O3 on Darwin and
  Linux targets; a wrong register, SUB-for-ADD or an RBX return is refuted. Win64
  and every shape outside the slice are unchanged (still refused by E0.2).
  Not run here: the AArch64-host-only suites covering the shared export/replay
  plumbing this touched (they compile to zero tests on x86-64).
- x86-64 proof lane, slice 2 of the source-bound body theorem. Pointer carriers:
  the LIR `Copy` the adapter makes of a pointer-width `PtrToPtr`/`PtrToInt`/
  `IntToPtr`, and pointer parameters carrying aggregate pointee metadata (the
  body reads no memory). Narrow carriers: B1/I8/I16/I32 parameters, results,
  constants, `Uextend`/`Sextend`/`Trunc`, same-carrier `Bitcast` (`i8 as u8`),
  with the encoder's width rules as verify-owned semantics (a 32-bit write
  zero-extends, `MOVZX`/`MOVSX`/`MOVSXD` write the full 64-bit extension).
  Arithmetic beyond congruence: `AddRI`/`SubRI`, `And`/`Or`/`Xor` in RR and RI
  form, `ShlRI`/`ShrRI`/`SarRI` by an in-range constant, `ImulRR`,
  register-base `LEA` and `LeaSib` (scale 1, 2, 4 or 8), commuted operands.
  The observable is the return bits every caller reads: RAX, EAX, AX or AL,
  and EAX = 0/1 for a `bool`. The psABI and an LLVM caller read only AL of a
  `bool`, but the backend's own B1 contract is a clean 32-bit carrier (its
  callers copy EAX and forward it to callees that rely on the extension), so
  a `bool` result with EAX bits 8..31 set is refuted; a function that takes
  and returns a `bool` is walked under the psABI and the clean-bool argument
  views. Documented residual: LLVM's Darwin callee convention also extends
  `i8`/`i16` returns for legacy callers (PR26665), which neither the backend
  nor the theorem promises. The seven preserved roots left the one canonical
  encoding (the walk judges preservation): with them AY 0.27.0 rejects its own
  proof of narrow and commuted theorems, replayed in the qualification test.
  Admission never depends on the replayer: SAR, a 32-bit multiply, a commuted
  64-bit multiply and a scaled LEA are admitted with exact semantics, do not
  certify on the qualification host (Carcara rejects AY's `bitblast_ashr`
  step; AY's strict certification rejects its own multiply proofs; the LEA
  proof prints a `hole`) and stay unverified, with each exact AY/Clean output
  recorded and checked by the qualification test; a wrong lowering of them is
  refuted. Measured on the Darwin x86-64 `core` O0 proof census (bridge built
  from the first revision of this change, which observed AL for a `bool` and
  kept SAR, the 32-bit multiply and the scaled LEA out of the domain; same
  stage-1 trustc): 3212 -> 3043 failed roots, `[TCG-PROOF-465]` 3209 -> 3040,
  169 roots newly promote, none newly fails, `[TCG-SOURCE-BOUND-X86-MISMATCH]`
  never occurs; that census's wall time was 943 s against 782 s for the
  slice-1 census (single unpaired runs; the new body replays are the likely
  cost). The census was not re-run after the clean-bool observable; the
  qualification test certifies every `bool` fixture shape under it (identity,
  constants, and/xor, truncation and zero extension). New
  bridge diagnostic knob `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=x86-body-trace` prints each
  classified function's lane outcome and, for a replay that credits nothing,
  the raw AY/Clean outcome with its `proof_gate` class.
  plumbing this touched (they compile to zero tests on x86-64). MEASURED on the
  Darwin x86-64 `library/core` O0 proof census (bridge at `bc8624b4d`,
  `reports/perf/2026-09-27-darwin-x86-64-census/`): 3341 -> 3212 failed roots,
  `[TCG-PROOF-465]` 3323 -> 3209 — 114 roots now promote on the body theorem.
- x86-64 proof lane, slice 3 of the source-bound body theorem: direct calls.
  A LIR `Call` (bound by symbol or to the exact module function) with 0-6
  B1/I8/I16/I32/I64 register arguments and at most one such result is in the
  body domain, including a void body and a body ending in a call that never
  returns (`Call; Trap`, pre-RA `CALL; UD2`). The observable adds every
  call's arguments, in order, at the bits the callee reads. The callee is
  modelled as an uninterpreted function of a world token and its arguments,
  stated in Ackermann-reduced form: the trusted walk pairs the k-th machine
  `CALL` with the k-th source call (callee symbol, exact-module binding, and
  `call_arg_regs`/`call_result_regs` equal to the System V table for the
  source signature, else a typed `[TCG-SOURCE-BOUND-X86-MISMATCH]`), both
  sides share that call's result as one free input `r{k}`, and a call
  clobbers RAX, RCX, RDX, RSI, RDI and R8-R11 (a later read is an undefined
  read; the bits of RAX above a narrow result are a free input `g{k}`). The
  UF + world form itself does not certify on this host, and the reduced form
  does. The qualification test replays the UF + world form of all 19 call
  shapes: AY 0.27.0 rejects its own proof of each one with an argument
  (`step t1 uses unverified trust rule`) and leaves one unproved step in the
  no-argument wrapper's. So callee identity and call order rest on the
  trusted Rust pairing, not on the replayed proof. One canonical encoding
  change: a theorem with several observed items (call arguments, or slice
  2's two `bool` walks) now states the conjunction of the per-item equations
  against `true` instead of one concatenation. The reason is that the same
  AY rejects its own proof of the seven-item concatenation of a six-argument
  wrapper while its conjunction certifies. Every two- and three-item
  concatenation certifies, and the qualification test replays the
  concatenated form of each several-item theorem. Single-item theorems keep
  their bytes. Selector fix found by the theorem:
  a `bool` call result was copied from EAX, but a callee defines only AL
  (psABI; LLVM returns `setb %al`, measured), so a body that returned or
  forwarded it passed EAX bits 8..31 on as its own clean 32-bit bool (a C
  callee returning AL = 0/1 with bits 8..31 set: 8 of 12 native checks
  failed through the rustc bridge). The x86-64 selector now re-extends a
  `bool` call result from AL (`MOVZX`) and declares 8 defined result bits;
  the theorem refutes the old copy. Outside the domain, with tests:
  indirect, variadic and invoke calls, stack arguments, sret callees,
  aggregate/i128/float arguments and results, a `bool` parameter forwarded
  as a `bool` argument, and a body with no result and no call argument
  (no observable): the `#[track_caller]` panic helpers that `panic=abort`
  lowers to `abort()` with a dead location parameter are such bodies, so
  they are NOT promoted by this slice. Host qualification (toolchain AY
  0.27.0 build 10530, Clean 5f09e36c): 19/19 call shapes certify through the
  real builder, including a `u16` (AX) result and a parameter received in
  RDX that lives across the call. The slice-1/2 set is unchanged (the six
  recorded gaps stay gaps). AY refutes with counterexamples seven wrong call
  lowerings: swapped arguments, a clobbered argument, RAX's undefined bits
  returned above a `u32` and above a `u16` result, the first result read
  after the second call, same-callee calls reordered, and a `bool` result
  copied from EAX. It also refutes the UF + world form of the swapped
  arguments. A wrong callee, binding, register metadata or call count is a
  typed mismatch (unit tests), and so is a read after a call of any
  caller-saved register through any width alias. The clobber table is pinned
  to the IR's System V caller-saved set, and narrow-alias extension sources
  have their own negative controls. The AOT diverging-shim test now holds
  the shim that forwards its formals (`Call(p, n); Trap`, the
  `panic_already_borrowed -> do_panic` shape) to the body theorem: without a
  replayed proof the compile is refused naming the missing replay, and with
  one the shim promotes on four `Formal` body-theorem rows, not on the
  `call_only_body` exemption. MEASURED through the rustc bridge (stage-1
  trustc d7f143f3b, Darwin x86-64, O0, proofs required): 20 call bodies and
  their leaf callee promote (every body theorem replays Valid) and pass 4295
  native checks against C callees that record the registers they receive and
  return garbage above their ABI bits, and the three `bool` call-result
  bodies now pass their 12 native checks; the `core` proof census goes 3078
  -> 2887 failed roots (`[TCG-PROOF-465]` 3076 -> 2885), 191 roots newly
  promote, none newly fails, `[TCG-SOURCE-BOUND-X86-MISMATCH]` never occurs
  and no resource-budget refusal occurred. That bridge was built before the
  last edit of `x86_source_bound_body.rs` (the verifier, not the selector);
  a bridge rebuilt from the committed tree `c2a7639c0` reproduces the census
  root set and the corpus traces and exit codes exactly
  (`reports/perf/2026-09-28-darwin-x86-64-census-slice3/`). Wall time
  carries no signal on this shared host: the same root set took 785 s and
  911 s. Of the 227 baseline roots whose only uncovered rows were
  `MovRR`/`MovRR32`, 143 promote; 51 are the no-observable bodies above and
  17 void bodies without a call (their only rows are dead copies of unused
  parameters).
- x86-64 proof lane, slice 4 of the source-bound body theorem: memory in
  straight-line bodies. Private stack slots (LIR `StackAddr`, pre-RA
  `lea r, [StackSlot + disp]` or a load/store through one) are bound by
  index (the machine slot table must equal the source's), each a distinct
  private region disjoint from the others and from incoming memory, modelled
  exactly byte by byte in both trusted walks and never observed; a slot
  whose address is used as anything but a load/store address escapes and is
  outside the domain. Incoming memory is one byte-addressed world the callees
  share, stated as an Ackermann-reduced access trace like the calls: the walk
  pairs the machine's `MovRM8/16/32`/`MovRM` and `MovMR8/16/32`/`MovMR`
  (`[register + disp]`) with the source's `Load`/`Store` by world-trace
  position, kind and width (else `X86BodyUnsupported::AccessTrace`, no
  claim); a paired load reads one shared free input `l{j}`; the observable
  adds every access's address and every store's value; no disjointness
  between pointer arguments is assumed and no access moves across a call.
  Exact width rules from the encoder and the register allocator: `mov
  r8/r16, m` define only the destination's low bits (the bits above are a
  free input `u{k}` even over a register that held a value, because
  allocation treats that destination as a pure definition), `mov r32, m`
  zero-extends, and a store's register operand names at least the stored
  bits (an 8-byte store of a 32-bit register is outside the domain, since
  allocation keeps only a 32-bit register's low 32 bits). A `bool` is never
  loaded from incoming memory in the domain (trust-ir reads its byte as
  `!= 0`, the selector reads it as is). Also admitted: `StructGep` (field offsets from a verify-owned
  C layout, checked against `Type::offset_of`), exactly folded constant
  offsets, and sret functions (stores through the leading hidden buffer are
  incoming stores; the observed return is RAX = the buffer, as System V
  requires). New typed mismatches `MemoryAddress`, `MemoryValue` and
  `StackSlotBounds`; a possible reordering the exact affine check finds (a
  permutation that moves each stored value with its address and keeps the
  order of accesses to one known location) makes no claim, and one it
  cannot see is refuted by the positional theorem.
  One canonical encoding, chosen by host qualification (toolchain AY 0.27.0
  build 10530, Clean 5f09e36c): one `(Array (_ BitVec 64) (_ BitVec 8))`
  memory and a 1-ary byte UF do not certify (AY rejects its own proof,
  `step t0/t1 uses unverified trust rule`, or refuses publication, #8821;
  the qualification test replays both and records the outcomes), while the
  pure-`QF_BV` trace certifies all 30 memory fixture shapes through the real
  builder (admitted bodies beyond the fixtures do not all certify; their
  rows stay Unverified and LIMITATIONS.md records the measured gaps). AY
  refutes with counterexamples eleven wrong lowerings (wrong slot, missing
  slot store, 4-byte store of an 8-byte local, wrong field offset, store
  through the wrong pointer, wrong stored value, forwarding across a
  may-alias store, a narrow load treated as zero-extending, the same over a
  register that held zero, store addresses permuted without their values,
  and the slot-`bool` finding below); a missing, reordered, resized or
  call-crossing incoming access is refused. FINDING, not fixed here: the
  selector lowers a `bool` `Load` to `mov r8, m` and returns the carrier
  with `mov eax, r32`, so a function returning a loaded `bool` leaves EAX
  bits 8..31 undefined (measured through the bridge: `movb (%rax), %cl; movl
  %ecx, %eax`, and with the caller's RCX preloaded 4 of 6 native calls
  returned `0x123456xx`/`0xffffffxx`); for a slot's `bool` its body theorem
  is refuted, so the rows fail. Diagnostic knob
  `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=x86-body-dump=DIR` writes the query of every body
  theorem that does not replay Valid, rendered with the replay's own
  configuration (an empty `DIR` writes nothing). MEASURED through
  the rustc bridge (stage-1 trustc d7f143f3b, Darwin x86-64, O0, proofs
  required): a 26-function memory corpus promotes (every body theorem
  replays Valid) and passes 18876 native checks against a C harness,
  including aliased pointer arguments; an sret writer and two struct-field
  readers promote and pass 1568 checks (RAX = buffer, no byte outside the
  buffer written); the `core` proof census goes 2887 -> 2727 failed roots
  (`[TCG-PROOF-465]`), 160 roots newly promote, none newly fails,
  `[TCG-SOURCE-BOUND-X86-MISMATCH]` never occurs and no resource-budget
  refusal occurred (`reports/perf/2026-09-28-darwin-x86-64-census-slice4/`).
  64 bound bodies stay unverified because AY rejects its own proof (12 are
  the slice-2/3 gaps, 52 are memory constructors of 54-242 rows) and one is
  refuted (`PanicInfo::can_unwind`, the `bool` finding). The largest
  remaining blockers among the 1418 flag-free failed roots are two-register
  results (433), sret callees (231), non-scalar results (150) and
  parameters (113), and slots whose address escapes into a call (101).
- Review fixes to slice 4 (credit soundness, no exceptions, integration).
  Two credit holes, each shown on a mutated selector stream through the
  real allocator, AY, Clean and native execution, are closed: a `mov r8/r16,
  m` into a register that already held a value was modelled as a merge,
  while register allocation treats that destination as a pure definition
  (a byte loaded into a zeroed register and returned without `movzx` was
  credited Formal and returned `0xabcdf07f` for `0x7f`); the bits above a
  narrow load are now always a free input. An 8-byte store of a 32-bit
  register read bits 32..63 that allocation does not preserve; a store's
  register operand must now name the stored width. A `bool` loaded from
  incoming memory is outside the domain: trust-ir reads its byte as `!= 0`
  and the selector reads it as is, and no trust-ir or LIR rule says the
  byte is 0 or 1 (an owner FINDING in LIMITATIONS.md). The reordering
  exemption now requires every stored value to move with its address (a
  permutation of addresses alone is a named `MemoryAddress` mismatch) and
  keeps the order of accesses to one known location. The `MixedStores`
  fixture joins the qualified set (30 shapes, with a new sign-extended
  store), and a test fails when an admitted fixture whose theorem holds is
  left out; SIB load/store controls are real; the pinned host-qualification
  outcomes are compared only under the AY/Clean pair they were measured
  with; the empty `x86-body-dump` knob no longer writes into the current
  directory, and the dump renders with the replay's own configuration.
  Merged with `main`: the frame refusal names its condition (main's
  attribution) over the four conditions slice 4 still refuses, and main's
  stack-slot reference scan now admits a slot only as the base of a modelled
  `[slot + disp]` operand. MEASURED with a bridge built from that tree (O0,
  proofs required): the `core` census has the same 2727-root set (160
  promote against `census-r38P`, 0 newly fail), only `PanicInfo::can_unwind`
  changes (refuted -> outside the domain), and the corpus harnesses pass
  18876 and 1568 native checks with 0 failures. LIMITATIONS.md records the
  four corpus bodies and 64 `core` bodies that do not certify, with the
  exact AY output, and the compile-time cost of replaying them.
- Stale-test fix: `ws2_stack_protector_target`'s
  `aarch64-unknown-unknown` row (it builds only with `--features driver`)
  still expected the canary classifier to raise `TargetObjectUnsupported`.
  The E0.3 merge (8b1eee10d) kept that refusal a frame-lowering refusal, as
  `stack_protector_target_abi` documents and trust-cg-codegen's own tests
  pin: the canary is a frame-lowering sequence and no object writer has run.
  The row now asserts `FrameLowering(LowerError::FrameLowering)` and the
  refusal's exact text, including the target and "native object format".

- x86 machine passes no longer delete the definition of a register an
  instruction reads through operand 0. `x86_produces_value` was a blacklist,
  so opcodes appended after it answered "operand 0 is a def": `JmpR`, the eight
  `Volatile*MR` stores and `Cmpxchg8`/`Cmpxchg16`, whose operand 0 is a read.
  x86 DCE therefore deleted the `Lea` forming a volatile store's address and
  the copy of a narrow compare-exchange's desired value. Measured on trust IR
  at O2 before the fix: a volatile store to an `Alloca` stored through a
  register nothing wrote, and an `i8` `CmpXchg` run under Rosetta returned 107
  for (slot 1, expected 1, desired 5). The classifier is now an exhaustive
  `match`, and a new exhaustive per-form `x86_operand0_may_be_read` gives
  both DCE tiers one use model, which also counts the tied two-operand
  `AddRR [off, base]` of the jump-table dispatch.

- x86 copy propagation and CSE respect a tied operand 0. Copy propagation
  renamed operand 0 of `Not [v]` as if it were a pure use, so
  `v1 := v0; NOT v1; return v1` became `NOT v0` and returned the
  un-inverted value. CSE keyed the tied two-operand `AddRR [d, s]` (and
  `SubRR`, `ImulRR`, `AndRR`, `OrRR`, `XorRR`) by `s` alone, so
  `d1 += s; d2 += s` became `d2 := d1`. Both measured on hand-built ISel
  through the production pass order before the fix (the check stops at the
  first failing level): `!x` returned `x` at O1, and `(x + z) - (y + z)`
  returned 0 at O2, the first level that runs CSE. Copy propagation
  now never renames a defined operand 0, and CSE refuses any form
  `effects::x86_operand0_may_be_read` says reads its destination. x86 LICM's
  flag-arithmetic tier had the same per-opcode list and admitted a tied
  `AddRR [d, s]` as invariant in `s`; it now asks the same predicate. The
  three private opcode lists are gone.

- `effects::x86_produces_value(StackAlloc)` is `true`: `StackAlloc [dst, ..]`
  writes `dst`. x86 LICM missed that write, so when `dst` also had a def
  before the loop, a `Lea` of the per-iteration allocation was hoisted to the
  preheader (measured at O1, where the check stopped). The round-8 JIT
  transcription of the classifier is re-pinned: the slice drops the arm, and
  the re-emitted fixture differs only in the dropped `119: bb2` key.

- The x86 register allocator reads `JmpR`'s target. The pipeline's
  `opcode_has_def` ended in `_ => true` without naming `JmpR`, so
  `x86_isel_to_regalloc` put the jump-table target in `defs`, and spill
  materialization emitted no reload before the jump and a store after it.
  `opcode_has_def` now delegates to the shared exhaustive classifier, and the
  allocator's per-form tie `first_operand_is_def_and_use` is an exhaustive
  `match`; it now also ties the in-place `[d, imm]` forms of `RolRI` and the
  packed immediate shifts, which the encoder emits as `op d, imm`. Jump
  tables are opt-in (`TCG_X86_JUMP_TABLE`), and no ISel path emits those
  two-operand shift forms, so neither was reached by default.

- x86-64 System V PARTIAL eightbytes, two SILENT MISCOMPILES fixed
  (`trust-cg-lower` `x86_64_isel.rs`). (1) The lane ASSEMBLY loaded each byte /
  word piece with `MOV r8/r16, [mem]`, which leaves the register's upper bits
  stale, then shifted and ORed it over them: a `[u8; 3]` or `[u8; 7]` passed or
  returned in a register read back garbage at O0 (`black_box([11, 12, 13])` as a
  slice: 214 or 9 instead of LLVM's 148, nondeterministic). Every narrow piece is
  now zero-extended (`MOVZX`) first; 4-byte loads already clear bits 32..63. (2)
  A call RESULT's partial lane was stored with ONE `lane.ty` store — 4 bytes for
  a 3-byte lane, one byte into the adjacent stack slot. The 2026-09-21
  partial-eightbyte change wired three lane-moving sites and missed this fourth;
  it now copies the result at the lane's width and stores width-exact pieces.
  Pinned by two ISel unit tests (every result store inside the object and
  covering it exactly; every narrow argument piece extended before any shift or
  OR) and the `partial_eightbyte_blackbox` corpus row plus a strict
  every-opt-level test (LLVM 53; 51 before at O0).
- rustc bridge, CELLED locals (a SILENT MISCOMPILE fixed): an entry argument
  whose address escapes and is written through it (`*identity(&mut p) = q;
  p.b`) keeps its live value only in its scalar cell, but every deref-base read
  took `value_for_scalar_binding`'s entry-arg fallback — the INCOMING parameter
  (`stale_celled_entry_arg`: 20 instead of 40 at O0). Each statement and
  terminator now loads the celled locals it reads from their cells before it is
  lowered (`preload_celled_reads`), and `value_for_scalar_binding` answers a
  celled local only from that load, refusing
  (`[TCG-SCALAR-CELL-PROJECTION]`) rather than returning a stale binding; the two
  `&raw (*r)` arms that read `scalar_values` directly route through it. The same
  class for `Index` operands (a celled index read stale: 5 instead of 17) is
  closed by the cell-aware `index_local_value` used by all five index readers.
  Strict test `former_silent_miscompiles_are_supported_across_opt_levels`.
- rustc bridge, `[TCG-SSA-071]`: a CELLED return place (`&_0` passed to a
  reference-returning callee, `io::error::repr::Repr::new_custom`) is returned
  from its cell instead of the never-defined `ValueId(0)`; and when the loop
  back-edge VC DECLINES (never when any flagged back-edge's VC is REFUTED in the
  VC model), the body is re-lowered with the misthreaded slots' locals in memory
  cells, so the unchanged SSA gate and every other gate re-run on the new IR
  (`overflowing_pow` u64/u128, `TwoWaySearcher::maximal_suffix`). Kill switch
  `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=no-ssa071-cell-retry`; retry attempts are muted in
  `diag-json`, and the back-edge VC returns a typed verdict.
- rustc bridge, x86-64 wide numerics: `carrying_mul_add` on `u128` and every
  signed width calls the intrinsic's own fallback body (already emitted as a mono
  item) instead of refusing; and a by-value `Option<u128>` / `Option<i128>` /
  `(u128, bool)` / `(u64, u128)` ARGUMENT keeps its 128-bit INTEGER scalars on the
  two-value Pair lane (`x86_64_pair_arg_admits_i128_lanes`, beside upstream's
  Linux AArch64 admission). Cross-backend matrix (LLVM/bridge rlib x bin, O0 and
  O2, incl. seven leading `u64`s and `(u128, bool)` after five): all four cells
  equal LLVM. Returns, and a 128-bit lane beside a float or pointer, keep the
  refusal.
- rustc bridge, three more `library/core` shapes: a fn-ITEM `FnPtrShim` whose
  tupled argument is a by-value aggregate (`Option::map(Map::into_inner)`); a
  pointer to a struct with a `dyn` TAIL passed on as two FnAbi-checked `Ptr`
  lanes (`<error::Request as Debug>::fmt`; every projection walker refuses a
  dyn-tail field at a non-zero offset, so nothing is addressed at the wrong
  offset); and a bare `&agg` stored as a VALUE into a closure / ADT / tuple
  (`<wtf8::EncodeWide as Iterator>::next`: the referent is memory-backed).
- MEASURED (lowering only, `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=no-proof-certs`, so NO proof
  claim): the x86-64 Darwin `library/core` O0 census goes 13 -> 3 failed roots
  on b397eb9aa + this change, with no new reason string and no ICE. The three
  left are `atomic_load::<i128/u128>` (needs `CMPXCHG16B`) and
  `panic::Location::caller` (the `#[track_caller]` hidden-argument ABI). The
  proof-required census is unchanged: every x86-64 function still fails
  `[TCG-PROOF-465]` until x86 has a source-bound lane.
- Sequences and boxed sets lower on AArch64 (ledger `L05-P8`). The pinned
  trust-ir states a `Ty::Sequence` only as "a packed buffer (length-prefixed)"
  and gives it no layout, so trust-cg defines one image in
  `trust_cg_lower::sequence_layout` and every path reads it: a `u64` count
  then the packed elements (`Bool`, 8- to 64-bit integers, `F32`, `F64`), a
  collection value is the image pointer in one register, and a
  collection-returning function takes a trailing caller-provided result
  buffer sized from the result length it publishes (one static count, or one
  sequence parameter's count, found by a fixpoint over the call graph once per
  module). A body another object may replace (`Weak`/`LinkOnce`, preemptible
  under `pic`, or dyld-coalescable) publishes no length, so a call to it is
  refused. Run-time witnesses trap: the callee on a returned image that is not
  its published length, the caller (after the call, so it detects but cannot
  undo an overrun) on a returned header that is not the count it sized for, a
  fixed slot on a source whose header is not its static count, and every
  header read at 2^56 elements or more. `SeqMapAddK`/`SeqMapNot`/`SeqMap` lower
  as counted loops in blocks of their own (a `pending_block_split` in
  `translate_block`), fixed slots only where the length is static and the
  block is on no cycle, fresh stack images otherwise; a `SeqMap` gives each
  element a fresh cell for the rest of the frame, as trust-ir's interpreter
  does. Boxed sets move in the constructor's order. Refused by name
  (`[TCG-SEQ]`): `ExtractElement` and
  `InsertElement` over any sequence, including the constant-sourced ones the
  adapter used to lower, because trust-ir's codegen gate names them
  `UnlowerableForCodegen` (the must-refuse corpus now pins that reason on
  every compiler lane); every load, store, alloca, GEP, cast or arithmetic
  that spells a collection; nesting; `SetRepr::Bitset`; set constants two of
  whose elements store the same image (`Int(-1)` and `Int(255)` in an `I8`
  set); other element types; results without one published length or through
  an indirect, invoked, variadic, declared or replaceable callee; every non-C
  calling convention; and every non-AArch64 target. Evidence:
  `e2e_aarch64_sequences.rs` (Darwin floor, 14 tests) executes constants of
  every element type, parameters, results, calls into C, selects, loops
  (including loop-carried images kept live across an iteration), recursion
  and the SeqMap family natively at O0-O3 against the trust-ir reference
  interpreter and a C model (the fresh-cell test against the C model only: the
  interpreter cannot call its C element function), shows each run-time length
  witness trapping in a forked child, and the strict adapter replays the
  SeqMap element calls as exact bindings. On top of the construct sweep, the
  construct inventory moves `Ty::Set`, `Ty::Sequence`, the three `SeqMap`
  instructions, `Constant::Sequence` and `Constant::Set` to executed (128
  executed, 13 model-only, 15 refused). This is native execution evidence on
  one host, not a proof, and the image is trust-cg's definition, not a
  trust-ir-certified layout.
- Vector, pair and LL/SC-window spills (ledger L10-P10). The evidence is
  native differential and structural testing on the Darwin host only; the
  Linux arm has not run.
  - **LL/SC pseudos.** Spilled operands now follow a whole-window strategy.
    Uses reload into X16/X17 first. Defs, and any further operand, borrow an
    allocatable register that is not an operand of the pseudo. A register
    dead after the pseudo is borrowed as is; a live one is saved to an
    emergency slot before and restored after it. All of this traffic sits
    outside the retry loop. Before, a third spilled operand was refused
    (`[TCG-LLSC-SPILL-SCRATCH]`, now reachable only on register exhaustion).
    A BASELINE fetch-add plus compare-exchange under 28 live vectors and 24
    live scalars hit that refusal at O0; it now compiles and matches its C
    model at O0-O3. `check_exclusive_windows` runs after expansion and at
    encoding. It refuses any spill access (`[TCG-LLSC-SPILL-WINDOW]`) or other
    memory access or call (`[TCG-LLSC-WINDOW]`) between a load-exclusive and
    the next store-exclusive or `CLREX` on any path.
  - **Frame dataflow net.** It now tracks the V8-V15 upper halves across
    calls: a Q-view read after a call that did not redefine the register is
    `call-clobbered-upper-half-read`. New unit controls cover 16-byte spill
    cells (a deleted store, half-cell shifts, a width mismatch, a wrong
    register, an unwritten cell) and pin the whole-cell shift gap.
  - **Spill shapes.** The allocator never forms pair spills. The encoders
    refuse a flagged pair (`[TCG-A64-PAIR-SPILL]`) or other non-`LDR`/`STR`
    spill shape (`[TCG-A64-SPILL-SHAPE]`), which the frame net used to
    decline silently.
  - **Native controls.** `e2e_aarch64_vector_spills` (Darwin floor, 14 tests)
    covers Q spills at O0-O3 against C models: vector-only, mixed
    scalar/vector, across a call, and a dynamic frame whose far FP-relative Q
    slots are legalized through X16. A branching LL/SC program saves a
    borrowed register that only a successor block reads. In a manual
    mutation run that zeroed the successor half of the borrow liveness, its O2
    result diverged from the C model. The file's corruption controls include a
    Q value kept in V8 across a call, a fused pair and a reload moved into an
    exclusive window. A whole-slot shift passes the net and is caught by
    native execution. None of this proves register allocation, spill
    placement, the exclusive monitor or forward progress.
- x86-64 formal-argument prologue, segment-wise path: a prefix that mixes
  intake-interleaved split connectors with stack-argument loads is no longer
  refused. `fixup_formal_arg_parallel_copy` used to fail closed on exactly that
  combination, because "stack-arg loads cannot be ordered against barriers
  without per-instruction dependence analysis". That analysis now exists
  (`prove_formal_arg_prefix_admits_loads`), and the refusal is lifted only for
  the shapes it clears.

  * THE PLACEMENT RULE IS THE MINIMAL ONE. Each load is emitted at its OWN
    position among the segments and connectors: after the resolved copies of the
    segment it was scanned inside, before that segment's closing connector, in
    scan order among that segment's other loads. Relative to every connector,
    every other segment and every other load the emitted order is IDENTICAL to
    the one ISel emitted — the only instructions a load moves across are the
    intakes of its own segment that followed it, and resolving the segment as a
    parallel copy makes those simultaneous anyway. Loads are no longer sunk
    below the whole group on this path, which is what made a connector READING a
    load's destination unorderable.
  * MEMORY INDEPENDENCE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ASSUMED. The only memory the prologue
    reads is the incoming argument area (`is_formal_stack_arg_load` accepts
    `[RBP+disp]` only at `disp >= 16`, at or above the return address); the only
    memory it writes is spill slots, which `compute_x86_stack_frame_layout`
    places at NEGATIVE displacements from RBP. A new unit test measures that on
    the layout rather than asserting it in a comment, and the analysis refuses
    outright any prologue that writes RBP — the premise both halves rest on.
  * REGISTER INDEPENDENCE IS DECIDED BY A PROOF. Both orders are run over a
    syntactic term domain over the function's entry state: the scan order with
    each intake carrying its CONTRACT value (its argument register's
    function-entry contents, which is the guarantee this pass exists to
    provide), and the order about to be emitted with each segment collapsed to
    one parallel copy. They must agree on every connector's READ, every spilled
    formal's STORE, and the final contents of every register the prologue
    writes. Equal terms denote equal runtime values, so agreement is a proof;
    the converse does not hold, so disagreement is a refusal and not a claim of
    a miscompile.
  * PARTIAL WRITES ARE MODELLED, AND THE CASE IS REACHED. The committed Clean
    fixtures load their stack-passed `b1` formals with `MovRM8` (`8A /r`), which
    writes the destination's low byte and PRESERVES the rest — so its value is a
    function of the register's OLD contents, and a reordering across it is not
    the clobber it looks like. The same distinction separates
    `movss xmm, m32` / `movsd xmm, m64` (which zero the upper lanes) from
    `movss xmm1, xmm2` / `movsd xmm1, xmm2` (which merge into them); the
    classification is keyed on the opcode for that reason, and pinned per
    opcode by a unit test.
  * WHAT STAYS REFUSED, BY NAME. The reordered pairs are enumerated directly so
    a refusal names a pair and not only the register whose contents came out
    wrong. Two unit tests pin refusals: a later intake in the same segment that
    writes the load's destination, and a load that destroys an incoming
    argument a later segment's intake still has to read — the second of which
    the pre-existing cross-segment hazard check does not see, because it
    compares segment sources against segment DESTINATIONS and a load is
    neither. An opcode whose destination width the proof does not model, a
    register it cannot key, and a load into the ABI's FIXED XMM cycle-breaking
    scratch are all refusals too.
  * The GPR cycle-breaking scratch now also avoids every stack-arg load's
    destination, which is the one hazard the placement rule cannot see (the
    resolver's scratch appears in neither order).
  * WHAT IS UNCHANGED. The duplicate-free (global) resolution path is untouched,
    and the segment-wise path with no stack-arg loads emits exactly what it did
    before — the proof runs only when the prefix actually carries loads. The
    analysis is an ORDER-EQUIVALENCE proof, not a proof that the prologue ISel
    and regalloc produced is itself correct, and not a width-fidelity proof.

  * TWO ROUTES, NOT ONE. The pass reorders exactly three things on this path: a
    segment's intakes (which the parallel-copy resolution makes simultaneous), a
    stack-arg load relative to the intakes of its OWN segment that follow it, and
    the spilled-formal saves (hoisted to the top). When the last two are absent
    the emitted order IS the order ISel emitted, so there is no reordering to
    justify — only the pass's own contract, that every intake delivers its
    argument register's function-entry contents, which is discharged by requiring
    every intake's source register to be untouched by everything positioned
    before its segment (a strengthening of the previous cross-segment check,
    which compared only intake destinations and only in the GPR bank). That
    route needs no value model at all, which is what lets it admit a prefix
    whose split connectors move values the allocator SPILLED — the O1 shape,
    where the prologue reaches those ends through the spiller's reload/store
    replay. The value-level proof is the second route, for prefixes where a load
    genuinely moves; it refuses a spilled connector end by name, and says in the
    same breath why the unreordered route did not apply.

  MEASURED on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` with stock rustc 1.97.1 (the
  `rust-toolchain.toml` pin, not this machine's aterm Trust default), by
  `cargo test -p trust-cg-codegen --test clean_fixture_host_lowering`, ON THE
  MERGE of this change with `origin/main` `b2bb3e518` — whose own
  portable-checker host qualification had closed the guard-carrier canary class
  the same day and raised this floor from 4 to 15. Closing the formal-arg prefix
  gap raises it again, from **15 of 38 to 31 of 38, at O0 AND at O1**, with the
  lowered set identical across the two levels; the refusal class disappears from
  the census (after the qualification it was the LARGEST remaining class, 21-22
  fixtures at O0 and 20 at O1). A SINGLE function carried the whole gap,
  `ExprMeta__pack`, in every fixture that hit it. The whole target takes 1844s
  and its only remaining class is the per-fixture deadline (7 at O0, 7 at
  O1): a fixture that used to be refused at instruction ten of its entry block
  now compiles every function in its module, so the compile that used to take
  0.2s takes as long as the module needs. That is the refusal having masked the
  compile time, not a new slowdown; how much longer any of them needs is
  unmeasured. The floor was raised only after TWO consecutive runs of the merged
  tree agreed on the 31 names, on their being the same at both opt levels, and on
  the same seven deadline fixtures (1844s and 1843s); the second run reads the
  target GREEN, 5 passed / 0 failed.

  A prologue change is exactly the kind that breaks an ABI test, so the suites
  that exercise the formal-argument prologue were run on the merge:
  `e2e_x86_64_aggregate_abi` 18/0, `e2e_x86_64_aggregate_byval_arg` 6/0,
  `e2e_x86_64_calling_conv` 18/0, and `e2e_x86_64_callee_saved` 4 passed /
  5 failed — which is EXACTLY what `origin/main`'s own `pipeline.rs` reads on
  this host, measured in this worktree by reverting that one file and rerunning
  the target: `cc: error: unrecognized command-line option '-arch'`, and four on
  the GNU-objdump prologue spelling `push %rbp` where the test's parser reads
  `pushq %rbp`. Both are host-toolchain gaps `docs/linux-x86-64-completion.md`
  already records. `cargo test -p trust-cg-codegen --lib` reads 4307 passed /
  19 failed, the same failures `origin/main`'s own `pipeline.rs` produces on
  this host BY NAME.
- Construct sweep, ledger `L05-P2` (Darwin row D05): four Darwin floor
  targets, `e2e_aarch64_construct_sweep_{types,insts,casts,tables}` (18
  tests), execute natively at O0-O3 constructs the inventory held model-only
  or refused. They check each run against the pinned trust-ir reference
  interpreter and, where the construct has one, its C meaning. Trap rows must
  die by a trap signal where the interpreter refuses. The adapter now lowers
  `Inst::MakeAggregate` for struct, tuple, record and array values; an enum
  variant stays refused by name. It also lowers `CastOp::Transmute` as an
  equal-size reinterpretation under trust-ir's own layout evidence, in
  registers for a same-width scalar pair and through a store/load slot
  otherwise. Unequal sizes, validity-carrying leaves, source padding and a
  struct whose emitted layout differs from its declared one stay refused by
  name. The interpreter executes `Transmute` only over integer/pointer
  scalars, so its other shapes are checked against the interpreter's
  `Bitcast` or store/load twin and a C `memcpy` model. The `files` table
  executes, checked by the object's DWARF source name. The proof, sidecar and
  import tables stay model-only: the object is byte-identical without them.
  The construct inventory moves from 93 executed / 40 model-only / 23 refused
  to 121 / 14 / 21. The conformance manifest's Transmute and MakeAggregate
  rows follow. This is testing evidence on aarch64-apple-darwin, not a proof;
  both lowerings stay outside trust-ir's lowering-target subset. They are
  target-neutral, so they also compile for x86-64 and Linux AArch64 with no
  native run there. `CompileService` refuses a `MakeAggregate` module by name
  (no tMBC identity image; pinned by the insts sweep), and an array
  `MakeAggregate` whose declared length disagrees with its operands is
  refused before any per-lane allocation.
- x86-64 guard-carrier expansion canary, Linux x86-64: the portable
  certificate tier is now authorized on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, so the
  canary can CONFIRM the `DivZero` expansion here instead of refusing it. The
  canary proves that the condition code a Sentinel-S5 guard carrier expands to
  makes its `Jcc` trap on exactly the carrier's intended set — the carrier
  opcode is gone before emission, so the per-instruction certificates see only
  an individually-correct `TEST`/`CMP` and `Jcc`, and a wrong cc would certify
  instruction by instruction while silently inverting the guard. Its i8 row is
  exhaustive; the i32/i64 rows that actually ship discharge through the
  committed `guard_*_{32,64}.lratcert` certificates. On this host stock 1.97.1's
  sysroot ships no `ay` AND `verdict_db/canary_certs/manifest.v1` carried no
  x86-64 Linux `host-checker` row, so neither lane could decide and the canary
  fell closed on every function carrying a division guard.

  WHAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS AUTHORIZED, because the alternative
  reading of that refusal is a miscompile: the emitted cc is right (the
  obligation compares TEST's own `(x & x) == 0` against an independently written
  `x <u 1`, all four carriers verify exhaustively at i8 and all four complements
  are refuted there, so `E` is proven and not merely unrefuted); the wide-lane
  outcome was "no solver admitted" plus a named certificate-identity miss, never
  a counterexample; and the committed certificates already replayed on this host
  BEFORE the manifest changed — 33 of 33 `verified=true` with this host's own
  `drat-trim`, whose queries the same run bound to the current live obligations.
  The missing artifact was a reviewed `(target, checker bytes)` pair, and only
  that.

  ONE MANIFEST ROW: `host-checker-count: 3` → `4` plus
  `host-checker: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu 6bd14b38…` — the exact bytes GCC
  15.2.0 builds from the pristine vendored `drat-trim.c` (unchanged at
  `d834b649…`), reproduced in six independent build directories across four
  checkout roots and both cargo profiles. No certificate body, cert/query/
  producer row, existing host row, legacy exception or acceptance rule changed.
  `host_qualified_schema_is_strict_and_preserves_only_the_recorded_legacy_exception`
  pins the fourth row and gains two more wrong-host refusals for the new bytes
  (`wrong_host_refusals` 8 → 10); a checker built by the `cc` wrapper some
  `PATH`s put ahead of `/usr/bin` hashes differently and stays an ordinary
  fail-closed identity miss.

  NOTHING WAS WIDENED. The obligation, its condition codes, the exhaustive i8
  rows, the wide-row requirement and every fail-closed path are unchanged; the
  wide rows are now discharged by an independently replayed certificate instead
  of being unknowable. Two validator tests were STRENGTHENED rather than
  relaxed: `guard_carrier_real_widths_verify` now requires all four carriers at
  i32 and i64 (it required two), and
  `wide_validators_use_portable_certs_before_missing_solver_and_mutation_fails_closed`
  now also pins `DivZero` `E` verified from the certificate alone against an
  inert AY fixture and `DivZero` `NE` failing closed. A wrong cc still produces
  different query bytes, still misses every certificate, and still refuses.

- L03-P11 (typed catches, filters and mixed personalities on
  `aarch64-apple-darwin`): trust-ir's `Inst::LandingPad` carries catch type
  indices only, so the compiler now binds index `k` to entry `k` of the
  module's reserved `__trust_cg_eh_type_table` global (an immutable array of
  zero-addend `SymbolAddr` typeinfo symbols, documented at
  `trust_cg_lower::function::EH_TYPE_TABLE_GLOBAL`; consumed by the adapter,
  never emitted). LSDA type tables use identity slots, and every bound slot is
  a `DW_EH_PE_indirect|pcrel|sdata4` entry relocated
  `ARM64_RELOC_POINTER_TO_GOT` in `__gcc_except_tab`, the form clang emits and
  ld64 and the standalone linker bind through the GOT. Typed catches are bound
  only under `__gxx_personality_v0`, whose selector is the matched catch type
  index; a catch-all match delivers `N + 1` for the module's `N`-entry table
  in a function that catches a typed exception and `1` in one that does not,
  fixed at lowering so pads the optimizer prunes cannot move it (an earlier
  draft numbered it from the surviving pads, so O0 and O1-O3 disagreed).
  `rust_eh_personality` ignores the type table and delivers selector 0, so a
  typed catch under it (through `Producer::TRust` or a module that declares
  that routine) is refused by name at lowering and in the LSDA builder. A
  module may mix `__gxx_personality_v0` and `rust_eh_personality`: a function
  stamped `Producer::TRust` takes the Rust personality, every other function
  the module default; each compact-unwind entry binds its own routine and the
  DWARF fallback emits one zPLR CIE per personality. Refused by name: a typed
  catch without a binding, with an index the table does not bind, or under a
  personality other than `__gxx_personality_v0` (`[TCG-EH-TTYPE]`);
  exception-specification filters (no trust-ir surface; the serializer refuses
  a negative action filter, `[TCG-EH-FILTER]`); ELF typed catches and ELF
  mixed personalities; JIT typed catches (`JitUnwindTypedCatchUnsupported`,
  mapped to the bridge's unwind diagnostic) and mixed personalities
  (`JitUnwindMultiplePersonalities`); and a `module_merge` input whose typed
  catch has no type table of its own beside an input that declares one.
  `EhFunctionInfo` is unchanged; `Function::eh_type_table` and
  `ExceptionHandlingMetadata::eh_type_table` carry the binding, so the
  retained LIR identity payload is v5. New Darwin floor target
  `e2e_aarch64_eh_typed` (13 tests): typed catch, non-matching fall-through
  to the enclosing C++ handler, a typed catch with a cleanup (a non-matching
  type runs the cleanup once and resumes to that handler), selector dispatch
  including non-contiguous identity slots (`[char, int]` = indices 3 and 1),
  and catch-all after typed, including a twin whose unreachable `char` pad is
  pruned at O1-O3 but not at O0, at O0-O3 through `c++`; an object-level
  decode of every function's LSDA (action chains and slot-to-typeinfo
  bindings) at O0-O3; a Rust panic through a Rust-personality CG cleanup
  frame to `catch_unwind` plus a C++ throw into a C++-personality CG typed
  catch from one object linked by `rustc` at O0-O3, once through
  compact-unwind frames and once through runtime-sized frames whose
  `__eh_frame` FDEs sit under one zPLR CIE per personality (the object pins
  both CIEs, each FDE's CIE and self-relative addends, and the DWARF mode);
  standalone-linker GOT binds at image level; and the named refusals. The
  backend-symbol shadow check also covers a `Producer::TRust` function's
  personality (`eh_personality_override`), now with a unit test. Native
  execution and object-inspection evidence on this Apple M4 Max, not a proof
  of the tables. The target is also registered on the Linux floor, where its
  native controls are compiled out (macOS-only `cfg`), so a Linux run
  executes the object-level and refusal tests; not yet run on a Linux host.

- x86-64 proof certificates, `call_only_body`: the structural exemption from the
  non-vacuous rule is now issued as a NAMED `verified` certificate, so a
  publication can be audited for exactly which functions promoted on it. Before
  this the same bodies promoted through an anonymous opcode-shape escape
  (`x86_64_report_is_empty_body`) that issues no certificate at all, leaving no
  audit trail of any granularity. The name is gated on the CONJUNCTION of two
  independent facts: every verifier row is the trap SKIP or a by-design
  UNVERIFIED control transfer (keyed on the verifier's own reason strings, with
  at least one row the trap the certificate claims), AND the LIR source handed to
  instruction selection is a bare DIVERGING transfer (`Jump* ; Trap`, or
  `Jump* ; Call (direct, no arguments, no results) ; Trap`). A report with no
  source is refused outright. Both halves are load-bearing and each is pinned
  with the other held fixed: the source alone admits a body whose rows the
  verifier FAILED or verified degenerately; the dispositions alone admit
  `call f; ret`, `call f; call g; ud2`, and a call whose arguments happened to
  need no reconstructed `MOV`. `trust-cg --emit-proofs` writes the exemption as
  an `eval-only` per-rule `.cert` and the lowering-sidecar builder skips it by
  name (it has no `ProofDatabase` obligation); the certificate carries its
  function's name, so the returned bundle names every function that promoted on
  it. `X86FunctionVerifier::{trap_skip_reason, no_proof_mapping_reason}` are
  public so the certificate keys on the verifier's exact reason strings and the
  one construction site spells the string once.

  THE NAME BUYS NO PROMOTION, and the promotion set is what it was before the
  category existed. Which bodies are exempt is still decided by
  `x86_64_report_is_empty_body` and by nothing else; the conjunction is consulted
  only for bodies that rule already exempts. Neither rule contains the other, so
  the order is what makes this hold: the conjunction admits `Jump* ; Trap` (rows
  `[Jmp, Ud2]`, the O0 two-block `-> !` body), which the opcode allowlist does
  not enumerate, and consulting it first would have replaced that class's
  `non_vacuous_function_evidence` refusal with a `verified` certificate and
  published it. That class therefore keeps its refusal and gets no name, because
  a refused function promotes nothing to audit. The certificate is also excluded
  from every gate that asks whether any obligation was discharged
  (`proof_evidence::certificate_is_discharge_evidence`): the verifying JIT's
  per-function verdict (`x86_certificates_show_verified_semantics`, and so
  `every_function_semantics_verified`), the JIT's module-level gate
  (`gate_jit_proofs_promotable`), and the rustc bridge's independent
  non-empty-bundle re-check. A trap-only or `call f; ud2` body therefore still
  has no verified semantics and the verifying JIT still refuses to publish it,
  exactly as when it carried no certificate at all. Both directions of the
  divergence, the surviving refusal in the named-only direction, and the
  exclusion from each gate are asserted by test rather than argued in a comment.

  MEASURED, so the claim is auditability and not root count: the `library/core`
  census at O0 with `-Cpanic=abort` against a bridge built from this change's
  original base (origin/main 43affd4a9, `trustc 3a3e781fe`, Linux x86-64,
  2026-09-24) reports 87 failed roots over 19 distinct reasons and 3345 emitted
  objects, with ZERO roots under `[TCG-PROOF-465]` — the 46 roots that class held
  on 2026-09-21 were already exempt, and they were exempt anonymously.
  LIMITATIONS.md documents the non-vacuous rule, the exemption decision, the
  audit name and what the name does not buy; it mentioned none of it before.
- x86-64 proof promotion, XD-01: a reconstructed obligation may earn `Formal`
  ONLY through an exact source/operand binding
  (`trust_cg_verify::x86_source_operand_binding`, fed by the two ISel
  chokepoints that resolve SSA values) — the witness's field is private to that
  module, so `discharge_reconstructed_obligation_with_exact_source_binding` is
  unreachable without passing a check. On the current tree that `Formal` is
  unreachable for a different reason as well, stated with the numbers below: the
  E0.2/E0.5 withdrawal removed the lane it discharged through, so what the
  binding contributes here is refutation and refusal, not credit.
  Eight schemas bind on the Linux x86-64 floor today:
  integer/bitwise binary ALU register forms, scalar FP binary, scalar
  loads/stores at a disp-0 bound address, `StructGep`/`ArrayGep` field and
  element addresses whose displacement and scale are re-derived from the
  declared aggregate type, and the two ABI ends of the function — the entry
  formal-argument moves and the return moves, each with its register re-derived
  from the DECLARED signature and calling convention. Every family checks the
  REPLAYED source opcode by equality before consulting the emission, so an
  `Iadd` lowered to `SUB` refutes instead of self-attesting, and a machine `MOV`
  that replaced its source instruction's computation earns nothing (pinned end
  to end through the real selector and the real verifier).
  REFUSED ON PURPOSE, each because the check that would matter is not available:
  a copy with one end in an ABI location where that end cannot be re-derived —
  an outgoing call argument or a call result, whose registers follow the
  CALLEE's declared types; the folded-immediate ALU forms, whose only available
  comparand is the immediate selection itself recorded; a folded effective
  address; an ISel-allocated scratch-slot `Lea`; and `i128`/aggregate/sret
  returns. MEASURED on this host, `fp-binary` (112 bound rows) and
  `scalar-load-at-bound-address` (74) bind and are then declined by AY
  (`incomplete self-check-rejected` / `proof-trusted`), so they stay on the
  sampling tier; three implemented schemas (`result-defining-copy`, `unary-alu`,
  `extend`) bind zero rows on the eight floor targets and have no observed
  solver answer at all. Those per-class counts were measured on base
  `bae05a7c2` and are the record for that revision
  (`reports/perf/2026-09-24-linux-x86-64-xd01/`), where the Linux x86-64 floor
  read 65 -> 72 of 117. They cannot be restated for this tree: the withdrawal
  also deleted the `TCG_TRACE_STATISTICAL` diagnostic that produced them.
  RE-MEASURED ON CURRENT UPSTREAM, the promotion effect is ZERO, and that is the
  number that applies here
  (`reports/perf/2026-09-27-linux-x86-64-xd01-on-current-upstream/`). The
  withdrawal deleted `lowering_proof::try_formal_on_miss`, the tier-0 MISS arm
  of `discharge_registry_obligation` that ran one live checked solve; that arm
  was where a bound reconstruction's `Formal` came from, because a freshly
  reconstructed obligation has neither a committed portable DRAT certificate nor
  a tier-0 row, so the two lanes that survive both miss. The binding therefore
  still CHECKS — a wrong source opcode, swapped operands, a wrong width or a
  wrong result register refutes instead of self-attesting, and
  `reconstruction_x86` is 142/0 on this tree and on upstream alike — but nothing
  it binds is credited, no certificate names a schema, and the eight floor
  targets read 70 of 117 against upstream's 69, the single difference being a
  stale-assertion repair in `jit_validation_modes_x86_64` rather than any
  binding credit. Upstream kept a live checked lane for obligations that ARE
  source-bound (`verdict_db::live_frame_discharge_with_request`,
  `live_bound_alu_discharge_with_request`, both gated on the admitted AY's
  binary identity), but it takes a `SourceBoundFrame`/`SourceBoundAlu` that
  only the AArch64 verifier constructs; giving the x86-64 bound reconstruction
  an equivalent lane is identified and deliberately not done here. This is a
  per-instruction evidence-strength mechanism with no current promotion effect,
  not a claim that trust-cg was compiled by a verifying compiler.
- Floor machinery, X13: the decided-absent row and the bridge lane were carried
  onto `origin/main`'s rewritten shared runner and RE-MEASURED there against a
  floor run of `origin/main` itself on the same host. This branch reads 47 of 67
  required targets; `origin/main` `9dd72f594` reads 46 of 66; the two runs differ
  in exactly two rows and match on every other row's verdict AND pass/fail
  counts, so nothing upstream requires is regressed. The two are
  `e2e_x86_64_calling_conv` (upstream 17/2 FAIL, here 18/0 PASS: the (E4) split
  and the `host_sym` symbol spelling fix both of upstream's failures on a
  GCC-and-GNU-ld host) and the added bridge row, which PASSED on 2026-09-24 and
  now FAILS on XD-01 — the vectorizer tiers all still fire and the compile is
  then refused by `[TCG-PROOF-465]` proof promotion for statistically-sampled
  opcodes, the same class as nine of upstream's own required rows, since
  `ProofPromotionEnvironment` was removed. It is left as a RED REQUIRED row:
  `TARGETS` stays all-required and `DECIDED_ABSENT` is for an owner decision with
  an id, not something a lane may mint for itself. What the row would need is
  MEASURED rather than argued: with a cache root only this user can write (so AY
  materializes and the guard-carrier canary stops failing) and the
  `no-proof-certs` backend knob that dozens of the bridge's own
  native-diagnostic tests already carry, the same target reads exactly its pinned
  2 of 2. Neither half is in what this branch ships — the first mutates a cache
  shared with every other lane on the machine, and the second reduces what a
  proof-oriented gate exercises, which is the owner's call. Both records, with
  every per-target log and that probe, are in
  `reports/perf/2026-09-27-linux-x86-64-floor-onto-upstream/`.
- Floor machinery, X13: carrying that lane onto upstream's runner added three
  fail-closed rules its new checks did not reach. Upstream now audits the Cargo
  configuration before any build tool runs; a bridge target runs ANOTHER build
  tool in ANOTHER workspace, so the bridge workspace's configuration is audited
  too — from `crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg` under the bridge build tool's own
  variable prefixes (`targo` reads `TARGO_*` as well as `CARGO_*`), before the
  pinned package is probed and again at the end, with both records in
  `report.json` (`bridge_cargo_config`, `final_bridge_cargo_config`). A bridge
  target also runs with `TCG_EXTERNAL_CLEAN_CHECKER` and `TCG_CLEAN_CHECKER`
  removed, exactly as upstream's Trust development lane strips them from its
  compiler: `trustc` refuses the whole `TCG_*`/`TRUST_CG_*` family as untracked
  compiler controls, so an ambient one would fail the build rather than change
  the reading. And a bridge row that declared a `TARGET_ENVIRONMENT` entry is
  REFUSED rather than run without it, because neither of upstream's two delivery
  routes (the Cargo process, or a Cargo target runner) exists for that lane; no
  bridge row declares one, and the gate test pins the refusal. The per-target
  command now composes with upstream's `target_build_command`, so a
  root-workspace row still picks up the `--trust-unverified` lane's
  `--config target.<host>.runner=...`; `environment_overrides` is gone in favour
  of upstream's `set_environment`; and each target record carries its `cwd`,

- The TrustIR pin moved `794227ad` -> `dcc5b9a3` without the two records
  that bind to it, so two gates went red on `main`:
  `trust_ir_construct_inventory::pinned_trust_ir_revision_matches_cargo_lock`
  and `fsym_ub_map::the_map_is_derived_from_the_pinned_trust_ir`. Both
