- Named refusal for a body-less function whose linkage names a definition
  (`internal`, `private`, `weak`, `linkonce` and their ODR forms).
  `Compiler::compile`, the JIT and the other translation routes failed on an
  unnamed `unknown block reference: BlockId(0)` (222 of 690 probed route
  results). Module merge bound such a stub to another input's definition and
  compiled the result; given two declarations of one name it kept the first,
  so the merged verdict depended on input order. The adapter's v41 surface
  gate now refuses it as `[TCG-DECLARATION-LINKAGE]`, and module merge refuses
  it first in either order. Both read one predicate
  (`function_declaration_linkage_is_admitted`), as does the adapter's import
  classification, which had its own copy of the rule. Like every surface
  refusal, the gate covers every function of the module. The public
  single-function (`translate_function*`, `wasm::lower_function`) and wasm
  island entries therefore also refuse a module carrying such a stub that they
  would not translate; the wasm island had bound it to a host import. A
  before/after differential over 375 in-repo trust-ir inputs on three targets
  (1,125 CLI runs) and the pinned must-refuse corpus (231 runs) changed no
  verdict, stderr or object. The L02-P6 visibility table asserts the code for
  its 45 such cases. An initializer-less `weak`/`linkonce` (or ODR) global
  keeps its tested meaning, a strong reference to a symbol whose definition
  elsewhere carries that linkage (`v41_global_linkage`); null-on-missing is
  `external_weak`.
- Performance lane, Linux AArch64 readiness (ledger L14-P3, L14-P11, L13-P12;
  no row recorded). The harness, its contract and the landing gates can now
  produce and judge a current-source Linux row. The row itself still has to be
  measured on a quiet machine. An adversarial review and three rounds of
  independent verification refuted parts of earlier versions; the fixes below
  include their repairs.
  - **Size and RSS predicates.** `benchmarks/beat-llvm/contract/gates.json`
    version 2 adds S1/S2 (linked-file size geomean at most 1.10x and 1.00x LLVM
    `-O3`, the July roadmap's parity-all and strictly-better thresholds applied
    to linked bytes). These are not preregistered in the strict sense: all 29
    committed ledger rows already record a size geomean. It preregisters R1 and
    R2 for `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, where no row had RSS. R1 fails when a
    matching program's bridge peak-RSS reading exceeds both LLVM's reading and
    the sampler floor by more than 5%. It passes only when every program's
    comparison is resolved (both readings above twice the floor) and is
    otherwise unmeasured. R2 requires a compiler peak-RSS geomean of at most
    1.00x LLVM `-O2` with no floor-bound reading. No existing gate predicate or
    threshold changed. The sampler reports the larger of its own resident set,
    which Linux carries across `exec` (about 13.7 MB here), and the program's
    peak. Most corpus programs peak below that, so R1 reads unmeasured on this
    host and the program-RSS geomean is reported, not gated.
    `metrics-contract.md` and `LIMITATIONS.md` describe this.
    `benchmarks/compile-apples/tools/harness_row.sh` now shows "fail" and
    "unmeasured" verdicts too.
  - **Exact, recomputed, fail-closed aggregates.** Gates were compared on
    values rounded to 3 decimals, so a size geomean of 1.0000187 passed S2's
    "at most 1.00". Every aggregate is now stamped exact, and rounding is for
    display only. This covers runtime and compile ratios, worst cases,
    coverage, size and RSS. Every aggregate is null unless every covered MATCH
    row has its value, and the missing rows are named. Before, `geomean`
    silently skipped a missing value. The aggregation lives once in
    `check_gates.py`: runtime and compile ratios come from each lane's raw
    samples. The checker and the ledger ratchet recompute it from the
    per-program table and reject a stamp that disagrees by more than a
    relative 1e-12 (the allowance for another platform's libm). A predicate whose
    input is null prints and records "unmeasured", never "fail". A run with a
    missing reading or sample, or an uncalibrated sampler, is not evidence.
    That includes a present but unusable `/usr/bin/time` cross-check. Each RSS
    sample is retained with the sampler's status.
  - **Ratchet.** `scripts/check_perf_ratchet.py` regression-checks every
    like-with-like row, evidence or not. Ineligibility used to skip the
    comparison, so a 1.5x runtime regression on a row with an unusable proof
    checker exited 0 and landing reported it green. A measured regression on
    a full-corpus row at the contract N is now red whatever the row's status.
    Baselines must match the row's host, target and program set. A `--progs`
    subset, another corpus or fewer samples than the contract N is
    inconclusive (exit 2), not a false red from comparing one program or one
    sample with the 18-program baseline. Such a row is never evidence and so
    never a baseline: a quiet single-program run used to count as evidence and
    could have become the best baseline. Under `--require-current`, a file not
    measured at HEAD is not current (exit 3) before any regression verdict.
    Coverage is compared as recomputed from the counts, so an identical 16/18
    no longer reads as a drop against a rounded legacy stamp. Peak-RSS
    baselines come only from rows of gates version 2 or later, so the version-1
    Darwin row measured with `/usr/bin/time -l` is no longer one.

    A change of corpus no longer disables the ratchet. Legacy baselines were
    matched by program count, so adding a 19th program to
    `progs/manifest.json` made every committed baseline a different set: a
    1.5x or 3x regression printed "SKIPPED" and exited 0, and `--append` would
    have recorded it as the new set's first baseline.
    - Rows now keep per-program ratios, and a changed program set is compared
      on the programs it shares with baselines that kept them. A regression
      there is red.
    - The rest is inconclusive and not appended until `--append --new-lineage
      '<reason>'` records an explicit new lineage. The row keeps the reason,
      the sets it replaces and whether shared programs could be compared, and
      `LEDGER.md` shows it. Only an eligible evidence row can declare a
      lineage, and only an evidence row of the new set settles it. A loaded
      row once declared one, after which an eligible 3x regression passed and
      became the set's first baseline.
    - A results JSON with duplicate keys, which `json.load` would silently
      resolve to the last entry, is refused.
    - Only a host/target with no evidence row at all is still skipped (the
      pre-existing behaviour).
    - Stray whitespace in a host or target no longer reads as a new machine.
    - Gates and condensed rows read the aggregates recomputed from the table,
      so a stamp within the tolerance cannot flip a threshold.

    The ratchet also fails on:
    - a linked-size regression over 5%;
    - a program or compiler peak-RSS regression over 10%;
    - a resolved program-RSS loss on a program the best baseline did not lose
      on;
    - a metric the baseline measured but the new row lacks. With the
      comparison no longer skipped, this now fires on the real harness path.

    It rejects proof opt-outs spelled as backend knobs (a space-separated
    list, as trustc reads it), as it rejects them as environment variables. A
    results JSON from before this version is missing current evidence (exit
    3), unless it records a MISMATCH, which stays P0 (exit 1).
    `--check-render` reports, without writing, that the committed
    `benchmarks/LEDGER.md` view is stale against the renderer. The next
    `--append` rewrites it.
  - **Linux and the Trust driver.** Both lanes' target defaults to the
    resolved compiler's host triple. The backend is the newest built
    `librustc_codegen_trust_cg` with the host's suffix (`.so` on Linux), from
    the new `scripts/bridge_backend.py`. It also owns the freshness rule for
    `run.py`, `compile_gate.py`, `scale_gate.py` and the shell gates. The rule
    now matches path components and covers every build input, not only `.rs`
    files: manifests, the bridge's `Cargo.lock` (the trust-ir pin) and
    toolchain pin, embedded data such as `verdict_db/tier0.vdb`, files named
    by `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`, the root `Cargo.toml` and
    `.cargo/config.toml`. Its old substring test skipped every
    `src/target*.rs` file and any checkout under a `/tests/` or `/target…`
    path.
    - `--cold` failed every compile, because trustc refuses `TCG_*`
      environment variables. It now gives each compile a fresh, empty, private
      `XDG_CACHE_HOME`: true cold, with population cost timed.
    - `--bridge-cg-arg` passes tracked backend knobs for diagnostic lanes,
      which are never evidence. Provenance is self-reported, including that
      knob list.
    - Provenance stamps each independent proof checker (Clean) candidate the
      backend considers, in its order, with its digest and whether
      `clean --version` ran. A run is ineligible when no candidate runs (a
      text file with the execute bit is not a checker) or when a bridge
      compile printed `verification is DEGRADED`. The probe proves only
      execution: any program that answers `--version` passes it, which
      `LIMITATIONS.md` states.
    - Fail-closed rows keep their cause codes, such as `[TCG-PROOF-465]`.
    - The warm cache record counts the certificate store before and after the
      run; the legacy verdict directory is always empty.
  - **Canary and sentinel.** `compile_time_canary.sh` and
    `compile_determinism_sentinel.sh` take the host target, the host-suffixed
    backend (refusing a missing or stale one) and `--target`/`--dylib`. They
    read load, CPU count and digests through Python instead of Darwin's
    `sysctl` and `shasum`.
    - A degraded proof checker is a configuration error. For the canary this
      is decided after the wrong-code check: an exit-code MISMATCH stays P0 in
      any checker state.
    - The canary also counts the certificate store.
    - The sentinel's cold attempts use fresh `XDG_CACHE_HOME` roots. Its
      `TCG_PROOF_CACHE_DIR` was refused by trustc, so every attempt failed.
    - On this host both scripts now run to a verdict. At `159f53415` that
      verdict is red: the production (certificates-on) bridge refuses every
      corpus program and both pinned programs with `[TCG-PROOF-465]` (ledger
      L07-P2).
- AY under umask 0002 (2026-09-26). Every trust-cg cache created its
  directories with `std::fs::create_dir_all`, so under umask `0002` (Ubuntu's
  default for a user with a user-private group) `<cache>/trust-cg` became
  `0775`. The AY private copy refuses any ancestor that group or others may
  write, so no AY ran in any process on such a host, and proof-required
  compiles were refused as if the evidence were a proof gap. On the Linux
  floor host `~/.cache/trust-cg` was `0775`, `ay-exec` was empty and
  `jit_fail_closed_proof_policy` passed 2 of 7.
  - **One creation rule.** `trust_cg_process_env::private_fs` creates each
    missing directory with mode exactly `0700` whatever the umask (a umask
    that clears owner bits, and a set-group-ID bit inherited from the parent,
    are corrected on the new directory by name, never through a symlink) and
    never changes one that exists. The AY private copy, the Alethe
    certificate store, the solver-identity memo, the JIT IR disk cache and
    the executable buffer cache use it; `trust-cg-opt`'s
    `create_private_dir_all`/`create_private_file` (the CEGIS cache) are now
    re-exports of it. The ancestor rule is unchanged: an existing
    group-writable directory is still refused.
  - **Diagnosable.** The ancestor refusal names the directory, its mode and
    the remedy (`chmod go-w <dir>`, or an `XDG_CACHE_HOME` only this user can
    write). When the build records an AY but none is admitted in the
    process, a proof-promotion refusal for unverified evidence ends with that
    `TCG-AY-IDENTITY-*` refusal (`ay_bridge::with_solver_refusal_note`). A
    build that records no AY (every stock-Rust build, the Darwin floor
    included) keeps its refusal text byte for byte, and exact-text checks
    compare `without_solver_refusal_note`, which removes exactly that note.
    What is accepted is unchanged.
  - **Floor.** `scripts/check_linux_aarch64.py --require-proof-tools` builds
    the CLI with the floor's build command and, before any target, requires
    `trust-cg --print-ay-identity` to admit exactly the resolved AY under the
    effective cache root (`report.json` `ay_admission`, through the AOT
    runner's `ay_admission`). A resolved AY that cannot run now fails the run
    with the rule's own refusal instead of every proof-replay target.
  - **Measured** (Trust `ae9c2c1d` development build, umask `0002`, a fresh
    `0700` `XDG_CACHE_HOME`): `ay-exec/<sha256>/ay` is materialized (`0500`,
    the toolchain `bin/ay`'s digest) and every created directory is `0700`.
    `jit_fail_closed_proof_policy` passes 6 of 8, including the new
    group-writable-cache refusal row. The two failures are existing gaps:
    `MOVXrr` has only a registry-name theorem, and the always-verify ADD has
    no proof-grade certificate. The pre-fix binary under the same setup left
    `trust-cg` at `0775` with no copy and passed 2 of 7. The Darwin floor
    minimum for the target is 9 (8), sum 1,758 (1,757).
  - **Tests.** The verify crate's unit-test exec root is created `0700`.
    Under umask `0002` tempfile made it `0775`, which refused every AY the
    unit tests admit. With AY now materializing there, a root per test
    process would have kept a 626 MB copy of the toolchain AY per process
    (104 processes, 65 GB, measured). The AY the build records is therefore
    copied once per user into `<temp dir>/trust-cg-verify-ay-exec-uid<uid>`
    and reused by every test process, as production reuses
    `<cache>/trust-cg/ay-exec/<sha256>`. Fixture executables keep a root per
    process, which is removed when the process exits, also after a failing
    test; so is the inert fixture's directory.
  - **Interrupted copies.** A writer now holds an exclusive lock on its
    `.ay-copy-*` temporary until it publishes or exits. Materialization
    (production and tests) removes a temporary in its `<sha256>` directory
    only when it is a regular file this user owns (opened without following
    a symlink), older than 300 s and with no lock held, so a writer killed
    mid-copy no longer leaves up to 655 MB behind. A live writer's
    temporary, a young one and the published `ay` are kept. Measured with
    the CLI: a SIGKILL mid-copy left a 52 MB `.ay-copy-*`; the next run kept
    it while young, and removed it once it was older than 300 s. With stock Rust (no AY recorded), `cargo test -p
    trust-cg-verify --lib` fails 60 tests on origin/main (the AY identity,
    private-copy and bridge fixture tests) and 10 here, all 10 also failing
    on main. With the Trust `ae9c2c1d` toolchain the change instead makes
    AY run where 61 solver-coupled tests used to pass by skipping ("no
    admitted ay solver"). Those tests fail exactly as on origin/main with AY
    admitted (umask `0022`): 43 non-batch and 19 `test_ay_batch_verify_*`
    tests fail on both, and `test_ay_batch_verify_all_categories_comprehensive`
    exceeds a 600 s bound on both. None is new; on this host they were
    hidden. 38 are AY's own strict-certification refusals
    (`(incomplete self-check-rejected)`; for `Sdiv_I32 -> SDIVWrr` AY
    reports "strict UNSAT proof validation failed: step t0 uses unsupported
    hole rule", and AY 0.26.0 build 9799, 0.27.0 tree `ba60326b` and 0.27.0
    build 10454 all answer the same). 3 are `(incomplete proof-trusted)`, 3
    are Clean rejections of AY's Alethe proof, 15 are GPU-synthesis checks
    whose verdict is not certified, 1 is a 30 s solver timeout, and 2 fail in
    every configuration (the cell-pipeline query-size pin and the x86 teeth
    audit).
  - **Refusal text.** A build that records no AY (the Darwin floor's stock
    lane) keeps every proof-promotion refusal byte for byte, so
    `darwin_frameless_leaves_never_publish_on_sampled_or_vacuous_evidence`
    (run on Linux with its macOS gate lifted) passes again; it had failed at
    the first version of this change, which appended the note to every
    refusal of a build without AY.
  - **Mode fix failures.** A directory the helper created but could not make
    `0700` (for example `fchmodat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` returning ENOTSUP on
    glibc before 2.32) is an error and is removed; only a directory that
    existed before the call is accepted as it is.


- AArch64 ELF, L02-P6 fifth closure-audit coverage (audit at `159f53415`;
  tests and floor configuration only, no emitted byte changes). The audit's
  coverage skeptic kept the row partial. Mutant S21 (`merge_modules` giving
  the merged visibility only to a function with a body) passed every test.
  Six more passed every floor target and were killed only by lib tests:
  S01 and S02 (the importer's global-address stub and a function-body
  `SymbolAddr` of data reading a default-visibility preemption check instead
  of the shared address predicate) and S06, S06a, S06b and S07 (the merge's
  handling of identical imports and identical definitions).
  - **Merges with no definition or identical ones.**
    `merged_declarations_and_identical_definitions_take_the_most_constraining_visibility`
    merges two inputs that only declare a function and import a word, and
    that define four read-only words (`linkonce_odr`, `weak`, `linkonce`,
    `weak_odr`) byte for byte, for every ordered pair of visibilities. The
    merged object must spell the most constraining visibility on each symbol
    under `static`, `pie` and `pic` at O0-O3. The declarations must be
    GOT-addressed, and the definitions GOT-addressed exactly when they are
    default under `pic`. The row also pins that an `external_weak` or
    `available_externally` input is refused by name. Its native twin links
    the (default, default) pair and the six ordered pairs of distinct
    visibilities, merged and compiled separately, into a `pic` shared
    library beside a C definition, with GNU ld, gold and LLD at O0-O3.
    Hidden names stay out of `.dynsym`, protected ones are `PROTECTED`, and
    an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer moves only the (default, default) reads.
  - **Data address forms.** `data_symbol_and_stub_addresses_read_the_shared_predicate`
    checks `GlobalAddr`, a function-body `SymbolAddr` and the global-address
    stub (offsets 0 and 8) of strong, read-only, `weak` and `linkonce_odr`
    words of each visibility. Each form must be the GOT pair exactly when
    the word is default under `pic`, and a PC-relative page otherwise. Its
    native twin links every form into one `pic` library with the three
    linkers at O0-O3. No dynamic relocation or GOT slot may name a hidden or
    protected word, each default word needs a `GLOB_DAT` slot, every form's
    address must equal the `GlobalAddr` one, and only the default words may
    interpose. Both native rows report every failed check of a level
    together, tagged by the check.
  - **Mutants, replayed.** The audit's seven mutants (the same edits) and
    seven new ones at neighbouring sites were applied one at a time to
    `063b6c49a`'s sources with these rows (`17df3d66d`). The seven floor
    targets `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding`, `e2e_aarch64_elf_relocation_model`,
    `v41_abi_residue_objects`, `e2e_aarch64_globals_linux`,
    `e2e_aarch64_elf_sections`, `e2e_aarch64_elf_link` and
    `e2e_aarch64_elf_tlsie` were run with `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD=1
    TCG_REQUIRE_GOLD=1` (unmutated: 81/21/18/15/26/11/13, no `SKIP` line).
    All 14 are killed. Each of the audit's seven is killed only by the two
    new rows of its class.
    - S21, S06, S06a and S06b: where the second input is more
      constraining, the merged object spells the first input's visibility,
      the merged library exports the name with it, and `LD_PRELOAD` takes

    - S01 and S02: under `pic` the object names each hidden and protected

      print the expected values, since the slots hold the library's own

    - New: N1 (the first input's global visibility dropped), N2 (a bodyless

      stub and a data `SymbolAddr` reading the import-only rule) and N6

      `pic` by the emitters' backstop in both address-form rows; N5 also
      fails a row of `e2e_aarch64_globals_linux`. N7 (a data `SymbolAddr`
      with an addend always through the GOT) is killed by both address-form
      rows and a JIT row of `e2e_aarch64_globals_linux`.
    - The row `native::data_symbol_and_stub_addresses_bind_like_global_addr_in_a_shared_object`
      lists each mutant's edit, so the run can be replayed.
  - **Floor.** The Linux floor pins `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` at 81 (77).
    It now runs `e2e_aarch64_elf_relocation_model` with `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD=1`.
    Before, its three LLD link legs could pass by printing `SKIP`; gate 36's
    `run-i50` records an empty environment for that target. The Darwin
    floor's host-neutral minimum is 48 (46), with a table sum of 1,759
    (1,757).
  - **Documentation.** `LIMITATIONS.md` said each of the visibility table's
    574 refused cases is compiled and its diagnostic asserted. For the 45
    bodyless functions with a definition linkage the row asserts trust-ir's

    the table rows had run only in the fourth repair's own runs; gate 36's
    `run-i50` ran them 77/77.
- Product fix (L02-P13): the LLVM IR importer (`trust_cg_llvm_import`) now
  carries the symbol facts an LLVM function or global states instead of
  defaulting them. Before, every function, defined or declared, imported as
  `External` with default visibility (`internal` and `private` as
  `Internal`), so a hidden function compiled `pic` was exported and
  interposable, a `linkonce_odr`/`weak_odr` pair in two objects failed with
  "multiple definition", an `available_externally` body became a strong
  definition and an `extern_weak` declaration a strong reference.
  - **Functions.** Every LLVM function linkage maps onto its trust-ir linkage
    (`external`, `internal`, `private`, `weak`, `weak_odr`, `linkonce`,
    `linkonce_odr`, `available_externally`, `extern_weak`), and
    default/hidden/protected visibility is carried on definitions and
    declarations, including a `declare` that follows the call that first
    named the function (clang's order). A linkage LLVM forbids in the
    position (`common`/`appending`, an `extern_weak` definition, a weak or
    link-once declaration), visibility on a local symbol, two headers that
    disagree about one function, and a skipped declaration that states a
    non-default fact are refused by name. A function's `section` is carried
    (it was dropped). A direct call of an `extern_weak` function is imported
    as a `CallIndirect` through its `SymbolAddr`, the one call trust-ir
    admits for a weak declaration. That lowering is not the direct call's on
    this
    base, so two shapes are refused by name instead: a 128-bit integer
    argument that the AArch64 conventions may pass on the stack (AArch64
    indirect calls store only its low half, L06-P15; with the rewrite,
    `(i64 x 7, i128)`, `(i128 x 5)`, `(i64, i128, i64, i128, i64, i128)`
    and `(i64 x 7, i128, i64)` returned wrong values through the weak call
    at O0-O3), and a variadic callee (no indirect variadic call is lowered).
    The base compiled both shapes, as a strong reference to the weak
    function. The refusal uses an upper bound on the general-purpose
    registers the earlier arguments take (one per pointer or `i1`-`i64`,
    none per `half`/`float`/`double`, an even-aligned pair per 128-bit
    integer). A parser test checks it against the backend's own AArch64
    argument classification, with each type read by the importer's
    `parse_ty` and translated by the backend's `translate_type`: every
    signature of up to six arguments over the ten scalar types the importer
    admits in a signature (1,111,111), and, for each of `ptr`, `i1`, `i8`,
    `i16`, `i32`, `half` and `float`, every signature of up to nine
    arguments over it, `i64`, `i128` and `double` (7 x 349,525). It covers
    both variants and equals the AAPCS64 placement. The check runs at
    import, before a target is chosen, so it applies to every target.
  - **Globals.** Linkage is read from the prefix before `global`/`constant`
    only. Before, the whole line was searched, so an exported string such as
    `c"internal\00"` became local. `weak`, `weak_odr`, `linkonce`,
    `linkonce_odr`, `available_externally` and `extern_weak` are carried
    (they imported as `External`). `common` (a tentative definition, which
    imported as a strong definition), `appending` (other than the
    `@llvm.used` arrays), `thread_local` (which imported as an ordinary
    shared global), `externally_initialized`, `dllimport`/`dllexport`,
    `partition`, an unknown prefix token and an
    initializer that contradicts the linkage are refused by name. The storage
    keyword is the first `global`/`constant`, not one spelled inside a
    string.
  - **Address spaces.** Every address space other than the default one is
    refused by name, at one check that runs before any line is read,
    wherever the module spells it: on a global, on a function (its
    `addrspace(N)` clause), on a call (`call addrspace(1) ...`) and in any
    type (a parameter, argument or return type, a loaded, stored or GEP
    pointer type, a constant such as `ptr addrspace(257) null`, a cast
    target). It covers glued, spaced and tab-separated clauses and every
    operand other than one or more `0` digits (`01` is address space 1;
    negative, out-of-range and symbolic `"P"` spaces are refused too). It
    follows LLVM's lexer, which ends an integer type `iN`, a numbered ID
    (`%0`, `@0`, `#0`, `!0`) and an integer literal at the first non-digit:
    `i8addrspace(270)*` and `%0addrspace(270)*` are clauses, while
    `%v1addrspace` and `@x1addrspace` are names. The round-4 verifier found
    the glued forms admitted by the previous check, which took the digit for
    a name byte. The importer then read `i8addrspace(270)*` as a 64-bit
    pointer: `ptrtoint` of `0x100000005` gave `0x100000005` where llc gives
    `0x5`, and a null test of `0x100000000` gave 0 where llc gives 1 (O0 and
    O2, AArch64 Linux). A parameter, call argument, stack-passed null,
    return type and global of that type were admitted the same way. The
    check also ends a comment at a carriage return, as LLVM's lexer does, so
    a clause after `; ...\r` is refused (the rest of the importer still
    drops the whole tail).
    Before, the clause was dropped wherever the importer read the position
    (a global, a function, a declaration's return type, a parameter, a call
    argument, a call), and the pointer was imported as an ordinary 64-bit
    one. LLVM's AArch64 data layouts make `addrspace(270)` a 32-bit pointer
    (`p270:32:32`), yet a stack argument of that type was placed like a
    64-bit pointer on `aarch64-apple-darwin` (the `i32` after it went to
    `[sp, #8]`, not `[sp, #4]`). `addrspace(0)` is admitted in every
    spelling (`addrspace ( 0 )`, `addrspace(00)`), and objects that spell
    it are byte-identical to the base's. The global and function-header
    readers only step over the default clause; a bare `addrspace` word
    where a global qualifier belongs is still an unknown qualifier. A
    parser test covers each position and spelling above, and names,
    strings, comments and `addrspacecast`, which are not clauses. It kills
    each of 12 round-3 mutants of the check and the global reader, among them
    admitting any operand that begins with `0`, ignoring the check's
    result, ignoring quotes, name bytes or sigils, requiring the `(` right
    after the word, skipping an unclosed clause and stepping over a spaced
    or glued clause wrongly. With the round-3 verifier's 67 address-space
    modules compiled for both AArch64 targets (134 runs), every non-default
    spelling is refused by name, and the 20 runs that spell only the default
    space or none give objects byte-identical to the base's. The same test
    now also covers the glued forms (an `iN` pointer as a parameter, call
    argument, return type and global type, `%0`, `@0`, `#0`, `!0`, an
    integer literal, a line that starts with the word or with `i8addrspace`),
    the names that stay names (`%v1addrspace`, `%i8addrspace`,
    `@x1addrspace`, `@vi32addrspace`, a label `addrspace:`) and the `\r`
    comment. It also covers a clause word that ends its line, whose operand
    LLVM reads from the next line. The check refuses that by name
    ("has its operand on a later line") instead of relying on the split line
    failing to parse, which is how the previous check refused it. The test
    kills 15 mutants of the token rule, the comment rule and the line-end
    rule, among them reading digits as name bytes (the round-4 finding),
    reading every `iN` as a name or every one as a type, dropping the
    numbered-ID case, running a comment to the end of the line and skipping
    a clause word that ends its line. It still kills three round-3 mutants
    re-run against the new check. Of the round-4 verifier's 62 modules, llc
    compiles 49. The importer refuses by name each of the 26 whose code
    spells a non-default address space (one only in a constant expression
    that LLVM folds away). It also refuses two where LLVM ignores the
    clause: unreferenced metadata, and a metadata string continued from an
    earlier line (the check tracks quotes one line at a time). It admits
    three that mention `addrspace(1)` only inside a string, and four that
    llc rejects.
  - **Block comments.** LLVM 22 accepts C-style `/* ... */` comments, as
    whitespace across lines; no reader of this importer knows them. The
    round-5 verifier showed a quote or `;` inside one hiding an address
    space from the pre-parse check. `ptr /*"*/ addrspace(270)` in a
    definition or declaration parameter, a call argument (null included), a
    function's and a call's own clause, and `define i64 @f() /* ; */
    addrspace(1)`, were all admitted. A swap reproducer printed `0x100000015`
    at O0-O3 where llc prints `0x15` (the base did the same). The same
    check now refuses any `/*` outside a string and a `;` comment by name
    ("block comments are not read by this importer"), since the text inside
    one would otherwise be read as code. A parser test covers those shapes,
    a plain and a multi-line block comment and one after a string, and
    `/*` inside a string, a quoted name, a section name and a `;` comment,
    which stay admitted. It kills the mutants that turn the refusal off or
    apply it inside strings. Moving it before the `;` rule is equivalent: at
    one position the byte is either `;` or `/`. All 21 of the verifier's
    block-comment modules are refused by name. No LLVM text in the
    repository spells `/*`, and the base-test corpus recount is unchanged.
  - **Whole-module lexing.** The pre-parse check now lexes the whole module
    once, as LLVM's lexer does, instead of one line at a time: a string runs
    to the next quote across lines, and a `;` comment ends at a newline or a
    carriage return. The round-6 verifier found a sixth line-scanner edge. A
    metadata string continued on a line beginning `;"` is closed there by
    LLVM, which reads the rest of the line as code and then skips a block
    comment. The per-line check took the line for a comment, so the importer
    read the block comment's lines as code. For `twoviews.ll`, llc built
    `@answer` returning 1 and the importer built one returning 2 (O0/O2).
    `hide2.ll` imported a definition LLVM never sees. The base did the same.
    The check (renamed `check_module_lexically`) refuses by name any string
    holding a raw newline or carriage return ("a string spanning lines is
    not read by this importer"), a string never closed, a carriage return
    inside a `;` comment with text after it, a `/*`, and a non-default
    address space. A module it admits has every string and comment closed on
    its own line, which is all the line-based reader handles. The token
    rules (`iN`/numbered-ID glue, names) are unchanged. A parser test covers
    the three reproducers, spanning and unclosed strings, the carriage-return
    comment, and one-line strings and comments (also with `\r\n` endings),
    which stay admitted. It kills nine mutants of the lexer, among them
    admitting a newline or a carriage return in a string, resetting the
    quote state at each line, admitting an unclosed string and not skipping
    comments or strings. Four earlier address-space mutants re-run against
    the new check are killed too. No tracked `.ll` file and no text of the
    base-test corpus spans a string across lines. The recount is unchanged
    (227 texts, 1,816 runs; only the five `common` fixtures change verdict;
    the 11 unimported texts unchanged).
  - **COMDAT and dropped permissions.** `$name = comdat <kind>` lines parse
    (they were a parse error). A self-keyed `any` COMDAT is admitted exactly
    where the backend emits the same group (ODR functions; link-once and ODR
    globals); every other COMDAT use is refused by name. `dso_local` and
    `unnamed_addr` are dropped: both only permit an optimization the backend
    does not make, so the object stays correct without them.
  - **Evidence.** `tests/symbol_linkage_elf.rs` (new; 5 host-neutral and 5
    AArch64 Linux native rows) reads every fact back from ELF objects at
    O0-O3 under `static`/`pie`/`pic`. It checks the importer's COMDAT
    admission against the backend's grouping for every linkage, and Mach-O
    `N_WEAK_DEF` definitions and named refusals. Its native rows use GNU ld,
    gold and LLD, and each is compared with a gcc/g++ twin (this host has no
    clang) and with the same LLVM text compiled by llc (see below). They
    cover `.dynsym` and `LD_PRELOAD` for a `pic` library
    and ODR coalescing across imported objects and g++ `inline` twins in both
    orders. They also cover hidden declarations binding inside the image,
    null-on-missing weak calls (the weak declaration placed before its first
    address use, since an address taken before the declaring line is still
    refused) and `available_externally` linking against the external
    definition. A native row runs a null-guarded weak call against the
    direct call and a gcc `-O0` twin for eight admitted signatures
    (register-pair 128-bit integers, also after one argument of each other
    general-purpose type; stack-passed `double`, `float`, `i8`/`i16`/`i32`,
    `i1` and pointer arguments) at O0-O3 with each linker, with and without
    a definition of the weak function. With the stack-i128 refusal disabled
    and `(i64 x 7, i128)` added, that row fails (`weak=48772 strong=51124`).
    A host-neutral row pins the two refusals. With the pre-change parser, all
    ten rows fail. With the parser before the refusal, only the refusal row
    fails.
    Every native row also compiles its LLVM text with llc (at the same
    optimization level; llc's `pic` model for `pie` and `pic`), links it with
    the same C driver and requires the same observation: the hidden,
    protected, weak-hidden and `linkonce_odr hidden` library, ODR coalescing
    (llc objects alone and mixed with imported ones in both orders), hidden
    declarations, `extern_weak` resolved and unresolved with
    `available_externally`, and all eight weak-call signatures. That is 64
    llc objects, each run with GNU ld, gold and LLD, and all agree with the
    importer. The test finds llc through `TCG_LLC`, the first `llc` in an
    absolute `PATH` entry, or the sysroot of the compiler that builds it
    (`$RUSTC --print sysroot`, else `rustc`'s, probed without `TCG_*`
    variables, which a Trust compiler refuses; then
    `<sysroot>/lib/rustlib/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/llc`). The llc must
    be an executable file whose LLVM major version equals that compiler's
    (`-vV`'s `LLVM version:`); the round-6 verifier found an LLVM 18 wrapper
    accepted. A relative `PATH` entry is not searched, since it would
    resolve against the test's and the floor's different working
    directories. The test prints the llc it used, its route and both
    versions. Without one the legs are skipped
    and named on stderr, and `TCG_REQUIRE_LLC` makes that a failure. The
    round-5 verifier found the floor red: it runs the target with
    `--nocapture`, and its classifier fails any transcript with a skip line,
    while llc was on neither `PATH` nor `TCG_LLC`. (An earlier sentence here
    said the floor ran only the gcc twins, which was false.) The floor now
    sets `TCG_REQUIRE_LLC=1` for this target, and its preflight resolves the
    same llc for the lane by the same rule (executable, absolute `PATH`
    entries, LLVM major equal to the lane compiler's). It records it as
    `provenance.llc` (path, route, LLVM version, SHA-256, and the compiler,
    release and sysroot that decided, so a `RUSTC` pointing elsewhere is
    visible) and refuses to run without one. The refusal and
    the test's own failure name the remedy:
    `rustup component add llvm-tools --toolchain 1.97.1-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`
    for the stock lane, or the Trust package's
    `lib/rustlib/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin` for the Trust lane. A gate
    test covers both lanes, the route order, a non-executable candidate, a
    relative `PATH` entry, an LLVM 18 llc, an llc or compiler that reports no
    version, and the x86-64 twin, which needs none. With the `llvm-tools` component installed on this host, both
    lanes run the llc twins when the target runs the floor's way (floor
    preflight, command, environment delivery and classifier). The stock
    lane passes 10/10 with the 1.97.1 toolchain's llc (LLVM 22.1.6), and
    `--trust-unverified` passes 10/10 with the Trust package's llc (LLVM
    22.1.2, found through `$RUSTC=trustc`). The host provisioning record
    lists the component.
    The round-2 verifier found three mutants of the refusal's bound that no
    test killed. As written, m05 moves the pointer into the floating-point
    arm (it takes no register), and m06/m07 move `i1` and `i16`/`i32` into
    the catch-all arm (all eight registers, a false refusal). With m05, a
    guarded weak call of `(ptr x 7, i128)` compiled and returned a wrong
    value in all 36 runs (O0-O3 under `static`/`pie`/`pic`, each with GNU
    ld, gold and LLD; for example `weak=3064 strong=5416`). So did
    `(i1 x 7, i128)` with `i1` in the floating-point arm, and
    `(i16 x 7, i128)` and `(i32 x 7, i128)` with `i16`/`i32` there. The
    parser tests and the host-neutral row now cover every scalar type. Their
    refusal rows put seven arguments of each general-purpose type, or one
    before four pairs, ahead of a 128-bit integer, and mix floating-point
    and general-purpose arguments. Their admitted rows put six before one.
    They kill all five mutants, and the native row also kills m06 and m07
    as written. The `default` visibility token (without it, `@g = default
    global` was refused as an unknown qualifier), the `thread_local`,
    `externally_initialized` and `available_externally` COMDAT messages and
    the unsigned 128-bit arm are pinned as well. All 12 round-2 mutants were
    killed; the two of a per-clause function address-space refusal target
    code the single address-space check replaced (see **Address spaces**).
    The texts the importer's own tests passed to `import_text` before this
    change were recorded by running the base test suite with a dump hook:
    227 distinct texts (188 from the parser's unit tests, the rest from the
    13 integration-test files and the driver's unit tests). They include all
    six `tests/fixtures` files and the modules the tests build with
    `format!`. Each was imported and compiled at O0 and O2 for
    `aarch64-apple-darwin` (`static`) and `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`
    (`static`, `pie` and `pic`), 1,816 runs, by the base importer and by this
    one. 1,192 objects are byte-identical and 584 refusals unchanged. The
    other 40 runs are the five texts that spelled `common` incidentally
    (three parser unit-test modules and two `intmm_arrays` modules), now
    refused by name. The two with functions compiled before (16 runs); the
    three without were already refused as empty modules (24 runs). Those
    fixtures now use plain definitions. None of the 227 texts declares an
    `extern_weak` function or gives a function a visibility or a linkage
    other than `external` or `internal` (which the base already imported as
    `Internal`). The 11 other LLVM-shaped string literals and `.ll` files in
    the tree, which no test imports (search fragments, a driver-test string
    and the two `tools/native_vector_witness` files), give 16 byte-identical
    objects and 72 unchanged refusals in the same 8 configurations.
  - **Documented limits.** LIMITATIONS also records the x86-64 ELF path
    (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `static` only). There, imported hidden or
    protected functions and `extern_weak` references are refused by the
    adapter; the base compiled them as default-visibility, strong symbols.
    `weak`, `weak_odr`, `linkonce` and `linkonce_odr` functions are still
    emitted as strong `GLOBAL` symbols with no COMDAT group (unchanged; at
    worst a "multiple definition" link failure). It also records an
    O1-only AArch64 ELF refusal that the weak-call rewrite exposes. A
    null-guarded weak call whose pointer arguments are GEPs of an external
    global fails at O1 from nine arguments (one on the stack) under
    `static`/`pie`/`pic` with "fixup Page21 addresses `wf`, a weak undefined
    symbol, PC-relatively". O0, O2 and O3 compile it. The base compiled it,
    as a strong direct call, under `static` and `pie` at every count
    measured (up to twelve) and under `pic` up to ten. Under `pic` at O1 the
    base refused a direct call or a call through a function-pointer
    parameter from eleven such arguments, and a call through a function
    address loaded from memory from ten; it compiled all three with nine.
    It fails closed.
  - **Floor.** The Linux floor adds `symbol_linkage_elf` (minimum 10, with
    `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`TCG_REQUIRE_GOLD`/`TCG_REQUIRE_LLC`); the Darwin floor
    adds its host-neutral rows (minimum 5, table sum 1,762), which never
    look for llc.
- AArch64 ELF, L02-P6 fourth closure-audit coverage (audit at `b2b9bba5c`;
  tests only, no emitted byte changes). The audit's coverage skeptic kept the
  row partial: 9 of 40 single-site visibility mutants survived every floor
  target. Each broke visibility natively: weak and COMDAT read-only data,
  COMDAT data with an explicit name, explicit-section protected data and
  thread-locals, functions in named text or function sections, COMDAT
  functions with an explicit name, the relocation-free emitter's data and the
  layout-less emitter's thread-local imports.
  - **One table instead of one more row per class.**
    `tests/aarch64_elf_symbol_binding/visibility_table.rs` generates 1,008
    symbol cases ({definition, declaration} x 8 linkages x 3 visibilities x 7
    kinds x 3 placements). It classifies each as admitted (337), refused by a
    named diagnostic (574, each compiled and its diagnostic asserted) or
    inexpressible with a witness (97). Every admitted case is checked through
    `Compiler::compile` (sequential and parallel, O0-O3) and the `Pipeline`
    unwind, layout-less and relocation-free emitters, under
    `static`/`pie`/`pic`, with and without function sections. The checks are
    binding, type, visibility, section name/type/flags, COMDAT group and
    signature, GOT or PC-relative addressing, TLS access, the `.Ltls` anchor
    and kept calls. The emitters' relocation-model backstop is checked for
    every PC-relative address it must refuse (580 case-route-model rows) or
    allow (1,102). Structural purity, read from the public module
    translation's pure callees, is checked against the same replacement
    predicates. Before, a purity predicate that ignored visibility passed
    every floor target: the AArch64 pure-call hoist that consumes it is
    opt-in, so no object byte changed.
  - **Native row.** Every route's `pic` object goes into one shared library,
    linked by GNU ld, gold and LLD at O0-O3 with and without function
    sections. It checks `.dynsym` for every admitted case, and runs 1,398
    reads plain and under an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer: only default-visibility
    definitions and declarations move.
  - **Mutants.** The audit's 40 mutants were recreated, plus 61 more that
    cover every visibility decision site: implicit and placed data rows by
    class, function symbols, undefined symbols, each emitter's rows, the TLS

    and the merge's) are killed by existing rows. Run alone, the native row
    kills each of the audit's nine survivors.

    (gates 32-35b) for the second and third repairs' rows; it said they had

    library reads its load base once a runtime definer exists. GCC 13.3's

- Product fix (the tenth L02-P10 closure audit, at `b2b9bba5c`): three
  routes the Linux link driver installed with a relocation value or a
  section it had not checked, one route past glibc's start-up code, and
  three false refusals.
  - **A link the linker refuses is never made to succeed.**
    `-Wl,--noinhibit-exec` made GNU ld 2.42, gold 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 exit
    0 after an out-of-window value: trust-cg's `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12`
    behind a 16 MiB `.tdata` was installed truncated through all three (the
    program wrote the C thread-local), and its `ADR_PREL_PG_HI21` to a word
    8 GiB away as `adrp x0, 0` through GNU ld and gold. It is refused by name
    in every spelling a linker reads, GNU ld's unlisted `noinhibit_exec`
    alias included (`[TCG-LINK-NOINHIBIT-EXEC]`), and a successful link
    whose standard error still reports such a value is refused
    (`[TCG-LINK-RANGE-WARNING]`).
  - **Loaded memory is what the sections hold.** `-Wl,--no-check-sections`
    let GNU ld (silently) and LLD load a C section over trust-cg's `.data`;
    the program read 0 for a global whose file bytes held 42. The option is
    refused by name (`[TCG-LINK-NO-CHECK-SECTIONS]`), and an image with
    overlapping segments or allocated sections, or a section not loaded from
    its own file bytes, is refused (`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]`).

    its own file bytes, is refused (`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]`). The
    eleventh audit found these byte-range rules blind to page-granular
    mapping; they are now a page model (above).
  - **Relocation formats glibc applies.** LLD's `-z rel` and
    `--pack-dyn-relocs=android` images (static, static-PIE, PIE) were
    installed and never relocated (SIGSEGV), and a `DT_RELR` PIE without the
    `GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR` dependency did not load. `-z rel` is refused by name,
    and `SHT_REL`/Android sections, `DT_REL`, a `DT_PLTREL` other than
    `DT_RELA`, Android tags, and `DT_RELR` that `ld.so` loads without that
    dependency refuse the image (`[TCG-LINK-RELOCATION-FORMAT]`).
  - **The entry point is read.** A static executable's IFUNC applier and a
    static PIE's relocator are glibc's only when the image starts at the C
    driver's start file's `_start`, placed through the driver's link map
    (stripped images too); `-e`, `--entry`, a `--defsym` of `_start` and a
    script's `ENTRY` are refused, where they were installed (hang, SIGSEGV).
  - **False refusals.** Static glibc links with GNU ld's address options
    (`-Ttext-segment=`, `-Tbss=`, `-Tdata=`, `-Ttext=`) and one-dash
    `-check-sections`/`-compress-debug-sections=` are read by the measured
    option table of the link's linker instead of as scripts. GCC `-fpic`
    GOT-base forms are left to GNU ld 2.42 and gold 2.42, which refuse them
    out of window, so their stripped links install; LLD's stripped image
    takes its GOT base from LLD's map, and an IPLT slot counts only for a
    symbol the image defines as an IFUNC (LLD's stripped `--static` link and
    a truncated IFUNC GOT load stay refused). A GCC LTO link through GNU ld
    or gold whose trace names the plugin's deleted objects is linked again
    with them kept in the stage, and installs; a positional input with GCC
    LTO IR makes a link traced (the plugin loads objects it compiles).
  - **After the verifier: silenced errors and option groups.** GNU ld's
    `-w`/`--no-warnings` suppresses errors too and exits 0, so trust-cg's
    truncated `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12` and `adrp x1, 0` were installed with
    nothing for `[TCG-LINK-RANGE-WARNING]` to read; it is refused in every
    spelling (`[TCG-LINK-NO-WARNINGS]`). gold (and GNU ld, for `-w`) read a
    one-dash piece that is not one of their long options as a group of
    short options: gold linked `-sofoo` into `foo` outside the stage and
    `-szexecstack` with an executable stack. Such groups are refused
    (`[TCG-LINK-OPTION-GROUP]`), except 217 one-dash long names measured to
    read through gold as their two-dash spellings. A scan of every flag of
    the three linkers against five links they refuse found the options that
    let an undefined reference link (`--warn-unresolved-symbols`,
    `--unresolved-symbols=ignore-all`/`ignore-in-object-files`, gold's
    `--weak-unresolved-symbols`, `-z undefs`), now refused
    (`[TCG-LINK-UNRESOLVED-SYMBOLS]`). An input path beginning with `-` is
    refused (`[TCG-LINK-OPTION-INPUT]`). An LLD shared object with
    `DT_RELR` and no version needs, which glibc loads, is no longer refused.
  - **After the second verifier: options that turn a relied-on refusal
    off, and the entry point.** gold's `-z nocopyreloc` resolved a
    `--no-pie` program's reference to a shared library's variable to 0
    (SIGSEGV), and LLD's `--ignore-data-address-equality` made the copy
    relocation of a protected variable that the linkers otherwise refuse
    (the program read 97, not 99). Both, and LLD's
    `--ignore-function-address-equality`, are refused in every spelling
    (`[TCG-LINK-COPY-RELOCATION]`). gold and LLD read `-export-dyn` as `-e
    xport-dyn` and wrote `e_entry` 0; those dynamic programs were
    installed and died before running. Every executable whose `e_entry` is
    0, or outside its executable segments' file contents, is now refused
    (`[TCG-LINK-ENTRY-POINT]`). A second scan of every flag against six
    links whose refusal or value trust-cg relies on (10,980 links) also
    found LLD's `--unique` and a `--start-lib` without a later
    `--end-lib`, which break the C runtime's `.init` (SIGILL); both are
    refused (`[TCG-LINK-C-RUNTIME-LAYOUT]`). Through the driver every
    flagged link is refused except `-z nodefaultlib`, whose programs fail
    to load (exit 127). The `DT_RELR` rule now follows glibc 2.39 exactly

    - each section could claim the whole input;
