- AArch64 ELF leaves without a frame owner are frameless. Linux has no red
  zone, and the zero-storage leaf policy kept the sixteen-byte FP/LR envelope
  around any ADD/SUB/immediate-LSL body or constant/copy return for the
  verifier's source-bound frame owner. That owner judges only a source inside
  its chain/diamond affine domain. For any other source, such as a multiply
  by a constant, a load or a store beside the ADD, the envelope earned no
  evidence. It added three instructions and two unmapped pair opcodes, and
  the leaf was framed on ELF but not on Mach-O. Frame lowering now asks the
  owner's own applicability check (`source_admits_frame_owner`) about the
  exact LIR source instruction selection consumed. When the owner never
  judges it, the ordinary zero-storage audit decides. Affine sources, raw
  machine callers and Mach-O are unchanged. Over the 215 distinct TrustIR
  blobs tracked at `a559dd62c`, at O0–O3, all 728 Mach-O objects are
  byte-identical. 1,067 ELF leaf instances lose exactly the envelope, and
  1,059 of them then match Mach-O word for word. Another 314 functions differ
  only in trailing alignment padding, and no other word changes. 2,968
  ELF-only leaf frames remain, 1,739 of them for unreferenced declared stack
  slots (see the
  2026-09-25 record).
- certified objects, L03-P13: exception tables carry no proof obligation
  (trusted base TB-12), so a proof-required compile whose object would carry
  any is now refused by name (`CompileError::ExceptionTablesUnproved`,
  `[TCG-EH-UNPROVED]` "exception tables carry no proof obligation"; the
  rustc bridge classifies it `[TCG-PROOF-465]`) on AArch64 and x86-64, before
  the relocation inventory and the certificates. The census counts a
  function's own EH structure and the walk-through tables x86-64 emitters add
  under whole-program `panic=unwind` (the Mach-O filler LSDA of every framed
  function; on ELF an LSDA for every function), read from the predicates the
  emitters use (`x86_module_emits_eh_frame`, `x86_macho_gets_filler_lsda`,
  `plan_x86_64_elf_module_unwind`). Before this gate a certified x86-64 Mach-O
  compile of an EH module, or of any `panic=unwind` module, promoted its
  exception tables. **Behaviour change:** the x86-64 object pipeline lowers
  every function with a frame, so under `panic=unwind` every non-empty
  x86-64 object carries exception tables, and with proof certificates on
  x86-64 now requires `-Cpanic=abort`. The rustc bridge's default
  configuration (certificates on, Rust's default `-Cpanic=unwind`) refuses
  EVERY x86-64 codegen unit (`x86_64-apple-darwin`,
  `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`) with `[TCG-EH-UNPROVED]`; compile with
  `-Cpanic=abort` or `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=no-proof-certs`. For a function
  without EH of its own the refusal names the `panic=unwind` walk-through
  tables. The bridge's x86-64 `panic=unwind` execution differentials
  (`panic_unwind_raise_x86`, including
  `returning_track_caller_extern_rlib_matches_llvm`,
  `m134_x86_needs_drop_elem_x86::element_drop_panic_unwind_matches_llvm` and
  the unwind leg of `m139_flatmap_bounded_x86`) compile with
  `no-proof-certs`; they run on x86-64 hosts. `m139`'s five lowering
  canaries compile for whatever host runs them (they are not host-gated),
  also without certificates, and now require their specific refusal:
  `[TCG-ITER-UNMODELED]` naming the canary crate's `main` for the four
  terminal shapes, `[TCG-MIR-UNSUPPORTED]` naming `FuseImpl::next` over
  `Fuse<Map<Range<_>, _>>` for the bare `for` loop, and never an internal
  compiler error, a panic or a link failure. They skip, and say why, when
  their same-host positive control (`sum_basic` compiles and exits 1) fails,
  as it does on AArch64 Linux today. A certified x86-64 COFF compile is
  refused either way, by its relocation inventory. The proof-grade AArch64
  JIT routes make the same decision through the same `ExceptionTableCensus`. The AArch64
  relocation-inventory certificate states that unwind tables of frames without
  EH are trusted, not proven (ELF `.eh_frame` FDEs, Mach-O compact unwind);
  the x86-64 certificates do not yet. Every relocation inventory report,
  AArch64 and x86-64, marks exception-table rows `Unverified`. A malformed
  exception-handling structure in any function of the unit (an orphan
  landing pad, or a `Resume` in a function without EH metadata beside a
  well-formed EH function) keeps its structural diagnostic under
  certificates. The `panic_unwind` documentation (`CompilerConfig`,
  `X86PipelineConfig`, `trust-cg --panic-unwind`) now states what it changes
  per output format.
- certified relocation inventory, L03-P13: an AArch64 ELF module with
  exception-handling metadata is inventoried instead of refused
  (`[TCG-REGALLOC-063]` "exception-handling sidecar unsupported ... does not
  yet enumerate"). The inventory mirrors the emitter's unwind-table records
  exactly: the zPLR CIE personality `R_AARCH64_PREL32` against
  `DW.ref.<personality>`, per function the FDE pc-begin `PREL32` against the
  anchor of the section defining the function (+ body offset) and the FDE
  LSDA `PREL32` against the `.gcc_except_table` anchor (+ LSDA offset), and
  the slot's `R_AARCH64_ABS64` to the personality. It checks every LSDA for
  relocation-bearing fields and the CIE's pointer encodings, classifies data
  placement with the emitters' own function (so a data global in `.eh_frame`
  or `.gcc_except_table` is refused alike, `[TCG-SECTION-RESERVED]`), and
  keeps named refusals for Mach-O EH, typed catches and filters, a second
  personality, unknown encodings and missing frame layouts. `Compiler::compile`
  compares every `.eh_frame` record and the record of the slot the CIE points
  at with the mirrored rows after emission, keyed by section and symbol
  index (two COMDAT bodies in same-named sections stay distinct; a data
  section named `.data.DW.ref.*` is not read as a slot). Every inventory
  report marks exception-table rows `Unverified`, so an EH module's report is
  never promotable. `fn main() {}` with `-Cpanic=unwind` through the rustc bridge
  no longer fails with `[TCG-REGALLOC-063]`: its `FnOnce::call_once` shim is
  refused with `[TCG-EH-UNPROVED]`, and the other items at the pair-opcode
  `[TCG-PROOF-465]` as with `-Cpanic=abort`. New Linux floor target
  `aarch64_elf_eh_relocation_inventory` (13 tests). The Darwin floor table
  also gains the `flat_gep_semantics` row the Linux floor added without it.
- rustc bridge diagnostics (trust-core AD-8 / E0.3, carried onto current
  main): every error variant main added since the classifiers lost their
  default arm is now filed under the layer that raises it, and so are main's
  new refusal sites that used the stringly `ISel` / `Encoding` variants
  (of 51 audited: 33 retyped to `ObjectEmission`, 1 to `ModuleIo` plus the
  decode unwrap that consumes it, 5 to the new
  `PipelineError::DebugInfoInput` (TCG-DEBUG-INFO), 2 to the new
  `PipelineError::IrLowering` carrying the adapter's typed byval/variadic
  refusal (TCG-IR-LOWER); 9 kept as the encoder's own; `load_module_as`'s
  conflicted read/decode sites carry `ModuleIo` too). `DwarfEmission` is
  merged into main's `DwarfEmit`. The stack-canary target refusal is a
  frame-lowering refusal again, now naming the target and object format.
  Main's x86-64 ELF exception-handling lane raised its 12 refusals as
  `X86PipelineError::FrameLowering` (TCG-REGALLOC-063); they are filed by the
  layer that raises them: 9 unwind-table refusals (the `.eh_frame` round-trip
  checks, the personality conflict, a function with no frame lowering or no
  bytes, an FDE the prologue cannot describe, the terminator strip, the CIE
  personality field and the FDE field count) are `Unwind` (TCG-EH-UNWIND), and
  the 3 symbol-table refusals (the `DW.ref` slot symbol, its COMDAT signature,
  the local-symbol reservation) are `ObjectEmission` (TCG-OBJECT-EMIT). The four
  planner refusals are driven directly, main's two end-to-end refusal tests now
  also assert the variant, and the eight sites no input reaches are pinned by
  source. The worker-pool refusals main moved into the fsym module scope keep
  `WorkerPool` (TCG-COMPILE-DRIVER). The ELF planner's synthetic filler LSDA
  refusal (an exception-table build refusal) is `MalformedEh`
  (TCG-EH-UNWIND) like its Mach-O twin, not `MalformedFunction`
  (TCG-REGALLOC-063); it is driven directly by an unrepresentable module
  personality. Of the error variants main added with KIND 4, the reader's
  `PipelineError::ProducerOmittedBodyGate` is filed as TCG-COMPILE-DRIVER
  (module decoding, before any compilation layer runs), and the reader's
  payload-deserialize and decoded-provenance refusals it raised as `ISel` are
  `ModuleIo`; both are driven through `decode_tmbc` in the bridge's tests. The
  three new `AdapterError` variants are the adapter's own and stay
  TCG-IR-LOWER.
- Rule discovery never accepts a rule without a certified proof. When CEGIS
  returned an error — no solver, AY's `unknown`, and also a working checker's
  or AY's own self-check rejection of AY's proof — `RuleDiscovery` fell back to
  sampled evaluation and returned `Accepted`, which `rewrite_admission`
  records as an `AYEquivalenceProof`. The evaluator may now only reject;
  otherwise the rule is `RuleResult::Inconclusive`, which carries the CEGIS
  verdict so a caller can tell AY's disclosed proof hole from a rejection.
  Measured with AY 0.13.0 build.8256 and clean 8606: `mul2_to_lsl1_32bit` was
  "accepted" this way after AY's self-check rejected its proof.
- trust-cg-verify tests that asserted nothing unless a proof succeeded now
  apply the shared skip rule (`formal_gap`: a rejected proof fails; only the
  named absent proof authority and AY's disclosed proof hole skip) in cegis,
  cegis_pass_x86, rule_discovery, synthesis and unified_synthesis, and in the
  i128 rows of `checked_overflow_proofs` (the add/sub rows must Verify like
  their i64 twins; the carry-chain rows tolerate only capacity). With AY
  build.8256 four of them now fail on AY's self-check rejection:
  `checked_overflow_add_sub_i128_formally_discharges`,
  `checked_i128_carry_chain_formally_discharges`,
  `discover_32bit_mul_to_shift` and `unified_neon_mul2_eq_shl1`.
- `checked_mul_i128_proofs::formal_attempt_never_refutes` no longer passes on
  a solver error or on an Unknown the strict gate files as a soundness failure
  (a checker's rejection, AY's self-check rejection); it tolerates only
  capacity, like the 64-bit checked-mul rows, and skips by name without AY.
- Resident AY's per-query deadline now measures solver time. It starts when
  the query is admitted to the resident server, not when the query starts
  waiting for it, so a query queued behind other solves is no longer timed out
  before it runs (measured before: a 328-byte plugin unit-test query returned
  `Timeout` after 30.001 s of queueing). Queueing is bounded separately: a
  waiter gets the named error `resident AY server wedged: ...` only once the
  query holding the server has run past its own budget plus a 10 s allowance;
  a holder under the unlimited (zero) timeout policy is waited for. Controls: a
  query with a 1.5 s budget queued behind a 3 s window completes, and fails
  when the deadline is started on arrival again; a waiter behind a holder
  inside its budget is admitted with its whole budget, and one behind a
  holder that overran is refused. The plugin's solver-coupled unit tests no
  longer exempt AY's self-check rejection (production files it as a soundness
  failure); with AY build.8256, 13 of them fail, with the same 13 names in 5
  default runs and 1 single-threaded run.
- The strict proof gate now files a working independent checker's rejection
  of AY's exact Alethe proof ("AY reported UNSAT but <checker> — which
  verified a known-good control proof, so it is a working checker — rejected
  or could not fully verify THIS Alethe proof") as a SOUNDNESS failure, like
  AY's own `self-check-rejected`. It was filed as PENDING(solver-capacity) and
  counted with timeouts as capacity debt; the gate still never passed on it.
  The plugin's solver-coupled unit tests now skip only when AY's own
  certificate discloses an unproved hole step with no foreign assumptions
  (tracked in ay `docs/ay-asks/2026-08-13-bv-certified-families`), or on the
  solver-absent lane. They used to also skip on a checker rejection, a replay
  that could not complete, a missing checker, missing proof evidence, and a
  gap on another obligation of the same test (that last fix reached the
  value-lane helpers only, not the 14 tests that went through
  `check_memory_sequence`; see the next entry).
- Refinement checks that must refine several obligations
  (`check_memory_sequence` and the block-arg, loop-carried and back-edge
  threading checks) now discharge EVERY obligation and report `Refuted` when
  any one refutes. They stopped at the first obligation that did not refine,
  so in the default refinement lane, which fails the compile on `Refuted` and
  skips `Inconclusive`, an undecided early obligation (a disclosed proof hole,
  AY's self-check rejection, a timeout) hid a refutation of a later one and the
  wrong memory lowering compiled. Measured with AY build.8256 on the plugin's
  memory tests: for 9 wrong store/copy lowerings the first obligation is
  undecided and a later one refutes. The new per-obligation API
  (`discharge_memory_sequence`, `discharge_each`, `ObligationVerdict`) lets a
  test see each verdict. Solver-coupled tests in both crates now fold every
  verdict: with a solver installed, any rejection or other undecided
  obligation fails the test (also a test expecting a refutation), a refutation
  fails a test expecting a refinement, and a test skips only when every
  undecided obligation is AY's disclosed proof hole. trust-cg-verify's own
  guards (`formal_gap`) follow the same rule as the plugin's: a working
  checker's rejection, AY's self-check rejection and a bare `unknown` fail
  instead of skipping, and a bare `unknown` is no longer re-probed through a
  different route. A resident-server queue refusal is specified not to switch
  the resident server off for later queries.

- Vectorizer loop idioms (TRUSTCG-01, TRUSTCG-18): the i32 induction-store
  rewrite (`a[i] = i + 1`, a NEON ST1 main loop in front of the scalar loop)
  stored its first vector at `a[0]` whatever the entry index, and its
  `index + 3 < bound` guard was an i32 add that wraps near `i32::MAX`; it had
  been quarantined off. It now addresses `a[entry]`, evaluates the guard on
  sign-extended 64-bit values and runs again in the default O2, Os and O3
  pipelines. Its matcher and the reverse-accumulation matcher
  (`dst[i] += src[i]`, counting down) checked only that every body
  instruction was in an allowed set. Both now share
  `vectorize/loop_contract.rs`: exact loop shape and block contents, datapath
  order by reaching definition, one dominating definition per constant,
  loop-invariant bases and bound, an index that only the latch writes, no
  loop value escaping the loop, and a private stack slot for a spilled
  index. A loop that fails a check stays scalar. The reverse rewrite now
  reads the invariant bases, not the body's copies of them, and still runs
  only with NoAlias and InBounds proof facts.
  Evidence: a strict test-only MachIR interpreter runs the scalar and the
  rewritten loop on the same inputs, in 10 tests of loops that are the idiom
  (zero, nonzero, negative and `i32::MAX`-adjacent ranges) and 30 fixtures
  that are not the idiom and must stay scalar. `ary3_init_o2_e2e` links and
  runs two imported-O0 fixtures that check every element and sentinel
  (executed on macOS ARM64; its Darwin floor minimum is now 2). The target
  is also on the Linux floor, where this change has not run yet. This is
  differential and execution evidence, not a proof of either rewrite.
- Floor machinery, X13: a target an OWNER DECISION removes from a regression
  floor is now DECLARED instead of deleted. The shared runner
  (`scripts/check_linux_aarch64.py`, loaded by the x86-64 twin) gains
  `DECIDED_ABSENT` — rows of `(package, target, decision id, reason)` that are
  never run but are printed before and after every run, listed by `--list`, and
  recorded in every `report.json` under `decided_absent`. `TARGETS` stays
  all-required, and the runner REFUSES to start when a decided-absent row also
  appears in `TARGETS` or its test file is gone, so the record cannot outlive
  the lane it describes and a lane cannot leave the floor by silently vanishing
  from the list. The AArch64 floor declares no rows; the x86-64 floor declares
  one: `e2e_x86_64_swiftcc` under XD-03, the swiftcc return-placement readings,
  which need a clang driver for `__attribute__((swiftcall))` (GCC ignores the
  attribute, so on a GCC-only host the "swiftcall" readings would silently be C
  readings and the divergence rows would refute nothing) and this host has no
  clang. Those readings are SPLIT OUT of `e2e_x86_64_calling_conv` into that
  target so they can be named: the (E3) admission controls and the C-convention
  oracles stay behind and keep running on every floor host, and the hand-written
  control assembly there now spells its symbols through `host_sym` so the same
  source links against the C driver on ELF and on Mach-O. A decided-absent RUN
  is not a licence to delete the evidence: `scripts/soundness_check.sh` gates the
  new target too (on a clang-less host it prints the conforming `SKIP: (E4) NOT
  RUN`, which the gate parser classifies as `skipped` and records as FAIL, rather than
  failing where `cc` is GCC), and the `soundness_manifest` `ABI-x86-cc`
  invariant now reads the swiftcc source for the (E4) test, the readings
  counter, the `__attribute__((swiftcall))` text, the not-a-no-op control check
  and the skip marker.
- Floor machinery, X13: a required floor target may now live in the rustc
  BRIDGE workspace. The shared runner resolves the pinned Trust package through
  `scripts/trust_toolchain.py` (`--trust-driver <package>/bin/trustc`; a PATH
  shim, a stock nightly, an unidentified compiler and a package built for
  another host are all refused), runs such a target in
  `crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg` with that package's
  `targo --unverified test --release --locked`, and passes the package `trustc`
  as `RUSTC` through a new `environment_overrides` argument applied AFTER the
  per-target unset list; each target's record now carries its `cwd` and its
  overrides. That lane is diagnostic and makes no Trust-verified-compilation
  claim. The Linux x86-64 floor registers one bridge target,
  `m143_x86_vectorize_trace`: the x86-64 SSE2 vectorizer's beat-llvm tiers must
  still fire on the p4/h1/v2 shapes at `-Copt-level=3` and the vectorized
  binaries must exit with the manifest codes, so a tier that stops firing is a
  floor failure rather than a timing regression noticed later. The floor's
  target count is pinned at 67 by `scripts/tests/test_linux_x86_64_gate.py`.
  MEASURED on `0bb155abf` with `--require-clean --jobs 4 --max-rss-gib 20` and
  the stage2 Trust package named by `--trust-driver`: the floor is **56 of 67**,
  `dirty: false`, `errors: []`, `decided_absent` present in `report.json` with
  its XD-03 reason, the refusal line printed before the first target and again
  with the verdict, and the bridge lane passing 2 of 2 at 1797 MiB peak RSS.
  `e2e_x86_64_calling_conv` reads 18 / 0 after the split where `origin/main`'s
  own copy of that file reads 17 / 2 on this host. The eleven remaining failures
  are pre-existing: seven XD-01 proof-promotion rows, two upstream fail-closed
  `Select scalar condition must be Bool` refusals, and two Darwin-only host
  assumptions (`cc -arch`, an explicit AArch64 `SKIP:`). Evidence, including
  every per-target log:
  `reports/perf/2026-09-24-linux-x86-64-decided-absent/`.

- x86-64 ELF, X03: exception handling is emitted for ELF modules, so the three
  x86-64 EH floor targets run on an x86-64 Linux GNU host instead of printing a
  Darwin-host SKIP (`tc_try_x86 returned 42`, `tc_try returned 42`,
  `cleanup_ran=1 caught=1`, 2026-09-24). `DwarfCie::x86_64_elf[_with_eh]` add the
  GNU/Linux CIEs; `emit_module_elf` adds a `.gcc_except_table` holding every
  function's LSDA (real for an EH function, an all-filler `landing_pad == 0`
  region for the rest), a zPLR `.eh_frame` giving EVERY function of an EH-bearing
  module an FDE, and the `DW.ref.<personality>` slot the CIE's
  `DW_EH_PE_indirect|pcrel|sdata4` field names — weak, hidden, alone in a
  `GRP_COMDAT` group it signs, holding `R_X86_64_64` to the personality;
  object-local for a personality the module defines `STB_LOCAL`, as on AArch64
  ELF. Every `.eh_frame` pointer is an `R_X86_64_PC32` against a LOCAL
  `STT_SECTION` anchor plus an addend, emitted in ascending `r_offset` order
  because GNU ld walks the section with one monotonic relocation cursor and
  otherwise creates no `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME`. The personality addend is 0: the ELF
  relocation is field-START relative, unlike the Darwin GOT reloc's field-END
  bias. Both ELF `.eh_frame` lanes now pass `verify_eh_frame_roundtrip` before
  emission, and the EH lane strips the terminator crtend.o owns. A function the
  lane cannot describe — no frame lowering, an empty body, a second personality —
  is refused by name. Five refusal sites moved deliberately:
  `reject_unwired_x86_eh_output` takes an emission lane, so ELF MODULE emission
  is admitted while SINGLE-FUNCTION ELF emission still refuses (it has no LSDA
  section, anchors or slot); the assembled-module inventory and the final
  emission boundary admit ELF; and compiler.rs's non-Mach-O AOT gate becomes
  `reject_x86_eh_for_unwired_aot_format`, still refusing COFF and raw bytes. The
  x86 JIT keeps refusing EH (no in-memory eh_frame). The `verify` relocation
  inventory predicts the new surface by CALLING the emitter's planner, and uses
  only already-registered relocation kinds, so no new proof strength is claimed.
  Controls: the trust-ir `Invoke`/`LandingPad` fixture compiles and RUNS at
  O0-O3; GNU `readelf` reads the CIE, the FDE, the ascending PC32 records and
  the slot's binding back, and the image `link_objects` stages carries `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME`; dropping the covering LSDA call-site row's landing pad
  loses the catch; turning the CIE personality encoding from `0x9b` to a DIRECT
  `0x1b` loses it too; two independent objects each carrying a slot both catch in
  one link; the object links as a SHARED object, and the same object with its
  personality record retargeted at `__gxx_personality_v0` directly is refused by
  GNU ld. Flag off, an ELF module emits no unwind surface and no relocation at
  all. Typed catches, filters and mixed personalities stay refused.
- rustc bridge, L03-P2: the Darwin-only unwind/cleanup control has a Linux
  ELF twin, `unwind_cleanup_linux`, and `check_linux_aarch64_bridge.py`
  requires it as a third native target (marker
  `TCG_BRIDGE_UNWIND_EXECUTION`). It compiles the Darwin crate and panicker
  byte-identically, plus a user-`Drop` `Guard`, a `Box<Guard>`, a typed
  payload and a second bridge frame, for `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` at O0–O3
  with the `no-proof-certs` knob. `readelf` checks each fixture function's
  LSDA rows, FDE LSDA pointer and `DW.ref.rust_eh_personality` slot; an
  LLVM-compiled Rust driver catches every panic with `catch_unwind` and must
  print the exact payloads, drop order, `Box` allocation/free counts and hook
  counts (the LLVM twin may remove the two never-read boxes above O0). Zeroing
  the landing pad of each protected call in a copy of its object loses
  exactly that frame's drops and frees, and `disable-unwind` refuses each
  fixture function by name. The artifacts directory is removed on success.
  On clean `92173b47d` it passes 2/2 (8 lanes, 12 controls, 4 refusals);
  the runner still fails, on the ABI target alone (L06-P1), and TLS passes
  2/2 (`reports/perf/2026-09-24-linux-bridge-unwind/`). `catch_unwind`
  inside a bridge frame stays refused.
- trust-ir adapter, L03-P2: an `Inst::Invoke` that follows another call of
  its trust-ir block (a LIR `Call`, `CallIndirect` or `CallVariadic`) moves
  into a block of its own, as an invoke with a by-reference argument already
  did. Before, such a block was refused, under one of two names: by the
  AArch64 call-site resolver ("exactly one is required by block-granular
  metadata"), or, when the landing pad reads a value computed in that block
  before the invoke, earlier by the frame check (`[TCG-A64-SPILL-SLOT] …
  caller-callee-saved-value-read`). The earlier call keeps a no-handler row.
  Calls the adapter emits split: trust-ir calls, `frem` (`fmod`/`fmodf`),
  i128 <-> f32/f64 casts (`__fix*ti`, `__float*ti*`), heap allocation and
  free, and the ARC operations. Calls that only instruction selection
  introduces stay refused by name: i128 `udiv`/`sdiv`/`urem`/`srem`
  (`__udivti3`, `__divti3`, `__umodti3`, `__modti3`) and an uninlined
  `Memcpy`/`Memmove`/`Memset` (an aggregate copy). `e2e_aarch64_eh_linux`
  adds `tc_merged`/`tr_merged` and `tc_early`/`tr_early`, whose earlier plain
  call throws or panics on odd input: at O0–O3 that exception passes the
  frame's pad to the caller with the pad's cleanup not run (20 C++ and 20
  Rust calls). Mutants at every level: the pad moved onto the earlier call's
  row loses the handler; the pad copied onto it (the invoke's row unchanged)
  runs for the earlier call's exception and is killed. Host-neutral rows pin
  the adapter's block shape and which earlier calls split or stay refused:
  12 tests, 6 host-neutral (the Darwin floor minimum is now 6). On x86-64,
  `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` refuses every EH module by name before and after,
  so the split is unreachable there; on `x86_64-apple-darwin` an independent
  verifier found the split fixture refused at `3be0b17c6`
  (`[TCG-POST-RA-DATAFLOW]` … "3 eligible calls") and compiling now at O0–O3,
  with a row covering exactly each invoke's call and its pad, no-handler rows
  for the earlier calls (an indirect call among them), and an object
  byte-identical to the explicit-`br` form: compiled and read back, not run.
- x86-64 selection: an `f16` formal parameter is refused by name
  (`[TCG-X86-F16-ABI]`) instead of panicking ("unsupported x86 XMM lane type:
  F16", seen on the `ty_primitives.tmbc` conformance fixture for
  `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`). `f16` call arguments and returns are unchanged.
- rustc bridge: `aarch64_c_fnabi_aggregate_linux` creates its artifacts
  directory under `$TMPDIR` instead of `/tmp` and removes it when the test
  ends, passing or failing (`C_FNABI_LINUX_KEEP_ARTIFACTS=1` retains it); it
  used to leave one behind on every (currently failing) run.
- AArch64 ELF, L02-P6 closure-audit residuals (audit at `3be0b17c6`):
  - Fix (soundness): `merge_modules` gives a merged GLOBAL the most
    constraining visibility any input states, as it already did for
    functions. A default definition that satisfied another input's hidden or
    protected data import used to keep default visibility, in both input
    orders. The merged `pic` library then exported the word and addressed it
    through the GOT, and an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer took over its load
    (`load_pw=bad`, expected 5), while the consumer compiled alone was
    refused.
  - Hidden and protected data DECLARATIONS compile instead of being refused
    with `ImportVisibilityUnsupported`: an initializer-less `External` or
    `ExternalWeak` global, an `AvailableExternally` one or a thread-local
    import. Its undefined symbol is `STB_GLOBAL` (`STB_WEAK` for
    `ExternalWeak`) with `STV_HIDDEN`/`STV_PROTECTED`, and its address stays
    GOT-indirect under the one shared rule. A data declaration may name a GNU
    IFUNC function, whose PC-relative address GNU ld and gold resolve to its
    PLT stub. The emitter backstop refuses a PC-relative page reference to
    such an import. Mach-O, the JIT data image, the x86-64 emitters (new
    `X86PipelineError::ImportVisibilityUnsupported`) and every other lowering
    entry keep refusing it, as does the ELF path for an `Internal`/`Private`
    thread-local import.
  - An external personality's `DW.ref.<personality>` slot is emitted as GCC
    emits it: `WEAK HIDDEN`, alone in a `GRP_COMDAT` group it signs. At the
    base it was weak default-visible and in no group, so GNU ld 2.42 and LLD
    refused to link a `pic` EH module into a shared object, and gold exported
    the slot. Objects with exception tables and an external personality
    change bytes (the slot's visibility, its group and section flags); a
    module-local personality's object-local slot does not.
  - The TLS descriptor relocations of a strong hidden thread-local
    definition name an object-local `STT_TLS` anchor at the definition, as
    GCC's section anchor does, so gold no longer lists it `TLS LOCAL HIDDEN`
    in a shared object's `.dynsym`.
  - The Linux floor pins `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` (59) and
    `e2e_aarch64_elf_relocation_model` (21); the Darwin floor's host-neutral
    minimums for them are 35 and 19. The three `rust-lld` legs of
    `e2e_aarch64_elf_relocation_model` fall back to an `ld.lld` and fail
    under `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD` when neither exists, instead of printing `SKIP`
    and passing; a new row pins that lookup.
  - Refusal (from the repair's independent verifier): a module that
    DEFINES a non-local data global named `DW.ref.__gxx_personality_v0` or
    `DW.ref.rust_eh_personality` is refused by name on every target
    (`DataShadowsBackendSymbol`). Every unwind table's slot of that name
    resolves to it: with GNU ld and gold a throw through the module's own
    frames died with `SIGBUS` (PIE and shared library), and LLD resolved the
    module's word to the slot or refused the link. Also from that verifier:
    the TLS anchor controls now anchor variables at nonzero offsets of
    `.tdata`, `.tbss` and an explicit section (an anchor placed at offset 0
    had passed every suite while its accessor used another variable's
    storage), and the test-only `ld.lld` search visits `TCG_LLD_DIR`,
    `~/.local/bin` and `PATH` in order.
  - New controls: native rows through GNU ld, gold and LLD at O0-O3 for a
    merged hidden data import under `LD_PRELOAD`, data declarations in
    non-PIE, static, PIE, static-PIE and shared images (copy relocations,
    IFUNC-named data, weak absent data, address and value equality with C),
    `pic` EH libraries in which a C++ throw crosses CG frames (one slot, none
    exported, mixed with g++ objects), and hidden and protected
    thread-locals in three threads under `LD_PRELOAD`.

- The multi-input sampling sweep reaches preconditions that relate its
  inputs (NEW-CG-SAMPLER). Its uniform draws are consecutive outputs of one
  power-of-two-modulus LCG, so two inputs were never both even, never equal
  and never equal to a named 64-bit constant, and an obligation whose
  preconditions needed that got no evidence: a claim false exactly there was
  the vacuous-sample `Unknown` instead of refuted. After the edge battery and
  the uniform trials, an obligation with preconditions now gets as many
  precondition-directed trials as uniform ones, up to 16,384, from an
  independent SplitMix64 stream: each input takes a uniform value, one of
  the preconditions' own constants, a small value, an aligned value, an
  earlier input's value plus a small power-of-two offset, or an edge value;
  then each equality precondition that pins one input (`x == e`,
  `x & m == k`) is solved for it. Every point is still checked against every
  precondition, and the verdict stays statistical. The fifteen registry
  obligations TRUSTCG-02 left as the vacuous sample (the atomic and
  symbolic-memory non-interference proofs, three Greedy RA proofs, TLSLE
  exact-address, the two LSDA coverage proofs) are `Valid` on at least 64
  directed points each; their tests pin that and keep their witnesses. A
  precondition the directed trials cannot solve (`a * K == C`) is still the
  vacuous sample, and the shared-width (two-input) sweep is unchanged.
- The slow full-database lane (`--features slow-full-database`,
  `full_proof_suite`) is green again (NEW-CG-FULLDB). Its one undecided row,
  the source-bound AArch64 leaf-frame theorem, quantifies over an arbitrary
  initial memory (`entry_memory`, an uninterpreted array) that concrete
  evaluation declines by contract; it is the lane's one audited
  evaluation-`Unknown`, required to give that reason, and its proof remains
  the strict AY gate's.
- The sampling evaluator no longer credits a sweep that compared nothing
  (TRUSTCG-02). A `verify_by_evaluation` sweep in which no edge-case or
  random sample satisfied the obligation's preconditions used to end in
  `Valid`; it now ends in an explicit `Unknown` naming the vacuous sample and
  the number of points tried, on every sampling route: the shared-width and
  multi-input sweeps, batched, compiled and interpreted evaluation, chunked
  and sequential, the structural-identity short-circuit (which now fires only
  when the obligation has no preconditions or a point of the sweep's own edge
  battery satisfies them) and the process-wide memo.
  `preconditions_hold` evaluates every precondition before deciding the
  conjunction, so a precondition the evaluator cannot interpret is named
  whatever its position. Fifteen registry obligations held `Valid` only by
  that vacuous credit — the seven atomic and two symbolic-memory
  non-interference proofs (both addresses aligned, which consecutive draws
  of the sampling LCG never are), the three Greedy RA proofs, the TLSLE
  exact-address proof and the two LSDA call-site coverage proofs. They now
  report the vacuous sample, their unit tests check each claim at explicit
  witnesses, and a formal claim for them can only come from the strict AY
  gate. No AArch64 walk query resolves to any of them, and the production
  callers treat a verdict other than `Valid` as undischarged.
- The FP-conversion evaluator (`verify_fp_convert_by_evaluation`) had the
  same defect (TRUSTCG-02) and follows the same rule: a sweep that compared
  no test input — every one excluded by the preconditions or failing to
  evaluate on a side — is `Unknown`, and a precondition it cannot interpret
  (or that is not boolean) is named instead of being read as false.
- The x86-64 address-teeth audit
  (`report_which_credited_opcodes_have_no_address_teeth`, TRUSTCG-04) passes
  again, and it now checks the property its count stood for. It pinned 37
  memory opcodes whose address the shared reconstruction cannot refute. Since
  88de9e199 gave the volatile forms the MemLoad/MemStore mapping of their plain
  siblings, fourteen of them reconstruct through that same `X == X` address, so
  the audit found 51 and failed. They lost no teeth: before that commit they
  did not reconstruct at all, and the byte-level address lane carries their
  address. The other two, `VolatileMovRM` and `VolatileMovsdRM`, were missing
  because their representative instances had a Gpr32 destination for a 64-bit
  load, which the reconstruction refuses. Every volatile representative now
  has the register class the ISel gives it, pinned by
  `volatile_representatives_use_the_isel_register_class`; `VolatileMovssRM`
  and the `VolatileMovMR`/`VolatileMovssMR`/`VolatileMovsdMR` stores also had
  a Gpr32 register where the ISel uses Gpr64 or XMM, though the reconstruction
  accepted them. The audit pins the 53 by name. For each one it requires that
  the coverage gate routes the row to the address lane
  (`x86_opcode_has_address_credit`) and that the lane's corpus holds captured
  encodings of it, and it requires the lane to discharge. `the_shared_reconstruction_still_has_no_address_teeth` requires
  every address-credited opcode to reconstruct instead of pinning two that do
  not. Comments that said the lane credits nothing, that Lea/LeaSib are
  outside it, or that 37 opcodes are toothless are corrected.
- AArch64 ELF, L02-P1: a trust-ir v45 hidden or protected function
  DECLARATION (bodyless `External` or `ExternalWeak`, or
  `AvailableExternally`) compiles instead of being refused
  (`[TCG-FUNCTION-VISIBILITY]` now covers only `Internal`/`Private`). Its
  undefined symbol is `STB_GLOBAL` (`STB_WEAK` for `ExternalWeak`) with
  `STV_HIDDEN`/`STV_PROTECTED`, and `ElfWriter::add_checked_symbol` admits
  it. The one address predicate is now
  `RelocationModel::symbol_address_is_got_indirect(SymbolBinding,
  Visibility)`; `definition_is_preemptible` is its definition case. Every
  declaration is addressed through the GOT under every model, hidden and
  protected ones included, and a call to a hidden or protected one binds
  without a PLT entry. (A first cut addressed strong hidden and protected
  declarations `ADRP`+`ADD`. An independent verifier found that wrong when
  the definition is a GNU IFUNC: GNU ld and gold resolve that form to the
  IFUNC's PLT stub in a PIE, a static PIE or a shared object, so the address
  differed from every GOT load of the same function.) The emitter backstop
  reads the same predicate from the object's symbols and refuses a
  PC-relative page reference to a weak undefined symbol or a declared
  function with a stated visibility under every model. `ModuleSymbolLinkage` carries
  undefined-reference visibility (Mach-O refuses it). `merge_modules` gives a
  merged function the most constraining visibility of its inputs, where it
  used to drop a declaration's. `classify_linker_stderr` classifies gold's
  and LLD's hidden/protected undefined-symbol errors. Native rows through GNU
  ld, gold and LLD, O0-O3, cover a library that binds its declarations
  locally, links that fail without a definition in the output, IFUNC
  definitions with one address in non-PIE, static, PIE, static-PIE and
  shared images, and absent weak hidden/protected references reading 0 (GNU
  ld and LLD also when only another shared library defines them; gold
  refuses that link). They also pin two gold 2.42
  defects that GCC code shares: an absent weak hidden reference in a PIE or
  library reads the load base, and a non-PIE executable gets no canonical
  address for any function it takes from a library.
- x86-64 bridge, cross-backend ABI (both directions): every Rust-ABI
  `PassMode::Pair` argument rides rustc's two independent argument values.
  A 16-byte two-INTEGER pair — the slice / `str` fat-pointer family,
  `NonNull<[u8]>`, `(u64, u64)`, `Range<usize>`, `Option<u64>`, a two-`u64`
  struct — was declared as one all-or-nothing aggregate: with exactly one
  integer register left rustc puts lane 0 in R9 and lane 1 on the stack, the
  bridge put the whole pair on the stack. `check_param_abi` classifies a
  parameter in isolation, so it passed; the divergence is numbering at
  exhaustion. Measured before: 70 of 160 cross-backend cells (O0, O2)
  disagreed, every one-register-left shape in BOTH directions (`&str`, two
  slices and an sret return SIGSEGV), while every same-backend cell and both
  controls agreed. The scope gate of `scalar_pair_param_plan` now offers every
  x86-64 `Pair` the lane (a non-`Pair` mode still gets no plan), so the
  declaration, the callee entry, every call site and the virtual `param_tys`
  move together; a slice-family `{ data, len }` slot is read and written through
  its own helpers (`slice_fat_ptr_call_arg_slot` holds the whole-slot arm's
  operand resolution). `m144` (320 cells at O0–O3, 0 failures) and
  `bridge_corpus/pair_arg_exhaustion.rs` (strict, exit 23) pin it; census
  62 → 62 with zero arity mismatches. Residual, fail-closed: closure bodies
  keep the whole slot and every cross-backend route to one is refused by name;
  AArch64 unchanged pending measurement.
- Fix, from the seventh independent verifier round of the L02-P1 lift (the
  sixth round's repair holds; no wrong code on any existing route). (1) The
  Core token was a convention. An external caller could construct it, pass
  it to the Core entry and emit the result through `Pipeline`, which gave
  `my_rem(5,3)` = 42 again. A new non-Core function in `trust-cg-codegen`
  could also reach it through the crate-private wrapper that built it, and
  the drift row missed both, because it counted only the constructor's name
  under `crates/`. `CoreQualificationFollows::caller_runs_core_qualification`
  is now a `pub const unsafe fn`. Its Safety section requires Core's
  qualification and address-free compilation checks before anything from
  the translation is emitted or run. The strict adapter's wrapper (renamed
  `translate_validated_core_module_under_core_qualification`) takes the
  token from its caller, and the one production construction is a private
  helper in `core_admission.rs`. The drift row pins, per file, every
  mention of the token, its constructor, the entry and both helpers in every
  Rust source of the checkout, tests and `fuzz/` included. A self-test
  plants the verifier's `transmute` forgery, a non-Core caller of the
  wrapper, a second caller of the helper, raw identifiers and a renaming
  import. (2) The drift scanner did not read text spliced in by `include!`;
  a non-test `include!` now fails every row. (3) The `trust-cg-lower` row
  pinned symbol-operand uses only in the two selectors; it now pins every
  file. (4) `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` left 24 scratch directories in
  `/tmp` per run from six older rows. Its scratch directories are now
  removed when a row ends normally, and kept when it panics.
- Product fix, from the sixth independent verifier round of the L02-P1 lift
  (the fifth round's repair holds). (1) Wrong code through the public API:
  the strict translation entries
  (`translate_module_strict_for_arch_with_tls_and_validation*` on a module,
  `translate_validated_module_strict_for_arch_with_tls_and_validation*` on a
  validation report) and `translate_function*` did not run the finder. Their
  LIR, prepared with `Pipeline::prepare_function_with_proofs` and emitted
  with `compile_module`, linked with a C driver to `my_rem(5,3)` = 42 for
  `frem` beside an Internal `fmod`, and to 42 for an i128 `sdiv` beside an
  Internal `__divti3`. Every public trust-ir translation entry now refuses
  such a module (`AdapterError::BackendSymbolShadowed`); the strict and
  per-function entries newly refuse the same modules the compatibility
  entries do (listed under the fifth round below). Closed-JIT Core
  admission translates through a new entry,
  `translate_validated_module_strict_for_core_qualification`, which skips
  the finder and takes a `CoreQualificationFollows` token that only Core
  admission constructs (a drift row pins the construction sites; the
  seventh round found this a convention and made the constructor `unsafe`).
  A Linux
  row takes both modules through all four public routes and links and runs
  any object a route lets through (every route now refuses them; with the
  refusal mutated off, the row prints 42 and fails).
  `JitCompiler::compile_raw` and a `Pipeline` given LIR built by hand take
  functions without linkage; `LIMITATIONS.md` records that they are outside
  the finder. (2) The fifth round's Core rationale named the wrong check.
  Calls the backend makes below LIR (the i128 division helpers, an aggregate
  copy's `memcpy`, the stack protector's `__stack_chk_fail`) are refused at
  address-free compilation by `FixupOccurrenceMismatch`, which a new
  `core_jit_planning` row pins at O0, O2 and O3, with and without a
  same-named Internal body. `InterposableModuleFixup` is not reachable from
  a module: a by-name fixup that passed the occurrence checks names a
  declared import, and trust-ir validation keeps that name distinct from
  every definition. (3) The drift rows share one test-only scanner
  (`trust-cg-lower/src/source_scan.rs`). It counts a symbol-operand use
  however the enum is spelled (a type alias, `Self`, `<MachOperand>`, a raw
  identifier, a `macro_rules!` body) and `ExactModuleSymbol` with its
  accessor. A file declared both as production and as test code is scanned
  as production code. The `trust-cg-lower` and frame-lowering rows now read
  every file of their module trees; `isel/branch_compare.rs`,
  `adapter_bounds_assert.rs`, `frame/instruction_view.rs` and
  `frame/zero_storage.rs` were not scanned before. The Darwin gate's minimum
  for `core_jit_planning` is now 13, and the pinned sum is 1,435.
- Fix, from the fifth independent verifier round of the L02-P1 lift (no wrong
  code; the fourth round's repair holds, including a 47-name JIT sweep). (1)
  The `trust-cg-opt` drift row cut each file at its first `#[cfg(test)]` test
  module, so code after an out-of-line `mod tests;` near the top of six pass
  files, and after `reaching_const.rs`'s inline test module, was never
  scanned; its reader detector also missed a match-arm read. The row now
  walks the crate's module tree from `lib.rs`, treats only files declared
  under `#[cfg(test)]` as test code, lexes the rest (comments dropped,
  literals kept as tokens), removes each `#[cfg(test)]` item by its own
  bounds, and pins per file every use of `MachOperand::Symbol`,
  `X86ISelOperand::Symbol` and `.as_symbol` (it found two unclassified
  name-blind uses, in the x86-64 LICM and SROA passes); a self-test plants
  each shape and requires detection. The `trust-cg-lower` and frame-lowering
  scans now fail if code follows their files' test modules. (2) Core
  admission no longer runs the finder, so an exactly called Internal body
  named `memcpy` is admitted again, as it was before the fourth round. Core's
  proof-grade qualification refuses a call the adapter makes on its own (no
  source call origin), which a new `core_jit_planning` row pins for `frem`
  beside a module-local `fmod`. Its address-free compilation refuses a call
  made below LIR (`FixupOccurrenceMismatch`, pinned in the sixth round; this
  entry first named `InterposableModuleFixup`, which no module reaches). (3) The vectorizer's `calloc` match no longer accepts
  `_calloc`, a different C symbol. (4) The finder now also runs in every
  compatibility `trust_cg_lower::translate_module*` entry
  (`AdapterError::BackendSymbolShadowed`), replacing the adapter's AArch64
  ELF-only runtime-call refusal and its `ModuleLocalFunctionBinding` policy
  (the sixth round extends the refusal to the strict and per-function
  entries). The old refusal applied only under the AArch64 ELF object policy
  and only when the lowering emitted the runtime call. Newly refused at the
  compatibility entries, although they lowered there before (outside that
  case):
  - a module-local function named like one of the 29 names, whether a
    runtime call, an exact call or nothing calls it (for example an
    uncalled `internal fn @malloc`), and, under the default object policy,
    a module-local `fmod` or `fmodf` beside `frem`;
  - module-local data named like one of the 29 names or the selected
    personality (for example local data `free`);
  - External, weak, link-once and ODR data named like a listed routine or
    either EH personality (for example External data `fmod` beside `frem`,
    or `global @__gxx_personality_v0`).

  `Compiler::compile` has refused all of these since the fourth round. A
  leftover sentence fragment in `LIMITATIONS.md` is removed. (5)
  `LIMITATIONS.md` records that a source call named `memcpy`/`memmove`/
  `memset` gets the C library semantics by name, and that a constant-length
  copy of up to 32 bytes is expanded inline, as a hosted C compiler does,
  not as under `-ffreestanding`.
- Product fix, from the fourth independent verifier round of the L02-P1 lift
  (no wrong code from the third round's repairs; the defects below were all
  present at base `aceeb3bb6`). A definition named like a symbol the backend
  references or reads by name on its own received that reference beyond
  AArch64 ELF: in the Linux AArch64 JIT a module-local `fmod` received
  `frem`'s call (`my_rem(5,3)` returned 42 at O0 and O2), in AArch64 Mach-O
  objects `bl _fmod` bound the local `_fmod` (and O2 inlined its body), the
  Darwin sin/cos merge's `__sincos_stret` call bound a local function or
  datum of that name, and x86-64 Mach-O branched into local data named
  `fmod`, `__divti3`, `memcpy`, `memset` or `malloc`. One finder,
  `trust_cg_lower::backend_symbol_shadow`, now runs before lowering in
  `Compiler::compile` on every target and in `Compiler::compile_module_to_jit`
  (and, after the fifth round, in every compatibility `translate_module*`
  entry; the fifth round took it back out of Core admission). It refuses a
  module-local function named
  like a listed symbol (`ModuleLocalFunctionShadowsRuntimeSymbol`, renamed
  from `AotModuleLocalFunctionShadowsRuntimeSymbol`), module-local data named
  like a listed symbol or the selected personality, and any other data
  definition named like a listed routine or either EH personality
  (`DataShadowsBackendSymbol`, renamed from
  `AotModuleLocalDataShadowsBackendSymbol`). The `RuntimeSymbol` list grows
  from 27 to 29 with `__sincos_stret` (emitted by the sin/cos merge) and

  satisfy that name match). It now covers the x86-64 selector, whose runtime
  names draw from it, and the `trust-cg-opt` passes, which a new drift row
  scans (its coverage is corrected in the fifth round below). A data-definition
  predicate, `is_data_definition`, has a drift row against the object-global
  mapping. Newly refused, on every target and in the JIT, although they
  compiled at the base: modules defining a module-local function or datum
  named like any of the 29 names (for example `internal fn @fmod` beside
  `frem`, `internal fn @__sincos_stret`, local data `memcpy`), External,
  weak, link-once and ODR data definitions named like a listed routine or an
  EH personality. (The fourth round also refused an exactly called Internal
  body named `memcpy` in Core admission; the fifth round reverted that false
  refusal.) A Linux JIT row executes the verifier's module
  (refused, or `my_rem(5,3)` = 2). The documentation's claim that the x86-64
  selector already refused a call to data was true only for x86-64 ELF and is
  corrected, and the merge's refusal of a leaf-only input beside a
  module-local personality is recorded as a known conservative false refusal.
  The Darwin gate's minimums are now 26 for `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` and
  6 for `jit_external_symbol_resolution_policy`, and the pinned sum is 1,433.
- Product fix, from the third independent verifier round of the L02-P1 lift
  (no wrong code found in the second round's repairs; two of the findings

  exception-handling structure gives every function an FDE under its one

  refused before lowering (now `DataShadowsBackendSymbol`), the

  read-back check (`AotCodeReferenceReachesData`) refuses a

  refused although they compiled or merged at the base: AArch64 modules
  defining module-local data named like a `RuntimeSymbol` name or the
  selected personality; on AArch64 ELF, through the new read-back check,

  data") and External and weak data `__gxx_personality_v0` in an EH module
  (the `DW.ref` slot rule), which Mach-O still accepted until the fourth
  round; and merges of any input with bodied functions beside another

- Product fix, from two independent verifier rounds of the L02-P1 lift. The
  first round found three wrong bindings. Two of them, (1) and (3), compiled
  to wrong code at the base. The third, (2), produced a wrong merged module
  at the base, which `Compiler::compile` refused until the lift. The second
  round found the first repair of (2) incomplete and the first repair of (3)
  broader than needed; both are reworked here. (1) A personality the module
  defines module-locally was reached through the shared weak
  `DW.ref.<personality>` slot. With two such objects in one link, one
  object's frames ran the other object's personality. It now gets an
  object-local slot, as GCC does for a `static` personality, and a new Linux
  control runs two such objects through GNU ld, gold and LLD in both link
  orders. (2) `merge_modules` resolves all inputs' names in one namespace,
  so a module-local function definition satisfied another input's
  declaration of the same name and captured another input's `SymbolAddr`
  naming it. The second verifier measured `b_ptr`, `b_callp`, `b_tbl` and
  `b_tbl_call` at 201 merged against 301 separately compiled. The merge now
  renames such a definition apart (`<name>.merge.<input>`) with every
  reference in its own input, and an independent walk and an exact inverse
  check each renaming. It also refuses inputs whose exception-handling
  frames would get a different personality merged than separately. (3) A
  call the backend makes by name reached a module-local function of that
  name: `frem` with a module-local `fmod` returned 42 at O0 and O2. On
  AArch64 ELF a module-local function named like one of the 27 runtime
  symbols of `trust_cg_lower::RuntimeSymbol` is refused before lowering.
  That list is the one the adapter, the AArch64 instruction selector and
  frame lowering draw their runtime names from, with source-scan drift rows.
  A runtime call the lowering itself emits is also refused when the module
  defines its name locally. The post-emission binding check also refuses a
  versioned spelling of a module-local function's name that the module does
  not itself declare, a non-local alias of the body, a relocation reaching
  the body through a non-local symbol, a synthesized data slot holding its
  address under a replaceable label, and a text reference to a module-local
  function no function body references (a per-function rule, silent when
  any body references it). The adapter's exact-binding sites read the
  shared module-local predicate, with a drift row. Now refused although
  they compiled or merged at the base: on AArch64 ELF, a module defining a
  module-local function named in the `RuntimeSymbol` list (`memcpy`,
  `memmove`, `memset`, `fmod`, `fmodf`, the eight i128 conversion helpers,
  the four i128 division helpers, `_Unwind_Resume`, `__stack_chk_fail`,
  `__stack_chk_guard`, `malloc`, `free`, `__rust_alloc`, `__rust_dealloc`
  and the three Clean RC entries) unless it called the function or took its
  `FnDef` address, which the base refused anyway; and a merge in which
  another input names a module-local EH personality, in which a `SymbolAddr`
  names another input's module-local global, or in which inputs with
  exception-handling frames select different personalities. Now merged
  although the base refused them as duplicate definitions: inputs that each
  define a function of one name when at least one is module-local.
  Module-local functions named like other library routines (`printf`,
  `puts`, `sqrt`, `log`, ...) compile as before. Documentation overclaims
  about what the pre-lift refusals covered, what "binding authority"
  requires and what the text-reference rule catches were corrected. A `pic`
  EH module with an external personality still could not be linked into a
  shared object by GNU ld or LLD (a weak default-visibility `DW.ref` slot;
  the L02-P6 closure-audit residual repair above makes the slot hidden), and
  a module that exports its own global named `DW.ref.<personality>`
  overrides other objects' slots; both are recorded in `LIMITATIONS.md`.
- Product change (L02-P1): on AArch64 ELF, `Compiler::compile` now compiles
  a direct call to, and every address form of, a bodied `Internal`/`Private`
  function. It used to refuse both on every target
  (`AotDirectModuleFunctionBindingUnsupported`,
  `AotStaticFunctionIdentityBindingUnsupported`), so no source call or
  `FnDef`/closure address could reach an `STB_LOCAL` function, and a C
  `static` function or a Rust private item could not be compiled as one. (A
  `SymbolAddr` naming one, a backend call by its name and a personality of its
  name already reached one, uncounted by the census.) The AArch64
  ELF emitters already bound such a function `STB_LOCAL` and resolved every
  text fixup and data slot through one name map whose entry for it is that
  definition; module validation makes names unique. One predicate,
  `Compiler::object_binds_module_local_functions`, lifts the two refusals and
  the adapter's withheld static-call refusal for that object path only.
  Mach-O, x86-64 and RISC-V keep them. The lift is backed by a check of the
  emitted bytes: every symbol spelling a module-local function must be a
  defined `STB_LOCAL` `STT_FUNC`, and no relocation may name such a name
  with another binding. A fresh object that fails it is not cached, and a
  cached one is re-checked (`AotModuleLocalFunctionBindingViolated`). A
  static-call candidate through such an address stays an indirect call.
  New object rows cover O0-O3, `static`/`pie`/`pic`, the sequential and
  parallel emitters, function and explicit sections, unique names and the
  refusals off AArch64 ELF. Two Linux controls run two modules, each with its
  own Internal or Private `helper`, beside a C object defining a global
  `helper`, through `run_link` (GNU ld), gold and LLD. Each module reaches
  only its own helper through direct calls, local and global function
  pointers and address takings, and objdump shows each module's call
  branching to its own local helper. With each module in its own
  `run_link` shared library, loaded together, an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer
  reaches none of them; with an External helper it takes over every
  reference to it. gcc twins built from `static` C functions print the same
  results. Mutation controls: a writer that binds the helper `STB_GLOBAL`, or
  relocates it against an undefined global twin, fails the post-emission
  check; with the check and the tests' own object checks off, the native
  controls still fail (a link with three global `helper` definitions, a
  PC-relative reference GNU ld will not put in a shared object, or every
  call reaching the C global helper). Widening the predicate to x86-64 ELF or to Mach-O fails the
  predicate unit row and the off-ELF refusal pins.
- x86-64 bridge, the capability half of the one-lane wide-pointer boundary
  guard (one census, 109 → 62, 47 roots gone, zero new or moved;
  `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` 23 → 2, `[TCG-RET-ABI]` 26 → 0): the `repr(transparent)`
  newtype chain over a slice / `str` fat pointer — `NonNull<[T]>`,
  `NonNull<str>`, `Unique<[T]>`, the bare `*const [T] is !null` pattern type —
  by value in a signature takes the SAME two-lane `{ data, len }` boundary
  slot `&[T]` has. ONE decision function
  (`transparent_wide_slice_newtype_layout`: the peeled chain, rustc's
  `ScalarPair` repr, 16 bytes at 8) is consulted in lockstep by the signature
  classifier (`fat_ptr_or_memory_aggregate_layout`), the slot classifier
  (`memory_backed_local_layout`), the memory-backed assignment dispatch and the
  slot-pointer call-argument branch, so the declaration, the entry block and
  every call site cannot answer differently for one type; `check_param_abi` /
  `[TCG-RET-ABI]` still compare the declared lanes against rustc's `FnAbi`.
  The IN-BODY data-only model is untouched: a scalarized `NonNull<[T]>` (the

  its data pointer plus side-table length, and only a whole copy of an

  transmute out of one is slotted. The slice `Transmute` lane now checks the
  SOURCE slot is a two-lane image before reading its lanes. Every GENERIC

  review of the first build measured three silent wrong-code paths (a
  deref-store through `&mut NonNull<[T]>` writing one lane, a raw store into a
  local the scalar-cell pass and the slot pass both claimed, a closure-call
  element pushed as one value); `memory_scalar_leaf_ty`,
  `memory_deref_store_target`, the scalar-cell pass and the closure lane now
  refuse them, and `m142` pins each (`torn`, `rawstore`, `clo`). A borrow of a
  newtype field binds the field's address (`Location::file`'s
  `&self.filename`, which the choke point had briefly refused). The predicted
  one-lane write of a `NonNull<[T]>` struct field measured whole
  (`bridge_corpus/nonnull_holder_field.rs`, exit 77 with a poisoned stack,
  strict at O0–O3). `Box<[T]>` (the
  `owned_box` lang struct is not `repr(transparent)`) keeps the guard as
  argument and as return at O0 and O2 (`m142` pins it). Measured cross-backend
  in all four rlib×bin combinations at O0–O3 for 9 `NonNull` shapes (144
  cells, zero mismatches, `m141`) and by
  `bridge_corpus/m143_nonnull_slice_boundary.rs` (exit 52 at O0–O3, strict).
  OPEN when this landed and CLOSED by the entry above, exposed by the same
  matrix and pre-existing (the previously pushed dylib shows it for a plain
  `&[u8]`): a fat-pointer ARGUMENT at
  register exhaustion with exactly one integer register left
  (`fn f(a, b, c, d, e: u64, s: &[u8])`) — rustc's `PassMode::Pair` puts
  `data` in R9 and `len` on the stack, the bridge's aggregate placement puts
  the whole pair on the stack; the backends disagree in both directions.
  Both lanes on the stack (six scalars before) agree.
- Product fix (the ninth L02-P10 closure audit, at `0996df987`): two routes
  the Linux link driver installed with every FDE truncated, and five
  residuals.
  - **Registration in every spelling.** An input that called libgcc's
    registration function through a versioned reference (`.symver`,
    `__register_frame_info@GLIBC_2.0`) or a `--wrap` alias
    (`__real___register_frame_info`) was taken to register nothing, so an
    LLD `--no-pie` program whose renamed `.eh_frame` it registered, linked
    with `-Wl,-Map=/dev/null`, was installed and backtraced one frame. Names
    are now normalised (`@`, `@@`, `@@@` versions; `__real_` and `__wrap_`)
    in objects and in shared objects' imports; a `--defsym` alias of a
    registration function, and a linker script that names one (`-T`
    scripts, scripts given as `-Wl` operands, which LLD's and gold's traces
    do not name, and traced scripts, now read whole), register frames; a
    script that `INCLUDE`s another may. A staged image's own imports are
    read as the loader binds them, whatever spelling reached them.
  - **A map that does not place the input refuses the image whatever its
    inputs.** An in-section symbol assignment is enough to make LLD's map
    unable to place the `.eh_frame` pieces, and an image whose inputs
    registered nothing was then installed unchecked: two LLD programs whose
    frames a `DT_NEEDED`-only library and a `dlsym` caller registered at run
    time were installed with 13 FDEs truncated. Such an output section must
    now be read whole already (a section named `.eh_frame`, or the one
    `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` locates), and a map that was written and cannot be
    read refuses the image too. The `dlsym`/`DT_NEEDED` boundary is reached
    only when the link wrote no map the driver reads.
  - **Diagnostics.** `classify_linker_stderr` kept one unnamed diagnostic
    per kind, so gold's refusal of trust-cg's own `ADRP` (`far_word.o:function
    tcg_read_far:(.text+0x0): error: relocation overflow in ...`) was
    dropped behind `crti.o`'s. Each place is now kept, gold's function (and
    the function of gold's `too far from TP` refusal, from its next line)
    is the subject, and the native window controls require the trust-cg
    access by name. A complete linker script that puts `.debug_str` into an
    allocated section at 4 GiB is refused by GNU ld, LLD and gold (a new
    `ABS32` control; `--section-start` does not move LLD's or gold's
    non-allocated `.debug_str`).
  - **False refusals.** Every `--static` link whose output name or
    directory held `%`, or whose name was 252-255 bytes, was refused as
    unproven. The driver's map is now `link.map` in the stage (a fresh
    temporary directory when the stage's path holds `%`).
  - **Loader crash.** LLD's dynamic `-nostdlib --no-pie` image with a
    `PT_INTERP` and no `PT_DYNAMIC`, which glibc's loader faults on, is
    refused as `[TCG-LINK-INTERP-NO-DYNAMIC]`.
  - **Evidence.** The Linux floor runs its three-linker targets with
    `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`/`TCG_REQUIRE_GOLD` (`TARGET_ENVIRONMENT`). The
    completion plan's matrix counts are corrected (62 of 66 ordinary links
    installed and ran; 4 are refused by design), and LIMITATIONS names the
    foreign LSDA TType entries it does not read.
  - **After its verifier.** Two scripts LLD read were not read by the
    driver, and LLD programs with 82 truncated FDEs were installed: a
    script operand with a control byte in a comment (an operand counted as
    a script only when its first 64 bytes were text), and a `-T` script
    found in a later `-L` directory than the `-L,=<dir>` one LLD used.
    Files are now classified as the linkers classify them (ELF, archive and
    LLVM bitcode by their magic, anything else a script), and every path a
    link's options lead the linker to is found as it finds it: `=` and
    `$SYSROOT` against the sysroot, relative paths in the current directory
    or every library directory (the C driver's own among them), `-l` as
    `lib<name>.so`/`.a`, following `INCLUDE`, `INPUT()`, `GROUP()` and
    `AS_NEEDED()`. What is not found or cannot be parsed may register.
    `LinkDiagnostic` gains `function` (the function a gold or LLD place

    gold's range failures at different places each print a line. An

    `--static` link given `-Wl,-Bdynamic`, which faults) is refused as
    `[TCG-LINK-NEEDED-NO-INTERP]`.
  - **After its round-2 verifier: the driver's own map, always.** Eight
    more LLD routes got a registering script past that reading (a
    `.deplibs` library, a script's `INPUT` in the script's own directory,
    `-sysroot=`, a joined `-L=<dir>` and a relative `=dA` under a sysroot,

- Product fix (the eighth L02-P10 closure audit, at `9a9eda112`): the Linux
  link driver's `.eh_frame` check found `.eh_frame` by section name or
  through `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME`, but libgcc reads a static executable's frames
  where `crtbeginT.o` registers them, whatever the output section is
  called. An LLD static executable whose linker script renamed the output
  `.eh_frame` (`.ehx`), linked with `-Wl,--no-eh-frame-hdr` and `.text` at
  `0xd0000000`, was installed with all 916 FDEs truncated and aborted in
  `_Unwind_Backtrace`.
  - **The link map.** Every staged Linux link now asks for the linker's map
    (`-Xlinker -Map=<staged image>.map`, before every `-Wl` group), and
    every `.eh_frame` input piece the GNU ld 2.42, gold 2.42 or LLD 22 map
    places is decoded too: in a renamed section, merged into `.rodata`,
    stripped (`-s`) or without section headers. A user's `-Map` replaces
    the driver's and is read in its place, and left. A static executable
    whose map was not written (`-Wl,-M`, a linker that ignores `-Map`), is
    unreadable, or cannot show where the input lies (LLD 22 prints the
    pieces from the start of their output section, so pieces sharing one
    with other input are not located) is refused as unproven by name. The
    audit's layout through LLD is refused as `[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-WINDOW]`
    and its near twins backtrace through all three linkers.
  - **Registration, not `PT_INTERP`.** The first cut required the map only
    in an `ET_EXEC` without `PT_INTERP`. Its independent verifier gave a
    `--static` link `-Wl,-Bdynamic`: the image then has a `PT_INTERP`,
    `crtbeginT.o` still registers its frames, and two LLD layouts without
    a readable map (`.eh_frame` merged into `.rodata`, or renamed with
    `-Map=/dev/null`) were installed with every registered FDE truncated.
    An image now needs a readable map when it registers frames: a static
    executable, or one whose link loaded an input that references a
    libgcc registration function it does not define or takes the address
    of its own `.eh_frame` input (as `crtbeginT.o` does), or whose inputs
    cannot all be read, whatever its kind. The inputs are read only when
    the answer matters, and overlapping FDEs in such an image are read as
    a registered search reads them. A zero-size thread-local at the end of
    a 2^32-byte block now counts for the `TPREL` refusal (`>=`), and GNU
    ld's `-M=<file>`/`--M=<file>`/`-Ma` spellings of `-Map` are read. The
    second verifier found the trace read only for relocatable objects (a
    shared object whose constructor calls `__register_frame_info`, linked
    with `-Map=/dev/null`, was installed): a shared object is now read for
    an imported registration function, an object that exports an address
    in its `.eh_frame` input registers frames, and LLVM bitcode, GCC LTO IR
    and any other format the driver does not read may (fail closed), while
    archives and linker scripts, whose contents the trace names, register
    nothing themselves. The third verifier found those imports read from
    the `.dynsym` section header, trusting its entry size and extent, so a
    library whose header gave 48-byte entries or too few entries was read
    as importing nothing while it registered frames at run time. Imports
    are now read through the dynamic section as the loader reads them (the
    undefined `DT_SYMTAB` symbols its `DT_JMPREL`, `DT_RELA` and `DT_REL`
    relocations bind), and a dynamic section, table, symbol or name the
    loader would read otherwise makes the library unreadable (may
    register). The native row's library now really registers the
    program's frames, linked `--no-as-needed`; a library `--as-needed`
    drops from `DT_NEEDED` is still taken to register (a known false
    refusal), and a library reached only as another library's `DT_NEEDED`
    is not read.
  - **GNU ld's truncated TLS relaxation.** GNU ld 2.42 relaxes an
    executable's initial-exec and TLS-descriptor accesses to a local-exec
    `MOVZ`/`MOVK` pair and writes a `TPREL` of 2^32 or more truncated
    without a diagnostic. An executable whose thread-local block (the
    16-byte TCB aligned up to `p_align`, then `p_memsz`, its end included)
    reaches 2^32 is refused (`[TCG-LINK-TLS-TPREL-UNPROVEN]`), and gold's `TLS variable
    referred by reloc N is too far from TP` is classified
    `relocation-out-of-range`.
  - **Evidence.** The direct `ADRP`, `ABS32` and `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12`
    overflow controls now run through GNU ld, LLD and gold, with a new
    `JUMP26` veneer control and a `TPREL` control. The 128 GiB read-back
    control measures its peak RSS with `wait4` instead of skipping without
    `/usr/bin/time`. The documented `--no-eh-frame-hdr` boundary is
    corrected: static executables through GNU ld and LLD still unwind
    through the registered search, while dynamic images find no FDEs (a
    throw terminates) through all three linkers.
- Product fix: the Linux link driver's `.eh_frame` check now refuses
  truncated pointers that land in other code or data, where the image
  shows it. The 2026-09-24 closure audit of L02-P10 found that the check
  refused a `pc_begin`, personality or LSDA pointer only when it resolved
  outside executable or allocated memory. LLD 22.1.6 and gold 2.42 write a
  `PREL32` value in `[2^31, 2^32)` truncated:
  - With trust-cg's code moved 2^32 above a 256 KiB function, both linkers
    installed a program whose FDEs describe that function.
  - With an LSDA moved 2^32 above the first load segment, LLD installed a
    C++ program that dies at its throw.

  Three rules close this:
  - **Wrap alias.** A pointer whose 4-byte (2-byte) field also gives
    another file-backed address 2^32 (2^16) away, where the pointer must
    lie, is `unclassified` (`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]`). That covers
    code for a `pc_begin`, contents for a personality slot or LSDA, and
    another section start for `eh_frame_ptr`.
  - **Hidden FDEs.** A live FDE that a lookup by start would miss is an
    observed failure (`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-WINDOW]`). A lookup takes the
    greatest start at or below a pc, and the last table entry among equal
    starts, so an FDE is missed when another begins inside its range, or
    when a narrower FDE is taken at its start.
  - **Where these come from.** An independent verifier found the second
    case: an empty function's zero-range FDE, written truncated into
    `middle`, hid `middle`'s FDE, and a throw through it terminated. The
    same review found that counting `.bss` as an alias region refused a
    correct C++ program with a 5 GiB `.bss`; only file-backed memory counts
    now.

  On this host, no ELF image has an aliasing pointer. The hidden-FDE rule
  finds 14 Qt6 libraries bundled with NVIDIA Nsight, linked by LLD 17. In
  each, LLD's table keeps one entry per start and names a zero-range FDE for
  a function's start, so libgcc finds no unwind information for that
  function. In `libQt6Qml.so.6` that function is
  `QV4::Compiler::Codegen::visit(QQmlJS::AST::ExportDeclaration *)`, which
  a throw can pass through.
- Product fix, from a fourth independent verifier of the `.eh_frame`
  refusals, which found two soundness regressions in the third repair:
  - **No table.** Without section headers and without a table, a walk that
    stopped at a record it took as foreign was accepted, but libgcc reads
    on to a zero length. GNU ld writes no table when it cannot parse an
    input `.eh_frame`, and installed a library with a 64-bit record whose
    throw aborts. Such a walk must now reach a terminator.
  - **Static narrow FDEs.** In a static executable the registered search
    returns any FDE that covers the pc, so a narrower FDE with a range that
    begins with a wider one is now undecided whatever the table names. An
    LLD static program with one terminated at its throw.
- Product fix, from a third independent verifier of the `.eh_frame`
  refusals, which found no soundness break but three false refusals from
  the second repair:
  - **Where the no-header walk ends.** It now ends at the first record that
    is not `.eh_frame`'s: one past the segment or into a following
    `.eh_frame_hdr`, one with a 64-bit length, or an FDE naming no CIE the
    walk read. GNU ld puts `.gcc_except_table` or `.sframe` right after
    `.eh_frame` and writes no terminator for a `-nostdlib` link, so a
    `-z nosectionheader` image with an LSDA had been refused. A table entry
    past where such a walk ended leaves the image unproven.
  - **The table decides zero-range ties again, static or not.** libgcc's
    registered-FDE search checks each range, never takes a zero-range FDE,
    and falls back to the table on a miss. In a static executable a hidden
    FDE is refused as unproven, not as an observed failure, since the
    registered search may run first and find it. (A fourth verifier
    narrowed this further; see the next entry.)
  - **LLD's placeholder.** LLD writes a zero-filled `.eh_frame_hdr` with no
    `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` when a linker script discards `.eh_frame`. It is now
    ignored.
  - **Wording.** The documents now say what the walk bound, the static-link
    flag and the tie rule actually do.
- Product fix, from a second independent verifier of the `.eh_frame`
  refusals:
  - **Without section headers.** Every record from `eh_frame_ptr` is now
    read, even with a table, to a terminator or to the end of
    `.eh_frame`'s segment (or `.eh_frame_hdr`). `-z nosectionheader` had let
    an FDE that LLD's table drops go unseen.
  - **gold `--static`.** A static Linux link now passes `--eh-frame-hdr`.
    gold 2.42's static C++ programs registered no unwind information
    (`crtbeginT.o`'s `__EH_FRAME_BEGIN__` resolved to 0), so every throw
    aborted.
  - **Undecided ties.** A tie that no table entry decides (a start the table
    does not locate, or any tie in a static executable, whose registered
    FDEs libgcc searches first) is now `unclassified`
    (`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]`), not an observed failure.
  - **Corrections.** The lookup the rule models is libgcc's; LLVM libunwind
    falls back to a linear scan. The hidden 0x20-byte FDE in
    `libQt6Core.so.6` is the leaf `QProcess::readData`'s, not the empty
    `QProcess::setupChildProcess`'s.
- Diagnostics: gold's `relocation overflow in R_AARCH64_*` and LLD's
  `improper alignment for relocation R_AARCH64_*` are now classified as
  `relocation-out-of-range`; they were `unclassified`.
- Test coverage: the native `CALL26` veneer control links through GNU ld,
  LLD and gold, with `.text` pinned. Without the pin, LLD placed `.text`
  next to the callee, so its leg never crossed 128 MiB. Each leg asserts the
  distance and that no `BL` branches to the callee directly.
- Product fix (L02-P6): under `pic`, a hidden or protected function's
  address came from the GOT, because the adapter read every function as
  default-visible when it chose the address form. It is now PC-relative
  (`ADRP`+`ADD`), like hidden and protected data. The inliner and structural
  purity inference also treated every non-local function as preemptible
  under `pic`. They now let a strong hidden or protected body be used. Weak
  and link-once ones stay excluded, because another object may replace them
  at static link. The decision had five copies that disagreed: data
  addresses, `FnDef` addresses, raw `SymbolAddr` addresses, the emitters'
  `pic` check, and the inliner and purity rules. They now all call
  `RelocationModel::definition_is_preemptible`. The weak and link-once
  exclusion also had two copies, the inliner's and purity's. Both now call
  `definition_is_link_replaceable`. Purity applies it on every target. The
  inliner applies it on AArch64 only, where `Weak` and `LinkOnce`
  definitions are emitted weak. Unit rows pin both scopes and purity's use
  of visibility. Internal/Private functions are unchanged:
  `Compiler::compile` still refuses a direct call to one or a materialized
  address of one on every target. The `SymbolAddr` copy also
  addressed an `AvailableExternally` global with an initializer
  PC-relatively and an initializer-less `Internal` one through the GOT,
  unlike `GlobalAddr`. It now uses the same helper. Protected data stays
  PC-relative. On the Linux host GNU ld 2.42, gold and LLD 22 refuse the copy
  relocation that would move it. GNU ld resolves a GOT slot for it with
  `R_AARCH64_RELATIVE`, so GCC's GOT form binds to the same copy. A
  host-neutral row checks the adapter, the emitter check and the inliner
  against the predicate for 51 relocation-model, linkage and visibility
  rows. A new Linux control runs a library with default, protected and hidden
  functions and data at O0-O3 through GNU ld, gold and LLD. It checks the
  object and the linked library's relocations, `.dynsym`, GOT slots and PLT
  branches. It also runs an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer and a non-PIE
  copy-relocation executable. Only the default references interpose, and
  every linker refuses to copy the protected word.
- Product fix: the Linux link driver no longer reads a staged image larger
  than 1 GiB whole for its image checks. A `--static --nostdlib --no-pie`
  link through LLD with `.far` placed at `0x2000000000` wrote a 128 GiB
  sparse image, and reading it back killed the CLI for memory (exit 137),
  leaving its `.tcg-link-*` staging directory. Such an image is now read as
  the ranges its checks read, run after run until they ask for nothing more,
  so each check sees exactly the bytes of the whole file. The audit's link
  completes and its program runs; a 2 GiB twin measured 2.03 GiB peak RSS
  before and 38 MB after. Such an image is refused with the new
  `[TCG-LINK-IMAGE-UNCHECKED]` (`unclassified`, naming the cause) when the
  ranges its checks read come to more than 1 GiB or still grow after 64
  runs, and its staging directory is removed.
- Robustness fixes in the linked-image checks, found by the read-back's
