  third independent verifier: three costs grew with a product a hostile
  image controls, and no step bound covered them; the repair's verifier
  found a fourth. Timings are release CLIs
  on the Linux AArch64 host before and after, each image copied into place
  by a stand-in linker.
  - **Symbol names.** Each symbol's name was read to its NUL: 1,000 symbols
    over a 64 MiB string table without NULs took 17.6 s, now 0.06 s. A
    wanted name is compared at its own length and the byte after it, and a
    function name for a diagnostic is read to at most 4 KiB.
  - **The `.eh_frame` pointer search.** Each FDE's search visited every
    executable span: 100,000 FDEs over as many sections took 11.8 s, now
    0.09 s. It takes no step when the pointer and the spans lie within one
    window of its field, as for every 4-byte pointer of the host's 6,626
    images (whose allocated memory spans at most 685 MiB). Otherwise it
    takes the fewer of one step per span and one per candidate address,
    counted toward 16,777,216 steps, past which the image is refused as an
    unproven `.eh_frame`. 100,000 sections spread 4 GiB apart installed
    after 11.9 s before and are refused in 0.09 s now; 3,000 such sections
    still install.
  - **Same-start FDE groups.** Each group scanned the whole `.eh_frame_hdr`
    table: 200,000 groups took 5.4 s, now 0.15 s. The table's last entry
    for each start is looked up in a map built once.
  - **Zero-filled `.eh_frame_hdr` sections.** Without a `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME`,
    each section of that name was scanned whole for LLD's zero-filled
    placeholder: 1,000 headers naming the same 64 MiB of zeros installed
    after 17.6 s (found by the repair's own verifier). The zeros scanned
    before a non-zero byte are now counted on their own, at most
    16,777,216 of them. That image is refused as an unproven `.eh_frame`
    in 0.06 s, and 16 MiB of placeholders, alone or before a real table,
    still install.
  - **Headroom.** The host image with the most dynamic relocation targets
    (an Electron executable, 595,711) names about 7 times fewer than
    `CHECK_ITEM_BOUND`, not the 11 times the largest library was said to.
- Robustness fixes in the linked-image checks, found by the read-back's
  independent verifier. A `.eh_frame_hdr` table was allocated for its
  declared entry count before any entry was read: `u64::MAX` panicked
  (capacity overflow) and smaller counts aborted the allocation. Offsets
  near 2^64 in the `IFUNC` relocations between `__rela_iplt_start` and
  `__rela_iplt_end`, in `elf_function_at`'s symbol reads and in
  `PT_DYNAMIC` overflowed (debug-build panics; release wrapped to a small
  offset). 1,000 relocation-section headers naming one 8 MiB table held
  350 million targets (a 19 GB allocation aborted). A relocation table that
  the dynamic section and a section header, or two headers, name alike
  (type, offset, size, entry size) is now read once. Each of the two layout
  checks holds at most 4,194,304 of each of section headers, relocation
  targets (all its tables together), dynamic-section entries, `.eh_frame`
  records, `.eh_frame_hdr` entries and GOT-base addresses, takes at most
  16,777,216 steps through relocation entries (`R_AARCH64_NONE` included),
  symbol tables and `.eh_frame` records, and copies at most 64 MiB of
  section and 64 MiB of dynamic-symbol names; an image with more than one
  `PT_DYNAMIC` is not read (loaders disagree on which applies). Such an
  image makes the check unreadable or unproven by name, and is refused: an
  unreadable GOT layout now whatever the inputs
  (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNCHECKED]`), since a linker-written PLT
  could not be ruled out in it (a well-formed image whose PLT slot lay
  8 GiB away was installed once its tables passed the target bound). A
  PLT with more than eight slots out of reach names eight and counts the
  rest (160,000 took 33 s and printed 107 MB). A GOT-base symbol defined at
  more than eight addresses lists eight. A staging directory is removed
  when a check's panic unwinds through `run_link`.
- Verifier hardening (L04-P11): the function verifier no longer promotes
  AArch64 register copies as covered-elsewhere. `MovR`, `MOVWrr`, `MOVXrr`,
  `FmovFprFpr`, `FmovFprGpr` and `FmovGprFpr` were exempt whatever their
  operands, and whether or not the ENC-5 decode check ran. Each copy now
  binds the registered decoded-word obligation of its form
  (`aarch64_value_decode_proofs`), proved once on the form's canonical word;
  ENC-5 alone checks each instruction's own word, and proof certificates do
  not record that it ran. The zero-source copies a zero-sized aggregate
  argument produces (`MOVXrr Xn, XZR`) and the FEAT_FP16 `FMOV Wd, Hn` /
  `FMOV Hd, Wn` bind their own forms; any other shape (a copy to SP or to a
  zero register, X<->H, half-precision or cross-width FMOVs, FMOVs naming the
  zero register, malformed operands) stays unverified, is refused by its
  exact shape and blocks proof-required promotion. Without the AY solver a
  bound copy is credited `Statistical`, so proof-required compiles with
  copies now depend on AY. `MOVWrr`/`MOVXrr`, which
  `pipeline::lower_copies` emits for every post-allocation GPR copy, had been
  excluded from the coverage gate as "never selected". They gain their own
  typed forms (width fixed by the opcode), captured encoder words and twelve
  refuting controls, ENC-5 checks their words, and they enter the
  denominator. The gate also counts the emitted `SubsRI` (the looped stack
  probe's counter decrement, formerly listed as never selected) as a deferred
  row and `AddTprelHi12`/`AddTprelLo12` (local-exec TLS) as deferred rows
  too, since the second review below: AArch64 172/282 -> 174/287 with 113
  deferred rows, static corpus 2,422 -> 2,431 obligations (the typed copy
  obligations are content-identical to the untyped ones). BR/BLR, RET, CBZ/CBNZ/TBZ/TBNZ and
  alignment NOPs stay covered-elsewhere, as the gate allowlists them.
- Verifier hardening (L04-P11, second review): `NeonOrrV` is no longer
  credited for the whole opcode. The `ORR Vd.16B, Vn.16B, Vn.16B` copy that
  post-allocation copy lowering emits for every H, S, D and Q copy binds a new
  decoded-word form (`MOV Vd.16B, Vn.16B`: captured words, seven refuting
  controls, and ENC-5 checks every emitted copy word); the three-register 16B
  ORR binds the lanewise obligation and ENC-5 checks its word's fields; every
  other shape is refused, including the 8B ORR of the V64 vector OR, which is
  therefore no longer promoted. The TLSLE TPREL adds are
  no longer credited: their obligations are relocation-arithmetic identities
  that bind no register, word or relocation site, and ENC-5 does not check the
  words. Both are deferred rows, and the function verifier refuses every
  instance, so neither instruction is promoted (in the reviewers' probes the
  local-exec functions were already refused for their frame pair, so no
  whole-compile verdict changed). NEON AND/EOR/BIC/NOT kept their opcode-wide
  lanewise credit; the third review below binds them like ORR, and lists the
  104 credited rows ENC-5 does not decode, not four. Documentation now states
  what a copy certificate proves: an
  identity over one canonical word's transcription (for `MOVXrr`,
  `x7 == 0 | (x7 << 0)`; the zero-source forms, `0 == 0 | (0 << 0)`); only
  ENC-5 checks each instance, and no certificate records it.
- Verifier hardening (L04-P11, third review): NEON AND, EOR, BIC and NOT are
  no longer credited for the whole opcode. Their lanewise obligations state
  the 16B arrangement, but ISel also emits them for `V64` (the 8B form), whose
  words were credited and allowlisted by ENC-5. All five bitwise opcodes now
  bind their obligation per instruction in the 16B shape only; ENC-5 decodes
  and field-checks that shape's word, and every 8B shape is refused by name.
  Virtual registers are numbered apart from physical operands, so a
  two-source ORR mixing them no longer reads as a copy in the pre-allocation
  verifier run. Disclosure: ENC-5 does not decode every emitted word. 167 of
  the 287 emitted AArch64 rows, including 104 of the 174 credited ones (88
  credited opcode-wide, 16 per instruction, as corrected by the fourth and
  fifth reviews), fall to its catch-all allowlist;
  LIMITATIONS.md lists them, a coverage test derives and pins the list, and
  ARCHITECTURE.md no longer says ENC-5 re-decodes every emitted instruction.
- Encoder and verifier hardening (L04-P11, fifth review): the AArch64
  encoder no longer reads a non-immediate operand as 0 in an immediate field.
  `LSL X0, X1, X2` given to the immediate form had encoded `MOV X0, X1` while
  the verifier credited it as a register shift; the encoder now returns an
  error (relocation targets stay placeholders for ADR/ADRP and the GOT/TLV
  loads), ENC-5 reports a mismatch, and the verifier refuses an
  immediate-form ALU instruction with a register third operand, and ADDS/SUBS
  or NEG with an extra operand. The coverage gate's representative for the
  immediate-form rows now carries an immediate. The ENC-5 disclosure
  classifies rows by verifying an operand-free instruction (88 opcode-wide,
  16 of them a degenerate X==X fallback, and 16 per instruction). A new
  derived inventory pins the 117 opcodes whose encoder does not read a
  trailing operand the verifier accepts; the encoder does not check arity,
  and LIMITATIONS.md lists that as an open gap. No emission site was found to
  produce any of the refused shapes (Linux floor, and an integration sweep
  of 455 targets).
- Verifier hardening (L04-P11, fourth review): register-register
  ADD/SUB/AND/ORR/EOR with an operand after the three registers is no longer
  credited. The encoder drops that operand and ENC-5 allowlisted any word for
  the shape; no emission site produces it. The ENC-5 disclosure now splits
  its 104 credited rows by the function verifier's per-instruction query (91
  opcode-wide, 13 per instruction, not 96 and 8), pins ENC-5's 30 named arm
  exits, and checks that the register-ALU arms decode the three-register
  shape. ARCHITECTURE.md, `docs/diagnostics.md` and one "Established" bullet
  of the closure ledger no longer say the decode checks re-decode every
  emitted instruction.
- Test coverage (L04-P11): `e2e_aarch64_switch` and
  `e2e_aarch64_indirect_call` run at O0-O3 (executed on the Linux floor host;
  the new tests are host-neutral but have not run on macOS). The switch
  target adds a 64-function selector-width and strategy matrix (i8-i64 and
  u8-u64 selectors; jump table, binary search and linear chain read back from
  the code words and, on Linux, from binutils `objdump`; block-argument edges;
  garbage upper argument bits on Linux) against a C `switch` oracle. The
  indirect-call target adds function-pointer tables (a relocated CG table and
  C tables), a call feeding a jump table, a switch choosing a call target,
  stack and mixed-class arguments, and values live across calls into C
  callees that overwrite X1-X17, V0-V7 and V16-V31 (not X18 or the
  caller-saved upper halves of V8-V15). The Linux floor gains
  per-target minimum passes (`TARGET_MINIMUM_PASSES`, 3 and 2 here); the
  Darwin floor's pins follow. Jump-table entry contents, the BR target
  binding and the link between the bounds check and the table size still
  have no instruction obligations. x86-64 `MovRI` is still exempted per
  instruction with no proof-grade forcing of its ENC-3 check (the x86 twin
  of this gap).
- Product fix: an explicit `x86_64-unknown-unknown` target no longer takes
  its object format from the host. `Compiler` emitted ELF for it on Linux,
  Mach-O on macOS and COFF on Windows. It is now refused on every host
  (`X86AotObjectFormatUnsupported`, target OS `unknown`), as
  `aarch64-unknown-unknown` already was. Only an architecture-only request
  derives its OS from the host. A unit row resolves the effective triple and
  x86-64 format of every explicit target for eleven host OS values and
  checks they are the same.
- Stale-test fix: two `trust-cg-llvm-import` tests that build only with
  `--features driver` had never run on Linux. `fp_e2e`'s f16 row compiled
  for the host-derived target, so it relied on Apple's AOT contract, which
  admits FEAT_FP16. Every `fp_e2e` program now compiles for explicit
  `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` targets. The f16 row
  uses the explicit `AArch64IsaProfile::FP16` profile and checks for
  `FADD Hd, Hn, Hm`, and a new twin pins the generic Linux baseline's
  refusal of the f16 constant by name. The `ws2_stack_protector_target`
  refusal for `aarch64-unknown-unknown` has been `[TCG-TARGET-ABI]` at ABI
  resolution on every host since the pipeline stopped defaulting unknown
  triples to Apple. It is no longer the canary refusal that named "Mach-O".
  The test now asserts the typed refusal, its exact text, the explicit
  target selection and the canary classifier's own refusal.
- Test coverage: the `trust-cg-llvm-import` driver integration tests now
  run their native legs on AArch64 Linux. There, 13 tests printed `skipping`
  and returned, which libtest counted as passes, and `casttest3_e2e` built no
  tests. Every native leg now compiles for the host's explicit triple (ELF
  `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` or Mach-O `aarch64-apple-darwin`), links with
  `cc` and runs the program. The container's own tools read the object:
  `otool`/`nm` for Mach-O, binutils `objdump`/`nm` for ELF. The in-tree Mach-O
  and ELF readers check both containers on every host. New ELF twins cover the
  printf string global (`.rodata`, a local `.str` object, an ADRP/ADD pair),
  the mutable byte globals (`.data` and `.bss`) and the stack-protected sieve.
  The sieve loads `__stack_chk_guard` through two
  `ADR_GOT_PAGE`/`LD64_GOT_LO12_NC` pairs and calls `__stack_chk_fail` by
  `CALL26`. With no `clang` on PATH, `intmm_o2_e2e` imports committed clang
  18.1.3 -O0 IR whose header must reproduce the test's C source. The host
  `cc` then builds the reference binary, and every reference must print the
  pinned output. `switch_e2e` compiles for both explicit triples and checks
  the container. On any host other than AArch64 Linux GNU or macOS, a native
  leg prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>`.
- Verifier hardening: the AArch64 view of the raw dataflow-integrity check
  (TV-3) accepted a fusion edge by its shape alone. It followed any recorded
  edge from an unwitnessed effect to a later instruction of the same source
  block that some non-pseudo machine instruction was stamped from. An
  independent probe edged a store through a pointer argument and a call to a
  plain add, and TV-3 reported nothing. The bit-reverse fold below is the
  only AArch64 edge producer, and it records only edges the tightened check
  admits. TV-3 now follows fusion edges only from a plain LIR `Store`, on
  every architecture: a call, atomic, fence, bulk-memory operation or
  volatile store needs a machine instruction stamped from itself. On AArch64
  the edge must also have the fold's shape: an `i32` or `i64` store to a
  declared stack slot (its address a `StackAddr` earlier in the block), a
  later `Bor` root in the same block that reads the slot back at the store's
  width after the store, and a non-pseudo `RBIT` of the store's width stamped
  from the root. The check covers that shape, not the slot's privacy. Unit
  rows cover the probe, a non-slot store beside a genuine fold, every other
  effect class in the store's place, a plain load's edge, and targets other
  than the `RBIT` root: an `ORR` witness, an `RBIT` of the other width or
  without operands, the read-back load, a root that ignores the slot or reads
  another slot, another width or only before the store, an undeclared slot,
  and backward and cross-block edges. An x86-64 row selects a v2i64 compare
  followed by an all-ones constant stack sequence: TV-3 still accepts the
  lane stores, which chain to the sequence anchor and on to the compare, and
  refuses a volatile store or a call in a lane store's position. With the old
  shape filter restored, three AArch64 rows fail; without the store-only
  rule, the cross-architecture row and the x86-64 row fail. Apart from the
  store-only rule, the x86-64 view still follows every recorded edge chain,
  with no block, direction or target check. Its producers are seven
  multi-instruction interceptors, which link each consumed instruction back
  to the sequence anchor, and cached or deferred vector values, which link
  forward or backward to the source that emits them. They share no single
  edge shape that the view could require, as the AArch64 view does.
  TV-3 also classified a `VolatileLoad` as a plain load, which may emit
  nothing, so a dropped volatile read went unreported on both architectures.
  It now requires a non-pseudo instruction stamped from every volatile load,
  used or not, and no fusion edge waives one (the diagnostic names it
  `volatile-load`). A plain load still need not be emitted. Both selectors
  already emit one stamped volatile load instruction per source volatile
  load (AArch64 `VolatileLdr*`, x86-64 `VolatileMov*`), and both refuse a
  volatile `i128` load. Unit rows refuse a dropped volatile load, a
  pseudo stamp and a fusion edge on both architectures, and accept an
  emitted one and an unused plain load. The real x86-64 selector's unused
  `i32`, `f64` and `v128` volatile loads pass, and so do AArch64's `i8`
  through `i64`, `f32`, `f64` and `v128` through `Pipeline::run_isel` at
  proof-grade enforcement. Removing any one load's machine code is refused.
  With the requirement removed, those three rows fail. Unused volatile loads
  of the same seven types also compile through the x86-64
  `compile_trust_ir_function`, which enforces TV-3, and the AArch64
  volatile-access targets pass unchanged.
- Product fix (a regression to refusal): AArch64 again compiles the
  stack-slot bit-reverse idiom, now only when the slot is provably private.
  Since 9519375b9 enforced the raw dataflow-integrity gate (TV-3) on every
  compile, the hand-written and clang -O0 `ReverseBits32`/`ReverseBits64` of
  `bitreverse_intrinsics` were refused on both hosts ("effectful LIR
  instruction store at (block 0, index 1) has NO emitted machine instruction
  stamped from it"). The selector folded the slot's loads and stores into one
  `RBIT` and, unlike the x86-64 selector, recorded no fusion edge for the
  dropped stores. The fold also never proved the slot private: it followed
  in-block values only, so another `StackAddr` of the same slot could read,
  write or leak it while its stores were dropped. Before the gate refused the
  fold, it therefore dropped stores that another access could observe. A new
  native row selects an escaping-slot and a re-read ladder and checks that
  neither selects an `RBIT` before running them against a C reference. With
  the privacy check removed, the row fails that structural assertion first
  (`O0 ReverseBits32Escaped`, left `true`, right `false`); it does not reach
  the native run, so no native mismatch has been observed. The selector now
  folds only when whole-function address facts show that every `StackAddr`
  of the slot, and every use of its address, is an exact-width load or store
  in the matched window, and the fixed-size slot covers the access. Otherwise it selects the ladder instruction by instruction and keeps
  every store. A fold links each dropped store to the `RBIT`, stamped at the
  ladder's root, with a fusion edge that `to_ir_func` carries to
  `MachFunction::source_fusion_targets`. The AArch64 TV-3 view follows only
  an edge of the fold's shape (see the TV-3 hardening entry above), and the
  edge must still end at an emitted instruction. The folded slot keeps its id
  but no storage, and a fixed zero-byte slot no longer keeps an otherwise
  frameless leaf's frame: the helpers are `rbit w0, w0; ret` on ELF, as they
  already were on Mach-O through the red zone. `bitreverse_intrinsics` passes 6 of 6 on AArch64
  Linux, including a new run against a C reference at O0-O3 with escaping,
  re-read and width-mismatched slots that must keep their stores. Unit rows
  pin the fold, each negative control, and TV-3's refusal when the edges are
  removed or misdirected or a store of an unfolded ladder is dropped.
- The Linux AArch64 floor runner can build a required target with Cargo
  features. `TARGET_FEATURES` names them. The runner passes `--features` to
  that target's own invocation, prints the features in `--list` and records
  them in `report.json`. It refuses to run when a required target's
  file-level `#![cfg(feature = ...)]` gate is covered neither by a default
  feature nor by its entry, or when an entry names an undeclared feature. The
  12 `trust-cg-llvm-import` driver targets, including
  `bitreverse_intrinsics` after the fix above, join the Linux floor with
  `driver`, for 166 targets. The Darwin floor mirrors them with the same
  features: 213 targets and 1419 minimum passes. The x86-64 twin sets an empty
  feature table.
- The trust-ir pin moves from `7b9146ba` to trust-ir main `4f09dab8`, with the
  Clean (`55a85e99` -> `ced17efb`) and AY (0.26.0 `849c19fa` -> 0.27.0
  `f28345ff`) revisions that trust-ir itself pins, across both manifests, all
  three locks, both cache identities and `publish/DECISIONS.md`. The locks
  change only first-party sources (no third-party package moves). Every new
  construct is lowered:
  `BinOp::RotL`/`RotR` (total, amount modulo the width; constant amounts
  become immediate shifts), `UnOp::CtLz`/`CtTz` (total, `0 -> width`, through
  CtPop), `UnOp::BSwap`/`BitReverse` (swap networks) and scalar and packed
  `BinOp::FCopySign` (sign-bit merge) expand into already-covered LIR opcodes;
  `Inst::MemCopy` lowers to memcpy (or memmove when `overlap`) and
  `Inst::MemSet` to memset. Vector rotates and bit intrinsics, `Char`
  operands and the wasm lane refuse by name. The expansions agree with
  trust-ir's interpreter at every width from 8 to 64 bits, signed and
  unsigned (136 functions; the action-equivalence harness now compares
  narrow returns at their declared width, since the Apple callee extends
  them); the new Darwin floor target `e2e_aarch64_bit_intrinsics_bulk_memory`
  executes all of them, plus the bulk-memory pair, against a C reference at
  O0-O3. The stack-slot sizing and stack-protector analyses account for bulk
  memory through a stack buffer. These constructs have no trust-ir wire tag
  yet, so the paths that key an identity on the canonical image (tMBC
  encoding, core JIT admission, proof custody) refuse such a module by name
  instead of reaching trust-ir's panicking writer; the object cache skips it.

- Every staged Linux image's `.eh_frame` is now decoded as an unwinder
  reads it (the L02-P10 closure audit at `5ddb13664`). trust-cg writes each
  FDE's `pc_begin` (and a module's personality and LSDA pointers) as a
  `DW_EH_PE_pcrel|sdata4` field through `R_AARCH64_PREL32`, whose aaelf64
  2026Q2 window is `-2^31 <= X < 2^31`, and left the window to the linker.
  GNU ld 2.42 refuses a value outside it, but LLD 22.1.6 and gold 2.42
  apply the earlier `X < 2^32` and write `[2^31, 2^32)`, which every
  unwinder reads as negative: `trust-cg -o btfar b1_scalars.tmbc -Wl,bt.o
  -Wl,--section-start=.eh_frame=0x10000000,--section-start=.eh_frame_hdr=0x0fff0000,--section-start=.text=0xd0000000`
  through either installed a program whose FDEs began at
  `0xffffffffd0000000..` and whose `backtrace()` found one frame (six in the
  near twin). `run_link` now stages every Linux link (a plain `-nostdlib`
  executable link too, without the input trace) and refuses an image whose
  FDE ranges (decoded with each CIE's `R` encoding) are not inside
  executable memory, whose personality or LSDA pointers are not inside
  allocated memory, or whose `.eh_frame_hdr` binary search table disagrees
  with its FDEs (`relocation-out-of-range`, `[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-WINDOW]`),
  and one the check cannot complete (an encoding or augmentation it does
  not read, a truncated record, a load-time relocation into `.eh_frame`, an
  image that is not ELF) as `unclassified` (`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]`);
  nothing reaches the requested output. The auditor's placement is refused
  through LLD and gold (GNU ld refuses it itself), and its near and window
  edge twins (`.text` at `0x8ffe0000`) link through all three linkers and
  backtrace through a trust-cg frame into `main` (`link_options`
  `an_eh_frame_pointer_out_of_the_prel32_window_is_refused_and_its_near_twin_backtraces`).
  trust-cg's own `zPLR` object with its LSDA and personality slot placed at
  `0xd0000000` is refused the same way through LLD and gold, whose own
  programs die with SIGSEGV at the throw (`e2e_aarch64_eh_catch`
  `eh_frame_personality_and_lsda_pointers_out_of_window_are_refused_by_run_link`).
  `R_AARCH64_PREL32`'s disposition is now
  `WindowDischarge::LinkerThenEhFrameImage` (the `Linker` variant, which
  only it used, is gone). A consequence: a plain `-nostdlib` Linux link now
  refuses `-o /dev/null` and needs a writable output directory, as every
  other staged link does.

- The linked-image GOT check now covers the `LDR` GOT-base forms
  `R_AARCH64_LD64_GOTPAGE_LO15` (GCC's small-PIC `-fpic` GOT load,
  `G(GDAT(S)) - Page(GOT)`) and `R_AARCH64_LD64_GOTOFF_LO15`, with their
  PAuth forms (`0 <= X < 2^15`). They had been exempted on the ground that
  the linker rejects an out-of-range value, which holds for GNU ld and gold
  2.42 but not for LLD 22: it writes `LD64_GOTPAGE_LO15` truncated to 15
  bits, and an independent verifier's 6,000-slot library (`trust-cg -shared
  -nostdlib --relocation-model pic -Wl,gb.o -o libgb.so b1_scalars.tmbc`
  through LLD) and PIE were installed and read the wrong slot. The check
  reads the GOT base from `_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_` in the image's symbol
  table (each linker's base; not always the start of `.got`) and requires
  the section holding it and each `GLOB_DAT`, `AUTH_GLOB_DAT` and
  `IRELATIVE` target to lie within 32 KiB above the base or its page. A use
  whose own `GLOB_DAT` slot is outside is an observed overflow
  (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`); other uses of an image not shown,
  including every image whose base cannot be located (stripped, no such
  symbol), are refused conservatively (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`). A
  probe of GNU ld, gold and LLD on all 26 aaelf64 GOT-base kinds found no
  other form written out of its window; the `MOVW` forms stay unchecked,
  and LIMITATIONS, the plan and the third closure audit's archive carry a
  dated correction of the exemption.
- The linked-image GOT check now models every aaelf64 relocation that
  addresses a GOT slot from the place it patches, each with its own window,
  and treats an `STT_GNU_IFUNC` definition as a page-window use (the third
  L02-P10 closure audit). The audit found three routes the CLI installed with
  a truncated GOT access: `R_AARCH64_TLSGD_ADR_PAGE21` (`trust-cg -shared
  -nostdlib --relocation-model pic -Wl,gd.o
  -Wl,--section-start=.got=0x200000000 -o libgd.so b1_scalars.tmbc`: `adrp
  x0, 0`, the user read module 0); the tiny-model
  `R_AARCH64_TLSIE_LD_GOTTPREL_PREL19` load literal followed by 1.5 MiB of
  text (user SIGSEGV), with `TLSGD_ADR_PREL21`, `TLSDESC_LD_PREL19` and
  `TLSDESC_ADR_PREL21` linked truncated the same way; and a static IFUNC
  program whose linker script merged `.iplt` into `.text` and `.rela.iplt`
  into a `PROGBITS` `.rodata`, or that was linked with `-z nosectionheader`,
  so the image showed no IPLT (SIGSEGV). `AARCH64_GOT_ADDRESSING_RELOCATIONS`
  now lists 17 kinds (the `ADRP` page kinds, +-4 GiB; the load-literal and
  `ADR` kinds, +-1 MiB; `GOTPCREL32`, +-2 GiB; and the PAuth forms), pinned
  against a transcript of every aaelf64 GOT kind by
  `got_addressing_kinds_match_the_psabi_tables`; each positional and traced
  use is checked against its own window from every possible site to every
  possible slot, and an image not in page reach whose input defines an IFUNC
  is refused naming it (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`). Every reproducer is
  refused with the output untouched, GNU ld's own image fails, and each near
  twin links and runs (`link_options`
  `general_dynamic_and_tiny_model_got_accesses_are_refused_and_their_near_twins_run`,
  `a_hidden_iplt_is_refused_through_its_ifunc_definition_and_its_near_twins_run`).
  Consequences: a narrow-window use in an image whose code and slots span
  more than 1 MiB is refused conservatively, such an image needs a readable
  linker trace (`-Wl,--verbose` then refuses it with
  `[TCG-LINK-INPUT-TRACE]`), and a static IFUNC program linked with `-z
  nosectionheader` is refused at any placement. `[TCG-LINK-NO-OUTPUT]` now
  says "GOT-addressing inputs". Execution and object evidence on one host's
  GNU ld 2.42, not proof.
- An image not shown to keep every GOT-page `ADRP` in reach is now refused
  when it holds GOT-addressing code the linker wrote itself, whatever its
  inputs (the second L02-P10 closure audit). A PLT call carries only
  `R_AARCH64_CALL26`, but GNU ld 2.42 writes each PLT entry's `adrp x16` to
  its `R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT` slot without checking the +-4 GiB page window:
  `trust-cg -shared -nostdlib --relocation-model pic -o libplt.so
  caller.trust_ir -Wl,--section-start=.got.plt=0x200010000` exited 0,
  installed a library whose `.plt` held `adrp x16, 0x10000`, and its user
  died with SIGSEGV. `run_link` now reads the staged image for a PLT
  (`R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT`, `DT_JMPREL` or an executable `.plt`), an IPLT
  (`R_AARCH64_IRELATIVE` or an executable `.iplt`) and the lazy TLS
  descriptor trampoline (`DT_TLSDESC_PLT`). A PLT entry's slot or the
  trampoline's `DT_TLSDESC_GOT` word that no code byte reaches is an
  observed overflow (`relocation-out-of-range`, `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`,
  naming the symbol); other such code is a conservative refusal
  (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`). The audit's reproducer is refused, alone
  and with `.got` far too, GNU ld's own library dies with SIGSEGV, and the
  2 GiB twin links and runs (`link_options`
  `a_linker_generated_plt_entry_out_of_reach_is_refused_and_its_near_twin_runs`).
  The GOT-page route and audit controls now also name the PLT entry and the
  trampoline (four refusals each instead of two). The `link_driver` unit
  tests write their scripted linkers through `install -m 755`, which removes
  an intermittent `ETXTBSY` ("Text file busy") spawn failure between
  parallel tests. Execution and object evidence on one host's GNU ld 2.42,
  not proof.
- The GOT-page `ADRP` window check now reads every AArch64 ELF relocatable
  object the linker loads, not only the positional inputs (L02-P10
  closure-audit residuals). The audit installed a library whose user died
  with SIGSEGV: `trust-cg -shared -nostdlib --relocation-model pic
  -Wl,got_page.o -Wl,--section-start=.got=0x200000000,...` exited 0 with the
  page deltas truncated, and so did `-l :got_page.o` and a `--whole-archive`
  member. On Linux the staged image is checked first; when it is not shown
  to keep every GOT-page `ADRP` in reach, the linker's input trace is read
  once, in the same pass as the local-exec check, and every
  `R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE`, `R_AARCH64_TLSIE_ADR_GOTTPREL_PAGE21` or
  `R_AARCH64_TLSDESC_ADR_PAGE21` use in a traced input refuses the image by
  name (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`, `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]` or
  `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNCHECKED]`, naming the loaded input). A trace that does
  not show what was loaded refuses such an image with `[TCG-LINK-INPUT-TRACE]`.
  A link with the C runtime is now traced too (a plain executable link must
  be `-nostdlib`): the host's `Scrt1.o`, `crti.o` and `crtbeginS.o` carry
  GOT-page `ADRP`s, and GNU ld links an executable with `.got` 8 GiB from its
  code that dies with SIGSEGV, which the CLI now refuses naming the start
  files. Every default `trust-cg -o <program>` link is therefore staged and
  refuses `-o /dev/null`. New controls: `link_options`
  `linux_got_page::got_page_objects_on_every_link_route_are_refused_by_name`
  refuses eight routes (`-Wl` operand, `-l :file`, archive member by
  reference and whole, thin archive, `INPUT()`, `GROUP()`, `--start-group`)
  with the GOT at 8 GiB, each with exactly two
  `error[link:relocation-out-of-range]` lines, no output and a pre-existing
  output untouched; GNU ld's unchecked library for each route makes its user
  die with SIGSEGV, and each 2 GiB twin links and runs. The audit's exact
  command and the C-runtime route have their own controls, and scripted
  unit tests pin the traced refusals, the image-first order and the combined
  `[TCG-LINK-INPUT-TRACE]` text. The text-offset ceilings of the encoder and
  EH resolver now have controls: a real compile reaches the jump-table
  `ADR` imm21 window (delta `2^20 - 4` admitted, `2^20` refused as `ADR->jump
  table offset 1048576 does not fit in imm21`), and the u32 block,
  instruction and jump-table offsets and the LSDA code length are pinned at
  `u32::MAX`/`2^32` by real compiles with a unit-test-only synthetic text
  prefix inside the four checks (a 4 GiB function is impractical). Evidence:
  `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-got-page-trace` (execution and object
  evidence on one host's GNU ld 2.42, not proof).
- Scalar `f16` and `f16` HFA arguments and returns now execute natively on
  Linux AArch64 (L01-P7). The Linux floor target `e2e_aarch64_f16_abi_linux`
  runs 29 shapes: twelve `f16` arguments, `f16` interleaved with `f32`,
  `f64` and integers until both register banks are full, one- to
  four-member HFAs at every register/stack boundary, and HFA returns from
  registers, from the stack and permuted. Every shape runs in both
  directions against GCC's `_Float16` at O0-O3, for the generic baseline
  and an explicit `fp16` profile. NaN payloads, signed zeros, subnormals and
  infinities agree bit for bit (11,136 calls and 100,608 slot checks; the
  two profiles produce byte-identical objects, so half of them run on
  distinct code). The test decodes the ELF objects with the `trust-cg-lift`
  decoder and checks them against its own AAPCS64 model: `f16` values move
  through H registers, and each stack `f16` is written and read at its
  8-byte slot.
  The same objects fail a packed-stack model and a model without the NSRN
  clamp. Mutated stack loads and stores are caught by the decoder and by
  the C oracle, as is a prototype that spells an `f16` argument `float`, in
  all 29 shapes. The baseline objects contain no FEAT_FP16 instruction.
  `f16` addition over the same boundary is refused by name without the
  profile; with it, the result matches the hardware `FADD H` bit for bit.
  The Darwin row runs the six host-neutral tests only. DarwinPCS packs HFA
  members on the stack at their natural size, and the Darwin classifier
  does not; LIMITATIONS.md records that divergence, and a separate
  `InsertField` aliasing miscompile this corpus found.
- CG-owned landing pads now run natively on AArch64 Linux GNU (L03-P2). The
  new floor target `e2e_aarch64_eh_linux` links ELF objects that own
  catch-all and cleanup-then-resume pads with libstdc++/libgcc_s, and with
  Rust std through a harness built by the checkout's stock `rustc`. It runs
  them at O0-O3 on both invoke successors: 160 C++ calls (100 exceptions;
  three CG catch pads read the payload through `__cxa_begin_catch`) and
  128 Rust calls (80 real panics caught by `catch_unwind`). Each call must match an
  exact stage, payload, destructor and cleanup model. GNU readelf,
  llvm-dwarfdump and llvm-objdump read back the `zPLR` CIE, the
  `DW.ref` personality slot and every LSDA, whose rows must cover each
  disassembled invoke with its pad. Mutating the linked image controls the
  runs: for each of the 20 invoke calls (four C++ functions and `tr_cleanup`
  at O0-O3), an unmutated reference run matches the model, then dropping
  the invoke's LSDA row makes the run terminate and retargeting its pad
  sends it down the normal path with the exception in flight. That is 40
  mutated images (32 C++, 8 Rust) and 20 reference runs; the
  `EH_LINUX_*_MUTATIONS` lines print the mutant, dropped, retargeted and
  reference counts separately. Linking without the personality's runtime
  fails naming exactly the personality. The fixtures exposed a lowering
  defect: an AArch64 `Resume` ended in `BL _Unwind_Resume` with no
  terminator, so the final-layout CFG gave the cleanup pad a fallthrough
  edge into the next block, and the frame net refused the function
  (`[TCG-A64-SPILL-SLOT]`). With only the `BRK` removed, a probe that
  compiles each fixture function on its own refused all four
  cleanup-then-resume functions at every level O0-O3 (16 of 16:
  `tc_cleanup`, `tr_cleanup` and `tr_nested` on
  `caller-callee-saved-value-read`, `tr_through` on
  `return-lane-holds-caller-value`) and compiled the five without a
  `Resume`. `Resume` now ends with `BRK #1`, as the x86-64 selector ends it
  with `UD2`. A block that ends in an invoke and makes another call stays
  refused by name. Evidence: `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-eh-landing-pads`.
  This is execution and tool-readback evidence, not proof; the Mach-O
  native EH legs were not rerun on macOS after the `BRK` change.
- The local-exec TLS guard now examines every input the linker loads, not
  only positional ones (L02-P9 closure-audit residuals). Before, `trust-cg
  --shared --relocation-model pic -o libx.so div.tmbc -Wl,le.o` (and `-L .
  -l :le.o`) linked a local-exec object into a library whose user exited
  236 instead of 42; `link_options` pinned that as the documented boundary.
  On Linux every link that is not a plain executable link (every `--shared`
  link, every link with `-l` or `-Wl`, and every link with a positional input
  the AArch64 ELF reader cannot read, which includes every non-AArch64 link)
  is now staged and run with the linker's input trace
  (`-Wl,--trace,--trace`, passed first). When the image is not an
  executable, every AArch64 ELF relocatable object the trace names
  is read, including archive members (GNU ld's `(archive)member`, LLD's
  `archive(member)`, thin-archive members) and files a linker script's
  `INPUT()` or `GROUP()` names, and a local-exec relocation in any of them
  refuses the image with `[TCG-LINK-TLS-MODEL]`, naming the loaded input.
  A trace that does not show what was loaded (a line naming no readable
  file, as `-Wl,--verbose` or `-Wl,-M` print; a positional object missing
  from it; an unreadable relocatable object) is refused with the new
  `[TCG-LINK-INPUT-TRACE]`. Shared-library inputs are not scanned (the link
  applies none of their relocations). Both scans now also read `SHT_REL`
  sections, which the reader skipped: GNU ld 2.42 applies them and linked a
  local-exec pair moved into `SHT_REL` into a `-shared` library outside the
  driver. The boundary test is replaced by
  per-route negative controls for eight routes (`-Wl` operand, `-l:`,
  archive member by reference and whole, thin archive, `INPUT()`, `GROUP()`,
  `--start-group`), each with exactly one `error[link:tls-model-mismatch]`,
  no output left and a pre-existing output untouched, and `pic` twins that
  link and return 42. New CLI controls link and run `--pie`, `--no-pie`,
  `--static` and `--nostdlib` outputs and check `ET_DYN`+`DF_1_PIE`,
  `ET_EXEC` and `PT_INTERP` with the driver's reader and `readelf`, with
  negative twins (`--shared --pie`, a static link against a shared-only
  library, `--nostdlib` without libgcc's `__divti3`). The TEXTREL control
  now pins its subject (`puts@@GLIBC_2.17`), runs through `run_link`, and
  has a twin without `-z text` whose `TEXTREL` flag `readelf -d` shows.
  Staging makes every such link refuse `-o /dev/null` and need a writable
  output directory. Not examined: a plain executable link, a file replaced
  between the link and the read, code a linker plugin generates without a
  traced file, a file a linker writes at another path, and links outside the
  driver. Evidence:
  `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-link-input-trace` (execution and object
  evidence on one host's GNU ld 2.42 and LLD 22, not proof).
- Wrong-code fix: an AArch64 call that passes a composite over 16 bytes
  that is not an HFA/HVA now passes storage the callee may own. AAPCS64
  B.4 (kept by DarwinPCS) passes such an argument as a pointer to a
  caller-allocated copy that the callee may write, and trust-cg passed the
  address of the value's own storage instead, so a C callee that assigned
  to its parameter changed the caller's value: the aggregate insert fix's
  `cg_calls_c` probe got 4 of 16 checks wrong at O0-O3 on Linux AArch64. A
  parameter, constant, load, block parameter or insert result, a value
  passed twice or in a loop, and calls through a function pointer, with an
  sret result, to a variadic callee or with the pointer spilled to the
  stack all miscompiled (13 of the first corpus's 19 shapes, 527 of 1,047
  checks at every level). The trust-ir adapter now passes every such
  argument as a pointer: to the value's own slot when a `Const`, `Load` or
  insert made it for that value alone and the call is its only use in the
  same block, otherwise to a fresh frame slot filled by a `Memcpy` (inline
  up to 32 bytes, a `memcpy` call above). An invoke with such an argument
  moves into a block of its own after the copy. A first version of this fix
  copied inline in instruction selection with no size limit, which made
  compile time grow quadratically with the argument (47 s at O1 for a
  72,000-byte argument, 288,000 bytes at O2 did not finish); the scaling
  corpus now compiles in under 0.4 s at every level with a bounded
  instruction count. The adapter types a function or block parameter
  forwarded as an anonymous variadic argument from its trust-ir value (at
  first such a parameter over 256 bytes was refused), and a Darwin invoke of
  a variadic callee is refused by name (`[TCG-VARARG-ABI]`): an invoke
  carries no fixed-argument count, so its anonymous arguments were placed in
  registers where DarwinPCS puts them on the stack. Selection still copies an aggregate-typed by-reference
  argument from another LIR producer, inline up to 256 bytes, and refuses a
  larger one (`[TCG-BYREF-COPY]`); sibling tail-call eligibility refuses
  such a call by name (`ByReferenceArgumentCopy`), and a copy in the
  caller's frame already blocks the tail branch. New Linux floor target
  `e2e_aarch64_large_aggregate_args_linux` (on the Darwin floor with six
  host-neutral rows) runs 23 shapes, 1,125 checks per level, against C
  callees and 6 invoke shapes against throwing C++ callees, all of which
  write every by-reference parameter, at O0-O3; it also checks that such
  calls in tail position keep their `BL`, the code-size bound, the
  invoke block shape and the adapter's copy decisions on Linux and Darwin. Evidence:
  `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-large-aggregate-args`. This is execution
  evidence on one host, not proof; the Darwin arm is not executed. The same
  change repairs a regression of the aggregate insert fix below: its copies
  of a zero-sized value (`()`, an empty struct) were zero-length `Memcpy`s,
  which selection lowers to no instruction and the dataflow-integrity gate
  refused, so two `()` or empty-struct block parameters on one edge, an
  empty-struct parameter fed from a constant, and an insert into a
  zero-sized struct whose source is used twice no longer compiled at O0-O3
  although the base did. Zero-sized values now own their slot but copy no
  bytes; `e2e_aarch64_aggregate_insert_linux` gains three rows (lowered
  LIR, Linux and Darwin objects at O0-O3, and a Linux run) over eight such
  shapes and the reported reproducer.
- ABI fix (wrong code at the C boundary): a homogeneous floating-point or
  short-vector aggregate is recognized over its flattened members. A struct
  with more than four declared fields was never homogeneous, so `struct {
  double a; struct {} z; double b, c, d; }` was passed by reference in x0
  where GCC 13 passes d0-d3 (a C callee computed the wrong digest), and a
  zero-length array member counted as nothing, so `struct { float a; float
  z[0]; float b; }` went in s0/s1 where GCC uses x0. An empty struct, `()`
  or an array of them now contributes no member and a zero-length array
  member makes the aggregate non-homogeneous, matching GCC and clang for
  arguments and returns. rustc ignores a Rust `[T; 0]` field; trust-cg
  follows the C ABI. New Linux floor target `e2e_aarch64_hfa_zero_sized_linux`
  (on the Darwin floor with three host-neutral rows) checks nine shapes in
  four directions against GCC at O0-O3.
- Wrong-code fix: `InsertField` and `InsertElement` on an aggregate value
  no longer write into the source aggregate's storage. The adapter stored
  the new member into the source and returned the same address, so any
  later read of the source saw the inserted member: `swap(s) =
  insert(insert(s, 0, s.1), 1, s.0)` returned `{2,2}` for `{1,2}` over
  `{i64,i64}`, `{f32,f32}` and `{f16,f16}` at O0-O3 on Linux AArch64. The
  same fault hit a parameter, load, global, constant, call result, `Copy`,
  `Select`, block parameter, nested field or stored source read after the
  insert, a 32-byte argument a trust-cg caller passed by reference, and
  loop-carried values. An insert now copies its source into a fresh stack
  slot, or reuses the source's slot only when a `Const`, `Load` or insert
  allocated it for that source alone and the insert, in the same block, is
  its only use. Aggregate block parameters now own their storage and every
  edge copies into it, which also repairs an aggregate `Load` re-executed
  in a loop while the previous iteration's value is still read. An
  `InsertField` through a pointer to an `Alloca` (the rustc bridge's field
  store) keeps its store-through lowering. New Linux floor target
  `e2e_aarch64_aggregate_insert_linux` (on the Darwin floor with six
  host-neutral rows) checks 27 shapes against a C oracle bit-exactly at
  O0-O3, the reference interpreter against a closed-form model on 21 of
  them, and the adapter's copy and in-place decisions on the lowered LIR.
  Evidence: `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-aggregate-insert`. This is
  execution evidence on one host, not proof. A by-value aggregate over 16
  bytes was then still passed to a callee as the address of the caller's own
  storage; the entry above fixes that.
- The GOT-page image check now also sees GOT slots in non-allocated
  sections (L02-P10, second repair). GNU ld 2.42 refuses a GOT in a
  `NOLOAD` section but links one into an `INFO`, `COPY`, `DSECT` or
  `OVERLAY` section. Such a section is not allocated, yet it keeps the
  address the script gives it, and the first repair read only allocated
  sections. A static `-nostdlib` executable whose script laid such a
  section over `NOLOAD` zero fill at 8 GiB was installed with `adrp x0, 0`
  for its undefined-weak slot and died with SIGSEGV; the slot reads zero,
  its right value, in the 1 GiB twin. Every non-allocated section at a
  nonzero address, or writable, now counts as a possible slot region. The
  sections an ordinary image does not load (`.comment`, `.symtab`,
  `.debug_*`) are at address 0 and not writable, and none of the 4,684 ELF
  images scanned on the host has another kind. An image without a section
  header table cannot show such a section, so it is now always refused as
  `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`: a `-z nosectionheader` link with a
  GOT-page input is refused even when in reach. The first repair's list of
  what the check cannot see was incomplete. It now names allocated zero fill
  that no relocation targets, a non-allocated read-only section at address
  0, Android's packed relocations and code not executable where it is
  loaded. New unit rows and a Linux row in `e2e_aarch64_link_runtime` cover
  all four section types at 8 GiB (refused) and 1 GiB (link and run), and
  the `-z nosectionheader` variant. Evidence:
  `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-got-page-region/records/repair` (codegen
  lib 4109 passed, `e2e_aarch64_link_runtime` 32/32, nine source mutants
  killed). This is linker and execution evidence on one host, not proof.
- The link driver's GOT-page image check no longer finds the GOT by section
  name (L02-P10 repair). It compared the farthest code byte with the
  farthest `.got`/`.got.*` byte. That admitted a library whose GOT slots a
  `-Wl,-T` `INSERT` script had moved into `.slots` 8 GiB away while
  `.got.plt` stayed at 2 GiB. GNU ld 2.42 wrote `adrp x1, 0` for the
  `ADR_GOT_PAGE` site, `trust-cg -shared` installed the library, and an
  executable using it died with SIGSEGV. The check now takes every
  executable byte as a possible site. It takes as a possible slot all
  file-backed allocated memory, every target of the dynamic relocation
  tables (read through the program headers) and of the allocated relocation
  sections, the GOT words `DT_PLTGOT` and `DT_TLSDESC_GOT` name, and each
  zero-fill region that holds such a target. Dynamic relocations alone would
  miss a position-dependent executable's linker-filled slots. A refused use
  stays `error[link:relocation-out-of-range]` `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`
  only when a dynamic relocation names its own slot and no code byte reaches
  that slot. Every other use is `error[link:unclassified]`
  `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`, a conservative refusal whose text no
  longer claims an overflow. It covers libraries that GNU ld and LLD link
  correctly, such as one with an executable section 8 GiB from a GOT that
  its code reaches. A large `.bss` is still admitted. New unit rows cover a
  renamed GOT, a dynamic image whose far slots have no relocation, stripped
  section headers read through dynamic tags, zero fill, static images and
  the certainty rule. New Linux rows in `e2e_aarch64_link_runtime` cover the
  script-moved GOT with and without section headers, a position-dependent
  executable's static slot moved the same way, the far executable section
  and a GOT 64 KiB past the window's upper edge. The check still cannot
  see a linker-filled slot placed in zero fill that no relocation names, or
  one filled through Android's packed relocations. Evidence:
  `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-got-page-region`. It records codegen lib
  4108 passed, `e2e_aarch64_link_runtime` 31/31, direct CLI probes against
  GNU ld's unchecked output, and six source mutants killed. This is linker
  and execution evidence on one host, not proof.
- AArch64 ELF explicit data sections now follow where GNU ld 2.42 and
  LLD 22.1.6 actually put each name (L02-P3, touching L02-P7). The
  data-global classifier's catch-all admitted any unlisted name as plain
  allocated data. This defect predates the L02-P7 work. A mutable
  zero-initialized global stored through `.tcommon`, `.gnu_extab`,
  `.gcc_except_table.x`, `.exception_ranges`, `.sframe` or `.eh_frame.x`
  died with SIGSEGV under GNU ld (the linker put the input inside
  `PT_GNU_RELRO`, and `.tcommon` in its `.tbss` output). `.jcr` faulted under
  both linkers. `object_sections::ELF_NAME_RULES` now records each name
  family's output under both linkers, and the classifier derives every
  refusal from that table. A mutable global in a read-only or `PT_GNU_RELRO`
  output of either linker is `[TCG-SECTION-READONLY]`: `.rodata1`, `.toc`,
  mutable constructor tables, and the existing `.rodata*`, `.data.rel.ro*`,
  `.bss.rel.ro*`. `.tcommon` is `[TCG-SECTION-TLS]`. `.stub` and `.iplt` are
  `[TCG-SECTION-EXEC]`. Unwind and exception families, `.igot*`,
  `.relro_padding`, `COMMON`, `.rela*`, `.relr.dyn`, stabs names, `.line`,
  `.gnu_debuglink`, `.jcr` and `.tm_clone_table` are `[TCG-SECTION-RESERVED]`.
  Names one character past a family stay orphans with the global's flags,
  except where BFD matches a raw name prefix outside the script. It parses
  every input named `.eh_frame_entry*` as compact unwind entries, which
  fails the GNU link, so `.eh_frame_entryx`, `.eh_frame_entry1`,
  `.eh_frame_entry_x`, `.eh_frame_entry-x` and `.eh_frame_entry$x` are
  `[TCG-SECTION-RESERVED]`. The first version matched only
  `.eh_frame_entry[.*]` and admitted them, until a verifier's sweep found
  it. The derivation test now also reads a retained list of BFD's by-name
  rules. A COMDAT definition's implicit `<base>.<symbol>` is classified by
  the same table, so a mutable link-once global named `rel.ro` (which got
  `.data.rel.ro` or `.bss.rel.ro`) is refused by name. A function section
  named `COMMON` is `[TCG-SECTION-DATA]`. A unit test re-derives the GNU
  column from the retained `ld --verbose` script and the by-name list. A
  Linux control links trust-cg's own bytes in 30 refused cases with both
  linkers and asserts each hazard. A C control fails the GNU link under
  each `.eh_frame_entry*` spelling. The honoured writable names survive a
  store under both linkers as PIEs and shared libraries. Ten source
  mutations are each caught, and the objects that escape a removed refusal
  are retained with their faults, link failures or misplacements.
  Run: `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-explicit-section-write-faults`. This
  is evidence about these two linker versions' default links, not a linker
  proof.
- The x86-64 link-and-run tests now use one host-capability probe,
  `common::rosetta::x86_64_link_run`, which proves that a host can link and
  run x86-64 code before any link or run leg starts. The old probe had been
  wrong since `f25be0dc4`. That commit dropped `-arch x86_64` off macOS on the
  assumption that an `is_x86_64()` gate always ran first, but five targets
  (`e2e_x86_64_correctness`, `e2e_x86_64_link`, `e2e_x86_64_i128_stack_abi`,
  `e2e_x86_64_scale_emergent`, `guard_kernel_gate_x86_linkrun`) call the probe
  without that gate. On the Linux AArch64 host the probe then linked and ran
  a native AArch64 `int main` and answered yes. Those targets then handed
  x86-64 ELF objects to the AArch64 `ld` and got 48 failures (`Relocations in
  generic ELF (EM: 62)`). Three `scale_emergent` tests passed without running
  anything, because they record a link failure as "not executed". The new
  probe links a program that has an `#error` unless the driver targets
  x86-64, checks that the executable header is `EM_X86_64` or
  `CPU_TYPE_X86_64`, and runs the program to a marker line. The driver is
  `cc -arch x86_64` on macOS (Rosetta still needs
  `TRUST_CG_RUN_ROSETTA_LINKRUN`), `cc` on an x86-64 host,
  `x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc` on other Linux hosts, or whatever
  `TRUST_CG_X86_64_CC` names. Every link command in these targets and in
  `common::x86_64_corpus` uses the proven driver. When the probe fails, only
  the link and run legs stop, and each prints `SKIP: <test>: <leg> not run:
  <probe result>`. The old `scale_emergent` lines were lowercase `skip:`,
  which the case-sensitive `scripts/matrix_results.py` classifier does not
  count. Compilation still runs on every host. A new check, `common::x86_64_object`, confirms each
  object is the host's x86-64 relocatable, that it defines the symbols the C
  driver calls and that it imports the C callees. The new test
  `test_x86_64_link_object_symbols_both_containers` covers that check on
  both ELF and Mach-O. On this host all five targets pass, 61 tests in
  total. 52 of those tests print a runtime `SKIP:` for their link or run
  leg, and nothing is linked or run. The `test_x86_64_link_clamp` and
  `test_x86_64_link_loop_sum` fixtures were also stale on every host. They
  predate the rule, added in `5f73a26f7`, that a machine function's successor
  metadata must match its branches, so they now record their CFG edges. Each
  test also asserts that the fixture without those edges is refused with the
  exact `MalformedFunction` successor-metadata error.
- `e2e_aarch64_copy_coalesce` no longer depends on the host target. It
  failed 3 of 4 on Linux AArch64 (sub2 5 vs 2, sum3 6 vs 3, const-return
  5 vs 2 instructions), but copy coalescing had not regressed: the
  coalesced bodies (`sub x0, x0, x1`, `add x3, x0, x1 ; add x0, x3, x2`,
  `mov x0, #42`) match the Darwin output word for word. The extra words
  are the deliberate sixteen-byte FP/LR envelope around them. Linux has no
  red zone (`18e1ab693`). Its zero-storage leaf policy (`e26492c26`) keeps
  that envelope as the source-bound Formal-evidence frame owner for
  ADD/SUB/LSL bodies (`ad795539f`) and for constant/copy returns
  (`b488c3cc1`). Builds of the unchanged test on this host pass 4/4 just
  before `18e1ab693`, 0/4 at it and just before `e26492c26`, 4/4 at
  `e26492c26`, 2/4 at `ad795539f` and 1/4 from `b488c3cc1` on. The test
  now compiles every module for both `aarch64-apple-darwin` and
  `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`. For each it
  asserts the exact code words, read with a parser independent of the
  emitter, and the instruction-count metric. Linux sub2, sum3 and
  const-return are enveloped; addmul (MADD) is frameless on both.
  Controls: `TRUST_CG_DISABLE_PASSES=post_ra` leaves the return copy
  (`mov x0, x2`, `mov x0, x3`) behind and fails sub2 and addmul.
  Reverting the SUB envelope rule makes Linux sub2 frameless and fails it.
  LIMITATIONS.md records the three-instruction ELF cost, and
  ARCHITECTURE.md now names the constant/copy-return envelope rule.
- `e2e_aarch64_swift_aggregate` no longer fails on Linux AArch64. It compiled
  its swiftcall aggregate module for the host-derived target, which is AAPCS64
  on Linux. Since `c6d2228c6`, Swift aggregate scalarization runs only for the
  DarwinPCS contract that clang `swiftcall` execution witnesses, so every shape
  was refused there as an unsupported calling convention. That refusal is
  deliberate and unchanged. The test now compiles the seven shapes for an
  explicit `aarch64-apple-darwin` target on every host and still links and
  runs them against clang only on macOS. A new test pins each shape's exact
  AAPCS64 refusal, naming the function and its aggregate parameter. It also
  compiles the same one-shape module for Darwin and a scalar swiftcc control
  for AAPCS64. The budget-5 and packed shapes now assert that exact refusal
  for both targets instead of any error. If the Darwin-only gate is removed,
  the new test fails. The Darwin gate minimum for this target rises from 3 to
  4. `LIMITATIONS.md` had said the scalarization also ran on AAPCS64; it now
  records the refusal. Linux Swift aggregate support remains open, because
  this host has no clang or Swift compiler to witness it.
- Two in-process JIT tests no longer hard-code `aarch64-apple-darwin`
  (test-only, no product change).
  `e2e_pipeline_integration::test_jit_metrics_surface_proof_optimization_summary`
  failed on Linux AArch64 with `JitTargetSpecMismatch`. `d4ecbee04` gave it
  the file's Mach-O object pin. Since `9107c5902` the JIT refuses any
  same-architecture spec whose OS/ABI is not the host's, so on Linux that pin
  is refused before any code is generated. The test now compiles for
  `TargetSpec::host()` and keeps every metric assertion. A new companion test
  checks the pin through the public JIT API. It compiles on macOS, where the
  pin is the host spec, and elsewhere must fail with the named refusal that
  reports both specs. `jit_integration`'s TrustIR helper prepared DarwinPCS
  code (red-zone leaves, packed narrow stack arguments) and ran it in the
  Linux process. At base all 59 tests still passed, so no wrong result was
  observed. The helper now prepares through `PipelineConfig::for_host_aarch64()`
  and refuses a prepared triple that differs from the one
  `JitCompiler::aarch64_target_triple` reports. On this host
  `e2e_pipeline_integration` passes 33 of 33 and `jit_integration` 59 of 59.
- AArch64 O2/O3 no longer refuses a TrustIR `switch` whose keys share a
  constant boolean arm joined through a block parameter (the SSA form of
  `matches!(x, 1 | 3)`). Since `6eafd20a8` the late boolean-diamond pass
  folded that shape. Its sparse compare chain (`CMP #1; B.EQ T; CMP #3;
  B.EQ T; B F`) puts two branches into one header, and the header still looked
  like a two-way diamond because cfg-simplify deduplicates edge lists. The pass
  converted on the last compare, deleted the arms and left the earlier
  `B.EQ` aimed at a removed block. The structural validator then refused the
  function ("successor target absent from block_order"), so this was a
  compile refusal, not wrong code. The diamond, triangle and tiny-loop
  if-conversion recognizers and `CmpSelectCombine` now share
  `if_convert::header_branch_is_sole_block_exit`, which requires the selected
  branch (plus its trailing `B`) to be the header's only block exit. Unit
  controls cover each recognizer and fail without the gate. The native row
  `e2e_aarch64_switch::e2e_aarch64_bool_switch_shared_arms_match_c_at_every_opt_level`
  checks four shared-arm switches against a C reference at O0-O3, and it fails
  at O2 without the fix. The 108 TrustIR fixtures embedded in the
  `e2e_trust_fns_round*` tests or stored as `tests/slices/*.tir` were
  JIT-compiled at O0-O3. Before the fix, three were refused at O2/O3 (in
  round 7, round 8 and `trust_reloc_word.tir`). After it none are, and no
  other fixture's outcome changed.
- `e2e_trust_fns_round8`'s x86 classifier fixture is re-pinned to production
  `x86_writes_flags`. Commit `10f0b0d4c` removed `Not`, because x86 NOT
  (`F7 /2`) affects no flags. This closes the stale-classifier failure that
  `docs/audit-2026-09-07.md` left open pending a reproducible regeneration.
  The slice drops the arm. The embedded emit was regenerated on aarch64 Linux
  with trust-ir frontend `00c45ab9d`, and that frontend first reproduced the
  old fixture from the old slice. The new emit differs from the old fixture
  only in the dropped `22: bb2` switch key. Its host target line and its new
  `; #loc:` comments were not adopted. The test now asserts `Not` writes no
  flags, and a new row repeats the exhaustive 193-opcode comparison at O0-O3.
- The rustc bridge now refuses `-Zcodegen-emit-retag` as `[TCG-EMIT-RETAG]`.
  Before this change it silently dropped the retag calls the option asks
  for. On the stock nightly, retag semantics reached the bridge as
  `StatementKind::Retag`, and its fail-closed statement fallback refused
  them. The Trust rustc the bridge moved to in `0d8cb948a` has no such
  statement. A retag there is a flag on `Rvalue::Use(_, WithRetag)`, which
  the bridge lowers as the plain copy or move that `rustc_codegen_ssa` emits
  when retag emission is off. That left `-Zcodegen-emit-retag` as the only
  remaining request for retag semantics, and the bridge accepted it without
  emitting anything. `codegen_crate` now refuses the whole compile before
  lowering anything. Metadata-only compiles never reach it. The new bridge
  target `codegen_emit_retag_refusal` pins the refusal both for the bare
  option and for one with a sub-option. Its controls check that a compile
  without the option still succeeds, that a metadata-only compile still
  succeeds, and that LLVM accepts the option on the same crate. The
  no-option control runs with `no-proof-certs`, because in the default lane
  the probe's frame prologue hits the `[TCG-PROOF-465]` proof wall. The
  same knob with the option is still refused. As a source-mutation control,
  the check was disabled and the target failed both tests. With that
  knob, the option then compiled to an object. The bridge has no retag
  emitter, so that object reproduced the silent drop this change fixes. The
  `Retag` row of `rustc-mir-coverage-inventory.md` names the new blocker.
  Its text guard `rustc_mir_coverage_inventory` had failed since
  `0d8cb948a`; it now checks the refusal, the executable test and the
  exhaustive `statement_kind_name`.
- The TRUST_IR binary-container fixtures now come from the trust-ir pin
  `7b9146ba` (previously `d41fa3f8`, which `SOURCE.txt` said to update when
  the pin moved). There are 40 conformance fixtures. Every `.tmbc` present
  at both pins is byte-identical. The upstream renames were `body_gate` and
  `ty_handle`, and the new fixtures include the v44/v45 ones. The container
  tests of `trust-cg-codegen` and `trust-cg-cli` no longer hard-code the
  reader window, which the pin widened to v45. They read it from
  `trust_ir::BUILD_IDENTITY`, and a window-edge control shows the refusals
  come from trust-ir's version gate. `func_param_abi` declares
  `struct_passing = AlwaysMemory`. It is pinned to that exact adapter
  refusal, `TargetStructPassingUnsupported`, which since `4427c5432` fires
  before its byval parameter is reached. `[TCG-BYVAL-ABI]` stays pinned by
  `abi_refusals`. `abi_function_symbol` is pinned to the v45 `protected`
  visibility refusal. `abi_enum_tag_repr`, `import_scheme` and
  `lean_library_envelope` compile to identical objects from binary and from
  JSON.
- An AArch64 CEGIS search whose candidates were all proven is no longer
  rolled back when the per-function budget (`--cegis-superopt=<SECS>`) ran
  out during its last query. The budget was checked before every
  instruction, so after an overrunning final verification the next
  non-candidate instruction reported `DeadlineExceeded`. The transactional
  pass then dropped the proven rewrites, and `compile_ir_function` refuses
  such a search with `CegisIncomplete`. On the Linux AArch64 host the first
  proof-bearing query in a process takes about 1.9 s in the unoptimized test
  build, mostly for content-hashing the 166 MB Clean checker. As a result,
  the three hand-optimized codegen cases in `e2e_cegis_superopt` failed
  against their 1 s budget on every run, alone or under load. The budget now
  gates only the start of a solver-backed verification. Its clock starts at
  the first one, and the structural walk always finishes. A function with at
  most one such candidate therefore gets the same outcome at any load, as
  long as that query finishes within the per-query limit (`per_query_ms`,
  5 s of wall-clock time in the pipeline, including solver waits and the
  Clean replay). A further verification is still refused once the budget has
  elapsed, and that search still fails closed.
  `CEGIS_SEARCH_SEMANTICS_REVISION` is now 2, and deterministic
  `cegis_payload` rows cover both cases. Whether a second or later query may
  start still depends on measured time. The walk the budget no longer bounds
  is now linear: the Layer B and C matchers counted a vreg's reads over the
  whole function, and Layer C also rescanned the block prefix, for every
  candidate-shaped instruction. On one block of `AddRR`/`AndRR` pairs a
  release build took 1.55 s at 32,000 instructions and 49.5 s at 128,000;
  it now takes 17 ms and 74 ms. The walk keeps those facts in an index
  instead. Randomized, hand-built and selected-corpus tests require the same
  candidates, verdicts and final function as the scanning matchers, so the
  semantics revision is unchanged.
  **Wrong-code fix (pre-existing):** the Layer B and C matchers, their
  indexed walk facts and cache replay counted a register's reads as every
  operand after operand 0. A constant that a store, compare or `Movk` also
  read at operand 0 therefore looked single-use and its `Movz`/`Movk` chain
  was spliced out, leaving that read undefined. At O2 a 64-bit mask
  `(0x55555555 << 32) | 0x55555555` that is both ANDed and stored compiled to
  `and x0, x0, #0x5555555555555555; str x2, [x1]`, which stored whatever `x2`
  held. Reads and definitions now follow the shared operand-role model; a
  write at any operand position or under another register class also hides
  the materializer. Layer B admits only `AddRI` immediates that `ADD #imm12`
  encodes, so a `Movz #5000` feeding an `AddRR` no longer fails to encode.
  The Layer A, B and C obligations no longer compare an expression with
  itself (`x & m` against `x & m`). Each is built from the original window,
  the materializer read from its encoded fields, and from the replacement
  with its immediate encoded as the encoder does and then decoded, so AY
  refutes a wrong immediate, register or operation.
  `CEGIS_SEARCH_SEMANTICS_REVISION` is now 3, so no revision 2 entry replays.
  **Wrong-code fix (cache replay, pre-existing):** a cache hit applied each
  recorded replacement body as recorded. Entries carry no MAC, the codec
  checks only their format, and the cache wrote them under the process umask
  (`0775` directories and `0664` files on the Linux host). Without `HOME` or
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` its root is `/tmp/.trust-cg-cegis-cache`, which every user
  of the host shares. Overwriting the 8-byte `AndRI` immediate of the
  `cegis_mask_only` entry (`0x5555555555555555` to `0x3333333333333333`, still
  a logical immediate) made the next compile return `0x3333333333333333` for
  `cegis_mask_only(-1)`. Replay now rebuilds each replacement with the
  search's matcher on the current body. It applies the rewrite only if the
  rebuilt body equals the recorded one in opcode, register ids and classes
  and immediates. Any other entry is stale: the function is searched again
  and the entry rewritten. A cache root is used only if the current user
  owns it and no one else can write it; otherwise the process warns once and
  uses an in-memory cache. The cache creates directories `0700` and entries
  `0600`, and a compile without CEGIS no longer creates the root. A function
  whose block schedule lists an instruction id twice is no longer
  optimized, since an in-place rewrite changed both copies.
  `CEGIS_SEARCH_SEMANTICS_REVISION` stays 3 and the entry format stays 7. The
  search is unchanged, and an honest entry is exactly the body the matcher
  rebuilds, so it still replays. A skipped function never reads its entry.
- A mutable global in an explicit `.bss.rel.ro` or `.bss.rel.ro.*` section
  is refused again, now as `[TCG-SECTION-READONLY]` (L02-P7 repair). The
  first L02-P7 change admitted it as SHT_NOBITS `SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE`
  because the name matched the `.bss` family, although base `722e7611f`
  refused it. GNU ld 2.42 folds that input into `.bss`, so the program ran,
  but lld folds it into a `.bss.rel.ro` output inside `PT_GNU_RELRO`, so the
  first store faulted. On this host a mutable zero global stored through
  that section linked with `cc -fuse-ld=lld` (LLD 22.1.6) and died with
  SIGSEGV, and a C global with the same section attribute did the same. The
  zero-fill arm now applies the `.data.rel.ro` mutability rule to
  `.bss.rel.ro[.*]`. An immutable all-zero global there stays SHT_NOBITS,
  and `.bss.rel.rox` (no `.` boundary) is ordinary `.bss` zero fill. A
  nonzero or relocated request there is still `[TCG-SECTION-NOBITS]`,
  because content is checked first. The classifier unit matrix and
  `e2e_aarch64_elf_sections::unhonorable_elf_sections_are_refused_by_name`
  pin the new refusal, and a source-mutation control that drops it is
  caught. This is object and refusal evidence. lld still has no positive
  native run.
- AArch64 ELF zero fill now covers COMDAT definitions and explicit zero-fill
  sections (L02-P7). A zero-initialized `LinkOnce`, `LinkOnceOdr` or `WeakOdr`
  mutable global, and an all-zero COMDAT thread-local template, are no longer
  PROGBITS `.data.<sym>`/`.tdata.<sym>` with file bytes. Each is an SHT_NOBITS
  `.bss.<sym>` (`SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE|SHF_GROUP`) or `.tbss.<sym>` (plus
  `SHF_TLS`) member of its own `GRP_COMDAT` group, with alignment, symbol size
  and `STT_TLS` preserved. One class decision,
  `object_sections::ElfImplicitSection`, now serves both the shared implicit
  sections and the COMDAT `<base>.<symbol>` names. An explicit `.bss*`,
  `.tbss*`, `.sbss*` or `.lbss*` request whose global is all zero with no
  pointer slot is now an SHT_NOBITS section (`SHF_TLS` on `.tbss*`). The
  exception is a mutable global in `.bss.rel.ro[.*]`, which is refused as
  `[TCG-SECTION-READONLY]` (see the repair above). A nonzero initializer or a
  relocated pointer slot there is still refused by name as
  `[TCG-SECTION-NOBITS]`, and a thread-local mismatch as `[TCG-SECTION-TLS]`.
  The placed-section funnel also refuses nonzero NOBITS content before the
  reparse gate does. New reparse-gate, pipeline and classifier unit tests
  cover grouped NOBITS members and their refutations.
  `e2e_aarch64_elf_stack_zero_fill` gains COMDAT object rows at O0-O3, a
  mutation control for its independent group/NOBITS oracle, and a Linux row in
  which two objects defining the same zero link-once data and thread-local
  link with `cc` into one executable at O0-O3. That executable shares one
  instance (one per thread for TLS), GNU ld discards the second object's
  groups, and strong twins fail with "multiple definition".
  `e2e_aarch64_elf_sections` gains explicit zero-fill object and Linux rows,
  and its `.bss.tcg` refusal pin now uses a nonzero initializer. Native
  evidence covers GNU ld 2.42 and glibc 2.39 on one Linux AArch64 host, not
  lld or other ELF linkers, and is not a proof.
- Every AArch64 ELF relocation kind has a modeled window or a named
  disposition (L02-P10). `AArch64RelocType::relocation_limit` returns a
  `RelocationLimit`: the psABI window and who refuses an out-of-window value
  (`WindowDischarge`), the checked page relocation an unchecked low-12 form
  pairs with, full width, or no value. `displacement_window` now also returns
  the windows of `TLSDESC_ADR_PAGE21`, `ABS32`, `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12` and the
  never-emitted `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_LO12`. The existing windows are unchanged
  except `PREL32`, which now has the signed bound `-2^31 <= X < 2^31` of
  aaelf64 2026Q2, the bound `.eh_frame` readers apply. A unit test pins every
  code the checked writer decodes. New refusals: a local-exec access whose
  `TPREL` this object already bounds at `2^24` or above
  (`PipelineError::LocalExecTlsWindowExceeded`, `[TCG-RELOC-WINDOW-TLSLE]`), a
  DWARF32 `ABS32` addend above `2^32 - 1`
  (`DwarfEmitError::Abs32AddendOutOfWindow`, `[TCG-RELOC-WINDOW-ABS32]`), and,
  after a successful link, a linked image whose GOT is out of the page window
  of its code when an AArch64 ELF input uses `ADR_GOT_PAGE`,
  `TLSIE_ADR_GOTTPREL_PAGE21` or `TLSDESC_ADR_PAGE21`
  (`link_driver::got_page_window_output_refusals`,
  `error[link:relocation-out-of-range]`, `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`). The
  last is needed because GNU ld 2.42 links such a GOT 8 GiB away without a
  diagnostic and writes the page delta truncated. LLD 22.1.6 refuses it. Such
  a link is staged like a local-exec link (L02-P9 second repair): the image is
  checked at the driver-owned staging path and installed only when it passes,
  so no refusal reads, writes or removes the requested output. A staged image
  that cannot be read as ELF is refused as `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNCHECKED]`
  (`error[link:unclassified]`), a staged link that writes nothing (for example
  `-Wl,--version` under the `pic` model) is refused with
  `[TCG-LINK-NO-OUTPUT]`, and a checked image never replaces an output that is
  neither a regular file nor a symbolic link. Every link through `run_link` or
  the CLI whose AArch64 ELF inputs carry a GOT-page `ADRP`, which every `pic`,
  initial-exec or TLS-descriptor object does, is therefore staged and needs a
  writable directory next to its output: `-o /dev/null` with such an input is
  refused. (The GOT region this bullet's check used was repaired later; see
  the first bullet.) `e2e_aarch64_link_runtime` gains
  native controls for the `TLSLE`, `ABS32` and GOT-page windows and for fused
  Q-register (`LDST128`) execution (28/28 on the Linux AArch64 host). This is
  linker and execution evidence, not proof. LIMITATIONS.md has the per-kind
  table.
- NEON LD1/ST1 post-index with a live base-register writeback now runs
  natively on Linux AArch64 (X-OPCODES-P11). The new floor target
  `neon_butterfly_writeback_execution` builds three trust-ir radix-2 FFT
  butterfly loops in the shape `neon_butterfly` admits and compiles them
  through `Compiler` at O0-O3. At O2 and O3 each kernel's vector body walks
  four pointers with two `LD1 {Vt.4S}, [Xn], #16` and two
  `ST1 {Vt.4S}, [Xn], #16` words. Nothing recomputes those pointers, so each
  writeback is the next iteration's address. Two decoders must agree on every
  word of the ELF and Mach-O objects. A walk over the decoded control flow
  shows each of the 12 writebacks is read as a base on the next iteration
  before any redefinition. The same walk calls the `neon_fmap` remainder
  writebacks dead, and calls the butterfly writebacks dead once the loop's
  backward branch is removed. The gate refuses O0/O1, O2 with
  `neon_butterfly` disabled, and 48 mutated words per container. A C oracle
  (one inline-asm scalar instruction per operation, in the loop's operand
  order) compares the whole buffer bit for bit after each of 28,899 calls per
  level. The calls cover vector pairs, odd scalar tails, whole-scalar calls
  and nineteen stream/twiddle placements, 12 admitted by the pass and 7
  routed to its scalar loop. At O2 and O3 all 48 single-word mutants fail the
  oracle. That includes the 24 that only drop the writeback (`[Xn]`) or
  replace `#16` by a register the decoded stream proves holds 8. Those fail
  only in calls with two or more vector pairs, never in one-pair or
  scalar-path calls. The [qualifying Linux
  run](reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-neon-butterfly-writeback/README.md)
  passed on clean `59ef39126`: 4 tests in the target and 4,089 codegen library
  tests. LLVM and GNU objdump agree with the counts, and in their listings
  each base register appears in the loop only as its own LD1/ST1's base. This
  is execution and object evidence for these shapes, not a proof. The target
  is also a Darwin floor row (minimum 4), not yet run on macOS.
- The Linux required-floor target `jit_icache_coherence` now fails when the
  walk inside `sys::flush_icache` (the function the publisher calls) omits
  its `ic ivau` loop or widens its stride (Linux half of L11-P4). Its
  republication rows land on fresh pages, which the kernel maintains itself,
  so they passed without the walk. The new public
  `jit::flush_instruction_cache(start, len)` calls that same function over
  caller-owned code; an empty range returns without visiting any line, so a
  dangling `start` with `len` 0 no longer faults. Two new Linux-only rows use
  it to rewrite a test-owned page in place 1,024 times: one executes on the
  writing core and one on a second pinned core after `isb`, each once per
  core type (the host has Cortex-X925 and Cortex-A725 cores). Unmaintained
  witness rounds alternate with production-walk rounds. Every production
  round must execute the new code. With CTR_EL0.DIC 0, at least one witness
  round must execute stale code, so the row cannot pass vacuously.
  On the Linux AArch64 host (CTR_EL0 `0x9444c004`), removing the `ic ivau`
  walk or doubling its stride to 128 bytes fails both rows in every retained
  run. The real and restored sources pass. Removing only the `dc cvau` walk
  is not detected, because the host's IDC is 1.
  These rows pin the walk's contents, not that publication calls it.
  Removing the publisher's call to the walk (in
  `MappedRegion::seal_rx_and_verify`) is not detected by any execution row
  on Linux, because the kernel maintains the fresh pages publication maps. A
  host-neutral structural row therefore reads a per-thread walk record
  (`jit::instruction_cache_walks_on_current_thread`) around each
  publication and requires a completed walk that starts at the image and
  covers it. It fails when the call is removed or walks half the image; a
  second row fails when the empty-range return is removed. The record shows
  the call, not its cache effect or its order relative to the seal. The
