  Darwin floor minimum for the target rises from 3 to 5.
  Evidence: `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-icache-in-place-control` and
  `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-icache-publisher-walk-control`. This is
  execution evidence from one host, not proof. The Darwin half has no
  retained run, so L11-P4 stays PARTIAL.
- The link driver's local-exec TLS guard now follows the output the linker
  actually wrote (L02-P9 repair). The first version ran only for a `--shared`
  request, so `-Wl,--shared` or `-Wl,--Bshareable` (and GNU ld's
  abbreviations such as `-Wl,-shar`) still produced a library that addressed
  the executable's TLS block (exit 236 instead of 42). `--shared` and
  `--Bshareable` are now driver-owned `-Wl` spellings. After any successful
  link that has a local-exec (`R_AARCH64_TLSLE_*`) AArch64 ELF input,
  `run_link` reads the output back. Unless the output is `ET_EXEC`, `ET_DYN`
  with `DF_1_PIE`, or `ET_REL`, it removes the file and refuses it by name
  (`LinkError::OutputRefused`, `error[link:tls-model-mismatch]`,
  `[TCG-LINK-TLS-MODEL]`).
  The classifier also names an executable's local-exec reference to a
  thread-local that a shared library defines as `tls-model-mismatch`. For
  GNU ld this is `relocation truncated to fit: R_AARCH64_TLSLE_* ... defined
  in <section> section in <lib>.so[.N]`; for lld it is `relocation
  R_AARCH64_TLSLE_* cannot be used against symbol ...; recompile with
  -fPIC`. Previously these were `relocation-out-of-range` and
  `non-pic-relocation`. The same truncation against a thread-local defined
  in an object stays `relocation-out-of-range`.
  Evidence: native CLI and e2e controls, and unit tests on complete captured
  stderr, in `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-tls-model-output-guard`. This is
  execution evidence from one host, not proof. Archive members and links
  made outside trust-cg are still not examined.
  Second repair (2026-09-23): that read-back read the requested output path
  itself, so `-Wl,--outp=<file>` or `-Wl,-o<file>` put a local-exec library
  elsewhere unchecked (exit 236) and `-Wl,--version` got an existing `-o`
  file read and deleted; on Linux `parse_wl_group` now refuses every `-Wl`
  spelling GNU ld 2.42 reads as a driver-owned option (abbreviations with
  one or two dashes, `=<value>`, `-o<file>`, `-h<name>`, `-R<dir>`, `-G`),
  and a link with a local-exec input writes to a driver-owned staging
  directory whose image is installed only after the check, a successful
  link that wrote nothing there is refused (`[TCG-LINK-NO-OUTPUT]`), and no
  refusal touches the output path (evidence: the same report, second
  repair).
  Third repair (2026-09-23): a forwarded value that begins with `@` (the
  output or an input path, `-L`, `-l`, the soname, a run-time search path)
  is now refused before anything runs (`[TCG-LINK-RESPONSE-FILE]`), because
  gcc, collect2 and GNU ld expand it as a response file (`--rpath @resp`
  with `resp` holding `/x --shared -o libevil.so` had GNU ld write a
  local-exec library), and the documentation now states that only
  positional AArch64 ELF64 relocatable inputs are scanned and that the staged
  read-back runs only when one of them carries `R_AARCH64_TLSLE_*`, so a
  local-exec object named inside a `-Wl` group, as `-l:<file>`, as an
  archive member, by a linker script's `INPUT()` or inside a shared-library
  input is not examined (evidence: the same report, third repair).
- The link driver names TLS-model mismatches and refuses local-exec TLS in a
  shared object (L02-P9). `LinkDiagnosticKind` gains `TlsModelMismatch`
  (`error[link:tls-model-mismatch]`) and `TlsSymbolTypeMismatch`
  (`error[link:tls-symbol-type-mismatch]`). The first matches lld's
  `relocation R_AARCH64_TLSLE_* against <symbol> cannot be used with -shared`
  and GNU ld's `TLS relocation R_AARCH64_TLSLE_* against undefined symbol`.
  The second matches GNU ld's four `TLS ... mismatches non-TLS ...` forms.
  Only exact psABI relocation names and the captured sentence shapes count;
  near misses stay `unclassified`. On the Linux AArch64 host, GNU ld 2.42
  linked a `trust-cg -shared` library whose `static`-model object defines
  and reads a thread-local with local-exec TLS. An executable with its own
  thread-local then exited 236 instead of 42, because the library had bumped
  the executable's variable. `link_driver::run_link` therefore reads every
  AArch64 ELF relocatable input of a shared-object link and refuses a
  `R_AARCH64_TLSLE_*` relocation by name (`[TCG-LINK-TLS-MODEL]`,
  `LinkError::InputRefused`) before the linker runs. Native controls: the
  CLI refuses the `static` and `pie` `-shared` links; the same module runs
  as an executable, and built `pic` it links `-shared` and runs (42); a
  TLS/non-TLS clash between two CLI inputs fails with the named kind and its
  thread-local twin runs; and the host GNU ld's refusal of a trust-cg
  local-exec import classifies as `tls-model-mismatch`. The object check
  does not examine archive members, shared libraries, linker scripts or
  links made outside the driver. Evidence:
  `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-tls-model-link-controls`.
- NEON LD1/ST1 post-index execution on Linux (X-OPCODES-P11): the new required
  floor target `neon_ld1_st1_post_execution` compiles ten trust-ir f32/f64 map
  loops through `Compiler` at O0-O3. At O2 and O3 `neon_fmap` vectorizes eight
  of them. Their one-vector remainder loops use `LD1 {Vt.4S|.2D}, [Xn], #16`
  and `ST1 {Vt.4S|.2D}, [Xn], #16`. The eight are in-place maps in both loop
  shapes and rotated two- and three-array maps behind the pass's runtime
  disjointness check. The target decodes every word of the final ELF and
  Mach-O objects with trust-cg-lift and with its own bit mask. It requires
  exact per-kernel LD1/ST1 counts (12 and 8) and refuses scalar-only objects
  (O0, O1, O2 with `neon_fmap` disabled) and 80 mutated LD1/ST1 words per
  container. It links the host object with `cc` against a C oracle (FP
  contraction off) and compares the whole buffer bit for bit after each of
  38,376 calls per level. The calls cover main-loop, remainder and scalar-tail
  lanes, guards, NaN, infinity and subnormal inputs, and overlapping layouts,
  including loop-carried ones. At O2 and O3, all 100 mutated objects fail
  against the oracle (each LD1/ST1 word narrowed to 64 bits or removed, and
  each vector FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV swapped). Evidence boundary: the oracle
  observes the LD1/ST1 transfer, not the post-index base update. `neon_fmap`
  recomputes every remainder pointer with MADD, so the writeback of all 20
  executed words is dead. The target enforces this: at O2 and O3 each word
  rewritten to the no-writeback `[Xn]` form or to register post-index `[Xn],
  X1` (40 objects per level) must pass the oracle and be refused by the decode
  gate, so the post-index form is pinned only by the decode gate. The only
  scheduled emitter with a live LD1/ST1 writeback, `neon_butterfly`, had no
  native control in that target; `neon_butterfly_writeback_execution` (entry
  above) now executes it. The target
  is also a Darwin floor row (minimum 4). The [qualifying Linux
  run](reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-neon-ld1-st1-post/README.md) passed on
  clean `4eafcaccf`: 4 tests in the target and 4,069 codegen library tests.
  LLVM and GNU objdump agree with the per-kernel counts. This is execution and
  object evidence, not a proof. The `neon_map.rs` and `neon_condstore.rs`
  LD1/ST1 emitters and the `vectorize.rs` contains4 LD1 are unreachable in
  the default pipelines and have no native control. The `vectorize.rs` i32
  induction-store ST1 runs by default again (Vectorizer loop idioms, above).
- TrustIR ARC operations run natively on Linux AArch64 (L05-P3): the new floor
  target `e2e_aarch64_arc_ops_linux` compiles a corpus that declares the exact
  Clean RC triple (`clean_inc`/`clean_dec`/`clean_is_exclusive`) and drives
  `Retain`/`Release`/`IsUnique` on `CMalloc` and `RustHeap` cells. At O0-O3 it
  links against a C counting runtime. That runtime keeps a side table seeded
  at count 1 by the wrapped allocators, frees at zero and sets the unspecified
  upper bits of its `u8` result. Every result must equal the trust-ir
  reference interpreter's, and per-step counts and frees must equal the
  driver's constant traces. Retain-leak and release-past-zero negative
  controls are included, and inverted-polarity and never-free driver builds
  are harness self-checks. Host-neutral rows pin 7/10/12 `R_AARCH64_CALL26`
  `BL` sites with three mutation negatives. The same bodies are refused by
  name without the exact triple, and `Ty::Rc`, `SwiftHeap`/`CleanHeap` cells
  and cross-function `Dealloc` stay refused. The target is registered on the
  Linux floor (146 targets) and on the Darwin floor (four host-neutral rows,
  which have not yet run on Darwin). The construct inventory keeps
  Retain/Release/IsUnique model-only, because its executed disposition
  requires native execution on aarch64-apple-darwin and the native row is
  compiled out there; each row's note cites the Linux-only native row. The
  qualifying run is retained in `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-arc-ops`. This
  is execution evidence against a stand-in runtime, not proof, and not an
  execution of the Clean runtime.
- Installed JIT bindings carry a kernel page-protection witness on Linux
  (L11-P6, still PARTIAL): `ExecutableMemoryProtection` gains a
  `PageProtectionWitness`: its source, the permissions its recorded
  protection implies (`r-xp`), and the kernel's `/proc/self/maps` permissions
  for the whole allocation, read right after the read-execute seal. macOS and
  Windows record an explicit `recorded_only` source. `InstalledPayloadBinding`
  moves to v6 and `trust-cg.artifact` manifests to v3; v5 bindings and v2
  manifests are refused, not migrated, and the `wp0` manifest goldens move
  once. Three installed routes (`get_contract_symbol_bound`,
  `native_install_gate_packet(_for_surface)` and `into_installed_artifact`)
  observe the kernel again before reading any code byte and refuse by name a
  writable-and-executable observation (`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-WX]`), any
  other difference from the recorded permissions
  (`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-MISMATCH]`), an uncovered range
  (`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-UNCOVERED]`) and an unreadable answer
  (`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-UNREADABLE]`); raw installed and buffer lookups
  (`entrypoint`, `entrypoint_ptr`, `ensure_published_entrypoint_ptr`) are not
  re-checked. The kernel is asked through the `PROCMAP_QUERY` ioctl (Linux
  6.11 and later), one self-consistent answer per VMA. The text fallback is
  built chunk by chunk with the lock dropped between chunks, so under
  concurrent mapping changes one read can list a VMA twice; it retries the
  whole file up to 16 times when rows at or after the range overlap or go
  backwards or the range is uncovered, tolerates disorder wholly below the
  range, refuses a malformed row at once, and refuses by name after the last
  attempt. (The first version refused any out-of-order row and failed the
  parallel library suite in 5 of 9 runs.) Resealed bindings with a foreign
  source (`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-SOURCE]`) or a forged recorded string
  (`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-RECORDED]`) are refused too. `jit_wx_refusal` gains
  six rows, including `mprotect` RW/RWX/no-access/read-only negatives on an
  installed allocation and a Linux churn row (eight threads mapping,
  protecting, unmapping and allocating) that requires zero spurious
  refusals; its Darwin minimum rises to 6. No observation is one instant of
  the whole process, and thread or lease context is still unbound. Only
  AArch64 Linux has run the witness.
- AArch64 ELF function sections are an allowlist, and the parallel emitter
  is tested (L02-P1, L02-P3 review repair):
  `object_sections::classify_elf_function_section` now honours only a
  `.text`-prefixed name or a name without a leading `.`. It refuses every
  other dot-prefixed name. `.jcr`, `.tm_clone_table`, `.rodata1`, `.tcommon`
  and the other data families get `[TCG-SECTION-DATA]`. The unwind and debug
  families (`.eh_frame*`, `.gcc_except_table*`, `.gnu_extab*`,
  `.exception_ranges*`, `.sframe*`, `.stab*`, `.line*`) and the rest get
  `[TCG-SECTION-RESERVED]`. The old deny-list accepted `.jcr`, which GNU ld
  2.42 linked into an RWX RELRO segment and which then crashed at run time;
  `.stab`, which broke the link; and `.rodata1` and `.eh_frame.x`, which were
  merged into data and unwind output. The `Compiler::compile` trace's
  `compile_module` entry now names the preparation and emission path
  (sequential, parallel with its worker count, or cached). The visibility
  object rows use a 48-definition module, and a new 40-definition
  explicit-section row asserts from that trace that the parallel emitter ran.
  The parallel object is also byte-identical to the sequential one. The
  2026-09-23 function-attrs evidence archive now stores its objects as
  `*.o.gz`, so its check passes on a clean checkout.
- AArch64 ELF function visibility and sections (L02-P1, L02-P3):
  `Compiler::compile` now honours trust-ir v45 `Function.visibility` and
  `Function.section` on AArch64 ELF. The adapter admits them only under the
  new `ObjectSymbolPolicy::AARCH64_ELF_MODULE`, which the compiler selects for
  that object path alone; every other entry keeps refusing both facets
  (`FunctionSymbolFactPolicy::Refuse`). `FunctionSymbolBinding::for_trust_ir_definition`
  now takes `(linkage, visibility)` and returns its refusal reason, so hidden
  and protected global or weak definitions become `STV_HIDDEN` /
  `STV_PROTECTED`. A named function's body lands in an
  `SHF_ALLOC|SHF_EXECINSTR` section of that name through the text planner
  that `--function-sections` uses, with its relocations and FDE anchored
  there. Functions naming one section share it, a COMDAT function gets its
  own grouped section of that name, and an explicit `.text` stays in the
  shared `.text`. `ModuleSymbolLinkage::with_explicit_function_sections`
  carries the names and `object_sections::classify_elf_function_section`
  validates them. Refused by name: visibility on an `Internal`/`Private`
  function or (at this entry) an import (`[TCG-FUNCTION-VISIBILITY]`), a
  section on a declaration, malformed names on every lane
  (`[TCG-SECTION-NAME]`), data-class names (the new `[TCG-SECTION-DATA]`),
  `.init`/`.fini` and owned names, a name shared with a data global, a
  COMDAT function naming `.text`, both facets on Mach-O, x86-64, RISC-V, the
  JIT and Wasm, and `-g` with the split text. At this entry hidden and
  protected functions stayed GOT-addressed and were never inlined under
  `pic`. Newer entries above in this section supersede both: the L02-P1
  declaration entry admits hidden and protected function declarations (the
  refusal now covers only `Internal`/`Private`), and the L02-P6 product fix
  makes a hidden or protected definition's address PC-relative and lets a
  strong one be inlined. New object rows read bindings, sections,
  relocations and FDE anchors with independent ELF
  readers, and mutation controls show those checkers refuse altered
  objects. New Linux rows run a `.trust_ir` text module through
  `Compiler::compile` (PIC, O0–O3) into a `cc -shared` library: hidden
  functions are absent from `.dynsym` and protected ones are
  `STV_PROTECTED`. An `LD_PRELOAD` interposer rebinds only the
  default-visibility call. Under `--gc-sections` the linker drops only the
  unreferenced named section. The pin-move floor gains rows for the three
  function facets. The
  [qualifying Linux run](reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-elf-function-attrs/README.md)
  passed on clean `b68b16269`: 19 and 18 tests in the two families, 4,067
  codegen and 1,879 lower library tests. This is object and execution
  evidence, not a proof;
  function `retained`, Mach-O function visibility and sections, and the
  bridge's `#[link_section]` and function visibility are still not carried.
- AArch64 ELF link (C-01): the link driver's `-Wl` parser refuses the BTI/PAC
  link requests `-z force-bti`, `-z pac-plt` and `-z bti-report[=<mode>]`, in
  the `-z,<keyword>` and `-z<keyword>` spellings and beside other options,
  with the named code `[TCG-LINK-BTI-PAC]` on every target. trust-cg emits no
  BTI landing pads, no PAC instructions and no
  `GNU_PROPERTY_AARCH64_FEATURE_1_AND` note. The reason differs per keyword,
  as checked on the Linux AArch64 host with GNU ld 2.42 and LLD 22.
  `-z force-bti` makes both linkers mark the output BTI. `-z pac-plt` makes
  lld mark the output PAC; GNU ld adds no property but emits authenticating
  PLT stubs (`DT_AARCH64_PAC_PLT`), and on that glibc 2.39 host even a C-only
  executable linked that way dies with SIGILL at the stub's `autia1716`.
  `-z bti-report` marks nothing (GNU ld ignores it, lld only reports
  unmarked inputs) and is refused only as part of a BTI link configuration.
  Each refusal message states its keyword's reason. The `-z execstack`
  refusal and the `-Wl,-z,noexecstack` request on every Linux link are
  unchanged. The link-driver unit test pins every spelling; the CLI unit test
  and `link_options` pin three each. On Linux AArch64,
  `e2e_aarch64_elf_stack_zero_fill` adds two controls. GNU `readelf -n`
  finds no `NT_GNU_PROPERTY_TYPE_0` in 48 route objects, and a compiler-made
  BTI/PAC object shows that the check detects one. A direct
  `cc -shared -Wl,-z,force-bti` link of a CG object succeeds with GNU ld's
  BTI warning naming it (matched by the warning text, not by a path
  containing `force-bti`) and a BTI-marked output. A startfile-free executable
  that calls the CG function through a pointer returns 42 when linked
  normally. When `/proc/cpuinfo` lists `bti`, the same executable linked
  with `-z force-bti` is run and its outcome recorded, not asserted: SIGILL
  after the call marker at O0–O3 on the Grace host. The RWE dlopen control
  must fail on glibc 2.41 or later. This host has glibc 2.39, which loads
  it, so only that load is recorded and the 2.41 assertion has never run.

- AArch64 DWARF (L03-P4 review repair): `aarch64_elf_dwarf` again checks
  two-function `-g` module objects from the legacy lines-only
  `compile_module_emission` entry, the description the `Compiler`/CLI `-g`
  path emits. At O0–O3, in both orders with the second function past offset
  0, they pass `llvm-dwarfdump --verify` and the line-row and symbol checks.
  They carry no `DW_TAG_formal_parameter`, no `DW_TAG_variable` and no
  `.debug_loc`. The lines-only object is also checked by the
  field-by-field relocation-target test, the relocation-neutralization
  mutations and the `-g` leg of the function-sections refusal, beside the
  provenance-bearing object. Doc comments, the plan and the retained report
  no longer present every unshifted module range as refused by emission. They
  also no longer claim that the gdb module leg checks each local wherever a
  range claims it. LIMITATIONS.md now records that a leaf-first module's
  single line sequence gives the fixture's prologue the leaf's last line.

- AArch64 DWARF (L03-P4): whole-module objects can now describe each
  function's parameters and variables. A `-g` preparation keeps the
  function's register-debug provenance in the new
  `PreparationMetrics::debug_provenance` field. The new sibling entry
  `Pipeline::compile_module_emission_with_debug_provenance` threads it into
  module DWARF emission. The single-function parameter/variable builder is
  factored out and reused per module function, over the instruction list the
  module encoder emitted (after the `RBIT`-return copy cleanup). Every
  location-list range is moved to the function's text offset. Emission
  refuses a range outside its function as
  `DwarfEmitError::AddressOutOfFunction`, which catches every unshifted
  entry-range parameter location; an unshifted range that lands inside the
  function is caught only by the tests' location checker and gdb.
  Without provenance, a function keeps single-function parity: parameters
  located, provenance-backed locals with empty location lists. No existing
  signature changed. The legacy and parallel module entries and the
  `Compiler`/CLI `-g` path still describe subprograms and lines only.
  `aarch64_elf_dwarf` now requires the fixture's and leaf's parameter and
  variable DIEs in module objects, with the fixture at text offset 0 and
  past the leaf, at O0–O3. The location checker accepts them against
  `llvm-objdump`, and its three mutation controls are refused on the module
  object. The target also adds a no-provenance parity test and a
  host-neutral Mach-O module control; its Darwin minimum rises from 11 to 13.
  `e2e_aarch64_elf_debugger_linux` adds a gdb leg over a linked module
  object at O0–O3 that reads the parameter at entry, the constant local and
  the spilled probe at the body-line stop, and the register-held probe at
  the start of its first range. This is object and debugger evidence for these
  fixtures, not a proof of value correspondence. Bridge debuginfo and
  function-section `-g` stay absent/refused. The qualifying Linux run is
  retained in `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-module-dwarf-variables/`. It
  also records a pre-existing stale-slot description of `acc` from O1,
  where gdb reads 0 for a source value of 10; LIMITATIONS.md states it.
- rustc bridge (L06-P4, L03-P7): the Darwin-only `#[thread_local]` fixture has
  a Linux ELF twin, `tls_thread_local_linux`, and `check_linux_aarch64_bridge.py`
  now requires it as a second native target. It compiles the same crate for
  `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` at O0–O3 through the runner's freshly built
  backend (bound by path and SHA-256) with the `no-proof-certs` knob, selects
  objects by defined symbol, and checks with `readelf` that `X` is one
  `STT_TLS` definition in `.tdata` that the accessor object imports as
  undefined `STT_TLS` through only complete relocation pairs of exactly one
  access model against `X` (observed: three initial-exec
  `R_AARCH64_TLSIE_*_GOTTPREL_*` pairs; local-exec is the only accepted
  alternative). Every CG and LLVM executable links with `cc -pthread`, carries
  `PT_TLS` and runs five times against the Darwin fixture's two-thread
  isolation driver. The plain-`static mut` control exits 3 (shared storage
  detected) with both compilers, and a `#[link_section = ".custom"]`
  thread-local is refused by name, leaving no object that defines an item,
  while LLVM places it in `.custom`. The runner runs both targets whatever the
  other's verdict, records a per-target `target_status`, and passes only when
  both pass, so it still fails overall on the ABI target's pre-existing
  `[TCG-PROOF-465]` refusal (L06-P1). Five new script tests pin the TLS
  marker, the fixture's backend and knob contract, and byte identity with the
  Darwin crate and driver. The shared knob-option probe no longer inherits the
  runner's `TCG_TEST_BACKEND_*` pair, which trustc refuses: a knob-using target
  would otherwise have skipped under the runner. Bridge comments that said
  non-Darwin TLS fails closed now describe the ELF models, the bridge's
  thread-local emission messages no longer call an ELF definition a TLV
  descriptor, and the provisioning table lists the runner's new `objdump`
  requirement. This is testing evidence without proof certificates (without
  the knob both accessors are refused at `[TCG-PROOF-465]`); the unwind,
  drop/heap, static-data and coroutine lanes stay Darwin-only, and both rows
  stay open.
- `compiler::tests::test_aarch64_parallel_and_serial_multi_function_byte_identical`
  had failed on main since the pair-memory proof credit was withdrawn: its six
  multiply-by-constant leaves keep frames with no proof owner (`Imul` is outside
  the source-bound affine lane), so every compilation with `emit_proofs` refused
  at `StpPreIndex`, and no gate runs the codegen library tests. The positive
  module is now six admitted affine leaves (add, sub, doubling, 12-bit, shifted
  and chained immediates) whose serial and parallel objects and proof bundles
  must be identical; like the JIT proof-policy tests it needs the AY solver and
  Clean checker on a pinned route, and fails with that named message without
  them. The multiply module stays as a control that serial and parallel
  compilation refuse identically, naming the unproved frame pair.
- AArch64 (L05-P10, L03-P6): a function-body `Constant::SymbolAddr` naming a
  thread-local the module declares (definition or import, any addend) is now
  refused by name in the trust-ir adapter (`[TCG-TLS-SYMBOL-ADDR]`; the adapter
  is shared by every target, but only AArch64 triples are tested) instead of lowering to a plain page reference: on Linux it emitted
  `R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21`/`ADD_ABS_LO12_NC` against the `STT_TLS` symbol,
  which GNU ld 2.42 only warns about and links to an address that is not
  `&tp`; on Mach-O the page reference named the TLV descriptor. `GlobalAddr`
  remains the TLS access path. Pinned by an adapter unit test (ELF static,
  PIE and PIC, and Mach-O) and a host-neutral `e2e_aarch64_globals_linux` row
  through the `Compiler` on Linux and Darwin triples, with plain-data controls
  that still compile; with the check disabled both fail. The Linux-only
  helpers of `e2e_aarch64_globals_linux` are now gated with its native module,
  so the target builds under the workspace's `warnings = "deny"` on hosts
  without the Linux GNU legs (checked here by compiling a temporary copy with

  handed to the `Pipeline` API that names a thread-local object global is not
  refused.
- AArch64 ELF (L05-P10, L03-P6): a thread-local whose initial-value template
  embeds symbol addresses (`__thread void *p = &x;`) is now emitted instead of
  refused: the template stays in PROGBITS `.tdata` and each slot is one
  `R_AARCH64_ABS64` (addend in `r_addend`) in `.rela.tdata`, the rows gcc
  emits; the relocation inventory counts those rows. A pointer slot whose
  target is itself a thread-local (data or template holder, definition or
  import) is refused by name on ELF, Mach-O, the inventory and the JIT data
  image (`[TCG-TLS-SLOT-TARGET]`); before this, neither a data slot nor a
  Mach-O template slot naming one had a refusal. New Linux floor target
  `e2e_aarch64_globals_linux` (15 tests; 6 host-neutral rows required on the
  Darwin floor) runs a pthread C driver against a
  `static __thread` C oracle at O0-O3 in static/PIE executables (LE/IE) and a
  `dlopen`ed TLSDESC shared object, checks `.rela.tdata` with readelf against
  gcc, and adds a record-drop byte mutation and a non-TLS driver-sensitivity
  control, plus Linux runs of the JIT data image, a body `SymbolAddr` addend
  and hidden/retained data attributes. `e2e_aarch64_elf_link`'s refusal pin
  became a positive `.rela.tdata` control; the Darwin pin in
  `e2e_aarch64_globals_darwin` was retargeted from a Linux host and has not
  run on macOS. Execution and object evidence, not proof.
- Linux AArch64 arithmetic AOT, linked-image byte binding (`L11-P3`, still
  PARTIAL): `scripts/check_aarch64_aot_arithmetic.py` (report schema v2) now
  binds each case's `cc`-linked PIE to its audited object. It parses both ELF64
  files with the Python standard library, locates `calculate` by its `.symtab`
  symbol through the executable `PT_LOAD` (a PIE's address is link-time), and
  requires its words to equal the object's `.text`. The object's one
  `.eh_frame` `R_AARCH64_PREL32` must resolve to exactly one linked FDE at that
  address whose CIE/FDE bytes match the object's modulo trailing `DW_CFA_nop`,
  and `.eh_frame_hdr` must index that FDE. Each row records the image SHA-256,
  address, file offset, size and relocation counts, and three per-case
  negatives must be refused as `linked-image-mismatch`: the last function word
  patched, the FDE `pc_begin` patched, and the oracle linked against a foreign
  same-named `calculate`. New classes `linked-image-mismatch`,
  `linked-image-unsupported` (any Mach-O image included) and
  `linked-image-control-failed`; the 48-case denominator, the failure classes'
  meanings and the nine-query replay are unchanged. The step is injectable, so
  the fake-tool tests keep running, and it is tested on minimal ELF64 fixtures
  and the 48 object/PIE pairs retained on 2026-09-20. The CLI's ELF
  `--emit-proofs` identity case now links the certified object with `cc` on
  aarch64 Linux (a missing `cc` fails it), compares `_identity`'s linked words
  with the object's `.text` and executes it. Both are byte comparisons by the
  runner and the test, not a certificate over the linked image. The
  [retained run](reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-linked-image-binding/README.md)
  at clean `f2a53aadf` passes 48/48 cases, binds all 48 executables and
  refuses all 144 negatives; GNU readelf and `llvm-objdump` agree with every
  recorded address, size, relocation, FDE and word.
- x86-64 bridge, a P0 the corpus sweep found (not the census): a closure whose
  OWN parameter is a `&[T]` / `&str` slice (`|s: &[u8]| ..`, `|t: &str, k| ..`)

- x86-64 selector (`trust-cg-lower`) and bridge, third batch (one census,

- L01-P5 (Linux hidden-result `sret` through X8): new Linux floor target
  `e2e_aarch64_sret_linux` (8 tests), the ELF and Linux-native twin of the
  Darwin `e2e_aarch64_sret` fixture over a corpus now shared through

  reader and the `trust-cg-lift` decoder that every corpus function is a
  defined global `STT_FUNC` of non-zero size in an executable section and
  every C callee an undefined global, and that the static-provenance
  `CallIndirect` edge to the pre-lowered `sret` declaration stays an indirect
  call (X8 written before a `BLR`, no `BL`, no `R_AARCH64_CALL26`/`JUMP26`
  against the declaration), each with byte-mutation controls, plus the
  refusals that stay (non-leading hidden parameter, hidden parameter beside a
  result, disagreeing edge, indirect variadic, variadic definition). The
  Linux-only rows link with the host `cc` (GCC 13.3 on the floor host) and
  execute C caller -> CG callee and CG caller -> C callee for both shapes
  through `volatile`/static/dynamic function pointers and variadic callees at
  O0-O3, all passing on the Linux AArch64 host in the first run. Where base
  AAPCS64 (Arm IHI 0055) differs from DarwinPCS the rule is encoded rather
  than copied: the two stack-passed `int32_t` arguments take 8-byte slots
  (§6.8.2 stage C rule C.16 in the current Arm numbering, C.14 being the NSAA
  rounding; a Linux-only wide-slot row calls the CG callees through an
  `int64_t` prototype with poisoned high halves and shows that AAPCS64 places
  the narrow pair in the same 8-byte slots and that the CG callees' `I32`
  add/sub results are unaffected by the high halves; because the corpus uses
  those arguments only in 32-bit add/sub, that row does not distinguish a
  callee reading the full slot from one reading its low 32 bits, so
  callee-side narrow handling is evidenced only by
  `e2e_aarch64_bool_abi_linux`, not here), and a variadic call's anonymous
  arguments take the remaining registers before the stack. Execution
  evidence, not proof of the convention; the
  structural-only Darwin residuals (dynamic pre-lowered pointers, indirect
  variadic calls, variadic definitions) are unchanged.
- L05-P10 (Darwin globals: relocated TLS templates, JIT data image, `SymbolAddr`
  addends, data-symbol attributes): the AArch64 Mach-O emitter now relocates

  initial-value template (`__thread void *p = &x;`, one `ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED`
  per slot with the addend baked in, registered in the relocation inventory),
  which ld64 and the standalone linker rebase so every thread starts from the
  fixed-up pointers; the AArch64 ELF and x86-64 Mach-O templates keep their
  named refusal. The in-memory AArch64 JIT places module globals in a
  JIT-owned read-write data image mapped beside the code: `GlobalRef`
  (`Page21`/`Pageoff12`) sites are patched at the final addresses, `ExternRef`
  (`GotLoadPage21`/`GotLoadPageoff12`) sites load imports, preemptible
  definitions and function addresses from JIT GOT slots, pointer slots inside
  the image are relocated, and the image manifest (placements, bytes,
  relocation list, imports) is bound into each function's certificate-cache
  identity, the buffer's live replay identity and its replay metadata
  (`ExecutableBuffer::data_image`, `data_symbol_ptr`,
  `JitCompiler::compile_raw_with_globals`). A verifying JIT request refuses
  every data or GOT site by name (`JitDataRelocationProofUnavailable`), and a
  body naming a thread-local, an explicit-section global or a weak import is
  refused (`JitDataGlobalUnplaceable`). A function-body
  `Constant::SymbolAddr` with a non-zero addend lowers as the bare symbol
  reference plus an explicit `Iconst`/`Iadd` (module batching no longer
  defers it). New Darwin floor target `e2e_aarch64_globals_darwin` (7 tests):
  relocated TLS templates (data, function and interior pointers; per-thread
  isolation and shared writes) against a pthread C driver, a JIT body that
  reads and writes a module global, a string constant, a function-pointer
  table and a data import without the leaked-heap workaround, `&arr + 16`
  against clang's `&arr[2]`, explicit sections / hidden / retained / weak data
  against a C driver defining its own weak twin (checked with `nm -m`,
  `otool -l`, `dyld_info` and `-dead_strip`), each linked by ld64 and the
  standalone linker at O0-O3, plus the named refusals that stay (`ExternalWeak`
  data on Mach-O, a thread-local in an explicit section, an ELF relocated TLS
  template, a JIT body naming a thread-local, verifying JIT data sites).
  Darwin-only: Linux carries no native evidence for this family.

- Fixed (logical bool masks at memory boundaries): a `<N x bool>` SIMD mask
  no longer reaches a memory layout. trust-ir's normative interpreter stores
  one `0xFF`/`0x00` byte per lane and reads any non-zero byte as true, while
  this backend carries the mask in its producer's register class (V128 of
  16-bit lanes for an `<8 x i16>` compare, V64 of byte lanes for an `<8 x i8>`
  compare) and sizes the type as V128 — measured on aarch64 (2026-09-22): a
  `Store { ty: <8 x bool> }` wrote 16 bytes `ff ff 00 00 ..` where the referee
  writes 8 bytes `ff 00 ff 00 ..`, `<4 x bool>` / `<2 x bool>` likewise, and a
  `Load` copied raw `01 00 ..` bytes the referee canonicalises to `ff 00 ..`.
  Under the 2026-09-21 ruling (the IR model must define the shape AND the proof
  lane must cover the lowering) and with no verify obligation for a
  lane-narrowing or canonicalising mask store/load, every layout use is now
  refused by name — `AdapterError::BoolLaneLayoutNotAdmitted` at Store, Load,
  their volatile forms, the atomics, Alloca, HeapAlloc/Dealloc, a GEP pointee,
  and any struct / array / tuple / enum / record / closure that stores a bool
  lane by value — and a mask crossing a return, call or block boundary in a
  carrier other than the slot's V128 is refused as
  `AdapterError::BoolMaskCarrierMismatch`. Compares, canonical mask constants,
  `Select` conditions, `vector.mask_to_bits` and opaque pass-through are
  unchanged. Pins: `trust-cg-lower/tests/bool_lane_layout_refusal.rs` (the
  referee's bytes through `trust_ir::Interpreter`, every boundary, the
  aggregate walk with pointer-edge and physical-vector controls, the carrier
  mismatch with its V128 control), the trust-ir conformance manifest (three
  fail-closed rows) and `e2e_aarch64_bool_mask_store_bytes.rs` (the measured
  table, the refusal on every host, a native `<8 x i16>` store control).

- L05-P2 (versioned trust-ir source-construct inventory gate): new Darwin
  floor target `crates/trust-cg-lower/tests/trust_ir_construct_inventory.rs`
  (15 tests) enumerates every `Ty` (40), `Inst` (58), `Constant` (15) and
  `CastOp` (17) variant and every `Module` table (20, plus the `globals.tls`
  sub-surface) of the pinned trust-ir `7b9146ba` from the crate itself,
  through exhaustive matches and an exhaustive struct pattern, so an upstream
  variant or field change fails the build. Each construct has exactly one
  disposition: executed (91 rows: names the Darwin floor test whose native
  run carries the construct), model-only (40 rows: names the adapter test that
  lowers it), or refused (20 rows: re-drives a minimal module through the
  adapter and checks the named diagnostic); ten supported rows also carry a
  re-driven negative twin. The gate fails when a named evidence file or test
  function is missing, the construct is not spelled in the named test's
  reachable source (its body and, transitively, the functions, macros and
  consts it names in its file or in the sibling modules the file declares;
  a spelling elsewhere in the file does not count), an executed file is not
  a `scripts/check_darwin_aarch64.py` target, a refusal is not produced, or
  the committed summary `reports/fixtures/trust-ir-construct-inventory.json`
  (a shipped path, since `docs/` never reaches the public snapshot whose
  workspace lane runs this target; regenerate with
  `TRUST_IR_CONSTRUCT_INVENTORY_WRITE=1`) is stale; the trust-ir revision is
  read from `Cargo.lock` and named in every failure. No lowering changed. The
  60 constructs without native Darwin execution are listed in the JSON
  (`no_native_execution`) and drive the next waves; the Linux floor registers
  the target unmeasured until a Linux host runs it. The conformance manifest
  now labels `Ty::Record without module record table` (fail-closed) and
  `Ty::Record with module record table` (supported) the way it already
  labels the closure type, so the two ledgers name the same construct alike.
- L01-P5 (Apple arm64 hidden-result `sret` through X8): an `Inst::CallIndirect`
  edge now carries a hidden return-buffer identity when trust-ir's own typed
  provenance (`Const FnDef` through `Copy` / `ReifyFnPointer`) resolves the
  callee to a declaration whose `ParamAttrs::sret` marks parameter 0. The
  pinned trust-ir states `sret` only on a declared `Function` (no `FuncTy`
  or call-site attribute slot), so no metadata was invented: the adapter
  records the callee VALUE in the new `Function::sret_arg_indirect_callees`,
  the AArch64 selector stages it into X8 before the `BLR` and numbers the
  remaining arguments as if it were absent, and an edge whose signature,
  variadic-ness or calling convention disagrees with the resolved declaration
  is refused with `[TCG-SRET-ABI]`. A pointer with no provenance keeps the
  ordinary call its signature declares; a dynamically-called hidden result is
  expressed structurally (`returns: [Struct]`), which the function type itself
  carries. Variadic sret CALLS (legal C `struct Big f(int n, ...)`) are lowered
  instead of refused: X8 for the buffer, the fixed tail and the Apple anonymous
  stack tail classified without it. The retained LIR identity payload is v4
  (the new field moves an argument between X8 and X0). New Darwin floor target
  `e2e_aarch64_sret` (6 tests) executes C caller -> CG callee and CG caller ->
  C callee for both shapes through function pointers, and CG caller -> C
  variadic sret callee (no CG variadic sret definition exists),
  with stack-passed integer, FP and packed narrow arguments and a clobbering
  call while every argument is live, at O0-O3 against a clang oracle, plus
  the refusals that stay (non-leading sret, sret with results, disagreeing
  edge, indirect variadic, variadic definition). Structural controls in
  `sret_abi_contract.rs` and the selector unit tests. Variadic DEFINITIONS
  with a hidden buffer stay refused (`[TCG-VARIADIC-DEFINITION]`).

- Added (closures, `L05-P4`): first-class closure values now lower on
  aarch64-apple-darwin following trust-ir G18-2. A `Constant::Closure` at
  `Ty::Closure` materializes the struct of its captures (trust-ir's `func`
  lane has no runtime layout, so no code pointer is stored), its capture
  arity and code target are checked against the closure-type table and the
  physical contract `captures ++ apparent params -> apparent returns`, and
  `Inst::CallIndirect` over a closure callee lowers as the direct call to the
  closure's static code identity (the defining literal reached through
  `Copy`/`InsertField`) with the captures extracted and spread as leading
  arguments through the canonical direct-call arm. Closure, `FnDef` and
  `SymbolAddr` constants nested as aggregate fields materialize. A closure
  callee whose literal is not statically visible (parameter, `Select`,
  projection out of an aggregate, `Call` result, memory), apparent/physical
  signature or calling-convention mismatches, a captured closure at a
  non-closure type, `PhantomData` and `Set` constants stay refused by name.
  The AOT local-binding census counts a closure application to a bodied
  `Internal`/`Private` body as a direct edge and no longer counts a
  `Ty::Closure` literal as a materialized function address. Evidence:
  `e2e_aarch64_closures.rs` (8 tests; closures with 0, 1 and 3 mixed-width
  captures, a pointer-typed capture sharing its pointee, `InsertField`-rebuilt
  environments and nested constants execute natively at O0–O3 against the
  trust-ir reference interpreter and a C model; named-refusal controls) is a
  required Darwin floor target and a registered, not yet run, Linux floor
  target; the trust-ir conformance manifest pins the new Supported and
  fail-closed rows.

- L05-P5 Linux twin (`e2e_aarch64_direct_enums_linux`, Linux floor): the
  direct-tag enum corpus, C driver, interpreter oracle and refusal fixtures of
  `e2e_aarch64_direct_enums` now live in the shared
  `tests/common/direct_enums_corpus.rs`; the Darwin target keeps its four
  tests and expectations. The twin compiles the corpus to ELF for
  aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu at O0-O3 and checks, with an independent ELF64
  reader, that every corpus function is a defined global `STT_FUNC` in an
  executable section and that the enum-, record- and relocation-bearing
  globals (`g_ord`, `g_mixed`, `g_slot`, `g_rec`, `g_bytes`) are defined
  `STT_OBJECT`s of the producer's size whose section bytes carry the
  direct-tag image at every lane the code reads, `g_slot`'s pointer payload
  relocated by `R_AARCH64_ABS64` against `ord_disc` (in `.data.rel.ro`, the
  mutable `g_mixed` in `.data`, the rest in `.rodata`), each with byte-mutation
  controls; it pins the reference interpreter to the closed forms and the six
  named refusals for the ELF triple. On aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu it links
  the object with the host `cc` and executes the shared driver at O0-O3
  (49 C checks and 16 oracle values equal to the trust-ir reference
  interpreter per level), and a second native row calls every `*_make`
  selector through `blr` with the unspecified upper bits of `x1` set — the
  AAPCS64 rule (Arm IHI 0055, "Parameter passing rules": rule C.9, the
  Stage C unused-bits preamble and "named integral values must be narrowed
  by the callee rather than the caller") that an Apple-ABI C caller never
  exercises — and requires the image to equal the plain C call's (28 checks
  per level; the Linux callee narrows with `uxtb`). Only the 12 checks on
  selectors below each function's default switch arm can tell a narrowing
  callee from one that reads all of `x1`; the other 16 land on the default
  arm either way, so the driver now counts the two classes apart and first
  runs a non-narrowing C callee through the same `blr` path, which must fail
  all 4 of its discriminating checks and none of its 2 default-arm checks.
  The five ELF mutation controls now assert their exact reasons. Executed on a Linux
  AArch64 host (6 tests); registered in the Linux floor (143 targets) and,
  for its four host-neutral tests, in the Darwin floor. Execution and
  object-structure evidence, not proof of enum semantics.
- L05-P5 (direct-tag enum semantics and enum/record globals): a direct-tag
  `Ty::Enum` now lowers through trust-ir's own tag tables and the producer's
  layout instead of the canonical index/unsigned/canonical-layout fragment.
  The new `trust_cg_lower::direct_enum` module is the one authority: the tag
  lane is `EnumDef::canonical_tag_repr` (explicit discriminants that are not
  the variant index, signed reprs such as `Ordering { -1, 0, 1 }` on an `i8`
  lane, producer-declared widths), the stored tag word is the discriminant
  VALUE, `Switch` cases and signed compares consume it as any integer, and a
  `Direct` v31 descriptor is read verbatim for the tag offset and every
  variant field offset. The canonical `Type::Enum` is kept only where it
  reproduces the declared bytes; a descriptor it does not reproduce (rustc's
  per-variant packing, reordered fields, a padded or `repr(C)` image) lowers
  to a byte-image carrier of exactly the declared size and alignment, so
  copies, slots and ABI classes are the producer's. `EnumCanonicalLayoutDisagrees`
  now applies only to descriptor-less enums, where trust-cg's canonical shape
  and trust-ir's `enum_layout_shape` must still agree. The Mach-O object path
  renders enum-typed globals (tag word plus fields at the same image the code
  reads, relocations included) and record-typed globals (natural-C fields,
  positional or `Constant::Record`), through `module_direct_enum_image` and
  `translate_type_in_module`. Refused by name (`[TCG-DIRECT-ENUM]`): duplicate
  or overflowing discriminants, a repr too narrow for its values, 128-bit tag
  lanes, a descriptor whose tag or fields overlap or leave the image, niche or
  untagged enum globals, and `InsertField` on a direct-tag enum (unchanged).
  Native evidence: `e2e_aarch64_direct_enums.rs` (Darwin floor, 4 tests)
  compiles `Ordering`, a `repr(u8)` enum with explicit discriminants at
  rustc's layout, a `repr(C)` enum, a field-reordered 4-byte enum, and
  enum/record/relocation globals at O0-O3, links a C driver whose oracle is
  the C spelling of each layout (49 checks), and requires every
  zero-argument function to equal the trust-ir reference interpreter.
  Manifest rows added in `trust_ir_conformance_manifest.rs`; the four
  lower-crate pins that required the old refusals now pin the new carriers.
  Not re-measured here: the 68-module corpus counts (38 explicit-discriminant
  and 42 layout-disagreement enums) come from a corpus that is not in this
  repository, so no updated count is claimed.

- Added (`L04-P10`, AArch64 i128 forms): `Inst::Switch` over `I128`/`U128`
  selectors now lowers instead of being refused by width. The adapter splits
  the selector into its 64-bit halves and dispatches on both: a balanced
  unsigned compare tree over the distinct high halves of the case constants,
  each leaf a 64-bit `Switch` over that group's low halves (ISel's ordinary
  jump table when dense, compare chain otherwise). Every case is honored as a
  full 128-bit value; duplicate 128-bit patterns, `Constant::U128` on an
  `I128` selector, negative `Constant::Int` on a `U128` selector and
  non-canonical `Constant::U128` are refused by name. The i128/u128
  checked-multiply idiom (low product plus the guarded `__udivti3`/`__divti3`
  division identity) gained a registered obligation family
  (`trust-cg-verify/src/checked_mul_i128_proofs.rs`: the `Imul I128`
  `MUL; UMULH; MADD; MADD` chain and both overflow flags against the exact
  256-bit product reconstructed from 64-bit limbs), a native-oracle boundary
  battery and eight negative controls; the coverage gate's `Umulh` row now
  requires that credit and a surviving control turns the row
  `ProofNotDischarged`. Ratio unchanged at 172/282 with 110 deferred rows;
  static database 2,419 -> 2,422 (the walk-query-resolution golden moves its
  literal `add`/`mul` match counts to 17/15 with unchanged resolutions, and
  the AY Arithmetic-subset test tolerates the three rows as named
  capacity-bound timeouts only). The decoded-word machine side, the runtime
  division and the per-compile UMULH binding are named deferrals, so this is
  evaluator regression evidence, not proof. New macOS-native control
  `crates/trust-cg-codegen/tests/e2e_aarch64_i128_switch.rs` (dense, sparse,
  negative, high-half-only-differing and block-argument switches plus
  checked-mul boundaries at O0-O3 against clang's `__int128`; 2 tests,
  Darwin floor minimum 2, Linux floor registered but not yet executed). The
  lower crate's evidence rows follow the moved boundary: the trust-ir
  conformance manifest's fail-closed `Inst::Switch unsupported selector width`
  row became the supported `Inst::Switch I128/U128 selector (split halves
  dispatch)` row (its check asserts the lowered function keeps a 64-bit
  `Switch` leaf) and `trust_ir_integration` asserts the lowering instead of
  the refusal. `scripts/check_panic_clippy.sh --package trust-cg-verify` now
  answers with the crash-free-codegen policy note (the verifier crate is
  exempt from the panic-family ratchet, as the full run already treats it)
  instead of a spurious `base=0` regression, and `soundness_manifest` gained
  the name-filterable `checked_mul_i128_credit_is_registered_and_has_teeth`
  wrapper around the meta gate's in-process check.

- Fixed (evaluation lane, fail closed): the registry-wide evaluator sweeps
  (`evaluator_returns_a_verdict_for_every_registry_obligation`,
  `whole_registry_verdicts_identical_sequential_vs_chunked`) aborted in
  `SmtExpr::eval` on the exportable source-bound frame theorem, whose sides
  apply the uninterpreted `entry_memory` array ("cannot concretely evaluate
  uninterpreted function 'entry_memory'"). Concrete evaluation is now
  fallible end to end (`preconditions_hold` and `check_single_point` report
  an unsupported source, machine or precondition term as
  `PointCheck::Inconclusive`, folded to `Unknown` naming the term), so an
  obligation the sampler cannot interpret is inconclusive rather than a
  panic or a vacuous credit. Controls: `lowering_proof_eval_errors.rs` and
  `evaluator_declines_the_registry_frame_theorem_naming_its_uninterpreted_memory`.

- Fixed (AArch64 layout cross-check vs LL/SC): the final-layout cross-check
  and the post-RA LL/SC loop expansion landed from parallel branches, and the
  cross-check refused every expanded exclusive retry loop (`[TCG-A64-LAYOUT-XCHECK]
  ... branch word at byte 24 targets byte 12, which is not a laid-out block
  start`), failing all 10 native cases of `e2e_aarch64_llsc_atomics` on every
  AArch64 route. `check_final_layout` now waives the block-start requirement
  only for branches inside an exactly matched expanded LL/SC template
  (`llsc::llsc_internal_branches`, the same set the resolved-stream CFG
  derivation excludes from inter-block edges); their displacements are still
  checked against the intent, and a template near miss keeps the ordinary
  refusal. Unit control
  `expanded_llsc_loop_branch_is_a_validated_intra_block_target`.

- Resident AY, FALSE `Timeout` under contention: the lane fixed the same
  queued-deadline defect as the entry "Resident AY's per-query deadline now
  measures solver time" above, independently (the window owned first, the
  budget started after). The merge keeps one fix, that entry's admission
  deadline with its separately bounded, named queue refusal. What the lane
  adds: measured in this crate's own suite, `test_checked_overflow_i64_z3_cli`
  (10 s budget) failed with `CheckedSmul_I8 ... returned TIMEOUT` whenever it
  queued behind the batch-comprehensive rollup's 10-35 s windows. Same slot,
  same session: the seven live-solver tests outside `ay_bridge` that did not
  take `formal_solver_test_lock` (`checked_overflow_proofs`, `fsym_summary`,
  `pass_validators`) now do -- measured, their real `ay` displaced a sibling's
  fake resident between its two queries (`started\nstarted\n`) when the two
  modules ran under the default parallel harness.
- Merge of `origin/main` (774 commits, diverged 2026-09-14). Beyond textual
  conflicts, three SEMANTIC overlaps were resolved, and one orphan cluster:
  (1) i128 atomics — main lowers every op through LDXP/STXP pair pseudos on
  every profile; the lane's paired `LDP` + barrier is kept as the FEAT_LSE2
  fast path with precedence, the pseudo everywhere else (see the 128-bit record
  below). (2) `(*r).field` aggregate reads and multi-variant-enum whole-value
  copies were implemented on BOTH sides; main's integrated arms are kept and the
  lane's parallel `lower_deref_whole_value_memory_copy` is dropped. (3) The
  lane's slice-tail DST reference model (`slice_tail_dst_pointee`,
  `memory_place_walk_base`) is kept beside main's `is_slice_reference_ty`
  predicate — the lane's is the general struct-with-slice-tail case, main's the
  `#[repr(transparent)]` wrapper case. (4) main's `9c523812f` ("preserve
  canonical runtime bounds assertions") retired the backend's dominated
  bounds-check-elimination probe but left behind its `bce-trace` knob, the two
  tests that assert `TCG-BCE-DOM fired` (`dom_bounds_refutation_x86`,
  `dom_bounds_dynamic_fail_closed`) — red on main, in a crate whose tests no
  lane runs. Both tests and the knob are removed here; their corpus guests stay,
  because `bridge_differential_x86` still runs them as ordinary programs.
  Restore the three together if the probe returns. Also fixed on the way: main's
  `direct_call_binding` test target did not compile against main's own
  `trust-ir` pin (`dfdb950` drops `Copy` from `ParamAttrs`; the test moved it
  twice), 120 test literals of `trust_ir::Function` in `trust-cg-lower` that
  predate the same pin's three new fields, and two 128-bit multiply helpers
  made dead by the canonical `Inst::Overflow` lowering are deleted. One real
  regression surfaced and is closed: on main's pin the bridge spells the
  `{ data, len }` lane tuple as `Ty::Array(lane, 2)` (an O(1) spelling of the
  tuple), so `arr.len()` reaches the back-edge model as `ExtractField { ty:
  Array(TyId, 2), field: 1 }` and the width rule written against `Ty::Tuple`
  left it untyped — `maximal_suffix` was a failed root again. The model now
  carries the module's type table (`model_back_edge_args_with_types`, which the
  bridge calls) and resolves the element through it; pinned by a mutation-proved
  test. Measured: `library/core` back at ROOTS=0 on the merged tree, against
  main's own 203.
- Portable CERT-SKIP tier, FIVE red tests with ONE cause: the committed
  `verdict_db/canary_certs/manifest.v1` authorizes the exact SHA-256 of the
  vendored `drat-trim` checker that `crates/trust-cg-drat-trim/build.rs`
  compiles at build time, and build.rs pinned opt-level, debug and `__FILE__`
  for byte identity but left the Apple deployment target to `cc`, which derives
  `-mmacosx-version-min` from `xcrun --show-sdk-version` (ignoring `SDKROOT`).
  That answer moved 26.5 -> 27.0 when CommandLineTools 26.6 installed on
  2026-09-13, `LC_BUILD_VERSION.minos` moved with it, and the checker's hash
  moved off the manifest's `0f634db2...` to `54c6f06f...` with identical source,
  clang, SDKROOT and flags -- so every portable replay declined at the
  identity gate, silently, and `canary_cert`, `function_verifier`,
  `lowering_proof` and three `pass_validators` pins went red together. The
  target is now pinned in build.rs (`MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=26.5`, the value
  the manifest was minted with, so the reviewed identity is reproduced and NO
  certificate is re-minted); the fail-closed path prints actual-vs-authorized
  identity and the `regen_canary_certs` command once per process instead of
  reading as a cache miss; `function_verifier`'s regression names the gate it
  declined at rather than passing its own precondition vacuously. Residual by
  design and now documented in `verdict_db/README.md`: a different clang or
  SDK still re-keys the checker, and that is a deliberate re-authorization.
- Certificate lane, NON-TERMINATION: the in-process proof memo was
  positive-only, so a query whose result was an attributed AY hole (every
  bitvector theory step; every bridge query is QF_BV) was re-solved at every
  occurrence and `--certs` ran until its budget died (measured: 1500 s,
  `VALID=NO timed_out=True`). A bounded NEGATIVE session memo keyed on the same
  (solver identity, exact smt2) now remembers a deterministic certification-gap
  `Unknown` and replays it; a bare `unknown`, a timeout or any
  environment-shaped reason is never memoised, a later positive evicts the
  entry, and a hit can only ever return the same `AYResult::Unknown(reason)` --
  no authority is granted and no verdict changes. Measured on `library/core`:
  the certs lane now completes in 82 s with `VALID=yes ROOTS=0`, the same
  verdict set as the no-certs lane, which is the confirmation the census
  instrument requires before a headline count is quoted.
- `lir_trap_is_a_hard_cfg_terminator_without_synthetic_fallthrough_branch`
  (trust-cg-codegen), red since 2026-09-10: `2b1995f87` changed AArch64
  `select_trap` from `call abort` + an unreachable `TrapOverflow` filler to a
  bare `BRK #1` and updated only trust-cg-lower's own test; this consumer pin
  kept searching the prepared function for `TrapOverflow`. It now asserts
  `Brk` is the block's final real instruction and that CFG repair appends no
  branch after it -- the property it always meant. Mutation-proved.
- `model_in_loop_diamond`'s two-arm "early continue" admit path was
  UNREACHABLE and is removed, on the theorem that retired the identical rule in
  `model_triangle` in `afdff746`: an arm can report `join == header` only from
  a block whose sole in-loop successor is the header, and under `loop_set`
  (backward reachability from the latch) such a block can only BE the latch --
  so the soundness guard fired every time. Replaced with a direct fail-closed
  refusal that states the theorem; `diamond_arm_taking_back_edge_is_rejected`
  still builds exactly that shape and still refuses. Measured: `library/core`
  unchanged at 0 failed roots.
- 128-bit atomic load lowering, RECORD: `68c67a6f` landed on this lane saying
  "IMPLEMENTED BUT UNMEASURED, do not merge as-is" and listing three
  preconditions. All are now met and measured on this tree: the "cold cache
  exceeds the census cap" precondition WAS the certificate-lane non-termination
  above; the census reads `VALID=yes emitted=44 harness_errors=0 degraded=0
  ROOTS=0` on both lanes; `AtomicU128`/`AtomicI128` loads compile through the
  bridge at O0 and O2 and emit LLVM's exact mapping (Relaxed `ldp`; Acquire
  `ldp; dmb ishld`; SeqCst `ldp; dmb ish`), the ordering jump table decodes
  0/2/4 to those and 1/3 to the panic arm, a runnable differential returns the
  same exit (224) on bridge O0, bridge O2, LLVM O0 and LLVM O2, and the verify
  suite's 53 atomic obligations pass including the `AtomicLoad_I128`
  single-copy proof and its refuted torn control. u128 store/swap/CAS fail
  closed with named diagnostics. The ISA-identity move it warned about
  (`APPLE_ARM64.feature_bits()` 7 -> 15, canonical `+lse2`) is pinned by
  `target.rs`. RECONCILED WITH `origin/main` in the merge that follows: main
  lowers every i128 atomic (load, store, RMW, CAS) through the LDXP/STXP pair
  pseudos on every profile; this lane's paired `LDP` + barrier is LLVM's exact
  mapping wherever FEAT_LSE2 is admitted. Both are kept, LSE2 taking precedence
  — one plain LDP where the profile admits it, the exclusive pair everywhere
  else — and the test that asserted "refuse without LSE2" now asserts "take the
  pair pseudo without LSE2". The duplicate `wip/` branch is deleted.
- MIR bridge, SIZED ARRAY value types (`[T; N]`, where the length is part of
  the type): `memory_aggregate_reference_pointee_lane_ty_reasoned` -- the
  byte-offset fallback that types an aggregate pointee the scalar-field
  flattening cannot represent -- enumerated the ARRAY shapes it would serve BY
  SHAPE (`has_nested_enum_leaf || has_nested_niche_enum_leaf || <element is
  itself an array>`) and covered bare TUPLE pointees not at all. Those are
  instances of ONE property, "the flattening failed", and the enumeration left
  the remaining instances refusing for no reason. Both arms now test the property
  directly, the same way the struct and closure arms already did. Every new
  decline carries its reason, as that function requires.
  * FIXED (a refusal, not wrong code): `&[(u16, [u16; 3]); N]` and
    `&(u16, [u16; 3])` -- the `core::unicode::unicode_data::conversions`
    multi-character case-mapping table and the element reference
    `<[(u16, [u16; 3])]>::get_unchecked` hands back from it. The decline the
    reason-carrying exits already named -- *"pointee `(u16, [u16; 3_usize])` is
    not a named ADT; only a struct pointee is typed as a memory-aggregate lane
    tuple here"* -- is exactly what the tuple arm answers.
  * MEASURED on `library/core` (census, one merged dylib, against stage1
    `0cb693917a`), baseline reproduced with this lane's OWN control dylib on
    `lane/integration-2026-09-14-d` @ `fa9ee589`: **143 roots / 39 reasons ->
    131 / 34**. 12 symbols fixed, **0 newly failing**. Five reasons vanish
    outright: `Ty::[u<n>` (4), `Ty::(u<n>, [u<n>` (1), `Ty::Adt multi-field
    struct unicode::unicode_data::conversions::Range` (4),
    `Ty::(unicode::unicode_data::conversions::Range, i<n>)` (1), and
    `Ty::Float(f<n>)` (2, `core_arch`'s `float16xN_t::as_array`, a pointer cast
    that moves no `f16` value -- every `f16` VALUE operation still fails closed).
    The same change measured **-12 in isolation** on `lane/integration-2026-09-14-b`
    @ `5e6a978c` (260 -> 248), so none of the twelve had been swept by another
    lane.
  * THE 45-ROOT DST CLUSTER IS UNTOUCHED, which is the point: `Ty::[u<n>]` (21),
    `Ty::[i<n>]` (9) and `IndexRange` (15) all key on an UNSIZED struct pointee
    and stay at their exact counts, and their `… is UNSIZED (a DST with a `[T]` /
    `str` tail)` reasons are byte-identical on the merged dylib (46 roots still
    carry one). The arms this lane rewrote are gated on `ty::Array` / `ty::Tuple`;
    a DST reaches neither.
  * NO SIZE BOUND IS ADDED, because the widening moves work OFF the O(len)
    spelling rather than onto it: the memory slot is `Ty::Array(lane, n)` built
    in O(1), while the flattening this arm catches is one leaf per element.
    Measured: an 8192-entry `[(u16, [u16; 3]); N]` table (64 KiB) compiles in
    0.51 s / 178 MB against LLVM's 0.30 s / 158 MB, and a `&[u8; 262144]`
    pointee (whose flattening SUCCEEDS, so the arm does not fire) is unchanged
    at 0.47 s on both sides.
  * A PRE-EXISTING REFUSAL IS LIFTED, CORRECTLY: `fix_e_zst_tuple_by_ref`
    (`&([u8; 0], u32, u32)`) refused with `[TCG-ZST-LANE-INDEX]` because "a tuple
    pointee has no rustc-layout byte-walker fallback, unlike a struct" -- a
    premise this change makes false. It now prints `10 20`, LLVM's exact output,
    at both opt levels, where the pre-refusal backend printed `20` for `t.1`. The
    refusal itself is untouched: it still rejects the FLAT LANE TUPLE, which is
    what keeps the value off the short tuple.
  * Falsifiers: `tests/sized_array_value_type_differential.rs`, 4 fixtures x 2
    opt levels, stdout compared ELEMENT BY ELEMENT against LLVM (an array's
    failure mode is a wrong element at the wrong stride, not a refusal, and a
    folded checksum absorbs it). **8/8 rows match patched, 4/8 unpatched**;
    `sized_array_escape_union_buf` (the `core::escape` `([T; N], Range<u8>)`
    shape plus the field-shift class) and `sized_array_controls` (`[T; 0]`, a
    thin `&[u16; 6]`, a `&[u16]` SLICE, a `&[[u8; 4]; 3]` nested-array pointee)
    compile on both and are live controls that must keep matching.

- AArch64 by-value ARGUMENTS, `PassMode::Pair`: **the two-value lane now lowers
  on the argument side**, so a by-value aggregate whose two scalars rustc places
  in two registers is emitted conformantly instead of refused
  (`[TCG-ARG-ABI]`). The argument twin of the `[TCG-RET-ABI]` scalar-pair return
  lane, and the largest single family left in the `core` census.
  * WHAT WAS REFUSED: rustc classifies a `BackendRepr::ScalarPair` aggregate
    `PassMode::Pair` — two independent ABI values of the scalars' own classes and
    widths, so `Option<u8>` arrives in `w0` AND `w1`. trust-cg declared the
    parameter as the slot's uniform lane tuple, which its AAPCS64 classifier puts
    WHOLE into ONE register for any composite of 8 bytes or fewer. 72 of the 73
    `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` roots were exactly that: *"rustc requires 2 register lane(s)
    and trust-cg would emit 1"*.
  * HOW THE 606-ARITY-MISMATCH HAZARD IS CLOSED. Enabling this lane on
    2026-09-11 turned 606 OTHER `core` roots into loud
    `Call argument arity mismatch` failures, because a PARAMETER declaration is
    global to the callee while several argument lists in the bridge are built by
    hand. Neither of the two properties that close it is a change to those lists.
    (1) `MirLoweringCtx::scalar_pair_param_plan` is the ONE decision function —
    the declaration (`classify_func_ty`), the callee body's entry block, and
    every call site (`lower_call_args_from_inputs` on the direct, coroutine,
    fn-pointer and virtual lanes, plus the virtual lane's hand-built `param_tys`)
    ask it with the same three facts and none re-derives it.
    (2) It engages ONLY where the whole-slot classification is ALREADY REFUSED by
    `check_param_abi`. A `&str` / `&[T]` / `&dyn` fat pointer is a
    `PassMode::Pair` too, and its 16-byte lane tuple already lands in the x0/x1
    pair rustc asks for, so it keeps the single slot-pointer argument every one
    of those hand-built lists builds for it. Nothing that compiles today takes a
    different path — this is strictly a refusal-to-conformance conversion.
    (3) And the scope is STRUCTURAL, not incidental: the lane declines outright
    for the two callable families whose call sites do NOT go through
    `lower_call_args_from_inputs` — a closure body or closure shim
    (`instance_ty` is `ty::Closure` / `ty::CoroutineClosure`), called by
    `emit_closure_call_n` / `finish_closure_call`, which hand-build one value per
    argument including `build_tuple_item_arg`'s by-value aggregate tuple item;
    and parameter 0 of a `FnOnce::call_once` VTABLE SHIM, which
    `classify_func_ty` forces to `Ptr` before any by-value classification runs.
    It also declines a `&dyn` receiver, expanded to two pointers by an earlier
    branch, and every C-compatible ABI, which has its own eightbyte lane. Each of
    those declines was measured to cost **zero** `core` roots.
  * THE `i128` LANE IS CARRIED, and the argument side is where it can be.
    `Option<u128>` (32 bytes) is still `PassMode::Pair` — of two `i128` scalars,
    each of which AAPCS64 §5.4 splits across TWO registers, so the value rides
    x0-x3 while trust-cg's whole-slot rule sends anything over 16 bytes through a
    caller-allocated copy addressed by pointer. The RETURN lane refuses an `i128`
    carrier because `classify_returns` cannot state a register PAIR for one of
    two return values; `classify_params` states exactly that
    (`ArgLocation::RegPair`), and `abi_reg_lanes` already models a `RegPair` as
    its two 8-byte lanes at +0/+8 — so the argument plan states four lanes at
    0/8/16/24, which is what rustc requires. `scalar_pair_abi_plan` is therefore
    parameterised by its carrier table (`scalar_pair_abi_plan_with`) and the
    argument side passes `scalar_pair_param_lane_ty`; the RETURN lane's table is
    unchanged. The table decides nothing on its own —
    `check_param_abi_lanes` compares the resulting placement against rustc's.
  * WHAT IT STILL REFUSES, by name: a scalar with no trust-ir carrier at all
    (`f16`/`f128`), and a pair whose scalars rustc marks `signext` — the lane's
    moves are ordinary typed loads, which zero-extend on AArch64. Measured over
    the whole census, NO `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` root carries a `Sext` lane (59
    `None`/`None`, 14 `Zext`/`None`), so declining it costs no capability and
    keeps the lane from silently acquiring a case it has never been measured on.
  * MEASURED (`library/core` census, Trust stage1 `0cb693917a`, same instrument
    and flags as the integration baseline, control dylib reproduced at 290):
    failed roots **290 -> 223**, `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` **73 -> 0 (the reason is
    GONE)**, **67 symbols fixed and ZERO newly-failing symbols**, 49 reasons
    before and after. The three reasons that grew are first-failure shifts of
    freed roots onto later honest refusals (`ManuallyDrop<Part>` fat pointer
    19 -> 21, `ControlFlow` `from_residual` 2 -> 4, bulk-append 0 -> 2).
    **Zero** `arity mismatch` lines in either census stderr.
  * DIFFERENTIAL (`benchmarks/regclass-xback`, separately compiled `rlib`
    callee, `#[inline(never)]`, four link directions, `-Copt-level=0` and `=2`):
    **0 failures, 0 declines — 72/72 cells match the `llvm x llvm` oracle**,
    against 24 declines on the control. Five new program pairs cover the census's
    own sub-families rather than only `iarg`'s `{i32,i32}`: `barg` (`Option<u8>`,
    `1 byte @0 ; 1 byte @1`, a `zeroext` tag lane, both variants exercised),
    `earg` (`Option<u32>`, a TAGGED enum), `harg` (`(i16,i16)`), `marg`
    (`{u32,u16}`, a MIXED-width pair whose second lane is narrower than its
    first) and `qarg` (`Option<u128>`, the two-register-pair lane, reading the
    HIGH half of the payload as well as the low). Every one was watched declining
    `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` on the control dylib first. Disassembled: the `iarg` callee
    now reads `w0` and `w1` where it read `ldr x0, [x1]`.
  * REGRESSION: all 174 `tests/bridge_corpus` rows x {-O0,-O2} on BOTH dylibs —
    **no value divergence anywhere and no row that matched before stopped
    matching**. MATCH 222 -> 225 (`i128_byval_aggregate_abi` at both opt levels
    and `option_take_loop` at O0 newly compile and agree with LLVM),
    TCG-REFUSED 55 -> 50, LLVM-BUILD-FAIL unchanged. The two extra MISMATCH rows
    are `fix_m_expect_user_error_payload`, which moved from a refusal into the
    PRE-EXISTING "panic message not lowered by trust-cg" class its two sibling
    rows already sat in: every MISMATCH row in the sweep, old and new, has the
    SAME exit code (134) on both sides and differs only in the panic text.
    `cargo test --lib` is 273 passed / 2 failed, identical to the control tree
    run on the same host (both failures are the E0514 spawned-driver environment
    issue, neither reachable from ABI classification).
- WS7.6 (F-112): a direct-tag `Ty::Enum` value is projected by `ExtractField`
  instead of being refused with "multi-index GEP expected struct, tuple, or
  record type, got Enum". Element 0 loads the tag word at the enum's canonical
  tag type; element `i > 0` loads payload field `i - 1` at the one offset all
  variants with a field of that type there agree on (wrong-variant reads are
  undefined behaviour in trust-ir). New named refusals: `EnumCanonicalLayoutDisagrees`
  (a descriptor-less enum whose `Type::Enum` layout differs from trust-ir's
  `enum_layout_shape` on any axis, checked before any projection),
  `EnumProjectionNoCandidate`, `EnumProjectionOffsetAmbiguous`,
  `EnumTagWriteUnsupported` (lane-0 `InsertField`, a re-tag) and
  `EnumPayloadInsertUnsupported` (payload `InsertField`, until the WS7.1
  fresh-slot insert lowering lands). New non-default `mutation-knobs` feature
  (`trust-cg-lower`, forwarded by `trust-cg-codegen`) with the
  `enum_payload_off_by_one` and `perturb_enum_canonical_layout` knobs;
  `trust_cg_lower::MUTATION_KNOBS` reports whether a build carries it. Tests:
  `trust-cg-codegen/tests/enum_field_projection.rs` (native vs interpreter vs
  the Part A-Lean kernel-certified values, rows `FORMAT_HOME.native.enum`,
  `AL.uf04`, `rerun.finding07`) and
  `trust-cg-lower/tests/direct_enum_projection.rs`; the conformance manifest
  gains three enum projection rows.

- WS7.6 review fix (miscompile): an ENUM-typed field of a struct is now carried
  by address like a struct or array field. The `ExtractField` struct arm (both
  the natural-layout and the declared-offset path) loaded a `Type::Enum` field
  as a scalar, and the declared-offset `InsertField` arm stored the enum's
  ADDRESS into the struct; once WS7.6 made enum projections lower, extracting
  a struct's enum field and projecting it handed the tag word to the
  projection as an address (SIGSEGV). Pinned natively by the `review_*` tests
  in `trust-cg-codegen/tests/enum_field_projection.rs` (with mixed-width,
  small, nested, in-memory, `Select`, block-parameter, `repr(u16)` and `i128`
  enums against the interpreter) and at the adapter by
  `enum_field_of_a_struct_is_carried_by_address_not_loaded` and
  `enum_value_inserted_into_a_declared_offset_struct_is_copied_not_stored`.

- `trust-cg-codegen` is back under both panic ratchets
  (`check_panic_clippy.sh`, `check_unwrap_ratchet.sh`) with
  `ratchet/unwrap_baseline.json` unchanged: the 15 production
  `unreachable!`/`expect` sites added over baseline now return the function's
  existing error (`EncodeError::InvalidOperand`, decode-check `Mismatch`,
  `PipelineError::ISel`), are removed by construction (the JIT and x86
  certificate cache keys can no longer be built without their verifier
  authority), or, in the `Drop`/`Clone` paths of JIT execution leases, fall
  into an absorbing pinned in-flight count that never unmaps. Behavioural API
  change: `ElfWriter::add_nobits_section` / `add_bss_section` take the byte
  count as `usize`; the ELF global emitter converts a `u64` layout size with
  `usize::try_from` and refuses a section this host cannot address instead of
  panicking (or, on the PROGBITS path, truncating on a 32-bit host).
- Binary input accepts the canonical bare `TRUST_IR` container that
  `trust_ir::binary::serialize_module` writes (trust-ir's conformance `.tmbc`
  fixtures, Clean's `--emit trustir-bin`) as well as the `tMBC` envelope
  (roadmap WS7.4, F-115). The new `decode_binary` picks the container by
  magic: `TRUST_IR` goes whole to the pinned trust-ir reader, so its version
  window, v26..=v28 refusal and trailing-byte check apply unchanged; `tMBC`
  keeps `decode_tmbc`; anything else is refused as "neither a TRUST_IR module
  nor a tMBC envelope" with its first 8 bytes. It backs `--format=binary`
  (the default), `--format=auto` and `load_module_from_bytes`. The CLI
  agreement test pins the compiling fixture set by name, and pins
  `func_param_abi` to its `[TCG-BYVAL-ABI]` refusal.

- The TrustIR adapter's caller-side narrow-integer extension and Swift
  aggregate register-fit check classify under the target's AArch64 calling
  convention instead of DarwinPCS for every target (`L01-P10`). The compiler
  (AOT and JIT), the strict Core adapter and the JIT source campaign pass the
  variant resolved from the triple; the TLS-dialect compatibility entries use
  their object format's convention; `prepare_module_for_lir_with_abi` records
  the convention and refuses a translation dialect of the other one; an
  unresolved convention refuses a narrow-argument call (`[TCG-TARGET-ABI]`).
  `AArch64AbiVariant` loses its derived DarwinPCS `Default`, and
  `InstructionSelector` refuses ABI classification until `set_abi_variant`
  names the convention. New `trust-cg-lower` test `adapter_target_abi` pins an
  `(i64, i128, i64, i64, i64, i8, i8)` call: AAPCS64 extends only the x7
  argument, DarwinPCS both.

- Mach-O objects record `LC_BUILD_VERSION` from the target's macOS deployment
  target instead of a fixed 14.0 (`X-DARWIN-P13`). `TargetSpec` parses
  `<arch>-apple-macos[x]<version>`, carries the version in its canonical triple
  and the compile policy's artifact projection (a new TLV present only with a
  version, so existing digests are unchanged), and accepts a driver-captured
  `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` (`with_macos_deployment_target_from_environment`);
  the `trust-cg` CLI captures it once for Apple targets and its Darwin link
  passes the same `-mmacosx-version-min`. Non-macOS Apple platforms, Darwin
  kernel versions, malformed values and arm64 versions below 11.0 are refused
  (`[TCG-MACHO-DEPLOYMENT]`). New tests `e2e_macho_deployment_target` (ld64
  links objects at 11.0-15.0 without a version warning; a default object
  linked at 12.0 warns) and the CLI's `macos_deployment_target`.

- Sibling tail-call eligibility reads the call's classified ABI facts, which
  instruction selection now records (`MachFunction::call_abi_facts` and
  `incoming_stack_arg_bytes`), instead of an operand-count heuristic
  (`L01-P6`). A call without facts, an indirect call, an `sret` call and
  variadic or aggregate stack arguments keep their call; stack arguments that
  fit the caller's own incoming area are redirected there and the call becomes
  a tail branch. New native test `e2e_aarch64_tail_call_abi` decodes `B`/`BL`
  for CG callers tail-calling clang callees with stack arguments, narrow stack
  arguments, swapped or duplicated forwarded incoming stack arguments and
  callee-saved pressure at O0-O3 and checks results and the
  driver's callee-saved checksum; it ran on macOS and is registered, not yet
  run, on Linux.

- The native link helper (`tests/common/aarch64_native.rs`) no longer lets two
  tests of one binary collide on a temporary directory.

- The Linux floor (`scripts/check_linux_aarch64.py`) gains `adapter_target_abi`
  and `e2e_aarch64_tail_call_abi` (118 targets); the Darwin floor gains those
  two, `e2e_macho_deployment_target` and the CLI's `macos_deployment_target`
  (158 targets, 1,085 minimum passes, each minimum the count executed natively
  on aarch64-apple-darwin). The two Linux additions have not run on a Linux
  host.

- AArch64 source-bound frame binding (L09-P4): `source_bound_frame` returns
  `Result<SourceBoundFrame, SourceBoundFrameRefusal>` instead of discarding the
  affine error kind. After an admitted source and a recognized frame and
  chain/diamond skeleton, a wrong constant, register, branch target or FP/LR
  envelope offset is a typed `FrameBindingMismatch`; other lowerings remain
  `FrameShapeUnsupported`. The AArch64 verifier turns an enforced mismatch into
  the new `FunctionVerificationPreconditionFailure::SourceBoundFrameMismatch`,
  so proof-required compiles, the sealed Core and verifying JIT certificates
  reject it by name (`[TCG-SOURCE-BOUND-FRAME-MISMATCH]`) instead of reporting
  an uncovered envelope; warn mode prints a diagnostic. The diamond walker now
  counts words with the encoder's emission predicate.
- AArch64 late layout (L10-P12): every encode, and the relaxing `lower` path,
  cross-checks the final words against block starts, branch displacements,
  jump-table ADR/entries, ADR/LDR-literal targets and fixup sites and symbols
  re-derived from the final layout (`aarch64::layout_crosscheck`,
  `PipelineError::Aarch64LayoutCrossCheck`). `Pipeline::with_proof_grade_aarch64_publication`
  (selected by `emit_proofs`, verifying JIT validation modes and
  `JitConfig::verify`; the sealed Core already used it) forces the
  reaching-definition, spill-slot and decode nets to Enforce without
  environment downgrade, binds every encoded edge to the recorded CFG and
  refuses `pipeline::AARCH64_LATE_LAYOUT_CONTROLS`
  (`PipelineError::AmbientLateLayoutControl`). New target
  `aarch64_final_layout_crosscheck` is registered in the Linux floor (117
  targets) and the Darwin floor (155 targets, 1,070 minimum passes); its
  host-JIT legs have not yet run on a Linux host.

- The AArch64 final-stream spill-slot net (`[TCG-A64-SPILL-SLOT]`,
  `trust_cg_verify::post_ra_spill_slots`) is now a frame dataflow net. It
  previously declined every framed function (SP adjustment, frame pointer,
  writeback pair, call, X29 base), i.e. every function that spills. It now
