  interprets the frame frame lowering emits (CFA-relative SP/X29 through
  saves, chunked allocation, unrolled and counted-loop stack probes, large-
  offset scratch addressing, dynamic-frame `mov sp, x29` and post-index
  teardown, landing-pad entry from call sites) and checks, on every modeled
  stream: each spill reload reads bytes that spill stores wrote on every path
  with no non-spill or callee-owned writer; no call-clobbered volatile
  register and no caller callee-saved value is consumed; and at every `RET`
  and tail call SP, X19-X28, X29, D8-D15 and the return address hold their
  entry values while no return lane is call-clobbered, holds a caller value
  or is written after teardown began. Streams it cannot model decline with a
  counted `DeclineReason`; the original frameless SP-only rule still runs.
  Spill traffic carries the new `InstFlags::SPILL_SLOT_ACCESS` provenance bit
  from AArch64 spill materialization. `tests/aarch64_frame_dataflow_net.rs`
  (Linux and Darwin floors, compile-only) corrupts real Darwin/Linux O0-O3
  pipeline output: deleted spill store, reload offset moved onto the saved
  FP or below the frame, reload offset shifted by half a slot, swapped reload
  register, reload hoisted above the clobbering call, dropped
  callee-save/frame-record restore, and a return lane written in the
  epilogue. A reload must read exactly the bytes one spill store wrote
  (`reload-misaligned-with-spill-store`); the stream carries no spill-slot
  identity, so a reload shifted by whole slots onto another fully
  spill-stored cell is still accepted. When the frame model declines a
  stream, the frameless legacy rule still checks its flagged reloads. Frame
  address arithmetic is checked, so a malformed stream with an access ending
  past `i64::MAX` declines instead of panicking. Hand-built test fixtures that returned through a
  BL-clobbered link register or redefined callee-saved registers without
  restoring them now save and restore them. The Darwin floor is 155 required
  targets with 1,073 minimum passes; the Linux floor lists 117 targets.
- The post-RA role model shared by the reaching-definition and frame nets
  now treats the STLXR status operand as a definition, as codegen's
  classifier does. The frame net's epilogue return-lane check is scoped to
  the exit block: a shrink-wrapped frame edge branches after its teardown to
  a return shared with a frameless path, whose code is not epilogue. Soaking
  327 test targets on macOS found these and the landing-pad entry state;
  a ten-suite census then modeled all 430 final streams, with no decline:
  126 framed, 2,626 spill reloads and 579 exits checked.
- The register-allocation validator adds gate (b'''): an independent
  recomputation of AArch64 physical-register liveness (its own alias keys,
  AAPCS64 call-kill table and solver) whose every live point must be reserved
  in the allocator's reservation map, reported as
  `PhysicalLivenessUnreserved`. Test builds inject two `reserve` corruptions
  (dropped successor live-in, ignored implicit sinks); the validator rejects
  both.

- AArch64 NZCV producer/consumer credits (X-OPCODES-P3/P5, L04-P8): new
  `aarch64_flag_consumer_proofs` registers 414 per-instruction obligations
  (FCMP packed NZCV per S/D width; FCMP -> CSET per width and condition;
  CSEL/CSINC/CSNEG per operation, width, reaching CMP/TST/FCMP producer and
  width, and condition) whose machine sides execute independently decoded
  captured words over the producer's modeled NZCV. The function verifier binds
  FCMP by operand width and CSET/selects by their reaching in-block producer
  (CSET also after X-width checked ADDS/SUBS and adjacent ADCS/SBCS) and fails
  closed otherwise; the source-bound CSET path shares the producer walk. The
  coverage gate credits FCMP, CSET, CSEL, CSINC and CSNEG only when every form
  discharges, every captured word decodes back, every own form agrees on a
  deterministic integer/IEEE boundary battery and every negative control
  (wrong condition, swapped arms, wrong width, stale flags, arm transform,
  ordered-versus-unordered predicates, x86-style unordered flags) refutes:
  AArch64 163/282 -> 168/282 with 114 deferred rows and no NoProofMapping row.
  Acceptance is sampled/finite evaluation, not formal proof: a strict-gate
  AY/Clean probe on this Mac certified none of four sampled rows (incomplete
  certificates for integer selects, `incomplete self-check-rejected` for the
  FCMP rows) and found no counterexample. The checked
  scalar-FP evaluator admits exactly one wider carrier, a packed 4-bit NZCV
  value. `nzcv.rs` gains AddWithCarry models for ADDS/SUBS/ADCS/SBCS/ADC/SBC;
  ENC-5 decodes every emitted S/D FCMP word and rejects an FCMP intent whose
  operands are not FP registers (the encoder derives the compare width from
  operand 0 alone and would spell `FCMP W1, W2` as `FCMP D1, D2`); half-
  precision and Q-register FCMP words remain counted, not verified. The
  registry tape census now measures the simplifier's fold without this
  fold-free family (34.9% over the rest of the registry). A natively recorded Apple M4 Max
  fixture (`aarch64_nzcv_silicon_truth.json`, generator
  `gen_aarch64_nzcv_silicon_truth.{c,sh}`) is replayed by the new
  `aarch64_nzcv_silicon_bridge` target; `aarch64_flag_consumer_gate` ties the
  captured words and real selector output to the verifier. Both are required in
  the Linux floor (134 targets; not yet run on Linux) and the Darwin floor (174
  targets, 1,193 minimum passes). `proof_gate_strict` pins the static corpus
  at 2,415 (2,001 + these 414 rows, live-bound; the capacity allowlist is
  unchanged). `--emit-proofs` on an FCMP module is now refused for sampled
  FCMP/CSET evidence instead of a missing mapping.

- AArch64 half-precision conversions (X-OPCODES-P7): `FcvtHS`, `FcvtHD`,
  `FcvtSH` and `FcvtDH` are credited through decoded-word obligations that
  compare the Arm ARM `FPConvert` transcription of each captured FCVT word with
  an independent IEEE 754 `convertFormat` intent (`aarch64_fcvt_half`), bit for
  bit over the whole destination register — exhaustively over every binary16
  for the widening forms, and on a structured tie/overflow/underflow/NaN
  battery plus sampling for the rounded forms. Wrong-direction, wrong-rounding,
  wrong-format (including BFCVT and the AHP alternative format), default-NaN
  and denormal-flush controls are refuted; ENC-5 runs the per-instance check
  and the function verifier binds each FCVT to exactly its form. The AArch64
  ratio moves from 168/282 to 172/282 (110 deferred rows, no missing
  mapping) and the static proof corpus from 2,415 to 2,419. Both
  sides assume the default FPCR; this is evaluator evidence, not a formal
  proof. New native target `e2e_aarch64_f16_fcvt` compares CG-compiled
  conversions with the hardware FCVT instruction (1,482,652 comparisons on an
  Apple M4; its Linux arm has not yet run).
- Explicit AArch64 ISA profile for object emission (L04-P9):
  `CompilerConfig::aarch64_isa_profile` and CLI `--aarch64-isa-features
  <fp16,lse,dotprod|none>` replace the target contract with exactly the named
  features — the only route by which a generic Linux object admits FEAT_FP16
  arithmetic — and are recorded in the compile policy (Artifact), the
  artifact-cache identity and the compile service's target features. The
  default contract is unchanged; non-AArch64 targets and in-process JIT refuse
  an explicit profile.
- Volatile access preservation (X-OPCODES-P6): every AArch64 function
  compiled from a lowered source (each preparation and `compile_to_object`)
  checks that the final machine stream performs the lowered source's volatile
  loads and stores on every path, in order, by direction and size, and fails
  closed otherwise (`volatile_access_preservation`,
  `PipelineError::VolatileAccessNotPreserved`). Addresses and values are not
  compared, and removed source paths are refused rather than accepted. The six
  volatile inventory rows now need both this facet and their plain
  counterpart's memory model; the plain rows are still RED (X-OPCODES-P1), so
  the volatile rows stay deferred. New target
  `aarch64_volatile_access_preservation` corrupts real prepared streams
  (deletion, duplication, demotion, reordering, merging, resizing,
  fabrication, a removed arm) and requires each refutation.

- AArch64 JIT exception handling (L03-P12, L11-P10): unchecked JIT
  compilation now publishes invoke/landing-pad functions, and `panic_unwind`
  plain frames, with in-memory unwind tables instead of refusing them. A new
  `jit_unwind` module appends LSDAs, a personality indirection slot and a
  terminated `.eh_frame` after the code, binds every pointer through an
  explicit relocation list (`ExecutableBuffer::unwind_tables()`), and
  re-decodes the relocated tables, LSDA call-site coverage, frame-pointer
  prologues and each FDE's CFA program (whose final rules must match the
  prologue's decoded saves) independently before mapping. Frames saving
  D8-D15 are still refused by name: the CFI generator now describes them
  with `DW_CFA_offset_extended` (DWARF 72-79) and the independent decoder
  accepts such FDEs, but no native control yet restores an FP/SIMD pair
  across a JIT landing pad. After the read-execute seal the
  tables are registered with the process unwinder (per FDE on Darwin
  libunwind, per section on Linux libgcc), each FDE is read back with
  `_Unwind_Find_FDE`, and teardown deregisters before unmapping, honoring
  leases and the process-lifetime policy. Proof-grade modes refuse EH and
  panic-unwind publication with `JitUnwindProofEvidenceUnavailable`; the raw
  `compile_raw` API keeps `RawJitEhUnsupported`; profile hooks, unbound or
  mixed personalities, and mismatched prologues are refused by name; the
  jit-matrix TCJ1 cache refuses buffers with unwind tables. New target
  `jit_exception_handling` (11 tests; Linux floor and Darwin gate): a C++
  exception crosses a JIT cleanup frame whose destructor call is counted and
  is caught by a JIT catch-all at O0-O3, walks through a plain JIT frame, a
  Rust panic resumes through a JIT cleanup under `rust_eh_personality` to
  `catch_unwind`, execution on four threads, and teardown deregistration.
  Its Linux run is pending.
- AArch64 JIT certificate-cache controls (L11-P7): new target
  `jit_cert_cache_identity_aarch64` (9 tests; Linux floor and Darwin gate)
  ports the x86-64-only cache identity and validation-mode controls over an
  exhaustively checked `zext i8 -> i32`: a same-process CachedVerified warm hit
  through `compile_module_to_jit` with 512 native calls, function-name and
  relocation-name binding at identical bytes, raw-versus-source-bound
  separation, a source-swapped report that neither matches nor promotes,
  AlwaysVerify and deep-override bypasses, and no caching of refused bytes.
  The in-crate campaign gains a default-run stale-source and raw-None negative
  through the private LIR continuation, and the raw request-cache module a
  default-run cache-poisoning control that plants five mismatched receipts
  under the victim's key (`planted_receipts_under_the_victim_key_are_never_served`). These need the discovered AY/Clean
  authority and fail without it; the formal-frame `JIT_SOURCE_NATIVE`
  campaigns stay opt-in. The floors grow to 138 Linux targets and 178 Darwin
  targets with 1,220 minimum passes.

- AArch64 Mach-O objects now carry trust-ir function linkage like ELF:
  `Internal`/`Private` definitions lose `N_EXT`, `Weak`/`LinkOnce` and their
  ODR forms are `N_WEAK_DEF` (a COMDAT function must be bound weak; Mach-O
  has no section groups), and non-ODR weak bodies stay out of the module
  inliner. The Mach-O AOT access model (`ObjectAccessModel::macho_dyld`)
  addresses non-hidden weak and link-once definitions through the GOT so dyld
  can coalesce them across images. Relocated immutable globals move from
  writable `__DATA,__data` to `__DATA,__const`, which ld64 and the standalone
  linker place in the read-only-after-fixup `__DATA_CONST` segment; a mutable
  global naming `__DATA,__const` is refused (`TCG-SECTION-READONLY`).
- The standalone Mach-O linker places input `__DATA,__const`/`__DATA_CONST`
  data in `__DATA_CONST,__const`, and `link_dylib` exports default-visibility
  weak definitions `[weak-def]`, binding every stubbed call, GOT slot and data
  pointer to one through a `BIND_SPECIAL_DYLIB_WEAK_LOOKUP` import
  (`MH_WEAK_DEFINES | MH_BINDS_TO_WEAK`). A direct page reference to such a
  definition is refused (`LinkerError::DirectWeakDefinitionReference`).
- New `e2e_aarch64_macho_dylib` (Darwin floor, 8 tests): CG objects with
  exported, hidden and weak functions and data linked into dylibs by ld64
  and `link_dylib`; natively, `dlsym` visibility, dyld weak coalescing under
  the two-level namespace and `-flat_namespace`, `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`
  interposition and store faults on the relocated vtable after dyld binding,
  with writable-vtable and direct-weak-reference mutation controls, and ld64
  `-dead_strip` keeping only the `N_NO_DEAD_STRIP` (retained) definition.
- New `e2e_aarch64_concurrency` (Darwin floor 7 tests; registered in the Linux
  floor, not yet run on Linux): contended eight-thread RMW (all ten ops at
  8/16/32/64 bits) and CAS-loop controls against C `__atomic` and Rust
  `std::sync::atomic` oracles, message-passing and store-buffering litmus
  runs plus a load-buffering litmus and a CAS/store-release spinlock that
  never showed a forbidden outcome (testing evidence, not a memory-model
  proof), a non-atomic mutation control, a per-function decode that pins
  every executed atomic's LSE op, access size and ordering form (`AL` RMW,
  `CASAL`, `LDAR`, `STLR`) against ordering-strip mutations the native
  harness does not reliably notice, and three-wave TLS
  initialization/identity/isolation controls at O0-O3. The floors now
  require 180 Darwin targets (1,235 minimum passes) and 139 Linux targets.

- Darwin code signing (`X-DARWIN-P14`): `macho::codesign::verify_ad_hoc_signature`
  independently re-reads an image's embedded ad-hoc signature (SuperBlob,
  SHA-256 CodeDirectories, every page and special-slot hash, executable
  segment, the empty CMS wrapper) and refuses unsigned, tampered, certificate,
  non-SHA-256 and bundle-bound signatures by name. The standalone linker runs
  it on every executable and dylib it emits (`LinkerError::CodeSignatureSelfCheck`
  and `CodeSignatureContract`) and its signature sizing returns
  `LayoutOverflow` instead of panicking past the 32-bit code limit.
  `link_driver::run_link` verifies ld64's signature on every arm64 Darwin output
  and removes an unsigned one (`error[link:code-signature]`). The JIT reports a
  kernel `MAP_JIT` refusal as `JitError::MapJitRefused` with the process's
  `csops` flags (`jit::process_code_signing_status`), naming
  `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` under the hardened runtime. New Darwin
  floor targets `macho_code_signature_native` (7) and `jit_map_jit_entitlement`
  (5), and `link_options` (8 to 10), take the floor to 182 targets and 1,249
  minimum passes; they compare the verifier with `codesign`, observe SIGKILL
  for tampered and unsigned images, and observe the typed MAP_JIT refusal
  without the entitlement and success with it on macOS 26.6. The verifier
  accepts only 4 KiB and 16 KiB code pages and a 32-bit `codeLimit` equal to
  the signature offset: `codesign --verify` accepts 0 and 8 KiB pages and a
  `codeLimit` that disagrees with `codeLimit64`, but the arm64 kernel kills
  those images at exec.

- A retained Darwin diagnosis
  (`reports/2026-09-18-darwin-ay-dev-build`) builds AY `2657db47c` and Clean
  `ed21fee39` (tree `ed2a80d1`) as development executables with the aterm
  Trust toolchain's explicit unverified lane. They are selected only through
  `AY_SOLVER_PATH` and `TCG_EXTERNAL_CLEAN_CHECKER` and are not packages.
  Managed AY 0.13.0 answers `unknown` for the source-bound leaf-frame query,
  and the Trust bundle's AY 0.26.0 answers `incomplete self-check-rejected`.
  AY `2657db47c` proves it. Managed Clean 0.9.0 rejects that proof at a
  Carcara `poly_simp` step, and Clean `ed2a80d1` accepts it. With the pair,
  the ELF frame export and the CLI arithmetic export pass on macOS. The four
  proof-required JIT policy cases and 144 of the 160 JIT arithmetic
  combinations still fail closed. Apple arm64 trivial leaves are frameless,
  so no source-bound owner forms. This behaviour already existed at
  `ef2d7eaf`. No production discovery, policy or obligation changed. A
  macOS-only control in `jit_fail_closed_proof_policy` stays green while the
  positive JIT tests fail there: explicit `AlwaysVerify` must refuse the
  frameless ADD and identity leaves at O0-O3 and may publish `ADD #4096` only
  with Formal, non-sampled certificate rows. Dropping either the statistical
  or the non-vacuity condition from the JIT certificate predicate fails it; the
  existing macOS results did not show either change. The Darwin floor minimum
  for that target is now 8, one more than before.

- The Darwin AArch64 floor (`scripts/check_darwin_aarch64.py`) classifies every
  Linux-floor and macOS-guarded target again after the closure merges: 154
  required targets with 1,064 minimum passes, each minimum the pass count a
  native run on aarch64-apple-darwin executed (capped at the file's own test
  census where tests live in `#[path]` helper modules). Five formerly
  compiled-out Linux families now run their Darwin arms;
  `e2e_aarch64_host_target_authority_linux` is reported compiled out. The
  census also counts host-gated `#[cfg_attr(<predicate>, test)]` functions.
  The guard-kernel and overflow-carrier link-run pins capture the host
  linker's output, which Apple ld's `-no_pie` deprecation warning otherwise
  split into libtest's result lines.

- AArch64 ELF gains an explicit relocation model (`static`/`pie`/`pic`) in
  `CompilerConfig`, `PipelineConfig` and `trust-cg --relocation-model`,
  recorded in the compile policy and artifact-cache identity. Under `pic`,
  preemptible (default-visibility, non-local) data and function addresses load
  from the GOT, preemptible callees stay relocated calls and are never inlined,
  and thread-locals use general-dynamic TLS descriptors (TLSDESC: new
  `TlsDescCall`/`LdrTlsdesc`/`AddTlsdescLo12`/`BlrTlsdesc` opcodes and the four
  `R_AARCH64_TLSDESC_*` relocations, with independent decode checks and an
  encode-time shape check). `static`/`pie` read defined thread-locals with
  local-exec and imports with initial-exec (previously local-exec for every
  ELF thread-local). The former GD/LD "unreachable-by-lane" ISel refusal is
  removed. Weak and ODR definitions are preemptible under `pic`; `ExternalWeak`
  references stay GOT-indirect under every model; the `Pipeline` emitters'
  `pic` check honors local, hidden and protected function symbol bindings.
  `pie`/`pic` are refused outside AArch64 ELF object emission, including
  single-function Mach-O objects. TLSDESC
  rows are named in the relocation inventory but not certified, and the three
  emitted slots enter the AArch64 coverage denominator as deferred rows
  (163/250 -> 163/253 with 88 deferred rows, after the decoded-word credits). New target `e2e_aarch64_elf_relocation_model` (registered in the
  required Linux floor and the Darwin gate) adds object, `rust-lld`
  link/relaxation and Linux-native `dlopen`/interposition controls.
- AArch64 Linux ELF stack canaries (L02-P8): stack-protected functions now
  compile for Linux ELF with a global `__stack_chk_guard` read through
  `R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE`/`LD64_GOT_LO12_NC` and `__stack_chk_fail` reached
  by `CALL26`; other non-Apple targets are refused by name
  (`pipeline::stack_protector_target_abi`). New `runtime_deps` manifests group
  each object's undefined symbols by provider; the CLI writes them with
  `--emit-runtime-deps` and includes them in `--metrics`.
- CLI link driver (L02-P9): `-shared`, `-pie`/`-no-pie`, `-static`,
  `-nostdlib`, `-soname`, `-rpath` and validated `-Wl,` groups, with named
  refusals, and classified `error[link:<kind>]` diagnostics on link failure
  (`link_driver`). Linux links keep `-Wl,-z,noexecstack`, and a `-Wl` group
  requesting an executable stack is refused. The Darwin native controls in
  `e2e_aarch64_link_runtime` and the CLI's `link_options` run on macOS; their
  Linux legs, registered in the Linux floor, have run on the Linux AArch64
  host since 2026-09-23 (first in
  `reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-integrated-gates-3`).
  The Darwin floor now also requires `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` and
  `e2e_aarch64_elf_stack_zero_fill`, which had joined only the Linux floor.
- AArch64 relocation limits (L02-P10): `elf::RelocationWindow` models the
  CALL26/JUMP26 and ADRP windows; objects whose own layout exceeds them are
  refused with `PipelineError::RelocationWindowExceeded`. ELF zero-offset
  accesses to suitably aligned local data now use fused `ADRP; LDR/STR
  #:lo12:` with `R_AARCH64_LDST{8,16,32,64,128}_ABS_LO12_NC`, checked by the
  ENC-5 decoder and registered with alignment-preconditioned value
  obligations (+5 static obligations; not yet formally proved on the
  development host, see LIMITATIONS.md). Behavior change: ELF objects
  from the `Compiler` path are one instruction shorter per fused access.
  `proof_gate_strict` now pins the static corpus at 2,001: 1,979 + these 5
  rows + the 17 decoded-word value obligations, which had been registered
  without re-pinning the count; both additions are bound name-by-name.
- trust-ir niche-encoded enums now have a discriminant path (audit row
  L05-P1). The new `niche_codec` module ports the niche formula already used by
  trust-ir's interpreter and the rustc bridge: wrapping subtraction of
  `niche_start`, an unsigned range test over the niche variant interval, and
  the untagged variant otherwise. `ExtractField` element 0 decodes the lane,
  `InsertField` element 0 writes a runtime discriminant in place, and
  `Constant::Aggregate` writes the variant's declared fields plus the reserved
  lane value. Before any of that, the codec checks the producer's niche
  parameters against trust-cg's own layout and refuses with `[TCG-NICHE-ENUM]`
  on disagreement. Payload-only access keeps its admission when the codec
  refuses. `niche_enum_codec` runs the emitted LIR on an in-file evaluator and
  compares it with trust-ir's reference formula for sixteen shapes: every value
  of 8- and 16-bit lanes, boundaries plus a fixed sample for wider lanes, and
  the malformed-descriptor refusals. `e2e_aarch64_niche_enum` runs `Option<&u64>`,
  `Option<NonZeroU32>`, `Option<bool>`, `Option<char>` and two three-variant
  enums natively at O0-O3 against a C oracle (882 checks per level). Its ELF
  twin `e2e_aarch64_niche_enum_linux` and the Linux leg of the updated
  `e2e_aarch64_nested_bytes` niche row have not run on a Linux host; the
  nested-bytes niche row runs natively on macOS. Both floor inventories
  list the new targets: 118 Linux-floor targets, and 157 Darwin-floor targets
  with 1,086 minimum passes.
- AArch64 ELF objects now carry DWARF 4 debug information under `-g`
  (`emit_debug`) (audit rows L03-P4, the internal part of L03-P10 and the ELF
  part of L10-P9). Before this change an ELF triple with `-g` silently
  produced an object without debug sections. All three ELF emitters attach
  `.debug_abbrev/.debug_info/.debug_str/.debug_line/.debug_loc` through the
  checked symbol API. Code addresses use `R_AARCH64_ABS64` and section
  offsets `R_AARCH64_ABS32`, and in-place fields are zeroed. Mach-O and ELF
  now share one debug-info builder per path. Emission refuses out-of-function
  or unordered line rows and empty or out-of-function location ranges with
  typed `DwarfEmitError`s. The certified relocation inventory refuses ELF
  objects with DWARF, as it already did for Mach-O. The external checks
  found and fixed these defects, which affected both formats:
  instruction-derived line rows assumed 4 bytes per IR instruction and so
  drifted past pseudo instructions; `.debug_loc` entries were not relative
  to the compile-unit base; register location ranges began at the defining
  instruction; frame-base locations also covered the prologue and epilogue
  tail; incoming stack arguments were described at `X29 + csa + offset`
  instead of `X29 + 16 + offset`; and CFI truncated callee-saved D8–D15
  (DWARF 72–79) to X8–X15 through the 6-bit `DW_CFA_offset` form. The
  AArch64 ELF and both Mach-O `eh_frame` serializations now run the
  independent `verify_eh_frame_roundtrip` check before emission. The unused
  DWARF v5 stub sections (`elf/debug.rs`, `ElfWriter::add_debug_sections`)
  are removed; the module is now `elf/metadata.rs`. New targets:
  `aarch64_elf_dwarf` (llvm-dwarfdump/readelf/objdump checks at O0-O3, and a
  macOS lldb static leg) and `aarch64_elf_cfi_differential`
  (`llvm-dwarfdump --eh-frame` against the disassembled prologue and
  `FrameLayout`, with mutation controls) pass on macOS. The Linux-cfg
  `e2e_aarch64_elf_debugger_linux` is registered in the Linux floor and has
  not run on a Linux host. Its lldb logic was exercised on macOS against a
  Mach-O build of the same fixture. The DWARF image describes one `.text`, so
  `-g` together with ELF function sections or COMDAT function text (bodies in
  their own `.text.<symbol>` sections) is refused by name (fail-closed);
  `aarch64_elf_dwarf` pins that refusal (11 tests). The floors now hold 121
  Linux targets and 159 Darwin targets with 1,100 minimum passes.

- AArch64 atomics no longer require FEAT_LSE (audit rows L03-P5, L04-P5 and
  the lowering part of C-03). On a profile without LSE, including the generic
  Linux AOT profile, `AtomicRmw` at 8/16/32/64 bits and `CmpXchg` (Bool and
  8-64 bits) select opaque LL/SC pseudos. They expand after register
  allocation into `LD{A}XR{B,H}`/`ST{L}XR{B,H}`/`CBNZ` retry loops, and a
  compare-exchange failure exits through `CLREX`. The pseudos previously
  failed closed with "LSE target capability is not enabled". 128-bit atomic
  load, store, RMW and compare-exchange now lower on every profile through
  `LD{A}XP`/`ST{L}XP` loops that write back the loaded pair. Bool atomic
  exchange, and, or and xor lower as byte atomics. The new encodings (LDXR,
  LDXRB/H, LDAXRB/H, STXR, STXRB/H, STLXRB/H, LDXP, LDAXP, STXP, STLXP,
  CLREX) are validated before encoding. ENC-5 and the lift decoder decode them
  independently, and tests pin LLVM-assembled words over every register
  tuple. The opcode evidence inventory gains 29 honest RED rows: 27 new
  opcodes, plus LDAXR/STLXR, which are now emitted. With the TLSDESC opcodes
  and decoded-word credits already on main, the AArch64 inventory is 325
  opcodes, 163/282 accepted, with 119 RED rows (117 deferred and the two
  withdrawn FCMP/CSET mappings). The new
  `e2e_aarch64_llsc_atomics` target is required on the Linux floor and the
  Darwin inventory. On the Darwin host with a forced baseline profile it
  executes:
  - 51,200 RMW and 246,720 compare-exchange C11 checks;
  - 64,512 sub-word checks whose CAS and min/max operand registers carry
    bits above the access width;
  - 150,208 128-bit checks on the baseline and LSE profiles;
  - 8-thread contention, CAS-loop and torn-read tests, with CG LL/SC loops
    racing clang's inline LSE atomics on shared words;
  - a register-pressure function whose decoded exclusive windows contain no
    load or store.
  All run at O0-O3. Its Linux-native legs and the updated
  `e2e_aarch64_bool_atomics_linux` controls have not yet run on a Linux host.
  The backend neither emits nor needs the `__aarch64_*` outline-atomics
  helpers. Behavior change: the generic Linux AOT profile no longer refuses
  the 64-bit and narrow LSE atomic families by name; `e2e_aarch64_atomics`
  and `e2e_aarch64_narrow_atomics` now pin that it emits no LSE word and
  exactly one LDAXR/STLXR pair per SeqCst atomic. The floors now hold 122
  Linux targets and 160 Darwin targets with 1,115 minimum passes.
- WS7.8 (F-031, trust-cg half): a struct whose producer-declared layout is
  COMPLETE (every field offset, plus size and align) but which the byte path
  cannot emit is now REFUSED with `AdapterError::DeclaredStructLayoutNotEmittable
  { struct_id, name, gate }`. It used to fall back silently to the
  declaration-ordered natural-C layout, which differs from rustc's layout for
  the same memory. `DeclaredLayoutGate` names the first gate that failed:
  `packed`, `totals`, `coherence`, `field-alignment`, `containment` or
  `overlap`. A struct with no layout, or a partial one, keeps the named
  natural-C fallback. A packed struct whose packed walk reproduces the
  declared layout exactly still compiles. The refusal is raised where the
  layout is asked for: field addresses, copy extents, array strides, and
  enclosing declared, fallback or packed layouts. It is also raised, before
  lowering, for any function that holds such a struct by value (signature,
  block parameter, SSA value, `Alloca`, `HeapAlloc`, `Load`, `Store`, `GEP`,
  field access, or the signature of a `Call` / `Invoke` / `CallIndirect`
  callee, whose by-value aggregate argument may be carried by address), because
  stack slots and the ABI classifier size it from the natural carrier. A
  function that only passes a pointer to it still lowers.
  Refused shapes include the `Mixed {a@10 b@0 c@8}` reorder, `repr(align(16))`,
  the reordering `repr(packed(2))`, and the c07 overlap. A census rerun over
  every decodable trust-ir module on this host (411 modules, 574 struct defs,
  383 complete) refuses 2 structs. The 69-module `clean_kernel` corpus was not
  available, so its refusal count is not established.

- The adapter's trust-ir surface floor is now a pin-move floor (WS7.17).
  `reject_unconsumed_v41_target_neutral_surface` and
  `reject_unconsumed_v41_surface` used to check named fields with `if`, so a
  field added by a later trust-ir pin was compiled with its default meaning.
  They now read `Module`, `Function`, `FuncAttrs`, `ParamAttrs`, `Global`,
  `StructDef`, `EnumDef`, `ProofObligation` and `TargetInfo` through
  destructures without `..`. Each field is marked CONSUMED (with its lowering
  site) or REFUSED-WHEN-NON-DEFAULT (with its own `AdapterError`). A pin move
  that adds a field fails to compile `trust-cg-lower` (E0027) until the field
  is classified; this was checked once against a scratch trust-ir with an
  extra `Function` field. `BodyGate` is covered by the wildcard-free match in
  `CodegenLicensePolicy::verdict`. The target-dependent half now also refuses
  a declared `TargetInfo` that contradicts the lowered architecture:
  `TargetPointerSizeMismatch` (pointer size is not 8),
  `TargetEndiannessUnsupported` (big-endian) and
  `TargetStructPassingUnsupported` (`AlwaysMemory`). `NativeC`,
  `Unclassified` and an absent `target_info` are still accepted, and the wasm
  lane's target-neutral floor is unchanged except for one clause: the shared
  floor now refuses `ParamAttrs.byval` on a codegen declaration
  (`ByvalParamUnsupported`, or `[TCG-SRET-ABI]` for a byval sret one). A
  definition and a direct callee were already refused, but a declaration's
  address reached an indirect call, whose `FuncTy` carries no attributes, and
  was lowered as a plain-pointer call. The table-driven test
  `tests/pin_move_floor.rs` checks every native entry: each refused field is
  refused under its own name, and its accepted neighbours still compile.

- AArch64 ELF objects from every emitter now carry an empty `.note.GNU-stack`,
  so links get a non-executable `PT_GNU_STACK` without `-z noexecstack`. CLI
  links for Linux targets also pass `-Wl,-z,noexecstack`. No BTI/PAC property
  note is emitted because the backend emits neither. Writable all-zero
  definitions now use SHT_NOBITS `.bss` and all-zero TLS templates `.tbss`,
  keeping alignment, symbol sizes, STT_TLS offsets and relocation records.
  The ELF reparse gate rejects non-zero NOBITS content and relocations into
  NOBITS sections. Object-level tests cover every public route at O0-O3. The
  new Linux-native controls (`e2e_aarch64_elf_stack_zero_fill`, registered in the
  required Linux floor) have not yet run on a Linux host. The existing
  `e2e_aarch64_elf_tlsie` zero-template executions now exercise `.tbss` and
  also need a Linux rerun.

- AArch64 ELF objects now carry function symbol linkage (audit rows L02-P1,
  L02-P4 and the object part of L02-P6). The three ELF module emitters add
  symbols through a checked `ElfSymbolId` API and resolve relocation indices
  only after the locals-first symbol table is complete. A late symbol fails
  the checked write, so a local or weak function cannot shift a relocation
  target. `Compiler::compile` maps trust-ir function linkage to ELF bindings:
  `Internal`/`Private` become `STB_LOCAL`, `Weak`/`LinkOnce` and their ODR
  forms become `STB_WEAK`, and `External` stays `STB_GLOBAL`. The `Pipeline`
  API also spells hidden and protected functions. `Linkage::ExternalWeak` is
  admitted only on AArch64 ELF, as an `STB_WEAK` undefined, GOT-addressed
  function or non-TLS global declaration. It stays refused elsewhere; Mach-O,
  x86-64 and the adapter default refuse it with typed errors. Non-ODR weak
  definitions are no longer inlined on AArch64 ELF. The certified relocation
  inventory refuses a direct branch to a weak undefined function. The new
  `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` target checks every binding and visibility pair
  with an independent ELF reader. It also contains Linux-native O0–O3
  link/execute controls, which are registered in the required Linux floor
  but have not yet run on a Linux host.

- AArch64 ABI fail-closed work from the 2026-09-17 completion ledger
  (X-DARWIN-P12, L01-P1 refusal, L01-P8, L01-P9):
  - The `Pipeline` API has no default target. An empty or unrecognized
    `PipelineConfig::target_triple` is refused with
    `PipelineError::TargetAbiUnresolved` (`[TCG-TARGET-ABI]`) at instruction
    selection, allocation fix-up, frame lowering, debug info and object
    emission. It no longer selects DarwinPCS, Mach-O or a red zone.
    `AArch64AbiVariant::from_target_triple` now returns a `Result`.
    `PipelineConfig::for_target` and `PipelineConfig::for_host_aarch64` name the
    target, and `Pipeline::default_o2` is deprecated. In-tree callers now name
    their target. The raw JIT uses the host triple, which is AAPCS64 on Linux.
    `Compiler::target_selection` and `CompilationResult::target_selection`
    record whether the OS/ABI was explicit or derived from the host.
  - Every lowering entry refuses variadic function definitions with
    `AdapterError::VariadicDefinitionUnsupported` (`[TCG-VARIADIC-DEFINITION]`):
    the adapter, TrustIR-sourced pipeline selection, compile-service install
    signatures and the wasm lane. The AOT compiler, JIT and CLI surface this
    refusal. Variadic calls still lower. `va_start`/`va_arg` lowering remains
    unimplemented.
  - `byval` parameters on lowered definitions and direct callees are refused
    with `AdapterError::ByvalParamUnsupported` (`[TCG-BYVAL-ABI]`) instead of
    being lowered as plain pointers.
  - A new native clang oracle found a real DarwinPCS variadic misplacement.
    After one 8-byte vararg, `__int128` was stored at `[sp, #8]` while clang
    uses `[sp, #16]`. The Darwin anonymous tail now 16-aligns `__int128`,
    128-bit vectors and 16-aligned non-homogeneous aggregates of up to 16 bytes.
    It refuses (`[TCG-VARARG-ABI]`) by-reference aggregates and short-vector
    HVAs. `tests/e2e_aarch64_darwin_variadic_wide.rs` covers these cases at
    O0–O3.
  - The Darwin anonymous tail now starts after the last packed fixed stack
    byte. With two narrow fixed `int32_t` stack arguments at `[sp]` and
    `[sp, #4]`, the first anonymous argument was placed at `[sp, #16]` while
    clang uses `[sp, #8]`; the same native oracle covers it at O0–O3.

- AArch64 frames now carry inline stack probes (audit gap C-02). Static local
  areas are allocated in 4096-byte steps with `str xzr, [sp]` after each
  (a counted loop from 20 KiB), residuals above 1 KiB are probed, and
  runtime-sized allocations probe every step and their final SP, matching
  LLVM's AArch64 `probe-stack=inline-asm` scheme. Decode-emulation tests
  cover 4096-byte, 4112-byte and 1 MiB frames and runtime allocations at
  O0–O3 for Mach-O and ELF; Darwin native tests execute 1.5 MiB far-end
  arrays through AOT and JIT and fault inside the first guard page of a
  256 KiB thread. The matching Linux controls are registered in the regression
  floor but have not run on a Linux host. `encode_and_emit`
  now resolves the branches frame lowering adds, and the source-bound frame
  checker refuses bodies that adjust or store through SP.

- JIT publication hardening (AArch64 audit L11-P4/P5/P6):
  - The AArch64 icache flush uses CTR_EL0 minimum line sizes, starting at the
    first byte's line, instead of a fixed 64-byte stride. Darwin traps EL0
    CTR_EL0 reads, so there it uses a recorded 16-byte fallback.
  - `ExecutableBuffer::request_page_protection` refuses RWX and RW requests
    with typed errors.
  - Buffers enforce their teardown policy. `RefCounted` defers the unmap until
    every `JitExecutionLease` is released; `ProcessLifetime` retains the
    mapping. Other policies are refused.
  - `InstalledPayloadBinding` v5 and `ArtifactManifestV1` v2
    (`trust-cg.artifact/v2`) bind page-protection and allocation state, and
    replay compares it. Existing v1 manifests and v4 bindings are rejected and
    manifest checksums change.
  - Five JIT targets join the required Linux floor. They have
    not yet run on Linux.

- New `trust_cg_verify::aarch64_value_decode_proofs` credits the AArch64
  register copies (`MovR`, `FmovFprFpr`, `FmovFprGpr`, `FmovGprFpr`) and the
  scalar value forms `Smull`, `Bfm`, `Rbit`, `AddRIShift12` and `Mrs`
  (TPIDR_EL0) through decoded-word obligations: an independent Arm ARM decode
  of captured encoder words, compared over the whole destination register with
  the machine-IR intent, with negative controls that must each be refuted for
  their stated reason. The AArch64 ratio moves from 154/250 to 163/250 (85
  deferred rows plus the two withdrawn FCMP/CSET mappings). The function
  verifier binds each concrete SMULL/BFM/RBIT/shifted-ADD/MRS to one form; ENC-5
  runs the word check on every emitted instance of all nine opcodes. The new
  `aarch64_value_decode_gate` target re-derives the corpus from the live
  encoder and sweeps 59,664 words; `aarch64_value_decode_native` compares the
  model with the host CPU. Sampled acceptance is not formal proof.
- The AArch64 encoder no longer spells a move from or to a physical SP/WSP
  register through ORR, whose register 31 is XZR (MOV X3, SP had become
  MOV X3, XZR); every SP spelling now uses `ADD Rd, Rn, #0`, and a move between
  SP and a zero register is refused. FMOV (general) now refuses the
  unallocated W/D and X/S pairings and wrong-bank operands instead of emitting
  them.
- The opcode evidence inventory gains an AArch64 form-polymorphic gate
  (`coverage_gate::aarch64_form_polymorphic_proofs`). `Movk` and `Movn` now
  earn opcode-wide credit only when the already-bound per-form obligation of
  every legal (width, halfword shift) pair discharges; a missing, duplicated
  or illegal W-form `#32`/`#48` entry leaves the row RED. The AArch64 ratio
  moves from 152/250 to 154/250 (94 deferred rows plus the two withdrawn
  FCMP/CSET mappings). MOVN forms are checked over their full 16-bit
  immediate domain; MOVK forms remain sampled evaluator evidence, not proof.

- The standalone AArch64 Mach-O linker now applies `GOT_LOAD_PAGE21/PAGEOFF12`,
  `POINTER_TO_GOT` and `TLVP_LOAD_PAGE21/PAGEOFF12` through `__DATA_CONST`
  `__got`/`__thread_ptrs` slots without relaxing the `LDR`, resolves
  `__thread_vars` descriptors against contiguous `__thread_data`/`__thread_bss`
  templates, and sets `MH_HAS_TLV_DESCRIPTORS`. Imports are bound and image
  addresses, including 64-bit data pointers that were previously written unslid,
  are rebased through chained fixups. Stubs exist only for branch targets. It
  refuses by name pc-relative `UNSIGNED`, unslidable pointers, direct import
  references, TLV misuse and unimplemented section types. Zero-fill input no
  longer reads header bytes, `S_ATTR_DEBUG` input is not loaded, and `PAGEOFF12`
  refuses unscaled offsets and scales Q-register loads by 16. `LayoutResult`
  no longer reports a GOT offset, and the slot-free `RelocationApplicator`
  refuses the GOT/TLVP kinds, including `POINTER_TO_GOT`, which it previously
  resolved to the target instead of a GOT slot.
  New `link_dylib` emits an `MH_DYLIB` (base 0, `LC_ID_DYLIB`, an exports
  trie with per-thread TLV exports) and refuses weak exports.
  `e2e_macho_standalone_got_tlv` runs stack-guard, two-thread TLS and libSystem
  data-import programs at O0–O3 next to ld64 twins, serves a CG dylib to an
  ld64-linked program next to an ld64-built twin and to a standalone-linked
  program, and validates with `dyld_info`.

- TrustIR `Inst::Dealloc` now lowers when its pointer resolves, within the
  same function, to `Inst::HeapAlloc` sites of one allocator through `Copy`,
  thin-pointer `PtrToPtr`, `Select` arms or non-entry block parameters:
  `RustHeap` calls `__rust_dealloc(ptr, size, align)` with the allocation's
  exact layout (a dynamic count only on a direct SSA chain) and `CMalloc`
  calls `free(ptr)`. Other pointers, mixed origins or layouts, `SwiftHeap`
  and `CleanHeap` origins and dominated double frees fail closed with
  `[TCG-DEALLOC]`; cross-function frees still need trust-ir allocator/layout
  operands. A counting-allocator corpus with leak and double-free negative
  controls runs natively at O0-O3 on aarch64-apple-darwin, its ELF call-site
  checks run on every host, and its Linux-native twin joins the Linux floor
  (51 targets) without a Linux run yet.

- trust-ir v41 `Global.section` is now placed on AArch64 instead of refused.
  The ELF emitters honor valid names with flags derived from the name's kind
  and the global (mutability, TLS, pointer slots), keep declared alignment,
  relocate pointer slots into the placed section, and turn `.init_array[.N]`,
  `.fini_array[.N]` and `.preinit_array` into `SHT_INIT_ARRAY`-class tables
  whose every slot must be an `R_AARCH64_ABS64` pointer. The Mach-O emitter
  honors `__DATA`/`__DATA_CONST`/`__TEXT` pairs and `__mod_init_func`
  constructor tables. Every other request is refused with a named
  `[TCG-SECTION-*]` diagnostic (`object_sections::SectionRefusal`); x86-64,
  RISC-V and wasm refuse every explicit section, and the shared adapter floor
  refuses only malformed names. `CompilerConfig::function_sections`
  (`--function-sections`) places each AArch64 ELF function in `.text.<symbol>`
  and is recorded in the compile policy and cache identity only when enabled.
  On AArch64 ELF, `LinkOnceOdr`/`WeakOdr` functions and
  `LinkOnce`/`LinkOnceOdr`/`WeakOdr` globals get their own sections in real
  `GRP_COMDAT` groups. COMDAT placement is carried by
  `ModuleSymbolLinkage::with_comdat_functions` next to the function bindings
  (a COMDAT function must be bound `STB_WEAK`; Mach-O refuses the set), and a
  group's signature is bound to its definition's checked `ElfSymbolId`.
  `Weak`/`LinkOnce` functions stay plain `STB_WEAK` definitions in `.text`;
  the structural purity inference now skips them (and, under `pic`, every
  preemptible definition), as the module inliner already did, so no caller
  relies on a body another object may replace. An explicit section on a JIT
  module is refused (`[TCG-SECTION-TARGET]`). The ELF writer's old `.group`
  helper wrote `sh_link`/`sh_info` 0 and is replaced, and the reparse gate now
  checks group payloads, `SHF_GROUP` and `sh_entsize`. Object-level tests and a Darwin
  constructor run pass here; the Linux constructor/destructor, `--gc-sections`
  and cross-object COMDAT controls (`e2e_aarch64_elf_sections`) have not run
  on a Linux host. The rustc bridge still refuses `#[link_section]`.

- AArch64 native tests now select their host through
  `tests/common/native_host.rs`. Twenty formerly Linux-only native targets
  (integer and FP conditional selects, the six memory decode matrices, raw
  dataflow, exclusive words and status spills, integer predicates, affine
  bytes, FP-to-integer widths, Bool/U8 LSE atomics, nested bytes, typed global
  layout, ODR globals, HVA and short-vector ABI) executed on macOS ARM64. Forty-six formerly macOS-only native targets gained Linux GNU
  arms, with LSE, FP16 and DotProd families on an explicit-profile pipeline
  lane and object-level controls pinning the generic Linux refusals; those
  Linux arms have not executed yet. These 48 targets join the required Linux
  floor (50 to 98 on their own base; 116 with the other closure targets), and `scripts/native_test_host_matrix.py --check` maintains
  `docs/testing/native-test-host-matrix.md`. The NEON array fixtures, red on
  macOS since the CMP width validator, now build same-width comparisons.

- The public TrustIR adapter now checks exact pointer/metadata source types,
  actual SSA operands and single-result arity before lowering `PtrData`,
  `PtrMetadata` and `PtrFromParts`, including Unit-metadata early returns.
  This prevents same-width length/vtable confusion and preserves body-only
  Rc ownership refusal. Twelve regression tests cover all three public routes;
  the final lower-library/conformance/sret campaign passes 1,839 tests.
  The required Linux regression inventory grows to 40 complete targets.
  Full source validity, compiler proof and the expanded floor remain separate
  requirements; see `docs/linux-aarch64-completion.md`.

- Linux integration review of the incoming aggregate ABI lanes adds explicit
  canonical-convention/native-target admission, locally validated sret
  declarations, sret-aware narrow-argument register counting, competing-return
  refusal and retained-identity mutation tests. The independent affine checker
  refuses the new ABI metadata. The scoped lower/verify campaign passes 334
  tests; actual private-API bridge and mixed-backend Linux qualification remain
  pending. Cross-backend benchmark runners now retain bounded execution
  evidence and distinguish expected ABI diagnostics from unrelated failures.
  The upstream measurements below remain historical Darwin results, not a
  fresh Linux qualification. See `docs/linux-aarch64-completion.md`.

- trust-ir v41 is now CONSUMED, not merely carried. The codegen LICENSE
  (`Function.body_gate`) is honored on every lowering entry, the JIT compile
  service, the wasm lane and the CLI, through one decision
  (`trust_cg_lower::CodegenLicensePolicy`): `Some(Ungated)` is refused under
  every policy (trust-ir: "a codegen consumer MUST refuse it"), `Some(Gated {
  authority })` compiles only when the authority is recognized (default set:
  `clean-kernel-tv`, what `clean-compiler` stamps; unrecognized is a refusal,
  never a pass), and `None` — the pre-v41 "no claim" grandfather state — is
  permitted by default and refusable by policy (`--refuse-unlicensed`;
  `--recognize-authority <NAME>` widens the set). The compiler enforces the
  policy on the caller's module BEFORE any compile-artifact cache lookup and
  again inside the adapter before any adapter-owned clone, so neither a cached
  artifact nor a rewrite can launder an ungated body. Measured: 132 hand-built
  lowering fixtures in `trust-cg-lower` (121 in `adapter.rs`, 11 in
  `compute_graph.rs`) had been stamped `Some(Ungated)` by the v41 adoption;
  under the normative semantics that is a refusal, so every one of them failed
  (123 red) until re-stamped `None` ("no claim"). The ABI/linkage residue is
  consumed where the object emitters can honor it and refused, typed, where
  they cannot — each proved at the object level on Mach-O and ELF for both
  x86-64 and AArch64 (`tests/v41_abi_residue_objects.rs`):
  `Linkage::{WeakOdr, LinkOnceOdr}` global definitions emit weak
  (`N_WEAK_DEF` / `STB_WEAK`) and functions classify exactly like
  `Weak`/`LinkOnce` (byte-identical objects); `AvailableExternally` is never a
  definition (a global becomes a cross-object import whatever its initializer,
  a function's body is never lowered and every call or address-take resolves
  to the external symbol); `Global.visibility` on a definition becomes Mach-O
  `N_PEXT` for hidden (protected is default there, as in LLVM) and ELF
  `STV_HIDDEN`/`STV_PROTECTED`; `Global.retained` becomes per-symbol
  `N_NO_DEAD_STRIP` on Mach-O and `SHF_GNU_RETAIN` on the global's section
  plus `ELFOSABI_GNU` on ELF (section granularity is exactly the granularity
  `--gc-sections` already had, since the emitters pack every data global of a
  kind into one section). REFUSED, each with its own `AdapterError` and a
  test: `ExternalWeak` (the writers can spell `N_WEAK_REF`/weak-undefined, but
  the pipelines register undefined symbols by fixup name with no linkage
  channel, and a strong reference would silently replace null-on-missing
  semantics), `Global.section` (no per-global section placement in the
  emitters; since superseded — AArch64 now places or refuses it by name),
  non-default visibility on an import, `FuncAttrs.naked` (the
  backend always emits a prologue/epilogue), `FuncAttrs.target_features`
  outside the per-target modeled vocabulary (`known_target_features`,
  parity-tested against the backend's own ISA-feature enums),
  `Module.global_asm` (opaque text no emitter can assemble — also refused by
  the module merge, which rebuilds the merged module and would otherwise drop
  it), completed-status `Termination`/`Ownership`/`Custom` obligations (no
  authority is granted for those kinds — no wildcard), and
  `ProofEvidence::InheritedFromCallee { external: Some(_) }` (unauthenticated
  cross-crate inheritance). `ObjectGlobal` carries `visibility` and
  `retained`; the Mach-O writer gained `add_defined_symbol_with_attrs` and the
  ELF writer `add_symbol_with_attrs` plus a visibility-aware symbol model, and
  both reparse gates check the new bits. The compat `Visibility` twin in
  `trust_ir_compat` is gone: the real `trust_ir::Visibility` is the one
  spelling, with the Mach-O mapping kept as `VisibilityMachOFlags`. The
  manifest visibility binding classifies every linkage kind explicitly
  (`AvailableExternally`/`ExternalWeak` are `Imported`, never `Exported`).

- Review follow-up on that v41 consumption — three findings, each measured
  against the code and closed with a test. (1) The wasm32 lane
  (`wasm::compile_module*`) had applied only the license floor, `global_asm`
  and `naked`; every other refusal the native adapter makes was bypassed, and
  because the lane lays out every global by initializer and lowers every
  bodied function without ever reading `linkage`, an `AvailableExternally`
  global or function was EMITTED AS A DEFINITION — the one thing that linkage
  forbids. The lane now runs the native adapter's own target-neutral gate
  (`trust_cg_lower::reject_unconsumed_v41_target_neutral_surface` — the arch
  gate minus its feature clause, so the two cannot drift; pinned equal
  refusal-for-refusal) and adds the two clauses specific to wasm: any
  `target_features` entry is refused (no wasm feature is modeled — `neon` is
  refused there even though the native AArch64 lane accepts it) and an
  `AvailableExternally` GLOBAL is refused (a global is an absolute
  linear-memory address; the lane has no data-import channel). An
  `AvailableExternally` FUNCTION is a declaration for the lane exactly as for
  the native adapter — never emitted, bound through the func-import policy or
  refused as unbound — pinned byte-identical to the module whose helper is a
  bodyless declaration. What the lane CONSUMES is pinned by bytes too:
  visibility and `retained` on a global definition are vacuous (no data symbol
  is ever emitted and nothing is ever stripped) and `WeakOdr`/`LinkOnceOdr`
  functions are definitions exactly like `Weak`/`LinkOnce`. New typed
  `WasmLowerError::ContractSurface`. (2)
  `Compiler::plan_core_module_for_jit_compilation` never consulted the
  compiler's `with_codegen_license` policy: Core admission lowers under the
  default floor, so `Refuse` / `recognizing_nothing()` was silently ignored
  on the one entry that consumes an admitted Core. The plan now re-decides the
  license on the admitted module before anything else
  (`CoreJitPlanningError::CodegenLicense`), returning the owner on refusal.
  (3) The single-function entries `translate_function*` lowered an
  `AvailableExternally` body that the module entries skip; they now refuse it
  (`AdapterError::DeclarationNotLowerable`, likewise for a bodyless
  `External`) rather than hand back a body for a symbol another object
  defines.

- AArch64 ISel, aggregates in registers: **a silent over-read is fixed and a
  refusal is lifted**, both through one helper
  (`trust-cg-lower/src/isel.rs` `emit_exact_aggregate_return_lane`).
  * FIXED (wrong bytes, not a refusal): `select_aggregate_arg`'s
    `ArgLocation::Reg` arm loaded **8 bytes whatever the aggregate's size
    was**, so a 1..7-byte by-value argument read memory the object does not
    own — a fault when the object ends at a page boundary, another object's
    bytes in the argument register's high half when it does not. Its
    `RegPair` twin did the same on the HIGH lane of a 9..15-byte aggregate
    (8 bytes read where only `size - 8` exist). Both now read their exact
    width. Watched failing at the pin: a 1-byte argument read 8 bytes, a
    9-byte pair read 16.
  * FIXED, same class, on the RETURN side: the width-4 lane emitted `LdrRI`
    with an **X** transfer register, and `LdrRI`'s access width is derived
    from that register's class (`aarch64::encode::scalar_transfer_scale`,
    Gpr64 -> 8), so "load its exact memory width" was an 8-byte load. It now
    names the W alias.
  * LIFTED (`[TCG-REGALLOC-063]`): the exact-width aggregate return lanes
    refused every width outside {1,2,4,8}. 3/5/6/7 are now COMPOSED from
    exact lanes (3 = 2+1, 5 = 4+1, 6 = 4+2, 7 = 4+2+1) — never widened to one
    8-byte load, which would be the over-read above. `library/core` census
    (Trust stage1 `0cb693917a`, same instrument and flags as the tip
    baseline): failed roots **363 -> 346**, `[TCG-REGALLOC-063]` **31 -> 14**,
    52 reasons unchanged, zero newly-failing roots, emitted objects
    3086 -> 3103.
  * Differential rows: `tests/bridge_corpus/fix_p_exact_width_aggregate_return.rs`
    (refused `[TCG-REGALLOC-063]` before, matches LLVM after, -O0 and -O2),
    plus `fix_o_byval_arg_page_boundary.rs` and `fix_o_byval_arg_high_bytes.rs`,
    which are watched-and-did-not-fire detectors whose headers record the
    measured reason.

- trust-ir pin `3c15deeac` -> `31e9e618` (trust-ir main, wire format v40).
  v40 adds `FatPtrKind::ContainerVtable`, the `dyn`-tail sibling of v38's
  `ContainerLen` (the `*const ArcInner<dyn Any>` inside `Arc<dyn Any>`), and
  `module_merge`'s three exhaustive `Ty` walks refused to compile against it
  (E0004). The kind is ID-LESS — no `TyId`, no trait id — so it rides the
  same paths as `ContainerLen`: passed through the remap verbatim, nothing to
  range-check, and equal to itself under same-name dedup. It is deliberately
  NOT paired with `TraitObject`: the two lay out identically (two pointer
  words, an opaque vtable metadata word) but mean different things (container
  header vs dispatched object), so a `ContainerVtable` field against a
  `TraitObject` field is reported as a structural conflict, pinned by test.
  All three Cargo locks (root, `crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg`, `fuzz`) move
  together; the transitive Clean pin follows trust-ir to `feb5b3a9`.

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` was red at main on macOS before the
  pin moved, on test targets only, and is green after it. Fixed forward with
  it: `tests/common/aarch64_native.rs` included `rosetta.rs` without its
  `process_termination.rs` sibling (`super::process_termination` E0433 in the
  seven targets that include the file); `tests/e2e_bridge.rs` built
  `trust_cg_lower::Function` literals without the sret lane's two fields
  (E0063); two `_linux` targets' helpers are only called under a Linux cfg and
  tripped the workspace's `warnings = "deny"` as dead code on any other host.
  The unchecked compile-artifact cache's AY identity
  (`COMPILE_ARTIFACT_DEFAULT_AY_IDENTITY`) is re-bound to the regalloc
  manifest's ay pin `eec6fd64` (0.26.0), which `dependency_authority` asserts
  and which had been left at `b57b705` when that pin moved.
  The preserving Linux integration keeps its already self-contained process
  runner dependency and exactly one copy of each sret fixture field. The
  upstream results above are historical macOS results, not qualification of
  the merged Linux dependency constellation.

- Integrated backend: the register-level ABI lanes (indirect/sret aggregate
  return, and the register class/count work below) now sit on top of the
  `&dyn`/fat-pointer memory-leaf and tracked-knobs lanes. Measured on
  `library/core` at `-Copt-level=0`, fail-closed roots **505 -> 363**, accounted
  symbol by symbol: 196 roots that were `[TCG-RET-ABI]` now compile (the sret
  lane), and 54 new `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` roots appear where the register-class lane
  deliberately refuses an integer sub-eightbyte argument pair the bridge's
  argument lists cannot yet express. A further 26 former `[TCG-RET-ABI]` roots
  stay roots for a LATER shape — the return gate no longer hides what is behind
  it. Whole-corpus differential over `tests/bridge_corpus` (162 programs x
  `-Copt-level=0`/`=2`, stdout + exit code against the LLVM oracle): 324 runs,
  264 match, 60 fail closed, **0 mismatches**.

- Closed a pre-existing SILENT MISCOMPILE in the by-reference pointee lane
  tuple. `rust_ty_to_trust_ir_ty` maps a `&str` / `&[T]` field to a single `Ptr`
  lane — the same one lane a thin `&T` gets — so a struct holding one flattened
  to a lane tuple 8 bytes SHORT per fat field, and every later field then sat at
  the wrong byte offset while the callee read `(*r).field` at rustc's real
  offsets. Measured: `struct Rec { head: i64, name: &str, tail: i64 }` read
  through `&Rec` returned a text-segment ADDRESS for `head` (`4374919382` where
  LLVM printed `8`). `reference_pointee_lane_field_ty` now refuses a fat field
  by name (`[TCG-FAT-POINTEE-LANE]`), which routes the aggregate onto the
  rustc-layout byte path instead; it is not a capability loss. The `&dyn Trait`
  leaf was already correct precisely because it had no mapping at all and so
  already took that path.

- Closed a CONFIRMED, live, silent wrong-value path in the by-value aggregate
  ABI: the register **CLASS** and **COUNT** of a `PassMode::Pair`. `822fdc69`'s
  `ReturnPlacement` had two variants — registers or caller buffer — so it agreed
  with rustc while the registers differed. Measured 2026-09-11 across a real
  codegen boundary at `-Copt-level=0` and `=2`: `struct P { a: f64, b: f64 }`
  returns in `d0`/`d1` for LLVM and was returned in the GPR pair by trust-cg
  (both mixed links exited 0, oracle 42); `struct Q { a: i32, b: i32 }` returns
  in `w0` AND `w1` for LLVM and was packed into ONE register by trust-cg (188/28
  and 20, oracle 42). The ARGUMENT side had the same hole, equally live (80 and
  60/80 for the float pair, 20 and 244/4 for the integer pair), and had no gate
  at all. `ReturnPlacement` now carries a LANE LIST — class, count, per-lane
  extent and per-lane value offset — read on the rustc side from `PassMode`,
  `CastTarget`/`Reg`/`RegKind` and `BackendRepr`, and on the trust-cg side from
  the backend's OWN `AppleAArch64ABI::classify_returns`/`classify_params`.
  `[TCG-RET-ABI]` compares it lane by lane and a new `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` does the
  same for by-value aggregate arguments. Two lanes now EMIT the conformant
  placement instead of refusing: the float scalar-pair carrier (`{f64,f64}` /
  `{f32,f32}` in `d0`/`d1`, reusing the AAPCS64 HFA carrier machinery, both
  directions) and the two-value `PassMode::Pair` RETURN on AArch64 (`w0`+`w1`,
  `d0`+`x0`, …). New `benchmarks/regclass-xback` measures all four shapes in the
  four-way mixed-link table; `core` census 316 -> 376 fail-closed roots with
  `[TCG-RET-ABI]` at 0, the 60 being the by-value ARGUMENT scalar pair, which is
  refused rather than emitted (a parameter declaration is global to the callee
  and several argument lists in the bridge are built by hand; enabling the lane
  there was measured and turned 606 roots into loud arity failures).

- Lowered `core::fmt::rt::ArgumentType` / `rt::Argument` / `fmt::Arguments` from
  rustc's own layout when they are LOCAL to the crate being compiled (the
  self-host lane, i.e. compiling `core` itself), instead of assuming them away by
  NAME. The `format!`/`write!`/`println!`/`panic!` interception decodes those
  types at compile time and had two layout gates and the deadness seeding keyed
  on the name alone, so inside `core` a real assignment could be skipped: measured
  2026-09-10, `core::panic::PanicInfo::message` compiled to a load from an
  UNINITIALISED stack slot instead of `self.message`. The deadness seeding is now
  re-rooted at the calls an interception actually consumes (a diverging panic
  block, `std::io::_print`/`_eprint`, `<String as fmt::Write>::write_fmt`,
  `alloc::fmt::format`, and the O2/O3-inlined `map_or_else` consumer), never a
  function parameter, and the call-to-no-op rule now consults that set rather than
  the type. Downstream-crate behaviour is unchanged by construction. The `core`
  census falls 438 -> 316 fail-closed roots with the `Ty::fmt::rt::ArgumentType`
  class at 0 (was 131), no newly failing symbol, and every previously emitted
  object byte-identical except the three `PanicInfo` accessors. New
  `benchmarks/fmt-selfhost` differential corpus compares stdout AND exit status at
  -O0/-O2 for both sides of the split.

- Took the by-value AGGREGATE RETURN convention from rustc's own `FnAbi`
  instead of the backend's aggregate classifier, and fail closed with
  `[TCG-RET-ABI]` when the two disagree. trust-cg places an aggregate return by
  the C rule (AAPCS64 §6.9 / System V: register pair up to 16 bytes, hidden
  return buffer above); rustc's RUST ABI keeps every `BackendRepr::Memory`
  aggregate larger than one pointer on `PassMode::Indirect`, i.e. in the `x8`
  buffer. Measured 2026-09-10 with an `rt::ArgumentType`-shaped 16-byte niche
  enum returned across a real codegen boundary: `LLVM x LLVM` exits 42,
  `trust-cg x trust-cg` exits 42, a trust-cg CALLER of an LLVM callee crashes
  (138), and an LLVM caller of a trust-cg callee gets a SILENT WRONG VALUE (0).
  Both sides are internally consistent, so no whole-program differential in this
  repo could see it. The mode was refused by name with its `PassMode` and the fix
  options rather than lowered, at a cost recorded not hidden: the `core` census
  went 316 -> 516 fail-closed roots, 221 of them `[TCG-RET-ABI]` (50 return an
  `rt::Argument`-family type; the rest are ordinary 9-16 byte Memory-repr
  returns such as `Option<ascii::EscapeDefault>`, `char::EscapeDebug`,
  `[char; 3]`) — objects that were previously emitted with the wrong convention.

- LOWERED that convention, which repays the refusal's whole cost. When rustc's
  `FnAbi` says `PassMode::Indirect`, the lowered function now takes a hidden
  LEADING return-buffer pointer parameter and returns nothing — the shape
  trust-ir already states and validates (`ParamAttrs::sret`: pointer-typed,
  unique, empty return list), so no trust-ir change was needed. The callee writes
  its result through that pointer; the caller allocates the buffer (it uses the
  destination slot, exactly as rustc's own `make_return_dest` does) and passes
  its address. Every placement fact comes from the target's own rule, never a
  size heuristic: **AAPCS64 §6.9 `x8`**, outside the X0-X7 argument bank, so the
  ordinary arguments are numbered as if the hidden one did not exist; **System V
  x86-64 `rdi`**, a hidden leading INTEGER argument that shifts the rest, plus
  the psABI §3.2.3 requirement that the callee return that address in `%rax`.
  Any other target REFUSES. The convention is carried to the selectors as
  `Function::abi_sret_param` / `Function::sret_arg_callees`, read by the adapter
  from the callee's own `ParamAttrs`, so the two sides of a call edge cannot
  derive it independently. INDIRECT calls (a `fn(..)` pointer, a vtable slot) do
  not lower it and keep failing closed: the marker is keyed by callee SYMBOL and
  neither has one. `[TCG-RET-ABI]` is UNCHANGED and still runs on every
  by-value aggregate return — it is told which placement the bridge will emit,
  compares that against rustc's, and goes silent only because they now AGREE.
  Measured 2026-09-11: all four mixed-link directions exit 42 at -O0 and -O2
  (new `benchmarks/sret-xback`, with the 42/42/0/138 table as its negative
  control); the `core` census returns to 316 fail-closed roots with
  `[TCG-RET-ABI]` at 0 and 200 more emitted objects (2933 -> 3133), and NO symbol
  that compiled before now fails.

- Required PROOF that every reader is intercepted before the self-host deadness
  seeding may skip a local's assignments. The fmt-dead region is rooted at the
  calls an interception consumes, and the diverging-panic arm deliberately roots
  every projection-free argument regardless of type (the `Arguments` often
  arrives wrapped, e.g. `assert_failed(kind, &l, &r, Some(args))`). Seeding on
  reachability alone therefore marked a local dead whenever it merely FLOWED
  INTO an interception, even with a live non-intercepted reader — and a local
  marked dead has its real assignments skipped, which is a miscompile, not a
  refusal. `fmt_locals_proved_only_intercepted` now computes a greatest fixpoint
  over the candidates, striking out any local with a runtime read or one feeding
  a struck-out local; it errs toward "runtime read" for every shape it does not
  model, so it can only shrink the dead set. Downstream-crate seeding is
  untouched. On `core` at `-O0` the change is byte-identical except one dead
  instruction in one panic block, so the defect was latent there; the new
  `benchmarks/fmt-selfhost/progs/selfhost_live_reader.rs` exercises it directly
  by compiling under `--crate-name core` (the only way a user-runnable program
  reaches the self-host branch) and refuses to compile on the pre-fix seeding.

- Corrected x86 flag-liveness handling across partial flag writers and calls.
- Fixed integer-array bound recognition substituting a widening source that
  could have been reassigned after capture. Preserve the compared value and
  check 64-bit bounds against the i32 projection before vector entry. Valid
  invariant wide bounds no longer require constant reconstruction, and i64
  reductions retain their lane width with widened bounds. Added native
  captured-value/width-boundary controls and checked-construction variants.
- Fixed integer-array loop-entry semantics: signed i64 ranges no longer use
  unsigned ordering; unsigned i32 chains and wider indices receive domain
  checks before address lowering. Bottom-tested GE loops retain their mandatory
  first iteration. Strict top-tested loops now require an effect-free entry
  guard matching the latch. Native scalar/vector controls reproduced the
  boundary failures and compare results plus observed vector-iteration counts.
- Migrated all five integer-array vectorizer builders to checked candidate
  construction. Removed copied allocator/emitter/layout/splice helpers; failures
  now discard preheader edits, fresh IDs and CFG changes together. DotProd target
  gating is unchanged. Added capacity, stale-anchor, repeat-pass
  and output-preservation controls; removed unstamped performance claims.
- Fixed scalar AArch64 integer/FP conversions always encoding 64-bit integers.
  SCVTF/UCVTF now read the integer source width; FCVTZS/FCVTZU use the integer
  destination width. Shared admission rejects malformed register files, SP and
  arity. Added independent assembler-word checks and bounded native FP fill
  comparisons; the native regression exposed negative i32 values being read as
  positive i64 values in the scalar fallback.
- Extended checked candidate construction to FP array reductions and iota fills;
  removed their copied allocator/emitter/splice helpers and three panic sites.
  Corrected fill alias ranges for negative starting indices. Declined repeated
  stores through one post-increment base and in-loop FP negation, whose old
  zero-minus lowering changed signed-zero/NaN behavior. Default mode and source
  fusion licenses are unchanged; unstamped performance claims were removed.
- Migrated integer-map, FP-map/count and private conditional-store construction
  to checked candidates, including runtime alias checks and vector remainders.
  Split integer MLA recognition from fallible lowering and removed copied
  construction helpers. Conditional-store's public pass remains inert without
  typed memory authority; the structural tests do not enable blind stores.
- Extended checked candidate construction to all five min/max and predicated-sum
  paths, including index tracking and widening chains. Construction failures
  leave the entire input unchanged; copied allocator and splice helpers are
  removed. Fixed argmin/argmax repeatedly vectorizing its own scalar remainder.
  Updated width/order comments and removed unstamped performance claims.
- Rejected negative statistical evidence in both verifying x86 JIT modes;
  object-report compatibility no longer authorizes a function whose published
  validation verdict would be false. Corrected proof-policy tests that confused
  opcode inventory, compatibility reports and proof-grade JIT publication.
  Merged-object symbol checks now fail on missing parse/compile results instead
  of silently omitting their assertions. Missing formal coverage is unchanged.
- Made resource-budget, identity-exhaustion, and selected malformed-input
  boundaries return errors; preserved the existing panic-ratchet limits.
- Made poisoned certificate caches miss and decline writes, and poisoned
  rewrite-admission caches decline optional rewrites without reusing damaged
  state. Saturated decoder telemetry counters and exposed their poison health
  flag instead of crashing or wrapping counts.
- Rejected empty recorded instruction extents before decoder dispatch and
  removed unstamped historical bridge size/speedup claims from build comments.
- Bound optimizer analysis-cache hits to exact CFG snapshots, saturated analysis
  and dominator timing counters, and widened dominator tour stamps. Re-enabled
  the forged-authority integration control under all features after verifying
  that its old ignore rationale no longer matched production capability handling.
- Reused the shared analysis cache in extended-register address folding, binding
  one lazy snapshot during recognition and removing paired optional-state
  bookkeeping. Removed unstamped timing and obsolete implementation claims from
  the reviewed reaching-definition, multiply-reduction, and block-merge comments.
- Checked conditional-swap's two-register reservation before mutation, preventing
  ID-counter overflow and release-mode wrapping. Corrected its stale opt-in
  documentation to match the pipeline's current default-on registration.
- Added checked machine-IR register allocation and migrated NEON FP reduction
  to it. Synchronize sparse IDs once instead of incrementally walking gaps;
  discard partial candidate construction on exhaustion or lowering/splice
  refusal. The legacy allocator and remaining callers are not yet migrated.
- Added shared machine-IR counter synchronization and checked block/stack-slot
  append APIs. Iota-fill now constructs a private candidate and propagates
  allocation, instruction-insertion and layout/splice refusal. FP reduction
  shares the counter/block APIs and now propagates failed instruction insertion
  and missing layout anchors too; legacy callers remain an open migration.
- Required AArch64 stack guards now reject missing, out-of-arena or malformed
  reserved storage before frame insertion. Reservation is fallible and
  idempotent, and the pipeline preserves typed frame-lowering errors.
- Shared checked candidate construction across six NEON vectorizers. Migrated
  fill, bit reversal, stencil and butterfly off repeated unchecked allocation;
  iota-fill and FP reduction now reuse the same emission, anchor and entry-edge
  helpers. Declined candidates cannot publish partial instruction/CFG metadata.
  Consolidated butterfly address construction and corrected fill's stale
  32-byte-loop, performance and blanket proof-coverage comments.
- Migrated both integer-reduction vectorizer paths to the same checked
  candidate boundary. ID exhaustion, missing setup/layout anchors and lowering
  refusal no longer leave partial preheader/CFG edits. Split shared-multiply
  recognition from fallible emission and removed the accumulator-lane assertion.
  Corrected reduction seed, pass ordering and formal-evidence comments.
- Replaced the regalloc model's infallible `alloc_vreg` with `try_alloc_vreg`.
  Phi lowering and parallel-copy resolution now return `Result`, planning all
  IDs/copy sequences before committing. Optional splits decline on exhaustion,
  and non-progress splits no longer consume an ID. Shared allocation errors
  preserve the previous `linear_scan::AllocError` import path. Corrected stale
  comments claiming call-crossing hints had no production consumer.
- Replaced the regalloc model's infallible stack-slot allocator with
  `try_alloc_stack_slot`. Spill and call-save insertion now return `Result`
  and plan slots/metadata before mutation, rejecting exhaustion without
  partial insertion or overwriting slots when counters are stale. Generic
  and target-owned spill paths share deduplication and canonical register
  sizes. Corrected obsolete pipeline, validator and AY differential comments.
- Shared dialect structure admission across conversion, legality and emission.
  Reject duplicate/undefined source values before renumbering; require explicit
  destination mappings and validate rebuilt output before publishing it.
  Direct `machir` emission now diagnoses missing function indices, checks
  canonical opcode types/return shapes, refuses unsupported block structure,
  and handles register exhaustion. Added typed `UnmappedValue`, `MissingFunction`,
  `InvalidFunction` and `VirtualRegisterExhausted` diagnostics.
- Completed argument/return transfers and full-width constant expansion for the
  single-block I64 dialect facade. Preserve unread argument-register live-ins,
  use canonical incoming stack operands, move results to X0, and emit legal
  MOVZ/MOVK halfwords. Added checked machine instruction insertion and the
  `InstructionIdExhausted` diagnostic; reject unsupported ABI parameter types.
  Added emitted-byte interpreter/native controls, including negative controls
  for a removed argument copy and a high-bit result mismatch. Corrected stale
  one-operation/one-instruction and incoming-frame-offset documentation.
- Saturated SAT event counters so exhaustion cannot reopen the divergence
  guard's warmup window. Corrected legacy telemetry descriptions that confused
  primary activity with authoritative returns and predicate shortcuts with
  independently checked agreements.
- Extracted AArch64 AOT counter insertion into a phase that validates and
  plans code, fresh IDs and metadata before mutation. Refuse poisoned maps,
  malformed layout, duplicate sites and exhaustion; preserve the existing
  counter-offset ceiling diagnostic. Public LIR and machine-IR compile/prepare
  routes now all honor the sink. Profile-generation batches prepare in input
  order, fixing worker-dependent slot assignment and emitted bytes. Nine
  armed regressions reproduced these defects before repair; boundary/API,
  native positive/negative and real importer GEN-to-USE checks now pass.
- Shared root-only/analyze-driver benchmark measurement controls: explicitly
  select distinct modes, restore flags on errors/unwind, exclude warmup from
  telemetry, and reject inconsistent or mismatched verdicts.
- Extended the shared boundary to every solve lane in both SAT benchmark
  drivers. Reject saturated/regressing rates; isolate disk experiments in an
  owned temporary directory with real I/O and priming checks. Removed stale
  amortization classifications and unmeasured cache-hit claims.
- Repaired Mach-O BSS mapping/alignment, dynamic stub/GOT layout and encoding,
  input symbol rebasing, weak/strong reference resolution, dead-strip relocation
  remapping, and malformed symbol/string-table admission. Reused the existing
  SHA-256 dependency while retaining independent signature test oracles.
- Rejected truncated/defaulted NEON control operands and invalid scalar shift
  intent. Repaired 64-bit element-duplication width selection and rejected
  nonvector destinations and reserved DUP arrangements. Bounded unwind
  decoding to each declared entry and rejected length arithmetic overflow and
  out-of-width LEB128 terminal groups.
- Bound proof-tool discovery to aterm's managed AY and Clean executables;
  evidence snapshots now follow changed tool selections. AY remains the sole
  solver. A corrected Clean package release is still needed.
- Removed the shared codegen command runner's blocking wait after a kill
  request. Both runners now use one nonblocking termination boundary and report
  unconfirmed exits and kill/poll errors. Migrated five copied EH supervisors
  and the LLDB fixture to it while preserving their status conventions.
  Corrected stale EH support, timeout-safety and proof claims in their comments
  and diagnostics. Native adapter controls do not claim successful EH execution
  or complete migration of production solver/checker supervisors.
- Shared complete, deadline-aware pipe capture for fresh AY execution, AY
  version probes and Lean replay. Drain both streams while waiting, require
  EOF plus child exit, and reject partial transcripts after a deadline. Lean
  checks retain late `sorry` diagnostics even after exit status zero. Preserve
  unreaped Unix child ownership for group cleanup; replace resident AY's
  blocking teardown wait with bounded polling and clean up setup failures.
  Existing timeout, argument and solver-authority policies are unchanged.
  Removed stale binary-size, startup and identity-hashing timing claims beside
  the changed paths.
- Replaced resident AY's blocking stdin write and detached output-reader thread
  with a polled two-way exchange. Include lock contention and both directions
  in one deadline, preserve partial writes/lines and frame boundaries, and
  stop frame-handler unwinds and prevent reuse of a stopped exchange. Discard
  poisoned sessions, check sentinel
  sequence exhaustion and retain timeout-without-retry and proof-cache guards.
  A large-request control reproduces the former deadline bypass; native/model
  controls do not establish real AY proof completeness or Windows runtime support.
- Bound Clean capability probes, proof replay and AY cache minting to the
  configured per-subprocess budget, preserving zero as unlimited. Distinguish
  timeout from proof rejection, avoid duplicate discovery on failed promotion,
  and keep transient process failures out of capability memos. Share owned
  no-clobber certificate publication across both writers; fix a Unicode
  diagnostic truncation panic and redirected writes through shared staging
