  symlinks. Correct synchronous-mint comments and remove stale timing claims.
- Marked the unrequested external-certificate campaign as a runtime SKIP and
  taught captured-result accounting its former opt-out spelling.
- Separated AY binary identification from proof-toolchain availability so an
  incapable Clean package is no longer misreported as a missing AY executable.
  Shared formal-floor prerequisite diagnostics without weakening admission.
- Made skipped soundness prerequisites fail completion and prevent re-pinning;
  the wasm encoding gate now includes its exhaustive signed-i32 sweep in release
  mode. Added a no-clobber, commit-bound exporter for the aterm VT-island tables.
- Marked unrequested formal campaigns as runtime SKIPs and recognized their
  former opt-out message in retained captures, removing false pass credit from
  both matrix and soundness reports.
- Corrected AY LRA ABI admission to require the complete callee-save register
  set, rejecting truncated or overstated descriptors. Replayed the portable
  certificate set before refreshing its checker-byte manifest binding.
- Reconciled the peephole registry assertion with its exact current entries;
  repaired repeated SSA definitions in batch-overflow fixtures, stale Mach-O
  alignment expectations, and missing ADCS/SBCS encoder-fuzz strategies.
- Admitted compatible repeated external declarations without collapsing their
  source function IDs or call authorizations; incompatible contracts and
  function/global definition collisions remain errors.
- Located the TLSIE object golden by its relocation pair, accounting for frame
  prologues while tightening immediate-field and register-dataflow checks.
- Replaced seven copied MIR watchdogs with a shared implementation that forwards
  worker panic payloads instead of misreporting them as timeouts.
- Corrected matrix result parsing/control isolation and benchmark prerequisite
  diagnostics, including rejection of a zero-attempt determinism run.
- Wired captured-output matrix reporting for stable and nightly libtest;
  separated raw passes, qualified passes, runtime SKIPs, and incomplete capture.
  Retained every shard log and used a monotonic elapsed-time clock.
- Reused captured-output validation for both soundness Cargo lanes, rejecting
  ignored/filtered cases and runtime SKIPs and preserving actual runtime failure
  classification. Kept the source-built Clean checker's packaged feature enabled.
- Reused the supervised executable runner for x86 EH integration timeouts;
  a blocked translated child no longer requires an unbounded synchronous reap
  in either EH fixture, and timeout diagnostics do not invent an unwind diagnosis.
- Made call-crossing differentials report missing oracle/JIT results as
  failures, check both direct and indirect paths, and reuse each compiled
  artifact across all input rows. Memory fixtures retain their JIT store/load
  and use an explicit equivalent register-only reference.
- Shared compile-once execution across comparison and nested-call fuzz drivers;
  required every selected reference result and retained every compiler failure.
  Added independent scalar coverage for comparison memory and wide-unsigned
  fixtures without reducing their shape, input, allocator, or optimization sets.
- Froze the WP-0 serialization fixture's historical ABI input without changing
  its golden checksums; verified that corrected ABI fields change artifact and
  bound-evidence identities.
- Shared bounded LLVM file input between library and driver; enforced the byte
  limit during reading and before UTF-8 decoding. Unified checked struct layout,
  preserved complete shared nested field types, and rejected initializer type
  mismatches and oversized byte images before writes or allocation.
- Prevented the panic-Clippy gate from reusing unlinted dependency artifacts
  as primary-package results. Required a consistent Cargo completion event;
  empty or partial logs cannot manufacture a passing lint census.
- Bound panic-review annotations to source hashes and exact site identities;
  changed guards and identical new snippets cannot inherit stale reviews.
  Kept unresolved poison boundaries explicit and the accepted counts unchanged.
- Updated maintained documentation, added a reproducible source inventory,
  and archived superseded reports without discarding their evidence. Existing
  benchmark measurements remain historical, not fresh audit results.

Development changes since 0.6.0, not a released package. Open failures and
limitations are in [`LIMITATIONS.md`](LIMITATIONS.md) and, in the development
tree, the AArch64 closure ledger (`docs/aarch64-completion-audit-2026-09-17.md`);
each change's evidence is in its commit and the report it cites.

### Fixed

- Raising panic blocks preserve ordinary statements before calling the panic
  runtime under both abort and unwind strategies. Panic hooks now observe
  preceding stores; unsupported live statements refuse rather than disappear.
- AArch64 functions with a conditional branch spanning more than +/-1 MiB
  (`B.cond`/`CBZ`/`CBNZ`) or +/-32 KiB (`TBZ`/`TBNZ`) now compile: the
  pipeline relaxes each such branch before resolution instead of refusing it
  at encoding (`branch offset ... out of signed 19-bit range`, hit by TY W4).
  `relax::relax_out_of_range_branches` keeps every target a block: the
  complemented branch to the layout successor over a `B` to the far target
  (`bcc_inv +8 ; B T`), a target swap with a near trailing `B`, or a split of
  a trailing run of branches into a new block, iterated to a fixed point. A
  function with no out-of-range branch is untouched (compile-corpus identity
  PASS, 534 entry-lanes). A far jump-table bounds branch, `B.al`/`B.nv` and an
  unconditional branch beyond +/-128 MiB are refused by name
  (`[TCG-A64-BRANCH-RELAX]`).
- Scalar-cell field accesses preserve writes to a scalar newtype with leading
  zero-sized fields. The projection selects the sole field occupying storage
  and retains the original allocation's checked offset, extent, alignment and
  scalar type; the existing cross-backend `ZstLead` regression now passes.
- AArch64 Rust scalar-pair arguments now use independent lanes on Apple as
  well as Linux, including floating pairs at register exhaustion. HFA planning
  yields parameters owned by that lane while preserving returns and C casts.
  Over-aligned scalar-newtype home projections retain the recorded rustc
  extent and the same scalar at offset zero.
- Reusing a linear-scan allocator now preserves the historical allocation,
  spill order and free pools by falling back from its cached active holders.
  A two-call regression compares the result with the original allocator.
- The Rust bridge's `no-x86-thin-ref-aggregate-addr` control now affects only
  x86-64; it preserves the existing AArch64 thin-reference address path.
- Darwin proof-tool assessment reports success only after the suspended-child
  check, successful kill and confirmed exact-child reap. Failed cleanup disables
  further assessment spawns. Process timing tests accept finite zero readings
  at kernel clock resolution, retaining ordering and elapsed-time bounds.
- Direct LIR loads/stores of whole structs, arrays and enums now refuse on
  all native selectors, including volatile accesses; scalar aggregate-constant
  fields also reject composite carriers. Producers must copy exact bytes or
  pass an address instead of silently truncating aggregate values.
- x86-64 boolean loads and stack arguments now zero-extend before ABI use;
  boolean complement masks its result to bit zero. The adapter refuses scalar
  `not bool` and non-boolean bitcasts into `bool`, and x86 selection rejects
  non-B1 carriers into B1. Incoming-memory boolean semantics retain their
  documented contract boundary.
- Requalify the Apple-silicon portable DRAT checker for the pinned 26.5
  deployment target, restoring exact-byte portable certificate replay. The
  checker report
  records the old/new identities and scoped regression results.
- Rust bridge referent-storage discovery now includes trait-object unsizing,
  thin reborrows and borrowed aggregate fields under the existing admission
  predicates. Unresolved identity and unsupported pointee shapes still refuse.
  Wide-leaf aggregate copies use lane tiling checked against rustc's full layout.
- Restore Linux builds of the JIT matrix cache by declaring its existing libc
  dependency on Linux as well as macOS, matching the getentropy call's cfg.
- Reconcile local ABI work with current lowering: use checked float closure
  result carriers, retain indirect-call ABI facts, and refuse unresolved
  trait-reference identity, Fn* shim and foreign-unwind boundaries instead of
  emitting unsafe code. Expand independent native regression coverage and
  document implemented compiler capabilities separately from qualification.
- Undefined IR, rustc bridge (WS7.1, F-111): the MIR lane emitted the store
  form of `InsertField` (a slot-pointer aggregate), which trust-ir does not
  define; its field writes are now an address and a typed `Store` that keeps
  the value-type gate (`[TCG-FIELD-STORE-TYPE]`) and the field offset of the
  lane that consumes the module (wasm32 pointers are four bytes), and the
  native adapter refuses the store form on every entry
  (`AggregateInsertNotValueForm`); the wasm32 lane still lowers it as a
  write-through.
- Wrong code, Linux link driver: images whose loaded pages held other bytes
  than the sections its checks read (page-granular `PT_LOAD` mapping at every
  AArch64 page size, sections outside every segment, non-zero `NOBITS` file
  bytes) or whose trust-cg data a store could not write are refused
  (`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]`, `[TCG-LINK-WRITE-PROTECTED]`), and seven kinds
  of ordinary link are no longer refused.
- Proof-grade AArch64 compiles for Apple targets (`--emit-proofs`, a
  verifying JIT) keep the FP/LR envelope the source-bound frame owner binds;
  the red zone had left trivial leaves frameless and refused. Ordinary
  compiles keep the red zone.
- Wrong linkage, LLVM importer: function and global linkage, visibility,
  COMDAT and section are carried instead of defaulted (a hidden `pic`
  function was exported); shapes this base cannot lower faithfully are
  refused by name (L02-P13).
- Undisclosed premise: structural purity inference read a bodied
  `AvailableExternally` function, whose calls reach another object's
  definition; it no longer does.
- Wrong linkage, LLVM importer: `define available_externally` was imported
  as an `External` definition, so the object carried a strong symbol LLVM
  never emits; it is now trust-ir `AvailableExternally` (never emitted, and an
  inline-only template at O1+).
- Wrong code, AArch64 Darwin shrink-wrapping: a frame path reaching a
  leaf-shared `ret` through a join the save block does not dominate returned
  with callee-saved registers, FP and LR unrestored; frame and leaf regions
  are now separated by reachability.
- Wrong code, rustc bridge ABI: `PassMode::Indirect { on_stack: false }`
  arguments (a pointer to a caller-made copy) are now lowered as rustc does on
  x86-64 and AArch64, where the bridge had passed the bytes (cross-backend
  SIGSEGVs and wrong values); padded scalar and pointer newtype returns,
  pointer-carrier unions, by-value closure environments shared by symbol and
  tupled `rust-call` routes that place differently are refused by name.
- Wrong code, rustc bridge: a scalar field read through a reference to a
  struct whose earlier field is a `repr(transparent)` newtype over a
  `str`/slice pointer was read 8 bytes early (`Location::line()` returned the
  filename length).
- Wrong code, rustc bridge: a celled entry argument whose address escapes and
  is written through it was read from the incoming parameter instead of its
  cell.
- Wrong code, rustc bridge: `.sum()`/`.product()` took their operator from
  the accumulator's scalar type, so `Saturating`/`Wrapping` and user `Sum`
  impls got a plain add or multiply and `-Coverflow-checks` was ignored; only
  core's own impls are modeled now, and a reversed reduction whose order is
  observable drives back to front or is refused (`[TCG-ITER-RFOLD-ORDER]`).
- Wrong code, rustc bridge: a local that was both memory-backed and
  address-captured got two homes, so a closure wrapper could hand its callee
  a never-written environment (SIGSEGV, restarted state, wrong
  `MaybeUninit` reads); such a local now has only its stack slot.
- Wrong code, rustc bridge: the by-reference pointee lane tuple gave a
  `&str`/`&[T]` field one `Ptr` lane, shifting later fields; such a field is
  refused by name (`[TCG-FAT-POINTEE-LANE]`) and routed onto the rustc-layout
  byte path.
- Wrong code, rustc bridge: the register class and count of `PassMode::Pair`
  returns and arguments disagreed with rustc across a codegen boundary; both
  are compared with rustc's `FnAbi`, and by-value aggregate returns now follow
  rustc's `PassMode::Indirect` through a hidden leading return buffer (refused
  as `[TCG-RET-ABI]` when the two disagree).
- Wrong code, rustc bridge self-host lane: fmt-dead seeding could skip real
  assignments of a local that flowed into an interception with a live reader;
  every reader must now be proved intercepted.
- Wrong code, x86-64 bridge: a closure whose own parameter is a `&[T]`/`&str`
  slice was called with one 8-byte pointer (SIGSEGV at O0).
- Wrong code, x86-64 bridge: a 16-byte two-integer `PassMode::Pair` argument
  with one register left was placed whole; every such pair now rides rustc's
  two values. A closure parameter pair, a `signext` lane and a 128-bit lane
  stay refused by name.
- Wrong code, x86-64 bridge: one-lane `NonNull<[T]>`/`Unique<[T]>`/`Box<[T]>`
  boundary values where rustc passes a pair are refused by name
  (`[TCG-ARG-ABI]`/`[TCG-RET-ABI]`), the `repr(transparent)` fat-pointer
  newtype chain takes the two-lane slot, and three generic one-lane write
  paths are closed by name.
- Wrong code, x86-64 System V partial eightbytes: narrow pieces were shifted
  over stale upper bits (`[u8; 3]` read back garbage), and a call result's
  partial lane was stored one byte into the adjacent slot.
- Wrong code, x86-64 machine passes: DCE deleted definitions read through
  operand 0 (`JmpR`, `Volatile*MR`, `Cmpxchg8`/`Cmpxchg16`); copy propagation
  and CSE ignored a tied operand 0; LICM missed `StackAlloc`'s write; the
  allocator took `JmpR`'s target as a def; flag liveness across partial flag
  writers and calls was wrong. The classifiers are now exhaustive.
- Wrong code, AArch64 `mac-reg-block`: six admitted nest shapes miscompiled
  (skipped early exit, live-out returned as 0, i32 values in 8-byte cells,
  unchecked or re-checked indices, j body in the header); each publication
  review item is now refused by name (`NestReject`).
- Wrong code, AArch64 calls: a non-HFA composite over 16 bytes was passed as
  the address of its own storage, so a C callee that wrote its parameter
  changed the caller's value; calls now pass a fresh copy.
- Wrong code, AArch64 C ABI: HFA/HVA recognition now works over flattened
  members (more than four declared fields, zero-length array members).
- Wrong code: `InsertField`/`InsertElement` wrote into the source aggregate's
  storage; an enum-typed struct field was loaded as a scalar and its address
  stored (SIGSEGV); a 1-7-byte register aggregate argument loaded 8 bytes.
- Wrong code, AArch64 encoder: moves from or to SP went through ORR (XZR); a
  register operand in an immediate field encoded as 0; FMOV (general) emitted
  unallocated pairings; NEON 64-bit element duplication chose the wrong width.
  Scalar integer/FP conversions now use the integer operand's width.
- Wrong code, vectorizers: the i32 induction-store rewrite stored at `a[0]`
  with a wrapping guard; integer-array bounds substituted a reassignable
  widening source, signed i64 ranges used unsigned order and bottom-tested
  loops lost their first iteration; argmin/argmax re-vectorized its remainder;
  FP fills used wrong alias ranges for negative starts; zero-minus-value
  negation and repeated stores through one post-increment base now stay
  scalar.
- Wrong code, AArch64 CEGIS: the Layer B/C matchers miscounted register reads
  and cache replay applied a recorded body as recorded.
- Wrong code, symbol capture: a module-local function or data definition named
  like a backend runtime symbol (`fmod`, `memcpy`, the i128 helpers) or like
  the personality received the backend's reference (Linux JIT, Mach-O, public
  strict entries); it is refused before lowering on every target
  (`BackendSymbolShadowed`, `DataShadowsBackendSymbol`), and the Core entry
  token can no longer be built outside its helper.
- Wrong code, `merge_modules`: an input without EH structure ran another
  input's module-local personality, and a default definition filling a hidden
  or protected data import stayed exported; merges now keep the most
  constraining visibility and refuse personality changes.
- Wrong code, AArch64 ELF: a function-body `SymbolAddr` naming a thread-local
  lowered to a plain page reference (`[TCG-TLS-SYMBOL-ADDR]` now); mutable
  globals in `.tcommon`, `.gnu_extab`, `.gcc_except_table.x`,
  `.exception_ranges`, `.sframe`, `.eh_frame.x`, `.jcr` or `.bss.rel.ro[.*]`
  faulted on store and are refused by name (`[TCG-SECTION-READONLY]`,
  `[TCG-SECTION-RESERVED]`).
- Wrong code, Linux link driver: GNU ld linked a local-exec TLS object into a
  shared library silently, and GNU ld, gold and LLD installed truncated
  GOT-page/PLT/IPLT/GOT-base relocations, truncated `.eh_frame` pointers,
  unrelocated `-z rel`/Android images, `--noinhibit-exec` and
  `--no-check-sections` outputs; each route is now refused (see Added).
- Wrong code, Mach-O linker: BSS mapping, stub/GOT layout, symbol rebasing,
  weak/strong resolution and dead-strip remapping repaired, and 64-bit data
  pointers are no longer written unslid.
- Soundness: rule discovery no longer accepts a rule on sampled evaluation
  when CEGIS cannot certify it (`Inconclusive`); the strict gate files a
  working checker's rejection of AY's proof as a soundness failure;
  multi-obligation refinement checks discharge every obligation; a vacuous
  sampling sweep is `Unknown`; verifying x86-64 JIT modes reject negative
  statistical evidence.
- Soundness, x86-64 verifying JIT: an empty `ret` body and a `call f; ud2`
  panic entry certified with nothing discharged, because the CALL, JMP and RET
  rows' `covered_elsewhere` certificates counted as discharge evidence; they
  no longer do, so the verifying JIT refuses those bodies (see the ABI
  envelope under Added).
- Resident AY timed out queued queries before they ran; its deadline now
  starts at admission, with a named queue refusal.
- The certificate lane re-solved attributed AY holes until its budget died; a
  bounded negative memo now remembers them.
- AY is no longer refused on hosts with umask 0002: trust-cg creates its cache
  directories `0700`.
- The first start of a new private AY copy, which macOS holds while it
  assesses the file, is made before any solver deadline starts (and recorded
  beside the copy), so a process's first AY query no longer times out on it.
- Refusals lifted: bridge `vec![..]`/`Rc<[T]>` alloc shapes at O2/O3, celled
  return places (`[TCG-SSA-071]`), x86-64 wide numerics and `Option<u128>`
  arguments, further `library/core` shapes and sized-array pointees; AArch64
  `switch` boolean diamonds at O2/O3, the private stack-slot bit-reverse
  idiom, the x86-64 formal-argument prefix with stack-argument loads, and
  three false refusals plus one nondeterministic refusal from the Trust pin
  move.
- The rustc bridge reports the panic location rustc reports; a failing bounds
  check under `panic=abort` traps (recorded in `LIMITATIONS.md`).
- The greedy allocator's split cascade is bounded (`split_depth_cap`); an
  earlier claim that the bound was a measured no-op was false and is
  retracted.
- Robustness: budget, ID-exhaustion and malformed-input boundaries return
  errors; poisoned caches miss; counters saturate; unwind, LEB128, Mach-O
  parse (truncated relocation tables and five related defects) and LLVM file
  input are bounded; hostile-product costs and 128 GiB sparse images in the
  linked-image checks are bounded; the ISel register-list leak is fixed.
- Wrong code, AArch64 LICM: hoisted code was placed before preheader stores
  and falls-through trap guards, so a hoisted load could read memory before a
  preheader store wrote it; it now lands after every preheader store, call and
  trap guard.
- Soundness, AArch64 bounds-check elimination: the carrier arm deleted a
  needed `TrapBoundsCheckExact` when the carrier's block could run again
  without passing the guard; that block is now scanned whole.
- Soundness, x86-64 coverage gate: the sixteen volatile memory rows were
  credited by the address lane alone; they are now credited only by their
  joint ADDRESS + VALUE + BOUNDARY obligation, and the 37 plain address rows
  also require their VALUE reconstruction to discharge.
- Over-refusal, AArch64 ENC-5: proof-grade routes refused every FRINTN word
  (emitted for the rustc bridge's `frintn` inline assembly) as
  `[TCG-DECODE-CHECK-UNDECODED]`; ENC-5 now decodes it from the Arm ARM
  layout. Its value proof stays a deferred row.
- `scripts/check_darwin_aarch64.py` refused to run because the Darwin floor
  inventory neither required nor excluded `trust-cg-lower/rust_empty_filter`;
  that target is now required.

### Added

- The x86-64 vector-compare certificates are re-run by a
  `scripts/soundness_check.sh` leg (`scripts/check_x86_icmp_certificates.py`):
  it builds AY at the revision `Cargo.lock` pins (which must be the one
  trust-ir's per-cell rule names), requires the rule's Clean by sha256,
  regenerates every cell's query from the code (the table
  `x86_icmp_manifest_cells` pins), and re-runs `ay --strict-proofs` and
  `clean cert verify-external` on each certificate-ground cell. A pass is an
  SMT proof of each query checked by the Carcara Alethe checker inside
  Clean, not a Clean-kernel certificate, and it holds only where the leg
  runs: nothing runs `soundness_check.sh` per landing today. A changed query,
  a proof with a `hole`, a Clean rejection, another Clean binary (named, or
  the only ones the search finds) and a missing input each fail by name;
  `SOUNDNESS_SKIP_X86_ICMP_CERTIFICATES=1` turns only a missing input (no
  `clean` at all, no AY source) into a loud SKIP.
- Local overlay toolchains for the formal proof campaign
  (`scripts/assemble_trust_overlay.py`): a Trust pack with a newer AY and
  Clean named by a manifest; a build from an overlay accepts only its Clean,
  and `TRUST_CG_PROOF_IDENTITY_OUT` records the AY and Clean a run executed.
- Linked-image evidence for AArch64 Darwin Mach-O (`L02-P5`; independent
  replay evidence on the image bytes, not a proof):
  `macho::linked_image::record_linked_image` replays the input objects'
  consumed relocations (excluding debug sections and `__LD,__compact_unwind`)
  against an ld64 or
  standalone executable or dylib, accounts every nonzero image byte to an
  object atom or a linker-synthesized section, and checks fixups, import
  ordinals, exports and `__DATA_CONST` placement; `trust-cg
  --linked-image-evidence` writes `<output>.linked-image.json` and removes
  the output on refusal, and every relink removes an earlier record.
- Inline-only runtime bodies (`docs/jit-inline-only-bodies.md`): trust-ir
  `AvailableExternally` bodies are spliced into by-name calls on the JIT path
  (`prepare_jit_lir_module`, which also brings OPT-4's module inliner to the
  JIT) and at the AOT seam (`admit_inline_only_bodies`); a one-block body with
  memory operations is a CFG-tier template. Each spliced body is a disclosed
  one-definition-rule premise (`inline_only_bodies` on the JIT, AOT and
  CompileService results); a proof-claiming compile withholds every body that
  is not authenticated, and `pic` withholds a preemptible one. Kill switches
  `TCG_NO_JIT_LIR_PREPARE` and `TCG_NO_INLINE_ONLY_BODIES`.
- Authenticated inline-only bodies: with dependency modules supplied
  (`Compiler::with_inline_only_dependencies`, `InlineOnlyAuthority`), a body
  whose verified import names a dependency defining the same translated LIR
  has a discharged premise and is the only kind a proof-claiming compile
  splices; supplying dependencies disables compile-artifact reuse.
- x86-64 internal multi-result convention past RAX:RDX (`Fast`/`Cold` edges);
  a `C`/`Rust` edge of that shape is refused by name
  (`[TCG-X86-MULTI-RESULT]`).
- x86-64: 128-bit atomic load (`AtomicLoadCmpxchg16b`; 128-bit store, swap,
  RMW and CAS stay refused), ELF exception handling (typed catches, filters
  and mixed personalities stay refused), the source-bound whole-body theorem
  (I64 chains, pointer and narrow carriers, direct calls, and straight-line
  memory through private stack slots, incoming memory, `StructGep` and sret;
  diagnostic knob `x86-body-dump`), a named
  `call_only_body` certificate, XD-01 exact source/operand binding, and the
  portable certificate tier on Linux.
- x86-64 JIT System V ABI envelope (`x86_source_bound_envelope`, category
  `x86_abi_envelope`): a verifying JIT judges an empty void body and a
  zero-argument `call f; ud2` panic entry by an envelope theorem over their
  final bytes and fixup manifest, replayed in parts and credited only when
  every part replays Valid; the toolchain AY certifies no part, so both
  shapes stay refused by default (a local overlay AY certifies every part).
- AArch64 lowering: i128 `Switch`, sequences and boxed sets (`[TCG-SEQ]`),
  first-class closures (G18-2), direct-tag and niche-encoded enums
  (`[TCG-DIRECT-ENUM]`), enum projection, `MakeAggregate`, same-size
  `Transmute`, constant-size `ArraySplat`/`Splat`, LL/SC atomics without
  FEAT_LSE, 128-bit atomic loads, relocated TLS templates, ARC operations on
  Linux (`Ty::Rc`, `SwiftHeap`/`CleanHeap` cells stay refused), typed catches
  under `__gxx_personality_v0` (`[TCG-EH-TTYPE]`), JIT exception handling
  (D8-D15 frames stay refused), and the `borrow-frame-undef-legalization`
  stage.
- AArch64 ELF: function linkage and visibility, module-local function
  references, hidden/protected declarations and data,
  `Global.section`/`Function.section`, constructor tables, COMDAT groups,
  function sections, SHT_NOBITS zero fill, DWARF 4 under `-g` with parameters
  and variables (`-g` with split text refused), `.note.GNU-stack`, stack
  canaries with runtime-dependency manifests, inline stack probes, fused
  `ADRP; LDR/STR :lo12:`, frameless leaves without a frame owner, and a
  `static`/`pie`/`pic` relocation model with GOT addressing and TLS
  descriptors.
- AArch64 Mach-O: function linkage, `LC_BUILD_VERSION` from the deployment
  target, relocated TLS templates, GOT/TLV slots and weak-def exports in the
  standalone linker (a direct reference to a weak definition is refused), and
  ad-hoc code-signature verification.
- Link driver: `-shared`, `-pie`/`-no-pie`, `-static`, `-nostdlib`, `-soname`,
  `-rpath`, validated `-Wl` groups and classified `error[link:<kind>]`
  diagnostics; refusal of BTI/PAC requests (`[TCG-LINK-BTI-PAC]`), local-exec
  TLS on every link route (`[TCG-LINK-TLS-MODEL]`) and `@` response files
  (`[TCG-LINK-RESPONSE-FILE]`); and, on Linux, staged image checks for
  relocation windows (`[TCG-RELOC-WINDOW-*]`), GOT-page/PLT/IPLT/GOT-base
  reach (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-*]`), `.eh_frame` window, alias and hidden FDEs
  (`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-*]`), TPREL 2^32, the entry point, relocation formats
  (`[TCG-LINK-RELOCATION-FORMAT]`), loaded bytes (`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]`)
  and silencing options (`[TCG-LINK-NOINHIBIT-EXEC]`,
  `[TCG-LINK-NO-CHECK-SECTIONS]`).
- Verifier: ENC-5 arms for every word-encodable AArch64 form (proof-grade
  routes refuse an undecoded word, `[TCG-DECODE-CHECK-UNDECODED]`),
  switch-dispatch binding to final bytes (`[TCG-A64-SWITCH-BIND]`), NZCV
  producer/consumer obligations, decoded-word value and FCVT obligations, the
  Movk/Movn form-polymorphic gate, volatile access preservation, the frame
  dataflow net, independent physical liveness, the final-layout cross-check,
  typed frame-binding mismatches and TV-3 fusion-edge checks.
- JIT: tier-up (`trust_cg_codegen::tier_up`), page-protection witnesses,
  CTR_EL0 icache flushing with refused RWX/RW requests, and AArch64
  certificate-cache identity controls.
- rustc bridge: the AArch64 two-value argument lane for `PassMode::Pair`
  (`Option<u128>` and `Sext` lanes stay refused), the matmul nest reaching
  `mac-reg-block` (`UnprovenBoundsCarrier` refusals), and Linux unwind/cleanup
  and `#[thread_local]` twins in the bridge runner (`catch_unwind` in a bridge
  frame and a `#[link_section]` thread-local stay refused).
- Evidence infrastructure: `benchmarks/compile-corpus` (Identity PASS
  required), the trust-ir construct inventory gate, the Linux fuzz lane with
  planted-failure controls, bridge-workspace, feature-gated and decided-absent
  floor rows, proof-tool identity recording, the Cargo configuration audit,
  Darwin twins of the Linux C-boundary, EH/RAII, construct-sweep, sret, `f16`
  and enum oracles, and linked-image byte binding of the arithmetic AOT
  leaves.
- Binary input accepts the bare `TRUST_IR` container; `--aarch64-isa-features`
  selects an explicit ISA profile; sibling tail calls read classified ABI
  facts.
- AArch64 optimizer: LICM hoists a not-guaranteed-to-execute load from one
  fixed-size stack slot (`licmframespec`), and bounds-check elimination folds
  an explicit `cmp; b.hs trap` dominated by a strict unsigned guard on the
  same index and length (`bcetrapbranch`).
- AArch64 Mach-O relocation inventory digest: every proofs-on object is
  reparsed and its relocation kinds must equal `object_relocation_inventory`
  (compared by kind, not placement).
- Proof-wall census (L07-P2): the bridge knob `opcode-inventory-trace` and
  `scripts/proof_wall_census.py`; instruction-derived obligations for admitted
  shapes of 34 AArch64 opcodes (`aarch64_instruction_word_proofs`), reported
  as unverified rather than credit, with ENC-5 requiring the emitted word to
  be the re-derived one.
- trust-ir round-trip gate (L05-P7; test-rung evidence over the pinned corpus
  and a generated sample, not a proof): `trust_ir_corpus_roundtrip` drives
  every module of the pinned trust-ir conformance corpus (live, `compat/`,
  `v41-reader-compat/` and must-refuse goldens in tMBC, JSON, text and
  MessagePack) through trust-cg's readers and writers, against trust-ir's own
  reader and the independent MessagePack codec: 232 module files read exactly,
  24 refused by the corpus-predicted name, 119 MessagePack files refused as
  not a trust-cg input. `tmbc_roundtrip_prop` gains a shrinking construct
  generator (aggregates, enums of every layout encoding, records, closures,
  collections, globals/TLS, handles, refinements, dialect, proof and lineage
  tables, v41-v50 metadata, wire-gap constructs). Both are on the Darwin and
  Linux floors (the Linux rows not yet run on a Linux host). Named residuals
  are listed in `LIMITATIONS.md`, including that JSON and text admit the nine
  modules whose tMBC form the reader refuses as a producer omission.

### Changed

- Decisions that spelled the same set as one of TrustIR's proved decision
  tables now call it: `AllocOrigin::is_reference_counted` (fsym's heap-object
  kind), `Ordering::is_legal_for_load` / `is_legal_for_store` (the adapter's
  atomic gates, the LIR compare-exchange failure rule and the LSE2 128-bit
  load gate) and `Linkage::is_module_local` (the module-local linkage checks
  in lowering, codegen, llvm-import and fsym). Each replacement is
  behaviour-identical on every input cell (an exhaustive cell comparison, not
  a proof about trust-cg). The deliberate differences stay their own tables
  with the reason stated, each held by a test that fails if it is collapsed
  onto the proved table: static-link replacement omits `ExternalWeak`,
  completion claims include `Trusted`, and fsym does not take the
  one-definition-rule premise (a bodied `WeakOdr` / `LinkOnceOdr` /
  `AvailableExternally` callee handed a pointer stays an unsummarized
  Unknown).
- Update the TrustIR pin from `9674bea5` to `86d978bb` (trust-ir `main`,
  2026-09-30), including workspace/bridge/fuzz locks and the compile-artifact
  identity salt. Clean stays `afe42324` and AY `f28345ff`. The range carries
  the allocation-bounds rework (`ALLOC_BYTE_BUDGET` is gone and
  `check_allocation_bounds` reports only sizes not provably bounded, with
  element sizes on every target), the function-dependency and
  type-reachability analyses (`CallableCarriers`), and persistent
  interpreter collections: sequence and set values are now `ArrayValue`
  ropes like arrays and vectors. Consumer change: the fsym run model's
  `forged_part` walks a sequence's or set's STORED values once (a splat's
  element once), as it already did for arrays and vectors, and
  `the_run_model_admits_exactly_its_runs` covers forged pointers and handles
  inside sequence and set ropes, splats included. No wire, corpus or
  construct-inventory change. Also fixed with the move: the source-module
  custody capture (`FunctionSourceModules::capture`) mirrored only two of
  `trust_ir_build::wire_identity_blocker`'s four probes, so a module
  carrying a completeness claim or a bound CleanCic recheck reached the
  binary writer's assertion and panicked; it now refuses both by name, in
  the validator's order. Its custody test, whose `UnOp::CtLz` stopped being
  a wire gap at v51, now pins that a v51 WS3.20 instruction binds and that
  each remaining non-wire construct is refused on either side.
  Dependency/corpus tests are regression evidence, not proof.
- Update the TrustIR pin from `85e5c2d6` to `9674bea5` (trust-ir `main`,
  2026-09-30), including workspace/bridge/fuzz locks and the compile-artifact
  identity salt. Clean stays `afe42324` and AY `f28345ff`. The range carries
  wire v51, the INST wire batch: `MakeAggregate`, `MemCopy`, `MemSet`,
  `RotL`/`RotR`/`FCopySign` and `CtLz`/`CtTz`/`BSwap`/`BitReverse` gain
  binary tags, so `Inst::binary_wire_gap` names none and the tMBC writer,
  proof custody and the compile service bind modules carrying them instead
  of refusing them as `NoTmbcWireImage` (the header rises to 51 only for such
  a module). Also the total must-refuse runner (`corpus()` returns
  `Result<Corpus, CorpusError>`, `Corpus::uncovered` replaces the free
  function), one fresh-id rule in core and `trust-ir-build`, and
  `trust-ir-ay` session poisoning. Consumer changes: both must-refuse
  targets and the corpus round trip take the typed corpus; the construct
  generator's v51 members must now round-trip exactly (only an inlining
  scope chain and a completeness claim remain wire gaps); the WS3.20 and
  compile-service tests pin the bound image (proof custody still fails closed
  at promotion); the corpus census gains the `inst_wire_batch` golden, and
  `tests/fixtures/trust_ir_binary_container/` re-vendors it as the fixture at
  the pinned writer's version. Dependency/corpus tests are regression
  evidence, not proof.
- Update the TrustIR pin from `c7ba4b33` to `85e5c2d6` (trust-ir `main`,
  2026-09-30), including workspace/bridge/fuzz locks and the compile-artifact
  identity salt. Clean stays `afe42324` and AY `f28345ff`. The range is
  documentation: the agent-instruction cut, the wire-allocation tool's
  reservation guidance (`wire_alloc.py`, `wire-allocations.toml`), two
  de-linked changelog citations and a dated-record label. In crates it touches
  only the comment header of `wire_versions.tsv`; no wire, type or ABI layout
  change. Dependency/corpus tests are regression evidence, not proof.
- Update the TrustIR pin from `dc37f640` to `c7ba4b33` (trust-ir `main`,
  2026-09-30), including workspace/bridge/fuzz locks and the compile-artifact
  identity salt. Clean stays `afe42324` and AY `f28345ff`. The range is
  gate 15 (an opt-in verified survey), gate-13 cell completeness over enum
  tables, SPEC §17 and dialect docs, the publish T1 revocation check, and the
  release of wire slot 53 (single-enum representation, obsolete; the later
  reserved slots renumber). In crates it touches only `trust-ir-laws`
  documentation and `wire_versions.tsv`; no wire, type or ABI layout change.
  Dependency/corpus tests are regression evidence, not proof.
- Update the TrustIR pin from `1814992a` to `dc37f640` (trust-ir `main`,
  2026-09-30), including workspace/bridge/fuzz locks and the compile-artifact
  identity salt. Clean stays `afe42324` and AY `f28345ff`. The range adds
  trust-ir's rule that freeing an allocation under a live borrow is undefined
  behaviour (`c06a487f`), gate-13 decision tables and publish/docs changes;
  no wire, type or ABI layout change. fsym follows the new interpreter site:
  the UB map owns "Dealloc: allocation is under a live borrow" as an owed
  InvalidFree verdict, and that verdict is no longer `Safe` for an object a
  call on the path could reach (the callee may leave a borrow of it live),
  in addition to a path that borrowed; the layout port's `alloc_with_slack`
  fingerprint is re-pinned (it only initializes the two new record fields).
  Dependency/corpus tests are regression evidence, not proof.
- Update the TrustIR pin from `fca90a2c` to `1814992a` and Clean from
  `9497ddd4` to `afe42324`, including workspace/bridge/fuzz locks and the
  compile-artifact identity salt. AY remains `f28345ff`. The TrustIR range
  updates proof-ID allocation and external proof infrastructure and reserves
  nominal-identity wire tags; it does not change the shipped type/ABI layout.
  Dependency/corpus tests are regression evidence, not proof.
- The codegen license is bound to evidence, and a claim-less body is refused
  by default (roadmap WS7.5; F-006, the F-116 residue, the F-103 consumer
  half; DG-73, DG-22). `CodegenLicensePolicy::verdict(&Module, FuncId)` and
  `enforce_module` run trust-ir's `codegen_license_errors` first and refuse
  its findings by name on every lane, wasm32 and the inline-only
  (`AvailableExternally`) lane included: `GatedWithoutEvidence` (an
  evidence-bound authority such as `clean-kernel-tv` without exactly one
  `Certified` TranslationValidation row whose `clean_backend_tv` certificate
  the kernel replays against the current body) and `GatedFunctionRefuted` (a
  `Failed` TranslationValidation, Precondition or Postcondition row about the
  body); a module with a `Gated` body whose function ids are not unique is
  refused (`ambiguous FuncId`) rather than trusting how the pin resolves the
  tie. `body_gate: None` is refused by default; the CLI's disclosed
  `--permit-unlicensed` and the census-pinned `UnlicensedPermitException`
  sites (the CLI and `ty_replay_jit_probe`, the closed-JIT Core admission
  floor, the in-process MIR lane on both its native and wasm32 arms, the JIT
  kernel matrix, the LLVM importer, the fuzz harnesses, the jit-matrix bench
  tools replaying claim-less corpora, the wasm32 lane's own runtime helper
  bodies `fmod` / `divmod128`) are the only ways to compile a claim-less body (the census also pins how
  many times each production file names the license types, so a glob import,
  rename, alias or trait impl cannot reach `Permit` uncounted), and hand-built
  test modules state `Permit`. WS7.5(c) (`BodyGate::Gated { evidence }`) waits
  for trust-ir WS1.12's wire part. Tests: `codegen_license_evidence` (lower,
  codegen) and `codegen_license_flags` (CLI), with a `mutation-knobs` control;
  Part A-Lean's `should_emit` harness and clean's legacy native fixture need
  `--permit-unlicensed`.
- The kernel-JIT fixture targets are qualified for the installed Trust
  compiler `trustc 0.10.0+g450403669` on `aarch64-apple-darwin`
  (`qualifies_current_kernel_fixtures`).
- AArch64 ELF symbol-binding coverage (L02-P6 fifth audit): floor rows for
  declaration-only and identical merges and the data `SymbolAddr`/stub
  address forms; no emitted bytes change.
- Darwin AArch64 rustc-bridge tests no longer pass without running (ledger
  `L06-P10`, `X-HOST-P12`; testing evidence, unverified lane). A missing
  prerequisite on this host fails by name, a refusal is never an accepted
  early return, and every test prints a positive-evidence marker.
  `scripts/check_darwin_aarch64_bridge.py` requires all 13 Darwin bridge
  targets (80 tests). It credits a pass only with the test's own marker, holds
  each target to an exact evidence profile and proofs-off count, and checks
  each marker's `certs=` against the backend-knob arguments the test built

  certificates-on test cannot quietly move to `no-proof-certs`. Its inventory
  check follows every module a required fixture compiles in (`#[path]`,

- trust-ir pin moves (to `fca90a2c`, with the Clean and AY revisions

- A complete but unemittable declared struct layout is refused

- Measurements (not proof): the L14-P8 Darwin arm64 re-measure at `80b0e03aa`
  (`reports/perf/2026-09-29-darwin-aarch64-remeasure/`) appended a second
  QUIET `aarch64-apple-darwin` ledger row whose coverage is still 0.0% (all 18

- Tests that asserted nothing unless a proof succeeded now fail on a rejected
  proof; unrequested formal campaigns are runtime SKIPs; skipped soundness
  prerequisites fail completion; bridge tests load the backend Cargo built for
  them; harnesses switch proof certificates explicitly.
- The compiler's AArch64 JIT (`Compiler::compile_module_to_jit`) links sealed
  functions: the encoder skips the final-stream check only when it equals the
  one preparation ran and passed (`TCG_NO_SEALED_JIT_LINK` disables it).
- Compile cost (measurements, not proof): superlinear pre-RA scheduling and
  register-allocation scans are replaced with objects byte-identical (L14-P6),
  and per-process proof-tool custody work is cut to one control proof per
  checker state (L14-P5); `trust_cg_verify::process_cost` counts checker

- Reduce repeated allocator and loop-pass scans and overlap Darwin proof-tool
  startup with private-copy verification. Active-register indexing, refreshed
  loop indexes and batch coalescing retain differential controls; scaling and

  records host/revision-bound measurements, remaining nonlinear terms and the
  inherited proof-enabled fixed-cost refusal. These are testing and measurement

- Size and memory accounting (L14-P10; measurement definitions, not proof):
  `benchmarks/beat-llvm/contract/gates.json` version 3 defines emitted-code
  size, the code and read-only data bytes of the linked image that the
  linker's map attributes to the compile's own objects
  (`benchmarks/beat-llvm/emitted_size.py`, gated by the new S3/S4), next to
  the linked file size, which includes the shared standard library and reads
  about 1.00x. Program and compiler peak RSS are now the median of 5
  interleaved samples per lane, all retained, with a spread-aware R1 band; a
  comparison whose relative sample spread exceeds 0.25 is noisy and never
  counts as parity, so one outlier sample makes R1 unmeasured instead of
  passing a real loss. A run with no MATCH row is held to the provenance
  RSS N only, in the checker and in the harness's eligibility stamp alike.
  Results schema `trust-cg-bench-v2`; ledger rows condensed from it carry
  `ledger_row_schema` 2, and older rows stay readable but are not baselines
  for the redefined metrics.
- Compiler memory (L14-P10; measurements, not proof): the rustc bridge
  compiles its lowered trust-ir in `join_codegen`, after rustc drops the type
  context, with every fail-closed routing decision taken beforehand, and two
  eager type renderings no longer compute rustc's visible-path map (a
  surfaced scalar-leaf refusal that embeds a type now names the type's
  defining-crate path, such as `core::` where it said `std::`). A committed
  test (`unsupported_program`
  `no_mangle_roots_are_never_dropped_when_their_object_compile_fails`) pins
  that a required root whose deferred object compile fails is a named failed
  root, never a dropped std-internal record (testing evidence: it fails
  against a backend whose deferred routes are all forced to the drop; the
  Darwin bridge runner credits it as an expected refusal and now requires
  81 tests). Emitted
  objects are byte-identical on the 18 beat-llvm programs and four
  `scale_gate.py` crates; in the `no-proof-certs` diagnostic lane compiler
  peak RSS falls from 1.188x to 1.109x LLVM `-O2` on the corpus and from
  298.1 MiB to 240.8 MiB (1.48x to 1.20x) on the 800-function scale crate
  (`reports/perf/2026-09-29-darwin-l14p10-size-memory/`).

### Removed

- The unreachable two-arm "early continue" admit path in
  `model_in_loop_diamond`.
- Unstamped historical performance, size and speedup claims in comments.

## [0.6.0] - 2026-08-30

### Fixed

- x86-64 O0 wrong code: the formal-argument fixup sank a live-range split
  connector below a parallel-copy group that overwrote its source register
  (six or more GPR arguments), and the first repair over-rotated by hoisting
  connectors above the stack-argument loads they depend on; barriers are now
  emitted only on a true source overwrite.
- x86-64 O0 wrong code: spill materialization aliased destination and
  left-hand operand to one scratch register when the right-hand operand was
  the destination vreg (`AddRR vX, vY, vX` with everything spilled), computing
  `p2 + p2` where `p3 + p2` was required.
- Optimizer recognition gates, each closing a demonstrated miscompile and
  each fail-closed: the x86-64 vectorizer requires the counter to enter the
  loop as a literal 0 from the preheader; the vectorizer refuses a non-`RBIT`
  instruction or a compare idiom at the wrong plan-wide element arrangement;
  `neon-fpred` requires the accumulator to enter as `+0.0`; the x86-64
  unroller refuses an invariant constant whose vreg meets a hidden
  (`Xchg`/`Cmpxchg`-class) def; the x86-64 pure-call hoist refuses a
  preheader splice point where `RFLAGS` is live across the call; AArch64
  `strided-store-unroll` refuses an early normal exit from the loop body and
  decides divergence by an opcode whitelist rather than "no `Ret`" (a
  `TailCall` is not a return); and the single-test `cbz` rotation refuses a
  body whose conditional also targets the header.
- x86-64 guard-carrier canaries: the per-kind memo now records the
  condition it validated and fails closed when a later request for the same
  kind names a different condition (salvaged from a retired Codex branch).
- The public-clone release gate parses `benchmarks/beat-llvm/run.py` before
  trusting it, so a syntax error in the differential harness fails the gate
  instead of silently producing no evidence (salvaged from a retired Codex
  branch, with unit tests).
- 20 production panic-family sites that landed after the 2026-08-26 audit
  baseline classified and repaired per the audit's own categories.
- A test that skips for a missing solver, checker, toolchain, target or C
  compiler now prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` instead of passing silently
  (154 sites across `trust-cg-verify` and the AArch64 link-and-run tests).

### Added

- x86-64, on by default: variable-count rotate `RolRCl` joins the proof
  perimeter and the bridge's 7-instruction variable-rotate expansion fuses to
  it (admission-gated); loop-exit branch inversion; frame-address spill fold,
  rematerialized LEA hop and dead self-copy elision; the flags-deadness scan
  continues through partial writers and `x7` lowers as two LEAs.
- x86-64 opt-in experiments: the two-address expand last-use gate and its
  call-shaped variants (refuted as defaults by paired A/B), and cold-arm
  sinking (`TCG_X86_COLD_ARM_SINK`, an opt-in soak pending real workloads).
- AArch64 post-RA: the narrow zero-extend collapse deletes a provably
  redundant `MOV`/`UXTW` pair and admits copy pseudos.
- AArch64 block layout, each behind its own kill switch: trap-sink,
  dominated `cbz` threading, and single-test do-while rotation.
- Seven adversarial kill-at-def tests for the AArch64 pre-RA coalescer's
  logical and shifted producers.
- `fuzz/repros/`: the differential-fuzz repro corpora, with runners that work
  from any checkout, and a README saying what each corpus pins.

### Changed

- Eight Codex-era remote heads pushed on 2026-08-29 were audited, two hunks
  salvaged, every tip archived under an annotated tag and a verified bundle,
  and the heads retired (`docs/archive/remote-branch-retirement-2026-08-29.md`).
- Rotates and memory-RMW opcodes are modeled in `writes_flags`.
- Dependency pins advanced through the released trust-ir 0.10.0, 0.11.0 and
  0.12.0 to 0.13.0, and through AY 0.19.0 to the 0.22.0 epoch; the soundness
  lock re-pinned; the publication mapping carries the compile-artifact cache
  partition identities.
- Per-pass timing and dump labels are built only when a consumer is enabled.
- `trust-cg-test ratchet warnings` is the single warnings-ratchet
  implementation; `TCG_SOLVER_PATH` is wired to what the code reads.
- `publish/DECISIONS.md` describes the current tree and dependency tuple;
  `CLAUDE.md`'s publication block is the generator's output again;
  `benchmarks/README.md` indexes the benchmark directories.

### Removed

- Dependencies nothing used (`clap_mangen`, `thiserror`, `tracing`, `blake3`,
  `constant_time_eq`, `arbitrary` and unused workspace crates); the three
  lockfiles stay `--locked`-clean.
- 38 dead definitions that `#[allow(dead_code)]` was hiding.
- The shell twins of the warnings and test ratchets, and the scripts that
  could not run (`scripts/fuzz/bench_ext.py`, `bench_prod.py`,
  `ws2_sweep.sh`, `dylib_load_bench.sh`, `tools/perf_sweep.py`).
- The seven root-level `.fuzz-*` directories (moved to `fuzz/repros/`).

## [0.5.0] - 2026-08-28

### Fixed

- Float-to-narrow-integer `as` casts (`i8`/`i16`/`i32`/`u8`/`u16`/`u32`) did
  not saturate: an out-of-range float produced a truncated value at every
  optimization level. Wrong code, reachable from ordinary Rust.
- AArch64 ABI: 16-byte-aligned GPR arguments now start on an even register
  (AAPCS64 C.8), an `i128` passed on the stack carries both of its words on
  both sides of the call, and Darwin `i128` register placement is honored.
- AArch64: a struct or array field offset past 4095 is now lowered through
  the total add-immediate form instead of failing in the encoder at O0/O1.
- The AArch64 symbolic-CFG authority check fired on `Trap*` guard carriers,
  refusing every program carrying an `InBounds` or `ShiftInRange` annotation.
- Vectorizer recognizer tiers: the carrier-drift soundness holes opened by the
  carriers-are-reads redesign are closed fail-closed across the tiers.
- Optimizer idempotence: `mac-reg-block`, `neon-fill`, `neon-bytesum` and nine
  more loop vectorizers re-fired on their own remainder loop every fixpoint
  iteration. Every loop-building pass now passes a second-run pin, and the
  x86-64 vectorizer runs once per function at O3, on the raw post-ISel shape
  its legality arguments assume.
- `rustc` bridge hard declines removed for `for` loops over const-folded
  ranges, aggregate-to-aggregate transmutes, whole-aggregate moves from
  projected memory-backed sources, and `&mut`-returning functions at O0/O1.
- `rustc` bridge emits canonical trust-ir: bool constants carry
  `Constant::Bool`, same-width integer reinterpret copies lower to `Bitcast`,
  constant shift amounts take the shifted value's type, vtable globals
  declare their aggregate type and are addressed by `GlobalAddr`, vtable-shim
  by-pointer receivers agree with their signature, `target_info` is stamped
  on modules entering merge, and merge admits `FatPtrKind::ContainerLen`.
  Dynamic bounds-check identity fails closed.
- Verification: the C flag is derived from the adder carry-out and the `UGE`
  proofs are back; a dead `Copy` of a carried-unchanged parameter no longer
  fails the loop-completeness gate; compiled `Var` slots are numbered by
  distinct input name; the FP evaluator's `FCMP` name parser fails closed and
  knows the wasm spelling; the session cache is bound to exact SMT2 bytes;
  AArch64 `ROR` immediates are reconstructed; return-register sinks are
  authenticated.
- The compile-artifact cache binds its unchecked-default identities to the
  dependency cohort and advances them with the manifest pins, so an artifact
  cannot replay across a dependency change.
- Windows codegen portability restored; JIT feature names compared by value.
- 153 production panic-family sites classified and repaired per the panic
  audit's own categories.
- Gate scripts: the Clean stock-cargo soundness lane was Darwin-only; one
  dependency graph is required across the standalone locks; `check_fmt`
  could not run on the pinned toolchain; the publication private-source
  assertion could not fail; the test suite no longer shells out
  `kill -KILL -<pid>`, which util-linux turns into `kill(-1)`.

### Added

- `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (alias `wasm32`): a closed-module
  WebAssembly lane taking exactly one trust-ir module to raw `.wasm` bytes,
  with named refusals for the object/linker/optimization/proof options that do
  not apply to it. It runs no optimization, register allocation, or object
  path, and emits no proof certificates. See [`LIMITATIONS.md`](LIMITATIONS.md).
- wasm lane: an import section and index space, memory policy, and islands
  living inside a host's memory under the `trust:island/abi@1` namespace;
  narrow types, sub-word memory, data segments and `br_table`; encoding,
  CFG-structural and memory/call-ABI obligation families in
  `scripts/soundness_check.sh` (necessary structural conditions, not a proof);
  node-based differential and CFG-fuzz oracles; island generator examples
  with a three-way differential runner over the shipped bytes; and
  `scripts/pure_lane_wasm.sh`, real Rust to wasm with no LLVM in the chain.
- `rustc` bridge shapes: constant-range subslices of arrays, `Vec` and `str`
  at O1 (all range kinds); const-pointer scalar, aggregate and enum/union
  reference call arguments at O1; `mem::swap` of aggregates; the discriminant
  of a projected fieldless enum (`match (state, input)`).
- x86-64 optimizations, on by default, each with a `TCG_NO_X86_*` kill switch:
  the c-row-in-register saxpyq tier, saxpyq x4 unroll with scalar `IMUL`
  products, 4-wide heap-sumq, LEA displacement fold, latch-advance collapse,
  small-constant `IMUL` strength reduction, function-wide constant-guard
  elimination, the masked-range guard tier, post-fixup XMM bridge-copy
  collapse, and memory-destination RMW fusion gated on the live
  reconstruction discharge.
- x86-64 opt-in experiments, measured and refuted as defaults: the
  commutative dying-source-first swap and the loop-rotation admission port.
- AArch64: packed `llvm.fmuladd.v4f32`/`.v2f64` imported as a native vector
  form with a tied-destination `FMLA` lowering, FP splats admitted by the
  importer, register-form `<2 x f64>` lane extract, the runtime-trip partial
  unroll gated on profile hotness, and call-crossing callee-saved hints wired
  into production.
- `rustc` bridge runtime: body-wide `assume` scratch elision, and `Vec::new`
  uses rustc's `RawVec` minimum non-zero capacity.
- Proof perimeter: `PUNPCKLQDQ` and memory-destination `XorMR`/`AddMR`
  (+SIB) join via reconstruction with no allowlist; certified removal of dead
  NZCV writes; `TST`-fed branches cite the `TST` obligation; opt-in precise
  `CMP`/`B.cond` citations (`TCG_PRECISE_CITATIONS=1`); a golden fixture
  pinning every certificate walk query's resolution; the static proof corpus
  audited from 1,877 to 1,907.
- JIT artifacts attest the selected host codegen profile.
- Test infrastructure: shape-coverage programs s26–s71 (trait objects,
  closures, iterators, u128, packed, float and signedness boundaries) with a
  ratchet on oracle builds and declines; `abi-xback` varies return types and
  fails closed on missing coverage; an in-repo 54-compile completeness gate;
  idempotence pins over every firing shape of the vectorizers and second-run
  pins for the remaining passes; layout-twin agreement over 5,000 random
  nested types; the alias-closure/overlap relation pinned over the whole
  encoding space; call-boundary ABI variant pins; benchmark evidence rejects
  stale or incomplete runs; `TCG_DIAG_CHANGED` reports silent mutation; a
  Trust default-authority gate.

### Changed

- Compile time, measured on the 18-program corpus: proofs-on warm compile
  went from 2.284x LLVM -O2 (first AArch64 evidence row, 2026-08-25) to
  1.008x vs -O2 and 0.995x vs -O3 in the latest headline-eligible ledger row
  (2026-08-26; cold 1.005x; runtime geomean 0.878x vs -O3; 18/18 match). The
  levers: the sweep lane (kind-parallel pre-warm, chunked and lane-batched
  sweeps, a u128 batched evaluator for the wide obligations, the speculative
  init sweep, asynchronous pre-warm), the per-box certificate cache on by
  default, memoized registry queries, the proof database and the fixed
  modules off the critical path, the register-allocation validator's
  per-instruction transfer precompiled once per function, the analysis cache
  carried across fixpoint iterations, a bounded global rayon pool sized by
  work, demand-driven bridge lowering, merge validating merged-first,
  per-wave NZCV liveness, and constant-factor work across the optimizer
  passes.
- Dependency pins: trust-ir at its v38 revision (`ContainerLen`), AY 0.17.0;
  the soundness lock and the compile-artifact cache identities re-pinned with
  them. The tracked toolchain remains Rust 1.97.1; Trust verification is an
  explicit, checked gate rather than a default-lane claim.
- The CEGIS cache uses an in-tree wire format (VERSION 6) instead of
  `rmp-serde`; its Layer A Alethe exemption is retired.
- Docs: v0.1.0-era staleness retired across the public surface
  (`LIMITATIONS.md` de-versioned with a WebAssembly section, `ROADMAP.md`
  points at the ledger instead of restating numbers), the promote tier
  described as it actually works, the trust-ir dominator patch retired after
  landing upstream, and repository links point at `alabsystems`.

### Removed

- `rmp-serde` and `rmp` from the shipping dependency closure.
- The staged trust-ir dominator patch under `patches/`.
- The CEGIS Alethe-gap test exemption.

## [0.4.0] - 2026-08-21

### Fixed

- AArch64 register allocation treated X8, the AAPCS64 `sret` pointer, as
  allocatable, producing wrong code at O0–O3.
- Twelve fail-closed recognition gates from two optimizer audit rounds, each
  closing a demonstrated miscompile, one of them an NZCV flag-liveness defect.
- Further optimizer fail-closed repairs: copy-chain resolution now requires a
  single reaching def, and LICM requires an insertion point on the entering
  path and an invariant load dominating every latch.
- `mac-reg-block` miscompiled matmuls over non-8-byte elements; `neon-reduce`
  overwrote the accumulator instead of folding the vector drain into it.
- `sret` and target-ABI selection on AArch64, and ABI return-register ordering
  in the scheduler.
- Vendored `drat-trim` failed to build under strict C99 on glibc.

### Added

- An AArch64 ELF relocation proof lane with `Certified` composition, emitted
  TLS rows bound to replayed object authority, and an artifact-level relocation
  row digest.
- Build-embedded portable canary certificates that replay without AY.
- A per-shape differential gate for the `rustc` bridge, checked against rustc's
  LLVM backend at O0–O3.

### Changed

- Optimizer and encoder performance work on both primary targets: x86 immediate
  step collapse into LEA, loop-aware spill weighting on by default, extended
  loop rotation, dominated zero-test resolution, NEON fill/map/array lanes.
- Compile-time work retiring the remaining `def_path_str` classifiers and the
  first-item warmup.
- trust-ir, AY, and Clean pinned at their release frontier.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-08-18

### Fixed

- Post-index address formation had a latent W/X sub-register blindness and a
  second, drifted copy of the register-overlap predicate.

### Added

- A runtime-trip partial-unroll tier, correct and measured but not enabled.
- Partial-unroll diagnostics now report not-recognized loops, not only declined
  ones.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-08-17

### Fixed

- 128-bit register-offset loads and stores were encoded as 64-bit.
- The differential oracle executed `PRFM` as a 64-bit load and accepted `LD1`/
  `ST1` `1D` forms that the target refuses as unallocated.
- The stack-protector canary is now hoisted above every local.

### Added

- AArch64 native and packed-FP vector lowering, and fail-closed vector-type
  support in the importer.
- Loop optimization: a partial (factor) unroller, call-bearing exact-trip full
  unroll, bounded-trip diamond unroll, multi-exit bounded unroll, innermost-loop
  layout preference, and single-block scan-loop rotation.
- Post-RA scalar post-index address formation, on by default.
- Complete AArch64 opcode-inventory and shifted-opcode coverage tests, and an
  exact opcode strategy census.
- Support for the trust-ir boolean connectives `BAnd`/`BOr`/`BXor`.

### Changed

- Proof and certificate authority hardening: exact proof-corpus cardinality,
  strict AY transcript authority, hard failure on rejected proof authority, and
  lattice replay sealed against carrier substitution.
- Compile-time work on the per-compile path-trimming machinery and lazy post-RA
  overlap masks.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-08-12

Initial research-preview source release.

### Included

- AArch64 and x86-64 compiler backends with AOT object emission and JIT paths.
- Experimental RISC-V 64 lowering and encoding.
- Binary tMBC input plus text and JSON debugging formats.
- Proof obligations, evaluator and solver-backed verification lanes,
  strict `tcg-lrat-cert-v2` canary certificates, structured proof artifacts,
  and fail-closed proof-required compilation.
- Differential, triple-oracle, fuzz, target, object, and soundness test
  infrastructure.
- The SAT-Competition 2026 trust-cg-sat experiment and reproducible benchmark
  material.
- A source-only workspace distribution with exact dependency identities,
  fail-closed publication mapping, and flattened, licensed MicroSAT and
  drat-trim sources.

### Release status

This is an alpha research release, not a production compiler or full Rust
backend. See [`LIMITATIONS.md`](LIMITATIONS.md).
